title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield in the ice machine was observed with accumulating mold slime during the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure that it is cleaned. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean so that Ready-To-Eat foods are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that there is not a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. PICs were notified -- their previous certification recently expired. PICs plan to renew their CFPM. Ensure that the PICs are CFPMs who are always present when food preparation is happening.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed an accumulation of soil residues on the following:
(i) the interior of the soda machine nozzles. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and cleaned the nozzles during the inspection until they were clean to sight and touch.
(ii) inside the ice machine. PIC was informed and instructed to clean and maintain the machine regularly to prevent contamination.
Ensure food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that several sanitizer buckets did not have a measureable amount of sanitizer in them - 0ppm (Chlorine) for the sanitizer bucket in the bar and 0ppm (quaternary ammonium) for the sanitizer buckets in the dish area. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and remade the buckets so that they measured a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer: 100ppm (Cl) for the bar sanitizer bucket made from bleach and water (1 capful of bleach to 1 gallon of water); and 200pm (quat) for the dish room sanitizer buckets (filled from the dispenser over the mop sink). Ensure that sanitizers are used per manufacturer instructions so that there is a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer for food-contact surfaces: 50-200 ppm for Chlorine-based sanitizer and 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium.
citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed a gap between the exterior door and door frame so that there was visible daylight along the bottom of the door. PIC was informed and will repair the door or attach a barrier to avoid entry of insects, rodents and other animals.
citation_text: 6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed an opened can of tomato purée that is stored in a cooler in its original can without a cover. Opened cans of food are not storage containers (once opened, the can itself can be source of potential contamination, especially if the food item is acidic). CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the product was removed from the cooler so that it could be repackaged in a cleanable container. Ensure that food is protected from potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the scoop in the chips in the server area stored with the handle touching the chips. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the scoop was moved to sit on top of the chip container where the handle does not touch the food. Since the handle is touched by bare hands it must be stored above the top of food. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single-use containers stored on top of the prep cooler upright where the food-contact surfaces are exposed to debris from above. CORRECTED: Staff were informed and inverted the containers so that the food-contact surfaces were protected from contamination. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are protected by either inversion or cover from a closed shelf or packaging.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed no lids on the trash cans in the women's restroom. PIC was made aware and will ensure that the women’s stalls each have covered trash receptacles.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(i) Observed a broken gasket in the hot box in the kitchen; PIC was informed and will repair the gasket. 
(ii) Observed the mop sink needs to be resealed to the wall as the original seal has crumbled; PIC was informed and will get the mop sink resealed.
Ensure that all physical facilities are in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.  [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mops drying on the floor in the mens rooms where they cannot drain or air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and moved the mops to hang above the mop sink where they can air-dry. PIC and Inspector also discussed that wet mops can sit in the upper basket of a mop bucket so they can drain and air-dry without contaminating the surrounding area. Ensure that after use mops are placed so that they can air-dry without soiling walls, floors, equipment, or supplies.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were dirty dishes observed in the basin of the handwashing sink. The dishes were removed and placed inside of the ware washing sink to correct the violation. Ensure that the handwashing sink remains unobstructed to allow easy access for employees to wash hands.
citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were raw beef patties stored above ready to eat foods inside of the main cooler. The RTE foods included veggies, sauces, and cheeses. Discussed with the PIC and the beef was moved to the bottom shelf of the cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that raw meats are always stored beneath RTE foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There is observed to not be a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present in the facility during today’s inspection. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was observed to be ice that had been dumped in the handwashing sink at the bar. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The drinking straws in the bar area were observed unwrapped and stored in close proximity to consumers. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the containers of straws to be behind the bar counter. Ensure that unwrapped straws are either stored behind the counter where they are controlled by employees or purchase wrapped straws for consumers.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be cracked and in need of repair:

1. The gaskets of the main preparation cooler on the cook-line. 
2. The gaskets of the silver freezer along the cook-line. 
3. The gaskets of the double-door cooler by the pizza preparation area. 
4. The gaskets of the pizza preparation cooler. 

Ensure that these gaskets are replaced and are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. SECOND REPEAT- The handwashing sink to the right of the cook-line is observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 
2. SECOND REPEAT- The table to the left of the dish machine is in need of being sealed to the wall. 
3. Observed a cracked tile on the floor of the cook-line in front of the prep cooler. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There was observed to be a phone charging on the top of the preparation cooler on the cook-line. There was also observed to be personal canned drinks in the double-door cooler in between trays of food for the facility. Discussed making sure to store personal items in a designated area to prevent contamination to food-contact surfaces and food for the facility. It is recommended to have a bucket on the bottom shelf of a cooler labeled “Personal” for employee food and drinks.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, there weren’t any employees who were food manager certified. Shortly throughout the visit, a CFPM arrived to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always an employee present who holds a manger’s certification if operating during business hours.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were at least two containers of salad dressings that lacked proper date marking inside of the dressing cooler. The items included tartar sauce and chipotle mayonnaise. Discussed with the PIC that in house dressings require date marking if being cold held longer than 24 hours. Ensure that dressings are date marked to make sure that they are getting used within the seven day timeframe.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single service to go containers stored with the food contact surfaces not inverted. Discussed with the PIC and the containers were properly inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always faced downward to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- Floor under dish machine’s drainboard was observed with accumulated food debris
- Floor in back-stock area (where bread rack is stored) was observed with accumulated food debris
Be sure to sweep the above mentioned areas as frequent as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed that a sanitizing solution was not available when Inspector arrived despite food preparation having just started. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and made a sanitizing bucket that tested at 100ppm (Chlorine), a safe and effective concentration of that sanitizer (Chlorine should be between 50-200ppm). Inspector discussed with the PIC that a sanitizing solution should be available at all times during food preparation for sanitizing surfaces, not just during times of warewashing. Ensure that a sanitizing solution is available for use for all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Observed that there was not a PIC present who demonstrated knowledge on proper warewashing procedures. When asked, PIC explained that the 2-compartment sink is used for warewashing, with wash and rinse happening in the two basins, then the sink is emptied and reset for sanitizing. A 3-compartment sink is available for warewashing in the meat room. All warewashing should take place there, where one basin each can be designated for wash, rinse, and sanitize. Ensure that the PIC demonstrates knowledge of correct sanitizing procedures.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(11) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (11) Explaining correct procedures for cleaning and SANITIZING UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that there was a not a staff member who had a Certified Food Protection Manager certification on the premises. PIC was notified. Ensure that a CFPM is on the premises at all times when food preparation can occur.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed ground meat stored over whole meat, and raw meat was stored above cured ready-to-eat meat in the deli meat 4-door display cooler. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and the meats in that cooler were moved so that RTE meat was stored above whole meat, and whole meat was stored above ground meat. Inspector provided educational handouts about storage order. Meats of different final cooking temperatures can be stored side-by-side as long as they are kept separate and they are not stored improperly over another item. Ensure that animal proteins are always stored according to internal cooking temperatures to avoid contamination: ready-to-eat foods (no cooking required/ pre-cooked), above whole meat (145 F), above ground meat (155 F), above chicken and turkey (165 F).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following areas that have an accumulation of soils:
(i) the walk-in cooler fans are dusty.
(ii) the walk-in freezer has significant ice accumulation.
PIC was notified that these areas need to be cleaned with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues so that they are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the trash receptacle in the women’s bathroom does not have a lid. PIC was notified that all bathroom stalls that are used by women have to have a covered trash receptacle. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have a covered trash can.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the coving along the wall in the meat department has come away from the wall and needs to be repaired. PIC was notified. Ensure that walls are coved and sealed to the floor.
citation_text: 6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. [C]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed that there is not an ambient thermometer in the refrigerator in the kitchen and the ambient thermometer in the storage room cooler is not functional. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all cold and hot holding units have a functional ambient thermometer in them to make sure that TCS foods are being properly cold or hot held.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: One of the PICs was observed to use the handwashing sink to fill the sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED- The PICs were both educated that handwashing sinks should only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing and that the triple sink should be used instead to fill the bucket. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for the purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIRD REPEAT- There was a pan of raw beef above a container of carrots in the bottom of the preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The beef was moved to the bottom and the carrots were moved above the raw beef. Due to this being a third repeat violation, the inspector will bring the health educator to the facility for education on storage order. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed that single-service and single-use articles and utensils were stored with the food-contact surfaces upright, including plastic cutlery single-use food cartons and nacho cheese holders. Customers and staff could potentially touch multiple food-contact surfaces when reaching for a utensil or a carton. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and utensils were flipped so that only there handles were upright, and cartons were flipped or placed underneath a closed shelf to protect the food-contact surfaces from debris from above. PIC and Inspector discussed additional ways that single-use utensils could be stored, including horizontal in either cleanable or disposable containers, as long as all the utensils are facing the same direction, so only handles will be touched when dispensed. Ensure that single-service and single-use utensils and articles are stored such that contamination of food-contact surfaces is prevented.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the individual trash receptacles in the stalls of the women’s bathroom do not have lids/covers. PIC was notified and Inspector discussed that covered trash receptacles are required in bathroom facilities used by women per IL Food Code, as it is more hygienic and protects plumbing from improperly flushed items. Inspector also discussed that upcoming Food Code updates (based on the 2026 FDA Food Code) will expand this need to all bathroom stalls, not just bathrooms used by women. Ensure all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed multiple large pieces of equipment that are no longer in use because they are completely inoperable and not able to be repaired, included two 3-door coolers, 2 ovens, 1 hot box (requires a gas hookup which doesn’t exist), several mobile bar carts, and some coffee and tea pots. PIC was notified. Ensure that the premises is free of items that are unnecessary to the operation such as equipment that is nonfunctional or no longer used.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Caulk frontline counter to the wall where tile was replaced.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were observed to be raw shell eggs on a bucket of pickles in the double-door cooler. CORRECTED- The eggs were moved to the bottom shelf of the cooler. Proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- The gasket on the double door cooler is observed to be cracked and needs to be replaced. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The caulking between the wall and the triple sink is observed to be in a state of disrepair. Ensure that this is repaired and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. THIRD REPEAT- The cove base in the kitchen under the fire extinguisher to the right of the triple sink is observed to be coming off. Ensure that this is sealed back to the wall. 
Due to these two above violations being third repeats, a follow up has been scheduled for 12/1/2026 to ensure that they have been corrected. 

3. SECOND REPEAT- The wall above the mop sink basin in the mop closet has a hole in it and is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this wall is repaired and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil and food debris on the shield and plunger of the milkshake machine. The PIC was informed and the machine was cleaned and sanitized to sight and touch. Ensure staff are cleaning food contact surfaces frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 
Observed that facility does not have written procedures for Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events(Norovirus) and also does not have proper chemical to assist with cleaning a norovirus event. PIC was made aware and written procedures was provided by inspectors and PIC assured that facility will purchase EPA certified bleach soon. Ensure that having proper EPA certified chemical and written procedures are available to respond to a vomit/diarrheal event. 

Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
4-703.11(C) 
REPEAT
The sanitizer bucket in the front side near soda machine tested at 0ppm (chlorine).The facility has QUAT available and the bucket was remade and tested at 400ppm(quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are tested after they are prepared to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(2) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPAregistered label use instructions by providing: (2) A contact time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50 MG/L that has a PH of 10 or less and a temperature of at least 38°C 100°F) or a PH of 8 or less and a temperature of at least 24°C (75°F).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) 
Observed dish machine sanitizing at 0 ppm (Chlorine)after multiple tries and sanitizer bucket was changed by PIC however, still concentrating at 0 ppm. PIC was made aware and called for service immediately. Ensure that the dish machine is functioning properly to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized.

Additionally, inspectors observed pink colored accumulation on the interior surface of the ice machine. PIC was informed. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and are always in good condition. 

Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment:
7-201.11
Observed all purpose chemicals and glass cleaner found on food prep tables within the dish room and kitchen area. PIC was informed and chemicals were removed and placed in the appropriate designated area. Ensure that toxic chemicals are stored separately away from food. 

Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 
REPEAT 
(1) The following areas are in need of a deep cleaning:
- Surfaces inside and outside of the dish machine
- Each basin of the triple sink has dried food debris
- Floors, walls, and the ceiling behind pieces of equipment inside of the dish room and the kitchen were observed with splatter and accumulated debris 
- Deep cleaning needed in dry storage underneath and behind the storage rack
Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.

(2) Observed coving coming out off the wall in between cooking oven and prep cooler. PIC was informed. Ensure that cove base is glued back to the wall to avoid food build up.

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) 
Observed a CAESAR WRAP pre packaged food which has expiration date of 11/15/2026 in the standing cooler number 3. PIC was informed and wrap was discarded. Ensure that date marking of food items monitored at a regular frequency. 

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspectors observed the hand sink to the left of the triple sink to be damaged. The faucet was detached from the sink and lying in the sink basin. The PIC was aware of the damage and has requested repair. Inspectors will follow-up at the facility on November 23, 2026 to ensure the sink has been repaired. Please contact the Department if repairs cannot be completed in the requested time.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-103.11(Q) Person In Charge. 11/13 inspection occurred as a result of confirmation of a falsified certified food manager certification present at the facility. Originally noted during the 11/12/26 inspection, inspector reached-out to SCDPH and ServSafe due to observation of the unique nature of the certificate. SCDPH observes 100s of certificates a year and this one presented with obvious doctored content. Upon confirmation, ServSafe did issue a certification to the individual in question, the certificate number and the expiration date are correct. The certificate given, however, is a false document that initially was issued to an employee Chase X. Someone doctored the available document. SCDPH recourse is to issue a follow-up to allow time for the facility to obtain proper certificates. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (Q) Written procedures and plans, where specified by this Code and as developed by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, are maintained and implemented as required.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: During the 11/12 inspection, the certification presented appeared to be doctored. Upon investigation, the document presented was not for the correct person. McDonald’s has a fantastic in-house certification process and there are traditionally multiple CFPM present. Yesterday, the manager present did not indicate that anyone besides the single present party was certified. Be sure to educate managers that conversations with inspectors are key to good evaluations. If another certified person was present, this should have been indicated. Certified persons are present today.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items included biscuits and gravy, sweet tea, and Canadian bacon. Education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed in use McRib utensil to be resting on a soiled tray. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper in use utensil storage and a new tray and utensil were used. Ensure any in use utensil is stored in a way that prevents any contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed walk in freezer fan unit to have ice accumulation present around hose. Discussed with PIC, unit will be serviced. Ensure staff is checking walk in freezer unit regularly to prevent any ice accumulation from building up.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed food debris/accumulation in the following areas:
1) (Repeatx2) The 2 door fry freezer was observed soiled with food debris. 
2) Small grease buildup on the floor near grills. 

Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination. 



Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
comment: Observed significant amount of refuse to be present behind washing machines. Discussed with PIC, area will be cleaned. Ensure any refuse is properly disposed of within facility.
citation_text: 5-502.11 Frequency. REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the PREMISES at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be stored in mop bucket with soiled mop water present. Discussed with PIC, mop water will be discarded and mop will be stored in a way that allows for air drying. Ensure mop is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the temperature-sensitive tape for the dish washer the facility uses is for 180 F, which means the water inside the dish washer is so hot that it is more steam than water when it hits the dishes. PIC states the facility normally uses a heavy wash cycle. Inspector measured the dish machine using a final temperature registering plate to be 151 F on the top rack, which is too low for sanitizing. Inspector used 160 F temperature-sensitive tape on the bottom rack which showed final temperatures of 160 F or above. PIC used 180 F temperature-sensitive tape on the bottom rack which showed final temperatures of 180 F or above. Inspector and PIC discussed using 160-170-180 F temperature-sensitive tape or a final temperature measuring plate to determine what is the optimal wash cycle and placement for dish sanitizing. Ensure that mechanical warewashing sanitizing water is between 160-170 F.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: Observed that the prep sink and 3 handwashing sinks in the classroom had low hot water pressure. PICs were notified and they discussed repairs with the custodian. Ensure that water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures.
citation_text: 5-103.12 Pressure. Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water supplied as specified under 5-104.12(A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure. [Pf]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the all gender single-use bathroom for adults did not have a lid on the trash can. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and ordered a lidded trash can that will arrive the next business day. Ensure that all bathrooms used by women have a covered trash receptacle in the stall.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. A CFPM arrived shortly into the inspection to correct. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to have one at the facility at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

Raw eggs were oberved over both cooked and raw bacon in the standing cooler in the kitchen. The PIC was shown and moved the items to correct. Ensure that storage locations for the raw foods in the facility are maintained so that cross contamination is safe in relation to the safe cooking temperatures of the foods involved.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility could not provide test strips for the sanitizer used in the facility during the inspection. A follow-up is being scheduled for 10 days to verify compliance. Ensure that test kits are available for the sanitizer solutions in the facility at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The three part sink was observed pulling away from the wall in the kitchen and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces around moisture and food surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle for the fountain drink machine was observed with encrusted, lumpy brown substances caked into the blades of the nozzle. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The items was disassembled and moved to dish for cleaning during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Painters tape was observed being used to hold a light fixture in place in the standing freezer next to the cook line. Tape is not considered a cleanable surface when exposure to moisture and food. This item should be repaired correctly using smooth and easily cleanable materials that do not pose a potential for food contamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 
Observed employee changing gloves without washing hands. CORRECTED- Inspector noticed and provided education.Ensure proper handwashing procedures are always followed.

When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment:
4-904.11
Observed that some dishes and cups were not inverted which can risk contamination. Discussed with PIC and Dishes and cups were inverted immediately. Make sure kitchenware and tableware displayed or stored inverted or wrapped to prevent contamination. 

(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) 
Observed duct tape from sides of table top cooler. PIC was made aware. Ensure that food and non food contact surface shall be smooth to clean to prevent dust, dirt, food residue and other derbies. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-
CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
6-101.11(A)
Observed the triple sink not caulked properly. Discussed with PIC and PIC stated that sink will be caulked. Make sure that Triple sink is caulked to the wall to provide smooth and easily cleanable surface.

(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-305.11 
Observed personal items such as Jacket in the dry storage with spices and water bottles in the cooler with other food. PIC was informed and removed those personal items. Ensure that Personal items shall be in a designated area away form the food to Prevent contamination. 

Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee turn off the faucet without using a barrier. CORRECTED: Employee was educated on using the paper towel as a barrier, and rewashed their hands, this time using a paper towel as a barrier when turning off the faucet handle. Ensure that a barrier is used to run off the faucet to avoid recontaminating clean hands after handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed the inside top of the microwave has an accumulation of food debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food debris. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and an employee cleaned the microwave, and updated cleaning procedures to include the inside top of the microwave. Ensure that the inside of the microwave to clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with white debris. The PIC was informed and believed the build-up to be due to hard water. The ice machine was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure staff are monitoring the cleanliness of the machine and sanitizing often to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the following items to be stored in improper packaging:
1. Multiple food items stored in repurposed bean sprout, egg roll, and raw chicken bags.
2. Multiple food items stored directly in grocery bags.

Food must be stored in either its original packaging or a container which is made for food contact or can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure these items are stored safely to prevent accidental contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
3rd Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Raw chicken and raw frog legs stored above cooked chicken in the walk-in cooler
2. Bowl of raw chicken liquid stored in direct contact with green bell peppers in the prep cooler top
3. Raw pork stored directly above sweet and sour sauce in the upright cooler

The PIC was informed and these items were moved. There is a storage order flyer posted on the walk-in cooler door with Chinese translation. Ensure staff are following the instructions listed on this flyer.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed four dead pests and two live pests present in the facility near the triple sink and upright cooling units. The PIC was informed and presented the inspectors with a Sentinel Pest service receipt dated 10/28/2026. Sentinel was aware of the issue and is servicing monthly. Ensure staff are continuing cleaning practices in the facility and limiting food availability. Sentinel advised the facility to inspect incoming food deliveries for pest presence. Inspectors will follow-up on November 24, 2026 to confirm cleaning has been completed under the triple sink and behind the upright cooling units. Inspector will also monitor pest presence during this upcoming visit.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed wet wiping cloths stored on the counter. Ensure that wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses to prevent microbial growth within the cloth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

The inspectors observed the following facility items in need of repair:
(1) The facility is missing coving in many areas of the kitchen.
(2) The triple sink is held up with bare wood between the sink basin and the floor.
(3) The ceiling is damaged with gaps between the seams in the back storage area and above the chest freezer.

Ensure these facility items are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection. Ceiling tiles need to be smooth and easily cleanable. Acoustic tiles are absorbent and not permissible in food-preparation spaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employees was observed bare-handling a waffle ice cream cone while inspector was present. The waffle cone ice cream was discarded. And education was provided. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to avoid contaminating ready eat food items with their bare hands.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: An employee hand-bag was observed on the condiments’ counter in the chill area by the ice cream machine. Education was provided. The bag was removed and the surface was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that employees are aware to put their personal belongings in the designated areas provided at all times.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be kept past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 
Observed employee change gloves without hand washing. PIC was made aware and education conducted. Ensure that all employees who handle food wash their hands properly after and before doning gloves. 

When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 
Observed paper towel dispenser to have ran out at the hand sink in the dish machine area. PIC was informed and corrected. Make sure all hand washing sinks are provided with paper towels at all times.

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 
Observed some rotten potatoes in an open cardboard box in the back room. PIC was informed and instructed to throw away. Make sure that all food shall be safe, unadulterated and honestly presented. The potatoes were discarded to correct. 

Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) 
(1) Multiple pans, utensils and knives stored throughout the facility were observed with contaminants remaining after cleaning and in storage. (2) Can opener blade observed to be soiled with residue. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. It is highly suggested that education is conducted in house for dish washers to ensure that food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use. 

Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Observed mops stored with the heads pooled up on the floor in the mop sink. PIC was made aware and corrected during the inspection. Ensure that mop heads must be stored in a manner that allows them to air dry and prevents contamination. 

Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) 
Observed personal drinks(soda glass, water bottles) in multiple area in the facility with food prep and storage areas (kitchen and walk in cooler). PIC was made aware and educated. Make sure personal drinks are stored in designated areas only to prevent potential contamination.

Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed no barrier to be used by staff when turning off hand sink faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off hand sink faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no hot water to be available within facility. Discussed with PIC, hot water will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure hot water is available within facility during all hours of operation. A follow up has been issued for 11/19/26.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed lettuce to held past its 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, lettuce and salads that contained said lettuce were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no allergen training to have been completed by CFM present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-204.11 Observed the facility to not have any appropriate sanitizing agent available in-house. The facility was not in operation and will not be cooking for another two weeks, however, an agent should available. There were multiple bleaches available, none are EPA certified. Keila stated that she will have the bleach present before her next cooking event. She is a small batch cook that does not have a store front and is not in operation daily. Keila will send inspector a photo of the bleach to correct violation prior to next operation. Failure to provide documentation of proper bleach by the follow-up date will result in a charge. 




Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed dirty dishes stored inside the basin of the handwashing sink. Discussed with the food program supervisor to separate the sinks used between handwashing and ware-washing. Dishes were removed and placed inside of the ware-washing sink. Ensure that hand-sinks are only used for handwashing purposes only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed that the interior of the lid on the ice machine has some bare insulation. Insulation is an absorbent material that is not smooth and easily cleanable. PIC was notified and will have the lid repaired so that the insulation is no longer uncovered. Ensure that food-contact surfaces of equipment are nonabsorbent and are smooth and easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the heat dish machine was not reaching a high enough surface temperature to effectively sanitize equipment. The final temperature measuring device measured a surface temperature of 148 F, when 160 F is required for sanitizing. A final temperature sticker also confirmed a temperature of less than 160 F. The PIC was notified and all dishes will instead be warewashed in the cafeteria facilities in another part of the building until the heat dish machine is repaired. Ensure that hot water warewashing reaches a utensil surface temperature of at least 160 F to effectively sanitize equipment
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous flies were observed remaining near the dish machine in the bakery area. The PIC was shown and instructed to continue remediation actions to remove the remaining pests. The other store locations previously noted (ie. the mop room and onion pallet) appear CORRECTED at the time of the inspection. A follow-up was scheduled for two weeks to allow for the remaining flies to be removed.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed that in the public bar there were unwrapped straws that were available for customers to handle. CORRECTED: PICs were notified that unwrapped straws should only be handled using a barrier, either with gloved hands or by replacing the straws with ith wrapped straws, so that the food-contact surfaces of the straws are safe from potential contamination from barehands. PICs discarded the unwrapped straws. Facility will only use wrapped straws from now on. Ensure ready-to-eat food-contact surfaces are protected from contamination from barehands by using a barrier.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Observed that the public bar and members-only bar do not have dedicated handwashing sinks:
* The public bar does have a triple sink for warewashing. 
* The members-only bar only has a double sink. 
PICs were notified that separate dedicated handwashing must be available for convenient use by employees and volunteers in areas where food and beverage preparation and dispensing occurs. 
PICs and Inspector discussed changing the sinks to be used only for handwashing and general preparation; items that need to be warewashed would be taken to the kitchen (a different room) where warewashing facilities exist (a large triple sink designated for warewashing):
* Public Bar: one compartment would be for handwashing only (complete with handwashing sign, hand soap, paper towels) and the other two compartments would be used for general prep activities e.g. dump sink, water filling, fruit washing, etc. (complete with signs).
* Members-only Bar: one compartment would be for handwashing only (complete handwashing sign, hand soap, paper towels) and the other compartment would be used for general prep activities (complete with sign).
PICs will confirm with Inspector when these changes have been made. 
Ensure handwashing sinks are available for convenient use during food and beverage preparation and dispensing.
citation_text: 5-204.11 Handwashing Sinks. A HANDWASHING SINK shall be located: (A) To allow convenient use by EMPLOYEES in FOOD preparation, FOOD dispensing, and WAREWASHING areas; and (B) In, or immediately adjacent to, toilet rooms. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket made with bleach had a too low concentration of Chlorine (10ppm). CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and added more sanitizer to the solution until it measured at a safe and effective concentration of Chlorine (50ppm). PIC and Inspector discussed that given the size of the bucket, 4 capfuls of sanitizer may be needed, and should be confirmed with test strips for Chlorine (see Violation #48). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are used per manufacturer’s instructions, and measure at safe and effective concentrations of sanitizer: 50-200ppm for Chlorine-based sanitizers like bleach.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the ice machine was heavily soiled on the inside. PICs were notified, and will have it cleaned. PICs SHALL remove the ice machine from service until it is cleaned AND the Inspector has confirmed that the ice machine has been sufficiently cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure that food-contact surfaces and equipment are cleaned with enough frequency that they are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed that the interior panel of the ice machine was previously repaired with duct tape, which is failing. PIC was notified. The ice machine must be repaired with a material that is smooth and easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of soils on the floor next to the cabinets of the public bar. PIC was notified. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that a mop was improperly stored between uses, sitting in the lower basin of a mop bucket submerged in water instead of hanging in the upper basket where it can drip-dry and air-dry. CORRECTED: PICs were notified, and the mop was moved to air-dry. Ensure that mops are allowed to air-dry between uses, either in the upper basket of the mop bucket or hanging above a mop sink, to prevent potential harborage for pests and pathogens.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed that there was no sanitizer available and food preparation was happening (samples being made from a larger product).
