CORRECTED: PIC was notified and arranged for a sanitizer bucket to be delivered to the venue with test strips. Sanitizer bucket (quaternary ammonium) measured at a concentration of 400ppm, a safe and effective concentration of sanitizer. Ensure that a sanitizer for cleaning is available during use when food preparation is happening.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that there was no handwashing sink despite the vendor serving samples that were generated on site. CORRECTED: PIC will handwash at the neighboring booth. Inspectors discussed preparing samples at the brick-and-mortar and pre-packaging the samples (each fully-encased) ahead of time so that handwashing would not be necessary at future temporary events. Ensure that handwashing is available for employees when food preparation will be occurring.
citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On inspector arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. Staff at the time of the inspection indicated that the manager on duty had gone to another location to open there and would be back shortly. Mr. Annerino arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts in an emergency.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, thus recontaminating their hands. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with staff and monitor hand washing as needed to ensure that all hand washing procedures are conducted safely at all times moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x3) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Two of the slicers under the counter in the back prep area were observed with food debris remaining on them. They appeared to have been stored without proper cleaning. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the food contact items within four hours of use. 2) (REPEAT x3) Soda nozzles in the drive thru area customer service area were observed soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean them. The food contact surfaces were cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate situation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There was an observed gap allowing light to enter through the bottom of the back door into the facility. This is an obvious possible pest entrance and should be repaired/resealed prior to the next routine inspection to prevent these possible pests. Ensure that all outer openings are sealed at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple roaches were observed around the kitchen and dish areas, specifically around the walls, wall gaps and spaces in the dish area. Multiple were also observed running through the open space in the middle of the rooms. Several generations appear to be in the facility and multiple adults were observed with obvious egg cases. The PIC was shown one such casing but several were observed throughout the inspection. The PIC was instructed to contact their pest control agency for targeted maintenance procedures for roaches. Pest control has been at the facility since the previous inspector visit and sprayed the morning of the inspection. After a conversation with AD the inspector will follow-up in two weeks for ongoing management of the pest issue currently taking place.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple gallons of milk to be held past date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, milk was discarded. Ensure any TSC item is discarded after its date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed the wastewater pipe running into the grease trap to have a leak. There was a catch basin under the pipe to survey leaking water. There was also a notable odor in the back room which may be caused by the leaking grease trap. Ensure the plumbing is repaired to prevent cross-contamination. A follow-up will be conducted on November 9, 2026 to ensure the plumbing is repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The available certified food manager’s certificates are expired. PIC was informed and stated that process of renewal would be initiated. Ensure that Food certificates should be maintained and monitored.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: The inspectors observed that container of shredded cheese and chicken fingers were found without date marking in the prep cooler in the back. PIC was informed and educated about date marking. Ensure that ready to eat items date marked properly. Dates were added to the items to correct.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Working bottle with chemical observed without labeling. PIC was informed and labeled with appropriate chemical name. Make sure that all working bottom with chemicals shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material/chemical.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Probe thermometers were available however, inspectors found thermometers to be out of calibration and were not reading accurate. Inspectors demonstrated proper way to calibrate of thermometer in and educated. Ensure that thermometers shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use.
citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the facility did not have test strips for the quaternary ammonium sanitizer solution. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, left during the inspection to acquire test strips, and returned with test strips. Ensure test strips are available at all times for testing sanitizer concentration levels for all sanitizers types used in the facility.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
1ST REPEAT: Observed the following surfaces need maintenance attention:
(i) The 2x4s under the windows of the dry storage area/preparation area are unsealed. Seal any bare wood,
(ii) Several floor tiles that are observed damaged. Replace the damaged floor tiles. Placing a rubber mat over the floor tiles is fine for the interim for safety and cleaning, but tiles should still be repaired.
(iii) The wall paint by the mop sink at the mop station is peeling off and the wall needs to be repainted.
PIC was notified of these areas still needing additional maintenance. Ensure floors, walls, ceilings, and bare wood are sealed to prevent movement between walls and kitchen.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a gasket in the back prep cooler is separating from the door, and could provide harborage for pathogens. PIC was notified and will get it repaired. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The nozzle on the horchata refresher was observed soiled. The PIC was made aware. The nozzle was removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The. Quaternary ammonia sanitizer in the sani bucket was observed reading between 100-0 ppm. The PIC was notified and the sani bucket was remade. Ensure that the concentration of the sani bucket is routinely checked.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed. 
1. The caulking on the utility sink was observed loose and in a state of disrepair. 
2. The coving tiles on the wall behind the soda syrups and the wall behind he fryers was observed coming off the wall.

Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the corrective actions for the areas mentioned above are taken.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed several staff members donning gloves without washing their hands. Discussed with the PIC and education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that all staff are knowledgeable to wash their hands before donning new gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was no paper towel observed in the dispenser at the hand sink by the walk-in cooler entrance. The PIC was made aware. The PIC restock the paper towel dispenser. Ensure that all hand sinks within the facility are supplied with the relevant materials to promote proper handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observe pork and chicken being stored above raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. Education was provided and the pork and chicken were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that proper storage order is observed and follow at all times.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were no sanitizer/sani bucket observed in the kitchen or prep area upon arrival and during today’s inspection. Education was carried out. PIC was informed. Sanitizer for the sani buckets were made and tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made and placed in the sani buckets during food prep, handling, and service at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There were multiple instances where food was observed to be in a package that exposed it to potential contaminants: 

1. There was observed to be mushrooms, cut pineapple and corn dogs stored directly in a grocery bag. CORRECTED- The food items were switched to be in another container.  
2. There was observed to be an open can of tomato purée with the tomato purée still stored inside of it. CORRECTED- The tomato purée was moved into another container. 

Education was conducted with the PIC. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and food should never be stored directly in them. After the can of an acidic food item is opened, the can is no longer meant to protect the integrity of its contents and the food item can be adulterated. Ensure that food is stored in a container that does not expose it to adulteration or to potential contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
PIC was unable to produce Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. Employees should obtain their Food Handler’s Certificate within 30 days of hire, and renew their certificates every 3 years. Ensure all employees complete food handler’s certificate training, and retain records on file for verification during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There were cans of cheese sauce that were observed to be in a hot holding cabinet. The employee stated that they put them in there to make it easier for the cheese sauce to come out. The hot holding cabinet has an ambient temperature of 136F, which is essentially cooking the cheese sauce in the can. Cans are not meant to be used as a cooking vessel, as they have a plastic liner in them that can expose the cheese sauce to adulteration when heated up. CORRECTED- The cans were removed from the hot holding cabinet and it was discussed to put the cheese sauce in containers to cook them in the future. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. title: Proper date marking and disposition.

It was discussed to have a container in the bottom of a cooler away from foods for the facility and to label the container “PERSONAL”. Ensure that employee items are stored in a manner that protects items for the facility from contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were approximately three juvenile roaches and one adult roach observed to be in a cabinet in the front behind the registers. There were cardboard boxes in this cabinet and the PIC removed them during the inspection. Discussed reducing cardboard, as it acts as food for the roaches. The last two pest control treatments are from 9/25/2026 and 10/23/2026. The District Manager stated that they called the technician to ask for weekly treatments and the technician stated that this was impossible. Sentinel is supposed to be treating the facility biweekly according to the PIC, but the last two treatment dates are almost a month from each other. Discussed potentially switching pest control companies to receive more consistent treatment. Ensure that deep cleaning is continuing to be done, cardboard is being reduced, and that dead roaches are being cleaned up to allow for proper monitoring. A follow up is scheduled for 11/30/2026 to ensure that the appropriate actions are being taken to reduce pest presence.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There aren’t any signed employee health forms available on site for any of the employees. Discussed the need to have all employees sign health forms to acknowledge that they won’t show up to work if ill. Employee health forms were given to the owner to have all employees sign. Will follow-up on November 5, 2026 to see that all employees have signed health forms.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There weren’t any paper towels available at the front hand-sink. Discussed with the owner and paper towels were provided to the towel dispenser. Additionally, there wasn't any hand soap available at the front hand-sink. The soap dispenser was nonfunctional at the moment. Discussed the need of having hand soap at all handsinks. The owner added batteries to the dispenser to allow for soap availability. Violation corrected.  Ensure that paper towels and hand soap are available at every hand-sink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
There are chocolate dipped grapes stored inside of the display cold holding case that lack proper labeling info. The grapes are covered with chocolate, as well as chopped peanuts. Discussed adding ingredients and major allergens on the packaging of the product. Ensure that correct labeling is available for products. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The owner is the only individual who holds a food certificate. There are three more individuals who handles food. Discussed the need to get all employees at least food handler certified. A reference sheet was provided to the owner. Ensure that all employees who handle food and clean dishes obtain at least a food handler certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed nine dented cans amongst the food storage inventory; Four cans of royal dragon hoisin sauce,  one can of baby corn, two hen’s tomato ketchup, one bamboo shoots can, and one pho sauce can. The PIC was made aware. The cans were removed from the inventory and stored separately to be returned. Ensure that prepackaged food items with package integrity issues are sorted out of the inventory at all times to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: An opened jug of milk was observed not date marked properly. Education was provided. The PIC told inspectors that the jug was opened two days prior (10/21/26). The PIC discarded the jug of milk while inspector was present. Ensure that food items are dated if they are going to be held for more than 24-hours within the establishment.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Multiple cardboard boxes of single service food containers and utensils including kitchenwares were observed being stored on the floor in the dry storage. Education was provided. The PIC assured inspectors that that the boxes will be removed from the floor. Ensure that the boxes are stored at least six inches above the floor to protect them from splash, dust, dirt, and other contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify allergen training certification for the certified food protection manager at the facility. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC told inspectors that that they will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure all certified food protection managers obtain the allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed no stem thermometer available at the stand for measuring the temperature of time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. The PIC was made aware and was informed to have a thermometer avaialble at the following event.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no hand sink available at the stand. The PIC was informed and was unaware of the requirement. A neighboring stand volunteered to share their hand sink for the duration of the event. Ensure a hand sink with a free-flowing spigot is available and equipped with soap, paper towel, and a catch bucket.
citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the coffee maker to have soil accumulation on the internal surface. PIC was made aware. PIC cleaned and sanitized the coffee maker. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the coffee maker are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The inspectors observed multiple cardboard boxes of food items stored directly on the floor. Discussed with the PIC and PIC removed the boxes to be stored properly. Ensure that Food boxes are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to avoid any form of contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil residue on the shelves of the Pepsi cooler in the lobby. PIC was notified.PIC assured inspectors that soil accumulation will be clean. Ensure that Soil accumulation is clean and non food contact shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

comment: The inspectors observed the caulking on the hand sink next to the prep station in a state of disrepair. PIC was notified. PIC and assured inspectors that sink will be caulked to the wall. Ensure that sink is repaired appropriately.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspectors observed the hand sink to the left of the triple sink to be damaged. The faucet was detached from the sink and lying in the sink basin. The PIC was aware of the damage and has requested repair. Inspectors will follow-up at the facility on October 26, 2026 to ensure the sink has been repaired. Please contact the Department if repairs cannot be completed in the requested time.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed a mop to be stored directly in the sink basin. This storage method does not allow for required drip-drying of the mop head. The PIC was informed and relocated the mop. Ensure the mop is stored in a manner that allows drip-drying to occur to prevent microbial growth.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed a tile to be damaged to the left of the mop sink. This tile seals the wall to the flooring of the kitchen space. Ensure this tile is repaired or replaced to prevent pest movement or microbial growth behind the tiles or inside the wall.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: (REPEAT X2) The PIC is not currently a CFPM and is missing critical food safety knowledge at the time of this inspection. Education was given in relation to the observed violations and concerns noted during this inspection. More knowledge is needed and would normally be covered by the CFPM course that is required. While education will be deemed as sufficient at this time other enforcement is likely if this becomes an ongoing issue.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(1) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE (PIC) shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: (REPEAT X2) On arrival, there is not a CFPM available in the facility. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all food handling shifts in the facility moving forward.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: (REPEAT X1) A bucket full of spout covers was observed to be stored in front of the handwashing sink at the bar. CORRECTED: Education was conducted. The bucket was relocated making the handwashing sink accessible. Ensure that all sinks within the facility designated for handwashing are accessible for handwashing at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution in the triple sink inside the kitchen tested below the manufacturer’s recommended concentration at 100ppm instead of between 200-400ppm. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and emptied the triple sink and remade it and it tested between 200-400ppm. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are prepared as directed by the EPA regulation label with a concentration between 200-400ppm.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil residues in the rubber holders of the soda nozzles at both bars. PIC was informed and staff will clean the rubber holders. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple open jars of Butch’s All Purpose hot sauce/marinade stored in the dry storage areas. According to the sauces packaging, these jars require refrigeration after opening. Ensure all foods that require cold holding are stored at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the open jars of sauce.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: (REPEAT X1) Inspectors observed a carton of heavy whipping cream in the reach in cooler at the bar to not be date marked. An employee was asked when the carton was opened and they were unsure of when it had been opened. CORRECTED: The carton of heavy whipping cream was voluntarily discarded. Ensure that all TCS or RTE food items that are going to stay over 24-hours from the date they were opened or prepared are date marked properly at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.

citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.

Ensure that in use utensils are stored in locations that are cleaned regularly. Inspector suggests using the magnetic knife rack or a separate cleanable container to store utensils properly.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed single-service containers on a shelf in the kitchen stored unprotected. CORRECTED: PIC was made aware and containers were inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that single-service items food-contact surfaces are protected by their original packaging or inverted to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.

citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.

The PIC mentioned that the facility will purchase a bottle of bleach as soon as possible. Ensure that an EPA approved bleach is available to respond to a norovirus event. Will follow-up on October 20, 2026 to see that bleach has been purchased.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.

citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.
