title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the mop to be stored in the mop sink. PIC was made aware and the mop was moved to have the bristles hanging to dry. Ensure that mops are positioned to allow them to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee drink cup on a shelf in the kitchen without a lid and straw. PIC was informed and the drink was removed to correct the violation. Ensure that employee drinks are covered with a lid and straw to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: (2nd REPEAT) Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to always wash their hands before donning gloves including in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspectors observed the cook in the kitchen using their bare hands to place toast on to plates to serve. PIC was made aware and the pieces of toast were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that contamination from hands is prevented by using a barrier when handling ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival the inspectors observed a soiled fork in the handwashing sink. PIC was made aware and the fork was removed to correct the violation. Ensure that handwashing sinks are used for handwashing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following:

Soil accumulation was observed on the baffles of the ice machine. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspectors that the ice machine will be cleaned. 

(REPEAT) Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the servers station to have a build-up of soils on them. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC, and PIC removed the nozzles to clean them immediately. 
Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: (2nd REPEAT) Inspector observed several drain flies in the utility closet and the first and second aisle in the dry storage. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the flies are dealt with using authorized pest control methods. Zappers and fly strips may be hung, but they must not be hung over food. Ensure that pest activities is reduced within the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed a large gap on the bottom of the back door of the dry storage area. PIC was informed. Ensure the gap is sealed by next routine inspection to prevent the entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: There was a  wet wiping cloths just laying on the back counter top in the prep area. PIC was made aware. Education was carried out. The wet cloth was taken to get laundered. Ensure that wiping cloth is kept in a sanitizer solution in between use.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: (REPEAT X 3) Inspector observed there to be a build-up of oils and food debris behind the grill and griddle on the line. Ensure that these areas are cleaned regularly enough to mitigate the build-up of oils and food debris. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed a glass of water without a lid and straw on the back counter in the prep area. PIC was made aware and the cup was removed to correct the violation. Ensure that employee drinks are covered with a lid and straw as well as stored in an area that protected from contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were still mouse droppings observed under shelving in the dry storage. The PIC was alerted and will have the custodian clean the droppings up. There are sticky traps in place and the facility is aware of the rodent issue. Discussed continuing to clean these mouse droppings to allow for proper monitoring of the rodent issue and ensuring that food is being protected in this area. Ensure that pest control is regularly treating for the issue and that any holes in the walls that are allowing access for the rodents are being sealed. A spot check will be conducted on 11/16/2026 to ensure that the mouse droppings are being cleaned and the issue is being monitored.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous ants were observed on the floor by the sink next to the entrance to the bakery preparation area. The PIC was shown and prepared a work order for the issue. While that was taking place the employee currently in the area indicated that a work order had already been placed. The PIC was able to find the order in the system and show the inspector during the inspection. The order was placed on 10/10. No action was observed in their system since then in relation to this situation. The inspector will follow-up in 10 days for compliance or progress.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The corner molding at the mop sink in the produce room next to the bakery area was observed with the covering damaged and missing. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces around sinks are smooth and easily cleanable to protect against mold growth.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle on the fountain drink machine in the Mellow Yellow spot was observed with a heavy build up of soilage. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item, as well as the rest of the nozzles to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent accumulation of filth.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

The PIC was unable to find a probe style thermometer at the time of the inspection. The inspector will follow-up in 10 days to ensure that a probe thermometer is acquired and available at the facility.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Over a dozen gnats were observed in the dish area of the facility. The PIC was shown and instructed to remove prior to the next routine inspection. They stated that they were only there because the fryers were cleaned. The inspector stated that the flys should still be removed and prevented from returning. While the inspector was typing the report the PIC stated that the situation was fixed. They sprayed the sanitizer used by the facility throughout the area, killing the flys that were observable. The inspector is willing to accept the situation is currently managed with the caveat that a spot check will be conducted in the next week or so to verify that the flys do not return.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of the inspection there was not a person with the requisite allergen training certificate available in the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have someone with the requisite training available in the facility at all times that it is in operation.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed a partially cooked chicken breast stored in the drawer cooler in direct contact with raw chicken breast. PIC was made aware and the pan with partially cooked chicken and raw chicken was removed from the cook line and voluntarily discarded. Par cooking is not a standard practice at this facility and the PIC was unaware of when or why the chicken was partially cooked.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.[P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed soiled white dishes to be stored on the utensil racks. PIC was informed and items were taken to the dish area to be cleaned. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple bags of flour stored on the ground near the walk in cooler. Ensure that all food is stored at least six inches off the floor to prevent contamination. Inspector will require proper storage prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inside the thaw cabinet a spill was observed to have accumulated along the right side of the interior. An accumulation of ice was also observed in the under the counter freezer on the cook line. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned regularly to prevent accumulation of soil and food debris. Inspector will confirm cabinet and freezer are clean to sight and touch on their next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following physical facilities to be in need of repair:
1. The handwashing sink near the dish area needs resealed to the wall
2. Multiple tiles missing along the baseboards throughout the kitchen
3. A consistent drip was observed from the walk in freezer condenser
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of ice and frost on the walk in freezer floors and ceilings. Ensure that the freezer is being cleaned regularly to prevent ice accumulation and contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: REPEAT X2 Inspector observed a used knife stored in the handwashing sink by the register. There were also a multi surface cleaner, and other cleaning supplies cluttering the sink surroundings. Discussed with PIC and the items were removed. Ensure that hand sinks are free and accessible at all times for handwashing. Handwashing sinks should not be use for storage or any other purpose other than their designated purpose.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed there to be no hand soap available at the handwashing sink in the back by coffee station and no paper towels at the hand sink in the back by the triple sink. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC refilled the soap dispenser and provided the paper towels for the hand sinks. Ensure that there is hand soap and paper towels are available at all hand sinks to enable proper handwashing at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the soda nozzles  to be soiled. The PIC was made aware. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored  and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Ten bags of Doritos were that have exceeded the expiration date were observed on the shelves. Education was provided, the bags were removed and discarded. Ensure that the date of prep packaged food items are monitored at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Facility recently dropped their Quaternary ammonium sanitizer test strips in water. CORRECTED- The inspector provided Quaternary ammonium test strips during the inspection. Ensure that there are always test strips available for every type of sanitizer to make sure that the sanitizer is at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed member of staff to wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off faucet after handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be hot holding between 110-125F. Discussed with PIC, items were over to stovetop to reheat to 165F and steam table was turned to a hotter temperature. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Observed the following items to be missing date marking:
1) (Repeat) Open cakes stored with no date marking present. 
2) Sauces in the walk in cooler. 

Discussed with PIC, cakes were purchased/made this week and the proper date marking was placed on cakes and sauces. Ensure any open TCS food held longer than 24 hours has the proper date marking available.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed multiple items ranging from soups, sauces, and other TCS items to be resting/cooling on the floor in kitchen line and walk in cooler. Discussed with staff, all containers were moved to at least 6 inches off of floor. Ensure all foods are kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed single service plates to be stored not inverted on shelf. Discussed with PIC, plates were inverted. Ensure plates are stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at server station hand sink. Discussed with PIC, a replacement part has been ordered. Ensure no leaks are present at hand sink.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer buckets were observed to test at a concentration of 100ppm. CORRECTED- The PIC was informed and they changed all sanitizer buckets. The sanitizer buckets tested to be at the label-recommended concentration of 200ppm. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and changed if not at the label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: The inspectors observed fry containers in a dispenser with their food-contact surface exposed to contamination next to the fryers (near drive through window). Ensure that single-service articles and utensils are inverted to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The sides of the fryers.
2. The table holding the fry baskets to the right of the fryers. 
3. The shelf holding receipt paper and copy paper to the right of the fryers, across from the office desk. 
4. The shelf in the back kitchen preparation area to the right of the preparation table holding the slicer. 
5. The walk-in cooler shelves. 
6. The rack and the sheet pans holding containers of food in the walk-in cooler. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The mop sink faucet is observed to have a dripping leak coming from it. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that plumbing systems are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The air vent grates above the clean dish shelves by the triple sink. 
2. The floor of the walk-in freezer. 
3. The wall behind the soda syrup boxes/shelf. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1.The coving behind the soda syrup boxes is observed to be coming away from the wall. Ensure that coving is sealed to the wall. 
2.The coving to the left of the back door is cracked and needs to be replaced.
3.The coving to the right side of the door is observed to be coming away from the wall. Ensure that the coving is sealed to the wall.

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Observed that there was not a stem thermometer available at the temporary service station to confirm receiving temperatures. PIC was informed that even for short food services, a food temperature measuring device is necessary to be able to confirm that proper temperatures are being maintained, especially following transit from the original kitchen where the items were cooked. Ensure that the establishment has a stem thermometer available at the next inspected event to confirm temperatures.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
comment: The unpasteurized juices in the display cooler in the lobby were observed to not have a Consumer Advisory label on them. The PIC stated that they ran out of labels and they are expected to get more by Tuesday. A follow up is scheduled for 10/26/2026 to ensure that each bottle of unpasteurized juice has the warning notice as follows: “WARNING: This product has not been pasteurized and, therefore, may contain harmful bacteria that can cause serious illness in children, the elderly, and persons with weakened immune systems.” In the event of running out of labels in the future, ensure that there is a back-up option to communicate this warning notice to consumers.
citation_text: 3-404.11(B) Treating Juice. Juice packaged in a food establishment shall be: (B) Labeled, if not treated to yield a 5-log reduction of the most resistant microorganism of public health significance: (1) As specified under § 3-602.11, and (2) As specified in 21 CFR 101.17(g) Food labeling, warning, notice, and safe handling statements, JUICES that have not been specifically processed to prevent, reduce, or eliminate the presence of pathogens with the following, “WARNING: This product has not been pasteurized and, therefore, may contain harmful bacteria that can cause serious illness in children, the elderly, and persons with weakened immune systems.”

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There was a personal bag observed to be on the top of a container of ginger in the kitchen cooler. The PIC was informed and moved the lunch bag away from the ginger. It is recommended to have a container in the bottom of the cooler labeled “Personal” for employee food and drinks. Ensure that personal items are in a designated area away from food-contact surfaces and food items to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspectors observed moist rags stored on the counter in multiple locations throughout the facility. PIC was made aware and the rags were returned to the sanitizer buckets to correct the violation. Ensure that wiping clothes are stored inside the sanitizer bucket with sanitizer solution when cloths are not in use.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).[C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspectors observed dishes to not be inverted above the cook line. PIC was made aware and will have staff invert the dishes on this shelf. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are protected during storage.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspectors observed the gasket on the walk in freezer in the basement to be falling off causing the door to not seal properly. PIC was made aware and will make arrangements to get the gasket repaired. Ensure that equipment is maintained in a state of repair that meets the manufactures standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: During the inspection the facility was unable to provide Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates for staff at the facility. The PIC contacted the primary manager for consultation. They could not find the certifications at the facility during the inspection. The inspectors will verify sufficient CFPMS at the next routine inspection. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs available to cover all shifted where foods are handled/prepared in the facility.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: During the inspection the facility was unable to provide verified and signed reporting agreements/documents from all staff. The PIC contacted the primary manager about this paperwork. However, they could not find it in the facility. The inspectors will verify all reporting agreements on next schedule follow up. Ensure that all reporting agreements should be available, signed, by all employees.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The inspectors observed significant soil on the blades of knives on the magnetic strip used for storing cleaned utensils that were ready for use. The PIC was made aware of it moved them to dish for re-cleaning.  Any food contact items should be cleaned and sanitized completely prior to storage and future use.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: During the inspection, inspectors observed that there was a gap underneath the back door with observable light coming through. This should be sealed so it protected against any type of pest/rodent entrance. Repaired prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The inspectors observed a pen and a lip balm in the pan along with empty oregano shakers on the prep-table. The PIC was notified and discarded the items to correct. The shakers were aLos moved to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces that make contact with ready to eat foods are protected from contamination from personal/ miscellaneous Items.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the ceiling piece of the microwave in the front of the facility was falling off. Repair prior to next routine inspection. Ensure that all physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: On arrival a personal drink was observed on the prep-table where foods were being actively portioned. The drink was moved to its appropriate designated location prior to notifying the PIC. Make sure that all personal items/food/drink should be separated from prep area, personal items can increase a risk of contamination of other food.
citation_text: 403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food Handler certificates were not able to be produced for all employees present at today’s inspection. To ensure safe food handling practices, all employees must obtain and be able to produce a Food Handler’s Card within 30 days of hire. Ensure all employees have their Food Handler’s Cards by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.[C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A single wiping cloth was observed left on a counter and moist with food residues. The PIC was shown and instructed to store the wiping cloths between uses in the available sani buckets to prevent pathogenic growths. The rag was moved to a sani bucket to correct.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Wastewater was observed backing up from floor drains on the cookline and in the dish area. Facility will close until plumbing is fixed and facility is cleaned.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed prep cooler next to salad dispenser to be cold holding at 52F. Discussed with PIC, inspector will follow up on cooler on October 14, 2026. TCS items within cooler were prepared and put in cooler 2 hours before facility opened. TCS items were moved to other working cooler units. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed ice accumulation to be present under fan unit in walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, walk in will be serviced. Ensure no ice accumulation is present within walk in freezer.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: The plumbing line under the triple sink in the back is still observed to be leaking. Discussed with PIC, a new triple sink has been ordered. Inspectors observed delivery on sink will take 2-3 weeks. A follow up is scheduled for 10/30/2026 to ensure that the waste water leak has been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to make sure that sewage is properly conveyed to the point of disposal.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 10 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Education was provided, dish machine can still be used but ensure dishes are put into a sanitizing solution for at least one minute. Ensure dish machine is properly sanitizing dishes, inspector will follow-up on 10/13/26.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizing bucket to be at 200+ ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizing solutions are kept at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed can opener to be soiled. Discussed with PIC, can opener will be cleaned. Ensure equipments is maintained food contact surfaces are clean to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items on buffet line to be held between 110-125F. Discussed with PIC, TCS items were reheated to 165 and returned to buffet line. Buffet line warmers were turned to a hotter setting, inspector observed all TCS items to be held above 135. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed buffet salad bar to be cold hold TCS items at 50F. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on ice baths and ice baths were remade. TCS items later tested below 41F. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: (Repeatx2) Observed multiple TCS items stored in walk in cooler to be held past its date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and items were discarded. Ensure all items held past date marking maximum are properly discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Observed the following violations:
1) (Repeat) Observed multiple food items in walk in cooler and freezer to not be 6 inches off of ground. 
2) Observed open seasoning to not be stored with a lid/overhead covering. 

Discussed with PIC, items will be moved to at least 6 inches off of ground. Lids were placed on seasonings.  Ensure any food item is stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths being stored on table in kitchen. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and cloths were placed in bucket. Ensure any wiping cloths in use are being stored in a sanitized solution.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed multiple sets of clean plates to not be inverted or stored under an overhead covering. Discussed with PIC, plates were inverted. Ensure clean plates are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at the walk in freezer fan unit. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. Ensure equipment is working up to manufacturers standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed walk in freezer gaskets to be in a state of disrepair. Discussed with PIC, gaskets will be replaced. Ensure equipment is maintained in a condition that meets the manufactures standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed hood system to be needing serviced. Discussed with PIC, hood system will be serviced. Ensure hood system is being serviced at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed spice table to be soiled with significant spice debris. Discussed with PIC, spice table will be serviced. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents spice debris buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to have black mold present by dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed food handler licenses to not be available for all staff members. Discussed with PIC, staff will all take steps to get licenses . Ensure all members of staff that handle food have the required food handlers license. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop in the upstairs bar was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This allows for bare hand contact with a ready to eat food, ice, when the employee grabs the handle of the scoop. The PIC was shown and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that all utensils are stored so that the read to eat foods are protected from bare hand contact moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical or temperature SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) On arrival the dish machine in the bar area would not register correct chemical sanitizer concentration on either the facility’s or inspector’s tests trips. The machine could not be brought into compliance during the inspection. The PIC contacted their EcoLab rep who stated that they would arrive in approximately one to two days to conducted maintenance. The inspector will follow up in three days to verify the maintinance has been completed. A card was left with the PIC. They should contact the inspector if there is an issue with the repair that needs more time. Until the repair can be completed the dishes produced at this location should be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitized) in another location or method. 
2) (REPEAT) On arrival the dish machine in the kitchen would not register correct sanitizer for either the temperature or chemical variations that the PIC indicated should be in effect. The machine was eventually brought into compliance by changing the CL concentrate jug and manually priming the machine.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed the coffee bar triple sink uses Bleach (Chlorine) but they do not have test strips to measure the concentration of Chlorine in the triple sink. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and acquired test strips during the inspection. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizing solution can be accurately determined with a test kit or other device
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following areas with an accumulation of soil residues:
(i) Back area staircase storage area has dust hanging from the walls.
(ii) 1ST REPEAT: Dairy walk-in cooler shelves have an accumulation of soil residues.
(iii) Dairy walk-in cooler floor underneath the shelves have an accumulation of soil residues.
(iv) Vents in several standing display coolers have an accumulation of dust.
(v) Bottom grates in several standing display coolers have an accumulation of soil residues.
PIC was notified, and stated that several of these areas are due for cleaning soon. PIC will have these areas cleaned by the next routine inspection. Ensure that Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the following food-contact surfaces that have an buildup of soil residues:
(i) the ice machine on the front panel and inside on the interior baffle.
(ii) the interior of the soda gun dispenser holder.
PIC was notified and will have these items cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a working bottle of a chemical without a label. PIC stated that it was a sanitizer. CORRECTED: PIC contacted another PIC, and the chemical was confirmed to be a quaternary ammonium-based sanitizer. PIC labeled the bottle “SANITIZER”. Ensure that all working containers that are storing potentially toxic materials are labeled with the common name of the material to prevent misuse.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces with an accumulation of soil residues:
(i) the underside of the coffee maker.
(ii) the interior edges of the mini freezer.
PIC was notified and will have these areas cleaned by the next routine inspection. Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment should be cleaned with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the backsplash above the handwashing sink is not sealed to the counter, leaving a crevice that cannot be easily cleaned. Also observed the same backsplash was not sealed to the window sill, leaving a gap that cannot be easily cleaned. Floors, walls, and ceilings must be made smooth, and easily cleanable. PIC will seal these crevices to prevent the entry and harborage of mold and other soil residues.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous flies were observed remaining near the dish machine in the bakery and the onion pallet in the back stock area. The PIC was made aware of the fly issue, inspector instructed PIC to contact their pest control company. A follow up is being set for one month from inspection date to allow time for adequate pest control to be conducted for the ongoing pest issue.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed a gap between the mop sink and the wall. PIC was informed. Ensure to seal mop sink to the wall.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the ice machine to be soiled with rust in the interior baffle of the machine. The metal panel at the top of the ice basin appears to be rusted. Inspector recommends emptying the machine, scrubbing any observed rust, and sanitizing thoroughly. If the rust cannot be removed by cleaning, replacement of the damaged parts will be required. The inspector will follow-up on October 20, 2026 to ensure the interior of the ice machine is clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The inspector observed the condenser unit of the walk-in cooler and freezer to be leaking water. The staff have placed plastic bins below the condenser to capture any leaking water. Inspector recommends continuing this process until the condenser is repaired. Repair of both the walk-in cooler and freezer is required prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Chlorine bleach used for sanitizer does not have an EPA-registration number. The product’s label does not bear instructions for use on food-contact surfaces. Ensure an EPA-registered chlorine bleach is used for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Facility does not operate on a regular set schedule. PIC will acquire an appropriate sanitizer before the next date of operation.
citation_text: 7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed member of staff to not use barrier when turning off handwashing faucet. Discussed with PIC, education on proper handwashing was provided and employee rewashed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed container of cut potatoes to be resting on floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and potatoes were moved to table. Ensure all food items are kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed multiple sets of plates to not be inverted or stored under shelf. Discussed with PIC, plates were moved to under shelf unit. Ensure clean plates are stored in way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to the left of dish machine to be in a a state of disrepair. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no CFM present to have completed the required Allergen training. Discussed with PIC, ensure all CFM’s have completed the required Allergen training and said licenses are available within facility. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a bottle of milk to be held past date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and milk was discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Insepctor observed an employee fail to remove gloves and hand wash prior to changing tasks on the prep line. Staff were observed wearing gloves to handle the register and immediately return to the prep line to handle food. Gloves must be removed prior to handling the cash register. Staff then must wash their hands thoroughly prior to donning new gloves. This practice needs to be completed every time staff change tasks during food service. Education was conducted during today’s visit.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector also observed the triple sink to be cracked between two basins. This allows water to leak from the sink to the floor.

The inspector will follow-up on November 9, 2026 to ensure the triple sink has been repaired or replaced. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food-contact surfaces in the facility to be in need of repair:
1. THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION- The shelving holding clean dishes, single-service containers, and the shelves above the triple sink were observed rusted and in need of repair/replacement.
2. SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - There are two holes under the triple sink on the right wall. Ensure these holes are patched to prevent moisture from accumulating in the walls.  

These areas which are not smooth and easily cleanable pose a hazard for bacterial accumulation and food-borne illness transmission. The inspector will follow-up on November 9, 2026 to ensure the shelving has been replaced.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed two staff members on site that did not have a valid food handler’s certification. The PIC is aware of the issue. Qdoba has recently changed policy to pay for food handler’s certification for staff. Ensure all employees have food handler’s certification prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after handwashing. Education was conducted and proper handwashing was observed. Ensure staff are using a paper towel to turn off the hand sink. The faucet is handled with dirty hands and is therefore a contamination point for clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer spray or buckets available during food preparation. The PIC was informed that a sanitizer solution must be accessible at all times during food preparation or service. A sanitizer spray bottle was prepared during the inspection, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure these spray bottles are prepared prior to starting food service.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed the dish machine in the kitchen measure 0ppm chlorine. The PIC was informed and discovered that the sanitizer solution hooked up to the machine has evaporated and weakened in concentration. The bucket of sanitizer was replaced, but the issue did not improve after multiple runs. Ecolab was contacted during the visit to request service. In the meantime, staff are required to place all dish-ware in a sanitizer solution following washing and rinsing in the dish machine. Ensure all dishes are fully submerged in the sink to guarantee proper sanitization. 
A follow-up will be conducted on October 12, 2026 to ensure the dish machine is repaired. Please contact the inspector if the machine is repaired sooner than the follow-up date.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Observed that the establishment does not have sufficient materials to respond to a vomiting or diarrheal event in that they do not have bleach available for disinfecting. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and bleach was acquired during the inspection. Ensure that food establishments have materials available for responding to biological hazardous events that can properly disinfect the contaminated areas.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

comment:
Observed that the other employee that handles food does not have a Food Handler certificate. PIC was notified. Ensure that all food handlers have certification from ANSI-certified training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days of employment and every 3 years thereafter.
