title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple roaches were observed around the kitchen area, specifically around the walls, wall gaps and spaces in the dish area. Multiple were also observed running through the open space in the middle of the room. The PIC was instructed to contact their pest control agency for targeted maintenance procedures for roaches. The inspector will follow up in approximately one month to allow for remediation procedures to take effect.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Several locations were discussed with the PIC in relation to detailed cleaning behind equipment, under equipment and in the naturally occurring space where walls are pulling apart. Food debris accumulation was observed in several such areas and cleaning of these types of spaces would likely be of great help for the overall issues noted. Cleaning of the facility will be re-evaluated at the follow up in one month as part of the already scheduled follow-up.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Several locations throughout the kitchen areas were observed with spaces that have formed between the walls, steps, floors and ceilings. Sealing these spaces would likely help with the overarching issues noted on this inspection. Several such locations were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to seal/repair as able moving forward. Overarching facility remodels and repairs have been discussed previously and again during this inspection, and are now becoming of a more immediate concern for facility processes. Information will be requested at the time of the follow up for a plan moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The hand sink in the kitchen and the one in the back by the triple sink were observed obstructed by the trash cans. The PIC was made aware. The Trash cans were removed. Ensure that all hand sinks within the facility are accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The nozzle of the tea dispenser was observed with soli accumulation. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC removed the nozzle, cleaned, and sanitized it immediately. Ensure that food contact surfaces are free of soil accumulation at all times.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The mop head was observed stored on the floor of the utility sink. Discussed with the PIC. The mop head was removed and stored properly. Ensure that used mop heads are stored in a position that allows them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: None of the employees working at the time of the inspection were food manager certified. The owner mentioned that he would work on getting employees manager certified. Ensure that at least two employees obtain food manager certificates to be sure that all hours of operation are covered.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee come from outside and not wash hands before attempting to handle food. The activity was discussed with the PIC to educate employees on when to wash hands. Ensure that all employees wash hands whenever contamination arises, as well as change gloves when a task is being interrupted.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles apart of the overhead hood system are heavily accumulated with dried grease. The baffles were shown to the owner. A third party hood service company should be contacted to clean the duct work. Baffles can be cleaned manually in the triple sink in between professional cleanings. Ensure that baffles are cleaned frequent enough to keep them clean.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop head stored in dirty mop water inside the storage closet. Shown to the PIC and the waste water was dumped and the mop head was placed on a hook to properly air dry. Ensure that mop heads are never stored in waste water after use and are stored in manner that allows for them to air dry properly.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food handler training
comment:
At least three employees working at the time of the inspection were not food handler certified. The owner mentioned that he would work on getting employees food handler certified. Ensure that employees who are not food manager certified obtain at least a food handler certificate if handling food or clean dishes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: The facility has written procedures for responding to a Norovirus event, however, there isn’t a chemical available to assist in cleaning. The PIC mentioned that the facility will purchase a bottle of bleach as soon as possible. Ensure that an EPA approved bleach is available to respond to a norovirus event. Will follow-up on October 20, 2026 to see that bleach has been purchased.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
comment: Trash was observed on the ground surrounding the outside dumpster. The dumpster lid was shut, however, there was discarded trash present on the ground. This can act as harboring conditions for rodents and insects. Ensure to educate employees on proper disposal of trash to prevent accumulation, as well as harboring conditions for unwanted pest.
citation_text: 5-501.19(A) Storage Areas, Redeeming Machines, Receptacles and Waste Handling Units, Location. (A) An area designated for REFUSE, recyclables, returnables, and, except as specified in (B) of this section, a redeeming machine for recyclables or returnables shall be located so that it is separate from FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and a public health HAZARD or nuisance is not created.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following sinks are in need of caulking:
- the triple sink where dishes are cleaned
- the handwashing sink to the right of the triple sink
Discussed with PIC. Ensure that sinks are re-caulked to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed that the ventilation hood lights are out and need replaced. PIC was notified and will get the light bulbs replaced before the next routine cleaning. Ensure that the light intensity where food employees are working is sufficiently bright enough to work with potentially dangerous equipment.
citation_text: 6-303.11(C) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (C) At least 540 lux (50 foot candles) at a surface where a FOOD EMPLOYEE is working with FOOD or working with UTENSILS or EQUIPMENT such as knives, slicers, grinders, or saws where EMPLOYEE safety is a factor. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that the PIC’s Allergen Awareness Training certificate has expired. PIC was notified and plans to renew certificates by the next routine inspection, and possibly have other staff members certified. Ensure that all CFPMs have training in basic allergen awareness principles.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There is still observed to not be a probe thermometer in the facility. There needs to be a probe thermometer to be able to measure the internal temperatures of TCS foods in the fridge. A follow up is scheduled for 10/16/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer available in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed mouse droppings under the shelving in the dry storage area. Sticky traps are in place. The PIC was made aware and droppings were swept up during the inspection. Ensure that pest control is preformed regularly to prevent pest harborage. A follow up is scheduled for 10/16/2026 to ensure that mouse droppings are continuing to be cleaned up and the proper actions are continuing to be taken to reduce rodent presence.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training for the third party food worker. The employee said that they had the certification however was unable to pull up the certification. Education was carried out. The facility will contact the third party company responsible for food prep to ensure that the employees coming to the facility for food prep have the relevant paperwork. Inspector will return on 10/8/2026 to follow up on the food handler training. Ensure that all food employees are trained in food safety and food handler are available for verification at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: The skim milk and whole milk in the standing cooler by the coffee bar were observed to not be date-marked. The PIC stated that they typically go through whole milk quickly. If the whole milk is used within 24 hours, there does not need to be date-marking. The PIC stated that they go through skim milk less often and the skim milk had a use by date of 9/29/2026. The skim milk was voluntarily discarded during the inspection due to being past the use by date. Ensure that the skim milk is being date-marked if it is not opened and used within 24 hours. TCS foods that are opened or prepared in-house and are held for over 24 hours should be date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is ice-build up on the pipes of the walk-in freezer. Ensure that the ice is removed and the issue that is causing the ice accumulation is repaired. 
2. The triple sink and both bathroom handwashing sinks are observed to be in need of being re-caulked. Ensure that the caulking is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The facility uses ShiftSmart to do their food preparation for them. The ShiftSmart employee was present and cooking food during today’s inspection. The employee did not have a food handler card. The employee showed the inspector their phone and the app that they use stated that “A food handler card is not needed to do food preparation in this area”. A food handler card is needed for every food employee that works in a facility that handles food or ice. Ensure that all employees doing food preparation in the facility have a food handler card. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Staff were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees are reminded to always wash their hands before donning lobbed in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The nozzles on both soda machines were observed with an accumulation of soil including the knives in the holder in the back. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC pulled all the nozzles and knives out and instructed an employee to clean and sanitize them. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned above are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer in the bucket on the cook line was observed reading between 100-0 ppm. The PIC was made aware. A staff member was instructed to remake the sanitizer. The new sanitizer tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizer is monitored and replaced as required at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the trim tile on the wall right of the dry storage entrance upstairs to be coming off. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspectors that that the trim tile will be sealed back to the wall. Ensure that the the trim tile is fix rendering the wall in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
Observed grab and go sandwiches are labeled with primary sandwich ingredients and price only. Items prepackaged in advance for sale should be labeled with all information below. See that labels are provided by next routine inspection.  

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed a leak from the ceiling near the mop sink. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained and in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple personal items stored in the walk in cooler among food intended for consumers. PIC was made aware and personal items were moved to different shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that all food for consumers is separated and protected to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed 3 pallets of apples and onions that were host to a swarm of fruit flies. Food was open to pests without cover in the storage area. A spoiled apple was removed from the container, but the fruit flies remained. CORRECTED: PIC moved the apples and onions to where they can be protected: the walk-in cooler. PIC also discarded any spoiled onions and apples. When PIC moved the apples and onions, and entire pallet of rotten bananas was revealed to be underneath, which also had fruit flies. The bananas were completely black and shriveled. PIC discarded the bananas. Inspector also observed that the potatoes in the same area were shriveled. Ensure that food is safe and unadulterated through good storage practices and frequent quality checks.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the facility was using “food-contact surface” wipes, but had no way to test the effectiveness of the sanitizing solution contained within. The concentration of the sanitizer could not be measured using Inspector’s test strips (Chlorine, quaternary ammonium). PIC did not have any test strips (see Violation #48). CORRECTED: Inspector had PIC make a standard sanitizer solution using bleach and water, which tested between 50-200ppm. Inspector reminder PIC to only use a cap of bleach when making an sanitizer bucket solution, because too much sanitizer is considered toxic. Ensure that chemical sanitizing solutions measure at safe and effective concentrations for food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed 3 pallets of onions and apples in the storage area that had a swarm of fruit flies on them. PIC was notified, and identified that some of the onions had rotted, which provides harborage to insects. PIC removed the rotten apple and plans to put the onions and apples in the walk-in cooler where they will be better protected from attracting insects. An additional pallet of rotten bananas was also uncovered and discarded. Inspector discussed changing pest control methods to a paid service instead of facility doing their own pest control. Ensure that the premises is free of pests by inspecting frequently for pests, providing suitable pest control methods for different types of pests, and protecting food from pests.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Observed areas where food was exposed to potential contamination due to where it was stored:
(i) onions and apples were stored above large cannisters and below the soda machine lines. CORRECTED: PIC moved the apples and onions to the walk-in cooler.
(ii) Eggs stored in the walk-in cooler were stored next to a dripping fan, where the drips were to be collected in a pan. CORRECTED: PIC moved the eggs farther away from the dripping.
(iii) Unwrapped bread was stored uncovered without protection from above on basement shelves (bread was unwrapped so it would dry out for a recipe). CORRECTED: PIC placed the bread under a plastic cover.
Ensure food is not stored near mechanical or environmental sources of contamination from above, below, or the sides.
citation_text: 3-305.12(A) and (C)-(I) Food Storage, Prohibited Areas. FOOD may not be stored: (A) In locker rooms; (C) In dressing rooms; (D) In garbage rooms; (E) In mechanical rooms; (F) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (G)Under leaking water lines, including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads, or under lines on which water has condensed; (H)Under open stairwells; or (I) Under other sources of contamination. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the facility does not have test strips for the available sanitizing wipes, which did not test with either Chlorine or quaternary ammonium test strips. CORRECTED: Working test strips for Chlorine were obtained. A separate sanitizer bucket using regular bleach (Chlorine) was prepared and tested. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to verify proper sanitizing concentrations.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces that are in need of cleaning to prevent accumulation of soil residues:
(i) the walls of all the freezers have a significant accumulation of ice which can fall onto food.
(ii) the gasket edges have an accumulation of black soil residues.
(iii) the filter of the cooking ventilation hood is completely encrusted with grease and soil residues. Inspector discussed changing hood cleaning methods to a paid service instead of facility doing their own hood cleanings, and more often hood cleanings.
Clean these areas with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues that can potentially contaminate food.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the kitchen and storage areas for the restaurant are cluttered with unnecessary items, making it difficult to clean with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues. Please clear the clutter so that the facility can be maintained for better functionality. Keep personal items separate from restaurant items in storage areas.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed personal foods intermixed with food for service in the triple door cooler. Discussed with the staff members that personal foods need to be completely separate from restaurant foods, either in separate sides of the cooler, or all personal foods on the bottom shelves. Ensure separation of items for personal use from items used for service to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the soap dispenser at the back handwashing sink (across from the triple sink) to not be working during today’s inspection. The PIC told inspector that they had put in a work order for the repair. Ensure all food handlers are using one of the two hand sinks that are fully supplied and working until the back hand sink is stocked and in working order. A follow up will occur on 10/05/26 to ensure all sinks are fully supplied and are in working order.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the nozzles of the slushie machine and the internal surface of the coffee maker to be soil. The PIC was made aware. The PIC clean the various food contact surfaces immediately. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the one mentioned above are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The plumbing line under the triple sink in the back was observed leaking. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspectors that the relevant plumbing repairs will be done. Ensure that the plumbing is repaired to be in compliance with the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored above cheese and raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk in cooler. The PIC was informed and these items were rearranged. Ensure staff are following proper storage order guidelines in the future.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed rice stored in the warming table to be stored in a black plastic bag. The PIC was informed that this bag is not food safe, and should not be used for food storage. Furthermore, this plastic is not rated to be heated in a warmer, and may result in melting plastic contaminating the food items within the bag. Ensure food is stored in properly rated containers. Inspector recommends using aluminum foil to protect the warming containers rather than plastic.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant between the counter and wall around the dish machine to be soiled or damaged. The PIC was instructed to wash and sanitize the sealant. If the sealant appears stained or damaged after sanitizing, the silicone will require replacement. Ensure the sealant is in good repair and clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC could not provide verification of their CFPM certification during this inspection. The rules were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have a CFPM available at all times of operation moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine were observed with accumulating soilage in the nozzle holes. The PIC was shown and stated that the nozzles were cleaned Monday (four days prior to the inspection) and that the observed brown stuff was soda. The same soilage was observed in the Mountain Dew and Lemonade nozzles. These nozzles need to be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) more often, preferably daily or every other day to ensure that they do not accumulate filth and potentially contaminate people’s drinks. The nozzles were cleaned during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight/touch at all times in the facility.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

The beef in the left most run of the right steam well in the front was observed with internal temperatures of 117F-119F. The PIC was shown and stated that the foods were placed into the unit approximately one hour prior to observation. The unit was turned up to provide for future safety concerns and the current batch of meat was discarded at the end of the shift (4 pm) to manage the immediate concern.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed several food items stored in grocery store sacks in several freezers and the walk-in cooler. Grocery store sacks are not approved food-grade storage packagings. PIC was notified and staff started the process of repackaging the items using an available roll of approved food-grade bags. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by always using food-grade packaging for storage.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspectors observed there to be no signed employee health reporting agreements during inspection. PIC was made aware. An email copy of the employee health reporting agreements was sent and copies were printed and employees signed the agreements to correct this violation. Ensure that all employees have signed an employee health reporting agreements and they are kept on file for future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Inspectors observed there to be no Norovirus clean up procedure available in the facility. PIC was informed and an email was sent to provide them with the norovirus clean up procedure. The Norovirus clean up procedure was printed and posted in the kitchen to correct the violation.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw chicken breast stored above ready to eat yogurt tubes in the fridge in the kitchen. Shell eggs were observed stored above milk and juice. PIC was made aware and education was conducted regarding proper storage order. Staff was instructed to move items to correct the violation. Inspector provided storage order hand out for future reference. Ensure that all food is stored to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed window cleaner and air freshener stored above food on the metal storage shelf in the kitchen. PIC was made aware and the incorrectly stored bottles were moved to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that chemicals and other cleaner are stored so they do not contaminate food or food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that the front handwashing sink was without paper towels at the beginning of the inspection. CORRECTED: PIC stated that new paper towels were available, but the key to open the dispenser had not yet been located, and instead they were using paper towels from the other handwashing sink in the other room. PIC located the key and replaced the paper towels during the inspection. Ensure that EACH handwashing sink is provided with disposable towels.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed 2 containers of house made pepper ranch in the prep cooler and the front 2-door cooler that had date marks for August, well beyond the 7 day period for discarding TCS foods. CORRECTED: PIC and staff discarded the items. Ensure that TCS, RTE foods are discarded within 7 days, with day 1 being date of preparation or opening, and day 7 being date of final use or discard.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of soil residues on the underside of the coffee maker. Notified PIC that the area needs to be cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free from an accumulation of food residues and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the oven/cooktop in the back kitchen is not functional and cannot be used. Repair or remove nonfunctional or unused equipment from the kitchen.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that there was duct tape on the handle of the back 2-door (egg) cooler. Duct tape is not an approved repair, because it is not smooth and easily cleanable. Eliminate duct tape and repair door handle with materials that are smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink by the drive thru and the hand sink by the three part sink were observed with gaps forming around the edges. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-seal the locations prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces in the food preparation and cleaning areas are maintained in a smooth and easily cleanable state to facilitate effective cleaning.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were drink particle residues observed dumped in the hand sink opposite of the ice machine. The PIC was made aware. The hand sink was cleaned. Ensure that all hand sinks within the facility are use for handwashing only and nothing else including dumping drinks and other items at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was no hand soap in the dispensers at the hand sink opposite of the ice machine and the hand sink on the right side of the standing freezer use to store the harsh browns. The PIC was made aware. Hand soap was provided for the dispensers mentioned. Ensure that every hand sinks within the facility is supplied with the appropriate material.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed that 12 cans were severely dented, top or bottom seams, or dents severe enough to cause sharp edges. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and cans were discarded. Inspector discussed protecting can integrity with PIC, including what type of damage should lead to cans being rejected. Ensure that canned packaging is in good condition so the food inside is protected from potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of food residue, grease, and other debris on the floor in the chemical and equipment storage room. The room is also where used cooking grease is taken before it is cleaned and put in the used cooking oil reservoir in the back. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Discussed with PIC and Staff about getting the floor cleaned, and additional measures to assist staff in keeping the floor clean, namely using temporary cardboard under the used cooking grease container. Ensure the floors are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the bathrooms that are used by women (womens room and employee bathroom) do not have covered trash cans. PIC was notified. Ensure that all bathrooms used by women have covered trash cans.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizing solution in the sanitizing bucket was a mixture of bleach (Chlorine) and detergent. Sanitizing buckets should only have sanitizer and water in them, no additional cleaning chemicals, as the mixture could change the effectiveness of the sanitizer. CORRECTED: PIC directed staff to remake all sanitizing buckets with only bleach and water, and from now on have separate buckets for washing with detergent and sanitizing. Inspector recommends marking each bucket to clarify which ones are for sanitizing and which are for washing. Ensure that chemical sanitizers are used per manufacturer’s instructions.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the triple sink caulking is separating from the wall and needs to be repaired. The sink must be sealed (ex. caulking) to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the sink is sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair:
1) There is no caulking between the hand washing sink (in front of the office) and the wall.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine contains an accumulation of debris, and is fragmented or absent in multiple areas.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the bar handwashing sink to be missing soap. CORRECTED: Staff was notified and soap was added. Ensure that handwashing sinks have a supply of soap.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed the following foods stored without covering:
(i) Breaded meat stored in a deep freezer without a cover, and the deep freezer had significant ice buildup. CORRECTED: Notified PIC that the meat item must be wrapped or covered before being stored in the deep freezer. PIC noted that in the past they were put in containers. PIC had staff wrap those items in plastic wrap.
(ii) Cut cake stored in a standing cooler without a cover beneath several different food items. CORRECTED: Notified a staff member and a lid was added.
Ensure food is protected from cross-contamination through wrappings, packaging, and covers.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw shrimp stored over pickle spirals in the pizza prep cooler. CORRECTED: Staff was notified and moved the contents of the cooler around so that all fish items were on the bottom shelf and all RTE foods were on the top shelf. Ensure that food is protected from cross-contamination by keeping RTE items stored above raw animal proteins in case of drips.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the interior baffle of the ice machine had an accumulation of soil residues. Notified PIC that the ice machine needs to be kept clean to sight and touch, including the interiors. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned with enough frequency to keep it clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of grease and soil residues in the kitchen ventilation hood. Inspector notes that the last professional cleaning was 12 November 2025, with a note that the next cleaning should be in 6 months, which was 4 months ago. Please clean the hood to remove the accumulation of grease and soil residues before it can fall into food or cause a fire. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free of accumulated soil residues through frequent cleaning.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the bottom of the prep cooler in the kitchen near the kitchen window has an accumulation of water in the bottom. Staff noted that they vacuum it regularly, but it keeps coming back. Ensure that is repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the bar triple sink to have a too low concentration of quaternary ammonium (100ppm). Water was hot to the touch. Triple sink had 4 tablets in it. CORRECTED: PIC and Staff were educated that the water temperature for quaternary ammonium-based sanitizing solutions needs to be room temperature to be effective (65-75 F). Staff remade the triple sink using cool water and 3 tablets (sink was mostly full) and it tested at 200ppm. Ensure that chemical sanitizing solutions are used per manufacturer’s instructions; for quaternary ammonium that is 65-75 F for water temperature and a concentration between 200-400ppm.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:
(i) 1ST REPEAT: The upper nonfood-contact surfaces above the soda nozzles have mineral buildup.
(ii) The coil on the ceiling of the walk-in cooler is dusty.
(iii) The box fan used in the dish room is dusty.
(iv) The walls near the fryers that are not stainless steel have an accumulation of grease and soil residues.
(v) The deep freezers have an accumulation of ice around the edges that can fall onto the food.
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that the only CFPM on staff was not present today. The General Manager is working on renewing their CFPM. Ensure that a Certified Food Protection Manager is present at all times of when food preparation is happening.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the handwashing sink in the bar was obstructed by a drink pitcher, and was out of paper towels and soap. CORRECTED: Staff were notified, the pitcher was removed from the handwashing sink, and the paper towels and soap were refilled. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for purposes other than handwashing, are fully accessible for handwashing at all times, and are fully stocked with soap and paper towels.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed that liquid eggs were stored above RTE foods like yogurt and strawberries in the front area 2-door cooler. CORRECTED: Inspector discussed with Staff, and eggs were moved below RTE foods. Inspector and Staff further discussed that items with different cooking temperatures can be stored side-by-side as long as they are not in contact with each other. Ensure that raw animal proteins are stored below RTE foods that do not require cooking to be eaten.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed that carafes of juice were being cold held in the service ice that is used for drinks. CORRECTED: Inspector educated staff that ice used for beverages (“eating ice” or “service ice”) is not to be used for a secondary purpose like cold holding beverages, as there is a strong potential for cross-contamination from both the exterior of the containers and from spills. Staff removed the containers from the service ice, and will cease this practice. Inspector discussed if Staff want to keep additional juices cold, they should use a separate cooler or a separate ice bath where the ice inside is only used for cooling. Ensure that service ice is only used for ice inside of beverages, and not for cooling food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket in the front part of the kitchen did not measure any concentration of quaternary ammonium sanitizer (0ppm). Sanitizing solution was hot to the touch. CORRECTED: Inspector asked Staff if the sanitizing solution was sourced from the triple sink hose, and it was. The triple sink’s bottle of sanitizer is not empty. Staff made the sanitizing solution how it had been made that morning, with hot water, and the sanitizing solution again read 0ppm. Inspector educated Staff that quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution should be made with water that is 75 F (room temperature). Staff remade the sanitizing solution, this time just using cold water. The sanitizing solution measured at 200ppm for quaternary ammonium. Ensure that chemical sanitizing solution of quaternary ammonium is used per manufacturer’s guidelines for temperature and chemical concentration: room temperature water (65-75 F) and a concentration that is effective for sanitizing, 200-400ppm.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
3RD REPEAT: Observed the stainless steel shelf above the three compartment sink is rusted above and below. The shelf must either be replaced or painted and sealed. Ensure that the shelf is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. NOTE that fixing the ventilation in that area (violation #56: non-working heat dish machine ventilation hood) may prevent additional rusting in the area.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:
(i) there is an accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezer. A tray that has been placed to catch the drips, but the ice is no longer contained in the tray, and is starting to fall on boxes.
(ii) many handles in the kitchen are sticky to the touch (hot box handles, the sauce cooler).
(iii) there is an accumulation of soil residues on the fans and the ceiling in the walk-in cooler.
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas that are in need of repair:
(i) FIRST REPEAT: the baseboards on the floor between and next to the walk-in cooler and freezer.
(ii) FIRST REPEAT: the walk-in cooler and freezer doors are difficult to shut and open - there is an accumulation of ice / water at the bottom areas.
(iii) the handwashing sink near the dish area has water pressure issues that is causing the water to spray everywhere.
The PIC was informed, and made plans for repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that equipment and physical facilities are in a state of good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the ventilation hood over the heat dish machine was not working, causing an excess of condensation in the surrounding area, including the ceiling HVAC vent (observed to be rusted), and excessive steam pushing out into the surrounding area. Steam rises up, pools in the ventilation hood, then bounces back down and out into the kitchen instead of sucked up by the ventilation. This could be contributing to the rusted shelving observed in the kitchen area as well. The PIC was informed, and made plans for its repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that ventilation hood systems are sufficient in capacity to prevent condensation from collecting.
citation_text: 4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival and throughout the inspection there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The PIC was instructed to have enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts in the facility. A hand out with the current courses known by this department was given to the PIC during the inspection to help facilitate enough CFPMs moving forward. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts where foods and food contact surfaces are being handled and/or prepared.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). 

When asked during the inspection the PIC could not provide reporting agreements or similar paperwork for any of the staff observed in the facility. Signed copies were found for other staff only. Fresh copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements were given to the PIC and signed during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all required paperwork is maintained in the facility at all times and updated as new staff is hired.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

On arrival there was not signage observed at either the kitchen or bathroom hand sinks. Signage was given during the inspection and put up to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks maintain signage designating them as intended for hand washing only at all times in the facility.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a certified food protection manager present at the start of the inspection. Discussed with PIC. The owner arrived shortly throughout the inspection, which he is the only person who is food manager certified. Violation corrected. Ensure that there is always a person who is food manager certified on site at all times if serving food.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was a dead fly observed inside of a container of broth within the walk in cooler. The broth was stored uncovered. Shown to the PIC and the broth was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are covered during storage to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The settings were altered on the machine during the visit and the machine was retested at 100ppm (CL). Violation corrected. Ensure that the dish machine tests at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following areas were observed with a SIGNIFICANT amount of mold on the food contact surfaces:
- baffle of the ice machine
- nozzles of the soda machine
Shown to the PIC and the soda nozzles were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection, however, a follow-up will be scheduled for October 8, 2026 to see that ice baffles have been cleaned and sanitized. Ensure to clean baffles as frequent as often to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed various Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods that lacked proper date marking. These foods included pizza sauces, cooked noodles, sliced deli meats, meatballs, etc. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are date marked if being stored in house longer than 24 hours. Provide a date marking for items with the date that foods are prepared and/or the discard date. Will follow-up on October 8, 2026 to see that foods are date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed rodent droppings on the floor and other surfaces throughout the dish room. There was a five inch gap in the corner behind the dish machine that could act an entry point for rodents. Shown and discussed with the PIC. Ensure that entry points are sealed and that a professional pest management company is contacted to service the facility. Will follow-up on  October 8, 2026 to check on pest activity.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The food containers inside of the top prep cooler were observed heavily accumulated with food debris. Ensure that containers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The additional employees that handles food are not food manager, nor food handler certified. Ensure that all employees who handle food or clean dishes are at least food handler certified. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer in the sani bucket on the counter in the lobby was measured between 100-0 ppm. The PIC was Made aware. The sani bucket was remade and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are monitored at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the hand sink by the kitchen entrance was observed coming oof the wall. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the sink will be repaired. Ensure that the caulking at this sink is repaired accordingly.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: The ventilation duct above the sandwich's station was observed with an accumulation of dust and soil. The PIC was made aware. Ensure that the vent duct is monitored, cleaned, and kept free of dust and soil at all times.
citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.
