title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine was observed with mold and soil accumulation. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspector that the accumulation will be cleaned and the baffles sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces such as the ice machine baffles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed leakage in the faucet of the triple sink and the hand sink on the cook line. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the sinks mentioned are repaired according to the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The nudo board coating on the wall left of the hand sink at the entrance of the dish room was observed coming off the wall. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the board will be sealed appropriately. Ensure that the gap is sealed providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There is observed to not be a probe thermometer in the facility. There needs to be a probe thermometer to be able to measure the internal temperatures of TCS foods in the fridge. A follow up is scheduled for 10/7/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer available in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed the handwashing sink at the bar to be out of paper towels. PIC was made aware and restocked the paper towels at this handwashing sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are stocked with a hand drying device or disposable towels at all times of food preparation and operation.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed raw chicken to be stored above other raw animal proteins in the outdoor walk in cooler. PIC was made aware and instructed staff members to relocate the raw chicken to be stored below other raw animal proteins. Ensure that all food is stored where it is protected from cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the frozen drink dispenser nozzles to have visible soil accumulation. PIC was made aware that this portion of the dispensers need to be cleaned frequently. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to avoid soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspectors observed a knife stored in the crevice between two prep coolers. PIC was made aware and the knife was removed and sent to the dish machine to be washed to correct the violation. Inspectors suggested magnetic knife rack or other storage area for knives. Ensure that utensils are stored in a frequently cleaned and sanitized space.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed slight mold build-up on the gaskets of the make line prep cooler (lower doors). Maintain gaskets clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that the designated handwashing sink in the bar area was being used as a dump sink, despite facility procedure to use a separate bucket for waste bar liquids. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and educated staff about only using the handwashing sink for handwashing, and that the separate bucket should be used for waste bar liquids. An additional sign was placed above the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for any other purposes other than handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed that a container of sausage gravy in the bottom part of the main prep cooler was measured at an internal temperature of 60 F. PIC stated that the sausage gravy had been recently put back in the cooler 30 minutes previously after being out for part of service. Inspector checked the internal temperature again 30 minutes later and the gravy was at 62 F. Inspector observes that all other items in the cooler are sufficiently cold holding at 41 F and below, and that the cooler has an ambient air temperature of 36 F. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the sausage gravy. Inspector and PIC discussed storing the sausage gravy, and other items that get cooled, in shallower pans so as to allow for more rapid cooling, and making sure staff are more aware of how long items are left on the counter. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F or less, and that items can cool quickly once placed in cold holding equipment.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the small ice machine had an accumulation of soil residues on the front of interior baffle and behind it. PIC was notified and a staff member started the process of cleaning it. Staff and PIC determined that a more professional cleaning would be needed. Ice machine was removed from service and PIC will buy bagged ice from an approved source. Facility will use bagged ice until ice machine can be thoroughly serviced. Ensure equipment food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that the right 2-door freezer in the back area had a significant accumulation of ice at the bottom. PIC was notified, had already noticed the ice accumulation, and was actively planning to move the items inside to a different freezer so that the 2-door freezer could be cleaned. Ensure nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: See previous FU #6

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed no sanitizer prepared in the facility during food preparation and service. Education was conducted on sanitizer requirements and a sanitizer bucket was prepared, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure a spray bottle is prepared at all times to ensure proper sanitization of food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to submit a service ticket for the ice machine. A follow-up will be conducted on October 5, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present during today’s visit. The PIC’s certification expired on 8/10/2026. The PIC has plans to take the exam at the District 186 Office. Ensure there is a CFPM present prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

The inspector observed the triple sink to be missing its sealant at the back of the sink. The sink needs to be sealed to the wall to prevent water and microbial accumulation. Ensure this repair is complete prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed a trash bag in the upright cooler to be storing flatbread. Trash bags are not considered smooth, easily cleanable, or food safe. Ensure all food items are stored in permitted packaging moving forward.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed a stack of clean cutting boards to be stored between cardboard boxes of gloves and cardboard boxes containing soda syrup. The PIC was informed that these cardboard surfaces are not considered clean or food safe. Ensure equipment and utensils are stored on food-grade, clean surfaces to prevent cross contamination. The cutting boards were relocated during today’s visit.
citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the interior of the upright freezer in the kitchen to have an excessive accumulation of frost. Ensure the freezer is defrosted regularly to prevent frost contamination with food in the freezer. This freezer will be inspected again during the next routine inspection to ensure defrost has been completed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were approximately four alive roaches and six dead roaches observed throughout the facility. There were no juvenile roaches observed. According to the PIC, Sentinel is currently treating the facility weekly. Discussed cleaning in the front kitchen more, as this is where all of the roaches were observed during the inspection. Facility has reduced the use of cardboard in areas where roaches were frequently spotted. Continue with this. Discussed making sure to clean up dead roaches to allow for better monitoring of the pest issue. A follow up is scheduled for 10/23/2026 to ensure that the facility is taking the appropriate measures to reduce pest presence in the facility, including but not limited to, cleaning, pest control, getting rid of cardboard, and cleaning up dead roaches. Ensure that the appropriate actions are being taken to reduce pest presence and to clean the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine to reach a dish plate temperature of 150-154F after running several cycles. Inspector discussed proper heat sanitizing temperatures with the person in charge (PIC). The facility has been directed to utilize the triple sink for chemical sanitation until the machine’s heat boosters have been adjusted to reach a minimum plate temperature of 158F (FDA food codes allows for +/-2 instrument error). Inform the inspector if the machine has been adjusted prior to the follow up date.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed a leak to be present under triple sink. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced. Ensure no leaks are present within facility, inspector will follow-up with facility on 9/29/26.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed milk and cream to be held past date marking. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item kept past its date marking is properly discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed back triple sink faucet to be leaking. Discussed with PIC, faucet will be serviced. Ensure a licensed plumber services faucet so that no leak is present.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the interior baffles of the ice machines had an accumulation of soil residues. CORRECTED: PIC stated that the ice machines had just been cleaned that morning. Inspector confirmed that the ice machine had just been cleaned, as there was very little ice in the machine. PIC immediately contacted the facility’s maintenance person, who arrived quickly and removed the ice machine from service to clean and sanitize the interior of the ice machine during the inspection. Inspector observed that the ice machine interior was now clean, and discussed with staff better methods of monitoring the hard-to-reach area (using a mobile phone camera and a flashlight). Ensure that food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: At the start of the inspection, there wasn't an employee who was food manager certified on the premise. Shortly throughout the inspection, the only employee who is food manager certified arrived. Discussed the need to have at least two employees who are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation. Ensure that a CFPM is present if open for operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A significant amount of mold was observed on a container of cooked chili within the line prep cooler along the cookline. Date marking was also lacking for this food item. Shown to the PIC and the chili was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that preparation/discard dates are checked daily to be sure that foods are getting rotated correctly and pulled before they get the chance to spoil or go bad.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a container of ground beef stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods inside a prep cooler along the cook-line. Shown the PIC and the ground beef was moved to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal proteins are always stored beneath RTE foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were many Time/Temperature Control foods that lacked date marking in the prep coolers along the cook-line. The foods include cheeses, sauces, chili, and cooked noodles. The foods were shown to the PIC and were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods are never stored in house longer than seven days after they are opened or prepared.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The bottom surfaces, as well as the shelving inside all prep coolers along the cook-line were observed with accumulated food debris. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that inner surfaces of prep coolers are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the handwashing sink next to the dry storage room does not have cold water; the handle fell off when turned. PIC was informed by staff that the Owner was aware of the situation and a replacement has been ordered, but the sink had not been removed from service to stop staff from using it. PIC removed the handwashing sink from service with signs, “No Usar/Out of Order”. Another handwashing sink is available for use by kitchen staff without having to leave the kitchen. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are equipped to provide hot water.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed the available test strips for Chlorine were damaged by water from the chemical dish machine. Facility does have test strips for quaternary ammonium, but does not have replacement strips for Chlorine (bleach). Ensure that concentrations of all sanitizing solutions can be accurately determined by using a test kit.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the walls behind the dish line have an accumulation of soil residues. PIC was notified. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The bleach available for assisting in the clean up of vomit/diarrhea isn’t an EPA approved chemical. The bleach is low splash and it lacks an EPA registration number. Ensure to purchase a regular bottle of bleach. Also, be sure that it has an EPA registration number and is approved to effectively kill norovirus. Will follow-up on October 5, 2026 to see that regular bleach has been purchased.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The faucet spout at the triple sink inside of the dish room is in disrepair. When water is turned on, the spout falls from the faucet. Ensure that the faucet is repaired by a licensed plumber.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There is a significant amount of ice build on the inner surfaces of the reach in freezer along the bar station. When time permits, be sure to unplug and defrost the freezer to melt the ice. Ensure that ice build up is maintained in freezer.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: Both hand-sinks in the kitchen and dish areas lacked hot water. The knobs at the hand-sinks appear to be broken, which is preventing hot water availability at the sinks. Ensure that all hand sinks are provided with hot water to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on October 5, 2026 to see that sinks are repaired.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Food handler training
comment:
At least two of the employees working at the time of inspection could not show proof of food handler certificates. Ensure that all employees who handle food or clean dishes are food handler certified if not food manager certified. Be sure that all certificates are printed out for future inspections. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets and interior of the sliding door meat display cooler to be soiled with food debris. The PIC was informed and plans to increase cleaning frequency of the surfaces of the cooler. Ensure the cooler is clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Small gnats were observed primarily around the soda nozzle in the bar area. Facility is cleaning and pest control is expected to be out this week. Continue efforts to eliminate gnat population. Inspectors will follow up in two weeks.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there to be no sanitizer bucket made for wiping surfaces during the inspection. PIC was made aware and an employee corrected the violation by filling a container with quaternary ammonia sanitizer that tested at 200ppm. Ensure that there is a sanitizer bucket with chemical sanitizer available during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following physical facilities to be in need of repair:
- 1st REPEAT caulking at hand washing sink near the triple sink needs repair the handwashing is separating from the wall
- 1st REPEAT standing water near the drain underneath the soda syrup storage
- hole in the wall underneath the hand washing sink near the triple sink
Ensure that all physical facilities are cleaned, maintained and in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mops stored on the floor in both mop rooms. PIC was made aware and mentioned the hanging devices that were installed do not function properly for the mop handles in the facility. Ensure that mops are hung to dry after each use.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Signed employee reporting agreements are not available on file at the facility. Education was conducted and blank copies in English were provided to PIC. Inspectors will drop off agreements in Chinese early next week. Follow up scheduled for Monday September 28, 2026. Ensure that all employees sign a health reporting agreement and keep them available for all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf[

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed the handwashing sink to not have soap available. There was two bottles of hand sanitizer near the handwashing sink. PIC was made aware and corrected the violation by providing soap for the handwashing sink. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are stocked with soap at all times of food preparation and hours of operation.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: (2nd REPEAT) Inspector observed foods improperly stored in several locations: 1) carrots stored in a cardboard box that previously contained frozen chicken. CORRECTED- Carrots were removed from the box. Store vegetables in their receiving boxes, in plastic containers, or directly on shelves. 2) Packages of raw pork observed above clams and seafood in the long open air cooler. CORRECTED: Pork was moved to store elsewhere in the cooler. 3) A bag of raw chicken observed stored above vegetables in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Chicken was moved to storage below vegetables and other animal proteins. Ensure foods are stored to prevent cross contamination. Store raw animal proteins in relation to their cooking temperatures.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed there to be no stem thermometers available at the facility. PIC was made aware that probe thermometers are required to monitor temperatures of food being stored at the facility. Follow up scheduled for Monday September 28, 2026. Ensure that a food temperature measuring device is always available at the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
Several items were observed without complete labeling. 1) Pitted haw (fruit) and tofu observed without any labeling. Ensure that prepackaged foods are labeled to indicate their contents and source. 2) Tofu and lo mein noodles observed without ingredient labeling. Label foods with their ingredients, or keep an ingredient binder with labels upon customer request. 3) Several animal proteins (shrimp, etc) observed without cooking instructions on packaging or posted nearby. Add safe cooking instruction to labels or post signage near all raw animal proteins with safe cooking instructions.
3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Several knives were observed stored in the gap between prep counters. CORRECTED- Knives were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Store knives on a clean surface, rather than between tables which is not easily cleanable or regularly sanitized.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.[C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

Multiple employees were observed to don gloves and begin food service without hand washing. Education was conducted with the manager and they were instructed to review hand washing with all food handlers and enforce good hand washing practices moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple dishes were observed stored while soiled with food debris and sticker residue. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained clean until use.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Mops were observed with the heads pooled up in the bottoms of the empty mop buckets. The PIC was shown and instructed to store the mops so that the bristles are allowed to hang and drip dry. Ensure mops are stored correctly moving forward. THe mops were moved by the inspector during the inspection to demonstrate and corrected the violation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Multiple locations throughout the facility were observed with the coving at the floor junction pulling away from the wall. This is exposing a gap that it not easily cleanable by staff. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the location re-sealed prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the seam between the dry storage wall and the floor was only sealed on one side (the side opposite the door) but not the side next to the door. Seal the dry storage wall to the floor on all sides to ensure a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed buildup of soil residues in the soda nozzles. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and relayed that establishment has a procedure for cleaning nozzles, and showed inspectors the sanitizing container, complete with a nozzle brush. Inspector and PIC discussed reminding staff to really scrub the nozzles so that they are clean to sight and touch. PIC had staff replace the used nozzles with clean nozzles during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed several instances where food contact surfaces of single-service and single-use articles were stored upright without protection from contamination from above: dishes on top of counters, dishes on open wire racks, dishes inside of coolers. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and corrected each instance through inversion. Inspectors and PIC discussed better storage methods for open wire racks including placing plastic mats or other coverings on shelves. PIC also plans to educate staff on consistent storage methods of single-service and single-use articles. Ensure that food contact surfaces are protected through cover or inversion.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Inspectors observed an accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezers and some reach-in freezers. PIC and Inspector discussed improved defrost procedures and increase cleaning frequency. Ensure that areas are smooth and easily cleanable, and are cleaned frequently.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-201.11(E) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person In Charge, and Conditional Employees. Responsibility of food employees and conditional employees to report. The person-in-charge did not have signed copies of the reporting agreement present for the available staff. The binder present in the bar had copies of Bassett, food handler, and CFPM. But no employee health or reporting agreement information was available. During the inspection, the employee health reporting agreement paperwork was provided as was the diagnosis and symptom paperwork. PIC was informed that it was his job to make appropriate number of copies and have staff sign the agreements. 

 (E) A FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE shall report to the PERSON IN CHARGE the information as specified under (A) of this section.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. There was not an available policy for removal of vomit and diarrhea during the inspection. Policy paperwork was provided during the inspection by CK. Corrected on-site. 

A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
citation_text:
3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. The facility is operating as a Class I facility. The kitchen is observed cooling and reheating a number of foods (inclusive of chicken, red sauce, cheese sauce, and chili). Cooling practices were discussed and seem appropriate. See that cooling methods are educated to additional staff supporting this behavior. Facility is operating as a Class II entity and is not currently allowed to cool and reheat but a simple upgrade of their permit classification will allow the behavior to change. The kitchen will be upgraded to a Class I kitchen and cooling and reheating may continue. 


 (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. The walk-in cooler is old and has portion of the ceiling where condensation leads to dripping. A containers of sauce that had a whole placed in the plastic wrap for cooling is observed to have water condensation accumulating on the surface. The water appears to be accumulating to one side of the plastic, but the viscous nature of the water means that possible cross-contamination cannot be ruled-out. During the inspection the water -laden contained food was discarded. 
Also, a container of single-service crackers is observed stored beneath the bug light on the counter by the dry storage. The crackers were pulled forward and away from the bug light. See that nothing is stored beneath the light. 

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. Observed the interior and the exterior of the triple sink to be soiled with accumulated soil and food debris. Also, the interior of the dish machine is noted to have accumulated food debris along the sides of the walls and within the external sump of the side of the dish machine. The dish machine operator was arriving around 130 and PIC stated that facility would be cleaned around that time. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Operator initially stated that the reheating temperature was 135F and then eventually stated that reheat temperature is 165F. Stem thermometers are available as are alcohol wipes. The operator was observed to be hot holding foods at 129 to 134F. Operator eventually increased the temperature of the steam table and then covered the foods. Stem thermometer should be used to monitor the reheating of foods in double boiler to insure 165F benchmark is met. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. There are two deli meats observed in the cookline preparation cooler that are beyond the seven day mark. One is hame from 9/10 and the other is a turkey product from a date in August. It is likely that the August date was an improperly scraped and washed container, however, both foods were discarded. See that dates are correctly marked, food is monitored to be discarded at appropriate time, and cleaning is conducted effectively. 

 (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. There is observed cardboard being used to hold single-service lids in the bar. Cardboard is not an easily cleanable material suitable for washing. Replace the cardboard with a material that is easily washable. Also, the upright freezer holding Butch’s pizzas is observed with an accumulation of frost. See that the unit is defrosted to allow for proper washing of the surface. 


NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. Upon initial entrance to the facility, there was no sani-bucket available. During the inspection a bucket was created for the kitchen. The bar had a bucket available and that bucket was recreated after the first waive of diners left and counters were wiped. The bucket was created using the wall-mounted chemical. Solution was tested at 200ppm Quat.  

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. Observed the interior of nearly every upright cooler in the kitchen and banquet hall to be soiled with spills and/or mold on the gaskets. There is observed spills beneath the two drawers on the bottom of the first cooler in the banquet space. The gaskets of the last cooler are observed thickly coated with mold. The refrigerator within the kitchen is also noted as having some soil related to splash. 


 (B) The non-FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. The employee bathroom does not have a self-closer. Provide a self-closer for this bathroom. 

Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. The ceiling tiles in the dry storage are observed to have water damage. Replace these damaged tiles.

The ceiling in the walk-in cooler is soiled with dust and accumulated soil and should be cleaned. The floor around the triple sink in the kitchen is soiled with accumulated food debris and needs a good detail clean. Finally, the floor around the bar triple sink is littered with bottle caps. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspectors observed no signed employee health reporting agreement present in the facility. The manager of the facility was not present during the inspection, and staff were not knowledgeable of the location of required paperwork. Ensure there is a CFPM present at all times that can direct that can direct inspectors to required documentation. Inspectors provided a blank copy of the employee health reporting agreement to make copies and have all staff members sign employee health reporting agreements. A follow up will be conducted on October 1, 2026 to ensure these forms are signed and available for view.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. During the routine inspection, KS noted that the larger white powder containers were being placed into the dish machine in such a manner as to not allow the interior food contact surface to be in-contact with the sprayer nozzles/heating element of the dish machine. The heat puck thermometer gauge was only getting to a reading of around 150F within these containers. The heat sanitizing was not working within these larger containers not in-contact with the sprayer nozzles. Multiple solutions are offered in the general comments. See that smaller containers are purchased so that proper sanitizing may be completed on these containers. The idea is to find containers that can fit within the dish machine without removing the interior tray AND still be in -contact with the sprayers. 


UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without washing their hands. Education was conducted with the PIC as there was a language barrier in effect with staff. They were instructed to pass along the instructions to staff and ensure that effective hand washing was taking place at all times that it is required in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was observed with a large trash can in front of it, blocking access. The PIC saw this as the inspector walked up to it and moved the trash can to correct and allow access. The situation was discussed and they are aware that the hand sink must remain accessible at all times in the facility to promote good hand washing practices in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

On arrival two knives were observed stored in the gap between the prep coolers. This gap was visibly soiled and could not be considered a clean or safe surface for food contact items. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the items moved to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times in the facility.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Two seperate wiping cloths were observed on the counters throughout the facility. Education was conducted and the PIC moved the cloths to the sani bucket to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all rags used on food contact surfaces are stored between use in a sanitizer solution of sufficient concentration to prevent the growth of pathogenic organisms.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the employee bathroom marked for “ladies” does not have a trash can with a lid. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles for disposal of hygiene products.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. Minimal dust accumulation on the fans in the walk-in cooler. Keep fans clean so soiled air does not move through space/hang over cooling foods. Discussed cleaning beneath the sinks in the preparation room to support elimiation of pests. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT (RTE) FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

A food handler was observed to handled cooked RTE foods as they were moving them to cold holding/cooling. Education was conducted with the PIC and should be trickled down to staff moving forward. Tongs or gloves are needed to handle RTE foods that do not have another kill step prior to service. Ensure that all RTE foods are handled safely at all times in the facility.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Cooked steak was observed in a pan at 120F internal temperatures. The pan is attempting a double boiler style of hot holding but the edges of the pans do not meet. This is allowing the hot air and steam to escape as apposed to being trapped and transferring the heat to the TCS foods. The procedures in place are not allowing for effective hot holding of the foods. Per the PIC the steak was prepared at noon and placed in the hot holding at that time. This puts the four hour limit for foods being out of temperature at 4 pm that afternoon. The PIC was instructed to discard the foods at that time, and they did. A new situation for the hot holding of these foods will need to be put in place moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

A mop was observed stored with the head pooled up in the bottom of the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mop so that it would drip/air dry effectively. Ensure that the mops are stored so that they effectively dry each time in the facility.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

During the inspection several cans were observed with significant dents. The PIC was shown and removed the cans for credit. Ensure that all cans are checked as they are stored or during receiving to ensure that possible Botulism infections are prevented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The nozzles of the soda machines within the facility were observed with soil accumulations. The PIC was made aware. The PIC immediately got a sanitizer bucket with water and brush to clean and sanitize the nozzles. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The fan unit in the walk-in cooler was observed with soil and dust accumulation. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspector that the fan will be cleaned. Ensure that the soil and dust are cleaned to prevent possible contamination of food items.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observe a leakage in the faucet abovethe triple sink. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that this line is repair to prevent it from leaking.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulking on the triple sink be in a state of disrepair. Discussed with the PIC and the PIC ensured inspector that the sink will  be caulked to the wall to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface . Ensure that the sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of grease was observed under the fryers.
2. There were several tiles observed missing under the fryers. The area had been filled with bare concrete that is continuously absorbing the grease and accumulating soil and dust including food debris.
3. An accumulation of ice was observed int he walk-in freezer.
 Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspector that the accumulations will be cleaned and the relevant repairs will be done.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that the handwashing sink in the serving kitchen had no hot water, only cold water (the hot water lever produced no water when turned). CORRECTED: PIC removed the handwashing sink from service and instead re-designated the triple sink in the serving kitchen for handwashing only until the handwashing sink can be repaired. The triple sink does have both hot and cold water. All warewashing of utensils and equipment from the serving kitchen will instead be done in the main kitchen which has adequate equipment for warewashing. Ensure that handwashing sinks are equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 85 F.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop in the main cooking kitchen that was stored in the bottom basin of the mop bucket in water where it cannot properly air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop to the upper basket where the mop can effectively air-dry between uses. Ensure that mops are stored properly so that they can air-dry and not attract pests or mildew.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were still a number of flies observed in the back area by the triple and mop sink. It is recommended to have pest control come more regularly to treat for the flies and to clean the back area to reduce pest harborage conditions. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that the pest presence has been reduced.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine is observed to only be reaching a heat-sanitizing temperature of 122F. The facility has a triple sink that will be used to sanitize the dishes in. A follow up is scheduled for 9/22/2026 to ensure that the dish machine is reaching a heat-sanitizing temperature of at least 160F.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- There is a broken piece of coving observed to the left of the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Ensure that this is repaired. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There are no signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that there are signed employee health reporting agreements in the facility. Ensure that these are always available in the facility for all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer in the triple sink at the bar by the bowling alley was observed to test at 0ppm. CORRECTED- The bottle was almost empty and was replaced. The sanitizer was remade and tested to be at 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizer is regularly checked and changed if not at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There is observed to not be any Chlorine test strips available for the dish machine that uses Chlorine to sanitize dishes. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that Chlorine test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are always test strips available to measure the concentration of each sanitizer that is used in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair:

1. FIRST REPEAT- The bare wood under the main bar across from the pass through windows needs to be sealed or painted. 
2. The spray foam under the dish machine needs to be cut flush and painted or sealed. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
There are no food handler certificates available for any of the staff. Ensure that within 30 days of hire that all employees who handle ice, food, or wash dishes have their food handler certificate. Ensure that these are always available to view at all future inspections. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the ice baffles have an accumulation of soil residues. CORRECTED: PICs were notified and ice machine was immediately removed from service for cleaning. Replacement ice was purchased from an approved source during the inspection. Staff drained, cleaned, and sanitized the ice machine during the inspection and Inspector observed the ice machine to be clean to sight and touch. Ensure ice machine interior is cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the following sanitizing operations were operating with too low sanitizer to be effective at sanitizing dishes:
(i) The triple sink was measured at 100 ppm (quaternary ammonium). CORRECTED: Staff determined that an extra pump of sanitizer shall be added to the triple sink to achieve 200ppm (3 pumps total). Inspector observed that the remade solution measured at an effective sanitizer level of 200ppm (quat). Ensure that the sanitizer concentration of quaternary ammonium is between 200-400ppm for safe and effective sanitizing for dishes.
(ii) The chemical dish machine was measured at less than 50ppm (Chlorine). CORRECTED: PIC were informed that the dish machine was too low for sanitizing and removed the dish machine from service immediately; staff instead would only do dishes in the triple sink instead of the supplementary chemical dish machine. Staff contacted a repair person, who arrived during the inspection and adjusted the dish machine. Inspector observes the repaired dish machine is sanitizing at 50ppm (Chlorine). Ensure that the sanitizer concentration of Chlorine is between 50-200ppm for safe and effective sanitizing for dishes.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B). [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
1ST REPEAT: Observed the following hand sinks to in need of repair:
(i) the hand sink in the hot kitchen appears to be separating from the wall, and there is an accumulation of dust behind it. Ensure this sink is repaired to be sealed to the wall tightly to prevent moisture accumulation between the sink and wall.
(ii) the hand sink in the front bathroom (not under the staircase) is missing sealant between the sink and wall. Silicone sealant will prevent moisture accumulation and microbial growth. 
Inspector and PICs discussed repair options. Ensure both hand sinks are properly sealed to the wall to prevent an accumulation of moisture and soil residues.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed the only hand sink in the kitchen to be obstructed with a pitcher and box of single-service items. The staff were informed that hand sinks must be accessible at all times of food preparation and service. The sink was cleared during the inspection. Ensure this sink remains available at all times to incentivize staff to wash hands regularly.
