citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple cheeses out of date marked and visibly molded. 
1. Sliced Cheddar(date marked July of 2026)
2. Sliced Provolone (date marked August of 2026)
3. Fresh Mozzarella (best by date April of 2026)
4. Shredded Mozzarella (opened and missing date marking)
5. Shredded Lettuce (opened and missing date marking)
All items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking the coolers daily to discard any out of date food items.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspectors observed two knives stored in between the knife storage block and the wall. This crevice is not considered easily cleanable and therefore is not safe for utensil storage. Items were moved during the inspection. Ensure that all cooking utensils are stored in a clean, dry location.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the caulking of the mop sink to be damaged. PIC was made aware and work order has been placed. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained and in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Overall, the PIC failed to perform basic managerial duties within the establishment. There are many priority/priority foundation violations observed during today’s visit. Cold holding temperatures were observed noncompliant. The ambient temperature of the kitchen was roughly 90F due to the air conditioning failing. There is a presence of live (and dead) insects on food and non food contact surfaces, many foods are unlabeled and not date marked, and the cleanliness of the place is lacking. SCDPH will schedule an educational visit in the near future. Discussed active managerial control duties with manager to enforce with staff.
citation_text: 2-102.11(B) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (B) Being a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Throughout the duration of the inspection, no handwashing was observed by any of the food employees. Employees should be washing hands frequently, including when switching tasks, and between each glove switch. Ensure to discuss proper handwashing with all food employees.
citation_text: 3-301.11(A) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wash their hands as specified under § 2-301.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the hand sink within the dish area. Discussed with the PIC and soap was provided to the sink to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always hand soap available at all hand sinks to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was a dead roach observed inside of a salt container stored within the service station. Shown to the PIC and the container was discarded. Ensure that food is protected with coverings and also rotated frequently to be sure that old foods are being used first. Because there is a presence of insect activity, foods and food contact surfaces should always be protected and stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The shelves that stores clean dishes in the dish area contained at least three dead insects on the shelving surface. No insects were observed on the dishes, however, the shelves shall be maintained clean and free of insects. Ensure to remove dishes from shelf to be re-cleaned and also clean shelves before returning dishes. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 to see that shelves have been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Overall, the facility lacks proper date marking. Many time/temperature foods (TCS) were observed without date marking. These items includes cooked meats, rice, sauces, cut melons, etc. Discussed the need to date mark TCS foods that will be held in house longer than 24 hours. Ensure that foods are date marked to be sure that foods are used within the seven day timeframe. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 too see that TCS foods are date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: The facility serves sushi and it appears that there is not a policy in place to control the safety of the sushi rice. There is only a small portion that is prepared at a time, however, the facility doesn’t follow a specific policy for safety reasons of the rice. Rice was observed covered and unlabeled. The PIC indicated that rice is being held on the counter to cool down and will be placed inside of the cooler at night. Discussed the need to either use time control for the rice or acidification. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 to put a plan into action for monitoring the safety of the rice.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The walk in cooler appears to not be functioning properly. Soup and a mayonnaise based sauce were probed at 53F. The hanging thermometers read between 58F-60F. The cooler is storing various foods including cut veggies, meats, soups, sauces, noodles, etc. The PIC mentioned that facility will contact a service technician to fix the cooler tomorrow. Ensure that cooler is adequate enough to maintain temperatures of 41F or below. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 to see that the cooler has been serviced and is holding cold holding temps of 41F or less.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: There was an abundance of foods stored within the facility that lacked proper labeling. Some foods were removed from the original container and could not be easily identified. These foods were stored in many areas of the facility including, inside coolers, on top of counters, in the dry storage area, etc. Ensure to label foods that aren’t visibly recognizable so that they are easily identified.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were at least five live roaches on the floor behind the cookline. The insects observed were fast moving and on the run. Shown to the PIC and she indicated that Orkin usually treats the premise monthly. The most recent receipts were from July 2026. Discussed the need to have pest service more frequent to reduce insect activity. Ensure that the premise is maintained free of roaches. Will follow-up on September 28, 2026 check on insect activity.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of the hood system were observed heavily accumulated with dried grease. The facility contracts Steam Power to service their hood system. Discussed with the PIC that baffles should be cleaned in house in between professional cleanings. Steam power last serviced the hood on May 17, 2026. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The facility overall is completely cluttered. There are various personal items mixed in with items intended for public consumption. These areas include shelves within the dry storage area, walk in units, and the service area. Discussed the need to remove unnecessary items from the premise if nonfunctional or if its doesn’t pertain to the operations of the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The facility could use some deep cleaning. The following areas are as followed: floor and wall behind cook-line line, shelving that stores clean dishes and food, ceilings, floors, and walls throughout the kitchen and dish area. There’s mainly an accumulation of food debris and dried grease on the above mentioned surfaces. Additionally, be sure to especially clean behind cook-line, as this is the area where live roaches were observed. The cove base has also pulled away from the wall behind the cookline. Be sure to reseal cove base back to wall and thoroughly clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The only employee is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) and recently started working at the facility. Ensure that there is always a Certified Food Protection Manager present in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There are observed to be no signed employee reporting agreements available in the facility. This was discussed with the employee and blank copies were provided. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that there are signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. Ensure that once these are signed, that they are always available for all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: The opened milk that the employee stated was opened on Monday was observed to not be date-marked. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that milk should be date-marked and this was dated during the inspection. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods should be date-marked after opening or preparation, with day one being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There is observed to not be a probe thermometer in the facility. There needs to be a probe thermometer to be able to measure the internal temperatures of TCS foods in the fridge. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer available in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: It was observed that there are no signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. The PIC stated that they store them digitally and are working on getting them into a binder to keep at the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that all employees have signed an employee health reporting agreement.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: There is observed to not be a chemical that kills Norovirus available in the facility. The PIC stated that they have bleach on delivery to come tomorrow. A follow up is scheduled for 9/28/2026 to ensure that there is a chemical that kills Norovirus available in the facility in case of a vomit/diarrheal event.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (D) After coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

1) A food handler was observed to don gloves without hand washing. 2) A food handler was observed to drink from a beverage can and not change gloves/ wash hands prior to continuing food service. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to review hand washing procedures and timing with all staff. Ensure that hand washing and glove use is consistently completed in manners that are required by the code.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer ready for use in the C-store kitchen. The PIC was asked about the situation and prepared a solution during the inspection to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer is available in the food preparation areas at all times that foods re being prepared.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were observed to be no signed employee health reporting agreements available at the facility. The PIC stated that they use most of the same employees from their other location and that the signed agreements are currently stored there. Discussed copying the agreements in the binder to make sure they are available at both locations. CORRECTED- All present employees signed an agreement during the inspection and the PIC stated that they will make sure all employees sign one. Ensure that these employee reporting agreements are available at all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

On arrival the ice machine was observed with black slime/mold growth accumulation. The PIC was shown and cleaned the location during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times to prevent possible pathogenic growth/illness.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair:

1. The facility got a new double-door standing cooler and the gaskets are observed to be in disrepair. Discussed replacing the gaskets. 
2. There is ice accumulation on the fan unit of the walk-in freezer. Ensure that the issue causing the ice accumulation is repaired and that the ice is removed. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the 
requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed that the back door was letting in some daylight at the bottom, indicating that the door was not tight-fitting as to protect against the entry of insects. PIC was informed and stated that there was a previous protective piece in place that is no longer there, and will work on getting it replaced by the next routine inspection. Ensure that outer openings of food establishments protect against entry of pests by filling gaps and having tight-fitting exterior doors.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the bathroom hand sink was without a hand drying ability. The inspector moved paper towels from the unused “kitchen” sink to the bathroom sink to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Milk and yogurt were observed in the display coolers with internal temperatures of 46F and 48F. The PIC was shown and instructed to discard the items to correct. The items were discarded during the inspection. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at effective cold holding temperatures at all times that they are in coolers.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The display cooler noted in line item #22 is not effectively holding TCS foods at temperature. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure that it is adjusted/ corrected.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REEPAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sanitizers in the facility did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was consulted and stated that they had changed to a different chemical (Purrell) and mixed it with water as they used to do with bleach. Education was conducted. The Purrell chemical is not a concentrate and should be used as-is out of the bottle for effective sanitizing of food contact surfaces. They were instructed to remake their buckets/bottles to be at effective concentrations. A bucket was made using CL/bleach instead. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times that food handling is taking place in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

On arrival multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine were observed soiled and in need of cleaning. The PIC was shown and cleaned the nozzles during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized regularly to prevent the accumulation of filth and likely contamination of foods in the  facility.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous flies were observed throughout the kitchen and service areas of the facility, particularly around the fountain drink machine. The PIC was shown and discussed. They stated that they tried vinegar and then contacted their pest control for remediation. The inspector will give three weeks for the remedial action to take place prior to following up.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility was using an alcohol based sanitizer (Purrell) and only had test strips effective for testing CL based sanitizers. Education was conducted and the PIC changed the in use sanitizer to a CL based chemical (bleach). This corrects the immediate violation. Ensure that the available sanitizers and test strips match moving forward.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspectors observed there to be multiple food items out of cold holding temperatures in the bottom of the prep cooler closest to the dish area. Probed temperature of cut watermelon 46 degree F, Probed temperature of brisket 50 degrees F, ambient temperature on the internal thermometer of the cooler 50 degree F. These food items had recently been placed in this cooler from the walk in cooler. All items in this cooler were moved to the other cooler on the cook line. Ensure that all cold holding equipment keeps food items at or below 41 degrees Fahrenheit. Follow up has been scheduled for Tuesday, September 29, 2026 to ensure that cooler is keeping food at or below 41 degrees Fahrenheit.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of ice on the floor and ceiling of the walk in freezer. The PIC mentioned a work order will be placed to address this issue. Ensure that the walk in freezer is maintained and free of ice accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: There was an accumulation of ice observed to be on the outside of the walk-in freezer door. The PIC stated that this was due to the door not latching properly. It was also discussed to re-seal the threshold under the walk-in freezer door, as it is coming up and allowing food debris to be trapped under it. Ensure that the issue is repaired and the ice accumulation is removed. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The bottom of the right prep cooler on the cook line. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The green metal shelving inside the walk-in cooler.
3. THIRD REPEAT- The crevices on the front and the outside of chip warmer. Due to this being a third repeat violation, a follow up is scheduled for 9/25/2026 to ensure the chip warmer has been cleaned. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The bottom of the gasket on the left door of the first prep cooler.
5. FIRST REPEAT- The gasket and crevices of the ice cream chest freezer door.

Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There is a dripping leak observed to be coming from the faucet of the handwashing sink in the back of the kitchen. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is a waste water leak coming from the pipes under the front handwashing sink in the kitchen. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 9/18/2026 to ensure that the leak has been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to make sure that sewage is conveyed to the proper point of disposal.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is observed to be coving that is separating from the wall to the right of the walk-in freezer door inside of the walk-in cooler. Ensure that this coving is re-sealed to the wall. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The drain to the left of the dish machine. 
2. SECOND REPEAT- The floor underneath and around the dish machine. There were a few fruit flies observed in this area. Ensure that this area is being cleaned to prevent pest harborage conditions. 
3. Under the soda station in the kitchen.
4. The drain under the back prep area. 
5. The drain under the triple sink in the kitchen. 

Ensure that all physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the interior of the cooler to be soiled with food debris. Ensure this cooler remains clean to sight and touch at all times to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

During the inspection all of the sanitizer buckets were observed to not register quaternary ammonia sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. These buckets were observed changed during the inspection and prior to observation. The inspector then checked the dispenser in the kitchen and did not find evidence of the dispenser correctly dispensing sanitizer on either their test strips or the facility test strips. The PIC was consulted at that point and more investigation conducted. The buckets were remade manually with the concentrate and a call will be put in to the company contracted to manage the dispenser (EcoLab) and maintenance will need to be conducted moving forward.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The dispenser used for sanitizers in the facility was not producing sanitizer at effective concentrations for sanitizing food contact surfaces. A temporary fix was put into place until EcoLab could be contacted and conduct maintenance. A ten day follow-up is being scheduled to allow for this maintenance to be completed.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizing bleach to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer was purchased from a nearby Dollar General. Sanitizer solution was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed one adult and one juvenile roach in the kitchen near the fryers and wok grill. Both pests were under or within equipment and not on food-contact surfaces. Orkin treated for pests yesterday, September 10, 2026. Orkin will continue to treat weekly for the next five weeks. Continue cleaning efforts in the kitchen to limit the pest’s food availability. Ensure all food containers are tightly sealed when not in use. Remove all unnecessary cardboard from the facility, as it acts as a food source and area of harborage. Ensure staff are NEVER using their own chemical to treat for pests. Only licensed, professional pest control operators are spraying chemical in the facility. A 30-day follow-up will be conducted on October 9, 2026 to ensure pest presence continues to improve in the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available on site while foods were being handled and prepared. The facility manager (who had a CFPM) arrived during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. A hand out was given to them with the known current available CFPM courses. Ensure that there is a CFPM available at all times that foods are being prepared in the facility.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide proof that staff was notified in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report reportable symptoms and diagnosis. A fresh copy will be sent to the PIC via email later the same as the inspection. The PIC was instructed to have signed copies available prior to the scheduled follow-up.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. 

Cases of paper bowls were observed on the floor behind the door in the kitchen. The PIC was shown and instructed to stored all food contact surfaces off of the floor moving forward. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored off of the floor at all times in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The new shelf in the kitchen was observed to have exposed particle board on the edges. The PIC was shown and instructed to seal prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspectors observed there to be no quaternary ammonia test strips available in the facility. PIC stated they expired recently and had not replaced them yet. Ensure that test strips are available for all sanitizers used in the facility at all times to check chemical concentrations. Follow up scheduled for Monday, September 28, 2026.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink at the bar was observed to be out of hand soap. CORRECTED- The PIC replaced the soap in the dispenser. Ensure that all handwashing sinks have a supply of soap at them to allow for proper handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- There was observed to be raw steak in a grocery bag in the bottom of a preparation cooler and chopped peppers in a grocery bag in the chest freezer. CORRECTED- These items were moved into other containers and this was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that grocery bags are NEVER used to directly store food in. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and cannot be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized to store food in.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was observed to be a gallon of milk that did not have date-marking on it. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they opened it two days ago and date-marked it during the inspection. Ensure that TCS foods that are opened or prepared in house and kept for over 24 hours are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The bar triple sink’s faucet is observed to be completely off. The PIC stated that it happened a couple of days ago and that they plan to repair it. The facility has the triple sink and dish machine in the kitchen that they can use to clean the bar dishes. Ensure that the faucet is replaced and that plumbing is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was observed to be a trash can in front of the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The trash can was moved to another location and this was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that the handwashing sink is always maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.

1. Walk in cooler fan covers.
2. Walk in cooler shelves.
3. Gaskets of the double door freezer closest to the kitchen.

Kitchen

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspectors observed there to be no certified food production manager (CFPM) who has their allergen awareness training on site during the inspection. The PIC stated they are in the process of obtaining their certificate. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs with their allergen awareness training to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

CORRECTED - the PIC placed a new roll of paper towels in the dispenser that stocks this handwashing sink with paper towels. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are stocked with paper towels or another hand drying device at all times during operation and food preparation.

Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed 6 cans in the back dry storage with severe dents along the seams (top/bottom) and sides. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the cans. PIC and Inspector discussed what types of dents to look for that should indicate a can should be rejected: major dents on the seams (top, bottom, side seam), and severe dents that indicate crushing or formation of sharp points. Ensure that cans that are received dented are rejected. Cans that are damaged during service can be used if repackaged immediately.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed ground beef stored over whole beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC had staff move the whole beef above the ground beef, following proper storage order by final cooking temperature. Ensure food is stored with ready-to-eat foods on top (no additional cooking required), followed by raw animal proteins that require cooking on the bottom. For animal proteins, the higher shelf would include fish and eggs (135-145 F final cooking temperature), stored over whole intact beef and pork (145 F), stored over ground “comminuted” beef and pork (155 F), stored over chicken and poultry of any kind on the bottom shelf (165 F). Foods with different final cooking temperatures can be stored side-by-side as long as they are in protective packaging that keeps them separate.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that the dish machine was tested at less than 50ppm (Chlorine). CORRECTED: The machine was cycled several times and still tested below 50ppm. A service technician was contacted during the visit. The machine was later adjusted and tested at 50ppm (Chlorine) to correct the violation. Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly, at least 50ppm.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed ice accumulation in the walk-in freezer (Freezer 1). This ice accumulation is contacting bagged vegetables stored on the top shelf in the walk-in. The head of maintenance was present during the inspection and stated that Henson Robinson has performed maintenance on the freezer in the last four weeks. There was thermal tape and insulation foam present on the leaking lines. It seems these fixes are inadequate to prevent leakage onto food and food contact surfaces. The staff were instructed to move the vegetables stored directly below the leaking lines to a dry location and keep a container under the lines to capture the water. Ensure food is stored in clean, dry locations at all times to prevent contamination. The freezer requires maintenance prior to the next routine inspection.

citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. title: Food handler training
comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed that the sanitizing solution (quaternary ammonium) in the sanitizer buckets was too low to effectively sanitize food-contact surfaces (100ppm). 
* The sanitizing solution is sourced from the triple sink sanitizing hose. The solution from the hose was at the lowest concentration that still effectively sanitizes (200ppm for quaternary ammonium). Because sanitizer can evaporate and deactivate over time, that indicates that the sanitizer buckets cannot maintain effective sanitizing concentration, as they were less than 1 hour old and already at a too low concentration.
* Inspector also observed that the water from the hose is hot, measuring at 124 F on a probe thermometer. Quaternary ammonium solutions should be used at room temperature water (75 F) per manufacturers instructions, as high temperatures can inactivate the sanitizer. Cold water is available at all facility faucets otherwise.
CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and will contact maintenance about the sanitizer hose temperature issue. PIC will cease using the sanitizing hose to fill sanitizer buckets until it is again providing proper concentrations for quaternary ammonium (200-400ppm). PIC remade the sanitizer buckets, this time using available bleach (Chlorine, effective concentration is 50-200ppm), which tested at 100ppm and 150ppm using facility’s test strips.
* PIC has quaternary ammonium tablets for the triple sink, and has sufficient test strips to check concentrations. 
* Most dishes are sanitized using the stationary rack dish machine (heat), which reaches effective sanitizing temperatures of 165 F.
Ensure sanitizing solutions are at safe and effective sanitizing concentrations for food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors EJ and AD observed multiple live cockroaches present under the wok grill near the service line in the kitchen. All roaches observed were fast moving. Pests were observed on top of and underneath the wok grill, on the spice cart containing open spice and sauce containers, annd within a cardboard box containing fried rice noodles. Inspectors strongly recommend placing glue traps around the facility for pest monitoring. Staff should NEVER be spraying their own chemical in the kitchen for pest control. The only sprays used in the facility should be administered by authorized pest control professionals only. Due to the presence of pests on food-contact surfaces, the facility will voluntarily close today to conduct a deep cleaning. The facility can open again tomorrow, September 10th pending pest control treatment and authorization from the public health inspector.
