comment: Observed that the hot box in the kitchen was not hot holding recently cooked food at 135 F and above: marinara was probed at 130 F and green beans were probed at 125 F. CORRECTED: PIC took all containers back to the oven and stove to reheat them above 165 F and determined that the hot box needed to be turned up higher. Temperatures were remeasured at 151 F (marinara) and 153 F (green beans) and the ambient air temperature of the hot box was measurably hot. Ensure that cooked food items are hot held at internal temperatures of 135 F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed that a spray bottle with degreaser solution was unlabeled. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the spray bottle was labeled immediately. Ensure that all chemicals that are in working containers be labeled to prevent food or surface contamination or improper use.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed several single-use containers and single-service articles stored upright where the food-contact surfaces were exposed to contamination from falling debris. CORRECTED: PIC had all items either inverted or placed under a shelf where they would be protected. Ensure all single-service and single-use articles and utensils are protected from contamination during storage, either through a protective container, inversion, or an upper barrier.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed the underside of the shelf above the steam table has accumulated debris from old food splashes. The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean it later and add it to the regular cleaning schedule. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are maintained clean of food residues.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the ice machine baffles to have visible mold accumulation. PIC was informed that these baffles directly contact ice, which poses a cross-contamination concern. A follow-up will be conducted on September 14, 2026 to ensure the ice machine has been deep cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There were no hanging thermometers present in all the cooling units. The PIC was informed that these devices are important in measuring and acquiring real time temperature in the units. The PIC told inspector that the thermometer will be ordered and placed in the various units respectively. Ensure that the thermometers are provided and placed within the units as discussed.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed employee personal food stored amongst other food items within the standing cooler on the right side of the fryers. Education was provided and the food items in question were tossed. Ensure that there is a designated area for employees in the cooling unit (s) to avoid possible cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed a leak in the plumbing of the sink compartments at the bar. A discussion about the sink was held and PIC informed inspector that these leak was previously fixed however, the leakage resumed. Hence, there is a work order for another technician to repair the sink. Ensure that the relevant plumbing repairs are done to be in compliance with the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: An accumulation of grease and food debris was observed underneath the grill and the fryers. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the mop bucket filled with used mop water in the utility sink. Discussed with the PIC. PIC told inspector that the water was from mopping the bathroom. The used mop water was discarded. Ensure that the water is disposed properly after mopping at all times.
citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several fruit/drain flies were observed in the facility during the inspection. At the time of the inspection a large amount of the flies were observed in the dry storage room specifically around the mops and dump sink. The violation is NOT considered corrected at the time of the inspection and the PIC is instructed to contact their pest control again for remedial action. The follow-up is being scheduled for one month to allow for remedial action to take effect.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

A partially used gallon of milk was observed in the front area standing cooler with a date placed on it of 8/25. This was a date 10 days prior to the date of observation. When discussed, the PIC indicated that the observed date was the day that the milk was brought into the facility and that the container had only been opened the Tuesday prior (four days prior to the inspection). Education was conducted. The date needed for seven day date marking is the day in which the container was opened. If there are other policies in play at the facility level this is acceptable, but they must be in addition to the seven day date marking required by the code. A date was added for Tuesday to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the date marking policies include those required by the code in the facility.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

On arrival several cases of to-go containers were observed on the floor in the back of the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC a they were instructed to stored these items off of the floor (at least six inches) prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning a new pair of gloves.The employee carried out multiple tasks; one of which involved the handling of raw meat. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Ensure employees always wash their hands prior to donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed a container filled with raw cut steak being stored over raw fish in the second prep cooler. The PIC was made aware. The items in question were rearranged to correct the storage order. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed at all times.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Two sani buckets (one in the kitchen and one at the bar) were observed with a quaternary ammonia sanitizer concentration reading between 100 ppm to 0 ppm. The staff were instructed to remake the sanitizer buckets. The buckets were remade and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that the concentration of sanitizers are routinely checked to ensure proper sanitation for food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil buildup in the dish machine. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspectors that the dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure that the accumulated soil buildup is cleaned and the dish machine is maintained cleaned to sight of touch at all times.
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There were no hanging thermometers available in the bottom of the two prep coolers in the kitchen. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspectors that the relevant temperature measuring devices will be provided. Ensure that there is at least one thermometer inside each cooling unit at all times.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed knives to be stored in the gap between two prep coolers. This space is not considered easily cleanable and is therefore not adequate for utensil storage. The knives were sent to dish during the inspection. Inspector recommends a magnetic strip or alternative knife storage.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: A jug of milk was observed not properly date marked in the standing cooler closest to the dish room in the kitchen. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC told inspectors that the jug was opened on Tuesday (9/1/2026). Education was provided. The jug of milk was dated. Ensure that all food items are date marked appropriately at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: The trash bin in the employee bathroom was observed without a lid. The bathroom is a unisex facility. The PIC was made aware. The PIC replaced the trash bin with a covered bin. Ensure that the bin in any unisex bathroom/facility has a lid.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The coving on the left and back walls in the storage room by the stove was observed missing. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspectors that the relevant repairs would be done. Ensure that the coving is installed sealing the walls and preventing pest entry.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed walk in freezer to have ice accumulation to be present under fan unit. Discussed with PIC, freezer will be serviced. Ensure equipment is working at manufactures level.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that a sanitizer bucket in the meat department was not registering levels of quaternary ammonium (0ppm). PIC investigated and found that the source of the sanitizing solution, a hose dispenser from the meat department triple sink, was using hot water, which deactivates the sanitizer in the solution. PIC determined that there was a plumbing issue that was causing hot water to come out of the dispenser without an option to make it cold. A plumber was contacted and arrived during the inspection. In the meantime, the meat department will source its sanitizing solution for surfaces and warewashing from the working sanitizer dispenser from the triple sink in the neighboring deli department. The new sanitizer bucket measured at 200pm for quaternary ammonium. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions are sanitizing at safe and effective concentrations, which is between 200-400ppm for quaternary ammonium, and that sanitizing solutions are created per manufacturer’s instructions.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed that the rotisserie chicken in the display warmer was hot holding at a temperature of 108 F, below the necessary 135 F. CORRECTED: PIC investigated and noted that the warming unit was turned off but the lights were turned on. PIC voluntarily discarded all rotisserie chickens that were in the display warmer. Ensure that foods that are hot held are kept at temperatures 135 F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed an accumulation of dust and soil residues on nonfood-contact surfaces that could potentially contaminate food-contact surfaces:
(i) the walls and floors in the dry goods storage in the deli department in the back room near the stairs.
(ii) the ceiling ventilation in the meat department.
(iii) the caulking behind the triple sinks.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the stalls in the women’s restroom did not have covered receptacles for sanitary napkins et. al. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have covered trash receptacles for hygiene purposes and to prevent feminine hygiene products from being disposed of in the toilets.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that 3 mops in the dish area of the deli department were not air-drying properly, siting on top of a hard surface that was not the mop sink where they cannot air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mops so that they can air-dry and drain above the mop sink. PIC also instructed staff to discard an older mop head that was not attached to a mop that had been in the same area. Ensure that mops are allowed to air-dry in a location where they cannot contaminate walls, equipment or supplies.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

Several employees were observed to don gloves without prior hand washing. Education was conducted to correct the situation and the PICs were instructed to ensure that all staff are washing their hands at all times that it is required.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

On arrival the ice scoop for the kitchen fountain drink machine was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would allow for bare hand contact of the Ready-To-Eat food (ice) when it is acquired for drinks. The PIC was shown and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that all utensils are stored so that the foods they are used for are protected from contamination from bare hand contact.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was without paper towels or another approved hand drying system. The PIC was shown and replaced the paper towels to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sanitizer bucket in the bar area was observed with a concentration of approximately 10 ppm CL during the inspection. The PIC was shown and asked when the bucket was made. They stated approximately 2:00 (45 minutes prior to observation). The bucket was brought into compliance at 200 ppm CL to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers in the facility are maintained at effective concentrations at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Numerous TCS foods in the walk in cooler were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-51F. The PIC was shown and discarded the items to correct the immediate violation. Items discarded during this inspection include: 1) multiple buckets of salsa, 2) two half pans of chicken breasts, 3) three full pans of beef strips, 4) one pan of ground beef, 5) half of a full pan of sliced tomatoes, 6) a half pan of shrimp, 7) one, five gallon bucket of chopped lettuce, 8) 1.5 gallons of milk, 9) six half pans of queso, 10) one case of whipped topping, 11) one carton of heavy whipping cream, 12) two pans of marinated chicken, 13) one mostly consumed pan of pork, 14) one pan of Beria beef and 15) one case of American cheese. The cooler itself is being placed onto the line item #33 violation for follow-up. The facility was instructed not to use this cooler until effective cold holding temperatures could be maintained.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler for this facility was observed with ambient air temperatures of approximately 50F-51F. The TCS foods were discarded (refer to line item #22). This violation is for the cooler not functioning correctly. Another manager from another facility arrived and helped translate, while also instructing them to leave the walk in freezer door open to help in the short term. The PIC was instructed to have the walk in cooler repaired and functioning correctly prior to the scheduled follow up on 9/14/26.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A moist cloth was observed on top of the counter in the back prep area of the facility. This rag should be stored between uses in the relevant bucket of sanitizer to prevent pathogenic replication from taking place. The PIC was consulted and had the rag moved to correct.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple knives were observed on the left most knife rack in the back prep area with brown lines on the blades. Investigation showed that the lines were from the magnetic rack that the knives were attached to. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The knives and rack were cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored in such a way as to be maintained clean prior to use.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A thick accumulation of frost and ice was observed in the walk in freezer on the shelves and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation moving forward. This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

A food handler was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted to correct. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Cardboard cases of cereal packages was observed on the floor in the dry storage room. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the cases picked up onto shelves to correct. Ensure that all foods and food contact containers are stored off of the floor to prevent possible contamination concerns.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. 

The facility had a lactic acid based sanitizer available for use and only quat based test strips in the facility. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to have test strips that match their sanitizer prior to the scheduled follow-up. Ensure that all food contact chemical concentrations can be verified as correct at all times in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed liquid eggs stored above butter packets and juice containers. CORRECTED: PIC and staff were notified, and the liquid eggs were moved to the bottom shelf below the ready-to-eat food. Ensure that raw animal products, including raw meat and raw egg products, are stored below RTE foods to prevent contamination from drips from above, as RTE foods are not cooked unlike the raw animal products.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The dispensers of the soda machine under the nozzles were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned the dispensers during the inspection. Ensure that staff are educated to clean both the nozzles and the dispensers of the soda machine. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The following TCS food items in the open-air cooler were observed to be above 41F: 

1. 26 packages of cheese and salami that probed to be between 48F and 55F. 
2. A chicken sandwich probed to be at 47F. 
3. A steak burrito probed to be at 52F. 
4. A chicken burrito probed to be at 49F. 
5. Two lunchables probed to be at 49F and 51F. 
6. Five egg and cheese protein packs probed to be between 46F and 55F. 
7. A bacon cheeseburger probed to be at 50F. 
8. A BBQ rib sandwich probed to be at 44F and 47F. 
9. A cheeseburger probed to be at 51F. 
10. Three jalapeño chicken sandwiches probed to be at 47F, 50F, and 51F. 
11. A country fried chicken sandwich probed to be at 52F. 
12. A pack of smoked ham and Swiss sliders probed to be at 46F. 
13. Two Italian style pinwheels probed to be at 48F and 54F. 
14. An Italian sandwich probed to be at 51F. 
15. A breakfast Stromboli probed to be at 50F. 
16. Two buffalo chicken wraps probed to be at 45F and 48F. 
17. Seven ham and cheese sandwiches that probed to be between 46F and 51F. 
18. Four turkey and cheese sandwiches that probed to be between 45F and 53F. 
19. Four packages of turkey and cheese sliders that probed to be between 47F and 53F. 

CORRECTED- The TCS food items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. It was discussed to minimally stock items in the cooler on extremely hot days and to check the temperatures of the food items regularly. Open-air coolers need to be stocked less and to have non-TCS foods on the corners to ensure that they are able to be properly cold held. Ensure that TCS foods are being cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to have an accumulation of dust on them and are in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The walk-in cooler fan covers. 
2. The walk-in cooler shelves. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed the prep cooler by the service counter to be holding time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above 41F. The TCS foods stored in the cooler are listed below:
1. Ranch dressing (75F, probe)
2. Sriracha mayonnaise
3. Chipotle mayonnaise
4. Cut tomatoes (64F, probe)
5. Cheese (62F, probe)

All TCS foods in the cooler were stored there overnight. The staff were unable to provide a log of recorded temperature checks to confirm when the temperature in the cooler rose above 41F. All food items listed above were voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the prep cooler by the service line fail to hold TCS foods at 41F or lower. The PIC stated that the cooler has been serviced recently. The ambient temperature of the kitchen was greater than 90F, with outdoor temperatures nearing 100F. Staff will use ice baths to hold TCS foods lower than 41F until the cooler is confirmed to be functioning. If the outdoor temperatures drop and the cooler is still not functioning, service will be required before the cooler can be returned to normal function. A follow-up will be conducted on September 7, 2026 to ensure the cooler is functioning properly.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed multiple flies present in the kitchen during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that pest control professionals are routinely spraying the facility for pests, but the flies persist. The inspector recommends sealing any exterior openings, adding air curtains to exterior doors to prevent pests entering during food deliveries, and continuing pest control treatments on the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on October 2, 2026 to ensure the facility is free of pests.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of the prep cooler and interior of the microwave to be soiled with debris. The PIC was informed that non-food contact surfaces are required to remain clean to sight and touch at all times. Ensure staff are cleaning and sanitizing these surfaces frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed multiple cooler units to be 49F. Discussed with PIC, coolers include WIC, the prep cooler to its left, and the standing cooler to the right. Items from the right cooler were actively cooling, wings and meatballs were moved back to walk in freezer. Items in the walk in cooler were probed and ran a temperature of 50F. Items included pizza sauce and pasta, items were discarded. The prep cooler later tested at 41F. Inspector will follow up on 9/4/26. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F. 

During inspection, Bormida arrived to service coolers. Inspector observed ambient air temperature to begin to drop, inspector will spot check facility on 9/3/26 if completely serviced.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the top of kitchen microwave to be soiled with food splash. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure facility is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food splash/debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspector observed one live, fast-moving juvenile cockroach near the back door of the facility.

The inspector recommends placing dated glue traps throughout the facility to track pest movement. Tracking is useful to better inform your pest control professional of pest location and number. An additional follow-up will be conducted on September 30, 2026 to monitor progress.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket inside of the kitchen area contained bleach, detergent, and degreaser. Discussed with the PIC that sanitizer solutions should only include bleach and water. The solution was remade and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The PIC was unable to show in a verifiable manner that employees are notified of their responsibility to report the reportable symptoms and diagnosis related to foodborne illnesses. A blank copy of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement given to the facility at the pre-opening was discovered in the facility binder. The PIC was instructed to make copies and have the three stated employees sign it prior the scheduled follow up.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A); or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

A partially used container of sour cream was observed with a date marking of 8/17. This puts the time since opening at 17 days at the time of the inspection. The PIC was shown and discarded the container to correct. The sour cream in the prep cooler was stated as likely being the same batch and did not have a separate date marking during the inspection. It was also discarded during the inspection. Education was conducted. Ensure that any TCS foods are properly date marked and discarded at the end of day seven since opening in the facility.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Observed that the facility did not have sufficient materials to respond to vomiting or diarrheal events - there was not bleach available to make a disinfecting solution, nor was there a bodily fluid cleanup kit. Ensure that the facility can properly disinfect in the event of a bodily fluid contamination event.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of grease and residues on several interior walls of the kitchen. Nonfood-contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following equipment that is in need of repair or replacement:
(i) The paper towel dispenser in the employee bathroom was not functioning; rolls of paper towels are available on the chemical storage shelf and the dispenser does have paper towels inside of it. The dispenser should be repaired so that employees have better access to paper towels for handwashing.
(ii) The triple sink caulking needs to be repaired, as it is deteriorating and there is an accumulation of soil residues. Repair the caulking so that the area behind the triple sink is sealed and cleanable.
(iii) A ceiling tile above the hot boxes has visible water damage. Replace the ceiling tile, and prevent additional water damage. 
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
3RD REPEAT: Employees working at the time of the inspection could not show proof of food handler certificates. All employees that handle food and are not food manager certified will need to obtain a food handler certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the middle sinks in the men and women bathrooms were observed to be in disrepair. Discussed with the PIC. The PIC assured inspectors that the caulking will be done either today or within a couple days. Ensure that closed spaces such as the space between the sinks and the wall is caulk and properly sealed to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed unwrapped straws on top of the bar for customer self-service, where customers would be able to barehand all the unwrapped straws. CORRECTED: PIC moved straws behind the bar where they will only be handled by gloved staff. Ensure that people are not touching ready-to-eat food or food-contact surfaces with barehands by using barriers (gloves, wrappers, deli tissue).
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed shell eggs stored above milk and lettuce. CORRECTED: PIC moved eggs onto lower shelf so they are no longer above RTE foods preventing contamination. Ensure that raw animal proteins are stored below RTE foods, which are not being cooked any further.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw shell eggs stored above ready-to-eat foods (string cheese and PB&J sandwiches) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the eggs were moved to a separate shelf where they were not above RTE food. Ensure that raw animal products (eggs and meat) are stored below RTE food (prepared produce, deli meat, cheese, beverages).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed that the ventilation system above the heat dish machine was not functioning, causing excessive steam and heat to accumulate in the dish area. Staff have placed floor fans to ventilate the area, as clean dishes take significant time to air-dry because of the excessive humidity caused by the non-functioning ventilation system. Repair the ventilation system by the next routine inspection to ensure that the ventilation hood system is sufficient in capacity to prevent condensation from collecting on equipment.
citation_text: 4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

A can was observed with major dents in the side and seams while it was intermixed with other cans on the shelf. The PIC was shown and moved the item to discard to correct. Ensure that the integrity of food packaging is maintained intact and safe at all times in the facility. Also ensure that any incoming foods are screened to ensure that the packaging and safety of the foods are maintained.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector in the ice machine in the kitchen was observed with off white and pink pathogenic slime growth. Some was wiped off with a paper towel and the PIC shown. They were instructed to clean/sanitize the item and maintain it clean moving forward. They wiped it with a sani rag during the inspection to correct the immediate violation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The fan over to the unit in the walk in cooler was observed with dust accumulation significant enough that pieces appeared read to fly off and potentially contaminate foods in the cooler. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The kitchen’s sanitizer bucket was tested at 0ppm (quat). The sani solution was recreated and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that all sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer's recommended concentration to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The gasket along the outdoor freezer is starting to tear. The PIC mentioned that new gaskets have been ordered to replace the current ones. Temperatures were observed compliant, however, be aware that the gasket will container to tear overtime. Ensure that gasket is replaced.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener was observed with dry debris contaminating it. The PIC was shown and moved the item to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a ready-for-use sanitizer (sani bucket) in the kitchen areas. When asked a bucket was produce at effective concentration for the kitchen that corrected the immediate violation. Ensure that a ready-for use sanitizer is available at all times that the facility is handling or preparing foods and food contact surfaces.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The CFPMs available for the facility had not completed the required allergen training at the time of the inspection. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to have the required training completed and the certificates available prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection was without a CFPM certificate available. When asked no-one else that was currently in the facility had the certification either. The PIC stated that someone that works in the facility was able to teach the class and he was planning on taking it for moving forward. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts in which foods are being handled/prepared.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Two cans were observed with significant dents in the storage rack in the dry storage room. The cans were shown to the PIC and education conducted. The cans were then moved for discard/credit during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all cans with significant dents are put aside so that they are not used and potential Botulism infections prevented.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed ice and cut fruit to be in bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sink is being used solely for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed bar dish machine to test at 0ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, the dish machine was primed and was observed to test at 100 ppm. Ensure sanitizing dish machines are testing at 100ppm to ensure dishes are being properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past 7 date marking maximum. Items included pie, noodles, sauces, and deli meats. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were discarded. Ensure any TCS item held longer than 7 days is discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed ice accumulation to be present at the snack bar walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure equipment is working at a level that meets the manufactures standard.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to resting on the floor in mop sink. Discussed with PIC, mop was placed in mop hanging station. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed current CFM to not have allergen training completed. Discussed with PIC, allergen training will be completed. Ensure the required allergen training is completed by all CFM’s. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink in the kitchen. Education was conducted with staff regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are using a paper towel to turn off the faucet to prevent contamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw pork brats to be stored above ready-to-eat pepperoni and raw fish in the walk-in cooler. Education was conducted regarding proper storage order, and the items were rearranged. Ensure proper storage order guidelines are followed to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: It was observed that there is not any allergen labeling on items throughout the breakfast buffet. According to the 2022 FDA Food Code, there needs to be allergen labeling on all buffet food items or bulk food items that are available for consumer self-service. Every food item on the buffet is labeled with the name of the food. If the allergen is not in the name of the food, the allergen needs to be listed for consumers to be aware of. This can be accomplished through a poster, on each individual item or display case, or as a QR code. Ensure that all buffet foods are labeled with the major allergens they contain by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed food handlers licenses to not be available for some staff members. Discussed with PIC, steps will be taken to certify remaining staff. Ensure any food handling employee has the required food handlers license. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Repeat Violation
citation_text:
6-501.111 EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments. Two live adults were observed under counters in the cook line and service line. One adult was observed fast-moving under the left side of the cook line. The other adult was observed live on a glue trap under a service line counter. The right side of the cook line near the grill and fryers used to be the focal point of pest presence, but no pests were observed in this area today. Glue traps were observed placed throughout the cook line and service line. SCDPH will continue to follow-up until no pests are observed. This means keeping the glue traps present as a monitoring tool and insuring treatment is curtailing life cycles. The next follow-up is scheduled for September 28, 2026. 

 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

A can of mushrooms was observed in the bottom of the prep cooler opened and with a moldy layer observed on the top of the foods. The PIC was shown and threw away the foods to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored in such a way so as to protect them from contamination. They should also be used prior to the point that pathogenic organisms begin to grow in the containers.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw beef and raw chicken were observed over raw shrimp in the standing cooler between the mop sink and hallway. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the shrimp moved to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored according to their cooking temperatures in the facility so as to ensure that the safety of the customers is maintained.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani bucket would not register the CL sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. When asked the PIC indicated that the sanitizer was made in the morning. The inspector stated that the chemical breaks down even if no use is taking place and quicker with use. The bucket needs to be remade regularly throughout the day so as to remain at effective concentration to reduce biological contamination concerns on the surfaces. The bucket was remade to correct.
