citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed a bag of guacamole to be stored in a container of cut tomatoes. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage of items and tomatoes were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available at meat department. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure each department has an sanitizer solution available during lol hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed black mold to be present at the back triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents black mold build up.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to grab cooked bacon before being added to a serving plate. The activity was ceased and corrected. The employee discarded the bacon and made sure to use gloves when handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. Ensure that RTE foods are handled with either utensils or gloved hands.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The employee bathroom lacked paper towel for handwashing. Discussed with the PIC and paper towels were provided to the handsink. Ensure that all handsinks are equipped with running warm water, hand soap, and paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed effectively.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The scoop used for ice in the bar area was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This would require an employee to touch the ice with their bare hand to acquire the scoop and use it. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review with staff to correct. Prevent all bare hand contact with ready to eat foods (ice in this case) in order to prevent possible contamination vectors.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

Someone was observed to pour and rinse out a cup in the hand sink in the kitchen area. The situation was discussed with the PIC to correct. Ensure that the hand washing sinks are not used for purposes other than hand washing at any time in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The lemonade nozzle, hibiscus refresher nozzle, pineapple refresher nozzle, and horchata nozzle were all observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in them. CORRECTED- These nozzles were cleaned during the inspection and it was discussed with the PIC to frequently clean drink nozzles. Ensure that nozzles are being regularly cleaned to maintain them clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There are no ambient thermometers observed in the hot holding display cases. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there are ambient thermometers in all hot and cold holding units.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There are cases of water bottles that are being stored outside in front of the facility. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that the cases of water bottles are stored inside of the facility to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The bottom of the preparation cooler in the kitchen. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The kitchen walk-in cooler fan covers. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- Inside of the cabinets under the coffee machines. 
4. The floor under and behind the soda syrups in the back room. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handwashing sink in the kitchen and the triple sink are observed to be in need of being re-sealed to the wall. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with black microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to hire a professional to clean the interior of the machine. A follow-up will be conducted on September 4, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch. 

Inspector also observed the nozzles of the soda machine at the server station to be soiled with black debris. The PIC stated the Pepsi advised against using sanitizer or soaking the nozzles overnight. Education was conducted regarding the requirement for all food-contact surfaces to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized routinely. The nozzles were replaced during the inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to wash their hands, then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. CORRECTED- The employee was educated to use a paper towel to turn off the faucet to avoid recontaminating their freshly washed hands. Ensure that employees are educated on the proper handwashing procedure to prevent contamination to food.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to have a concentration of 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at a concentration of 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and remade if not at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were two alive roaches observed during the inspection, one by the wraps on the bottom of the cook-line and one on the wall behind the alto-shaams across from the cook-line. There were approximately 8 to 10 dead roaches observed throughout the facility. These alive and dead roaches were of varying life stages. The facility currently has Sentinel Pest Control coming weekly. There were no notes available from the pest control company. The facility has improved on cleaning and is continuing to work on it. The PIC also stated that they are working on getting rid of cardboard throughout the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 9/23/2026 to ensure that the facility is taking the appropriate measures to reduce pest presence in the facility, including but not limited to, cleaning, pest control, getting rid of cardboard, and cleaning up dead roaches. Ensure that the appropriate actions are being taken to reduce pest presence and clean the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: On arrival the facility did not have signed copies of the reporting agreements for the staff in the unit. Copies were signed during this inspection to correct.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: On arrival the hand sink (and the entire unit) was without paper towels. Paper towels were brought to the unit to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Bowls and baskets stored along the cookline were observed with the food contact surface faced upward. Discussed with the PIC and items were inverted to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are stored in a manner that doesn’t expose the food contact surface to contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Both soda gun nozzles in the bar area were observed soiled with dried liquids. Additionally, the rubber gun holders were also observed soiled. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nozzles and gun holders are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed TCS foods not being cold held below 41 F in a broken prep cooler. CORRECTED: PIC and staff discarded TCS food items that were inside the prep cooler if they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago, and TCS items prepared under 4 hours were moved to a working cooler. This cooler cannot be used for service unless it is repaired (see Violation #33) or a Time as Control Policy is created and used. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed that the prep cooler on the far end of the kitchen by the office was still observed not keeping the appropriate temperature range. The average temperature within the cooler using the infrared thermometer was 55F. Temperatures obtained by probing was 45F. PICs previously told Inspector that the unit will be repaired accordingly, but per PICs they are still waiting on a part. Cease using the prep cooler for cold holding until it is repaired. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done enabling the unit to have the appropriate temperature capacity.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The bar dish machine is observed to be testing at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that staff are using the triple sink at the bar to wash, rinse, and sanitize until the dish machine has been serviced. A follow up is scheduled for 8/18/2026 to ensure that the bar dish machine is properly sanitizing at a label-recommended concentration of Chlorine.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no hot water to be available at hand sink. Discussed with PIC, hot water will be serviced. Ensure hot water is available at all times.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed walk in cooler to have an ambient temperature of 45F-47F. Discussed with PIC, walk in cooler was observed to be set at 50F. Setting was dropped down to 40F. Inspector will follow up  Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F. 

Later during inspection, walk in cooler was observed to have dropped to 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw chicken was observed being stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the chicken to be stored appropriately. Ensure that the proper storage order procedure is followed to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed three containers of tomato sauce with a label “Use First” without their production dates. The PIC was made aware. The PIC told inspector that the sauces were made a couple days before. Education was provided. The respective dates were added to teh containers immediately. Ensure that date marking guidelines are followed to the letter at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection did not have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) completed and available. They were instructed to have enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda gun in the bar area was observed with mold growth in the holes and around the inner rim of the nozzle. The bar manager was shown and education conducted. This item counts as a food contact surface and needs to be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) regularly to prevent pathogenic growth from accumulating. The item was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

A gallon of milk in the walk in cooler was observed partially consumed and without a date marking. When asked the PIC indicated that it was opened a couple days prior. Education was conducted and a date marking added to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are correctly date marked at all times in the facility.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were multiple alive and dead roaches observed throughout the facility, including but not limited to, one alive roach on the cook-line, one dead in the bottom of the preparation cooler, one on a shelf of the cook-line, one dead and one alive on the bread rack, two alive on the wall behind the shake machine, and one alive in the cabinets under the soda machines in the lobby. These roaches were of different life stages and they were all fast-moving. According to the PIC, Sentinel, the facility’s pest control company, is currently coming every two weeks. The last receipt available was 7/16/2026 and there were no notes available from the pest control company. A follow up is scheduled for 8/18/2026 to ensure that the facility is taking the appropriate actions to reduce pest presence, including but not limited to, removing cardboard from the facility, using glue traps to monitor pest presence (no glue traps were observed), having pest control treat the facility, and cleaning floors and walls (accumulation of grease on them).
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is a leak coming from a pipe in the middle of the walk-in cooler. Ensure that this leak is repaired. 
2. There is ice on the fan unit in the walk-in freezer and on the wall. Ensure that the issue is repaired and the ice accumulation is removed. 

Ensure that equipment is repaired and maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The walk-in cooler fan cover. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The shelf under the chicken hot holding to the left of the cook-line. 
3. The bread rack shelving has an accumulation of food debris on it. 
4. The hood baffles. 
5. The sides of the preparation cooler. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are regularly cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The splash guard on the right side of the handwashing sink needs to be fully sealed to the sink. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The triple sink’s caulking is in a state of disrepair and needs re-sealed. 
3. The coving to the left under the handwashing sink is observed to be coming away from the wall and needs re-sealed. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- There are small holes in the wall above and to the right of the triple sink that need sealed. 
5. There are small holes in the wall above the preparation table in the back that need sealed. 
6. There are holes above the office area and the single service storage that need sealed. 
7. FIRST REPEAT- There is a missing piece of coving in the right of the doorway that leads to the cook-line from the warewashing and preparation area that needs replaced. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The wall and piping behind the fryer has an accumulation of dust and grease on it. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The floors, specifically underneath equipment, throughout the facility are observed to have an accumulation of grease on them. 
3. The walls around the fryers are observed to have an accumulation of grease on them. 

Ensure that physical facilities are regularly cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There is tomato purée in the bottom of the preparation cooler that is observed to still be in the open can. Tomato purée is acidic and should not continue to be stored in the can after it is opened, as it can contaminate the tomato purée. The facility did not have another container to transfer the tomato purée to, as there are not enough containers for all of their food. A follow up is scheduled for 8/26/2026 to ensure that there are enough containers for food to be stored in to prevent contamination to food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There are no lids observed for the steam table to protect and cover the food. Lids are also useful for trapping the heat to allow for proper hot holding. A follow up is scheduled for 8/26/2026 to ensure that lids have been obtained for the steam table. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by storing it in covered containers.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing upon arrival. Education was carried out. Ensure that employees are aware to properly wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed using their bare hands inside the fries bags before pouring the fries and placing a finger inside the bag while placing it into the meal bag. The service was stopped. Education was provided. The bag of fries was tossed. Ensure that gloves is use when handling ready to eat food to avoid contamination from the employee’s bare hands.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed grease and dust debris on hood baffles above fryers. Informed PIC that hood needs to be cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of grease and dust. Ensure the hood system is clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine at the bar is observed to be testing at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that staff are using the triple sink at the bar to wash, rinse, and sanitize until the dish machine has been serviced. A follow up is scheduled for 8/10/2026 to ensure that the bar dish machine is properly sanitizing at a label-recommended concentration of Chlorine.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine is observed to be testing at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine sanitizer. A follow up is scheduled for 8/14/2026 to ensure that the dish machine has been serviced and is testing at a label-recommended concentration of Chlorine sanitizer. Ensure that the dish machine is being regularly tested and serviced if not at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: REPEAT- The PIC is not a Certified Food Protection Manager. The PIC stated that her son will be working on obtaining their CFPM certificate. Ensure that a CFPM is available to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Two gallons of milk in the walk in cooler were observed partially used and without a date marking. When an employee was asked they believed that the containers were opened a couple days prior. Education was conducted and dates added to the containers to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are dated once opened and if they are not emptied within 24 hours.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the kitchen would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Employees conducted troubleshooting on the equipment and the machine began functioning correctly prior to the inspector leaving. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are functioning correctly at all times in the facility.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location.

A container labeled “seafood utensils” at a prep station was observed with standing water and floating debris in the bottom of the container. A nearby employee stated that it should be for clean utensils. The employee was shown and moved the container to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact utensils are maintained clean and protected from contamination until use.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: There were two drinks stored directly above clean dishes on a storage rack inside of the dish room. Shown to the PIC and the drinks were placed in a designated drink area. Ensure that personal drinks are never stored above clean dishes to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Grease droplets formed within the duct work of the hood system were observed dripping onto the flat top grill. The hood baffles were removed to be cleaned, however, the ansul and duct work were heavily accumulation with grease debris. The last visit from the facility’s technical company, Cintas, visited the facility last on January 14, 2026. Discussed the need to have the hood serviced more often. Will follow up on August 10, 2026 to see that system has been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Despite the facility being in full operation, there wasn’t a sanitizer solution present in the bar area. The bar area serves drinks, handles garnishes, and also slices fruits, therefore, a sanitizer solution is needed during operating hours. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- ice buildup was observed on the floor of the walk in unit (directly under air compressor)
- both bottom selves of the drawer coolers along tho cook-line were observed with accumulated debris, one drawer stores spring mix lettuce and the other drawer stores meats
- floor underneath produce wash station was observed with accumulated food deris
When time permits, be sure to clean the areas referenced above to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, there wasn’t an employee present who was food manager certified. Discussed getting at least one more individual food manger certified to ensure that all hours of operation are covered.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed at least two home made sauces stored at room temperature along the cookline. The PIC mentioned that the sauces are pulled from the cooler as needed. Discussed if wanting to keep sauces on counter that the facility will need to use time control for safety of the sauces. Time/Temperature (TCS) foods must either be refrigerated when not in use or placed on time control for up to four hours and then discarded. In the future, the facility will use time control or place sauces on ice bath for temperature control.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were no signed employee health reporting agreements available in the facility. The owner stated that they moved them to their off-site office. Paperwork that is required for health inspections should stay in the facility to be viewed at every inspection. A follow up is scheduled for 8/25/2026 to ensure that there are signed employee health reporting agreements available for every employee.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: The facility did not have a Norovirus cleanup policy available. CORRECTED- The inspector provided a written policy and the facility possesses bleach to effectively complete the procedure. Ensure that there is always a vomit and diarrhea clean-up policy in the facility at all times.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink in the dish room area was observed to have multiple dishes in it. CORRECTED- The PIC removed all dishes from the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for their intended purpose of handwashing and that they are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The back two handwashing sinks were observed to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- The PIC replaced the paper towels in both dispensers. Ensure that staff are educated to replace the paper towels at handwashing sinks when they are out to allow for the proper handwashing procedure.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine at the bar is observed to be testing at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. The PIC stated that they are waiting on more chemicals to come and that they mainly use the triple sink at the bar to wash, rinse, and sanitize. A follow up is scheduled for 8/7/2026 to ensure that the bar dish machine is properly sanitizing at a label-recommended concentration of Chlorine.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was not a sanitizer bucket made along the cook-line, despite food preparation taking place. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket made and available during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: All of the handwashing sinks, the preparation sink, and the triple sink are observed to need to be sealed to the wall. There is a gap between the wall and each of the sinks. Ensure that these sinks are sealed to the wall and the sealing is made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
There were no food handler certificates available to view in the facility for any of the employees. The owner stated that they moved them to their off-site office. All paperwork that is required for health inspections should stay at the facility to be viewed at each inspection. Ensure that food handler cards are available in the facility for all staff and that all staff have completed their food handler training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) who has their Allergen Awareness training. This was discussed with the CFPM, who stated that they will work on obtaining their allergen training. Ensure that there is always a CFPM who has completed their Allergen Awareness training in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the heat dish machine is still not repaired, and not reaching a high enough temperatures for sanitizing (165°F). PIC is working with a repair service to get the heat machine back up to a sanitizing temperature of 165°F. Facility is using their triple sinks to sanitize until the heat dish machine is repaired. Inspector will follow up with facility to confirm machine is repaired. Ensure that the temperature of a heat dish machine shall reach 165°F.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia during today’s visit. The PIC was informed and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. Inspector recommends increasing the frequency of bucket replacement. Printed labels are used to indicate the discard time for sanitizer, but the bucket measuring 0ppm was not due to expire for another two hours.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the green shelves holding pizza dough and rolling cart holding raw chicken to be soiled with microbial growth. The PIC was informed and plans to deep clean/sanitize the shelving. Ensure staff are monitoring cleanliness in the cooler and sanitizing surfaces frequently to prevent the accumulation of microbial growth. Ensure the shelves are clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the bottom shelf of the stainless steel table across from the chicken fryers to be rusted and in disrepair. This shelf is used to store extra broaster equipment, which comes in direct contact with food. Ensure this table is sealed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.

Inspector also observed the green wire shelves in the dish area to be rusted and in disrepair. These shelves hold clean dishes, which are direct food contact surfaces. Ensure these shelves are sealed or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: An open employee drink was observed sitting on the chopping surface of the prep cooler on the cook line. Education was carried out. The drink was removed. Ensure that employees are remember to have a lid on their drinks and stored in a place the helps prevent contamination.
citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was provided and the behavior was corrected.  Ensure that employees are reminded to always properly wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple cans of ripe olives dented along the seams. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the cans from service to be returned to the supplier. Ensure cans are frequently checked for dents along the seams to prevent the entry and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed both bar soda nozzles and soda gun holders to be soiled. CORRECTED- Employees cleaned and sanitized the food contact surfaces. Ensure soda nozzles and the soda gun holder are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation. Food contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
REPEAT x2: The following were observed. 
1. Inspector observed 2 sanitizer buckets to be between 0-100 ppm of quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- buckets were remade at a proper concentration (200 ppm). 
2. The sanitizer concentration in the dish machine was observed reading opposite for chlorine. CORRECTED- The EcoLab technician was called and the dish machine was repaired at the end of the inspection.
 Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at frequency to maintain the sanitizer concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label including frequently checking the sanitizer concentration within the dish machine.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler on the far end of the kitchen by the office was observed not keeping the appropriate temperature range. A discussion was held about the appropriate action needed. The average temperature within the cooler using the infrared thermometer was 55F. Temperatures obtained by probing was 44F. The food items were removed to a different unit. The PIC told inspector that the unit will be repaired accordingly. Ensure that teh necessary repairs are done enabling the unit to have the appropriate temperature capacity.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Multiple boxes of food items which includes but not limited to grilled chicken and hame were observed being stored on the floor in both the walk-in cooler and the walk-in freezer. Discussed with the PIC. The items were removed to be stored appropriately. Ensure that food items are stored at least six inches above the cooler to avoid exposure to splash or other contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the door between the walk in cooler and walk in freezer to contain a sizable gap, and the gaskets to be loose. The PIC stated a new frame is being ordered. Ensure the door is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: FOURTH REPEAT: The wire shelving on the far right corner by the entrance of the walk-in freezer in the walk in cooler is soiled and rusted. Inspector discussed getting shelf liners, cleaning/ painting, or replacing shelves. One large green shelf was replaced and the other cleaned. The PIC stated they will be ordering new shelving. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The hood baffles and fire suppression system were observed to contain an accumulation of grease drips and debris. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination to ready to eat (RTE) foods, and can serve as a fire hazard. Ensure the hood vent system and baffles are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: An accumulation of grease, soil, and food debris was observed under the fryers. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspector that they do get accumulation buildup will be cleaned. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The mop head was observed stored improperly in the mop bucket. The PIC was made aware. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a way that allows them to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the plastic container holding disposable forks to be soiled with debris. The PIC was informed and immediately sent the container to the dish room for washing and sanitizing. Ensure these containers are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent an accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was a dented can of beets stored on a rack with other canned goods. The PIC pulled the can from the shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that canned goods are free of any dents along the seams and body of the can to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.
