The items were date marked July 26, 2026 and July 27, 2026. Discussed with the PIC and the soups were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that temperature/time control (TCS) foods are never held past their seven day date marking.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The two door prep cooler along the cook line was observed with a broken door handle. The PIC mentioned that the handle broke a few weeks prior to the inspection. Ensure that the handle is repaired and is in good condition.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- the top surface of the drawer cooler was observed with accumulated grease and food debris
- the bottom shelf of the drawer cooler was observed with accumulated spilled liquids and food debris

The PIC instructed an employee to clean the surfaces during the visit. Ensure that non food contact surfaces of pieces of equipment are cleaned at a frequency to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the following items to be stored in improper packaging:
1. Egg rolls and crab rangoon stored atop paper menus in the upright cooler
2. Crab rangoon stored in repurposed bean sprout bag
3. Cooked pork stored in a grocery bag in the upright 2-door cooler.

Food must be stored in either its original packaging or a container which is made for food contact or can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure these items are stored safely to prevent accidental contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed two dented cans in the back dry storage area. The PIC was informed and the cans were separated from the other food items. Ensure deliveries are inspected for dented/damaged goods and any damaged items are returned or discarded. Dented cans can be immediately opened following the damage, but dented cans discovered on the shelf must be discarded due to contamination risks.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Raw chicken stored above cooked shrimp in the upright cooler
2. Bowl of raw chicken liquid stored in direct contact with peas in the prep cooler top

The PIC was informed and these items were moved. There is a storage order flyer posted on the walk-in cooler door with Chinese translation. Ensure staff are following the instructions listed on this flyer.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed an employee wash and rinse multiple dishes without sanitizing. The triple sink was not prepared for proper wash, rinse, and sanitize. The staff was halted by inspectors. The PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper wash, rinse sanitize practices. The triple sink was properly prepared during the inspection. A handout with Chinese translation was also provided. Ensure proper wash, rinse, sanitize practices are followed for every dish that is cleaned in the facility.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation.

Inspectors observed no date marking on prepared food containers in the facility. A container of prepared rice noodles were confirmed to be stored in the facility from the day prior. However, most items are prepared or thawed for same day service. All temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum. Inspector will spot check date marking on August 19, 2026.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed a yellow food dye bottle repurposed as a water squirt bottle. The lid of the bottle has holes bored to allow water to spray from the container. This lid was observed soiled with debris. The PIC was informed that a repurposed container must be relabeled to properly reflect current contents. The bottle was emptied and moved to the dish area during today’s visit.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed several foods (ex. egg rolls, wontons, chicken wings, crab rangoon) in the clear sliding cooler were not covered during storage. Items were also stored in the 2-door upright cooler and walk-in cooler without protective coverings. Ensure coverings are used for all food in coolers to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed an open paper bag of sugar stored directly on the floor in the back storage room. The PIC was informed of proper storage requirements. There is a container labeled for sugar storage already present in the back room. Ensure food items are stored at least 6 inches off the ground with protective coverings at all times to prevent contamination or pest harborage.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of food reside in the bottom gaskets of the clear sliding door cooler.
(2) THIS IS A FOURTH REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of debris inside of the fan above the double door cooler. 
(3) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The prep table in the back of the kitchen was covered in flour/corn starch.
(4) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The shelving used for drying dishes above the triple sink is rusted and soiled.
(5) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The handle of the coolers and chest freezer are soiled with food debris.
(6) The shelving in the back storage room was observed soiled with considerable food debris accumulated on the floor below.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The inspectors observed the following facility items in need of repair:
(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION:The facility is missing coving in many areas of the kitchen.
(2) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The triple sink is held up with bare wood between the sink basin and the floor.
(3) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The ceiling is damaged with gaps between the seams in the back storage area.
(4) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The shelving above the triple sink is heavily rusted and damaged.
(5) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The ceiling in the back room and above the chest freezer is heavily soiled/damaged.

Ensure these facility items are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspector observed two open beverage containers stored on the shelf above the prep cooler in the kitchen. The PIC was informed that personal items including beverages should never be stored above food or food-contact surfaces to prevent cross-contamination. The drinks were moved to a bottom shelf during today’s visit.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn’t any hand soap available at either hand sinks along the deli’s cook-line. A bottle of soap was provided to both hand sinks to correct the violation. Ensure that hand soap is available at all hand sinks to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn’t any paper towel available at one of the hand sinks in the deli area. Paper towels were provided to the hand sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are provided with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Despite the facility being in full operation, there weren’t any sanitizer solutions present. Discussed with the PIC and a sanitizer bucket was created and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present if food is being handled, prepared, or served on site.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The employee’s allergen certificate expired in June of 2026. Discussed getting re-certified to ensure that the certificate is valid. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed that unwrapped drinking straws were made available to customers in the bar area to grab with barehands. CORRECTED: PIC and staff were educated that this exposes the food-contact surfaces of the straws to barehand contact by everyone, and that unwrapped straws should be removed from the customer area and only handled with gloved hands by staff (with the gloves acting as a barrier) or the unwrapped straws should be replaced with wrapped straws, where the wrapping acts as a barrier preventing barehand contact. Staff moved the unwrapped straws behind the bar area out of reach of customers, and the PIC plans to purchase wrapped straws instead. Ensure food-contact surfaces of straws are handled with a barrier to prevent barehand contact.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that the handwashing sink in the bar area had a strainer inside of it, obstructing the sink from being used for handwashing and and the handwashing sink was being used for purposes other than handwashing. CORRECTED: the strainer was removed and staff was reminded that handwashing sinks must only be used for handwashing purposes, nothing else. Ensure that handwashing sinks are accessible and maintained at all times for handwashing use by employees, and only for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed comminuted ground meat (burgers) stored over whole fish and frog legs (which are included in the “FISH” category by the FDA) in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC moved the fish and frog legs to a different shelf where they were not below meat of a higher final cooking temperature. Ensure that storage order in coolers are in order of final cooking temperature, so that any cross-contamination from above is resolved with the higher cooking temperature of the item below.
- Top shelf = ready-to-eat food (RTE) which does not require cooking;
- 2nd shelf = fresh unprepared produce that requires washing or cooking
- 3rd shelf = whole meats (fish and frog legs) and raw eggs, final cooking temperature at 145 F.
- 4th shelf = whole meats (pork and beef), final cooking temperature at 145 F.
- 5th shelf = comminuted ground meat and pooled eggs, final cooking temperature at 155 F.
- Bottom shelf = all poultry products, final cooking temperature at 165 F.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that a wet mop was being stored in the lower basin of the mop bucket where it cannot air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop to that the mop head was in the upper basket of the mop bucket, and any liquids can drain through the basket and be collected in the lower basin. Ensure that after use mops are placed so that they can air-dry without soiling their surroundings.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on the sides. CORRECTED- One of the PICs cleaned this during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned regularly and maintained clean.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The gasket of the mini cooler in a cabinet at the coffee bar is observed to be in disrepair. This was shown to the PIC. Ensure that this gasket is replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The sliders of the doors on the front display cases. 
2. The walk-in cooler shelves. 
3. The bottom of the sheet pan storage rack in the bakery area. 

These were discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and they were instructed to review hand washing procedures with all food handlers in the facility. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet after hand washing in order to protect the freshly washed hands from re-contamination.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

There was not a CFPM available during the inspection. The PIC stated that his had lapsed and he had not re-done it yet. They were instructed to have enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts that have food handling in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink nearest to the door was blocked with a trash can. The inspector moved the can in order to begin the inspection quicker and discussed the situation with the PIC later in the inspection. Education was conducted with the PIC during the inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks are readily accessible at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani bucket in the facility was observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. Effective concentrations for CL sanitizers is 50-200 ppm. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective concentrations at all times in the facility.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

On arrival the hot holding unit next to the rice cooker and window was observed to not be on with TCS foods inside. Chicken was probed and observed at 84F internal temperature. The unit was turned back on and the foods currently in it discarded. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at proper temperatures at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the chemical dish machine was not sanitizing at an effective concentration of Chlorine (10ppm). CORRECTED: PIC determined that the sanitizer dispenser was empty and replaced the dispenser with a new bucket during the inspection. Chemical dish machine was then measured to be sanitizing at effective concentration of Chlorine for warewashing (50ppm). Ensure that chemical sanitizers used in mechanical warewashing are used per manufacturer’s instructions regarding pH.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods (see Violation #33):

(i) sliced tomatoes (probed 52°F) and shredded lettuce (47°F). CORRECTED: tomatoes and lettuce were voluntarily discarded, as they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago; previously prepped tomatoes and lettuce were taken from the walk-in cooler and placed in ice baths, which will be monitored for cold holding temperatures.

(ii) shredded cheese (52°F) and cooked spaghetti (56°F). CORRECTED: shredded cheese and cooked spaghetti were voluntarily discarded, as they were removed from proper cold holding temperatures longer than 4 hours ago; a new container of shredded cheese was prepared and new packages of cook spaghetti were moved from the walk-in cooler and both were kept in a nearby short cooler that was sufficiently cold holding.

(iii) milk (42°F) and manufactured sauces that require refrigeration (clucked sauce, mayonnaise, and garlic spread - 43°F). CORRECTED: sauces were moved to nearby coolers that were sufficiently cold holding.

Ensure that TCS foods are kept at temperatures of 41°F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed the front dress prep cooler was not sufficiently cooling and cold holding TCS foods. PIC took care of TCS foods so that they will be properly cold holding in the interim (see Violation #22). PIC is contacting a repair company. Inspector will Follow Up with establishment to confirm that the prep cooler has been repaired. Ensure that equipment for cooling and cold holding is sufficient to provide food temperatures of 41°F or less.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Observed that the following freezers had significant ice drip buildup that was falling onto food:
(i) the walk-in freezer. Staff had placed a pan to collect drips, but additional ice drips had formed missing the pan and falling onto food. CORRECTED: PIC moved food away from the fans where the ice is forming and dripping.
(ii) the 2-door standing freezer. CORRECTED: PIC placed a tray directly underneath where the ice drips are forming so that when they defrost they do not fall below onto the food.
Ensure that freezers do not get significant ice buildup, and that the ice does not contaminated the food stored in the freezers.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was set up and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available and at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be coming apart to the left of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed members of staff to be missing food handlers training. Discussed with PIC, remaining staff will complete training. Ensure any food handling staff members have completed the food handlers training within 30 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed allergen training to have been expired by the current CFM. Discussed with PIC, CFM will complete the required allergen training. Ensure all CFMs have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrie to shut the faucet after washing their hands. PIC was made aware of the observed behavior. The appropriate correction was made. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable on proper handwashing etiquette.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed a plumbing leak in the lines beneath the three compartment sink in the chill station where the ice cream machines are the lines under the dump sink in the back. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done according to the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Multiple mop heads were observed not stored properly. Discussed with PIC. The mop heads were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that the mop heads are always stored in a position that allows them to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during the inspection was unable to provide a CFPM certificate for an employee available at the facility during the inspection. They stated that they had taken and passed the test but the tester had a surgery and had not yet given them the certificate. The inspector directed them to servesafe’s website to attempt and get a copy that way. No certification was provided by the end of the inspection. Ensure that there are enough CFPM’s available at the facility to cover all shifts and that they certification is available at the facility at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hand to turn off the water faucet. Education was conducted. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to turn off the faucet so that the freshly cleaned hands are not re-contaminated immediately after washing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

A food handler was observed to put on gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted. Ensure that hands are washed when needed per the code, including prior to donning gloves.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

One of the two observed sani buckets showed approximately 100 ppm quat on the inspector’s test strips. Effective concentrations for this chemical are a minimum of 200 ppm. The PIC was shown and remade the bucket to correct.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling.

The spray bottles used for lactic acid sanitizer were observed at extremely high concentrations on both the inspector’s and facility’s test strips. It appeared that the dispenser is producing the concentration at the high level. The PIC is instructed to contact their chemical company (EcoLab) and have the equipment adjusted to safe use levels for food contact surfaces prior to the follow up. In the short term bottles were made and manually diluted with water to safe levels. This is a temporary measure and the machine still needs adjusting.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

The hand sink next to the three part sink was observed with a cart in front of it, blocking access and use. The PIC was shown and removed the cart to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times in the facility.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the beginning of the inspection there was no a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) available at the facility. One was called and arrived during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that there is a CFPM available at all times that the kitchen is in use in the facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Multiple items in the walk in cooler were observed with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-50F. The PIC was shown and the TCS items discarded to correct the violations. Items discarded included corned beef, coleslaw, ham, cheese, pizza, marinara, cheese sauce, chicken breast, and BBQ pulled pork. Ensure that the cold old int in the facility is maintained at correct temperatures at all times. This violation is for the foods being out of safe temperature ranges only. Refer to line item #33 for the cooler.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

A half gallon of milk was observed in the server cooler partially used and without a date marking. When asked, staff indicated that it was opened “a couple days ago”. Education was conducted and a date marking added to the container to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods in the facility are properly dated once they are prepared or the packaging is opened.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler was observed to be holding foods with internal temperatures ranging from 45F-50F. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the cooler repaired prior to the follow up in 10 days. This violation is for the cooler not functioning correctly.

title: Food handler training
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Food Handler Certificates were unavailable for multiple employees on staff during today’s inspection. Ensure all food service staff obtain a Food Handler’s certificate to be made available during future inspections. Inspector provided guidance on where to find ANSI-approved Food Handler’s certificate Courses.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

None of the CFPMs employed by the facility currently had an allergen training certificate available during the inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that the CFPMs complete the training and maintain a copy of the certificates at the facility moving forward.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The CFPM arrived approximately 45 minutes to an hour after the inspection began to correct the violation. Ensure that a CFPM is available at the facility at all times that foods and food contact surfaces are being handled.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

1) The hand sink in the front of the kitchen would not dispense soap. The equipment appeared to have run out of battery. The batteries were replaced and the equipment began to function correctly. Violation corrected. 2) The hand sink in the back of the kitchen appeared to have run out of soap in the dispenser. The soup was replaced with a new container and began dispensing correctly during the inspection. Both locations were shown to the PIC and education conducted. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied with soap at al times in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The hand sink in the front of the kitchen was observed without paper towels at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC was consulted and supplied new paper towels to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: via an approved method. 

Two packages of beef were observed in one of the sinks thawing in standing water. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the water turned on to correct. Ensure that thawing takes place in the facility in a method approved by the code moving forward.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Mozzarella cheese was observed stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. Several other boxes of assorted foods were observed stored on the floor in the walk in freezer. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to store all foods off of the ground (at least 6 inches) prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all foods are stored off of the floor at all times in the facility.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation 

Inspector observed mashed potatoes, brown gravy, and white gravy to be stored beyond the 7-day date mark in the “Monster Energy” cooler. The PIC was informed and the items were discarded. Ensure staff are checking coolers at the start or end of each day and discarding any items beyond the 7-day mark. 

Inspector observed deli beef and deli turkey in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler to be stored past its 7-day date mark. The beef was marked 2/24 and the turkey was marked 2/23. Ensure staff are monitoring coolers daily and discarding any items stored beyond 7 days. The items were discarded during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a mouse on a glue trap in the back storage area of the facility. The PIC was informed and plans to contact pest control for treatment. Inspector recommends ensuring all outer openings are properly sealed and the exterior of the building is treated for pests. Ensure all food items in the dry storage area are protected from rodents. Inspector recommends placing any food items in plastic or cardboard into hard plastic bins. A follow-up will be conducted on August 31, 2026 to ensure all pests have been removed from the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the floors around the fryers to have an accumulation of grease and dust debris. Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Boxes of plastic to-go containers were observed on the floor in the backstock area where the produce department stores their containers. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. The items were moved during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored up off of the ground at all times in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Multiple hand sinks throughout the facility were observed with missing or cracking seals round the sinks. The individual sinks were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to repair/re-seal the sinks to the walls to maintain a smooth and easily cleanable surface at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a cutting board being stored behind the faucet handles of the triple sink. Shown to the PIC and the board was removed and placed in different location that doesn’t expose the food contact surface to contamination. Ensure that cutting boards are never stored behind faucet handles to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Two not in use mop heads were observed stored inside of mop buckets containing waste water. Shown to the PIC and the mop heads were placed on the walls of the mop sink to dry properly. Ensure that not in use mop heads are never stored in wastewater and are placed in a positions that allows for proper drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs to be stored above green beans and milk in the upright kitchen cooler. The PIC was informed and the eggs were relocated to the bottom shelf. Ensure all animal products are stored below ready-to-eat foods in the cooler to prevent cross contamination. A handout was provided by the inspector to staff for future reference.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the ventilation covers and shelves above the triple sink and hand sink to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure staff are cleaning these surfaces frequently to prevent cross contamination with food containers and clean dishes. Ensure these surfaces are clean prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation 

Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets in the kitchen to read 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed and all buckets in the facility were replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure the buckets are monitored with test strips to prevent inadequate sanitization of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the dish machine at the bar measure 0ppm chlorine after multiple attempts to troubleshoot the machine. The PIC was informed and plans to contact MJK for repair. In the meantime, all dishes from the bar must be sanitized in the kitchen dish machine until the bar machine is repaired. A follow-up will be conducted on August 4, 2026 for dish machine repair.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed all three soda nozzles at the bar to be soiled with black microbial growth. The PIC was informed of the soil. The nozzles are considered a food-contact surface, and therefore must be kept clean to sight and touch at all times. The nozzles were removed and sanitized during today’s visit. Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation
Inspector observed the following items to be stored beyond its 7-day date mark:
1. Pork (expired July 22)
2. Beef x2 (expired July 18)
3. Chicken x2 (expired 7/22)
4. Ground beef x3 (expired July 28)
5. Beans x2 (expired July 28)
6. Beans x2 (expired July 22)

There were also multiple other containers with expired date marks that the inspector could not easily access due to stacking. The PIC was made aware that all items past the date mark must be discarded. A follow-up will be conducted on August 4, 2026 to ensure that proper date marking guidelines are being followed in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspector observed 1 live roach crawling on a prep table between the walk-in cooler and cook line. The PIC was informed and plans to contact Orkin for service. Ensure receipts of this treatment is maintained on file for the inspector to view. 

A follow-up is scheduled for August 31, 2026 to ensure pest presence is reduced. Continue to have Orkin treat the facility and retain all receipts.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed food items and single-service items to be stored directly on the floor in the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and the dry storage room connected to the walk-in cooler. Ensure food items are stored at least 6 inches off the ground to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available in the facility. There were chlorine test strips available for testing the dish machine, but a quaternary ammonia sanitizer dispenser is used for filling all sanitizer buckets. Ensure test strips of both varieties are available at all times for proper testing. A follow-up will be conducted on August 10, 2026 for test strip availability.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation.

The floor of the walk in freezer was observed with chunks of ice build up. Ensure that the freezer floor is maintained as often as necessary to prevent ice accumulation. Repairs may be necessary on the cooling unit of the freezer to prevent dripping.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of repair:
1. The ceiling light above the right side of the cook line is broken and exposing the bulbs. This poses a glass contamination hazard if the bulb were to break.
2. The shelves in the walk-in cooler were observed damaged and rusted. Rust can impart contaminates into food stored on the shelves. Ensure these shelves are sealed or replaced. 

Ensure these facility repairs are completed prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

An open package of raw ground beef was observed in a cooler drawer alongside an opened package of Ready-To-Eat (RTE) sliced cheese. Juices were observed throughout the bottom of the drawer. The PIC and cook were shown and the foods in the drawer discarded to correct. Education was conducted. Ensure that raw and RTE foods are stored so that cross contamination does not take place.

title: Gloves used properly.
citation_text:
3-304.15 (A) Glove Use (A) if used, SINGLE-USE gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discard when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation. 

An employee was observed to handle a bluetooth speaker with their gloved hands and then handle ready for service meals and foods. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to educate staff as to when gloves should be changed. Change gloves whenever moving between tasks or whenever they may have become contaminated, and prior to handling foods.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. Another cook with a valid certification was supposed to be present but came late. Inspector was able to verify the certification validity.  Ensure that there is at least one certified food protection manager present at all times.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: An accumulation of ice and frost was observed in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the ice and frost are cleaned out providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. Appropriate handwashing procedures were followed. Ensure that staff remember to always wash their hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed three cans of tomatoes, one can of olive, and one can of pineapple dented in the middle of the can shelving. PIC was made aware. The dented cans were removed. Ensure that food items with compromised package integrity are removed from the inventory and returned appropriately.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of soil build up was observed on the shelvings use to hold dishes above the triple sink. 
2. The coving tiles under the steam table, triple sink, and the wall in front of the refrigerator by the kitchen entrance were observed coming off the wall.  
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the relevant action will be taken. Ensure that corrective actions are taken providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The preparation cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F in the bottom. The PIC stated that Falcon Restaurant Company replaced the control board in the preparation cooler yesterday. The following TCS food items were probed and discarded if above 41F:

1. A container of pepper jack cheese probed to be at 46.6F. 
2. A container of provolone cheese probed to be at 50F. 
3. A container of turkey probed to be at 47.3F. 
4. A container of ham probed to be at 49.9F. 
5. A container of butter probed to be at 46F. 

The owner voluntarily discarded these TCS food items and contacted Falcon to repair the cooler. The facility has multiple other coolers available to cold hold TCS food items in. A spot check will be conducted on 8/4/2026 to ensure that the preparation cooler is repaired and is properly cold holding at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

The corner strip in the dry storage room nearest to the door was observed with the Nudo board pulling away and exposing a gap in the corner. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal the corner so that it is smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that all facilities are maintained smooth and easily cleanable at all times.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

Raw eggs were observed stored over ready to eat foods on wire shelves in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and the eggs moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored according to their cooking temperatures in the facility at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda nozzles in the drive thru area are observed soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean them. The nozzles were removed and disassembled and then cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate situation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

6-501.111 EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments.
