comment: Inspector observed raw chicken stored above cooked soups and waffle batter in the corner prep cooler. PIC was informed and the items were rearranged. Ensure staff are storing raw meat below ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: An accumulation of soil was observed inside the nozzles of the soda machine. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: A container of soup in the corner prep cooler was observed without proper date marking. PIC was made aware. The soup was tossed into the trash. Ensure that food items being held over 24-hour within a food establishment are properly date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There was no hanging thermometer available in the large white standing cooler in the basement. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspector that thermometer will be provided. Ensure that there are adequate temperature measuring devices available to assess the appropriate temperature within cooling units at all times.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed a knife stored in the crevice between two prep counters and the ice scoop stored directly on top of the ice machine. The PIC was informed that in-use utensils must be stored on an easily cleanable surface to prevent cross contamination. The ice scoop was moved to a tray, and the knife was placed in the dish area during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a mop stored directly in the basin of the mop bucket. The PIC was informed and the mop was moved. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to drip dry. This practices prevents microbial growth in the mop head.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler certification for a couple employee present. The PIC assured inspector that the training for the certification will be done. Ensure that food employee acquire their food handler certification within 30 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify allergen training certification for any certified food protection manager during today’s inspection. PIC was made aware. Eduardo that the allergen training is done to be in compliance. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Two out of the four handwashing sinks in the kitchen area were without hand soap. Discussed with the PIC. New batteries were added to the soap dispenser and soap was provided. Ensure that hand soap is available at every hand-sink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was mold observed on a couple strawberries stored inside a container within the walk in cooler. Shown to the PIC and the strawberries were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that food is always in good condition and never containing mold on surfaces.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw chicken was observed above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods and a container of eggs within both the walk in cooler and a prep cooler. Shown to PIC and the chicken products were placed to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. There are many reference sheets for proper storage order posted throughout the kitchen area. Ensure that all chicken products are stored at the bottom shelf to protect against cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A red cutting board was observed stored behind handles of the triple sink. Discussed the possibility of contaminating the food contact surface due to improper storage location. Faucet handles aren't typically cleaned frequently as needed to keep them clean, therefore, refrain from storing cutting board behind handles. The board was placed through the dish machine and stored in another location to correct the violation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Breaded shrimp inside of the 2 door black line cooler (across from cookline) was probed at 57F. The ambient temperature of the cooler was recorded between 57F-61F. All food items were transferred to the walk in cooler since the items were placed inside of the unit at 11am. Violation corrected. Ensure that all TCS foods are cold held at a temperature of 41F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was a container of breading (used to bread seafood) being stored inside of the dry storage area. The dry breading contained leftover pieces of seafood and is used to bread shrimp and fish for frying purposes. Discussed the need of sifting batter frequently and refrigerating batter if there are plans to reuse the next day. Refrain from storing batters on counters if not refrigerated at end of night. The breading was pulled from shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that batters are sifted at least every few hours and/or held under refrigeration.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The black two door cooler across from the cookline was observed with an ambient temperature of 57F. Both internal thermometers recorded between 57F-61F. The cooler is holding various Time/Temperature Control Foods (TCS) such as seafood and meats. The items were placed inside of the unit at opening time (11am). The facility was instructed to place foods inside of the walk in cooler until the unit can be serviced. Will follow-up August 6, 2026 to see that unit has been repaired or replaced.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There is a dispense rack that stores unwrapped ice cream cones in the service area. The ice cream station is self serve, however, the food contact surface is exposed to contamination, as the cone lacks protection. Discussed purchasing wrapped cones with the PIC so that customers aren't able to contamination bare ice cream cones.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is waste water starting to back up at the drain in front of the cookline. The PIC mentioned contacting a plumber in the past but the company has yet to arrive. Ensure that plumbing is serviced to prevent waste water from back up in floor drain. Will follow-up August 6, 2026 to see that plumbing has been serviced.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The ice scoop in the bar ice basin was observed to have the handle in contact with the ice. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC, who then corrected the scoop handle to be above the ice. Employees use their bare hands to scoop ice using the ice scoop, therefore, the ice scoop should be stored with the handle above the ice to protect the ice from contamination from bare hand contact.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- There were raw, shelled eggs on the top shelf in the walk-in cooler observed to be stored above cut onions and other cut vegetables. CORRECTED- The raw, shelled eggs were moved to the bottom shelf under ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There are Parmesan cheese shakers observed to be stored on tables for consumer use. According to the PIC in the kitchen, these shakers are put in the cooler every night and then placed on the tables every day for consumer use. The cheese is imported grated pecorino Romano cheese from Casale and the box is stored in the walk-in cooler and states to “KEEP REFRIGERATED”. The facility can either cease this practice and store the Parmesan cheese shakers in a cooler and remove them only when a consumer wants to use them OR can reach out to the manufacturer to determine if the Parmesan cheese only needs to be refrigerated for QUALITY and not SAFETY. A follow up is scheduled for 8/5/2026 to allow time for the facility to decide and to reach out to the manufacturer. Ensure that proof is provided if reaching out to the manufacturer. If there are any questions, please reach out to the inspector.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: The drinking straws in the bar area were observed unwrapped and stored in close proximity to consumers. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the containers of straws to be behind the bar counter. Ensure that unwrapped straws are either stored behind the counter where they are controlled by employees or purchase wrapped straws for consumers.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair:

1. The top right door of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be missing. An employee stated that they are working on repairing it and the cooler is observed to be properly cold holding at this time. Ensure that this door is repaired and put back on the cooler. 
2. The walk-in freezer is observed to have frost accumulation around the fan unit and the door. The PIC stated that they have a plan for repairing it. Ensure that the frost accumulation issue is repaired and all frost build-up is removed. 

Ensure that equipment is repaired and maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The walk-in cooler shelves.
2. The gaskets of the main preparation cooler on the cook-line. 
3. The gaskets of the silver freezer along the cook-line. 
4. The gaskets of the double-door cooler by the pizza preparation area. 
5. The gaskets of the pizza preparation cooler. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink to the right of the cook-line is observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink in the back preparation area of the kitchen is observed to need to be sealed to the wall. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- There are holes in the wall above the pizza preparation cooler. Ensure that these holes are sealed. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The table to the left of the dish machine is in need of being sealed to the wall. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were a handful of gnats observed in the dry storage area where soda boxes are stored. The facility has a glow LED light trap for insect control. Discussed purchasing insect glue traps to hang from ceiling in non food prep areas. Ensure that the premise is maintained free of insects.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The hood baffles above the fryer station were observed accumulated with grease debris. PIC mentioned that Steam Power services the hood system and that the company is behind on cleaning services. Discussed that baffles can be manually cleaned by staff in between professional cleanings. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning in the following areas:
- Floors throughout the kitchen (underneath and behind equipment)
- Outer surfaces of equipment
- Walls and ceilings throughout the entire facility
When time permits, be sure to clean physical facilities at a frequency to prevent buildup of grease and food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The ceiling tile, close to the food prep station area for prepping chicken, was observed with mold buildup. Shown to the PIC and the tile was cleaned to correct the violation. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment:
Observed the following instances of improper storage:
(i) 1ST REPEAT: Soup/Salad bowls were stored on open shelves near the prep line upright instead of inverted, and are open to falling debris through the upper shelves. PIC was notified and plans to place mats on the upper shelves to protect the dishes and prevent falling debris, as the shape of the bowls does not allow for inversion.
(ii) Clean bowls and other dishes were stored in the dish room in the open and upright position instead of protected or inverted. Of particular concern were large metal bowls that were air-drying where the water inside was not able to drain because they were not inverted. CORRECTED: the bowls were inverted during the inspection, and PIC was notified that all clean articles need to be protected by inversion or a cover.
Ensure all equipment, utensils, and single-service or single-use articles are kept protected through cover or inversion.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed in use mop to be resting directly on floor. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to mop ringer. Ensure after use mop is stored in a way that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the heat dish machine was not reaching a high enough temperatures for sanitizing, with the highest temperature reached after 3 cycles being 141.8°F. PIC will contact a repair service to get the heat machine back up to a sanitizing temperature of 165°F. Facility will use their triple sinks to sanitize until the heat dish machine is repaired. Inspector will follow up with facility to confirm machine is repaired. Ensure that the temperature of a heat dish machine shall reach 165°F.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a container of cream (a TCS product) with a date mark beyond the 7 day rule. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the cream, and discussed with Inspector rules for date marking TCS, RTE products. Ensure that any TCS, RTE foods are date marked if they will be in the facility beyond 24 hours of their open or prep date, with the date of prep or open being day 1, and day 7 being the day of final use or discard.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: 2ND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of dust on the walk-in freezer fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in freezer fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed 2 employee bathrooms that are used by women where there was not a lid on the trash receptacles. Inspector discussed with PIC the importance of providing a lidded trash receptacles for bathrooms used by women, including for hygiene purposes and to protect the facility’s plumbing from improperly discarded feminine hygiene products. Ensure that all toilet rooms used by women have a covered trash receptacle.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a wet mop being stored in the lower basin of a mop bucket where it cannot air-dry. Observed 2 wet mops being stored against a wall (which can soil the wall), with one of two mops not being inverted and allowed to air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC relocated both mops to better locations where they can air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. Ensure mops be stored in positions and locations where they can fully air-dry between uses.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed member of staff to not use a barrier when turning off faucet after hand washing. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used after hand washing to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed a bag of sugar to be stored in a container of opened raisins. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper food storage. Raisins were discarded and bag of sugar will no longer be stored with raisins. Ensure food items a re stored in a way that prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-306.11 Food Display. Except for nuts in the shell and whole, raw fruits and vegetables that are intended for hulling, peeling, or washing by the CONSUMER before consumption, FOOD on display shall be protected from contamination by the use of PACKAGING; counter, service line, or salad bar FOOD guards; display cases; or other effective means.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the chemical dish machine is not sanitizing to effective concentrations of Chlorine (currently measuring at 0ppm), as measured from the interior top of the dish machine. Observed that the chemical sanitizer bottle was registering a non-zero concentration of Chlorine, so PIC will work with maintenance staff to fix the chemical dish machine; the chemical dish machine will be removed from service until it is fixed. CORRECTED: Staff will use the triple sink to sanitize dishes (mostly water bottles) using approved bleach (Cl) which is unscented and NOT “low splash”. Ensure that the chemical sanitizer bleach (Chlorine) is used per manufacturer’s instructions to reach a safe and effective level of sanitizer, 50-200ppm for Chlorine.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A couple trays raw chicken breast were observed stored above raw ground beef and pre-cooked diced chicken in the walk-in cooler. Education was provided and PIC removed the items mentioned and placed them in their appropriate storage order. Ensure that food items are stored appropriately to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking above the counter top on the right side of the dish machine was observed coming off the wall. In addition, a couple broken floor tiles were observed in the dish room as well. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the counter top will be re-caulked to the wall. citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple containers of foods in the front walk in cooler were observed without lids and/or other coverings to protect them from miscellaneous contamination during storage. The PIC was shown and had staff add coverings or lids to all of the observed food items during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all stored foods are protected from contaminants while they are being stored.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer solution to test at 300 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solutions was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizer solutions are prepared at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a cooler to be at 70F. Discussed with PIC, items within cooler are only kept for 2 hours and discarded. Time as control was introduced to facility, inspector will spot check cooler at the next lunch.

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no allergen training to have been completed. Discussed with PIC, allergen training will be completed. Ensure all certified food managers have the required allergen training completed. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas were observed with accumulated debris:
- the shelves underneath the grill tops were heavily accumulated with spilled oils and food debris
- spaces in between standing coolers/freezers and other kitchen equipment were observed with dried grease debris
- the vent covers above the back prep station (near walk in cooler) were observed coated with dried debris. 
Ensure that non food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There was a build of grease and food debris observed on floors and walls throughout the kitchen area, mainly along the cook-line. The PIC is aware of the areas that are in need of cleaning and the facility is working to have the areas cleaned. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

The volunteers in the kitchen said that they had just moved the items to that cooler a little while ago. The items were removed and placed in the four compartment cooler in the serving area. citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink in the kitchen was observed to be used to hold the sanitizer dispensing tube. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the tube was removed from the handwashing sink. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sides and top of the inside of the ice machine are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that the inside of the ice machine has been cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The facility has a TIME AS CONTROL policy in place for foods on the breakfast buffet, but the employee stated that they have been keeping some items to save on food cost. The following TCS food items were observed to be above 41F:

1. Waffle batter probed to be at 48F. Waffle batters are cold held using ice packs on the sides of the dispenser, which does not allow for proper cold holding below 41F. The employee stated that they have been putting the leftover waffle batters in the cooler to use for the next day. Cease doing this, as the waffle batters are not being properly cold held at below 41F and the package states to refrigerate the batter after it is made. 
2. There are two cold holding buffet lines that are cold held using ice below the containers. Cantaloupe probed to be at 47F and yogurt probed to be at 50F on one line. Cottage cheese probed to be at 48F, tomatoes probed to be at 47F, and watermelon probed to be at 50F on the second cold holding line. The employee stated that they had been saving the leftovers of these items. It was discussed to discard the leftovers after breakfast and to place less of the items out if wanting to save on food cost. 
3. There are two milk carafes, one containing 2% milk and the other containing almond milk. The employee stated that they place these back in the cooler after breakfast and the containers are emptied and cleaned every other day. Cease this practice. The milks should be discarded after breakfast and the containers should be cleaned daily. 

TIME AS CONTROL should be used for the breakfast buffet, as the facility does not have the equipment that allows for proper cold holding at 41F and below. The PIC stated that their policy is to use time as control. Ensure that all staff are educated on this and are being trained to discard items after breakfast. Ensure that TCS foods are being held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Illinois adopted the 2022 FDA Food Code which requires bulk/buffet items in establishments to have the major allergens listed on them. The items on the buffet need to have the major allergens listed in some form. This can be accomplished by a picture of the allergen outside of each one, a poster that lists the allergen next to each food item, or another form that clearly communicates the allergens container to the consumer.
citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were ants observed to be on the counter by the waffle maker, potato hot holding, and the microwave. The employee stated that they had been having an ant issue. Ensure that pest control is treating the facility for ants and that the counter is being frequently cleaned. A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that the ants have been eliminated from the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a fork observed to be in the front handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The fork was removed from the handwashing sink and it was discussed to only use the handwashing sink for handwashing. Ensure that all staff are educated that handwashing sinks should only be used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

comment: The mini fridge that holds sauces is observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. The PIC stated that most of the sauces had been made and put in the cooler about an hour prior to the inspection. These sauces were moved to another cooler, while the rest of the sauces were voluntarily discarded (a bottle of honey mustard and a bottle of Western dressing.) The facility has enough cold holding without the use of this mini fridge. The PIC stated that they will be attempting to get a new one. Ensure that if a new mini fridge is obtained that it is properly cold holding at 41F or below.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.

comment:

All Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM) must also complete training in basic allergen awareness principles. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of repair:
1. The shelving in the walk-in cooler was observed rusted and in need of repair. Inspector recommends sealing the shelving with paint or replacing with coated shelving to prevent future rust accumulation.

2. The walk-in freezer has an accumulation of ice on food containers, walls, ceiling, floors, and shelving. Inspector recommends defrosting and cleaning the freezer. If accumulation persists, the freezer will require repair. 

Ensure these physical facility items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
The bathroom that is off to the side of the bar is observed to have coving that is pulled away from the wall. There were observed to be multiple fast-moving roaches that came out of this coving when the coving was disturbed. 

In the main men’s bathroom, there were observed to be two dead baby roaches, one on the floor and one in the cabinets. 

In the kitchen, there was observed to be a fast-moving roach under the soda fountain area and another fast-moving roach in the back corner that went into coving that is pulled away from the wall. There were over a dozen dead roaches of all life stages on the floor throughout the kitchen. 

Throughout the kitchen, there is observed to be missing coving and coving that is no longer sealed to the wall. There is also observed to be cardboard that is being kept in the kitchen. There needs to be attention to cleaning as well to ensure that the dead roaches are being regularly cleaned up. The back door was observed to be cracked open, potentially allowing more pests to enter the facility. 

The PIC was unsure of where pest control records would be kept. In the past, Terminix and Bacon’s were listed as the pest control companies. The PIC stated that pest control has come frequently in the past two months. 

A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that cleaning is occurring throughout the facility to clean dead roaches, that pest control is regularly coming, and that proper actions are being taken by the facility to reduce pest presence (removing cardboard, keeping the back door shut, sealing coving, etc.).
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There was observed to be two dead baby roaches in the men’s bathroom, one in the cabinet and one on the floor. There were also over a dozen dead roaches of all life-stages observed throughout the kitchen. There needs to be attention to cleaning to allow for proper monitoring of the pest issue. A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that dead roaches are being cleaned up.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following were observed during today’s inspection,
1. The sanitizer concentration in the dish machine was measured at 0ppm. PIC told inspector that they will use the three compartment sink until the dish machine is fixed.
2. The chlorine sanitizer in the sani bucket in the kitchen was observed to be unreadable. PIC was made aware and a new sani bucket was made. (COS) 
 Ensure that the sanitizer concentration in the sanitizer buckets and dish machine is continuously checked at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

PIC told inspector that they were going to call the EcoLab technician to get the issue fix. Ensure that the relevant repairs is done to be in compliance with the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

comment: Inspector observed an employee not using appropriate barrier to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Education was provided. Ensure that employees are always aware to use a barrier after handwashing to avoid recontaminating their hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed employee touching ready to eat cookies with the bare hands while wrapping the cookies individually for sale. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees are aware and reminded to avoid touching or handling ready to eat food items with their bare hands at all times.
citation_text: 3-301.11. (B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The dish table to the right of the dish machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in the caulking and needs to be re-sealed. 
2. The holes in the wall to the right of the dish machine need to be sealed. 
3. The handwashing sink in the women’s bathroom that is on the right side of the building is observed to have the sealing separated from the wall. Ensure that this is re-sealed. 
4. There is frost accumulation on the fans of the walk-in freezer. Ensure that the issue causing the frost accumulation is repaired. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide verification that the food handlers were notified and acknowledge their responsibility to report potential foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis. A fresh copy of the Reporting Agreement given out by SCDPH was given to the PIC. They are instructed to make copies and have all food handlers in the facility review and sign one. Maintain these copies available at the facility for future verifications. The inspector planned to follow-up on this matter at the same time that the sink repairs were reviewed 10 days from this inspection.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. 

On arrival there was not an available procedure for cleaning up vomit/diarrheal events in the facility. A fresh copy of the procedure given by SCDPH was given during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that a procedure is maintained at the facility and that all staff know where it is and how to use it moving forward.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. 

1) An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. 2) An employee was observed to begin handling food contact single service items without hand washing. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to review hand washing, specifically WHEN to wash hands with all staff in the facility. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times required by the code moving forward.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

Raw eggs were observed over milk in the display walk in cooler. The PIC was consulted and the eggs moved to the bottom shelf to correct. Ensure that foods in the coolers are stored so that raw items are not stored over items that are considered Ready-To-Eat.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sanitizer available in the three part sink was observed low on the inspector’s test strips. Approximate concentration of quat was observed below 100 ppm. This chemical needs a minimum concentration of 200-400 ppm to effectively sanitizer food contact surfaces. The kitchen staff and PIC were consulted and remade the water to correct. Only a single table was placed in the sink at that time and was not sufficient for reaching the correct concentration. Education was conducted and the bottle read to them. One tablet is sufficient for 1.5 gallons of water and there were 3-4 gallons of water in the sink at the time that it was made. More tablets were added to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are produced and maintained at effective concentrations at all times in the facility.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. title: Food separated and protected.

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
Cooler still not fixed from the July 8, 2026 inspection.
The drawer cooler across from the cookline was observed with an ambient temperature of 57F-60F. The facility does not keep a record log and the employees were unaware of when the cooler stopped working. See that the unit is serviced to maintain proper cold holding temperatures of 41F of below. The employees were instructed to not use the cooler until it is serviced. Will follow-up on July 24, 2026.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with a biofilm. The PIC was informed and turned off the machine. The facility will purchase food-grade ice for service until the machine can be emptied and sanitized. Inspector will follow-up on July 31, 2026 to ensure the ice machine interior is clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the floor and walls below the triple sink and dish machine to be damaged and harboring drain flies. The PIC stated that a previous inspector advised sealing the wall with spray foam, but this foam is not easily cleanable and therefore has become damaged and soiled over time. Inspector recommends cutting out all foam and repairing with a durable, non-absorbent material (painted drywall, NUDO panel, silicone sealant, etc.). Removing this foam will also benefit in pest control measures. Ensure walls and floors are sealed to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of cooked shrimp stored inside of a line cooler that lacked date marking. The PIC added a date marking to the shrimps to correct the violation. Ensure that all cooked foods are date marked with the date that it is prepared.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide a vomit/diarrheal event clean up kit or procedures. They normally have a body fluid kit sufficient for this issue available but were unable to find/produce it during this inspection. A procedure was given during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the procedures/kit is available at al times in the facility.

[C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

1) An employee was observed to handle their phone and not wash their hands prior to resuming food service. 2) An employee was observed to change gloves without hand washing. 3) An employee was observed to touch their clothing and head without hand washing. 4) An employee was observed to have a drink and not wash their hands prior to resuming food service. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to refresh hand washing procedures (including when to wash hands) with all staff to prevent future issues. Wash hands whenever they are contaminated and prior to handling foods/food contact surfaces.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Employee vitamins and supplements were observed stored intermixed with items for service in the sushi station. CORRECTED: PIC moved items to separate storage away from items for service, into the areas designated for employee use.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed multiple containers of cooked rice that were cooling inside of sealed plastic containers. The rice had only been cooling for about 30 minutes. CORRECTED: PIC was educated that containers must be uncovered during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. Inspectors and PIC also discussed using shallower pans (like baking trays) to cool the rice, as they cool faster than deep trays. During the inspection the covers were removed. Ensure that food is always cooled using the proper procedure.
citation_text: 3-501.15(B) Cooling Methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers in which FOOD is being cooled shall be: (1) Arranged in the EQUIPMENT to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls; and (2) Loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination as specified under Subparagraph 3-305.11(A)(2), during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the FOOD. [C]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed fish with a label stating that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing was thawing within the package in the sushi station. CORRECTED: The PIC was educated and employees removed the fish from the packaging. Ensure that reduced oxygen packaged fish is always removed from the package before thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

See that all employees are educated on correct handwashing procedures. Always use a barrier (paper towel) to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. This prevents recontaminating freshly washed hands.

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Not all employees working at the time of the inspection had food handler certificates. Discussed with PIC that all employees will need to have at least a food handler certificate if not a certified food protection manager. Ensure that every employee obtains a food handler certificate if handling food or clean dishes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
Inspector observed the prep table fail to hold proper cold holding temperatures during today’s visit. A part has been ordered for the cooler which should deliver either today or tomorrow. Time as a control is in use for items in the prep cooler until the repairs are complete. Inspector observed a dry erase board for time monitoring, but a loading time was not listed. An employee was able to tell the inspector what time the cooler was loaded, and the cooler was within the 4-hour window. Ensure time records are kept at ALL TIMES. Inspector will follow-up on July 24, 2026 to ensure the prep table is repaired. 

The prep table was also not functioning during today’s visit. The PIC was aware of the issue and is using ice baths in the cooler. However, the ice baths are inadequate for cold holding. A tray of sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler measured 53.3F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the prep table was loaded at 11am. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the prep cooler (sliced tomatoes, diced tomatoes, sliced cheese, cut lettuce, dairy based sauces, deli ham) were discarded at 3pm. The service technician claims that the coils of the prep cooler are clogged with grease. The technician is currently working to clean the coils and repair the equipment. Until the repair is complete, staff must use time as a control for items in the prep table. Ice baths are not required in addition to time as a control, but are useful for quality. 
A follow-up will be conducted on July 13, 2026 to ensure proper cold holding is restored in the walk-ins and prep table.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspectors observed foods listed as “white tuna” on the tablet menu for customers. On the letter of parasite destruction, it was observed the facility orders “Escolar”, which is not the same species as “white tuna.” According to the FDA, Escolar (Lepidocybium flavobrunneum) is not to be sold under the name white tuna. Acceptable market names for this fish are escolar or oilfish. White tuna refers to albacore tuna (Thunnus alalunga). CORRECTED- PIC changed the electronic menus to list escolar properly. Ensure that foods are labeled as ordered to prevent misbranding.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented. [P]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler due to lack of access. Discussed with PIC. PIC said that the certification will be brought to the facility. Ensure that a folder containing all paperwork is available and accessible at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple instances of hand washing, which ended by using bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted as the inspector modeled proper hand washing. Ensure hand washing occurs for at least 20 seconds, with soap, and warm running water. Hand washing should conclude with drying hands with a paper towel, and then using that same paper towel to turn off the faucet (to avoid recontaminating hands).
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. Ensure the dish machine is primed and tested at a frequency to ensure the proper concentration of food contact surfaces- as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine).

citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the following temperature control for food safety (TCS) items stored in the non-operational standing cooler: ranch, blue cheese, thousand island dressing, and French dressing (all labeled either “Refrigerate after opening, or keep Refrigerated”- this categorization indicates that the foods are TCS). Blue cheese (stated to have been in the cooler the longest) was observed to have an internal temperature of 56F. The toppings labeled  “refrigerate after opening” in the countertop cooler were also observed at 45F.  CORRECTED- items in the cheesecake cooler were moved to the walk in cooler, and items in the dessert topping station were moved to the front. All cold held TCS foods must be held under 41F. The temperature danger zone is 41-135F. Pathogens that cause food-borne illness proliferate in this temperature range.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. comment: Inspector observed the counter top cooler (used for dessert toppings) as well as the standing silver cheesecake cooler to fail to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #33. The PIC stated the item is under warranty and they are waiting on a part. Do NOT store any TCS foods (including those labeled “Refrigerate after opening”) in this cooler until it is fixed. The ambient temperature was observed to be 52F. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/20/26.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

comment:
Inspector observed the retail cooler for self service “to-go” cheesecake samples to not be labeled. Labeling must include a list of ingredients by weight, and identification of common allergens. Inspector will verify compliance during the 7/20 follow up inspection.

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Several cans of cream of coconut were observed with major dents and stored on the rack as if they were ready for use. When discussed the PIC stated that they had already requested a refund, however it would be easy for an employee to grab a can and use it as if it were available and safe to use. Once asked, the PIC moved the cans to the back by their desk so that they were separated and not easily used by mistake. Ensure that foods with damaged packaging are stored separately from foods intended for service to prevent possible mistakes and illnesses.
