title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Numerous flies are still observed throughout the facility, specifically by the hand sink and the mop sink next to the ice machine. Fly strips were suggested by the PIC and an enzymatic cleaner was suggested by the inspector for the drains. The PIC is instructed to contact their pest control agency for maintenance and to reduce/remove the pests. A follow up is being set for one month out to allow time for the chemicals likely needed to take effect.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was no sanitizer observed in the deli kitchen as food was being portioned during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. A sani bucket was made. Ensure that there is a sanitizer present and at the appropriate concentration at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Staff was observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees are reminded to always wash their hands before donning new gloves in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the hand sink adjacent the large standing freezer in the back was observed to be coming off. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspector observed a food handler on staff who had not signed their Employee Health Reporting Agreement. CORRECTED- employee read and signed the SCDPH acknowledgement of reportable food-borne illnesses. Ensure all food handlers are aware of reportable Foodborne illnesses, and symptoms associated with food borne illness.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Allergen awareness notice
comment:
Inspector observed no Allergen awareness signage posted. Inspector will either email or drop off a paper copy to the person in charge (PIC) so that the allergen notice may be posted to be visible at the point of sale. Facilities should display an allergen notice to remind consumers to report potential food associated allergens to the facility.

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods above 41F.
1) FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs sitting at an ambient temperature of 58F.
2) TCS foods in the kitchen prep cooler (including but not limited to raw hamburger, cut tomatoes, shredded lettuce, and cheese) to have internal temperatures between 56-59F.
The PIC verified the eggs and items in the prep cooler had been out since 8 AM (2 hours).  CORRECTED- items were moved under TIME AS CONTROL- to be used or discarded with a total of 4 hours (by 2PM). When items are unable to maintain temperature control (below 41F or above 135F) they must be used or discarded within 4 hours. Ensure all  temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F, OR marked to be used or discarded within 4 hours after removing from temperature control to limit the growth of pathogens.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the kitchen prep cooler (nearest the dish machine) to be failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F. The PIC stated the unit will be serviced or replaced. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/20 to verify compliance. Contact the inspector sooner if the problem is resolved.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed single service to-go containers with the food contact surface facing upwards at the server station. CORRECTED- the containers were flipped. Ensure food contact surfaces are inverted or placed under covering to protect from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the inner gaskets of the double door cooler (at the kitchen’s entry) to be significantly frayed. Discussed with the PIC. Replace by the next routine inspection to prevent potential contamination of foods.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed an electrical outlet below the kitchen microwave to be lacking plate covers. Place covers on these outlets to prevent the entry of food or other debris, which may enter the wall. Physical facilities should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee wash hands, then fail to use a barrier to shut off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was conducted. Ensure hand washing ends with the use of a barrier to shut off the faucet after drying hands to prevent recontaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 6 cans (4 tomato paste and 2 green beans) with large dents along the seams. CORRECTED- discussed with the person in charge (PIC). Items were removed from service to be returned to their supplier for credit. Ensure all hermetically sealed cans are inspected upon arrival. Large dents along the body and any dents along the seams may act as a point of entry and harborage for Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed ground beef stored above pollock in the outdoor 2 door cooler. CORRECTED- the ground beef was moved above the chicken. Ensure all foods in coolers are stored to reflect proper storage order (ready to eat foods on top, followed by increasing cooking temperatures) to prevent cross contamination. Inspector provided an educational handout to share with employees.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the baffles of the ice machine. CORRECTED- the PIC wiped the baffles with a sanitizer cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple methods of food contact sanitation failing to meet sanitizing requirements:
1) The chemical sanitizing quaternary ammonia at the bar triple sink was below the required concentration. CORRECTED- an extra sanitizer tablet was added, and 200 ppm quaternary ammonia was observed.
2) The kitchen’s heat sanitizing dish machine took 3 runs to meet proper heat sanitizing temperatures (160F and above). 
Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to ensure proper sanitizing concentration (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia) and temperatures (160F and above).
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed a difference of 6F between the facility’s heat plate and their own. Discussed replacing the battery. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/16 to verify that the facility’s temperature sanitizing dish plate is able to accurately measure the surface temperature of dishes.
citation_text: 4-203.12 Temperature Measuring Devices, Ambient Air and Water. (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be designed to be easily readable and accurate to ±1.5°C in the intended range of use. (B) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. [Pf]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Two of the three employees present during today’s inspection do not have Food Handler Certificates. The inspector provided a handout of ANSI-Approved courses to the PIC. Ensure all employees who do any degree of food handling (including bar tending and waiting tables) complete Food Handler training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed the continuous donning of gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. Ensure that proper handwashing is practiced before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) in the facility at the start of the inspection and there was food preparation and serving taking place. CORRECTED- A CFPM arrived during the inspection and was educated on making sure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of food preparation, cooking, and serving.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The three-door cooler in the facility is observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Crab Rangoon filling probed to be at 50F. Raw beef probed to be at 51F. The TCS food items in the cooler will be discarded. An employee stated that they will be taking the tofu, eggs, and meat in the cooler home. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The three-door cooler in the facility is observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Raw beef was probed to be at a temperature of 51F and crab Rangoon filling probed to be at 50F. The TCS food items in the cooler will be voluntarily discarded. A follow up is scheduled for 7/10/2026 to ensure that the cooler is repaired and is properly cold holding. A spot check will be conducted on 7/9/2026 regarding the cooler.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: The PIC is not currently a CFPM and is missing critical food safety knowledge at the time of this inspection. Education was given in relation to the observed violations and concerns noted during this inspection. More knowledge is needed and would normally be covered by the CFPM course that is required. While education will be deemed as sufficient at this time other enforcement is likely if this becomes an ongoing issue.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(1) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE (PIC) shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: On arrival, there is not a CFPM available in the facility. The kitchen manager stated that they should be going through the process soon. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all food handling shifts in the facility moving forward.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed employee donning gloves multiple times without handwashing. Activities were halted and education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees are reminded to always wash their hands before donning gloves including in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival, a cluster of scrubs and other items were observed stored in the hand sink. Education was carried out. The items were removed making the hand sink accessible. Ensure that all hand sink within the facility designated for handwashing are use for handwashing only at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw pork chops stored over tomatoes and other ready to eat food items in the walk-in cooler. The kitchen manager was made aware. The pork chops were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored in the appropriate order to avoid cross contamination at all times.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was no sanitizer observed int he kitchen at the beginning of today’s inspection. Education was carried out. A sani bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm for quaternary ammonia. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made and available during food prep and service at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
The following date marking issues were observed. 
1. A container of cooked and cooled green beans were observed without the adequate date marking in the walk-in cooler by the kitchen.
2. A container of cooked and cooled chess and potatoes was observed not properly date marked in the walk-in cooler next to the kitchen. 
3. A container of cooked and cooled brisket was observed without proper date marking in the walk-in cooler outside the building by the stage.
The kitchen manager told inspector that the items listed above were made yesterday but the person on shift forgot to date marked in them. Ensure that all food items that are going to stay over 24-hours from the date they were cooked or made are date marked properly at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
comment: Inspector did not observe any sign of a consumer advisory present within the facility during today’s inspection. Education was carried out and a placard was provided. Ensure that there is a display of a consumer advisory visible for patron to see within the facility.
citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed a series of boxes filled with food items stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. The boxes were removed and stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least sis inches above the floor protecting food items from splash and other contaminations at all times.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Allergen awareness notice
comment:
There was no visible allergen awareness notice observed within the facility during today’s inspection. A copy was provided for correction. Ensure that the allergen awareness is posted and visible for customers at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed no barrier to be used by staff when hand washing. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were properly rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used when handling handwashing faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed cheese to be cold holding at 55F. Discussed with PIC, cheese was placed in the back right corner of prep cooler directly next to hot holding. A lid was brought to cheese and was moved to a different location is prep cooler, cheese then tested at 41F. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Observed no thermometer to be present within walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, thermometer was brought to walk in cooler. Ensure all coolers have a thermometer available.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed top of microwave and hot holding trays to have an accumulation of food debris present. Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the three compartment sink, dump sink, and the hand sink adjacent the dump sink were observed not sealed properly. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the sinks mentioned will be caulked appropriately. Ensure that these sinks are caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed a missed handwashing opportunity with a staff member preparing food items. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and hands were washed. Ensure staff is washing hands as needed.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed a coffee pot to be resting in hand sink. Discussed with PIC, pot was removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sinks are used solely for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers licenses to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, licenses will be acquired by staff. Ensure any food handling employee has completed the food handlers training within 30 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a certified food protection manager present despite the facility being in full operation. The PIC mentioned that she is working to become a CFPM pretty soon. Ensure that there is always CFPM available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer solution along the cookline was observed with a concentration of 0ppm (CL). The employees mentioned that the solution was prepared early in the morning. Discussed frequently changing sani solutions, as the solution loses its concentration the longer it sits. The solution was remade and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that sani solutions are maintained at the manufacturer's recommended concentration and are switched roughly every 4 hours (or if soiled).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was residue starting to form on the baffles of the ice machine. Shown to the PIC. Suggested cleaning ice baffles as frequent as necessary to keep them clean. Ensure that baffles are cleaned to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There were various time/temperature control foods (TCS) stored inside of a nonfunctional drawer cooler with an internal temperature of 57F-60F. The PIC mentioned that the foods were placed inside of the cooler at 9am. The facility was instructed to discard foods due to being held well above 41F. Violation corrected. The ambient temperature of the kitchen was above 75F degrees and the extreme heat could be exhausting the drawer coolers. See that the cooler is serviced to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The drawer cooler across from the cookline was observed with an ambient temperature of 57F-60F. The facility does not keep a record log and the employees were unaware of when the cooler stopped working. See that the unit is serviced to maintain proper cold holding temperatures of 41F of below. The employees were instructed to not use the cooler until it is serviced. Will follow-up on July 21, 2026.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, the only employee who is a certified food protection manager wasn’t present. The cfpm arrived shortly into the visit to correct the violation. The other two owners (married couple), are certified food handlers. Discussed the need of having at least 2 employees manager certified to cover all hours of operation. A website link was provided to the PIC to assist at least one employee with the certified manager’s course in Mandarin.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were a couple bins of raw chicken stored above raw beef inside of the walk in cooler. Shown to the PIC and the bins were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that raw chicken is always stored beneath any raw beef products to protect against cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution created despite the facility being in full operation. A sanitizer solution was created and tested at 100ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that a sani solution is always available if preparing, handling, or serving food.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed beef thawing on the countertop in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and the beef was moved to the sink to thaw under running cold water. Ensure staff are thawing food under refrigeration or running water at all times. Thawing cannot occur on the countertop in ambient temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket on the cook line measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed and replaced the bucket. There were multiple rags stored in the same small bucket. Too many rags in the same bucket can cause the concentration of the chemical to rapidly decrease. Inspector recommends reducing the number of rags in the bucket or increasing the size of the bucket to prevent this issue from occurring in the future.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed a food handler use their phone with gloved hands. CORRECTED- education was conducted about times to wash hands. Hands must be washed after (but not limited to) any of the following activities: touching a personal electronic device, using the restroom, between working with raw and ready to eat foods, and after touching anything that may contaminate hands. Educate staff regularly about times to wash hands and proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: THIRD REPEAT: Inspector observed single use to-go bowls submerged in a 5 gallon buckets of soy sauce, tea, and sugar (for use as a scoop). The inspector informed the person in charge (PIC) that scoops in service must have handles to avoid bare hand contact with the ready to eat (RTE) food items. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the soup bowl with a gloved hand. Inspector advised the use of ladles or scoops with handle for the future. Utensils used for RTE foods, ice, and sauces must have a distinction between food contact and hand contact surfaces to prevent bare hands contamination. Due to the fact that this violation has been noted for four consecutive inspections, a follow up date is scheduled for 7/22 with the SCDPH Food Program Supervisor to conduct education.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw chicken stored over raw beef in the grill protein cooler. CORRECTED- items were rearranged to reflect proper storage order. Beef must be cooked to 155F, and chicken must be cooked to 165F to eliminate pathogens that may cause food-borne illness.  Ensure all foods in cooling units are stored in a manner to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the front baffles of the ice machine. CORRECTED- the baffles were wiped with a sanitizer cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of any debris. Food contact surfaces must be maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed an accumulation of rust on the shelves of the walk in cooler. Discussed either cleaning/ repainting, or replacing the shelves. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and designed to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.[C]

comment: Inspector observed personal items for staff stored above items for service in the sliding beverage cooler at the entry to the sushi station. Education was conducted regarding the storage of personal items. Personal items should be stored below items for service to prevent potential contamination of foods.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed jalapeños (stated to have been opened yesterday by the person in charge (PIC)) being stored in the can. CORRECTED- kitchen staff transferred the contents of the can into a food safe container. The original can is not rated to safely hold the food material after opening the can. Ensure acidic food items from cans (such as jalapeños and tomato paste) are transferred (and date marked) into a food safe container if held over 24 hours to prevent contamination of ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw chicken and beef stored above ready to eat items (tamales and cut vegetables) in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED-kitchen staff moved the chicken to the bottom shelf, and the beef between the chicken and ready to eat foods. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.

comment: Inspector observed cut lettuce in an open container below the refrigeration lines in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- a lid was placed over the lettuce. Ensure all foods in cooling units are covered to protect against contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris at the soda gun nozzle at the bar. CORRECTED- the item was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed foods in the toppings prep cooler to have internal temperatures between 45-48F. CORRECTED foods were voluntarily discarded. Replacement items were put in an ice bath. All items in the top of the cooler are time/ temperature control for food safety (TCS); (pico de gallo, cut tomatoes, shredded lettuce, shredded cheese, and sour cream). TCS foods must be keep below 41F, above 135F, or moved under time as control (to be used or discarded within 4 hours). Discussed monitoring foods on ice bath with a thermometer, or using small batches and implementing time as control.

comment: Inspector observed the toppings prep cooler failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #22. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/17 to verify compliance. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
(1) Observed several items in the sandwich meat prep cooler were not below 41°F, including: beef 47°F (probed), rotisserie chicken 49°F (probed), provolone 47°F (probed), cheddar 47°F (probed), turkey 47°F (probed), ham 47°F (probed), tuna 48°F (probed). CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded these items, as they had been prepared longer than 4 hours previously, so they were not being controlled by either time or temperature. All other items that were sufficiently cold holding at or below 41°F were moved to the walk-in cooler.
(2) Observed sliced tomatoes in the short cooler was not below 41°F, and was measured at 52°F (probed). CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the tomatoes, as they had been prepared longer than 4 hours previously, so they were not being controlled by either time or temperature. All other items that were cold holding in the short cooler were moved to the walk-in cooler, as they were either not RTE, TCS, or had been prepared within 4 hours.
Ensure that RTE, TCS foods are cold held at 41°F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
(1) Observed that sandwich meat prep cooler was not holding proper temperatures for cold holding non-frozen foods. Temperatures were too warm, over 41°F (see #22). Staff reports that the prep cooler ices over when left running overnight (running too cold), so staff procedure to is store food in the walk-in cooler overnight and turn off the prep cooler, and then turn on the prep cooler in the morning and move the food from the walk-in to the prep cooler. PIC has placed a work order to fix the prep cooler.
(2) Observed that short counter cooler was not holding proper temperatures for cold holding non-frozen foods. Internal food temperatures were too warm, over 41°F (see #22). Ambient temperature was above 46°F. Please repair the short cooler so that it holds foods below 41°F.
Until coolers are repaired, staff will prepare smaller amounts of food and work out of the walk-in cooler. If items must be out of the walk-in cooler for a length of time, then staff will use time as a control: food will be used or discarded within 4 hours.
Inspector will Follow Up to confirm that prep cooler and short cooler are keeping proper cold-holding temperatures. Ensure that all cold holding equipment is sufficient to maintain foods at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.

CORRECTED: PIC was able to borrow their neighboring establishment’s probe-style thermometer during the inspection, and located their own probe-style thermometer soon after the inspection had concluded. Ensure that a probe-styled thermometer is readily accessible to measure temperatures.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

Surfaces around floors and walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure these repairs occur before the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop that was stored on the floor, and not stored above the mop sink nor in the basket of the mop bucket where it can sufficiently air-dry. title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: A sanitizer bucket was observed to be in the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the sanitizer bucket was removed from the sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are accessible at all times for employee use and are only used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There were observed to be cut vegetables stored directly in grocery bags. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the vegetables were switched into a ziploc bag. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and cannot be sanitized. Ensure that food is stored in a package that protects the integrity of the contents to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The Chlorine sanitizer bucket was observed to test at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and are remade if not at a label-recommended concentration. It is typically recommended to change sanitizer buckets every two to four hours.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The bar gun soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- These nozzles and dispensers were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that nozzles and soda machines are frequently cleaned to prevent an accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- An employee was observed to wash their hands, then not use a barrier when turning off the faucet. CORRECTED- The employee was educated on proper handwashing and the use of a barrier when turning off the faucet. Ensure that staff are educated on proper handwashing procedures.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.

Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and cannot be properly sanitized. Ensure that food is stored in a package that protects the integrity of the contents and does not expose it to contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

comment: There was observed to be raw chicken in a cooler drawer above raw pork. There was also raw bacon stored behind eggrolls in another cooler drawer. CORRECTED- The raw pork was moved to be above the raw chicken and the raw bacon was moved in front of the eggrolls. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display. A storage order handout was provided to the facility.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice baffle was observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the ice baffle was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: An employee was observed to wash and rinse dishes in the triple sink, but did not sanitize them prior to air drying. The sanitizer compartment of the triple sink was observed to not be set-up to be able to sanitize the dishes. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and a handout was provided in Spanish on proper warewashing procedures. The dishes were sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that staff are educated on proper warewashing procedures and utensils and equipment food-contact surfaces are being properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-703.11(A) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (A) Hot water manual operations by immersion for at least 30 seconds and as specified under § 4-501.111.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The following TCS foods were observed to be held above 41F: 

- The Traditional Barbecue sauce that states to “Refrigerate After Opening” on the label was observed to be stored outside of cold holding under the steam table. The PIC stated that it was opened two days ago and voluntarily discarded it. This barbecue sauce was previously placed under time as control, but the facility has since ceased using that method. The PIC stated that the sauce will be stored in the cooler moving forward. 
- There were portioned cups of sauces that were observed to be stored outside of cold holding. These sauces were placed outside of cold holding at 10am, according to the PIC, and it was discussed to discard these by 2pm. The PIC stated that they will cold hold these sauces on ice going forward. 
- The preparation cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F in the bottom of the cooler and lettuce probed to be at 48F in the top of the cooler. The PIC stated that the lid of the preparation cooler was left open overnight, but that only limes were left in the cooler. The TCS foods in the top of the cooler were placed under Time as Control to allow them to still work out of the cooler. The PIC stated that these foods were placed in the cooler at 10:30am and will be discarded by 2:30pm. The foods in the bottom of the cooler were recently placed in it and were moved into the walk-in cooler. The bottom of the preparation cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 38F by the end of the inspection. It was discussed to make sure to check the temperature of the cooler before placing TCS foods in it if it has been left open overnight. It is also recommended to close the lid of the preparation cooler in-between uses. The temperature of the preparation cooler will be spot checked at the 7/14/2026 follow up for violation #48. 

Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There were multiple TCS food items made in-house in the walk-in cooler that were observed to not be date-marked, including:

- A container of rice. 
- A container of beans. 
- A container of cheese sauce. 

The kitchen manager date-marked these items during the inspection. There was also inconsistent date-marking observed in the walk-in cooler. According to the PIC, staff members were date-marking use the day of the month and the year (ex: 3/26). Ensure that the method of date-marking is consistent and that staff are trained to date-mark TCS food items that are made or opened in-house and are held for over 24 hours. Date-marking will be spot checked at the 7/14/2026 scheduled follow-up for violation #48.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: An employee was observed to use a wiping cloth to wipe food-contact surfaces and store it on the counter in between uses. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are trained to store wiping cloths in the sanitizer bucket in-between uses to prevent bacteria growth on the wiping cloth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility is observed to not have any Quaternary ammonium sanitizer test strips. A follow up is scheduled for 7/14/2026 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are test strips for every type of sanitizer that is used in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were cove tiles to the left of the mop sink that were observed to be coming loose and need sealed back to the wall. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that the cove tiles are repaired.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is observed to not be a drain cover on the drain in front of the triple sink. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always a drain cover on all drains to prevent clogging.
citation_text:
6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning 
methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

title: Food handler training
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There were no food handler certificates available for any of the employees. The PIC was instructed to ensure that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The Certified Food Protection Manager was observed to not have their Allergen training certificate. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility that has their Allergen training during all hours of operation and food preparation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) A knife hanging in ready to use position in the kitchen.
2) The ice scoop holder at the server station.
CORRECTED- items were brought to the main kitchen dish machine for ware-washing.
Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency to remain clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed the multiple dish machines failing to meet sanitizing requirements:
1) The heat sanitizing restaurant dish machine reached 153F after four runs. The facility consulted their engineer to check the heat boosters. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/10 to verify that the machine is reaching a minimum heat sanitizing temperature of 160F.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The chemical sanitizing dish machine at the Globe was dispensing 0 ppm sanitizer. CORRECTED- the machine was primed multiple times and the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Chlorine. 
Dishes produced in the restaurant should must be brought to the main kitchen dish machine for proper ware washing until the machine is serviced. Ensure all dish machines are tested frequently to verify that the machine is reaching the sanitizing concentration (or a minimum temperature of 160F) as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed the shelving in the walk-in cooler to be heavily soiled with debris and microbial growth. The PIC was informed that the walk-in cooler must be kept clean to sight and touch at all times. Mold and other microbial growth poses a hazard for food items that are cooling in the walk-in uncovered. A follow-up will be conducted on July 17, 2026 to ensure proper sanitization of all shelves in the walk-in cooler.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the sandwich cooler 1 fail to properly cold hold foods. The PIC is aware of the issue and has requested replacement coolers. Ice baths or time as a control are currently in use for all TCS foods in these coolers. A follow-up will be conducted on July 17, 2026 to ensure adequate coolers have been acquired that hold TCS foods at 41F or less at all times.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The PIC was observed to make a sanitizer bucket that tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium. The PIC used the sanitizer dispenser to fill the bottom of the bucket and then filled the rest with water. The PIC was educated that the sanitizer dispenser is diluted and does not need to be mixed with more water. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade using only the dispenser and tested to be at 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are at a label-recommended concentration to make sure that food-contact surfaces are being properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was not a sanitizer bucket made at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 200ppm of Quaternary ammonium. The PIC was educated to make sure that there is always a sanitizer bucket made and available during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The triple sink in the preparation area and both bathroom sinks next to the fireplace area are observed to be in need of being re-sealed. Ensure that they are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Portioned salsa containers are being stored in a cooler where the shelves are coated with mold. The containers are uncovered and are in direct contact with mold spores possibly contaminating food items. Discussed the high risk of cross contamination with the person in charge. Ensure that salsas are moved to a different cooler and the shelves are cleaned to remove the mold. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There were uncovered sauces stored inside of the produce cooler that were directly underneath the air compressor. The ceiling of the cooler also contained a bit of mold accumulation. Ensure that foods are always covered and protected against any possible contamination. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026 to see that foods are covered or discarded.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

As for the other products, they were transferred to a different container/box as a way to reduce attraction and remove insects. Discussed washing produce thoroughly before prepping for service.
