citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

The test strip was shown to the PIC and more water was added to the solution to correct the violation. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzle of the gun holder in the bar area is accumulated with black debris on the inner surfaces. Shown to the PIC. Because this surface is in direct contact with liquids, see that the surface is sanitized every night when closing. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were various Time/Temperature control foods that lacked date marking inside of both walk in coolers. These items included meats, sauces, rice, etc. Discussed with the PIC that any TCS foods that are prepared in house must be date marked with the date of preparation. Ensure that TCS foods are never held longer than seven days after they are prepared. Will follow-up on July 16, 2026.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There was an abundance of gnats mainly in the back storage area where dry goods are stored, as well as the room furthest to the back of the premise (where ice machine is located). The gnats appeared inside of mesh bags that contained whole onions, chile, and potatoes. The facility was instructed to stored onions in a different container/box to remove the trapped insects. While the onions were transferred to a different container, the amount of gnats present will cause for a follow-up. Ensure that the premise is free of insects and be sure to transferred vegetables to sealed tight containers if attracting insects. Will follow-up July 16, 2026.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

Shown to the PIC and he mentioned having the shelves cleaned as soon as possible. Ensure that shelves are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold buildup (and other debris) and to protect against cross contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

See that the plumbing is serviced by a license plumber. Ensure that sewage is maintained in a sanitary manner and never present inside of the facility. citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Garbage and refuse are properly disposed; facilities are maintained.
comment: There was leftover food and beer bottles that appeared left from previous nights inside of the back storage room. There were several gnats swarming the leftover food. Shown to the PIC and the objects were discarded to correct the violation. Discussed that all trash should be removed from the premise when closing for the night to prevent harboring conditions for insects and pest. Ensure to educate staff on the removal of all trash within the facility.
citation_text: 5-502.11 Frequency. REFUSE, recyclables, and returnables shall be removed from the PREMISES at a frequency that will minimize the development of objectionable odors and other conditions that attract or harbor insects and rodents.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed burger holder to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, warmer was turned to a hotter setting and tested at 155F. Ensure any TCS item is being hot held at at least 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Personal cleanliness.
comment: Observed PIC to be wearing a sleeveless shirt. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and sleeveless shirts will no longer be used. Ensure proper clothing is worn in kitchen to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-304.11 Clean Condition. Food employees shall wear clean outer clothing to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed food items to be stored on floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were moved to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the hand sink int he kitchen was observed to be coming off. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the hand sink will be caulked to the wall properly. Ensure that the hand sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past/missing the correct date marking. Discussed with PIC, items that were missing dates were properly date marked, and items held past date marking maximum were discarded. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked, and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia sanitizer available in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure there is sanitizer available in the kitchen at all times to promote proper sanitization.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and prep table fail to hold proper cold holding temperatures during today’s visit. A baked potato in the walk-in measured 52.5F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the cooler only started warming this early afternoon. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food were moved to the beer cooler until repairs can be completed. 
The prep table was also not functioning during today’s visit. The PIC was aware of the issue and is using ice baths in the cooler. However, the ice baths are inadequate for cold holding. A tray of sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler measured 53.3F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the prep table was loaded at 11am. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the prep cooler (sliced tomatoes, diced tomatoes, sliced cheese, cut lettuce, dairy based sauces, deli ham, and shell egg) were discarded at 3pm. Until the repair is complete, staff must use time as a control for items in the prep table. Ice baths are not required in addition to time as a control, but are useful for quality. Staff plan to use dry erase marker on the glass lid of the table to indicate discard time for each item.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
3rd Repeat Violation

Observed cooked pork stored in the prep cooler and cheese sauce and green beans stored in the walk-in cooler to be missing a proper date mark. These items are considered ready-to-eat (RTE), time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Any RTE TCS foods need to be date marked after opening, preparing, or portioning into a new container. Ensure staff are practicing proper date marking to prevent bacteria accumulation in food. A follow-up will be conducted on 7/6/2026 to ensure proper date marking practices are being conducted in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
Inspector observed the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and prep table fail to hold proper cold holding temperatures during today’s visit. The walk-in cooler is below 41F, but not functioning. Items in the freezer measured 36F during today’s visit. A baked potato in the walk-in measured 52.5F with a probe thermometer. The PIC is aware of the issue and a service technician was on site during today’s visit. The service technician stated that the vent on the roof is completely clogged with cottonwood fibers. The technician has cleaned the fibers from the vents and now needs to place the cooler in a defrost setting to calibrate/replenish Freon in the system. 

The prep table was also not functioning during today’s visit. The PIC was aware of the issue and is using ice baths in the cooler. However, the ice baths are inadequate for cold holding. A tray of sliced tomatoes in the prep cooler measured 53.3F with a probe thermometer. The PIC stated that the prep table was loaded at 11am. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the prep cooler (sliced tomatoes, diced tomatoes, sliced cheese, cut lettuce, dairy based sauces, deli ham) were discarded at 3pm. The service technician claims that the coils of the prep cooler are clogged with grease. The technician is currently working to clean the coils and repair the equipment. Until the repair is complete, staff must use time as a control for items in the prep table. Ice baths are not required in addition to time as a control, but are useful for quality. 
A follow-up will be conducted on July 13, 2026 to ensure proper cold holding is restored in the walk-ins and prep table.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed flies present in the dish area of the facility. Old frying equipment is being stored on the ground next to the triple sink. The PIC also stated that the lid to the grease trap is damaged. This, along with the moisture from the triple sink, is contributing to fly harborage. Ensure the old equipment is removed and the grease trap lid is repaired. Inspector will follow up on August 4, 2026 to ensure there are no pests present in the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Inspector observed the following storage order violations on the facility:
1. Raw chicken stored above cooked beef barbacoa and carrots
2. Packaged raw whole chickens stored on top of packaged butter and above raw beef
3. Raw beef stored above celery 

The PIC was informed of proper storage order guidelines and the cooler was rearranged. The inspector provided a storage order flyer for staff education.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed scented bleach in use for food-contact sanitizing. The PIC was informed of chemical requirements for food contact surfaces. Proper bleach was available on site. The sanitizer bucket was emptied and refilled with proper chemical. Ensure staff are using unscented, plain bleach with a valid EPA-registered label for sanitizing food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Inspector observed shell eggs stored on the counter with no time as a public health control label indicating discard time. The PIC was informed and labels were added to each flat of eggs. Ensure staff are marking cartons with the time they are removed from the cooler and using or discarding within four hours.
citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Inspector observed a bag of onions, canned cheese, and single service items stored directly on the ground in the dry storage area. The PIC was informed and plans to acquire pallets or crates to elevate the food items from the floor. Ensure all food items are stored at least 6 inches off the ground prior to the next routine inspection. 

Inspector observed no splash guard present between the sods syrup boxes and the mop sink. The shelf of syrups is located right next to the mop sink, risking splash contamination of the syrup boxes from the mop water. Ensure a splash guard is installed prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the head of the mop stored directly in the basin of the mop sink. The PIC was informed and the mop was inverted. Ensure staff are storing the mop in the manner that allows for proper drip drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee wash their hands, turn-off the faucet, and then dry hands. A barrier was not used to turn-off the faucet. Corrected during the inspection by halting the behavior and having a discussion with the employee. Hand washing was revisited. Proper technique was discussed and demonstrated.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed the following areas that are in need of cleaning or a change of container to prevent cross-contamination of food:
(i) The ventilation hood has grease and dust dripping from the baffles and beginning to accumulate beyond the drip tray of the unit. The baffles are a portion of the hood system able to be cleaned by the facility staff. See that the baffles are cleaned at a frequency suitable to maintain them clean and free of hanging debris. 
(ii) Observed a grocery sack being used to store dried orange peel that will be used for a future sauce. Grocery sacks are not an approved food-grade package. CORRECTED: Staff moved the orange peels to a food-grade package.
(iii) Observed trays of food in the 2-door freezer without a cover. Foods that are not actively cooling should be covered.
(iv) Observed uncovered marinating chicken in a bulk container within the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: covered with baking sheets during the inspection.
(v) Observed the shelving in the walk-in cooler the have some mold growth along the right side beneath the fans. Also, observed a molded can being used to support the base shelving of the lowest right base shelf beneath the fans. See that the shelving is cleaned and the molded can is removed from use. 
(vi) Observed grocery sacks being used to store foods in the reach-in freezers in the back room. See above - cease use of grocery bags for food storage. 
Ensure that food items are covered to prevent cross-contamination or that equipment is cleaned to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The triple sink is observed with some grease and soil around the flood rim. See that the sinks are regularly cleaned between change in use. Clean and scrub the interior basin of the triple sink.
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of breaded sweet and sour chicken that had an internal temperature above 41°F (probed at 50°F). The food had been prepared 2 days before, and had spent an unknown time on the counter and out of temperature. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the chicken. Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at internal temperatures below 41°F if it will not be used within 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a container of egg rolls with a date-mark of 25 June, which was 8 days ago, beyond the 7 day window for keeping TCS, RTE foods. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded the egg rolls. Ensure that RTE, TCS foods that will be kept beyond 24 hours should have a date mark and should be discarded within 7 days, with day 1 being day of preparation or opening, and day 7 being day of discard of final use.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single-use aluminum pans stored upright above the 2-door freezer. CORRECTED: PIC inverted the aluminum pans during the inspection. Ensure that all single-use and single-service articles are stored to protect them from contamination until used, either under a shelf or through inversion.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed the facility to have surplus storage in the gaming room adjacent to the kitchen facility that is unorganized and without proper shelving. Most of the boxes of single-service and food items are observed on the floor and atop each-other. See that foods being stored in the gaming room, back storage room, and even the dining room are stored 6” off the floor and organized so you can take count of available product, clean around the product, and insure pests are not present.
citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and (A)(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The upright freezer in the back storage area has a thick accumulation of frost. The frost is so thick as to nearly prevent the movement of the food from the unit. Defrost the freezer.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:
(i) The food debris and spills inside the bottom of the prep cooler.
(ii) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The plumbing beneath the triple sink is observed to be soiled with accumulated grease and food debris. Clean the plumbing and the floor drain. 
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following concerns to be repeated from the pre-opening inspection:
(i) Ceiling tiles in the bathrooms to be acoustic; (1st REPEAT)
(ii) Silicon caulking around the triple sink; (1st REPEAT)
(iii) Lucky Trading/Rice Steamer cabinet is old and base is rotting and vinyl laminate top is peeling; (1st REPEAT)
(iv) Gasket on double door cooler is peeling-away from the door; (1st REPEAT)
(v) Several floor tiles beneath the triple sink remain to be replaced. (1st REPEAT)
Repair the aforementioned items.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: The facility has a number of items stored in the dining room of the facility, the gaming room that is adjacent to the kitchen facility, and in the back storage space. The gaming room space is ideal for the storage of the bulk products associated with the facility. Use the gaming room space and provide some shelving space. Store boxes of single service and food 6” off the floor so they are organized and able to be cleaned around. Move the items from the back storage area that are not food service
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that staff who are handling food do not have Food Handler certificates. Discussed with PIC that there are courses available online in Chinese. Ensure that all staff who are handling food are Food Handler certification from an accredited program.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of both ice machines inside of the kitchen area and the serving station contained mold on the food contact surfaces. Shown to the PIC. The facility will work on getting the baffles cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to maintain them clean. Will follow-up July 14, 2026 to check that baffles have been cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were containers of sliced tomatoes and shredded lettuce stored in drawer coolers with a date marking of 6/21/2026. Time/temperature control (TCS) foods must only be held for a maximum of seven days. The items were discarded by of the employee to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods never exceed the seven day timeframe.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: There are various clean dishes placed on storage racks with the food contact surface faced upright. Discussed with PIC proper storage for clean dishes. Ensure that clean dishes are covered or inverted during storage to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed employee washed their hands, then turned the faucet off with their newly cleaned hands. Reviewed proper handwashing procedure with PIC. Educate staff to use a barrier (such as a paper towel) to turn the faucet off after washing hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
(i) Observed an employee washing a cooking utensil in the cookline handwashing sink. CORRECTED: The practice was interrupted and employees were educated on proper use of handwashing sinks and proper warewashing procedures. Handwashing sinks should only be used for handwashing. Nothing else. When warewashing, utensils must be washed with soapy water, rinsed with clean water, submerged in sanitizer for the manufacturer-recommended contact time, and allowed to air dry before returning to use.
(ii) The bar handsink was observed to contain ice and a spoon. CORRECTED: Staff removed the spoon from the handsink and melted the ice. Ensure handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing, no other purpose.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed containers of raw fish and beef stored over a container of tomatoes in the bottom of a prep cooler. CORRECTED: Staff moved around the food items so that the sliced fresh produce that is not getting cooked was stored above raw animal proteins that are getting cooked. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination, and that raw animal proteins are stored in order of final cooking temperature, with fish and eggs on top, pork and beef in the middle, and chicken and poultry on the bottom.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Multiple containers of whipped cream in the bar cooler were observed without date-marking. CORRECTED: Unlabeled whipped creams were labeled with the date they were opened. Any whipped cream containers that the PIC was unsure of the open date were voluntarily discarded. Ensure ready-to-eat, time/temperature controlled for safety foods are labeled with the date they were opened, and that they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening (day 1 is day of preparation or initial opening).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed some of the staff working did not have Food Handler certificates. PIC is working on scheduling training for staff. Ensure that all staff who handle or prepare food and beverages have Food Handler certificates from an accredited provider by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The handwashing sink in the front customer bathroom now has hot water, but the back employee bathrooms still do not have hot water, according to the PIC. The PIC stated that the water heater needs to be replaced. A follow up is scheduled for 7/13/2026 to ensure that the handwashing sinks in the employee bathrooms have hot and cold water at them. Ensure that all sinks have cold and hot water at them.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were raw, shelled eggs above containers of sauces in the double-door cooler in the dish area. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the eggs to the bottom shelf of the cooler and proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The cooler drawers on the cook-line were observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F. Salmon in the bottom cooler drawer was probed at 50F and beef patties in the top cooler drawer were probed at 49F. According to the PIC, the temperature of the cooler drawers were last checked at 12pm and were observed to be at 39F. The TCS food items in this cooler were placed under Time as Control. It was discussed to use or discard the items by 4pm. The PIC stated that they will cook all of the food items before 4pm. 

The front preparation cooler in the kitchen was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F. A salad dressing in the top of the preparation cooler was probed at 54F and bread was probed in the bottom of the preparation cooler at 58F. According to the PIC, the temperature of the cooler was last checked at 12pm and was at 37F. The TCS food items in the cooler were placed under Time as Control. It was discussed to use or discard the items in this cooler by 4pm. 

Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The cooler drawers were observed to have an ambient temperature of 50F and the front preparation cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 52F. TCS food items in the cooler drawers were probed to be at 50F and 49F and TCS food items in the front preparation cooler were probed to be at 54F and 58F. These food items were placed under Time as Control (see violation #22). A follow up is scheduled on 7/13/2026 to ensure that these coolers have been repaired and are properly cold holding at 41F and below. The top of the front preparation cooler was observed to be being left open when not in use. The kitchen is observed to be extremely hot and it is highly recommended to leave cooler doors closed when they are not actively in use. It is also recommended to check the internal temperatures of coolers at least every two hours to make sure that TCS foods are being properly cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There is not a probe thermometer available to use in the facility. This was discussed with the PIC, who will be ordering another one. A follow up is scheduled for 7/13/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer to accurately measure the internal temperature of foods.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair:

1. FIRST REPEAT- There is tape on the missing handle of the left door of the double door cooler. Tape is not an approved repair mechanism. Ensure that this door handle is properly repaired and the tape is removed.
2. The gaskets on the left preparation cooler in the kitchen are observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that these gaskets are replaced. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall behind the dish machine and behind the sprayer is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it and is in need of being cleaned. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that this is cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

The procedure available in the facility indicates the use of a chemical that is not effective for disinfecting Norovirus, which is a primary concern for this situation. Education was conducted and the company consulted. A bottle of bleach was acquired during this inspection and a hand out given related to the use of bleach to correct. Ensure that all procedures and chemicals in the facility are effective for the health concerns that they are intended to manage.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A rag was observed on the counter during the inspection. The PIC confirmed that it was intended for wiping the counter throughout the day. Education was conducted and the rag moved to the sani bucket to correct. Ensure that the sani rags are stored in a sanitizer of effective concentration at all times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On the inspector’s arrival, the facility was without a ready for use sanitizer as the jug of concentrate had run dry. Education was conducted and the company contacted. A new jug was received during the inspection to correct. Ensure that there is always an available sanitizer in the facility when it is in operation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager at the facility during the inspection. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Both handwashing sinks in the kitchen were observed to be blocked with a trash can. CORRECTED- The trash cans were moved to be next to the handwashing sink and this was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that handwashing sinks are never blocked to allow them to be accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffle of the ice machine and the top of the inside of the ice machine are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- Pepsi arrived during the inspection and cleaned the ice machine. Ensure that the ice machine is being frequently cleaned to make sure it is clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The bar dish machine tested to be at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine sanitizer. The PIC called EcoLab during the inspection. It was discussed to not use the bar dish machine, unless dishes will be manually sanitized after it is used. Ensure that the dish machines are being routinely tested and serviced if not at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The salad preparation cooler was observed to be probing at 64F and was found to be unplugged. CORRECTED- All TCS items in the cooler were discarded and the cooler was plugged back in. It was discussed with the PIC to not store TCS food items in this cooler until it reaches below 41F or to use an ice bath. Ensure that TCS food is stored at 41F and below. The facility has enough cold holding without the use of this cooler. The temperature of this cooler will be spot checked at the scheduled follow up for violation #16 on 7/6/2026.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The back door by the chemicals is observed to have a gap in the bottom of it that allows an entryway for insects and rodents. Discussed weatherstripping the door with the PIC. Ensure that this gap is closed to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The floor in the room with the soda syrups. 
2. The top of the dish machine. 
3. The vent above the dish machine. 
4. The pipes and wall below the dish machine are observed to have a significant accumulation of soil residue. Ensure that this is cleaned to prevent pest harborage conditions. 
5. The floor of the walk-in freezer. 
6. The sliders and bottom of the black display cheesecake cooler. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The dish area is in need of being resealed. The current caulking is observed to be in disrepair and has an accumulation of soil residue on it. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The gasket of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be in disrepair. 
3. The gasket of the cooler drawer containing raw beef patties is observed to be in disrepair. 
4. The gasket of the cooler on the end of the line is observed to be in disrepair. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility uses both quaternary ammonia (wipes) and chlorine bleach (triple sink) to sanitize food contact surfaces. The facility still does not did not have a test kit for chlorine bleach, and the test kit for the quaternary ammonia was observed to have expired 7/1/24. Obtain new test strips for both sanitizers. All chemical sanitizing solutions used for food contact surfaces must have a test kit to verify the concentration recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple area in need of physical repair:
1) The caulking around the mop sink is beginning to darken and fragment.
2) The wall to the left of the dish machine has an accumulation of debris.
Discussed with the person in charge. Replace caulking at the mop sink and clean the wall next to the dish machine.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed single service articles stored on the floor in the dry storage area (black door). Discussed with the person in charge (PIC). Food contact surfaces should be stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against potential contamination. Reorganize or obtain shelving (or milk crates) to store single service articles above the ground.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed loose and missing coving in the hallway and restrooms. Place and seal coving by the next routine inspection to protect walls from water entry.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed were two dead insects underneath the triple sink and under a rack that stores pizza boxes. The facility has active pest control, however, discussed the need to routinely clean back storage areas to help prevent harboring conditions for insects. There was minimal food residue and other debris on the floors of the back storage area. Ensure that insects are removed and the premise is maintained free of insects.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The current caulk that is at the back of the handwashing sink is starting to pull from the wall. There was a significant amount of debris accumulation observed where the broken caulk is placed. Ensure to remove current caulk and seal gap to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There are several broken floor tiles throughout the back storage area. The missing tiles in front of the triple sink have been replaced, however, there are broken and missing tiles under the prep table and along the back wall where the back door is located. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair and that the floor tiles are replaced.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The corner wall seal leading to the entrance of the office area is pulling away from the wall. Shown to the PIC. See that seal is replaced or repaired.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several dented cans stored on the storage rack by the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the dented cans were removed from the storage rack. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect the integrity of food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a container of bleach without a EPA registration number in-use for sanitizer solutions in the bar and sushi areas. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and a different container of bleach that does have a EPA-registered label for food-contact surfaces was located and replaced the other container. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions food food-contact surfaces are made using a chemical with an EPA certification for food grade surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed boba pearls did not have a preparation date listed on them in the bar cooler. PIC clarified that the boba pearls had been cooked and frozen more than 24 hours before service. CORRECTED: PIC added the date of preparation to the boba pearls, and was reminded that any foods that are cooked become Ready-to-Eat foods that require datemarking if stored beyond 24 hours. Ensure that all RTE, TCS foods are date-marked, with preparation/opening date being day 1, and day 7 being the time of final use or discard. Freezing does not reset the date-marking to start time, but instead pauses the count on the day of freezing, and resumes the count on the day of thawing or use.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed several white powders (flour, corn starch, sugar, monosodium glutamate, and tempura batter) stored in large containers (not the original packaging) without a label. CORRECTED: PIC stated that the labels from the last inspection had washed off and the containers were re-labeled during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that the containers must be labeled again when required. Ensure that foods not in the original packaging and easily mistakable are always labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Observed several food items that were stored in such a way that they were potentially exposed to environmental sources of contamination:
(i) An open bag of corn starch on a shelf. CORRECTED: the bag was sealed during the inspection.
(ii) Various food items stored in grocery bags in freezers, in direct contact with the non-food-grade grocery bags. 
(iii) An opened container of soy sauce, partially covered with its lid, stored underneath the handwashing sink. CORRECTED: the container was moved away from the handwashing sink.
(iv) Open containers of corn starch on shelves. CORRECTED: the containers had their lids placed back on.
(v) Canned bamboo shoots in a prep cooler where the lid was inside the can. CORRECTED: the bamboo shoots were placed in a separate cleanable container.
Ensure that all unpackaged food or open packaged food are protected from contamination, by changing location, putting a lid on the container, or repackaging the food item into a cleanable container.
citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed personal drinks and personal items stored on food prep areas or on shelves used for facility food items. The PIC was educated that personal drinks and personal items must be stored away from food preparation areas to avoid contamination. Ensure that personal items are kept in designated areas for employee storage.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that no staff beyond the CFPMs currently have a Food Handlers Certificate. PIC was notified and made plans to get staff certified. Ensure that all staff who are handling food are certified as Food Handlers through and accredited program.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed the area in the back of the soda machines has several areas where there is a build up of moisture and soil residues, and the area cannot easily cleaned by staff as the equipment is bolted to the floor. There is a concern for mold. Inspector will Follow Up to make sure the area behind the soda machines is cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the time of the inspection there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The PIC is instructed to maintain enough CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts in the facility moving forward.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301. 

An employee was observed to rinse their hands quickly in the hand sink without taking the requisite time or using soap. Education was conducted and will be followed-up on with the use of a translator in the future.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

A food handler was observed to change gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted and will be followed-up on at the educational visit in the future.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

An employee was observed to wash hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet with their bare hands. Education was conducted and will be followed-up on at the future educational visit.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The hand sink in the bathroom was without hand soap at the time of the inspection. The PIC was instructed to replace the soap and a cup of soap was provided to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

Several items were observed stored on the shelving after being cleaned and with remaining food debris on them. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the items cleaned again. The dishes were re-cleaned to correct. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use in the faiclity.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. Education was conducted and the fish moved to a bucket to allow for running water. This is an ongoing issue at this facility. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

An open can of strawberry glaze was observed in the walk in cooler without effective covering. The PIC was shown and instructed to ensure that all containers of food are protected from possible contamination at all times that they are not actively in use.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The roof of the microwave was observed heavily soiled with food splash. One of the food handlers in the kitchen wiped the microwave out with a sani rag to correct. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly to prevent possible incidental contamination of foods place inside.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple employee drinks (some partially consumed) were observed in the walk in cooler on shelving and intermixed (next to and above) foods intended for consumers. Education was conducted with the PIC. The items should be stored separately from foods intended for consumers moving forward.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of the inspection there was not a person with the requisite allergen training certificate available in the facility. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have someone with the requisite training available in the facility at all times that it is in operation.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: Inspector observed two uncovered drinks in the kitchen. CORRECTED- education was conducted and drinks were removed from food prep area to be covered. Ensure personal drinks are in a designated space, and have a lid and straw to prevent potential contamination.
citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed the ice scoop handle touching ice in the ice machine. CORRECTED- the scoop was removed for ware washing. Ensure ready to eat foods (consumables such as ice) are handled with utensils that have handles, that do NOT make contact with food products. Scoops must either be stored in a way that the scoop is stored separate from the food, or sticking outwards so as not to touch the food products, to prevent bare hand contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 5 dented cans of mushrooms (X4) and tomato sauce (X1) in dry storage. CORRECTED- education was conducted regarding dented cans, and the items were removed from service to be returned to the supplier for credit. Large dents along the body, and ANY dents along the seams may allow for the growth and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods to contain an internal temperature between 48-52F in the dessert topping cooler and the back room cheesecake cooler. Foods include, but are not limited to strawberry topping labeled “refrigerate after opening” (48-49F), and sour cream (52F). CORRECTED- items in the countertop dessert cooler were switched (items in the front are non-TCS, and are probing within acceptable range). Items in the standing dessert cooler were moved to the walk in cooling units. Ensure all TCS items are held 41F, or time as control (TAC) is implemented, with the items to be used or discarded within 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the counter dessert cooler and standing dessert cooler to have ambient temperatures ranging between 48-52F. This is not a safe cold holding range for TCS foods, as noted by violation #22. The PIC contacted their HVAC technician during the inspection. Ensure the unit is serviced or replaced by 7/10
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
citation_text:
2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking: Observed an employee with gloved hands eating foods over a cutting board. Discussed the need to cease snacking on foods during preparation. Halted the process and asked employee to go wash hands and change gloves. Had majority of staff demonstrate hand washing. Discussed with owner and manager the need to discuss glove use with staff. See that staff understands the need to change gloves between tasks. Owner stated that there is a specific designated area for staff to eat foods outside of the kitchen. 


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: There are at least eight employees that handle food inside of the kitchen area and no handwashing was observed. Many employees were instructed to wash hands and performed the handwashing process correctly. Be sure to educate all employees on the frequency and importance of handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.11 Clean Condition. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. Observed a cup being used as a scoop in the bulk sugar container. Also, observed handles inside the bulk containers of flour and cornstarch. See that proper scoops are used with handle extended OUT of foods. 

(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: The facility was observed storing food in packaging that could expose food to corrosion. There was a container of opened ketchup and Hoisin sauce stored in its original container.
