Due to the acidity of the food contaminants, the item must be transferred to a different container. Highly acid foods can corrode the interior of aluminum cans, causing a hazard to the food items. Ensure that acidic items are transferred to a different container to avoid corrosion.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. The dish machine’s sanitizer concentration tested at 0ppm (CL). Present operator was well aware of how to maintain the machine and was able to change the empty sanitizing bucket. Once new chemical was added, the operator primed sanitizing agent and then primed rinse agent to insure proper concentration. Owner stated that she is present everyday and testing the machine, however, the bucket was empty from previous days’ use and the lack of chemical residual was missed. 

Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to sanitize dishes correctly. 

 After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-502.13 Single-Service and Single-Use Articles, Use Limitation. Observed hiyashi Wakame containers being reused to hold fish and cut pork. Cease use of these containers as one of the ingredients is sesame oil. Sesame is now considered a main allergen and these containers should not be reused. 
(A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be reused. (B) The bulk milk container dispensing tube shall be cut on the diagonal leaving no more than one inch protruding from the chilled dispensing head.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Facility has test strips that were not properly recording the concentration of the dish machine chemical. Test strips were available from various locations. The dish machine test strips were expired in 2024. They were discarded. 

 Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
There were leaks observed at the following sinks:
-Hot water faucet of the dish machine room hand sink;
- Both necks of the two faucets at the triple sink. 

Ensure that sink faucets are maintained in good repair and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There was a box of pizza stored directly on top of noodles inside of the walk in cooler. Discussed with the PIC personal storage for employees. The pizza box was discarded to correct the violation. Educate employees on proper storage of personal items. Personal items must always be stored underneath or separate from items intended for public consumption. Ensure that personal items are stored in designated spaces.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to provide disinfection procedures in the case of vomit or diarrhea. CORRECTED- the CDC Norovirus procedure handout was given to the PIC, and bleach is available. Ensure directions are made readily available in order to properly disinfect in the case of a vomit or diarrhea incident.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee don gloves without prior hand washing. CORRECTED- education regarding times to wash hands was conducted. Instances where hand washing is required includes (but is not limited to): before donning gloves, after touching a personal electronic device, after using cleaning products, when switching between raw and ready to eat foods. Review times to wash hands with all food handlers to ensure proper employee hygiene.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.[P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector verified the process of moving foods from the grill to the concessions. The Certified Food Protection Manager stated that foods are brought from the grill to concessions with no covering. Cease this practice. Cover foods with a lid or foil between buildings to prevent the contamination of foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed liquid cheese and cooked hamburgers to have internal temperatures of 112F and 128F respectively. CORRECTED- the temperature of the hot holding units were increased, and the foods were observed above 135F. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens. If TCS foods are out of temperature, time as control (food is to be used or discarded within 4 hours) should be implemented.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The hot holding units holding liquid cheese and cooked meats were holding foods below 135F (see violation #22). CORRECTED- the temperature of the units was increased, so that foods were observed above 135F. Ensure all hot holding units are set so that TCS foods have an internal temperature above 135F (in the case of hot foods, cold foods must be kept at or below 41F).
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Multiple boxes housing single service containers were observed on the floor in both the main concessions area, as well as in the 3rd base concessions/ storage area. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure all foods and food contact surfaces are stored 6 inches or more above the ground to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed spoons at the main concessions stand in a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- the spoons were rearranged with a gloved hand so that all handles are facing outward. Ensure single service utensils are arranged so that the food contact and hand contact surfaces are separate to prevent potential bare hand contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed mouse droppings on the floor of the dry storage area, as well as on top of unused dish racks that are stored inside of the dish room. The facility has active pest control, however, frequent cleaning should occur to eliminate harboring conditions. The floor in the dry storage area contained spilled foods, which are environments that keep insects and pests around to feed. Additionally, a dead insect was observed underneath the triple sink inside of the dish room.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Despite the kitchen being in full operation, there wasn't a sanitizer solution present. A sanitizer solution was created and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer solution present if food handling, preparing, or serving is occurring.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There was a significant amount of ice buildup on the shelves, floor, and food items inside of the walk in freezer. PIC mentioned that the facility has noticed the increase of ice buildup due to the humidity outdoors. The gasket of the freezer door is broken, as well as other parts of the door are broken, not allowing it to close properly. Ensure that the door and the gasket is replaced to prevent the accumulation of ice buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be resting on floor in dry storage area. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to mop sink hanging area. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The only certified food protection manager was not present during the visit. There wasn't any cooking occurring, however, the facility was in the process of butchering meats on site. Any time food handling, cooking, or preparation is occurring, a CFPM is needed. Ensure that there is at least two employees who are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The cove base is pulling away from the wall (right of kitchen’s handsink). Ensure that the coving is resealed to prevent the accumulation of unwanted debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed four sanitizer buckets in the facility measure 0ppm chlorine with a test strip. The PIC was informed. The chemical in sanitizer will evaporate faster than usual in increased temperatures. Ensure staff are monitoring the buckets with test strips and replacing the buckets more frequently. The buckets were replaced during today’s visit.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed the following cold holding violations in the facility:
1. The prep cooler (tomato 45.2F, probe thermometer)
2. The drawer cooler below the grill (chicken 55.4F, probe thermometer)
3. The upright cooler next to the stairs (shrimp 54.2, probe thermometer)

The facility is experiencing higher than normal temperatures in the kitchen (90.8F ambient) due to an ongoing heat advisory. The walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer were both holding adequate temperatures. All TCS food items from the upright cooler and drawer coolers were moved to the walk-ins. Only the upright cooler was able to reach 41F after leaving the doors sealed. As a temporary solution until temperatures can resolve, time as a control will be used for all TCS foods stored outside of the walk-in cooler and freezer during dinner service. The chef is well informed regarding proper time as a control practices and will also keep food items on an ice bath during service. A follow-up will be conducted tomorrow afternoon during lunch to check cooler temperatures and determine an action plan for combatting the heat in the kitchen.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the prep cooler, upright cooler near the stairs, and drawer coolers below the grill to be holding food items above 41F during today’s visit. The ambient temperature of the kitchen measured 90.8F. The owner, Bruno, attempted to contact a service technician during today’s visit. In the meantime, these three coolers are not considered adequate for cold holding and alternative cooling must be used. The chef developed a plan to use time as a control for all TCS foods stored outside the walk-in coolers during dinner rush. These trays will be clearly marked with a time of removal from the cooler as well as the four-hour discard time. The inspector will follow-up on cooler repair on July 10, 2026.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Two cans in dry storage were observed with significant dents in the upper seam. The PC was shown and education conducted. The cans were discarded to correct. Ensure that the integrity of packaging of all foods are maintained in the facility at all times. If damaged packaging is received return that package or refuse receiving.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not register sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation revealed an empty jug of sanitizer concentrate attached to the machine. The jug was replaced with a fresh jug and primed by the inspector and staff. Afterwards the machine registered correct amounts of sanitizer. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective concentrations at all times in the facility.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
citation_text: 3-501.14(B) Cooling. (B) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours to 5°C (41°F) or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature, such as reconstituted FOODS and canned tuna. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the follow nonfood-contact surfaces in need of more frequent cleaning:
(i) the underside of the soda fountain where several residues have accumulated;
(ii) the hose going into the fan in the walk-in cooler where a significant amount of ice has accumulated.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of residues by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(i) Observed a cutting board being stored behind the handles of the triple sink. CORRECTED: PIC moved the cutting board to a place where it can air-dry and not be contaminated from spills. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
(ii) Observed one of the nozzles from the drink dispenser had an accumulation of soils. CORRECTED: Staff removed the nozzles for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing. Nozzles should be cleaned at a frequency to keep the food-contact surfaces clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed that the door for the right walk-in cooler is damaged, requiring significant effort to open and keep shut. Duct tape has been added to the handle to provide for a better grip. The PIC was notified. Ensure that equipment components for doors and hinges are kept intact, tight, and properly adjusted.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed equipment that needs more frequent cleaning:
(i) the sliding doors behind the storage shelves.
(ii) the doors on both sides of the 6-compartment cooler (currently used for equipment storage).
(iii) the bottom part of the oven.
(iv) the sides of the front area grill.
(v) the back walls underneath the hood behind the grill and fryers.
Ensure that these areas are cleaned with regular frequency to keep them clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed several pieces of equipment that are in disrepair, are no longer working and should be removed from service, or are not in service and should be removed if they will not be cleaned frequently:
(i) The reach-in freezer lid is broken; the lid no longer stays upright when opened, and it can potentially injure employees when it slams shut; the visible damage to the lid is no longer smooth and easily cleanable.
(ii) The middle walk-in cooler has a steady drip that needs to be fixed; staff placed a catch basin to catch the drip during the inspection.
(iii) The sanitizer dispenser hose for the triple sink is not dispensing enough sanitizer in a timely manner, requiring several minutes of running to reach an effective quaternary ammonium sanitizing solution. Staff cannot fill their sanitizing buckets from the dispenser hose; instead staff must scoop sanitizing solution from a full triple sink.
(iv) The automatic paper towel dispenser in the serving area is damaged and not dispensing paper towels; staff are using a separate paper towel roll to complete handwashing.
(v) The prep sink in the back kitchen is not working; it is no longer being used to prepare food.
(vi) The 2-door cooler in the back kitchen is not working due to a drip issue; it is no longer being used for cold-holding or for dry goods storage.
(vii) The 1-door hot box in the back kitchen is broken beyond repair; it is still waiting to be removed from the facility.
(viii) The pizza oven is no longer being used, as pizza is not made by the establishment.
Ensure physical equipment is either maintained in good repair or removed from service.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Facility was observed to have no written policy or bleach available for responding to vomit/diarrheal events. The PIC was informed and plans to purchase bleach. A procedural handout was provided. Bleach was acquired during today’s visit.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed soda syrup boxes to be stored directly on the ground in the kitchen. The PIC was informed that food items must be stored at least 6” off the ground to prevent cross-contamination. Milk crates and plastic pallets are adequate for storage. Ensure these items are stored correctly prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several pans on a shelf being stored as clean were observed soiled with remaining food debris and stickers. The PIC was shown and education conducted. They moved the items back to dish for re-cleaning. Reviewing of procedures and oversight of the dish cleaners is suggested to prevent future issues. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage and re-use in the facility.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler to the left of the fryers was observed holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 48.5F. Due to the situation with the fryers and per the PIC this cooler is not likely to have been opened much since that situation kicked off two days ago. At this time the TCS foods are being discarded due to the situation taking place with the fryers. The cooler itself still needs to be functioning correctly and that is what this violation is for. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days to ensure that the equipment has maintenance conducted and is functioning correctly.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple rags used for wiping counters were observed stored on the counters in the kitchen. The PIC was consulted and moved the rags back into the buckets of sanitizer to correct. Ensure that all wet rags are stored between uses in sanitizer of effective concentration to prevent the proliferation of biological pathogens.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The “Imperial” hot box on the prep line was observed heavily soiled during this inspection. Per the PIC this item should be cleaned nightly by staff. This appeared to not be happening at the time of the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain clean. The temperature inside of this was observed over 400F and biological contamination is not the concern. Pieces falling out of this equipment into the open sauces underneath was the concern and the impetus for maintaining this equipment clean at the time of the inspection. Ensure that all physical equipment is maintained clean at all times in the facility.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

1) An employee shirt was observed in a container of flatbreads on the prep line. 2) A purse was observed stored on a wire shelf over consumer foods. Both locations were shown to the PIC and the items moved to correct. The flatbreads were also discarded to allay the potential concerns related contamination concerns. Ensure that all employee personal items are stored so that contamination of consumer foods is mitigated.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the backside of the ice machine baffles to contain an accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- The PIC covered the ice and sanitized the baffles. Discussed increasing the frequency of cleaning during summer months. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of consumables.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to initially be dispensing 10 ppm. CORRECTED-the dish machine was observed to be dispensing 50 ppm chlorine after the machine was primed and chemicals were refreshed. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently tested to verify proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed foods in the salad prep cooler to have internal temperatures ranging from 46-57F. CORRECTED- items were moved under time as control. Foods that are not used will be discarded at the end of service (the facility is open for 4 hours at a time). Ensure temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are used or discarded within 4 hours when out of temperature control (below 41F and above 135F respectively).
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the salad prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. For temperatures within the cooler, reference violation 22. The ladles were replaced with ones with shorter handles, allowing the top to close more completely. Items cooled significantly in a 30 minute time period.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair:

1. The front handwashing sink is observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 
2. There is a leak in the bottom corners of the walk-in cooler door that is creating mold accumulation. Ensure that this issue is repaired and the floor and walk-in cooler door are cleaned to remove the accumulation. 
3. There is a broken cove tile behind the standing freezer by the first drive-through window. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed a bowl submerged in a soy sauce container. CORRECTED- the bowl was removed. Ensure ready to eat foods are handled with scoops that have a clear differentiation between food contact and hand contact surfaces to prevent bare hand contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed uncovered crepe wraps in the top drawer of the counter unit (right of prep area). The drawers are soiled and there was one immobile roach present on the side of the unit. Discussed keeping foods covered when in these drawers due to past pest presence. The pest problem has been an ongoing problem that is being handled. Adams is visiting two times a month. See General Comments for additional pest notes. The crepes were wrapped during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation.  (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizers (sanitizer bucket and triple sink) to be at a low concentration (10 ppm Chlorine). CORRECTED- the sanitizers were remade to 200 and 100 ppm Cl respectively. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to ensure they are at the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed spicy mayo in the refrigerator dated 6/6. CORRECTED- the sauce was made on 6/26, and the correct date was placed. Ensure  all food contact surfaces undergo proper ware washing, and are date marked on the day of preparation to be used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed eel thawing on the dry storage rack (observed at an acceptable temperature). CORRECTED- eel was moved into the two door cooler. Thawing at room temperature is not an approved practice. Approved practices include thawing in refrigeration, cooking, or placing under cold running water.
citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The freezer top of the mini-fridge beneath the display/service area was observed to be coated with frost. Defrost the freezer so surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The rice steamer on the front line has a crack along the top rim. The facility has an additional steamer in the back of the store and is going to replace the unit this evening. Cease use of the steamer and replace.
citation_text: 4-201.11 Equipment and Utensils. EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The front of the mini-fridges and the cabinets of the frontline were observed to be soiled with food splash. See that these surfaces are cleaned. Discussed cleaning strategies with owner and staff. This was the only location where a live pest was observed. Keep surfaces clean to remove food sources.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed that the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility has not completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the CFPM completes the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: It was observed that no employees present during today’s inspection had completed a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) course. A CFM should be present at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM is able to oversee proper employee hygiene, food handling practices, safe holding temperatures, and overall reduces the risk of food-borne illness. Ensure a CFM is present on staff during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.[C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to operate the faucet handles after completing the handwashing process. Be sure to educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. After washing hands, make sure to use a barrier to operate faucet handles to prevent contaminating freshly washed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris on the following food contact surfaces:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Biofilm at several soda nozzles at the drink station directly south of the car.. CORRECTED- staff removed the nozzles to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized at the three part sink.
2) Biofilm at the soda gun holder on the North side of the bar. CORRECTED- the space was wiped with a sanitizer cloth. 
Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The gasket of the kitchen salad prep cooler was observed to be loose. This loose gasket may affect the ability of the unit to cold hold, and may act as a potential food contaminant. Replace or repair the gasket by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.  [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was no sanitizer bucket available along the cook-line at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure making a sanitizer bucket is a part of opening procedures, so that food contact surfaces may be frequently sanitized.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the hand washing sink at the bar to be separated from the wall. Reseal to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of debris in the following areas:
1) Dust on the fans of the (chicken) walk in cooler.
2) General debris and dirt on the wall behind the dish machine, and between the dish machine and triple sink.
Ensure physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall/baseboard behind the fryers is still observed to be in need of cleaning. There has been some progress, but more is still needed. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 7/29/2026 to ensure that the wall/baseboard behind the fryers has been cleaned. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed chicken to be thawing next to triple sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper thawing practices and chicken was moved to under running water in triple sink. Ensure proper thawing techniques are used when thawing chicken.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be resting in dirty mop water in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to mop strainer and water was discarded. Ensure mops are placed in a way that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The nozzles of the soda gun at the bar was observed to be soiled. Education was carried out. A staff member cleaned and sanitized the soda nozzles while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
Inspector observed the following leakages in the plumbing lines within the facility.
1. (Repeat) The faucet and the line under the triple sink at the bar was observed leaking. 
2. The flush line on the urinal in the men’s bathroom was observed leaking water causing water to settle on the floor in the men’s bathroom.
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that this leak is sealed to be in compliance with the LAW. Inspector will return on 6/30/26 for a follow up.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the three compartment sink was observed to be coming off. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the sink is caulked providing a Smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the three compartment sink was observed to be coming off. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the three compartment sink is caulked providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant (caulking) to be damaged or inadequate around the hot line units and counter to the left of the dish machine. Ensure these areas are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that sanitizing solution (quaternary ammonium) in the sanitizer buckets was testing between 0ppm-100ppm, which below an effective concentration of that sanitizer. CORRECTED: PIC remade each bucket and tested the chemical concentrations to be at a safe and effective concentrations between 200-400ppm. Ensure that chemical sanitizer is used per EPA-registered label use instructions, and is tested frequently for a safe and effective concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed that the handwashing sink in the back is leaking wastewater during usage. PIC was notified and contacted a repair person for a timely repair. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm the repair. Ensure that all plumbing is maintained in good repair to prevent contamination or slips, trips, or falls.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed several personal items (phones, wallets, keys, drinks, etc.) being stored in food prep or food storage areas. CORRECTED: PIC and Inspector discussed long-term solutions for employee item storage, including using the office shelves in the back of the store, or providing separate bins for employee storage. PIC had employees move personal items to the office shelves during the inspection. Ensure that designated areas are used for employee personal items to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, clean linens, single-service and single-use articles.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to always wash their hands before donning gloves including in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Four packs of raw breakfast sausages were observed being stored above lettuce and boiled potatoes. Education was carried out. The sausages were removed and stored correctly. Ensure that staff are reminded to properly store food items in order to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The internal surface of the coffee maker was observed soiled. PIC was made aware. An employee cleaned and sanitized the coffee maker while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the coffee maker are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed several drain flies in the utility closet and the first and second aisle in the dry storage. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the flies are dealt with using authorized pest control methods. Zappers and fly strips may be hung, but they must not be hung over food. Ensure that pest activities is reduced within the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment:
(Repeatx2) 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. There is no food protection manager present. The CFPM was out for the morning but did arrive during inspection. See that a CFPM is present during all hours of operation. The store should have one certified food manager present during all hours of operation. Discussed with the two additional food handlers present that now is the time to have the proper education. Goal is to have the test conducted in-facility sometime in September. 

 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The paperwork for employee health has been presented to the facility multiple times but is not available today. Paperwork was presented and signed by staff. See that staff is aware of the employee illness policy and knows when to come to work and when to call-in sick. Keep paperwork in a known location. 

The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. Operator is observed washing hands and turning-off the faucet using clean hands and not a barrier. Discussed hand washing with operator. Proper hand washing was observed. Properly wash hands and use a barrier when turning off the faucet. 

(C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. REPEAT X 1: The interior of the microwave was observed soiled with food splash. Also, new to this inspection, the can opener was observed soiled. The soil is from the previous day’s use. Discussed closing and opening operations and that both functions should properly occur for the kitchen to operate smoothly. Cleaning began during the inspection  

UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. There is a sanitizing bucket present from the previous day on the cookline. Sani-buckets should be emptied nightly and dishes should be removed for cleaning nightly.   Not having an available sani-bucket is an unacceptable practice and one that has been discussed at length throughout the last several months. 
 See that wiping cloths are being stored within a proper sanitizing bucket. The bucket should be sized to hold several cloths and still allow space for a hand to be submerged. The most important part of sanitizing is that a testable residual of sanitizer is present in the bucket. 

Keep a sani-bucket, that is holding proper chemical residual, available for holding wet wiping cloths. Bucket was created during the inspection. Discussed use of test strips and proper bleach. 

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
citation_text:
3-403.11(A) Reheating for Hot Holding. The facility is observed reheating foods for hot holding at an insufficient time to allow temperatures to reach 165F. A probe thermometer is available, but was not being used to monitor the temperature. The lamb reheated and placed in hot holding is observed at 85F. The reheat time was insufficient. A discussion was held and the facility began using the stem thermometer and properly reheating foods. Rice and a number of other foods were being prepped for reheat. A discussion of 165 F for the reheat temperature was discussed. 

REHEAT TEMPERATURE IS 165F. For everything. Use your stem thermometer to monitor the reheating temperatures. 


(A) Except as specified under (B) and (C) and in (E) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the FOOD reach a temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) for 15 seconds.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. There are observed two or three containers of cooked/covered foods stored with a date of 6/18 in the walk-in cooler. Foods were discarded during the inspection. The walk-in cooler was clean and overall organized. No other foods were observed uncovered or improperly dated. 

 (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.

(A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. CFPM is not allergen certified. Discussed two additional staff becoming CFPM THESE TWO SHOULD ALSO BE ALLERGEN CERTIFIED. The current CFPM should acquire the allergen certificate. Discussed available options. One of the food handlers believes that he has the allergen certificate and should be able to produce the paperwork at the next routine inspection. 

 (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets at the bar measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC repeated the test with her own strip, also measuring 0ppm. The PIC informed bar staff and the buckets were replaced. Ensure sanitizer concentration is monitored with test strips and the buckets are replaced frequently to prevent improper sanitizing of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the following food items out of the appropriate temperature range:
1. Garlic cream sauce - sauté hot cooler
2. Chicken breast - sauté hot cooler - 45F, probe
3. Piccata sauce - sauté sauce cooler
4. Jambalaya - sauté sauce cooler - 48F, probe
5. Cut tomatoes - sauté sauce cooler
6. Sliced cheese - sauté sauce cooler
7 Whipped cream - dessert cooler

The inspector was present directly after lunch rush, so the coolers were open for an extended time during service. The coolers were closed and left to cool during the rest of the inspection. The inspector returned at the end of the inspection (roughly 1 hour later) and the dessert cooler was able to reach proper cold holding temperatures. The sauté hot cooler, however, failed to cool within the timeframe. 

CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods within the cooler were discarded. The staff plan to cease use of the cooler until it can be repaired or replaced.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

1) The sani bucket near the registers was observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. 2) The sanitizer bay of the three part sink was observed with a CL concentration of approximately 10 ppm. title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple missed hand washing opportunities:
1) One employee touched their hat, and donned a new pair of gloves without hand washing.
2) Another individual wearing gloves pulled up their pants and returned to food prep.
CORRECTED- times to wash hands were reviewed with the person in charge (PIC), who stated two new employees are on the line. An educational handout was provided by the inspector. Review times to wash hands with all employees, including, but not limited to: after touching ones self, after touching a cell phone, after handling money, after handling cleaning products, after taking the garbage out, and after changing tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a phone with an active screen on the drive thru prep counter. CORRECTED- the phone was removed from the area, and food contact surfaces were sanitized. Ensure phones (and any items that may introduce contamination to foods or food contact surfaces) are kept separate from areas of food preparation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred. [P]
