title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to missing date marking in multiple coolers and walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, items were prepared before the 7 day date marking maximum so proper date marking was placed on items. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed beef/steaks to be improperly thawing outside of cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper thawing practices and beef was moved to walk in cooler. Ensure when thawing, any TCS item is placed in a cooler or under running water.
citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed onions in dry storage room to be resting directly on floor. Discussed with PIC, items were removed from floor and placed at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any food items is at least 6 inches off of ground.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed clean utensils to not be inverted. Discussed with PIC, utensil were put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process and inverted. Ensure any cleaned utensils are inverted to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed kitchen line prep coolers to be soiled with food debris under lids. Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed leak to be present under fan unit in walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. A container was placed under leak to contain it, ensure walk in cooler is working to meet manufactures standards.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed food handler training to be missing for some members of staff. Discussed with PIC, remaining staff members will receive license. Ensure any food handling employee has completed the required food handlers training within 30 days of hiring. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed CFM on duty to not have allergen training completed. DIscussed with PIC, training will be completed. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, PIC will ensure a certified food manager is brought in. Ensure a certified food manager is available within the facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed kitchen hand sinks to be missing paper towels. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with paper towels.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm Cl. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Triple sink will be used until dish machine is serviced. Ensure dish machine is sanitizing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed open juices to be stored in a cooler at 70F. Discussed with PIC, cooler is observed to be down and items were discarded. Any juices in the future will be stored in walk in cooler. Ensure any TCS item is cold held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There is observed to be soil residue accumulation in a container that holds packages of hard boiled eggs and on the outside of two containers of Barbecue sauce in the walk-in cooler. This was discussed with the PIC, who stated that they will clean the container holding the eggs and the containers of Barbecue sauces will be discarded. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
There were multiple food items that were observed to be held past the 7-day date-marking: 

1. A container of cups of tartar sauces that are made in-house that had a date of 6/15. 
2. A container of cheddar garlic mashed potatoes that had a date of 6/17. 
3. A container of turkey gravy that had a date of 6/15. 

CORRECTED- These food items were discarded by the PIC. Ensure that dates on foods are routinely checked and the food is discarded if held past the 7-day allowed date-marking.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler shelves. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- The gaskets of the batter station cooler. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The fan covers of the three-door cooler and the milk cooler. 
5. FIRST REPEAT- The bottom of the cooler across from the batter station. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no soap to be available at the back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with soap.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed multiple items to be resting within back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, items were removed from hand sinks are. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used to wash hands.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed water bottles to be stored outside of store. Discussed with PIC, bottles will be moved back inside. Ensure water bottles are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to coming apart in the bathroom hand sinks. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop sink. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to strainer. Ensure mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a single use 2 oz cup stored in powdered sugar and cinnamon sugar. CORRECTED- the cup was removed and discarded. The person in charge (PIC) stated they are actively reminding employees to not use scoops without handles in ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure all RTE foods are handled with gloves, deli paper, or a scoop with a handle- to differentiate between the food contact and hand contact surface moving forward to prevent bare hand contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food handler training
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a food handler on shift with no Food Handler certificate available. All employees must have food handler who handle food must have certificates to be made available during inspections within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
SECOND REPEAT: The CFM has not completed Allergen Training. Complete training and test to be made available by the next routine inspection. Certified Food Protection Managers at high risk establishments must complete Allergen Awareness training and test within 30 days of employment, to be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, there wasn't a certified food protection manager available. A CFPM arrived shortly after the start of the inspection to correct the violation. Person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the facility will work to get the main cook food manager certified. Ensure that there is always at least one employee who is food manager certified during operating hours.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were a handful of mouse dropping observed on floor of the dry storage area. Shown to the PIC and discussed routinely cleaning of storage area. Ensure that the area is cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent the accumulation of droppings.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There were two containers of bread loafs stored on the floor of the indoor building. The PIC mentioned that the breads are normally stored off the floor and in a different area. Ensure that bread loafs are stored at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution present inside of the shed where food is being cold held, hot held, prepped, and served. Discussed with the PIC that a sanitizer solution shall be present to sanitize all food contact surfaces. The facility will use a sanitizer bottle for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food handler training
comment:
None of the employees working at the time of the inspection could show proof of food handler certificates. The PIC was given a reference sheet of websites so that employees can obtain food handler licenses. Ensure that all employees who aren't food manager certified obtain food handler certificates. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There were various Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods stored inside of the prep cooler that were probed between 45F - 50F. These items included salads, mayonnaise, cheeses, meats, and dressings. The PIC mentioned that the cooler had recently been restocked at 1:30pm after lunch. The facility was instructed to place bulk items back into the walk in cooler and to use time control for the items at the top of the cooler. The facility will discard items after four hours. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F or below. Will follow up on July 6, 2026.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler had an ambient temperature of 50F. See violation #22 for further details. Ensure that the prep cooler is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow up on July 6, 2026 to see that the cooler has been serviced or replaced.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The service prep cooler did not contain an internal thermometer to measure the ambient temperature. Discussed with the PIC. Ensure that an internal thermometer is available to accurately measure ambient temperatures of cold holding equipment. Will follow-up on July 6, 2026 to see that the unit has a thermometer available.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: THIRD REPEAT- The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). An employee stated that they are currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: All three employees were observed to not use a barrier when turning off the faucet of the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The employees were educated on using a barrier when turning off the faucet to prevent contamination to clean hands. Ensure that staff are educated on proper handwashing procedures to prevent contamination to clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- An employee was observed to handle raw chicken with their gloves, wipe their gloves off with a towel, and then touch tongs and other items with the same gloves. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that after handling raw chicken, the gloves need to be discarded and hands should be washed before donning gloves again. 

An employee was observed to use their gloves to make a sanitizer bucket with bleach and touch the triple sink faucet handles, then proceed to prepare food. CORRECTED- The employee was educated to discard their gloves, wash their hands, and don gloves again before preparing food. 

Ensure that employees are properly educated on when to wash their hands. A handout was given that is translated to Thai and it is highly recommended to post this in the facility.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The ice scoop was observed to have the handle in direct contact with the ice in the ice machine. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and an employee to have the handle of the ice scoop stored above the ice. The scoop handle was moved to be stored above the ice. Ensure that food is protected from contamination from bare-hand contact by having the scoop handle stored above the food.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was observed to be two chairs in front of the only handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The owner moved the chairs away from the handwashing sink and was educated about making sure the handwashing sink is accessible to employees at all times. Ensure that the handwashing sink is always accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was a package of raw bacon on the top shelf of the three-door cooler above containers of sauces. CORRECTED- The bacon was moved to the bottom shelf of the cooler and proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There is a container of noodles that is observed to be stored uncovered in the three-door cooler and there is a container of wontons that is observed to be uncovered in the chest freezer. When opening the chest freezer door, there is frost from the door that is falling onto the wontons. This was discussed with the PIC.  Ensure that food is stored in covered containers, wrappings, or packages to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen tested to be at 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 150ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that the sanitizer is frequently tested and remade if not at a label-recommended concentration. It is recommended to remake the sanitizer buckets every two to four hours.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were multiple cutting boards stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. CORRECTED- The cutting boards were moved from behind the faucet and will be washed, rinsed, and sanitized before being placed with the clean dishes. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was an opened bottle of Golden Mountain Seasoning Sauce, two opened bottles of Unagi Sushi Sauce, and an opened bottle of Hoison Sauce that were observed to be stored at room temperature and their labels stated to “Refrigerate After Opening”. CORRECTED- These bottles of sauces were discarded and the PIC was educated to read the label after opening the food item. Storing these sauces in the cooler in the future was discussed. Ensure that TCS foods are stored at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There are multiple boxes of food items that are observed to be stored on the floor throughout the kitchen. The kitchen is very cluttered and there is not enough storage for all of the items in the kitchen. Ensure that food items are stored at least six inches above the ground. It is recommended to reduce the clutter in the kitchen to allow for more storage space.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment:
The employee and owner were observed to make a sanitizer bucket using Purell sanitizer, but did not have any test strips for the sanitizer. It was discussed to cease using the Purell sanitizer unless test strips have been obtained for it. 

The facility is also observed to be using Quaternary ammonium sanitizer, but do not have any Quaternary ammonium test strips for the sanitizer. A follow up is scheduled for 7/8/2026 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are test strips available for every type of sanitizer that is utilized in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The gaskets of the doors of the larger preparation cooler in the kitchen. 
2. The standing white freezer needs to be defrosted. 
3. The bottom of the three-door cooler. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The hood baffles. These are observed to have an accumulation of grease on them. Ensure that these are cleaned before they begin to drip and contaminate cooking food. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The floor behind and under the cook-line equipment. This was shown to the PIC. There is significant accumulation of grease and food debris under and behind the cook-line. Ensure that this is cleaned to prevent pest harborage conditions. 
3. The floor in the mop sink area is observed to be in need of cleaning. 

Ensure that physical facilities are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There is observed to be personal items mixed in with items intended for the restaurant in the three-door cooler. Personal storage was discussed with the PIC and the majority of the items were moved to be on the bottom shelf. Ensure that personal items are stored in the bottom of the cooler away from items for the facility to prevent contamination to food.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The blade of the can opener in the kitchen was observed heavily soiled. The PIC believed that the equipment was used last the day before observation. 2) The nozzle for the soda gun at the bar farthest from the door was observed heavily soiled around the inside of the nozzle. Both items were shown to staff and washed during the inspection to correct the violations.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

1) Rice and cooked macaroni were observed with internal temperatures of 54F-65F during the inspection in the top of a prep cooler. The PIC was shown and discarded the items to correct. Investigation showed the cooler had been shut off on accident. The cooler was switched back on and the foods discarded to correct. 2) TCS foods in the cooler under the grills were observed with internal temperatures of 45F-56F. The PIC was shown and discarded the TCS foods in the cooler to correct the immediate concern. Foods discarded include fish, chicken. Beef patties, cheeses and grilled onions. This corrects the immediate violation for this situation. Refer to line item #33 for a scheduled follow-up for the cooler.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler located under the grill was observed to not be holding TCS foods at correct temperature. The PIC called for maintinance to be conducted during the inspection. A follow-up was set for 10 days to ensure that the cooler is brought into compliance.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

A charger cord was observed hanging down from a shelf and laying partially on the counter beneath. This counter has food preparation take place on it. The PIC was shown and instructed to ensure that the cord does not hang down moving forward. Ensure that foods are protected form contamination at all times. The cord was moved to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Triple sink will be used in the meantime. Ensure dish machine is testing at the proper concentration to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is made at the proper concentration and is available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed open BBQ sauce that was not refrigerated after opening. Discussed with PIC, BBQ sauce was from the previous week. BBQ sauce was discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly cold held after opening.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to strainer portion of mop bucket. Ensure after use, mops are placed in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed multiple instances of employees not using barrier when turning off handwashing faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper handwashing practices. Ensure after hand washing, a barrier is used to turn off faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed in use ice scoop and ice scoop bin to be soiled with red food splash. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop and container were placed through wash, rinse, and sanitize process. Ensure ice scoop are clean and are being stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed multiple sanitizer buckets to not be at the proper concentration. DIscussed with PIC, sanitizer buckets were remade and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Observed the following date marking issues:
1) (Repeatx2) Observed multiple sauce bottles located at the front line, front line cooler, and back sauce prep cooler to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. 
2) Observed Cole slaw to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. 

Discussed with PIC, all items were discarded. PIC claimed items were going to be pulled and discarded, however multiple items were dated to be discarded multiple days ago. Ensure staff is properly date marking any TCS item, and that all TCS items are following the 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the top microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact areas at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed mop sink drain to be clogged and not draining. Discussed with PIC, plumber will be contacted and sink will not be used in the meantime. Ensure all plumbing systems are working at the manufactures standards.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that staff remember to wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The coving on the wall left of the hot box at the entrance of the cook line was observed coming off the wall. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the coving will be sealed to the wall properly. Ensure that the coving is sealed the wall properly providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the front and back of the ice machine baffles. A new follow up inspection is scheduled for 7/1/26 to verify compliance. Empty, clean, and sanitize the ice machine. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility uses both quaternary ammonia (wipes) and chlorine bleach (triple sink) to sanitize food contact surfaces. The facility did not have a test kit for chlorine bleach, and the test kit for the quaternary ammonia was observed to have expired 7/1/24. Obtain new test strips for both sanitizers. All chemical sanitizing solutions used for food contact surfaces must have a test kit to verify the concentration recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a pan of raw fish observed to be above a box of avocados in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The pan of raw fish was moved to be below the avocados. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order and that food is protected from contamination during preparation, storage, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The walk-in cooler shelves were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. Discussed cleaning the shelves with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: There is observed to still be no hot water at the front women’s bathroom and both employee bathrooms. The PIC was unsure if any repairs had been made. A follow up is scheduled for 7/1/2026 to ensure that the handwashing sinks in these bathrooms have hot and cold water at them. Ensure that all sinks have cold and hot water at them.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The manual ware washing station was set up in the incorrect order. The sinks were as followed: wash, sanitize, rinse. The correct setup was discussed with the owner to ensure that dishes are getting cleaned properly. Sanitation should always be the last step of cleaning to be sure that the correct contact times are being met.
citation_text: 4-703.11(A) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (A) Hot water manual operations by immersion for at least 30 seconds and as specified under § 4-501.111.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
SECOND REPEAT- There was observed to be raw pork belly on a package of imitation crab meat. CORRECTED- The raw pork belly was moved to be on another shelf and the PIC was educated on proper storage order. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Proper storage order should be as follows: 
1. Ready-to-Eat Foods. 
2. Unwashed fruits and vegetables. 
3. Partially cooked foods (ex: par-cooked chicken). 
4. Seafood and shell eggs. 
5. Beef and Pork. 
6. Chicken.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzles were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The PIC removed the soda nozzles and cleaned them along with the dispenser part of the machine. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. Soda nozzles should be frequently cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

comment:

1. The hood baffles. 
2. The inside of the green single-service tubes. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned these during the inspection. 
3. The bottom of the chest freezer to the left of the back door. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

comment: Inspector observed shell eggs and raw pork stored on top of buckets containing ready-to-eat (RTE) sauces in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was an informed and the items were rearranged. Ensure raw animal foods are stored below RTE foods to prevent cross-contamination.

comment: Inspector observed an employee wash and lather hands, then turn off the faucet before using paper towels. CORRECTED- education was provided. Review hand washing procedures with staff, a paper towel should be used to dry hands and THEN turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed egg rolls and fried chicken in the standing cooler without covering. CORRECTED- plastic wrap was placed over the foods. Ensure foods in cooling units are covered to protect from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed unwashed produce stored on the floor in the walk in cooler. Store foods at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with debris. The PIC was informed and cleaned/sanitized the ice machine during today’s visit. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized frequently to avoid an accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The inspector observed the door and shelving of the walk-in cooler to have exposed wood. Ensure this bare wood is sealed prior to the next routine inspection. 

The inspector observed the ceiling tiles above the bathroom hand sink to be water damaged and soiled with mold. The PIC was informed that the tiles need to be replaced with non-absorbent tiles prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(i) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink, where it could be contaminated by food debris or water splashes. CORRECTED: PIC moved the cutting board up above onto the drying rack during the inspection. Ensure that cutting boards are always stored in a position that does not pose the risk of contamination.
(ii) Observed that the baffles inside the ice machine contained a buildup of soil residues. PIC and inspector discussed the establishment’s regular cleaning schedule, but found that the baffles had not been on the cleaning schedule. Inspector will Follow Up with the establishment to confirm that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure that all equipment food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Observed that the establishment does not currently have a probe style thermometer. PIC will have a new probe style thermometer in the establishment by the Follow Up date, and will contact the Inspector when the thermometer has arrived. Ensure that all food temperature measuring device is provided and available for use to maintain food temperatures.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed the reach-in freezer in the ware washing room has an accumulation of frost. The inspector and PIC discussed unplugging the freezer for a complete defrost. Ensure that the reach-in freezer is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 
(i) THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION. The grease accumulation around the fryer. The accumulation is on the floor and sides and on the pipes above the fryer. The grease above the fryer could potentially drip onto food cooking below.
(ii) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The dust accumulation behind and underneath the soda machine in the kitchen.
Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the drying rack shelves in the dishwashing room were deteriorating, collapsing during the inspection. PIC will have the shelves repaired by the next routine inspection. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: (THRICE REPEAT) No employees at the establishment had access to a CFPM license. Ensure that at least one employee has access to their Certified Food Protection Manager credentials at all times food is being prepared. Correct by next routine inspection (at least 90 days from today).
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspector was unable to verify employees health reporting agreement during today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. A few reporting forms were provided to be signed. Ensure that the employee health paperwork is available for verification at all times.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees practice adequate handwashing before donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine was observed soiled. PIC was made aware. PIC began dumping the ice from the ice machine to get it cleaned. The ice machine was cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ice machine baffles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
(REPEAT X2) Inspector observed the door seals of the prep cooler in the kitchen to be repaired with duct tape. Discussed with PIC and Cook, both informed inspector that the parts are already being looked at to properly repair the unit. Ensure that equipment is smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Duct tape is not considered smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Ensure this is completed by the next routine inspection (at least 90 days from now).

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: A few spatulas were observed torn creating little crevices on the surface. Discussed with PIC. The spatulas were discarded. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the one described above maintains their smooth surface and in good repair. 4-502.11(A) Good Repair and Calibration. (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The faucet in the men’s bathroom was observed leaking severely. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the plumbing is repair to be in compliance with the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following facility maintenance and cleaning issues were observed. 
1. (REPEAT x3) Inspector observed the wall above the mops sink splash guard to be crumbling. Ensure this area is repaired and repainted to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface.
2. (REPEAT)Grease and soil accumulations were observed beneath the fryers, grill, and stove in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. Ensure that these accumulations are cleaned to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
3. (REPEAT) Inspector observed the accumulation of dust, rust, and soil on the shelvings in the dish room. Ensure that these accumulations are shelvings are routinely monitored and cleaned. 
4. Broken tiles on the floor and a hole in the wall left of the ice machine in the serving area. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed a leakage and rots in the ceiling on the far end of the dry storage area by the walk-ins in the basement. PIC was made area. PIC informed inspector that a technician is scheduled to come and do the repairs soon. Ensure that this is repair to ensure that the facility is in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training certification during today’s inspection. PIC said that those documents were locked away and they had no access to them. Inspector told PIC to have copies of certifications in a folder accessible for inspection purposes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify allergen training due to the restricted Acces to paperwork at the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the paperwork is provided or the training done to be in compliance. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed a standing cooler obstructing the hand sink. Discussed with PIC and the cooler location was adjusted to ensure an accessible hand sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are accessible at all time for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed dumped ice in the handwashing sink. PIC was made aware. And education was carried out. Ensure that employees are aware to use all handwashing sink for handwashing purpose only at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer in the dish machine was tested at 0 ppm at the beginning of today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. The technician was called. The sanitizer was retested after the repairs and it tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that the sanitizer in the dish machine is always tested and maintained within an appropriate concentration range at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The standing cooler in the kitchen was observed not holding the appropriate temperature range.  PIC was made aware. PIC informed inspector that the food items in the cooler were placed in the cooler on 6/14/2026 (two days prior to the inspection). The food items in the cooler was discarded. The cooler was repaired and the ambient temperature collected was 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There was no hanging thermometer present in the standing cooler in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC provided a hanging thermometer for the cooler. Ensure that there is always a hanging thermometer present in all cold holding units at all times.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: An accumulation of food debris was observed under the fryer in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the surface would get clean. Ensure that closed spaces under equipments are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the triple sink was observed coming off breaking the sealing of the triple sink to the wall. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the caulking is redone providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The gasket on the standing cooler in the kitchen was observed in disrepair and coming off the door. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the gasket is changed or repair to ensure the unit maintain the appropriate temperatures.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. An accumulation of grease and dust were observed dangling from the hood filters in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that the third-party company that usually clean the hood were scheduled to be at the facility a couple days before but canceled due to scheduling conflicts. Hence, they are scheduled to be in the facility within a day.  Ensure that the filters are cleaned to avoid the contamination of food.
citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The PIC stated a cooler has not been obtained. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/29/26. Contact the inspector as soon as the new cooling unit has been obtained to verify proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed a staff member wash their hands, then fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was provided. Ensure the use of a barrier after completing hand washing to prevent re-contaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed ground beef at 119F. CORRECTED- it was verified that the food had been in the unit less than 4 hours, and the unit was turned from “1” to “3”. Food was then observed to have an internal temperature of 140F.
