Ensure hot holding units are always set so that hot temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods have an internal temperature of 135F or higher.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed TCS foods in the standing cooler (nearest the door) to have internal temperatures between 45-50 (hotdogs and hamburgers respectively). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit less than 4 hours were moved to a working cooler or implemented under time as control (items are to be used or discarded within 4 hours). Items housed in the unit over 4 hours were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods (including all animal proteins, house made products using mayo as an ingredient, cut tomatoes, and shredded lettuce) are cold held at or below 41F, or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the standing cooler nearest to door to have an ambient temperature of 50F, and failing to hold TCS items at or below 41F (see violation #22). A follow up is being scheduled for 6/26/26 to verify compliance. Ensure the unit has been serviced to cold hold foods below 41F.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) on staff does not have Allergen Awareness training. Inspector provided Allergen Awareness training information to the PIC. Ensure all CFMs obtain Allergen Awareness training, to be maintained on file every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The bar hand washing sink was obstructed by the garbage can. CORRECTED- the can was moved. Find a new placement for the trash can that does not block the sink. Hand washing sinks must be maintained accessible at all times to allow for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the baffles of the ice machine to contain an accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- The ice was covered, and baffles were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of consumables.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing freezer upstairs to be in disrepair. The current handle is corner trim and duct tape. Duct tape is an adhesive, and therefore deteriorates. Discussed applying a sheet metal with a convex handle. CORRECTED- the duct tape was removed.  All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed no barrier to be used when hand washing. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing and hands were rewashed. Ensure a barrier is used when washing hands to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed cut tomatoes to be held past date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, tomatoes will be discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the beginning of this inspection there was not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and called the owner during the inspection. They arrived to correct the immediate violation. They were instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

An employee was observed to dump a sani bucket into a hand sink during the inspection. Education was conducted to correct. Ensure that hand sinks are only used for hand washing and no other purpose int he facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani buckets in the front of the kitchen as well as the bar area were observed low at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section.

1) A container of salsa in the walk-in cooler was observed with an incorrect date. The cook stated that the sticker would not come off when washed. 2) A container of pico was observed without a date marking in the walk in cooler. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and corrected during this inspection. Ensure that date marking is correctly managed by all employees in the facility at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A bag of onion were observed stored on the floor in the kitchen. The cook was shown and the onions moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to prevent possible pest concerns and contamination from the floor.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

The sink in the bar area is leaking from both the faucet connection as well as the drain pipe. The PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all plumbing fixtures in the facility are maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee’s can of sprite was observed in the standing cooler next to open salsas ready for service. The PIC was consulted and instructed to store employee foods separate from foods intended for consumers moving forward. Store employee belongings in such a way so that there is not a concern for contamination of consumer foods.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
The metal board sealing the door of the walk-in cooler was observed not properly sealing the gap under the walk-in cooler door. This gap was observed during facility’s routine inspection on 6/4/2026. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the  gap will be fixed allowing the door to seal cooler properly. 
Ensure that this gap is closed to avoid food spoilage and a damage to the cooling unit.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a metal scrubber stored in the basin of the hand sink next to the ice machine. The person in charge (PIC) was informed and the scrubber was removed. Ensure staff are using the triple sink or utility sink to scrub dishes and never the hand sinks. This violation was corrected on site.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed the egg rolls to be stored in direct contact with a washing cloth. This cloth was heavily saturated with water. The PIC stated that the egg rolls release water as they thaw and become soggy in the metal container. Inspector recommends using a straining insert to keep the egg rolls dry and prevent cross-contamination. Ensure egg rolls are stored properly to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.13 Linens and Napkins, Use Limitation. LINENS, such as cloth napkins, may not be used in contact with FOOD unless they are used to line a container for the service of FOODS and the LINENS and napkins are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new CONSUMER.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed a knife to be stored in the crevice between the prep cooler and stainless steel countertop. The PIC was informed that this crevice is not easily cleanable. Therefore, the knife cannot be stored here. The inspector recommends purchasing a magnetic knife block to attach to the shelf of the prep cooler for safe storage. The knife was moved to the dish area during today’s visit. This violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed a wastewater leak coming from the hand sink to the left of the grill. The leak is coming from the connection between the PVC plumbing and the metal sink basin. Wastewater leaks pose a cross-contamination hazard, especially located so close to the cook line. A follow-up will be conducted on Monday, June 22, 2026 to ensure the leak has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: There was not a CFPM present at the start of the inspection and there were a number of priority and priority foundation violations observed during the inspection, including but not limited to: no sanitizer bucket made and available, switching tasks without washing hands and changing gloves, improper storage order, and improper reheating procedures. CORRECTED- The CFPM arrived during the inspection and these violations were corrected during the inspection. The CFPM was observed to educate staff on these violations. Based on this number of priority and priority foundation violations, an educational visit will be conducted with the Spanish translator at SCDPH, Kelly Hamlin.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: A Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was not present at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to switch from washing a dish to engaging in food preparation. CORRECTED- The PIC educated the employee on when to wash their hands. Ensure that staff are educated on when to wash hands and on proper handwashing procedures. Further education will be conducted regarding handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The trash can in the kitchen was observed to be in front of and obstructing the only handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the employees. The trash can was moved to another spot. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
There were multiple instances where food was observed to be in a package that exposed it to potential contaminants: 

1. There was observed to be raw meat stored directly in a grocery bag. CORRECTED- The raw meat was switched to be in another container. 
2. There was observed to be an open can of tomato purée, an open can of jalapeños, and an open can of chipotle peppers. CORRECTED- These food items were moved into another container. 

Education was conducted with the PIC. Grocery bags are not a food-contact surface and food should never be stored directly in them. After the can of an acidic food item is opened, the can is no longer meant to protect the integrity of its contents and the food item can be adulterated. Ensure that food is stored in a container that does not expose it to adulteration or to potential contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was observed to be raw, shelled eggs above yogurts and other ready-to-eat food items in one of the double-door standing coolers in the kitchen. In the same cooler, there was also observed to be raw sirloin tip on top of a pan of cooked meat. CORRECTED- The raw eggs and the raw sirloin tip were moved to be on the bottom shelf of the cooler, below other ready-to-eat food items. A storage order handout that is in Spanish was provided and an English one is already posted on a cooler. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were multiple containers of food that were observed to not have a cover on them in the double-door standing coolers. This was discussed with the PIC. Saran Wrap is observed to be used to cover some of the containers and it was recommended continue this practice with all of them. Ensure that food is stored in a package, a covered container, or is wrapped to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
comment: There was a pan of cheese sauce that was probed to be at a temperature of 97F on the steam table. The employees stated that it was being reheated on the steam table. CORRECTED- The PIC and the employees were educated that reheating should be done on the grill or the stove to make sure that the food item reaches a temperature of at least 165F. The cheese sauce was placed on the stove to be reheated. The probe thermometer was observed to still be in the package and the PIC was educated that this should be in use to make sure the reheated food is reaching the correct temperature. Steam tables are not typically made to be able to rapidly reach a temperature of 165F, which is why they should not be used for reheating. Ensure that food is being reheated to at least 165F before being placed in hot holding.
citation_text: 3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of cheese sauce, a container of cooked meat, and a pan of cooked meat that were observed to not have any date-marking on them. CORRECTED- The employee stated that the food items were made yesterday and the foods were date-marked. Date-marking was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods that are kept for more than 24 hours are date-marked with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day. Further education will be conducted regarding date-marking.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The bleach that was being used to make sanitizer buckets was observed to be a bleach that is not EPA-Registered and is meant for “whitening and brightening”. CORRECTED- The Disinfecting, EPA-Registered Clorox Bleach was in the dry storage room and was shown to the PIC to use for sanitizing food-contact surfaces. Ensure that chemicals used for sanitizers are EPA-Registered and are safe to use on food-contact surfaces. Ensure that staff are educated on this.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was not a sanitizer bucket made and available for use in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that staff are educated that a sanitizer bucket should be made before engaging in food preparation or cooking.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink in the kitchen is observed to need to be re-sealed to the wall.
2. The bare wood above the triple sink needs to be painted or sealed. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The handwashing sink in the banquet area was observed to be blocked by a trash can. CORRECTED- The inspector moved the trash can and discussed this with the PIC. 

The handwashing sink in the bar is observed to have a strainer in it, indicating that drinks are being dumped in the sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the strainer will be removed.  

Handwashing sinks should be accessible at all times for employee use and they should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine in the kitchen is observed to only be reaching a temperature of 138F and is not registering a concentration of Chlorine. A follow up is scheduled for 6/17/2026 to ensure that the dish machine is either reaching a temperature of 160F or is sanitizing at a concentration of 50ppm of Chlorine or above. It was discussed with the PIC that the dish machine can still be used but the dishes need to be manually sanitized in the triple sink after using it. Ensure that the dish machine is being frequently tested to make sure that it is properly sanitizing food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The ice machine baffle was observed to have rust on the baffle from a nail that has water going over it. CORRECTED- This was cleaned during the inspection and it was discussed with the PIC to contact maintenance to replace the nail to prevent contamination to the ice from rust. 

The ice scoop for the banquet ice machine is observed to be stored on top of the ice machine. CORRECTED- The scoop was washed, rinsed, and sanitized and will be placed in a container going forward. 

Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was a bottle of opened teriyaki sauce that states to “Refrigerate After Opening” observed to be in the dry storage room. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the teriyaki sauce was discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are being refrigerated after being opened. Educate staff to read labels to determine if it needs to be refrigerated.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There are single-service plates in a brown cart and on the buffet line that are observed to not be inverted. These plates are being stored in a manner that exposes the food-contact surface to contamination. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that single-service articles and utensils are being stored inverted to prevent contamination to the food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The walk-in freezer is observed to have ice accumulation on the fans and on the ground under the fans. Ensure that the issue causing the accumulation is repaired and that the ice is removed to allow the surfaces to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There is a leak coming from the single faucet to the left of the triple sink that is observed to be dripping into a bucket. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that this leak is repaired. Plumbing should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The floor in the soda syrup room. 
2. The shelves in the main walk-in cooler. 
3. The wall behind the dish machine. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The coving across from the dish machine is observed to be coming away from the wall. Ensure that this is re-sealed to the wall. 
2. There is a piece of broken coving to the left of the dish shelves in the dish area. This was shown to the PIC. 
3. There is a broken tile in the dish area that is observed to have water pooling under and around it. Ensure that this floor tile is repaired. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed multiple buckets in the hand sink obstructing handwashing. Education was carried out. The buckets were removed. Ensure that the hand sink is always available and accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was no sanitizer ready and available at the beginning of today’s  inspection. Education was carried out. A sani bucket was made and tested at 100 ppm for Chlorine. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made at the appropriate concentration during operation at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Personal cleanliness.
comment: Employees were observed without hair covering. Education was carried out. PIC left to get hair coverings. Appropriate hair covering was provided. Ensure that employees always have the appropriate hair covering at all times.
citation_text: 2-402.11 Effectiveness. (A) Except as provided in (B) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wear hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings or nets, beard restraints, and clothing that covers body hair, that are designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed TCS vegetables to be resting on prep table at 70F. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled 2 hours before and are in use as orders come in. Education was provided on proper cold holding expectations, and facility will be using a Time as Control for the vegetables. PIC is unsure if this will be a permanent addition, however inspector provided facility with paperwork and education if facility would like to continue. Ensure any TCS item is being cold held below 41F or discarded after 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and items were dated. Ensure after 24 hours, any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is date marked and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed TCS item in walk in cooler to be resting on floor. Discussed with PIC, items were moved to at least 6 inches off of ground. Ensure any TCS item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there were not signed employee health reporting agreements at the facility. The PIC was provided with agreements today and all present employees signed copies. Ensure that all employees who handle food sign the employee health reporting agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the single-user bathroom does not dispense water when the handle is turned to the hot setting. Cold water is readily available when turned to the cold water setting. PIC was informed that the sink should be serviced. Inspector will Follow Up to see that this handwashing sink is dispensing hot water. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are equipped to provide hot water.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that a sanitizing solution for food-contact surfaces had not been made while food was being prepared. CORRECTED: PIC made a sanitizing solution using food-grade Bleach (Chlorine) that tested at a safe and effective concentration of 100ppm. PIC and Inspector also discussed procedures for both triple sinks, and keeping a sanitizing solution near both establishment’s food prep areas. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces that are being used for food preparation or serving are cleaned regularly use an EPA approved chemical-sanitizer for food grade surfaces, and that they are regularly tested using test strips for safe and effective concentrations of the chemical. For Chlorine/Bleach, test for concentrations between 50-200ppm.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a buildup of residues in the ice machine in the front area. PIC was informed that the ice machine should be cleaned. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm that the ice machine is clean to sign and touch. Ensure that the ice machine’s food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed that RTE, TCS foods were being cold held beyond 7 days of their initial preparation date. CORRECTED: PIC voluntarily discarded these items that were held beyond 7 days from their initial preparation date, per their datemark: sliced tomatoes, and hotdogs. PIC and Inspector discussed the 7-day rule (day 1 is date of opening or preparation of RTE or TCS foods, and day 7 is the date the food item should be either used or discarded). PIC made a plan for when TCS & RTE food should be prepped every week, and when it should be discarded, so as to align with the 7 day rule. This included preparing appropriate amounts of food to meet customer demand during those 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single-use food carton being stored upright instead of inverted. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and inverted the food cartons, so that the food-contact surfaces inside of the cartons are protected from debris. Ensure that single-service and single-use articles are stored so that the food-contact surfaces are are protected form contamination, including through inversion, underneath a shelf, or inside their original packaging.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that the undersides of the coffee maker has an accumulation of residues. PIC was informed, and the coffee makers will be cleaned by the next routine inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the mop was being stored in the lower basin of the mop bucket instead of the upper basket where it can air-dry. CORRECTED: PIC moved the mop to the upper basket of the mop bucket where it can effectively air-dry between uses. Ensure that mops are stored after use in a position that allows for air-drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that water is accumulating in the bottom of the standing cooler in the storage area. PIC was informed. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed raw chicken being stored above raw fish, and raw fish being stored above ready-to-eat foods (sauces and sliced peppers) in the 2-door stacked standing cooler and the bottom of the prep cooler. CORRECTED: The raw chicken was moved below the raw fish, and the ready-to-eat foods were moved to a separate part of the prep cooler so that they were not stored below raw meat. Inspector and PIC discussed keeping meat in separate doors of the prep cooler. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods, and that meats are stored in order of final cooking temperature, with the highest temperature on the bottom: fish & shrimp & eggs (135 F), whole intact beef and pork (145 F), ground beef and pork (155 F), and chicken and poultry (165 F) always on the bottom.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed several food items stored inside the 3-door standing cooler that were well above the cold holding temperature of 41°F. CORRECTED: PIC and Inspectors checked all food items with a calibrated stem thermometer and either discarded items or moved items to working coolers: 
- items that were too warm and were prepared outside of the safe cooling time window were discarded; 
- items that were still cooling inside the safe cooling time window were moved to working coolers to continue cooling.
Items voluntarily discarded included: ~6 containers of raw chicken (47-52°F), 2 containers of raw steak (52°F), a 2 containers of cooked chicken (49-85°F), and 3 small containers of cooked potatoes (50°F).
PIC will work on getting the 3-door standing cooler repaired (see Violation #33) and will confirm with Inspector before resuming food service in the cooler. Ensure that all TCS Foods are cold held at temperatures of 41°F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed the 3-door standing cooler was no longer cooling or cold holding, with several food items measured at temperatures above 41°F. PIC and Inspectors checked all food items with a stem thermometer and discarded or moved items as determined by temperature and cooling time (see Violation #22). Inspector will Follow Up to check the progress of repairing the 3-door standing cooler. Cease all food storage in the 3-door standing cooler until Inspector can confirm the cooler is effectively cooling and cold holding food. Ensure that all equipment for cooling and cold holding is sufficient in capacity to provide temperatures below 41°F.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: SECOND REPEAT- The only employee working was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The employee has been working on the course and should be taking the CFPM test soon. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were raw, shell eggs observed to be stored above a container of marshmallow fluff and other ready-to-eat food items in one of the fridges. CORRECTED- The eggs were moved to be on the bottom shelf and this was discussed with the owner and the PIC. The owner mentioned making a sign for the fridge to keep the eggs on the bottom. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments. Three live juveniles were observed under equipment on the cook line. All pests observed today were fast-moving. Ensure glue traps are out and dated at all times to monitor activity. SCDPH will continue to follow-up until no pests are observed. This means keeping the glue traps present as a monitoring tool and insuring treatment is curtailing life cycles. The next follow-up is scheduled for July 29, 2026. 

 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to provide written procedures for cleanup of vomit or diarrhea. CORRECTED- inspector provided CDC Norovirus cleanup handout to the PIC. Ensure these directions are either kept on file or posted so that staff may follow proper disinfection procedures to prevent the potential spread of Norovirus.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the front and back of the ice machine baffles. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/22/26 to verify compliance. Empty, clean, and sanitize the ice machine. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility uses both quaternary ammonia (wipes) and chlorine bleach (triple sink) to sanitize food contact surfaces. The facility did not have a test kit for chlorine bleach, and the test kit for the quaternary ammonia was observed to have expired 7/1/24. Obtain new test strips for both sanitizers. All chemical sanitizing solutions used for food contact surfaces must have a test kit to verify the concentration recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of the standing cooler to contain an accumulation of debris. Ensure nonfood contain surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may contaminate foods of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the physical facility in need of repair.
1) SECOND REPEAT: The wall in the kitchen is missing caulking behind the rinse and wash portions of the triple sink. Ensure the sink is resealed to the wall to allow for a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The backsplash of the sink in the women’s restroom is bare wood. Paint or seal the bare wood so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
3) FIRST REPEAT: A gap exists between the mop sink and the wall directly to the left. Re-adhere the sink basin to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
4) The wall to the left of the hand washing sink in the men’s restroom contains holes and bare wood, where the previous soap dispenser was located. Fill holes and paint bare wood.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in proper repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed duct tape on 2 areas of the grill cooler. The person in charge (PIC) stated it’s purpose was to cover switches. Discussed replacing the duct tape (which contains an adhesive that can degrade) with plastic or sheet metal. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Correct by next routine inspectino.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were various cooked food that lacked date marking inside of the prep cooler. These items were cooked noodles and cooked chicken. Discussed with the PIC and the items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that time/temperature control (TCS) foods are date marked with the date of preparation if being held for longer than 24 hours in house.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of the ventilation system were observed heavily accumulated with dried grease. The PIC mentioned that the facility cleans the baffles every Saturday, however, the baffles were black in color and will need to be cleaned more frequently due to the amount of frying in the facility. The ansul system was also accumulated in grease debris. See that a professional hood cleaning company services the duct work of the hood system.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: There isn’t any hot water available at the handwashing sink inside of the only functional bathroom. The PIC mentioned that the facility is aware of the issue and a plumber will be to service the sink soon. Ensure that all handsinks are equipped with hot water to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026 to check for running hot water.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There is massive leak at the handwashing sink across from the cookline. Waste water is spilling onto the floor from the pipe underneath the basin. The facility is aware of the leak and will have a plumber service the sink soon. Ensure that all piping of handsinks are in good repair and never in leaking condition. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Overall, the facility could benefit from a detail cleaning. Floors and walls throughout the kitchen are coated with dried grease and debris. During slow periods, be sure to pull equipment from wall to sweep, mop, and scrub accumulated areas. The inner surfaces inside of the drawer cooler were observed with spilled liquids and debris. Shown it the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as possible to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine were observed with black mold on the food contact surface. Shown to the PIC. See that the interior surfaces of the ice machine are cleaned as frequent as possible to prevent mold build up. Will followup on 6/22/2026 to ensure that baffles have been cleaned and are free of mold.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A mini cooler along the service line was observed with an ambient temperature of 60F (probed). The PIC indicated that the cooling switch was accidentally turned off, not allowing for efficient cold holding temperatures. The food products were recently added to the cooler and items were placed on an ice bath to correct the violation. The cooler’s temperature was observed to decrease in temperature after the switch was flipped on. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to maintain temperatures of 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A second mini cooler was observed not holding proper cold holding temperatures. A portion of milk was probed at 50F. The temperature knob was placed on level 4 and the knob was turned to level 7 to make sure that the cooler is functioning properly. The cooler holds dairy products and the items were recently placed inside of the cooler. The temperature of the cooler started to decrease after adjusting the knob. Violation corrected. Ensure that the cold holding equipment is sufficient for maintaining temperatures of 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Despite the facility being in full operation, there weren’t any sanitizer buckets present for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC and a bucket was created and tested at 400ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that there is alway a sani solution available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The interior of the hood system was observed accumulated with dust. Shown to the PIC. A professional hood cleaning company will need to service the system to clean the duct work. Ensure that hood system is cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food handler training
comment:
At least four of the individuals working at the time of the inspection had expired food handler certificates. Be sure to get employees re-certified and compliant with food safety guidelines. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple chemical sanitizers to not meet required chemical sanitizing concentrations:
1) The dish machine at the bar (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- sanitizer was replaced, machine was primed, and ran until it was observed to be in compliance.
2) The sanitizer bucket was observed at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the bucket was remade to 200 ppm.
Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine, and 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed a gallon of milk held past it’s expiration date (6/9/26). CORRECTED- the milk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure prepackaged foods are not held past their expiration or “best by” dates to prevent the growth of pathogens.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets along the 3 door refrigerator to be frayed. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained in proper repair. Correct by next routine inspection.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.

citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The following TCS food items were observed to be out of temperature: 

1. There were 76 bottles of lemonade that were probed to be at temperatures between 57F and 62F. These bottles of lemonade state to “Keep Refrigerated” and were placed in a open-air unit that did not allow proper cold holding. All of these bottles were voluntarily discarded by the PIC.

The ambient temperature of these containers of watermelon and cantaloupe were between 55F and 60F. The PIC voluntarily agreed to place these containers of cut TCS fruit on Time as Control and these containers will be sold or discarded by 5pm.

Ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held at 41F and below.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.

comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The fan covers in the meat walk-in cooler. 
2. The shelves in the dairy walk-in cooler. 

This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
