title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of soil build-up in the dish machine. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspectors that the soil accumulation will be clean. Ensure that the accumulation is monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
The following plumbing repairs requirements were observed.
1. The left faucet on the triple sink was observed leaking. 
2. The faucet on the dump sink was observed leaking continuously.
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the plumbings is in good repair according to the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of grease build up was observed on the sides of the  fryers. 
2. The coving trim tile under the drink station was observed coming off the wall. 
3. Inspectors observed a hole in the trim edge of the door to the dry storage. 
Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspectors that the areas mentioned will receive the relevant corrections. Ensure that these corrections are made to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The deli/bakery walk-in cooler is observed to have ice accumulation on the ground and coming from the fan units. Ensure that the issue causing the ice build-up is repaired and that all the ice is scraped off to allow the floor to be smooth and easily cleanable. Due to this being a third repeat violation, a follow up is scheduled for 7/13/2026 to ensure that this violation is corrected. 

2. The shelf closest to the door on the left side of the deli walk-in cooler is observed to be significantly rusted on the bottom shelf. Ensure that this shelf is repaired or replaced to prevent contamination to food from rust. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
The following plumbing systems are in need of repair: 

1. There is a leak coming from the kitchen triple sink’s left faucet. 
2. There is a leak coming from the handles of the faucet of the kitchen handwashing sink. 

Ensure that these leaks are repaired. Plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The hood baffles. 
2. SECOND REPEAT- The floor under the fryers in the kitchen of the deli is observed to have an accumulation of grease and food debris on them. Ensure that these floors are being regularly cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soil residues. 
3. The wall and baseboard under the kitchen triple sink. 
4. The dish shelves to the right of the kitchen triple sink. 
5. The floor to the right of and behind the Henny Penny in the kitchen of the deli. 

Ensure that physical facilities are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

A small amount of slime/mold is observed on the underside of the ice chute of the fountain drink machine. The inspector wiped the area to show the PIC. Ensure that this is maintained clean at all times moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any soap available at the hand washing sink near the dish room. A new bag of soap was added to the soap dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always soap available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The machine was cycled and primed several times without a change in concentration. The facility was instructed to sanitize all dishes in triple sink until the dish machine can be serviced. Ensure that machine is serviced and sanitizing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration. Will follow-up 6/15/2026.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There were storage racks inside of the walk in cooler that contained a fuzzy debris on the outer surfaces. Shown to the PIC. Suggests that racks are taken outdoors to be power washed during down time. Ensure that racks are cleaned as frequently as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the back food preparation area is nonfunctional. The PIC mentioned that the wiring has been stripped and was unable to provide water to the hand-sink. Ensure that all hand-sinks are functional and are able to meet the needs for adequate handwashing. Will follow-up on 6/22/2026 to ensure that the sink has been serviced.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Despite being if full operation, there weren’t any sanitizer solutions available. Discussed with the PIC and a solution was prepared and tested at 300ppm (quat). Violation corrected on site. Ensure that sani solutions are available to sanitize food contact surfaces during operational hours.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor directly in front of the utility closet is starting to bubble. The PIC mentioned that there hasn’t been any recent water damage to the facility. See that the flooring is lifted and repaired to ensure a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is ice build-up coming from the fans in the bakery walk-in freezer that is being caught on a green tray. Ensure that the issue is repaired and that the ice is removed. 
2. There is a slow leak coming from the ceiling of the bakery walk-in cooler. Ensure that this leak is repaired. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is missing coving to the right of the bakery walk-in freezer. Ensure that this coving is replaced and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The sealing on the bakery handwashing sink is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this is re-sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. There is observed to be a gap in the NUDO board behind the ice machine in the bakery. Ensure that this is re-sealed. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The bakery walk-in cooler fan covers were observed to have an accumulation of dust on them. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that these fan covers are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no soap or paper towel available at the back room hand sink. The PIC was informed and both dispensers were refilled. Ensure hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote frequent hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a Purell alcohol-based sanitizing solution in use without a proper testing device to confirm product concentration. The PIC was informed that Purell test strips must be purchased in order to continue use of this product on food-contact surfaces. Instead, the PIC created a bleach solution that measured 100ppm with a test strip. This bottle was clearly labeled as bleach sanitizer spray.
citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed milk in walk in cooler to be less than 6 inches above floor. Discussed with PIC, milk will be placed in a location that is 6 inches above ground, ensure all food items are kept 6 inches above flooring
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed icicle forming in back walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure walk in freezer unit is working to th manufactures standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM was not available in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have a CFPM available at all times that the facility is in operation.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

The side door to the facility was observed to have a gap along the bottom seam sufficient to allow visible sunlight through. This indicates a gap sufficient for pest entrance into the facility. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Approximately 10 flies were observed throughout the facility, specifically by the hand sink, by the mop sink and in the storage room by the walk in cooler. The PIC is instructed to contact their pest control agency for maintenance and to reduce/remove the pests. A follow up is being set for one month out to allow time for the chemicals likely needed to take effect.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

A moist cloth was observed on top of the container of dry beans in the back of the facility. It appears to be a hold over from the most recent cleaning took place for the nearby counter. This rag should be stored between uses in the relevant bucket of sanitizer to prevent pathogenic replication from taking place. The PIC was consulted and had the rag moved to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A thick accumulation of frost and ice is observed in the walk in freezer on the shelves and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation moving forward. This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee drink was observed stored in a container including sauces for consumers and other foods. The cook was shown and removed the item to correct. Ensure that all personal foods are stored separately from those intended for consumers in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be prepared upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitzer solution is available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed microwave to be soiled with food splash debris. Discussed with PIC, microwave was cleaned with a sanitizer rag. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to change gloves without washing their hands and immediately moving to preparing a sandwich. Raw chicken was handled prior to this glove change. Education was conducted and the hands washed to correct. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times required by the code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation revealed an empty container of sanitizer concentrate. The PIC was shown and had the jug replaced. A recheck later in the inspection still showed no color change on the chemical test strips. Education was conducted in relation to priming the machine. The machine was primed by the inspector and registered correctly afterwards.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Cheese sauce is observed in the far right well of the steam table and with an internal temperature of 128F. The cook was consulted and stated that the items came from the cooking process recently. This was supported by other observations made during the inspection. This container is the only item in this well and the other side is open. It is believed that this is the issue and that was stated to the cook. A lid was added to the back side to trap in the escaping heat. The cheese was allowed to be brought back up to temperature to save it and correct the violation. Ensure that all hot held TCS foods are maintained at 135F or hotter at all times in the facility.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

1) The inner wall of the cooler under the pizza prep station is observed soiled with food debris. 2) The chest freezer has major frost accumulation observed. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all of the non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean to prevent possible contamination in the kitchen.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor in the walk in cooler is in need of cleaning, especially under the shelves, along the walls and in the corners. 2) The wall next to the fryer is observed heavily soiled with baked on grease. These two locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facilities are maintained clean at all times.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

A personal water bottle is observed in the standing cooler next to the manager’s office intermixed with foods intended for consumers. The PIC was told and instructed to remove. Ensure that all employee foods are stored separately from foods intended for consumers at all times. The bottle was removed to correct.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed carrots stored below raw fish in the prep cooler. CORRECTED- carrots were voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Ensure ready to eat food are always stored ABOVE raw foods to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the paper towel dispenser at the juice hand washing station to be non-operational. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) informed maintenance, who cleared the jam in the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always readily available to complete proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The standing cooler in the sampling prep room does not have an ambient thermometer. Ensure ambient thermometers are present at the front of cooling units to monitor the warmest temperature of the unit- which should be at or below 41F. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the ice machine to be soiled on the interior baffles. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned and sanitized frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil. A follow-up will be conducted on 06/22/2026 to ensure the ice machine has been properly cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed steel wool and wet paper towels in the basin of the hand washing sink in the cold room. CORRECTED- items were removed. Hand washing sinks are not to be used for any other purpose than hand washing, so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs stored over ready to eat foods (including but not limited to heavy whipping cream and prepared cakes). CORRECTED- the shelled eggs were moved below the ready to eat items. Ensure raw product is always stored below ready to eat product to prevent cross contamination of foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket to contain a concentration higher than was able to be registered by the facility’s test strips. CORRECTED- the sanitizer was remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizers used for foods contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.[P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple chemical sanitizers failing to meet sanitizing concentrations for food contact surfaces: 
1) The dish machine was observed to be failing to dispense sanitizer (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- the sanitizer bottle was replaced, and observed to be meeting required concentration for the sanitization of food contact surfaces. 
2) The bar triple sink was observed at 10 ppm Cl. CORRECTED- the sanitizer compartment was remade to 150 ppm Cl.
Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration recommended by the manufacturers label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm in the soda nozzles are the server station. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized at the bar triple sink. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed the following nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Dust on the fan by the mop sink (left of the triple sink).
2) Food residue inside of the pasta and salad prep cooler (left of the standing freezer)
3) Dust on the shelves holding pizza rounds.
4) Food debris in the microwave’s interior.
5) Rust and debris on the shelves in the walk in cooler. 
6) Dust on the fan above the back door.
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food reside, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The cooler drawers under the grill are observed to have an ambient temperature of 48F. The PIC stated that it was 37F this morning. The cooler drawers are likely having an issue keeping foods under 41F, due to the heat from the grill directly above it. There were multiple TCS food items that had just been prepared and placed in the cooler, including but not limited to, two pans of steaks, a pan of chicken, and multiple pans of riblets. A pan of pasta that probed to be at 48F had been placed in the cooler at 11am was placed on Time as Control and will be discarded at 5pm. Ensure that TCS foods are being cold held at 41F or under.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed on their phone and donning gloves right after without handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees stay off their phone and always wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. The PIC was reminded that all employees who do not have Certified Food Protection Manager certificates must obtain training in basic food handling principles within 30 days of employment. Ensure that all required employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. Ensure that all food contact surfaces remain free of contaminants at all times. 

Multiple nozzles for the drive thru fountain drink machine were observed soiled during this inspection. Per the PIC they should be being cleaned every night as part of the closing procedure. This appears to not be happening. The PIC was shown a nozzle and instructed to clean them.  All of the nozzles were removed during this inspection and cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) to correct the violation.  The PIC should review cleaning procedures with the relevant staff to ensure that this is not an issue again.

comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink in the dish room needs to be re-sealed to the wall. 
2. There is missing coving to the left of the dish machine. Ensure that this coving is replaced. 

Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The back of the hand washing sink is starting to pull away from the wall. There is about a half inch gap between the wall and the back of the sink. See that the sink is recaulked and sealed to prevent debris accumulation. Ensure that the old caulk is pulled and replaced at the handsink.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There were personal food items stored above items intended for public consumption inside of the reach in cooler. The personal items were stored above several gallons of milk. Discussed with the PIC that all personal items must be seperate from food intended for public consumption. The PIC moved the items to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure the employees’ personal items are stored below public food items to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: The facility does not have any written procedures for responding to a vomit/diarrheal event. The facility will need to purchase bleach, a bodily fluid kit, or chemical to use as disinfectant for responding to a Norovirus event. Ensure that a disinfectant and written procedures for cleanup are available to respond to a vomit/Norovirus event. Will follow-up on 6/18/2026.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The facility could not produce food handler certificates for most of the employees working at the time of the inspection. Discussed with the PIC that all employees that handle clean dishes or food must obtain food handler certificates if not already food manager certified. Recommended gathering a folder or binder with all printed documentation for future inspections. Ensure that food handler certificates are available at all times.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed creamer dispenser did not have a drip tray, so liquid creamer was dripping straight onto the counter. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the drip tray was located, put in place, and drips were cleaned up. Ensure that all nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free of an accumulation of residue.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that the PIC does not currently have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificate. No one on staff has a CFPM. Staff only have Certified Food Handler cards. Medium Risk establishments must have a CFPM present in the establishment when food preparation is happening. Inspector will return for Spot Check to confirm that establishment has a CFPM present during food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed fresh produce (whole onions, halved and whole green peppers) had split and/or spilled in the walk-in cooler and were on the floor, and had rolled to various places. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and picked up and discarded the contaminated produced. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect food from potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]]

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were multiple employees and no signed employee reporting agreements available. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: All temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items were observed to be out of temperature in the facility’s prep cooler. Items include, but are not limited to: ham (64F), ham salad (69F), chicken breasts (70F), roast beef (65F), and ham salad (64F). CORRECTED- items that had been in the unit for over 4 hours were voluntarily discarded. Items that had been in the unit for less than 2 hours were either moved to time as control or moved to the working standing cooler. TCS foods must be used or discarded within 4 hours after being removed from temperature control (41F and under for cold holding).
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 60F, and is failing to hold TCS foods at temperature- see violation #22. The PIC stated the AC in the building is scheduled to be fixed the following morning, and that will hopefully prevent the unit from over working. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 6/15/26 to verify that the prep cooler is holding TCS foods at or below 41F.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed multiple sanitizer buckets at 10 ppm chlorine bleach. CORRECTED- buckets were remade to 100 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested to be at concentrations recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the Diet Pepsi and Pepsi Zero soda nozzles at the drive thru to contain an accumulation of biofilm. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed to washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed light coming in along the left perimeter of the back door. Outer opening shall be protected from the entry of pests. Ensure weather stripping is placed to prevent gaps in the door, where pests may enter by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Multiple wet mop heads were observed to be stored in the empty basin of the mop bucket (kitchen and lobby mop sink). CORRECTED- Education about mop storage was conducted, and mop heads were moved to top of the mop bucket so they bristles could air dry. Ensure used mops are positioned to air dry to prevent the growth and harborage of bacteria with high water activity.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that PIC does not currently have a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificate. No staff have a CFPM certificate. Medium Risk establishments must have a CFPM present when food preparation is occurring. Inspector will return for a Spot Check to confirm a CFPM is present during food preparation. Ensure the PIC is a CFPM.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed staff putting on gloves when switching tasks without washing their hands. CORRECTED: Staff washed their hands before putting on food safe gloves. Ensure that staff thoroughly clean hands between tasks that could cause cross-contamination, and especially before putting on food gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that the handwashing sink was out of paper towels. CORRECTED: Paper towels were located and placed near the handwashing sink. PIC later refilled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are provided with disposable towels that are used to both dry hands and act as a barrier between clean hands and the sink handles.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed several pieces of equipment in need of cleaning:
(i) The hood above the fryers and pizza oven has a significant buildup of grease and soil residues in the vent, which can contaminate food and is a potential fire hazard. The vent is also missing a protective screen to prevent residues from dripping onto prepared food. Staff do not recall when the hood was last cleaned. The hood MUST be cleaned PROFESSIONALLY, and cleaned at a frequency to prevent the build up of soil residues. Inspector will Follow Up to confirm the hood is cleaned.
(ii) The area in the back of the soda machines has a build up of moisture and soil residues in several areas. There is a concern for mold. The area cannot easily cleaned by staff (equipment is bolted to the floor). Inspector will Follow Up to confirm the area is cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(i) Observed that the sanitizer bucket (quaternary ammonium) was measured at concentrations too low for effective sanitizing (50ppm). CORRECTED: PIC refilled the bucket from the triple sink, and the sanitizer bucket was tested at an effective concentration of 200pm. Ensure that all sanitizing solutions are tested frequently to confirm effective sanitizing strength (200-400ppm for quat). Testing frequently also confirms if the triple sink is effectively sanitizing.
(ii) Observed that the kitchen area does not have a sanitizer bucket available; the main sanitizer bucket is in the front of the store. CORRECTED: PIC made a new separate sanitizer bucket for the kitchen. Ensure that a sanitizer bucket is available where food prep is happening.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed several nonfood-contact surfaces in need of more frequent cleaning:
(i) The drip tray of the soda dispensers had a significant buildup of soil residues. CORRECTED: During inspection, staff cleaned the residues in the drip tray and will prevent future buildup by cleaning the drip trays with more frequency.
(ii) The floor in several areas in the kitchen and the walk-ins has an accumulation of debris and soils.
(iii) The coffee makers have an accumulation of residues at the top.
Please clean these areas by the next routine inspection. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent an accumulation of residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed several mops stored incorrectly, preventing them from air-drying: (i) on the floor with no place to drain; (ii) in the water basin of a mop bucket instead of the upper basket; (iii) in the bottom of the mop sink instead of hanging above the mop sink. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and staff fixed all mop storage issues. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air-dry and drain without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

The PIC stated that there are no plans to fix this cooler. The facility has enough cold holding without the use of this cooler. Ensure that this cooler is removed from the facility or is repaired. citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.

citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed microwave to be significantly soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure facility is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(Repeatx2) Observed the following areas to be in need of repairs:
1) Light shield is cracked in the kitchen.
2) Ceiling tiles need replaced throughout kitchen- old, some are torn/missing.

Discussed with PIC, repairs will be made to facility. Ensure staff is monitoring facility at a frequency that prevents such repairs to be needed.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing in between tasks. Education was carried out and the behavior was abolished. Ensure that staff are reminded to always wash their hands before donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The coffee maker was observed soiled. PIC was made aware. The coffee maker was cleaned and sanitized to sight of touch while inspector was present. Ensure that food. Contact surfaces such as the coffee maker is monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
The metal board sealing the door of the walk-in cooler was observed not properly sealing the gap under the walk-in cooler door. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the  gap will be fixed allowing the door to seal cooler properly. 
Ensure that this gap is closed to avoid food spoilage and a damage to the cooling unit.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed.
1. REPEAT Inspector observed multiple holes in the wall above the triple sink and the wall right of the triple sink in the kitchen.
2. There were broken tiles holding grease and soil accumulation observed under the fryers and grill in the kitchen.
3. The coving trim tiles along the wall right of the mop sink was observed fallen off the wall.
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that these spaces are sealed appropriately providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Inspector observed storage order in the following locations. 
1. Raw chicken was observed stored over cooked chicken in the standing cooler in the kitchen. 
2. Raw chicken was observed being stored over watermelon in the walk-in cooler.
Education was carried out and a storage order flyer was provided. PIC corrected the storage order while inspector was present. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on duty at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The owner who is a CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM with their Allergen training on duty during all hours of operation and food preparation. It is recommended to have multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were no signed employee reporting agreements available during the inspection. A follow up is scheduled for 6/15/2026 to ensure that there are signed employee reporting agreements available for every employee. Ensure that there are signed employee reporting agreements available for every employee and that there is a person in charge that is knowledgeable on where they are in the facility.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: There was not a Norovirus cleanup policy available in the facility. CORRECTED- A Norovirus cleanup policy was provided and the facility possesses bleach to effectively complete the procedure. Ensure that there is always a vomit/diarrhea clean-up policy available in the facility.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was observed to be ice in the server station handwashing sink, indicating that a drink had been dumped in the sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated that handwashing sinks should only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was observed to be raw pork over ready-to-eat food items in the bottom of the preparation cooler along the cook-line. CORRECTED- An employee switched the pork to be below the ready-to-eat food items. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice scoop for the ice machine was observed to be stored on a soda syrup box. CORRECTED- This was discussed with an employee, who switched the scoop to be in a pan. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are being stored on a clean, sanitized surface.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen that is used by the servers was observed to bleach out the Chlorine test strip, indicating that it is at a disinfectant level and is toxic to use on food-contact surfaces. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was re-made and tested to be at 200ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that staff are educated on how to properly make a sanitizer bucket to make sure that it is at a label-recommended concentration that is safe to use on food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: The bowls next to the soup hot holding were observed to be stored with their food-contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that single-service articles and utensils, including bowls that are going to be used once for a customer and then warewashed, are handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent contamination to food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The floor under the fryers is observed to have an accumulation of food debris and soil residue on it. Ensure that these floors are cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed a leak to be present in piping under triple sink. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. Ensure a licensed plumber services leak.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to be coming apart in the following locations:
1) Both hand sinks in bathroom
2) The mop sink. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and prepared at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared and available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: Observed that the establishment is hot holding manufactured cheese sauce in a dispenser (opened on day 1, and discarded on day 7), which is beyond the terms of their Category 3A - Low Risk permit, which does not allow for hot holding of any food items. CORRECTED: PIC and Owner were informed, and will cease serving hot held cheese sauce. Please contact SCDPH if establishment plans to change the menu to include food preparation like hot holding. Inspectors suggested acquiring single service shelf stable sauces that can be heated up by customers in the establishment’s microwave.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee moving from washing dirty dishes to donning gloves to begin food prep without washing hands between tasks. CORRECTED: Inspectors discussed handwashing and glove use procedures with PIC and Staff, including education on how hands should always be washed between tasks, and new gloves used for different tasks. Hands can quickly accumulate debris and microorganisms, which is why they should be cleaned frequently, especially as some contamination may not always be visible or noticeable. Ensure that all staff wash hands before putting on new gloves between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw hamburger patties being stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods like cheese in the front prep cooler bottom area. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and moved the raw hamburger patties below the RTE foods. Ensure that RTE foods are stored above raw foods, including raw meat.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizer buckets (quaternary ammonium) were at concentrations too low for effective sanitizing (50 ppm). CORRECTED: PIC went to the source of the sanitizer (the hose for the triple sink sanitizing compartment) and realized that its container of sanitizer was empty. PIC promptly replaced the container and refilled the sanitizer buckets, which then measured at effective concentrations (200-400ppm). Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are measured frequently throughout service to confirm sanitizing effectiveness.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of debris inside the prep cooler lid (the back ledge) in the front kitchen. PIC was notified, and will have that area cleaned by the next routine inspection, adding to their regular clean rotation. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free from an accumulation of food residues and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Was informed by the PIC that the oven/cooktop in the back kitchen is not functional and cannot be used. Repair or remove nonfunctional or unused equipment from the kitchen.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following equipment was observed in need of repair:
(i) Leaks were observed inside of two freezers (front 1-door and back 2-door), and the back 2-door (egg) cooler. Facility is taking additional measures in the meantime to prevent leaks from contaminating food. 
(ii) A leak was observed from the bottom of the steam table, resulting in water collecting on the floor of the cookline/service line. 
(iii) Duct tape on the back 2-door (egg) cooler is not an approved repair. Eliminate duct tape and repair door handle with materials that are smooth and easily cleanable.
Maintain equipment in good repair. Fix leaks to prevent water ponding on floors and inside coolers.
