citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that staff Food Handler certificates were not available in the facility, and certificates were not provided to the Inspector electronically. Ensure that all food handlers employed at the facility have Food Handler certificates which are available upon request.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to operate faucet handles after completing the handwashing process. The activity was ceased and corrected on site. The employee rewashed hands and used a paper towel to turn off the faucet handles. Ensure that a barrier is used to operate faucet handles after completing the handwashing process to protect against recontamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The facility is storing cooked egg rolls in a container and is using time control to maintain safety of food, however, an employee was observed bare handing a cooked egg-roll. The activity was ceased and the egg rolls were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that ready-to-eat (RTE) foods are never handled using bare hands. Instead, use single service gloves or utensils to protect against contamination of food items.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The owners could not locate any probe style thermometers for measuring the internal temperature of foods. The owners mentioned purchasing thermometers as soon as possible. Ensure that probe thermometers are always readily available. Will follow-up on 6/12/2026 to ensure that thermometers have been purchased.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were a couple dead insects observed on the floor underneath a storage rack that stores clean dishes. The dead insects were shown to the PIC and the insects were swept and discarded. The facility contracts with Adam’s Pest Control to provide treatment the building (serviced monthly). Ensure that the premise is cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of unwanted insects.
citation_text: 6-501.112 Removing Dead or Trapped Birds, Insects, Rodents, and Other Pests. Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
3rd Repeat Violation

The sealant between the counter and the wall to the right of the dish machine was observed heavily soiled in black residue. The PIC is new to the kitchen and was unaware of the ongoing violations. The PIC stated that a maintenance request will be submitted today for the sealant to be replaced. Ensure this sealant is monitored and replaced as needed, as moisture from the dish machine will cause it to degrade over time.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door drawer cooler under the grill:
1. Gyro meat (60.9F with probe)
2. Two containers of raw hamburger (60.0F and 62.3F with probe
3. Sliced cheese (63.4F with probe)
4. BBQ Pork (56.8F with probe)
The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC investigated the cooler further and discovered that the power switch had been accidentally turned off. The cooler was turned on and reached 41F during today’s visit. Since the items were discarded and the cooler is operational, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation
Inspector observed the following areas to need a deep-cleaning:
1. Flooring in kitchen under all shelving and equipment.
Ensure these areas are kept clean to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple live, slow moving adults, and dead adult roaches throughout the facility. Areas where roaches were observed included behind the bar, in the kitchen (along walls, and in one empty quinoa container), and dry storage. The person in charge (PIC) was notified. The PIC stated that pest control comes to the facility twice a month, and they are in the process of changing providers. Inspectors will conduct a follow up inspection on 7/1/26 to check progress of managing pests.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was raw beef observed to be stored directly inside a grocery bag in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the beef was moved into another container. Ensure that plastic grocery bags are never used to store food items directly in, as they are not a food-contact surface.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was a package of raw chorizo in the bottom of the preparation cooler on a shelf above a bag of vegan chorizo crumbles and vegan cheese. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the employee. The storage order of the items was switched and the vegan items were moved above the chorizo. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen was observed to have a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The PIC remade the sanitizer bucket and it was discussed to frequently check the concentration of the sanitizer. It is typically recommended to replace the sanitizer every two to four hours, depending on frequency of usage. Ensure that sanitizer is at a label-recommended concentration to make sure that food-contact surfaces are being properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: There was a container of refried black beans that were probed to be at 124F and a container of queso cheese probed to be at 128F in the steam table in the kitchen. CORRECTED- These items were reheated to be above 165F. The black beans were probed to be at 170F and the queso cheese was probed to be at 165F after being reheated. Ensure that TCS food is being hot held at 135F and above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of salsa that is made in-house with a date of 5/20/2026 and a container of mole that is made in-house with a date of 5/8/2026 on it. CORRECTED- These items were past the 7-day date-marking and were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS food items are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There is not observed to be any Chlorine test strips for the Chlorine sanitizer or Chlorine-sanitizing dish machine in the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 6/11/2026 to ensure that Chlorine test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are always test strips available in the facility for each type of sanitizer that the facility uses.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw beef to be stored under eggs in cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage order and beef was moved to above eggs. Ensure proper storage order is maintained to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 3 cans of food (mushrooms X2 and green beans) to contain significant dents along the seams. CORRECTED- cans were segregated from those for service to be returned to food supplier for credit. Ensure hermetically sealed cans are inspected for dents along the seams, and large dents along the body while stocking dry storage. Cans that are dented along the seams may allow for the entry and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The sanitizer bucket used for wiping food contact surfaces was observed to have no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made at a frequency to hold the concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The gallons of milk in the single standing cooler at the kitchen’s entry were probed to have an internal temperatures between 48-50F. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the milk had been delivered the previous day, so the milk (9 gallons) was discarded. A prune juice that was opened to take measure its internal temperature (labeled “refrigerate after opening”) was moved to the working 3 door cooler. Ensure all animal proteins, cut tomatoes and melons, and items labeled “keep refrigerated” are kept at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed opened milk, cut tomatoes, and prepared salads to lack date marking. CORRECTED- items were opened or prepared the previous day, and marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all ready to eat, temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with a date after preparation/ thawing/ opening, to be used or discarded within seven days to prevent the growth and harborage of Listeria. The day of opening/ thawing/ preparation counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed an open gallon of milk with a 5/24 expiration date in the memory care refrigerator. CORRECTED- the milk was discarded. Ensure milk is DATE MARKED once opened, to be used or discarded within seven days of date marking, OR by the expiration date, whichever comes first.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The standing single cooler at the kitchen’s entry was observed to have an ambient temperature of approximately 50F. The PIC stated the unit had been serviced approximately two weeks ago. At this time, the unit is failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #22. Ensure the unit is serviced or repaired by 6/8/26 to hold TCS foods at or below 41F.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The ambient thermometer in the kitchen’s standing cooler was observed to be broken. CORRECTED- the thermometer was replaced with a new working thermometer, and placed towards the front of the unit. Ensure cooling units contain working ambient thermometers to monitor temperatures of cooling units to be at or below 41F.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 3 boxes of canned foods stored on the floor of dry storage. Ensure all food and food contact surfaces are stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed forks, spoons, and knives in Memory Care stored with food contact surfaces facing UPWARDS. CORRECTED- the utensils were rearranged with a gloved hand so that only the hand contact surfaces were available to be dispensed. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a manner to prevent potential bare hand or environmental contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the top of the dish machine to contain a significant accumulation of debris. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Nonfood contact surfaces that contain debris may contaminate food contact surfaces. Increase the frequency at which this surfaces is cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning new gloves. Donning gloves with soiled hands poses a cross-contamination risk. The PIC was informed and education was conducted with staff. Ensure staff are washing hands properly prior to donning gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed the prep table on the service line to be damaged and temporarily protected with tape. The broken edge of the prep table is very sharp, and poses a hazard to staff. However, the tape is not food-safe and therefore cannot remain on the surface. Ensure the prep table is replaced to prevent food safety or employee safety hazards. 

FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed the triple sink in the food preparation space to be damaged and tipping away from the wall. Due to the incorrect angle of the sink basin, water is collecting and standing in the basin. Ensure this is repaired to prevent water retention in the sink. 

SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector also observed the triple sink to be cracked between two basins. This allows water to leak from the sink to the floor.

Ensure these items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant of both hand sinks to be damaged. This damage has resulted in a crevice between the sink and wall which allows for moisture to accumulate. The sinks must be maintained so that they are easily cleanable. Ensure the sealant is replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION - Observed interior of coolers to be soiled with food debris. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil.

Inspector observed the shelving above the triple sink to be heavily soiled. As clean dishes are stored on this shelf, this poses a contamination risk. Ensure the shelf is clean to sight and touch prior to the next routine inspection. 

Inspector observed the shelving in the walk-in cooler to be soiled with mold. The moisture in the walk-in cooler is contributing to this issue. Ensure the cooler is repaired and deep cleaned/sanitized prior to the next routine inspection. 

Inspector observed the triple sink to be soiled with black debris. This debris is building up around the sanitizer and detergent dispenser as well as the right corner of the sink. The right corner of the sink is not graded correctly, resulting in water collecting near the wall and pouring down the wall to the floor. This area is heavily soiled. Ensure the sink is cleaned, sanitized, and repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector observed the following areas in need of a deep cleaning:
1. Floor under stoves and fryers
2. Floors of dish area
3. Floors of walk-in cooler

Inspector also observed the vent of the walk-in cooler to be soiled with dust and debris.

 Ensure facility has been deep cleaned prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food-contact surfaces in the facility to be in need of repair:
1. SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION- The shelving holding clean dishes, single-service containers, and the selves above the triple sink were observed rusted and in need of repair/replacement.
2. REPEAT VIOLATION - There are two holes under the triple sink on the right wall. Ensure these holes are patched to prevent moisture from accumulating in the walls.  

These areas which are not smooth and easily cleanable pose a hazard for bacterial accumulation and food-borne illness transmission. Ensure these areas are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed two staff members on site that did not have a valid food handler’s certification. The PIC is aware of the issue. Qdoba has recently changed policy to pay for food handler’s certification for staff. Ensure all employees have food handler’s certification prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were raw ground beef patties observed to be above a package of impossible burgers in the bottom of a preparation cooler along the cook-line. CORRECTED- The raw ground beef patties were moved to be below the impossible burgers and it was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that raw proteins are arranged by cooking temperature to protect food items from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them: 

1. The baffle of the inside of the ice machine.
2. The soda gun nozzle at the bar. 

A follow up is scheduled for 6/8/2026 to ensure that both of these food-contact surfaces have been cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The cooler drawers under the grill in the facility are observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. The following food items were probed: 
- Three pans of steak: probed to be at 48F, 50F, and 52F. 
- A pan of chicken: 46F. 
- A pan of riblets: 50F. 
- A pan of cooked fettuccini noodles: 49F. 
CORRECTED- These items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. A pan of cooked Penne noodles were moved into another cooler, due to only being placed in the cooler about 30 minutes prior. It is recommended to check temperatures of coolers more frequently. Ensure that TCS foods are being cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The cooler drawers under the grill were observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. TCS food items that were above 41F were voluntarily discarded by the PIC (see violation #22). A follow up is scheduled for 6/8/2026 to ensure that the cooler drawers have been repaired and are cold holding at 41F or below. Ensure that equipment used for cold and hot holding is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There are observed to be flies next to the soda syrup boxes in the back of facility that are flying around a large puddle of pooling water. A follow up is scheduled on 6/8/2026 to ensure that the flies have been eliminated and the pooling water has been cleaned up. Ensure that pest control is routinely treating the facility, the facility is being maintained cleaned, and water is not allowed to pool to prevent pest harborage conditions.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The handle is observed to be broken off of the bar cooler containing glasses. There is no handle and employees have to use a tool to pry open the door. Ensure that this handle is replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
There are a number of nonfood contact surfaces that are observed to be in need of cleaning in the facility. The following nonfood contact surfaces are in need of cleaning: 

1. SECOND REPEAT- The crevices on the front and the outside of the chip warmer. 
2. The bottom of the gasket on the left door of the first preparation cooler. 
3. The gasket and crevices of the ice cream chest freezer door. 
4. The handwashing sink in the bar area is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on and in it. 
5. The wire shelves in the walk-in cooler have an accumulation of food debris and soil residue on them. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- There are broken tiles next to a drain in the dish area that are allowing pooling water. Ensure that these tiles are replaced. 
2. The drain under the dish machine is observed to have broken tiles next to it that is allowing food debris and water to pool. Ensure that this is cleaned and that the tiles are replaced. 
3. The baseboard coving to the left of the walk-in freezer door inside of the walk-in cooler are observed to be coming away from the wall. Ensure that these are re-sealed to the wall. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. All repairs should be made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The wall/baseboard behind the fryers. 
2. SIXTH REPEAT- The floor under equipment in the bar area. 
3. FIFTH REPEAT- The walk-in freezer floor. 
4. THIRD REPEAT- The drain to the left of the dish machine. 

Due to these first four items being repeated violations, a follow up is being scheduled for 6/29/2026 to ensure that these violations have been corrected and that cleaning is being done in the facility. 

5. FIRST REPEAT- The floor under and around the dish machine. 
6. The floor under the fryers. 
7. The vent in the hood above the dish machine. 
8. The walls and ceilings in both walk-in coolers are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue and mold on them. 
9. There is pooling water in the corner by the soda syrup boxes that is allowing pooling water. Ensure that water is not allowed to pool to prevent pest harborage conditions. 

Ensure that physical facilities are being cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the food handler certification for the employee present. PIC assured inspector that the certificate will be acquired. Ensure that employee acquire their food handler certificate after 30 days of employment.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was no CFPM present during today's inspection. PIC informed inspector that they will get the training done. Ensure that there is always certified food protection manager present at all times.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was a phone observed to be stored on top of a lid to a bread container. CORRECTED- The PIC removed the phone and educated the employee. Phones hold a significant amount of bacteria and should never be stored on a food-contact surface. Ensure that employee items are stored separately to avoid contaminating food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There is a bottle of Sushi Sauce that states to “Refrigerate After Opening” that is observed to be stored at room temperature in the dry storage area. The PIC was unsure of where the sauce is intended to be stored and will be looking at the trainings. The PIC stated that they will discard the sauce if it is required to be refrigerated. A follow up is scheduled for 5/29/2026 to ensure that the sauce has either been discarded or if it has been determined that the sauce is safe to be stored at room temperature.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: There were two knives observed to be stored with the blade between the side of the preparation cooler and the side of a preparation table. CORRECTED- Both knives were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Proper utensil storage was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that utensils are stored on food-contact surfaces that are frequently cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is observed to be no sealing between the dish table and the wall to the right of the dish machine. Ensure that the table is sealed to the wall and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The metal plate under the walk-in cooler door is observed to be loose and is allowing water to pool under it. Ensure that this metal plate is re-sealed to the ground to prevent food debris and water from accumulating under it.

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The back left corner (to the right of the reach-in coolers) and the front right corner (under the front soda nozzle) of the floor in the bar area are observed to be in need of cleaning. This was shown to the PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed several staff members donning gloves without washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that all staff are knowledgeable to wash their hands before donning new gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed grabbing ready to eat food (fries) for multiple orders with their bare hands. Education was carried out. Four plates of food involved in the bare handling were discarded while inspector was present. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that employees are reminder to avoid bare handling ready to eat food at all times.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled.
1. The soda nozzles on the lobby soda machine. PIC was made aware. The nozzles were cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. (COS)
2. (REPEAT) The ice machine baffle was observed to have soil accumulation. The PIC was informed to have the baffle cleaned, sanitized and kept free of soil accumulation. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles and the ice machine baffle is cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will follow-up on 06/08/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were no sanitizer/sani bucket observed in the kitchen or prep area upon arrival and during today’s inspection. Education was carried out. PIC was informed. Sanitizer for the sani buckets were made and tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made and placed in the sani buckets during food prep, handling, and service at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to be in need of repair:

1. SECOND REPEAT  Holes were observed in the wall above the dish machine on the right side. The condition was discussed with the PIC to have the holes sealed.
2. REPEAT Coving tiles beneath the drive-through, between the walk-in freezer and cooler, and behind the ice machine were observed to have peeled away from the wall. The PIC was informed and instructed to have the tiles properly secured and caulked.
3. Inspector observed a broken tile trapping soil and grease underneath the middle grill on the cook line. 

Ensure walls, tiles, and fixtures are maintained in good repair and sealed to allow for proper cleaning at all times.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THRICE REPEAT: The walk-in freezer door was observed not closing completely due to improper latching and ice accumulation. Cold air was observed leaking from gaps around the doors. The ice accumulation was cleaned and the door closed properly. Ensure that ice accumulations are removed to avoid the improper sealing of the Walk-in freezer.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A probe thermometer placed in an empty pan in the cooler read 54F. The cooler's digital read-out indicates 54F. All time/temperature controlled for safety (TCS) foods in the veggie prep cooler were recently placed in the cooler and therefore would not be indicative of the cooler's function. Time as a control will be used for TCS foods in the meantime until the veggie prep cooler is functioning properly. Foods must be used or discarded within 4 hours of prep/removal from walk-in or reach-in cooler. Inspector will follow up in 10 days to see that the veggie prep cooler is functioning properly.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The stand was displaying large slabs of focaccia which is pre-cut and served with tongs. The PIC was informed that the focaccia needs to be protected from sneeze, splash, and debris during display. The PIC created a temporary solution in the form of a box and plastic lid. A follow-up will be conducted on June 3, 2026 to ensure the focaccia is properly protected.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a significant number of drain flies present at the floor drain under the pretzel prep table. The PIC was aware of the issue and is in contact with Orkin. A follow-up will be conducted in one month (June 26, 2026) to ensure the pest concern has been resolved. Maintain pest control receipts for inspector to view.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspector observed no employee health/reporting agreements available or signed by staff. Education was conducted regarding this document and its importance to food safety. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure this document is signed by all staff and on file in the facility for the inspector to view.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Inspector observed no written procedure for vomit/diarrhea incidents in the facility. Education was conducted with the PIC and a policy was provided. The facility has bleach available for conducting the procedure. Ensure this policy is maintained on file for employees to refer to in the event of a vomit/diarrheal event in the facility.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed no non-latex gloves available at the bar for garnish handling. The PIC stated that their current practice for peeling oranges for garnish does not include wearing gloves. Edible flowers and cherries were also observed to be bare handed during today’s visit. Inspector conducted food handling education. The PIC was informed that all ready-to-eat foods must be handled with clean, gloved hands at all times. Ensure gloves are used in the future to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no hand washing sign present at the bar/kitchen hand sink or two bathroom hand sinks. The PIC was informed and hand washing signs were provided. Ensure these signs are posted by all three handwashing sinks and are clearly visible for all staff to view.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the PIC use the bar/kitchen hand sink to empty/refill the sanitizer bucket. The bucket was temporarily stored in the sink basin. Education was conducted regarding hand sinks. Ensure hand sinks are for hand washing only. Hand sinks cannot be obstructed under any conditions, especially since the facility only has one sink for the bar and kitchen.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the bar/kitchen sanitizer bucket measure 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer was not strong enough, and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure the bucket is monitored for proper chemical concentration. The sanitizer will weaken over time and must be replaced frequently.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with a black debris. The PIC was informed that the ice machine needs to be deep cleaned and sanitized. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed a container of pico de gallo in the prep cooler top measure 55F with the infrared probe. The pico de gallo was stored in a plastic container within a metal container in the cooler. This “doubling” prevents adequate air movement and refrigeration of the container. Since the pico de gallo had no date mark and the PIC did not know when the item was prepared, the container was discarded. Ensure proper cold holding is monitored with a stem thermometer. Storage in the prep cooler needs to promote proper cooling. A spot check will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored properly in the cooler and maintaining a temperature of 41F or less at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food items to be missing a date mark:

1. Pico de gallo
2. Shrimp
3. Sausage
4. Pork pieces

The PIC was informed that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) and ready-to-eat (RTE) foods must be date marked within 24 hours of opening/prepping. These items must be discarded within 7 days of marking. A handout was provided with extra details regarding proper date marking methods. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to ensure proper date marking practices are taking place in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no ambient thermometers stored in the prep cooler or upright cooler in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and plans to acquire thermometers for the cooler. Ensure all coolers have ambient thermometers prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed multiple dishes to be stored on a top shelf with their food contact surfaces exposed to splash and dust. The PIC was informed that the items need to be inverted to prevent contamination. Ensure these items are properly stored prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available at the facility. Quaternary ammonia is in use as sanitizer in both the sanitizer buckets and triple sink. The PIC was informed and stated she could not find the test strips. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 to confirm test strip availability. Inspector recommends having extra packs of test strips available to prevent future violations.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the seams of the wall paneling to be bubbling and separating. A white tape was used in areas to seal the seams, but this tape is already separating from the wall. Ensure the wall is repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Inspector observed the PIC describe inaccurate food handling procedures in the facility. The PIC stated that oranges and other garnishes are not handled with gloved hands. The inspector also observed the PIC training new staff on beverage preparation. The PIC was observed bare handing cherries, edible flowers, and citrus garnishes during this training event. The person in charge is responsible for knowing, understanding, and accurately communicating proper food handling procedures to staff members in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on June 5, 2026 regarding the PIC's knowledge of proper food handling practices in the facility.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (8) Describing the relationship between the prevention of foodborne illness and the management and control of the following: (a) Cross contamination, (b) Hand contact with READY-TO-EAT FOODS, (c) Handwashing, and (d) Maintaining the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in a clean condition and in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed a container of frappe mix being stored inside the ice machine with the container touching the ice used for drinks. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the mix was moved to the cooler. Ensure that food - in this case the ice that goes into drinks - is protected from cross contamination by keeping it separate from other food items and food packaging. Ice used for drinks should not be used for cold holding other food items.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed mold accumulation in the following areas: 
(Repeat) 1) The bar soda gun. 

Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned with a sanitizing solution. Ensure soda guns are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer line was adjusted and dish machine tested at 100ppm CL. Ensure facility is monitoring dish machine to ensure sanitizer levels are at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed with the accumulation of soil buildup. 
1. The baffles of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink mold.
2. The internal surface of the tea and coffee makers were observed to have a buildup of soil.

Discussed with PIC. All food contact surfaces mentioned were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) The following facility maintenance issues were observed.
1. The tile trim in the utility closet was observed coming off the wall. 
2. (REPEAT ) An accumulation of grease and food debris were observed under the fryers and grill in the kitchen. 
 PIC was made aware. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned and trim sealed properly providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Multiple wet mop heads were observed stored on the floor on the utility closet including in the draining pit. Discussed with PIC. PIC instructed a staff member to remove the mop heads and have them stored properly. Ensure that proper mop storage procedures are followed at all times.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Inspector observed missing Employee Health Reporting Agreements for two of the three staff members who were present during today’s inspection. All staff who work in a food establishment must be informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report food-borne illness symptoms and diagnoses to their employees. Inspector will verify compliance on 6/1/26. Ensure all staff read and sign Employee Health Reporting Agreements within 30 days of hire, to be maintained on file for inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: The inspector observed the basin of the back of house hand washing sink to contain a bucket and cleaning supplies. CORRECTED- the inspector moved the items to wash hands. Education occurred with the Person in Charge (PIC) regarding hand sink availability. All designated hand washing sinks must be used for hand washing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 3 cans of food dented along the seams. CORRECTED- items were removed from service. Ensure all hermetically sealed containers are inspected for bulging, rust, and dents along the seams to prevent the entry and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: A large quantity of foods that are either temperature control for food safety (TCS) or labeled “keep refrigerated” were observed to have an internal temperature between 46-60F in the open air cooler. Foods include but are not limited to: calzones, deli sandwiches, desserts with cream cheese icing, sandwiches, cottage cheese, hard boiled (and peeled) eggs, cheesewiches, Naked juice, and pickles (labeled “keep refrigerated”). In addition, a pallet of Simply Juices labeled “Keep refrigerated” was stored at room temperature in dry storage. CORRECTED- items in the open air cooler were removed from service, and the PIC ensured the inspector that all foods and drinks aforementioned would be discarded after logging waste. All TCS foods (including those labeled “keep refrigerated”- the label is the law) under cold holding must be at or under 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens that cause food-borne illnesses.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The mocha iced coffee bag was observed without date marking. CORRECTED- the inspector asked the PIC when the coffee bag was opened. PIC stated the bag was opened two days ago, and marked the bag with the corresponding date. Once TCS foods that are ready to eat and require cold holding are opened, they must bear date mark to be used or discarded within 7 days time.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the open air cooler to be failing to hold TCS foods at an internal temperature of 41F or below (see violation #22). Inspector recommends having the machine serviced to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. All cold holding units must have the capacity to maintain safe food temperatures. Inspector will return on 6/1/26 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed two stem thermometers 5-8F out of calibration. CORRECTED- the inspector modeled calibration using the ice water method to the PIC. Ensure all thermometers are maintained to be calibrated according to the manufacturer's instructions to provide accurate internal temperatures for TCS foods.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets of multiple standing coolers to be in disrepair. The following coolers need their gaskets repaired or replaced. Those housing: water, Gatorade, Celsius, Alani/ Bang, Monster (both) , and Mountain Dew. Ensure these repairs take place by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed build up on multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
1) A significant accumulation of ice in the blue bunny sliding freezer. Defrost and remove build up.
2) Soil debris on the outside of the ice shoots (soda stations).
Nonfood contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a wet mop stored in the basin of the mop bucket. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the mop was positioned to air dry. Mops function to clean up fats, oils, and greases- therefore must be placed in a position to air dry immediately after use to prevent the harborage of bacteria.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: At least three shelves inside of the walk in cooler were observed with dried debris. The shelves are used to store food, while some food items were uncovered and could possibility be exposed to cross contamination. Discussed and shown to the PIC. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors to be power washed and cleaned to remove the unwanted debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There is a bit of ice build up on the floor underneath the shelves of the indoor walk in cooler (shelves mentioned in violation #49). Shown to the PIC. Ensure that the ice is removed and that the cooler is maintained free of ice accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There was grease buildup observed along the floor and the wall behind the cookline in the kitchen area. Shown to the PIC. Be sure that a cleaning schedule is in place to ensure that employees are frequently cleaning hard to reach areas (behind cookline) to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The ceiling along the cook-line is observed to have an accumulation of flour on the tiles and light covers. There is observed to be flour coming from the ceiling onto food-contact surfaces and into the batter stations. This is a potential for cross contamination. This violation is still present today.
