The PIC stated that they are working on cleaning the ceiling. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 (combined with the scheduled follow up for violation #47) to ensure that the ceiling along the cook-line has been cleaned to prevent cross contamination to food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Two cans of Jalapeño cheese sauce were observed to be dented. PIC was made aware. The cans were removed from the inventory and stored separately to be returned. Ensure that all food product with compromised package integrity are removed from stock to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
FOLLOW UP REPEAT:
(i) The baffles of the hood system were previously coated with grease as to be observed with hanging debris. The operator has since the last inspection replaced 7 of 8 baffles with brand new baffles, with the 8th baffle to be replaced shortly.
(ii) There is dust and grease hanging from the Ansul system. See that the hood duct work is cleaned. The operator has scheduled hood maintenance for the end of May.
Inspector will Follow Up on 1 June 2026 to check that the hood has been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: On arrival there was not a CFPM available on site. Ensure that a CFPM is available on site at all times that they are in operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: A food handler was observed to change gloves without hand washing. Education conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The temporary hand washing station is observed in the hand sink on arrival and is deem not easily accessible. It was moved so the inspector could wash their hands and then m oved back after. Education conducted. Ensure that the hand washing set up is easily accessible to promote hand washing.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Various items that are packaged in house lacked specific label information. These items included packaged breads, veggies, seafood, etc. in many coolers, freezers, and shelves throughout the facility. Discussed with the PIC the required label information: common name of food, list of ingredients, name and place of business of manufacturer/distributor, and food source for each major food allergen. Ensure that the necessary information is included on packaged labels.
citation_text: 3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

An employee phone was observed on the cutting board of a prep cooler. A cut eggplant and knife were observed next to it as well as other foods being prepared. The PIC was shown and removed the phone to correct. The cutting board was sanitized as well. Ensure that employee belongings do not become a concern for contamination of foods and equipment.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair in the following locations:

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed no soap available at the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) placed hand soap at the sink, to be hung from a hook moving forward (also discussed installing a soap dispenser- as long as it is available and functional, it is in compliance with the food code). Ensure hand washing sinks are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels to allow for proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Discussed with PIC and education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to use a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The internal surface of the dish machine in the kitchen was observed with a buildup of soil accumulation. 
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the above mentioned surfaces would be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored, cleaned, sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The temperatures of the cut veggies in the prep cooler in the serving area were observed out of the appropriate range. PIC told inspector that all the food items in the unit may have been placed in the unit between last night and 9:00 AM today. The carrots were measured at 54 F and Celery was measured at 53 F.  The carrots (two trays) and celery (two trays and half a bag) were tossed. Ensure that chopped ready to eat food items are held within the appropriate temperature range to avoid bacteria growth.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler holding vegetables in the serving area was observed to not be holding temperature. The ambient temperature in the unit using an infrared thermometer was 61. The food items probed in the unit was temped at 53.5 on average. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the unit will be repaired within the follow-up timeframe. Ensure that the temperature of cold holding units are checked on a regular basis.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed a couple boxes of food items being stored on the floor in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. The boxes were removed to be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to avoid contamination through splash at all times.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the top of the kitchen dish machine to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning dish machine at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed dish machine to measure 0ppm chlorine after repeated cycles. The PIC was informed and maintenance was requested. The PIC told the inspector that the staff are currently using the triple sink to wash, rinse, and sanitize before items pass through the dish machine. Ensure wash, rinse, sanitize practices with the triple sink are maintained until the dish machine is repaired. A follow-up will be conducted on 5/21/2026 to ensure the dish machine is repaired.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the interior baffles of the ice machine to be soiled with black debris. The PIC was informed and plans to deep clean/sanitize the machine. Ensure the ice machine is clean to sight and touch prior to the follow-up scheduled on 5/28/2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following physical facilities in need of repair:
1. There is a hole in the wall near the door of the dry storage area.
2. There is a hole in the wall near the back door of the facility.
3. The wall behind the soda syrup boxes is damaged and brittle. 

Ensure these areas are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored directly above grapefruit in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed and the eggs were relocated. Ensure proper storage order is followed to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods (fruit pizza between 67-68F) above 41F. CORRECTED- items were moved to time as control- to be used or discarded within 4 hours. Items failing to hold below 41F must be used or discarded by the end of the day's market.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Current cold holding methods (hard sided cooler with not enough cold packs and cooler tray) are failing to hold TCS items below 41F. Discussed ice baths or using many more cold packs. Inspectors will check for compliance at the 5/23/26 market.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Inspector observed no disinfectant available for bodily fluid clean up. Obtain bleach or another disinfectant by 5/26/26 to ensure disinfectant is available to minimize the spread or contamination of food, food contact surfaces, employees, or consumers by vomit or fecal matter.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One employee who was present did not have a Food Handler's certificate available during today's inspection. All employees handling food must be certified as either a food handler, or certified food protection manager. Obtain necessary paperwork to be made available by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

1) The hand sink in the back of the facility was without paper towels during this inspection. 2) (REPEAT) The men’s bathroom was missing paper towels. Paper towels were supplied during the inspection to correct. Ensure all handwashing sinks are provided with hot running water, soap, and paper towels at all times.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

An open bag of hot dogs was observed in the walk in cooler without a date. This facility should not be serving any hot food per their risk classification. The hot dog package was likely opened in relation to the 4/10/26 inspection violation and should have been discarded at that time. The PIC was shown and discarded the package during this inspection to correct.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
(REPEAT from the Pre-Opening) 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

On arrival open boxes of foods were observed on the floor in the walk in freezer. This situation was noted on the previous inspection and is being placed here at this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to stored the cases of food on the available shelves moving forward.

4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. 

Only quat test strips are available in the facility and only CL (bleach) sanitizer is available. The situation was discussed and the PIC was instructed to get new test strips prior to the follow-up.

4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

When asked about wiping the counter for coffee or drink spill the PIC indicated that they use a spray Windex cleaner and towel. This is not acceptable and will need to be changed. comment:

1) Repair damaged cabinet laminate. Exposed particleboard should be sealed. 2) Replace acoustic ceiling tiles over the drinks station and over the back of the soda fountain with smooth easily cleanable vinyl ceiling tiles. 3) Caulk countertops to backsplash at drinks station. These situations were discussed with the PIC and owner at the pre-opening and were reviewed during this inspection. Correct prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT from the Pre-Opening) 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

These items are still in violation from the pre-opening: 1) Clean floors under the back of the soda fountain and under shelving in the walk-in cooler. 2) Clean fan covers in the walk-in coolers. These locations were shown to the PIC and they are instructed to clean these areas and maintain them clean moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Water is observed leaking from the ceiling at two separate locations in the customer area of the building. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace the damaged tiles and the ceiling to prevent new damage from accruing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The ceiling along the cook-line is observed to have an accumulation of flour on the tiles and light covers. There is observed to be flour coming from the ceiling onto food-contact surfaces and into the batter stations. This is a potential for cross-contamination. A follow up will be conducted on 5/21/2026 to ensure that the ceiling along the cook-line has been cleaned to prevent cross contamination to food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The lemonade nozzle on both soda machines in the facility were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- Both nozzles were cleaned during the inspection and this was discussed with both PICs. Ensure that soda nozzles are being cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There are multiple dipping sauces that state to “Keep Refrigerated” that are being held at room temperature. These sauces are stored in the walk-in cooler until they are needed and are stored in a container in the drive-through at room temperature. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that these sauces were placed on the counter at around 9am and the sauces were voluntarily discarded due to being kept past the allowed 4 hours under Time as Control. These sauces will be stored in the bottom of the preparation cooler going forward. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items are stored at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The walk-in cooler is observed to have an ambient temperature of 46F to 49F. Chicken was probed to be at 48F and 49F. This was discussed with the PIC, who stated that the walk-in cooler was checked at 9am that morning and was at 38F. The chicken that was delivered that morning was moved into the walk-in freezer and the other TCS items that were recently delivered were moved into other coolers. CORRECTED- The following items were probed and voluntarily discarded during the inspection: 
1. 4 pans of chicken (4 bags of classic and 4 bags of boneless): 47F and 48F. 
2. Multiple boxes of sauces, including buttermilk ranch (48F) and 8 boxes of blackened ranch (48F). 
3. Tartar sauce (48F). 
4. 1 box of havarti cheese (47F). 
5. 1 bag of shredded cheddar cheese (47F). 
6. 2 boxes of cabbage (49F). 
All other TCS food items that were within the proper temperature range were moved into another cooler or the walk-in freezer. The PIC stated that there is a company on the way to repair the walk-in cooler. Ensure that other TCS food items are not put into the walk-in cooler until it is properly holding temperature at 41F and below. Ensure that TCS food items are properly cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: In the batter stations, raw chicken probed to be at 52F and egg wash probed to be at 56F. The batter stations rely on ice baths for proper cold holding and there was no ice observed underneath the pans of food. The ice machine in the back of the kitchen is not functioning, according to the PIC, and they have to use the lobby ice machine for their ice baths. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that ice had been added under the pans only an hour before this. Ice was added to the water underneath the pans. Egg wash was probed to be at 41F and chicken was probed to be at 39F. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always plenty of ice and water to submerge the bottom of the pans to allow for proper cold holding of 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

The facility only has one preparation cooler and one standing cooler besides the walk-in cooler. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 to ensure that the walk-in cooler has been repaired and is properly cold holding at 41F and below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

Ice baths are used for cold holding for the batter stations and these were observed to not be properly cold holding during today’s inspection (see violation #22). Without the ice machine in the kitchen, they have to rely on the soda machines for ice. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2026 to ensure that the ice machine has been repaired or replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. THIRD REPEAT- The dish shelves across from the ice machine are rusted. The shelves either need to be sealed or replaced to prevent contamination to clean dishes. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The drain of the sanitizer compartment of the triple sink is observed to have an issue where even if it is closed, there is a slow leak coming from it. The facility is using a stopper in place of using the drain handle. Ensure that this issue is repaired to prevent the need for a stopper. The triple sink should be in good repair. 
3. SECOND REPEAT- There is ice build-up on the walk-in freezer pipes on the fan unit. Ensure that this ice is scraped off and that the issue causing the ice build up is repaired. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair or replaced as needed.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of being cleaned: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan covers were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the current method of cold holding to be insufficient (cheese surface temperature 68F). CORRECTED: Display cheese will not be sold to the consumer. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed during today’s inspection.
1. The stainless steel sheet sealing the edge of the wall behind the hand sink by the drinks station.
2. The tiles placement around the drainage system between the dish area and the cook line were observed broken.
3. caulking on the multi-compartment sink in the produce prep area was observed coming off.
4. The caulking sealing the countertop right of the dish machine was observed coming off the wall.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm QUat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available and at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

SCDPH will follow-up on the mobile unit's next operating event for warm water for handwashing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket was tested at 100ppm (quat). The employees mentioned that solution was provided by the dispenser at the brick and mortar. Discussed that the concentration was too low and needed to be at least 200ppm to properly sanitizer food contact surfaces. The inspector was able to get more Sani tablets from a different vendor to add to the concentration to correct the violation.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

CORRECTED- The PIC remade the sanitizer bucket using Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tablets and it tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The blue sea cream was discarded and proper date-marking was discussed with the operator. citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed metal bowls used to toss cooked fried food with RTE sauces and seasonings. When asked how often they are cleaned, the PIC stated every night. Inspectors informed the PIC that in-use saucing bowls should be cleaned every 4 hours. CORRECTED: the bowls were cleaned, and the PIC and inspectors created a formal TIME AS CONTROL STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE for the saucing bowls: “Remove all saucing bowls for cleaning [Wash, Rinse, Sanitize, Air Dry] at the following times: 3:00PM, 7:00PM, and CLOSING TIME”. Ensure that food that is not kept under temperature control is instead kept under time control.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(5) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (5) The FOOD in unmarked containers or PACKAGES, or marked to exceed a 4-hour limit shall be discarded.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed disinfecting wipes stored with food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the items were moved to a separate area away from food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils. Ensure that toxic materials like cleaning chemicals are stored so they CANNOT contaminate food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed fish thawing in a sink of water without running water. Faucet was turned on twice before staff was appropriately conveyed knowledge of proper thawing. Discussed thawing being a process significantly different from a process we complete in our homes. Triple sinks were designed to allow for water to overflow. PIC also recognized that thawing the fish in a cooler was an approved thawing method. CORRECTED: through education and practice. Ensure that proteins are thawed using a method that does not allow thawed portions of RTE food to rise above 5°C (41°F).
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed a clean cutting board being stored behind the faucet of the double sink. This storage practice should cease as it allows for splash from the ‘mop’ sink to come into contact with the board. CORRECTED through storage: during the inspection, the cutting board was properly stored on a storage shelf away from the splash of the sink. Ensure equipment and utensils are stored where they are not exposed to contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed a rubber spatula to be damaged to the point where 50% of the face was ripped away. CORRECTED: PIC discarded the spatula during the inspection. Cease using materials once they have become damaged or broken.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the facility to be using cardboard to hold portion cups of sauces. Cease use of cardboard and use materials that are smooth and easily cleanable. Most of the facility storage containers are plastic. Follow suit and replace cardboard containers with similar plastic containers.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the reach-in freezers in the extra storage room to have a soiled lid AND observed the base shelf beneath the wooded grates of the kitchen 4 door cooler (beneath chicken boxes) to be soiled. Clean these cold storage units by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed mop water to be grey and cold in the mop bucket. The mop bucket was moved from in-front of the hand sink (not obstructing) to the back room without being emptied. See that mop water is emptied after use and not allowed to remain stagnant in the bucket. CORRECTED: PIC emptied the mop bucket during the inspection.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed that the grease trap has a strong sewer oder emanating from the unit and appears to have a flaking metal lid. Upon calling Ace Disposal (the company serviced the grease trap 19 March 2026), it appears the grease trap has a missing baffle, broken lid, and damaged container. The grease trap has failed. The repair will be costly and SCDPH is giving six (6) month to complete this task (12 November 2026). Keep SCDPH updated on repair progress until then.
citation_text: 5-403.11 Approved Sewage Disposal System. SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant; or (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed that personal items, including clothing and personal food, are being stored next to food and single-use/single-service articles and utensils. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the items were moved to a separate area. Ensure that suitable facilities are used for the orderly storage of employee clothing and other possessions.
citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed multiple storage order violations throughout coolers. Eggs were observed to be above beef and vegetables in 2 cooler units. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage order and eggs were moved to bottom shelf on cooler. Ensure proper storage order is maintained to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: (Repeatx2) Observed multiple TCS food items to be kept at room temperature. Discussed with PIC, items were prepared this morning. Inspector provided education in regard to cold holding TCS foods, ice baths were created for sauces, and larger items were placed in cooler. Ensure all TCS foods being cold held are kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS foods to not have date marking available. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and dates were placed on TCS foods. Ensure all foods kept longer than 24 hours are properly date marked and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed beef to be thawing in a pan of water. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper thawing practices and pan was moved to under running water.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed single service bowls to be resting on soiled paper towels. Discussed with PIC, soiled paper towels were replaced with aluminum foil and bowls were discarded. Ensure if used, paper towels are replaced at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking at mop sink to be in a state of disrepair. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents disrepair from occurring.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be completed by staff. Discussed with PIC, staff is limited to only 2 members as of now. 1 is the certified food manger, and the other will take the steps to complete training. Ensure any food handling employee has the required food handlers licens within 30 days of employment. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following areas to have food debris accumulation:
1) The seasoning lids were observed to have an accumulation of food debris.
2) The inside top of microwave was observed to have food debris accumulation.

Discussed with PIC, the following areas will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC at the time of this inspection does not have a current CFPM certificate. They stated that they are in the process of being sent to a course but it is not for another couple weeks. Education was conducted. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility moving forward.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

1) The meats in the reach in cooler in the front of the facility are observed with internal temperatures around 48F. 2) Lettuce, tomatoes and spinach are observed with internal temperatures of 50F in the left prep cooler in the front of the facility. Both locations were discussed with the PIC. Steak was discarded immediately as it was in its cooler since the day before. Sliced tomatoes were allowed to be put back in the walk in cooler as they were only prepared approximately an hour prior to observation. All other items were prepared and placed in their coolers between 2-3 hours prior to observation. These items will be allowed to remain in use until four hours has elapsed and then any remains must be discarded. This will correct the immediate violation. The issue of the coolers not functioning correctly will be handled under line item #33 of this report.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

1) The reach in cooler in the front of the facility was observed holding TCS foods at approximately 48F internal temperatures. 2) The left prep cooler used for vegetable storage and sandwich prep was observed holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 50F. The PIC was shown both locations. The TCS foods in both locations are being discarded at the end of four hours from prep and time control is going to be used until repairs can be completed. Per the owner (via the PIC) Bormida was contacted during the inspection and should be at the facility the next morning to conduct maintenance on the coolers and bring them into compliance. A follow up is being set for the next available day after ten days to ensure compliance.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The cubby used for storing knives in the sandwich prep area was observed soiled during the inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the location and maintain it clean to prevent possible contamination of the cleaned knives stored here. The cubby was removed and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact items are stored in clean locations.

4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

There is not an available sanitizer in the front of the facility at the time of this inspection. The PIC indicated that a wet rag is used to wipe the surfaces throughout the day. This is not a safe practice. The food contact surfaces should be wiped with a sanitizer regularly to prevent possible pathogenic growth on the food contact surfaces. Education was conducted and the PIC prepared a spray bottle of sanitizer for these surfaces to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The floors under shelving in the back room as well as in the walk in cooler are observed soiled and needing to be cleaned, specifically under shelving and near the walls.  The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all floor are cleaned at a frequency that precludes the accumulation of filth.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no test strips available on site for the quaternary ammonia sanitizer. The PIC was informed and test strips were acquired during today's inspection. Ensure test strips are available at all times for testing sanitizer efficacy.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments. There were only a few glue traps present during today’s inspection Critical areas such as the floor behind equipment on the cook line were without glue traps. Three live adults and one live juveniles were observed under equipment on the cook line. All pests observed today were fast-moving. Ensure glue traps are out and dated at all times to monitor activity. SCDPH will continue to follow-up until no pests are observed. This means keeping the glue traps present as a monitoring tool and insuring treatment is curtailing life cycles. The next follow-up is scheduled for June 15, 2026. 

 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

Ensure that a certified food protection manager is present at the facility during operational hours.

citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The nozzles on the soda machine were observed to be soiled. Discussed with PIC. PIC removed the nozzles, cleaned and sanitized them while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee begin to don gloves without handwashing. CORRECTED- the employee was interrupted and directed to wash hands. The employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. Inspector provided education and demonstrated correct hand washing, which the employee modeled afterwards (rinse hands, scrub with soap, dry with paper towel and use barrier to turn off to avoid recontaminating hands). Review hand washing procedures and times to wash with all employees who serve or handle food. Inspector provided a handout regarding times to wash hands. Times to wash hands include but are not limited to: before donning gloves, after using using the restroom, between working with raw and ready to eat foods, etc.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed cooked rice holding an internal temperature of 114F. CORRECTED- the item was moved under TIME AS CONTROL (TAC)- the item was stated to have been prepared at 11 AM, and will be used or discarded by 3PM. Once rice (or noodles, or vegetables) are cooked they become temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods- and therefore must be held below 41F or above 135F to prevent the growth of pathogens. Ensure all TCS foods are kept outside of the temperature danger zone.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

A can was observed with a dent in the bottom seam. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. Ensure that all cans are removed if there is a dent observed in any of the three seams (top, bottom or side) to protect consumers from possible botulism infections. The can was moved to discard to correct.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed multiple pieces of fruit to be resting in bar ice machine. Discussed with PIC, fruit items were removed from ice. Ensure ice is being protected from any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice scoop handle to be in contact with ice at bar ice machine. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was moved so handle is outside of ice. Ensure ice scoop handle is kept out of contact with ice to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS item kept in coolers to be kept past its 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and items were discarded. Ensure any item kept longer than its 7 day date marking maximum is discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a floor vent to have an accumulation of dust. Discussed with PIC, vent will be replaced. Ensure vents are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents dust accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed dishes to be washed in the front hand sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper dish washing and practice was stopped. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used for hand washing, and that dishes are put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed Sammy eggs to be resting at 70F, eggs were prepared 2 hours before. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper cold holding/cooling and eggs were moved to cooler. Education was provided on possibly placing eggs under a TAC, however PIC decided on cold holding the eggs. Ensure any TCS item is being cold held at or below 41F
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed in use quiche to not have date marking available. Discussed with PIC, quiche was prepared within the last 7 days. Education on proper date marking was provided and date was placed on quiche. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours has the required date marking available.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The kitchen hand washing sink (nearest the dish machine) was observed to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- the PIC brought napkins to the area for hand drying. Ensure hand washing sinks are stocked with paper towels at all times to allow for hand drying, and use of a barrier to turn off the faucet.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector probed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods on the cold buffet line and observed internal temperatures over 41F (pork at 45F, dark meat chicken at 48F, light meat chicken and 46F, and beef at 45F). The inspector returned after about 20 minutes and the temperatures did not decrease. CORRECTED- items were moved under time as control (a post-it was placed, indicating foods must be used or discarded by 7PM). Ensure TCS foods are held EITHER at or below 41F, OR used or discarded within 4 hours of being moved out of cold holding units (41F or below) to prevent the growth of pathogens.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The cold holding unit on the buffet line is failing to hold TCS foods at or below 41F- see violation #22. Ensure the unit is serviced so that foods have an internal temperature at or below 41F. Equipment must have the capacity to cold hold foods at or below 41F. Inspector will return on or by May 11 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand-sink by the back door to have no hot water. There is no water coming from the faucet when the hot water handle is turned. A follow-up will be conducted on May 14, 2026 to ensure the sink has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The employee restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. The inspector instructed the operator to ensure hot water is provided at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. A follow-up (re-inspection) will be conducted on May 11, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed the following items to be stored beyond its 7-day date mark:
1. Pork (expired April 16)
2. Beef (expired April 26)

There were also multiple other containers with expired date marks that the inspector could not easily access due to stacking. The PIC was made aware that all items past the date mark must be discarded. A follow-up will be conducted on May 4, 2026 to ensure that proper date marking guidelines are being followed in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer was not attached to dish machine. Inspector attached sanitizer, and dish machine tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizing dish machine is sanitizing at the proper concentration to ensure dishes are being properly cleaned.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be coming apart to the left of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed allergen training to have been expired by the current CFM. Discussed with PIC, CFM will complete the required allergen training. Ensure all CFMs have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer in the sani bucket in the lobby area was measured at 0 ppm. PIC was made aware. PIC remade the sanitizer and it was tested at 300 ppm. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizer is constantly monitored and tested to ensure adequate sanitation at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The gasket on the door of the aisle cooler walk-in section was observed to be broken and coming off. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the gasket will be fixed. Ensure that this is repair appropriately.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspectors observed three canned goods with significant dents near the top/bottom of the can. CORRECTED: Discussed with PIC checking cans for visible dents and which areas of the can to check, and the PIC excluded the cans from service. Ensure that canned foods are in good condition and not exposed to potential contamination, in this case the damage to the inner lining from dents at the top, bottom, or side seam.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed no measurable concentration of Chlorine in the the sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED: Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer bucket was remade, and observed a concentration of 50pm. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are measuring at effective concentrations - 50-200pm.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Inspectors observed that the scoop inside the salt bin does not have a handle. Scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have handles that are stored above the top of food to avoid contamination. Ensure that the salt bin has a scoop with a handle by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed several personal items, like sweaters, hanging above food service items in the dry storage areas. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and the items were moved to a designated area that is away from food service items. Ensure that personal items are kept separate from food service areas and food content surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Inspectors observed that not all employees have completed the food handler training. The PIC was educated that all employees who do not have a CFPM (Certified Food Protection Manager) certificate must have food handler certificates. Ensure that all required employees complete the food handler training and copies of the certificates are kept at the facility by the next routine inspection. Inspector will return on Monday, 1 June 2026 to check that staff have Food Handler certificates.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There weren’t any paper towels available at the hand-sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with the PIC and paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that paper towels are always available at all hand-sinks to be sure that hands are getting properly dried after completing the handwashing process.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed a member of staff wash hands without using a barrier to turn off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing, and employee rehashed hands. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off hand sink faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed employee bare hand a cooked pizza from oven to tray. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper bare hand food handling practices. Ensure any ready to eat foods are properly handled by employees.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed staff to be date marking items in multiple coolers, however inspector observed date marking to be missing on multiple TCS items throughout multiple coolers and walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking practices. Dates were placed on all TCS items, ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed a bag of chicken to be thawing near pizza oven. Discussed with PIC, education on proper thawing practices was provided, chicken was moved to a pan under running water. Ensure facility is properly thawing TCS items to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing.
