Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed multiple in use rags to not be stored in sanitizer buckets between use. Discussed with PIC, education on sanitizer rags was provided. Rags were all moved to sanitizer buckets testing at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure any in use rag is being stored in a sanitizer solution to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed in use pizza cutter to be resting on a soiled rag on counter. Discussed with PIC, pizza cutter was put through wash, rinse, and sanitize process and stored in an approved location. Ensure in use utensils are stored in cleaned and sanitized locations.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed pizza sauce splash to be present on the lids of prep cooler. Discussed with PIC, area will be wiped down and cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed touching ready to eat fries with their bare hands. Education was carried out. The packet of fries was discarded. Ensure that employee are knowledgeable and always remember to avoid bare handling ready to eat food items by donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following was observed the following.
1. The internal surface of the coffee maker was observed soiled. (COS)
2. The nozzles of the soda machine in the lobby were observed to have a buildup of soil accumulation.

Discussed with PIC. The nozzles were removed to be cleaned and the coffee maker was cleaned and sanitized.  The soda machine will be out of order until the nozzles are cleaned properly. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the coffee maker and soda machine nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized on a regular basis. Inspector will return on 05/08/26 to followup on the nozzles.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed visible light coming through the back exit door at the bottom and top area. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repair will be done to have the door sealed properly discouraging the entry of pests. Ensure that the spaces allowing light to pass through are sealed properly.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The coving tiles on the wall left of the tea brewing station by the ice machine was observed coming off the wall. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the coving tiles are sealed appropriately to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink next to the grills was observed without paper towels or another hand drying method. The PIC was shown and refilled the paper towel dispenser during this inspection to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani bucket in the food preparation area was oberved to not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. This was discussed with the PIC. A new jug replaced the one in the dispenser and a new bucket filled. The new bucket was observed at effective concentration and the violation was considered corrected.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

The dish machine in the kitchen was not able to produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Multiple attempts were made and it was observed that concentrate was not metering into the water solution when it should in the cycle. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their maintenance company. The PIC is instructed to have the machine serviced and functional prior to the follow up. The follow-up would normally land on a Saturday. Due to this it is being pushed back to Monday.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer on the cook line measure 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the concentration was too low, and the bucket was replaced, measuring 200ppm. Ensure the buckets are tested and replaced frequently to guarantee proper sanitization of food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed PIC to wash hands for 2 seconds without soap use. Discussed with PIC, inspector attempted to offer education on proper hand washing education. Ensure any food employees washes hands for at least 20 seconds without soap use the use of a cleaning compound.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed PIC to not use a barrier after the attempted hand wash. Discussed with PIC, education was again attempted to be provided. Ensure a barrier is used to turn off faucet after hand washing to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed PIC to be bare handling hash browns cooking on stovetop. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on bare hand contact with exposed foods and PIC was instructed to wash hands and use gloves in the future. Ensure employees minimize bare hand contact with exposed foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, the sanitizer set up to dish machine had run out. A new bottle was switched out and dish machine tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizing dish machine is testing at the proper concentration to ensure dishes are properly being wash, rinsed, and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed open cakes to stored with no date marking present. Discussed with PIC, cakes were purchased/made this week and the proper date marking was placed on cakes. Ensure any open TCS food held longer than 24 hours has the proper date marking available.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed multiple container ranging from soups, sauces, and other TCS items to be resting/cooling on the floor in kitchen line and walk in cooler. Discussed with staff, all containers were moved to at least 6 inches off of floor. Ensure all foods are kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed food debris buildup to be present under the left prep cooler lid in cook line. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed soda gun at the waiter station to be soiled with mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff is cleaning soda guns at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed hollandaise sauce to be hot holding at 100F. Discussed with PIC, sauce was moved to stovetop and reheated to 165F. Ensure any TCS item being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed an open gallon of milk to be kept past its date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, milk was discarded and education was provided on date marking. Ensure any TCS item is properly date marked and discarded after.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed a package of lobster to be thawing in a container of water with no running water. Discussed with PIC, thawing education was provided and container was moved to sink under running water. Ensure facility is maintaining proper thawing practices.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspectors observed that the triple sink had a steady leak at the faucet. PIC is aware of the issue and plans to get it repaired as soon as the plumber is available. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed an old vent in the kitchen that was “closed” with a rag, which is an absorbent material that is not being cleaned regularly. PIC was notified and made plans to replace the seal. Options include sealing it off fully with metal or a similar covering, or a screen that can be cleaned and prevent pests and maintain airflow. Ensure that all surfaces are constructed to smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas that need to be cleaned with more frequency:
(A) the microwave,
(B) the walls behind the stove and fryer.
PIC was notified and made plans to clean these areas. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed a food handler touch arugula with their bare hands on the kitchen prep line. CORRECTED- the item was removed from service to be discarded. Ensure all ready to eat foods and garnishes are handled with washed and gloved hands to prevent contamination of foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine fail to reach proper sanitizing temperatures after multiple cycles. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was replaced and the machine was observed to be reaching temperatures over 160F. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently checked with test kits (in this case a maximum register thermometer or test strip) to verify proper sanitizing temperatures (160-194F).
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple foods in cold holding to be held past their seven day date marking period:
1) Cut grape tomatoes dated 4/21 in a prep cooler.
2) Cooked ribs dated 4/21 in the walk in cooler.
CORRECTED- Foods were removed from service to be discarded. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked if held over 24 hours to be used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation counts as day 1 (foods dated 4/21 were to be used or discarded by 4/27- “plus 6”).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
comment: No consumer advisory was available in the menus or posted otherwise in the facility. The inspector can bring consumer advisory signs to display during the 5/8 follow up until a new menu is printed. The increased risk of food-borne illness by consuming raw or undercooked animal proteins must be available and communicated to consumers.
citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed the facility to not have a maximum heat registering test strip or dish plate to verify heat sanitizing temperatures for the dish machine. Devices used for sanitation of food contact surfaces must have a test kits to verify proper heat sanitizing temperatures. Inspector will return on or by 5/8 to ensure a maximum heat registering dish puck or test strips have been purchased and are in use.
citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: One dead mouse was observed in the upstairs bar area in a space where a cooler was recently removed. The facility was observed otherwise free of evidence of pests or harborage conditions. Facility has routine pest control providing service monthly and is attentive to cleaning processes. The mouse was removed and the surrounding floor will be cleaned. Glasses stored in the adjacent space were removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Continue routine pest control and cleaning. Inspect facility regularly to monitor for pest activity.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed that the chemical dish machine (Chlorine) was not sanitizing at sufficient concentrations (no measurable sanitizer was present). Chlorine dish machines should have sanitizer concentrations between 50-200ppm. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and implement alternative ware washing procedures: dishes would be run through the dish machine for wash and rinse, and then would be finished in the triple sink sanitizing compartment which had a sanitizing concentration of 200ppm (quaternary ammonia). PIC also made plans to get a new bucket of sanitizer installed at the chemical dish machine. The PIC will send the Inspector a picture of the new bucket of sanitizer when it is installed, along with a test strip confirming the correct concentration. Ensure that chemical dish machines are sanitizing at proper concentrations, which for Chlorine is 50-200ppm, and use test strips frequently to verify the concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice machine baffle was observed to have soil accumulation. The operator was informed and instructed to clean the baffle and maintain it free of soil buildup. Ensure the ice machine baffle is cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will follow up on May 7, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometers was observed in the walk-in cooler. The operator informed the inspector that there is an ambient thermometer in the walk-in cooler but was unable to show the inspector during the inspection. The inspector instructed operator to ensure an internal thermometers is provided in the walk-in cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Ants were observed crawling on the soiled floor under the shelf in the non-functional walk-in freezer. The inspector informed and instructed the operator to ensure the ants are removed from the facility. The inspector will follow-up on May 7, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Soil accumulation was observed on the floor under the shelf in the non-functional walk-in freezer. The inspector informed and instructed the operator to ensure the floor is cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of food and various debris on the top of the dish machine and the lids of the soft serve ice cream containers. Discussed with the person in charge (PIC). Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the contamination of ready to eat foods or food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the floors below the fryers on the dry storage side of the restaurant to contain a significant build up of grease and food debris. Discussed increasing the frequency at which this space is cleaned. Ensure that spaces under the fryers are free of the accumulation of grease and food debris to prevent the harborage of pests. Physical characteristics must be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.[C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a coving tile beneath the North wall’s fire safety system to be loose. Repair by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: The inspectors didn’t observe any handwashing during the visit. An employee was observed rinsing hands inside of the hand sink. Discussed that handwashing shall occur frequently and whenever contamination of the hands occur. Most of the handsinks throughout the facility are supplied with running weather, paper towels, and hand soap, with the exception of one sink (see violation #10). Ensure to educate employees on proper handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed at least two employees bare hand cooked pizza during the visit. The activity was ceased and corrected. Ensure to never use bare hands with any ready-to-eat food items. Utensils or single use gloves shall always be used to handle RTE foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the men’s restroom to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- the PIC was informed and paper towels were placed. Ensure all sinks intended for hand washing always have warm running water, soap, and paper towels to complete proper handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs stored above cooked meats in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- education was conducted with the PIC and the eggs were moved below the meats. Ensure all raw products are stored below cooked products to prevent potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed Italian dressing labeled “refrigerate after opening” stored on the counter next to the salad prep cooler (surface temperature of 72F probed). CORRECTED- the dressing was placed in the cold holding unit. Ensure all temperature control safety (TCS) food items and items labeled “Keep Refrigerated” or “Refrigerate after opening” are held at or below 41F to limit the growth of pathogens that may cause food-borne illness.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Overall, the facility lacks proper date marking for TCS foods in the walk in cooler. These items include but aren’t limited to items containing cooked chicken, pork, pasta sauces, and other various items. Discussed with PIC proper date marking and that TCS foods shall never be held longer than 7 days after preparation. Items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that any TCS foods held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed at least five dead insects throughout the facility, these areas included the storage/office space and in the basement area. The owner mentioned that the facility currently doesn’t have pest control and will be getting a new pest control company soon. Discussed that a professional  pest control  company shall provide treatment to the facility to help eliminate the presence of insects. The facility is also expected to clean frequently and prevent harboring conditions for insects. Will follow-up on 5/27/2026 to ensure that the premise is free of insects.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The additional food employees couldn’t show proof of food handler certificates. Discussed with both the employee and the owner that a food certificate is required for any employee that handles food or clean dishes. Ensure that a food handler certificate is obtained by the next routine visit. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Kitchen: cease use of laminate wrap on shelves; walls and ceiling should be light colored; repair holes in ceiling and walls; self closer on back door; triple sink large enough to support biggest piece of equipment; cut flush and paint all spray foam; seal left side of triple sink to wall (drainboard); secure hand sink to wall; cease use of acoustic ceiling tiles.
Prep space
Ceiling tiles should be smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable. Seal floor to wall.

Lighting: more lighting in prep space. Shatterproof or shielded bulbs

Storage space: shelving smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable - painted and seal wall to floor

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety foods held past their seven day date marking period:
1) Mushrooms sauce in the downstairs walk in cooler (dated 4/16)
2) French onion soup in the downstairs walk in cooler (dated 4/15)
3) Creme brulée in the upstairs standing cooler (next to the grill) (dated 4/16)
4) Roasted duck in the ground level walk in cooler (dated 4/16)
5) Mushroom sauce in the ground level walk in cooler (dated 4/14)
CORRECTED- the aforementioned foods will be discarded. Continue educating staff about date marking requirements and holding times. Ensure all TCS foods are marked to be used or DISCARDED within seven days (the day of preparation counts as DAY ONE).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The hand-sink in the dish room area was obstructed with a container holding various items. Discussed that all hand-sinks must remain unobstructed to allow employees to wash hands. Be sure to educate employees on never placing items in sink because it can interfere with proper handwashing. Ensure that hand sinks remain unobstructed.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The soap dispenser at the bar’s handwashing sink was observed empty. A bag of soap was replaced by the PIC to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are supplied with hand-soap to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical dish washing machine was tested at 0ppm (CL). The machine was primed and still tested at an improper concentration. The facility removed all of the buckets associated with mechanical ware washing, including detergent, rinse, and sanitizer because they were empty. The quaternary ammonium dispenser at the triple sink was also observed empty. The facility uses quat tablets for their sanitizer buckets. The facility was instructed to create a sanitizer solution at the triple sink with the tablets until the chlorine chemical arrives (later today) for the dish machine. The sanitizing chemical arrived in the midst of the inspection and was tested at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that the dish machine is always testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: A bean sauce placed on an ice bath was probed at 71F. The PIC indicated that the sauce was recently placed on ice but most of the ice was observed melted.The PIC was shown how to properly create an ice bath, where the ice level matched the food level. As ice melts, be sure that more ice is added to maintain cold temperatures. Ensure that ice baths are sufficient to maintain a temperature of 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Various sauces are placed on ice baths throughout the facility. A bean sauce was probed at 71F. The kitchen manager indicated that the sauce was recently placed on ice. Most of the ice was observed melted and at improper cold holding temperatures. The manager was instructed to add more ice to the container to ensure that all outer areas of the containers are covered with ice. Ensure that all TCS foods held on ice baths are kept at a temperature of 41F or less to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There weren’t any sanitizer buckets present in the kitchen area, despite the facility being in full operation. Sani solutions were prepared and placed at each station to correct the violation. All buckets were tested between 200ppm - 400ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are always available if food is being prepared, handled, and served.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The chlorine test strips that the facility has available are completely soiled. Discussed with both the owner and the kitchen manager that test strips shall be in good condition to accurately test sanitizer concentration. A container of CL test strips were given to the owner to correct the violation. Ensure that test strips are always available to accurately measure sanitizing concentrations.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There was a mop bucket that contained waste water stored inside of the waste room. The PIC indicated that facility usually dumps water outdoors. Educated the employee that dumping waste water outdoors on the ground is prohibited and to immediately stop the activity. There is a mop sink that is available for proper disposal inside of the facility. Instructed the facility to ALWAYS use the mop sink for waste water disposal.
citation_text: 5-403.11 Approved Sewage Disposal System. SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant; or (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is about a half inch gap in between the sink and the wall located in the food prep room. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that the handsink is sealed to the wall to prevent accumulated food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no allergen training to have been completed by staff. Discussed with PIC, allergen training will be completed by certified food protection manager. Ensure all CFPM’s have completed the required allergen training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. Hand washing was completed without using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Discussed with staff the proper technique for hand washing. Teach your staff to properly wash their hands. 



(B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were multiple containers of raw chicken above raw beef in the walk-in cooler. This was previously discussed and was to be followed-up on today. Some foods were moved to accommodate Code.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. The back storage room (with canned goods) still has some mouse dropppings on the floor. Clean the floor of the back storage area so all droppings are removed. 

Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics.  The walk-in cooler floor is observed soiled. Operator mentioned that the floor is cleaned on Sundays, but the floor should be cleaned at a frequency sufficient to maintain the surface clean. If it is Friday and the floor is observed soiled, then clean the floor at least twice a week.
See General Comments for discussion of organization. There is too much in this space. Reduce menu or move storage into an additional space. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed food splash to be accumulating in the following areas:
1) The bottom of the upstairs cooler.
2) The inside of the upstairs microwave.

Discussed with PIC, areas wil be cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed a leak to be present from pipe below triple sink. Discussed with PIC, a licensed plumber will be contacted to service leak. Ensure a licensed plumber services leak, inspector will follow up on 4/28/26.
citation_text: 5-403.11 Approved Sewage Disposal System. SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant; or (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The PIC has her CFPM, but had to leave right before the inspection, so was not on site during the inspection. Inspectors did speak with the CFPM over the phone during the inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed the ceiling tiles in the room with the ware washing and fryers are deteriorating. There are portions of the ceiling tiles that are peeling off over food preparation areas. The ceiling tiles must be repaired/replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Other employee’s Food Handler certificate has expired, and will be renewed by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One staff member on site was observed to have an expired certification (CFPM certificate, but no Food Handler’s certificate in supplementation). All staff who do any degree of food handling must have a minimum of a Food Handler certificate, to be obtained within 30 days of hire and maintained every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: A bucket was observed in the basin of the handwashing sink at the kitchen, causing obstruction for handwashing. CORRECTED - The inspector informed the operator; the bucket was removed and the handwashing sink was made accessible. Ensure handwashing sinks are not obstructed and remain accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [PF]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice machine baffle was observed to have soil accumulation. The operator was informed and instructed to clean the baffle and maintain it free of soil buildup. Ensure the ice machine baffle is cleaned and sanitized to sight and touch. The inspector will follow up on May 4, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Single-use Styrofoam plates were observed stored uncovered and not inverted, creating potential exposure to dust and other contamination. CORRECTED - The inspector instructed the operator to invert the plates when not in active use, and the plates were properly inverted. Ensure single-use items are stored inverted and protected from contamination at all times.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The hood baffles on the right side were observed to have significant grease accumulation.
2. The fan covers in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.

The inspector instructed the operator to clean the above-mentioned surfaces to sight and touch. Ensure all nonfood-contact surfaces are routinely cleaned and maintained free of grease and dust accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods lacking date marking throughout the facility:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The standing pass through cooler contained cooked noodles and freshly prepared sauces.
2) The walk in meat cooler contained minestrone and French onion soup.
3) The two door standing cooler contained multiple sauces and in house prepared foods.
CORRECTED- items were marked with the date of preparation (being either Saturday 4/18 or Wed. 4/15). Foods marked 4/15 (downstairs walk in cooler) must be used or discarded today. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked to be used or discarded within SEVEN days. The date of preparation counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5ºC (41ºF) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be in disrepair:
1) The gaskets of the ground level walk in cooler are frayed.
2) The gaskets of the pass through cooler on the kitchen line are frayed and deteriorating. 
3) The shelves of the standing freezer on the south side of the kitchen line contain rust.
Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the contamination of foods. Replace gaskets and either repaint or replace shelves by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspector observed the downstairs hand washing sink nearest the stairs to be leaking water just below the basin. Once water passes the basin it is considered waste water. Ensure repairs are made by law to properly convey the waste water on or by 4/24/26.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facilities to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The fan covers of the ground level walk in cooler contain an accumulation of dust. 
2) The floor in the Southeast corner of the server line contains an accumulation of food debris.
3) The floor next to the basement water heater needs cleaned more frequently to better monitor potential pests.
Ensure physical facilities and nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: (2ND REPEAT) Employees were observed using bare hands to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. To ensure that hands are getting washed properly, a barrier must be used to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. Be sure to educate all employees on proper handwashing procedures.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a hand sink to be missing paper towels. A reusable cloth was placed atop the paper towel dispenser. An employee stated that the cloth was in use as a replacement. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure disposable paper towels are used at all times to prevent cross-contamination. Never use reusable towels for drying clean hands. The hand sink was properly supplied during the inspection.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand-sink by the back door to have no hot water. There is no water coming from the faucet when the hot water handle is turned. A follow-up will be conducted on May 4, 2026 to ensure the sink has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed an ice scoop handle directly contacting ice in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and the scoop was moved to the dish area. Ensure the scoop’s handle never contacts ice as the handle is touched with un-gloved hands.
citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets in the kitchen to read 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed and all buckets in the facility were replaced, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure the buckets are monitored with test strips to prevent inadequate sanitization of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed the following items to be stored beyond its 7-day date mark:
1. Pork (expired April 16)
2. Chile (expired April 5)
3. Taco beef (expired April 12)

There were also multiple other containers with expired date marks that the inspector could not easily access due to stacking. The PIC was made aware that all items past the date mark must be discarded. A follow-up will be conducted on April 27, 2026 to ensure that proper date marking guidelines are being followed in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed reduced-oxygen packaged (ROP) salmon to be thawed in its original packaging. ROP fish must be removed from its original packaging prior to thawing to prevent the growth of Clostridium botulinum (the bacteria that produces the botulism toxin). A follow-up will be conducted on May 4, 2026 to ensure the salmon is removed from its original packaging prior to thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no stem thermometer available during today’s inspection. The facility has an infrared thermometer, but the PIC was informed that this device is not adequate for testing the internal cook temperatures for meats and other food items. A follow-up will be conducted on May 4, 2026 to ensure a stem thermometer is available.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed food items and single-service items to be stored directly on the floor in the walk-in cooler and the dry storage room connected to the walk-in cooler. Ensure food items are stored at least 6 inches off the ground to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Repeat Violation.

The floor of the walk in freezer was observed with chunks of ice build up. Ensure that the freezer floor is maintained as often as necessary to prevent ice accumulation. Repairs may be necessary on the cooling unit of the freezer to prevent dripping.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the ceiling tile above the mop sink to be damaged and partially missing. Ensure this tile is replaced to prevent moisture accumulation in the ceiling.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the floors of the walk-in cooler and freezer to have an accumulation of soil. Ensure these floors are cleaned frequently to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the back door of the facility to be slightly open. A window with no screen was also open. PIC was informed that outer openings of the facility need to be protected to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the air conditioning system above the prep table to be soiled with grease accumulation and dust. The hood above the pizza oven was also heavily soiled with grease and dust. These non-food contact surfaces pose a cross-contamination risk, as the dust can fall directly onto food and food contact surfaces. Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation : Inspector observed floors and walls around dough mixing machines to be soiled with flour dust. Clean floors and walls around dough machine. 

Repeat Violation : Inspector observed the floor of the walk-in freezer to be soiled with food debris. Ensure this space is cleaned frequently.

Inspector observed the prep cooler top to be heavily soiled with food residue. Ensure the prep cooler is cleaned thoroughly (including under and behind lid to prep top).
The bottom of the 2-door cooler in the back room had standing murky water. Ensure this cooler is cleaned to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation
Observed a mop stored in the bottom of a dump sink in the back maintenance area. PIC was informed that mop heads need to be stored hanging so that they can drip dry. Mops left sitting on a surface can promote bacterial accumulation and cause cross-contamination. Ensure staff are hanging mop heads to drip dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation : Observed bare wood being used to hold paper towel dispenser to wall in cook area. Bare wood is absorbent, and is therefore not considered smooth or easily cleanable. Either seal wood or replace with a different material prior to next routine inspection. 

Repeat Violation : Observed caulking in need of repair around hand sink in cooking area as well as around the triple sink. Caulking ensures that there is no soil accumulation between equipment and walls, and also creates a smooth surface for cleaning. Ensure the caulking is replaced prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Two meat slicers were observed with remaining food debris. When asked, the employee indicated that neither had been used that day, meaning that they had not been properly cleaned/sanitized after the prior use. The employee was shown and disassembled the two slicers for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned regularly/as needed to maintain food safety standards.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
citation_text:
3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

A knife was observed in the deli area in contact with a notebook. Paper products are not generally cleanable or able to be sanitized. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. The knife was moved to dish for re-cleaning to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all in use utensils are stored between uses in such a way so as to be protected from possible contamination.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Two coffee tumblers and an open Monster energy drink were observed in a shelving unit next to plastic containers used for food service. The PIC was shown and removed the open drinks to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that employee foods and drinks are stored seperately from any foods or food contact surfaces intended for consumers.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: GAn employee was observed eating on one of the prep table in the kitchen. Education was carried out. The employee was asked to change location. Ensure that employees have a designated area within the facility to eat in order to avoid possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
