comment: The nozzle of the soda machine was observed soiled. Education was carried out. The soda nozzle was removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensured that food contact surfaces such as the nozzles of the soda machine are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized routinely.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11 The following were observed
1. Three containers filled with pasta being stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler.
2. Ground beef in cardboard box stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler. 
Discussed with PIC. PIC removed the food items mentioned from the floor and stored them properly. Ensure that employees remember to store food appropriately to avoid contamination by spill or splash etc. 


(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed an opened can of pasta sauce being stored in the walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware. The can was tossed away. Ensure that can foods are placed into a different container for storage after opening.
citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION 4-101.19 Inspector observed other accumulation of soil in the following places.
1. The gasket of the standing freezer located by the back exit was observed to have an accumulation of soil. 
2. The gasket of the pizza prep cooler was observed with the accumulation of soil build up.
Discussed with PIC. PIC ensured inspector that the soil accumulation will be cleaned appropriately. Ensure that the gaskets of equipments such as coolers and freezers are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to prevent sealing difficulties and food contamination.

Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION. The shelves use for storing dishes and utensils above the triple sink and opposite the triple sink in the kitchen area were observed to have an accumulation of soils. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the shelves will be clean. Ensure that surfaces like the shelves are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION 6-101.11 Inspector observed a build up of soil and grease on the sides and beneath the fryer. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspector that the soil and grease build up would be cleaned appropriately. Ensure that this accumulation is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed that in the 1st display cooler that shell eggs were stored above milk. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the eggs were moved below the milk. Ensure that raw animal products, like eggs, are stored below ready-to-eat foods, including milk.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed that the establishment does not yet have probe-style thermometers available. The PIC has made a plan to purchase probe-style thermometers and will notify the inspectors when they have arrived on or by Monday, 4 May 2026. Ensure that food temperature measuring devices are readily accessible in the establishment.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine in the bar area was tested at 0ppm. After several cycles, a bottle replacement, and priming of the machine, the concentration tested at 100ppm (CL). It appears that the chlorine bottle was empty and needed to be replaced. Additionally, the sanitizer chemical (at triple sink) in the kitchen area was also tested at 0ppm (CL). The facility uses the chemical at the dispenser to sanitize food contact surfaces. Instructed the facility to manually make the buckets until the dispenser can be serviced. Violation corrected on site. Ensure that sanitizer concentrations are always testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was a slight accumulation of dried debris on the food contact surfaces of the can opener. Shown to the owner and the can opener was placed through the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There were several boxes of food stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and walk in freezer. Suggested purchasing metal racks (or crates) that are at least six inches from the floor to protect against contamination. Ensure that food is never stored on the floor and is at least six inches from ground level.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The bar’s handwashing sink was obstructed with several bar mats. The mats were removed to correct the violation. The PIC mentioned that mats were temporarily placed over the sink. Be sure to keep all handwashing sinks unobstructed so that sinks are accessible at all times for handwashing purposes.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine in the bar area was tested at 0ppm (CL). The sanitizer bottle was replaced and primed after several cycles before testing at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that dish machines are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration level.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Both soda gun nozzles in the bar area were observed soiled with dried liquids. Additionally, the rubber gun holders were also observed soiled. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that nozzles and gun holders are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The facility uses a dry and liquid batter for frying meats, seafood, and veggies. The dry batter is replaced every few hours. While the liquid batter is held on an ice bath, the internal temperature was probed at 51F. Ice was only covering the bottom surface of the container. Demonstrated to the kitchen employee how to effectively set up an ice bath to ensure proper cold holding temperatures for time/temperature TCS foods. Be sure that ice covers all outer surfaces of containers to maintain a temperature of 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The facility’s temperature sanitizing dish machine appears to not be functioning properly. The machine was cycled at least six times and the surface temperatures ranged between 145F-152F. The PIC will contact a service technician to have the machine repaired. Temperatures for accurately measuring sanitizing levels for food contact surfaces shall be at least 160F. Ensure that the machine is repaired and reaching at least 160F. Will follow-up on 4/27/2026 to make sure that the machine is reaching proper sanitizing temperatures. In the meantime, the facility was instructed to use the triple sink for sanitizing food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There weren’t any sanitizer solutions available in the kitchen area, despite the kitchen being in full operation. Several buckets were prepared and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Discussed with the person-in-charge (PIC) that sanitizer solutions shall always be available if the facility is preparing, handling, and serving food to the public. Ensure that sani solutions are present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed multiple bowls and plates to not be inverted near dish machine area. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and plates were inverted. Ensure any cleaned equipment or utensils are properly stored to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed food debris accumulation to be present on top of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure facility is cleaning dish machine at a frequency that prevents any accumulation from building.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at the triple sink faucet. Discussed with PIC, faucet will be serviced. Ensure a licensed plumber is contacted to service faucet so no leaks are present within facility.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed floor drain in between triple sink and hand sink to be blocked and starting to overflow. Discussed with PIC, a work order has been placed. Maintenance was contacted and it was determined the hand sink and triple sink basin were the reason floor drain is overflowing. Both sinks will not be used until drain is serviced. Inspector will follow up with facility on 4/24/26.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed salmon in the walk-in cooler to be thawed in its original reduced oxygen packaging. The packaging bore a label indicating that the packaging had to be opened prior to thawing. Education was conducted regarding the risks of thawing fish in reduced oxygen packaging. The packages were opened during the inspection. Ensure staff are opening the packaging prior to thawing to prevent the growth of clostridium botulinum, the organism that causes botulism toxicity.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed knives to be stored in the gap between two prep coolers. This space is not considered easily cleanable and is therefore not adequate for utensil storage. The knives were sent to dish during the inspection. Inspector recommends a magnetic strip or alternative knife storage.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed raw bacon being stored above cut onions in the prep cooler bottom area. CORRECTED: The PIC was informed and moved the bacon below and the onions above. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination by storing raw animal food below ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspectors observed that disposable containers were stored upright without protection. CORRECTED: The PIC was notified, the top container was discarded and the remaining containers were inverted. Ensure that single-service and single-use articles are protected from debris through cover or inversion.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Due to the significant number of priority and priority foundation violations observed during today’s visit, the person-in-charge (PIC) and employees have failed to demonstrate proper knowledge of food safety and the prevention of foodborne illness. Upon arrival, the plumbing at the kitchen’s handwashing sink was observed in complete disrepair. A large portion of the drain pipe was missing, allowing for wastewater to flow onto the floor and counter below. The facility was not aware of the leak, which brings question to if handwashing is occurring as frequent as necessary. Additionally, the facility was observed bare handing ready-to-eat foods, improperly storing foods in refrigerated units, insufficient food handler certificates, improperly storing foods on the floor (including walk in units and underneath counter tops and prep tables), the lack of time as control records for TCS foods, and low concentrated sanitizer buckets. There will be additional follow-ups scheduled to ensure that the facility is brought into compliance and that the risks that contribute to the spread of food borne illnesses are reduced.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: There are at least eight employees that handle food inside of the kitchen area and the inspectors did not observe any handwashing. There were several missed opportunities for handwashing. There are two sinks in the back of the house - one along the cook-line which isn't functional (see violation #51 for further details) and the other is in the dish room (which lacked hand soap). Discussed with the owner the importance of proper and frequent handwashing, as improper handwashing is the leading contributor to food borne illness. Be sure to educate ALL employees on adequate handwashing. Will follow-up on 4/24/2026 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed an employee bare hand battered shrimps that were just removed from the frying station. The activity was ceased and corrected. The employee was instructed to wash hands and use gloves as a protective barrier. Violation corrected on site. Discussed with the owner to educate employees on proper food handling and to never use bare hands when handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. Ensure that employees are either using gloves or utensils to handle RTE foods to protect against cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels at the hand-sink in the employee bathroom. Shown to the owner and paper towels were provided to the handsink to correct the violation. Single use paper towels are essential for handwashing. Ensure that all hand-sinks are stocked with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The facility is observed to be storing food in packages that expose the food to corrosion contamination, including:
- The facility is re-using aluminum and plastic containers to store food items. After the original food item is used, the facility uses the same container to store new foods such as a can of ketchup, baby corn, bamboo shoots, etc. Highly acid foods can corrode the interior of cans, causing a hazard to the food items. Refrain from using cans or containers after the original item is finished. If wanting to transfer foods to different containers, be sure to use food grade approved containers (which were observed in the facility).

2. The facility is observed to be storing raw meat directly in grocery bags. There was raw chicken placed in a grocery bag that was observed on the floor under a table and another bag of raw meat in the walk-in freezer. Grocery bags are not food grade and should not be used as storage containers for food items, as the bags cannot withstand repeated wash cycles and cannot be sanitized. Cease the use of grocery bags for storage purposes.
Ensure that the use of grocery bags and the re-use of can storage is stopped and obtain food-grade containers/bags. A follow up is scheduled for 5/1/2026 to ensure that cans and grocery bags are no longer being used to store food in.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were multiple containers of raw chicken above raw beef in the walk-in cooler. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order and that food is protected from contamination during storage, holding, preparation, and display. A reference sheet for proper storage order was given to the owner to post near walk in units. A follow up is scheduled for 4/24/2026 to ensure that storage order has been corrected in the walk-in cooler.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
There were multiple food items observed to be stored on the floor, including but not limited to:

1. There was a sheet pan of blocks of cream cheese and imitation crab sticks observed on the floor under the cook-line. 
2. Multiple pots of sauces stored on the floor under a table. These pots of sauces were under a table to the right of the handwashing sink that has a broken pipe. The waste water leaking from the broken pipe was directly touching the bottom of these pans. This is why it is important that food is stored at least six inches from the ground. 
3. A container of raw chicken in a grocery bag stored on the floor under a table. 

Ensure that food items and container of food items should be stored at least six inches off of the floor.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the service station was tested at 0ppm (CL). Discussed with the owner and more bleach was added to the solution. The sani bucket was retested at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that all sanitizer solutions test at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration level.
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment:
There are multiple food items in the facility under TIME AS CONTROL that are not being properly marked with the time removed from cold or hot holding, including: 

1. Multiple containers of water that is used for the rice scoop. 
2. Eggs on the cook-line. 
3. Cooked breaded shrimp and chicken that are stored along the cookline

Ensure that the time is being recorded and written down for food items that are removed from cold or hot holding that are under time as control. CORRECTED- A Time as Control policy was filled out during the inspection and this was discussed with the PIC. The facility plans to label food items with tape indicating the time that the food was prepared and will be discarded after four hours if any leftovers are present.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The facility does not have a probe thermometer available. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 5/1/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer has been obtained. There should always be a probe thermometer in the facility to ensure that foods are being cooked to the correct internal temperature.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: There were at least five unlabeled white bins storing similar white powders in the dry storage hallway. The items are similar in appearance and could be easily mistaken for one another. Discussed with the owner. Ensure that all bins are labeled with the name of the item that’s being stored for identification purposes.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There was about a half inch gap at the bottom of the back door. It appears that the door’s weather stripping is damaged and is allowing sun light through the door. Shown to the owner and she mentioned getting the door repaired. Ensure that all outer doors are tight fitting and never exposed to gaps or cracks that might allow the entry of unwanted pests and/or insects.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were mouse droppings observed on a pan that also stores canned good items in the dry storage area. The owner mentioned that the droppings are old and that she will have the pan removed from the premise. The back storage area is significantly cluttered and could be causing a harboring environment for pest. When time permits, be sure to get rid of items that are no longer useful to the facility. Will follow-up on 5/1/2026 to ensure that mouse droppings have been cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There is observed to be a significant amount of food items on the floor throughout the facility, including but not limited to boxes of food in the walk-in freezer, a shelf in the walk-in cooler that is not sufficiently six inches above the floor holding a container of raw chicken, and a box of cans of ketchup under a shelf in the kitchen. All food should be stored at least SIX inches above the ground to protect from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The facility is re-using containers to store food in, including but not limited to, mayonnaise containers and containers that stored seaweed salad and seasoned squid in them. Cease re-using single-use containers to store food in. Utensils and food-contact surfaces should be durable, able to withstand repeated warewashing, and be smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The handwashing sink in the kitchen had paper towels in the drain at the start of the inspection. The PIC removed the paper towels and stated that the handwashing sink was functional. The inspector began washing their hands using the handwashing sink and the water flowed down the drain and onto the floor. The handwashing sink has a broken pipe that is allowing the waste water to leak onto the table and floor below it. This pipe is observed to be improperly repaired using plastic wrap. A follow up is scheduled for 4/24/2026 to ensure that this handwashing sink has been repaired and is properly functioning.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There is not any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerated units to allow visibility for food service workers.
citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility could not produce food handler certificates for cooks and other employees that handle food and clean dishes. Employees who are not manager certified must obtain a food handler’s certification if handling food and clean dishes.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, a sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed in use utensils to be resting on top of hot holding box. Discussed with PIC, utensils were pulled and placed through dish machine. Ensure any in use utensil is stored in a a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed the person in charge (PIC) wash their hands prior to donning gloves, but failed to use a barrier to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the PIC was reminded to use a barrier to complete proper hand washing. Ensure a barrier is used at the end of hand washing to prevent re-contaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The accumulation of soil buildup was observed underneath the grill in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the soil buildup will be cleaned. Ensure that closed and tight space within the facility are monitored and cleaned on a regular basis providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were uncovered containers of raw meat, cut broccoli, and sauces that were observed to be in the walk-in cooler. This was discussed with the PIC. The PIC has lids in the cooler and states that they leave the lids off during busy times. This is acceptable for items that are in-use, but the other items still need covers on them. All food should be covered in open-air coolers to protect the food from contamination. Ensure that food is stored in packages, in covered containers, or in wrappings to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
1ST REPEAT:
Inspectors observed ready to eat foods stored below animal proteins in the kitchen’s 3 door cooler, including, but not limited to:
1) shelled eggs over milk
2) ham over tomatoes.
CORRECTED- ready to eat items were moved above raw items. Inspectors provided an handout with pictures reflecting proper storage order. Ensure food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination (top to bottom= ready to eat> washed produce> unwashed produce> eggs > beef > chicken).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Multiple temperature control for food safety foods were oberved to be without date marking in the triple door cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed dates on TCS items used for service. Ensure all TCS foods used for service are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation counts as day ONE.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed the chlorine bleach sanitizing bucket “bleaching out”, meaning the sanitizer concentration exceeded the maximum sanitizing level for a food-contact surface, as specified by manufacturer. CORRECTED: The sanitizer bucket was remade and observed at an appropriate concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces. Ensure that all sanitizers shall meet the requirements for use on food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions). [P]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility’s test strips were not testing with the sanitizer bucket that was prepared. CORRECTED- working test strips were obtained. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to verify proper sanitizing concentrations.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed personal foods intermixed with food for service in the triple door cooler. Discussed with the staff members. Separate items for personal use from items used for service to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice dispensers on the two soda machines were observed to have a pink and black mold buildup. PIC was made aware. The two dispensers were cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ice dispenser on the soda machines are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized routinely.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Three cans of split black olives were observed dented in the middle of the can shelf. PIC was made aware. The dented cans were removed. Ensure that food items with compromised package integrity are removed from the inventory and returned appropriately.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw shell eggs were observed being stored directly above cooked lasagna in the large standing refrigerator at the beginning of the cook line. PIC was made aware. The raw shell eggs were removed and stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored properly at all times to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The ambient temperature within the triple doors standing cooler in the far back of the kitchen was observed  higher than 41F. The average surface temperature collected was 57F. The recorded probing temperatures were 45F and 44F. PIC was made aware. PIC stated added an additional hanging thermometer into the unit. The food items were removed from the unit and placed in another unit. 
Ensure that this unit is repaired appropriately to avoid food spoilage.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed a container of white powder under the prep table by the pizza dough mixer. The powder was later identified as flour. PIC was made aware. The container was labeled immediately. Ensure that white powders placed in containers other than their original containers are labeled properly at all times.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food being stored in cans in the prep cooler.
1. Black olives were observed being stored in an opened can in the prep cooler.
2. Mackerels as per PIC were opened the day before was observed stored in the can in the prep cooler.

PIC was made aware. The food items mentioned were removed and placed in appropriate containers for proper storage. Ensure that can food when opened are place in appropriate containers to avoid botulism contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following were observed. 
1. The internal surface of the microwaves in the kitchen were observed with encrusted food particles and debris. PIC had the microwaves cleaned immediately. (COS)
2. Molded food particles were observed scatted in the bottom of the prep cooler. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the surface of the cooler bottom will be cleaned. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces such as the inside of the prep cooler bottom and microwaves are kept free of encrusted food deposits and soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The gasket of the left door of the pizza prep cooler was observed loose. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that a new gasket had been ordered. Ensure that the gasket is repaired ensuring that the door of the cooler is properly sealed to avoid food spoilage.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed .
1. The hoods covering the fan in the standing cooler were observed with an accumulation to soil and dust. 
2. Inspector observed accumulated soil and dust in multiple areas in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the kitchen and all relevant areas will be cleaned. Ensure that the cleaning frequency of the kitchen is increase to avoid the accumulation of soil and dust.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the food handler certification of a couple employees. PIC told inspector that they were unsure whether the employees had the certification or not. Ensure that all employees handling food are trained and certified. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify a valid allergen certification for the only certified food protection manager in the facility. PIC told inspector that they will look for the certification or get the training done. Ensure that the training is done to be in compliance with the law.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed employees not using a barriers to shut off the faucet after handwashing. Education was carried out. The behavior was corrected. Endure that the appropriate procedures for handwashing are followed always to avoid recontaminating your hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzles were observed with an accumulation of soil. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the soda nozzles and began cleaning them immediately. The nozzles were cleaned and inspected. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the nozzles of the soda machine are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following were observed.
1. The bins holding the lids for the single service cups on the right of the soda machine were observed to be soiled. PIC cleaned the bins. (COS)
2. The shelvings use to hold the bread trays and wrapping papers were observed with an accumulation of soil and dust. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the soil and dusts are cleaned to avoid possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspector observed leaking/ponding water and a bit of rust in the bottom of the Prep cooler in the serving area. Discussed PIC and PIC assured inspector that the bottom of the prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure that the ponding water and rust are cleaned appropriately.
citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed;
1. Broken tiles were observed at the front of the back exit door to the facility.
2. An accumulation of food debris over the bread oven and the enclosed space behind the lids of the prep cooler. 
3. Soil and dust in other areas within the facility. 

Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the relevant actions will be taken. Ensure that these paces are cleaned properly and the relevant repairs be done for the tiles providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water siding in the mop bucket in the back. Inspector inquired about the mop water, employee told inspector that the water was from the night before. Education was carried out. The mope water was discarded. Ensure that the dirty mop water is always discarded after mopping at all times.
citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the food handling certification of the PIC. The other employee in the facility had a Food protection manager certification.  PIC told inspector that their certification had expired. PIC  assured inspector that they will get the training for the certification done. Ensure that the certification is acquired to be in compliance with the law.
