Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a dish on the handwashing sink in the back area and a dish in it. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and both items were removed from the handwashing sink. Ensure that staff are educated that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were at least ten ants on the counter to the left of the drive through window. Shown to the PIC and the facility mentioned contacting EcoLab to come provide treatment to the premise. Ensure to throughly clean countertops that are exposed to splatter and dripping syrups to prevent the presence of insects and also accumulated debris.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The walk-in freezer has a significant accumulation of ice and frost on the fan units, walls, ceiling, floor, and boxes of food. This was discussed with the PIC, who stated that the gasket of the freezer door needs replaced and should arrive by Wednesday. Ensure that the issue is repaired and that all frost and ice is removed.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas were observed accumulated with debris:
- The inside cabinet space of the fry station contained a significant amount of debris such as salt, discarded fries, etc.
- The inside cabinet space of the ice cream machine was observed with a significant amount of spilled syrup
- The top of the inside of the tea machine, where the tea is dispensed from has an accumulation of residue on it.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The front handwashing sink has an accumulation of soil residue in the caulking. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that this handwashing sink is resealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
Additionally, the facility could use some cleaning along the coffee station. Floors underneath coffee equipment were observed with splatter and food debris. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed 2 gallons of milk to be stored past its 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking and milk was discarded. Ensure any TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple temperature controls for food safety (TCS) to lack date marking, including but not limited to:
1) sausage at the long prep cooler
2) buttermilk in the standing 2 door cooler
3) carrot cake in the walk in cooler
CORRECTED- dates were placed on all of the aforementioned items. Ensure all TCS items are date marked with the day of preparation to be used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed that two of the sanitizer buckets (quaternary ammonia) were at concentrations exceeding the maximum toxicity level for a food-contact surface, as specified by manufacturer. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the concentration of both sanitizer buckets was adjusted. Inspector and PIC clarified how many sanitizing tablets should be used in each sanitizer bucket (2 tablets). Ensure that all sanitizers shall meet the requirements for use on food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:
(1) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: The bottom shelf of the double cooler has an accumulation of food debris.
(2) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: The inside of the microwave has an accumulation of debris.
(3) The non-food-contact surfaces surrounding the soda nozzles require more frequent cleaning.
(4) The top covering of the chicken breading container had an accumulation of debris.
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following physical facilities are not maintained in good repair:
(a) Replace the wood top counter under the pass-thru window in the kitchen with stainless steel. 
(b) Replace rotted cabinets underneath the hand washing sink in the kitchen. 
(c) Replace the table that holds the meat slicer.
(d) Replace the old mop sink with the new mop sink that was purchased. 
(e) Replace the wood shelving above the triple sink with stainless shelving to allow for air drying of dishes.
Ensure that the above referenced physical facilities are repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
PIC was unable to produce record of an Allergen Awareness Training. PIC will provide a record of Allergen Awareness Training by the next routing inspection. Ensure that all CFPMs have training in Allergen Awareness within 30 days of employment, and renew it every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed all food handlers licenses to be not available during follow up. Discussed with PIC, 3 food handlers licenses were available however there are still staff member that do not have the required license. Ensure all members of staff that handle food have a valid food handlers license available within facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspector observed a wastewater leak from the plumbing under the hand sink. The PIC was informed and was able to tighten the plumbing and repair the leak during the inspection. Ensure plumbing is tightened and monitored after moving the truck to avoid wastewater spills.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink was observed to have several items stored inside the basin, including drink packages, paper towels, and handwashing soap, obstructing its use. The operator requested that the inspector use the three-compartment sink for handwashing; however, the inspector educated the operator on the designated use of each sink. CORRECTED - The items were removed from the handwashing sink, and the sink was made accessible. Ensure the handwashing sink is kept clear of all items and used exclusively for handwashing, and that the three-compartment sink is used only for warewashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [PF]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Ice cubes in the ice machine were observed to be contaminated due to mold present on the baffles and inner corner surfaces of the machine. CORRECTED - The inspector instructed the operator to discard the ice due to mold contamination and bare hand contact and the ice cubes were discarded. Ensure the ice machine is properly cleaned and sanitized and maintained free of mold to prevent contamination of ice. The inspector will follow up on April 27, 2026 regarding the ice machine (see Violation #16).
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The ice machine baffle and inner corner surfaces were observed to have mold. 
2. The soda gun and soda holster were observed to have significant soil accumulation.
3. The pizza oven was observed to have food debris accumulation.

The operator was informed and instructed to clean the above-mentioned surfaces and maintain them free of soil and food debris buildup. The operator attempted to clean the soda gun and soda holster during the inspection; however, soil accumulation was still observed. Ensure all food-contact surfaces are properly cleaned and sanitized and maintained free of soil, mold, and food debris. The inspector will follow up on April 27, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Quaternary ammonium (quats) test strips at the facility were observed to be soiled and unusable, and the operator was unable to locate the quats sanitizer tablets. The inspector advised the operator to use the EPA-approved bleach available for sanitizing food-contact surfaces; however, no chlorine (bleach) test strips were available. CORRECTED - The inspector provided chlorine test strips for interim use until new test strips are obtained. Ensure appropriate sanitizer test strips are available, clean, and usable at all times for monitoring sanitizer concentrations. The inspector will follow up on April 27, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: An uncovered trash can was observed in the female restroom. CORRECTED - The inspector discussed with the operator the need to provide a covered waste receptacle for sanitary napkins. Ensure a covered trash receptacle is provided and maintained in female restrooms.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to handle ready-to-eat (RTE) foods in the additional kitchen space. The items include sliced American cheese and sliced breads. The activity was ceased and corrected. Discussed always using gloves to handles RTE foods and what foods are considered RTE. Bare hands usage should only be used to a minimal if handling raw animal protein or if there is a kill step occurring.  Ensure that bare hands are never used to handle RTE foods to protect against cross contamination of food items.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was improper storage order observed inside of the prep cooler placed in the additional kitchen space. There were raw tenderloins observed above RTE foods (sliced cheeses and deli meats). Shown to the PIC and the items were rearranged to correct the violation. Handouts referencing safe storage order in refrigerated units was given to the facility. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below all RTE foods to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The rubber soda gun holster in the main bar area was observed with dried liquids on the inner surfaces. The surface was shown to the PIC and the holster was cleaned and sanitized during the visit to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces of soda guns and gun holsters are cleaned as frequent as often to prevent accumulated debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A container of cheese sauce that was recently cooked was in the process of actively being cooled. The employees mentioned that the cheese sauce was placed inside of the cooler 45 minutes prior to the visit. The cheese sauce was probed at 95F and contained a tight fitting lid. Discussed with the employees proper timeframes for safe cooling and approved cooling methods. The facility was instructed to break down cheese sauce into smaller portions, containers that allow heat to transfer easily, and keep the containers uncovered so that heat can escape. A handout referencing proper cooling methods was given the facility. Ensure that TCS are cooled within the proper timeframe of 6 hours, as well use an approved cooling method.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- The floor and wall around the fryers in the main kitchen contains accumulated grease debris
- The floors and walls underneath and behind pieces of equipment in the additional kitchen space has accumulated debris 
Ensure that these areas are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: An employee was observed to fill a container in the handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated and aware that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a container of raw salmon above a container of cooked beef in the bottom of a preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the PIC corrected the storage order (the salmon was moved below the beef in the cooler). Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The walk-in cooler fan has a leak coming from it that the PIC stated had just started today. The PIC discarded food items that were under it and moved others to protect them from contamination. Bins were placed under the leak until it can be repaired. The PIC stated that the walk-in cooler might be in defrost mode. Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand sink in the kitchen to be missing paper towels. The PIC was informed and paper towels were refilled. Ensure hand sinks are supplied with disposable towels at all times to use as a barrier to turn off the faucet.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen to “bleach out” the test strip. This is an indicator that the sanitizer concentration is too strong. An employee was informed and the bucket was diluted with water. Ensure test strips are used to test sanitizer concentration to prevent incorrect preparation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed a knife stored in the crevice between two prep counters and the ice scoop stored directly on top of the ice machine. The PIC was informed that in-use utensils must be stored on an easily cleanable surface to prevent cross contamination. The ice scoop was moved to a tray, and the knife was placed in the dish area during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a mop stored directly in the basin of the mop bucket. The PIC was informed and the mop was moved. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to drip dry. This practices prevents microbial growth in the mop head.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets in the facility measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC was informed and the buckets were replaced. Ensure sanitizer buckets are tested and replaced frequently to guarantee proper sanitization. If buckets are consistently measuring 0ppm before replacement time, the frequency of replace needs to be increased.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Personal cleanliness.
comment: Inspector observed an employee handling food without a proper hair restraint. The PIC was informed that restraints are required to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure all employees have their hair restrained prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-402.11 Effectiveness. (A) Except as provided in (B) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall wear hair restraints such as hats, hair coverings or nets, beard restraints, and clothing that covers body hair, that are designed and worn to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the interior of the tray warmers to be soiled with food debris. Clean the interior of the warmers to prevent cross-contamination. Inspector also observed the hood above the fryers to be soiled. Ensure hood system is cleaned by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation - Observed standing water in the dry storage room. The water was not in contact with food items stored in the room. The PIC stated that rain water is encroaching from the exterior wall. PIC plans to schedule service to have the exterior wall repaired. Ensure exterior walls are in good repair to prevent the encroachment of contaminated water into the facility. In the meantime, ensure water is cleaned off floor when encroachment occurs. 

Repeat Violation - Observed considerable ice accumulation at the walk-in freezer door and above the fans in the walk-in freezer. Ensure walk-in freezer is in good repair to prevent the accumulation of ice.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine at the bar to be reaching temperatures between 130-150F. Discussed using a temporary sanitizer set up using quaternary ammonia until the machine is serviced (verify with test strips), OR taking to kitchen dish machine or triple sink. Ensure food contact surfaces are sanitized using a chemical solution that reaches the concentration for sanitation of food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer's label until the machine is serviced. Inspector will return on or by April 20 to verify the dish machine is reaching a minimum sanitizing temperature of 160F.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.[P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bottles to register a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bottles were remade to proper concentration- 200 ppm (200-400 ppm is required for quaternary ammonia). Discussed letting the line run for a few seconds before filling the bottles in the future. Ensure sanitizer solutions are tested to verify they are reaching chemical sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed a mushroom sauce in the walk in cooler to be held past it’s 7 day date mark (4/2). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the sauce will be discarded. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked to be used or discarded within seven days- the day of preparation/ opening/ thawing counts as day ONE.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.[Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled bottle containing a clear liquid in the kitchen. CORRECTED- bottle was confirmed to be sanitizer and labeled accordingly. Ensure all chemicals removed from bulk containers are labeled to prevent contamination of food and nonfood contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed the facility does not have a way to verify sanitizing temperatures of the bar dish machine. Discussed the need for a heat plate or irreversible measuring test strips for heat sanitation of food contact surfaces. Inspector will check for compliance on or by April 27, 2026. Ensure the facility obtains a dish plate or heat strips to verify minimum heat sanitizing temperatures of 160F.
citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas in the physical facility needing repair:
1) SECOND REPEAT: Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The bar hand-sink needs sealed to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
3) FIRST REPEAT There are tiles underneath the dry storage along the north wall of the kitchen have separated from the wall.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.

[P]

comment: Inspector observed that the sliding cooler in the storage room to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed an ambient thermometer in the cooler.Ensure all cooling units holding temperature control for food safety (TCS) contain an ambient thermometer to monitor air temperatures at or below 41F.

citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

comment:
(REPEAT x2) 6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Acoustic type ceiling tiles are observed in the bathrooms. Ceiling coverings should be smooth and easily cleanable. The locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

comment: Inspectors observed that the large standing cooler for the establishment’s bulk dressings and sauces was not cooling sufficiently - sauces were probed at a temperature of 45°F. The PIC was informed, and the cooler was set to a colder temperature. CORRECTED: TCS foods were moved to the walk-in cooler for the time being, and the PIC will monitor the temperature of the standing cooler to see if it is adequate for cooling going forward. Ensure that the cooler is functioning properly - cold holding below 41°F - before returning TCS foods to it.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION (x2): Observed the stainless steel shelf above the three compartment sink is rusted above and below. The shelf must either be replaced or painted and sealed. Ensure that the shelf is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. NOTE that fixing the ventilation in that area (violation #56: non-working heat dish machine ventilation hood) may prevent additional rusting in the area.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas that are in need of repair:
(1) the baseboards on the floor between and next to the walk-in cooler and freezer.
(2) the ventilation in the walk-in freezer is dripping and has a tray that has been placed to catch the drips - inspectors also noted that the fans spray water when they turn on.
(3) the microwave door in the front kitchen has interior damage.
(4) the walk-in cooler and freezer doors are difficult to shut - there is an accumulation of ice / water at the bottom areas.
The PIC was informed, and made plans for repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that equipment and physical facilities are in a state of good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed that the ventilation hood over the heat dish machine was not working, causing an excess of condensation in the surrounding area, including the ceiling HVAC vent (observed to be rusted and with visible water drips), and excessive steam pushing out into the surrounding area. This could be contributing to the rusted shelving observed in the kitchen area as well. The PIC was informed, and made plans for its repair by the next routine inspection. Ensure that ventilation hood systems are sufficient in capacity to prevent condensation from collecting.
citation_text: 4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were several insect glue traps that contained at least 15 dead roaches throughout the facility. There weren’t any live roaches found, however, each of the glue traps contained many dead insects. The facility contracts with Bacon’s Termite & Pest Control as their pest provider. The owner mentioned that the traps are old and have not been replaced in several months. Ensure that the premise is free of insects (live or dead) and to monitor the presence of insects through trapping devices and keeping the facility clean. Will follow-up on April 27, 2026 to check on the replacement of traps.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There were unwrapped straws mixed with wrapped straws on top of the bar’s counter. The unwrapped straws are in close proximity to customers are presents exposure to the food contact surface. Ensure to purchase wrapped straws or place the unwrapped behind the counter where they are controlled by employees.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility was observed operating without sanitizer solutions. The restaurant had recently opened and was in the process of serving customers upon arrival. Two sanitizer buckets were prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are always present if the facility is preparing, handling, and serving food to the public.

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas inside of the kitchen are in need of cleaning:
- underneath the prep table (directly next to the prep cooler)
- walls behind the prep table that’s mentioned above

The floor has accumulated food debris underneath the prep table and the wall contains dried grease. Ensure that these areas are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There weren’t any signed employee health forms for any of the employees working at the facility. The owner had two blank copies of employee reporting forms and an additional blank copy was given to the facility. Each employee shall have the employee health form signed to acknowledge that they wont come into work sick and that they will report to the PIC if any illnesses are present. Will follow-up on 4/24/2026 to ensure that forms have been signed and completed by all employees.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

Ensure to use a barrier when operating faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.

The items were removed from both sinks to correct the violation. Discussed with owner. Be sure to educate employees on the importance of handwashing and to avoid obstructing handsinks so that they are easily accessible at all times to wash hands.

Shown to the PIC and he mentioned that he would contact a technician to have the machine cleaned internally. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed at least two different time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored at room temperature. The owner mentioned that the items were recently cooked and were suppose to be in the process of cooling. The items were tomato sauce and shelled eggs. The owner mentioned that the eggs are served with ramen dishes, which the shell is typically removed from the egg, causing it to be TCS. The items were properly placed on ice baths to correct the violation. When cooling TCS foods, ensure that items are cooled within the six hour timeframe using the approved methods of ice baths, ice wands, adding ice as a component, or inside of cold holding equipment.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There were not any sanitizer buckets available, although food service was occuring. Discussed with the PIC and sanitizer buckets were prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat). Buckets were placed in various stations of the restaurant to correct the violation. Be sure to educate employees that sanitizer solutions must always be available if preparing, handling, or serving food. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are available during all hours of operation.

Be sure that test strips are available to ensure that solutions are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration levels. Will follow-up on 4/24/2026.

Additionally, the fan grates (also near the hand-sink along the cook-line) were heavily accumulated with dust. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food handler certificates were not available for any of the employees working at the time of the inspection. Discussed with PIC that any employee that handles food, clean dishes, or ice must obtain a food handler certificate. Ensure that food handler certificates are printed and available for all employees who are not food manager certified.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be held past there date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled and discarded. Ensure TCS item is discarded after its 7 day date marking maximum.

(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.

Ensure single service containers are being stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) If used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

comment:

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.[P]

(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following:
(1) a buildup of soil residues on the shelves of the walk-in cooler.
(2) underneath the prep tables on a shelf was a paint scraper with with sticky green liquid.
The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean these areas more frequently.
Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned frequently to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed that the mop was sitting in the water part of the mop bucket where it is unable to air dry. CORRECTED: The PIC was informed that the mop was not properly stored, and the PIC removed the mop from the mop bucket and hung it to dry. Ensure that after use mops are able to fully air dry in a place where they cannot soil walls, equipment, or supplies.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A can of mixed vegetables and a can of tomato paste stored on shelves in the dry storage area were observed to be swollen, indicating potential bacterial activity. Also, two cans of mandarin oranges were observed to have dents along the seams. The inspector discussed the need to remove swollen and dented cans due to the risk of food contamination. CORRECTED - The operator removed the affected cans from the shelves. Ensure swollen or dented canned foods are not stored or served.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: A sanitizer bucket was not observed in the kitchen during the inspection. Two sanitizer buckets testing at 400 ppm were observed in the dinning hall near the kitchen. The inspector educated and instructed the operator to ensure a sanitizer bucket is available and maintained in the kitchen during all hours of operation, while the facility could still maintain the sanitizer buckets in the dinning hall. CORRECTED - The operator prepared a sanitizer bucket, which tested at 400 ppm. A sanitizer bucket should always be in the kitchen during all hours of operation for sanitizing surfaces and equipments.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The microwave in the serving station at the dinning hall was observed to have food debris and soil accumulation. The inspector instructed the operator to ensure the microwave is cleaned to sight and touch and kept free of food debris and soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. CORRECTED- The employee was educated on properly washing their hands. Ensure that all staff are trained to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands to prevent recontaminating their hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice shoots of the soda machine were observed soiled with black and pinkish debris. Shown and discussed with the PIC. The facility mentioned that the ice shoots will be cleaned in the near future. Suggested contacting the manufacturing company to service internal work. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation. Will schedule an additional follow-up for April 23, 2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The two storage racks inside of the walk in cooler still contained visible mold on the surfaces.  A presence of mold inside of any cold holding equipment poses several health risks to food items, as well as food contact surfaces. The employees cleaned the racks prior to the visit, however, mold was still observed on surfaces. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors and are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold buildup up.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The handwashing sink along the cooking line was not observed leaking, however, there has been a repeated history of the bottom pipe leaking water. During the April 4th routine inspection, waste water was observed leaking from the pipe, but the PIC tightened the pipe to stop the leak as a temporary fix. The sink is also being supported by a 2x4 wood plank. Will schedule an additional followup for 4/23/2026 to ensure that the sink has been completely repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler being stored above ready-to-eat produce. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and the eggs were moved below the RTE foods. Ensure that storage order is followed with ready-to-eat foods stored above raw animal proteins, and proteins with the highest final cooking temperatures stored bottom to top.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple Time/Temperature Control for Safety Foods (TCS) being cold held at temperatures above 41°F (5°C):
(a) barbecue sauce labeled “refrigerate after opening”, probed at 61°F,
(b) blue cheese dressing labeled “refrigerate after opening”, probed at 52 °F, and
(c) chicken in batter, probed at 57 °F.
For the sauce station (a and b), inspectors checked the original containers of the manufactured products to see if items needed to be refrigerated after opening, and all but the Frank’s Red Hot Buffalo sauce needed to be refrigerated after opening. The current cold holding method was found to be insufficient, and the PIC was educated on better cold holding methods (deeper ice baths) or using time as a control (discard sauces after 4 hours if not held at 41°F or below). CORRECTED: PIC discarded the sauces.
CORRECTED: The chicken batter (c) was voluntarily discarded, and a new ice bath with ice surrounding multiple sides of the holding container was created.
Ensure that TCS foods are held at temperatures below 41°F or above 135°F. If cold holding temperatures cannot be maintained, then items should be discarded after 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed that spray bottles with repackaged cleaning chemicals were not labeled. CORRECTED: PIC was informed that repackaged chemicals should be clearly and individually labeled with common names, and PIC placed corresponding labels on all spray bottles without labels. Ensure that working containers used for storing chemicals are clearly identified with common names to prevent accidental contamination or misuse.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspectors observed that establishment’s test strips were expired. CORRECTED: PIC was informed, and acquired new test strips during the inspetion. Ensure that sanitizing solutions used for food contact surfaces have a test kit or test strips to verify concentration of sanitizing agents.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink after handwashing. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure all staff are using a barrier to turn off the faucet after handwashing to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 EJ and SM present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments. There were only a few glue traps present during today’s inspection Critical areas such as the floor behind equipment on the cook line were without glue traps. Two live adults and two live juveniles were observed under equipment on the cook line. Ensure glue traps are out and dated at all times to monitor activity. SCDPH will continue to follow-up until no pests are observed. This means keeping the glue traps present as a monitoring tool and insuring treatment is curtailing life cycles. The next follow-up is scheduled for May 13, 2026. 

 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. comment: Inspectors observed triple sink to have a leak present from faucet. PIC stated that a whole new apparatus is on order. Inspector will return on or by Wednesday, 13 May 2026.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employee was observed shutting the faucet with bare hands after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC. The behavior was corrected. Ensure that a barrier is used to shut the facet after handwashing to avoid recontaminating your clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was no sani bucket observed in the kitchen as food prep began. Discussed with PIC. Inspector asked PIC to have a Sani bucket made. The Sanitizer for the sani bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer is always made and placed in a sani bucket before any food prep or handling at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the certified food manager’s allergen training certification. PIC told inspector that they had the training done but they cannot find it now however, they will look through their documents and find the certification. Ensure that all paperwork are available and accessible for viewing and verification at all times. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Sausage croissants, Lunchables and snack packs in the standing display cooler as you enter the facility are observed with internal temperatures of 45.3F. The PIC was shown and discarded the TCS foods in this cooler to correct the immediate violation. The cooler functioning correctly is being handled on line item #33 of this report. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at safe temperatures throughout storage until service.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY.

The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the follow-up. The normal follow-up time frame is being pushed back to coincide with the other follow ups on this report. citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler used for storage of sausage, cheese and other proteins is holding foods at 45.3F. The PIC was consulted and instructed to have the cooler repaired prior to the follow-up.

4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Both CL and Quat based sanitizers are available in the facility. Test strips are only available for the CL sanitizer during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to acquired test strips for both sanitizers used in the facility prior to the follow-up.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
citation_text:
3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

On the inspector’s arrival the facility had hot dogs on the rollers.  As a Class-III facility this is not allowed. The situation was discussed and the hot dogs discarded to correct. The equipment was turned off. Ensure that the facility is only operating within its classification at all times.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be available during spot check. Discussed with PIC, ensure all members of staff that handle food have a valid food handlers license available within facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was not a temporary handwashing station available and the facility is scooping ice for drinks. It was discussed with the PIC that the bathroom sinks are not close enough to be suitable for handwashing. CORRECTED- A temporary handwashing station was set up. citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed that the trash can in the unisex bathroom did not have a lid. PIC was informed, and will replace the trash can with a lidded trash can. Ensure that toilet rooms used by females have covered receptacles for sanitary napkins for both hygienic purposes and to prevent plumbing issues from flushed feminine hygiene products.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Chicken was stored directly above fish in the bottom of the prep cooler on the cook line.
2. Raw beef was stored directly above strawberries in the bottom of the prep cooler on the cook line. 
3. Inspector observed chicken stored directly above beef in the walk-in cooler

The PIC was informed of these violations and storage order was corrected. Ensure all staff are following proper storage order practices in the coolers to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

Repeat Violation

3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the mop head stored directly on the floor by the mop sink. This violation was previously noted in September 2024, March 2025, June 2025, and February 2026, and March 2026. This storage method does not allow for proper drip drying. The PIC was informed, and stated that the hooks present around the mop sink cannot hold the mop handle. The inspector recommended propping the mop against the wall of the mop sink with the mop head upright to drip dry, or storing the mop in the straining basin of the bucket rather than the basin of the bucket or the floor. A follow-up will be conducted on April 15, 2026 to ensure proper mop storage is being conducted in the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed cooled chili in the prep cooler to lack date marking. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the item was prepared yesterday and placed the correct corresponding date on the food. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with the day of preparation/ thawing/ opening to be used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Allergen awareness notice
comment:
The facility did not have an allergen awareness sign posted. CORRECTED- a sign was placed on the left side of the ordering window. Ensure allergen awareness signage is always visible to the consumer when ordering.

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink nearest the entry of the kitchen to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- paper towels were placed in the unit. Ensure all hand washing sinks are always stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels for proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed a staff person put on gloves without handwashing first. Education was carried out. Ensure that staff know to wash their hands before putting on gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.16(B) Hand Antiseptics. (B) If a hand antiseptic or a hand antiseptic solution used as a hand dip does not meet the criteria specified under Subparagraph (A)(2) of this section, use shall be: (1) Followed by thorough hand rinsing in clean water before hand contact with FOOD or by the use of gloves; or (2) Limited to situations that involve no direct contact with FOOD by the bare hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed improper storage order of raw meat, specifically steak stored above fish, in a cooler. The PIC was notified about the issue, and the steak was moved below the fish. Ensure that food is properly stored per storage order guidelines.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed buildup of soil residues in the soda nozzles. PIC was notified, and the nozzles were removed for cleaning and sanitizing, and also replaced some with newer clean nozzles. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following items that need cleaning:
(1) The area between the grill and reach-in coolers in the Grill area was observed to have an accumulation of grease and soil residues.
(2) An accumulation of food debris and grease on surfaces near the fryer area.
(3) An accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezers and reach-in freezer.
Ensure that areas are smooth and easily cleanable, and are cleaned frequently.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There were two packages of moldy onions stored in one of the produce containers on the main floor. The onions were pulled from the shelf by the PIC to correct the violation. Ensure that food items are in good condition and never moldy.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A floor cooler storing various cheeses was observed to have an ambient temperature of 49F (measured on inspector’s thermometer). The internal thermometer of the unit read 50F, and gradually decreased to 45F.
