Most of the cheeses were measured at compliant temperatures, however, the top left rack of shredded cheeses were measuring between 47F - 55F. The cheeses were pulled from the shelf and the facility will have the unit serviced soon. Ensure that time/temperature control (TCS) foods are maintained at proper cold holding temperatures of 41F or below. Will follow-up on April 20, 2026 to be sure that the unit is holding proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a container of raw beef stored above cooked seafood in a prep cooler along the cookline. The items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal proteins are never stored above any ready-to-eat (RTE) foods to protect against cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: All sanitizer solutions throughout the restaurants were testing less than 100ppm (quat). These included sanitizer from the main triple sink and all buckets stored along the cookline. The sanitizer bag connected to the sink dispenser was observed empty. The bag was replaced by the PIC and retested at 200ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentrations to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. 

Boxes of food items were observed on the floor in the kitchen area as well as the dry storage area during the inspection. The PIC stated that the items were received a couple days prior. The situation was discussed and they were instructed to store all food items six inches above the floor to allow for cleaning and reduce pest concerns in the future.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

A moist rag is observed on the counter int he back. The rag is being used for wiping down the surfaces in the kitchen. It should be held between uses in a sanitizer of sufficient concentration to prevent the growth of pathogenic organisms. The PIC was consulted and instructed to adjust their procedure moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT from the pre-opening) 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

Items remaining from the pre-opening that are in need of correction include: 1) Replace ceiling tiles in the kitchen and restrooms with smooth, easily cleanable surface-- vinyl ceiling tiles or gloss/semigloss paint. 2) Paint bare plywood and drywall edge above the utility sink. 3) Seal back door to eliminate daylight visible along the bottom edge. Repair/replace these items prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw beef was observed to be stored over cooked chicken in the prep cooler opposite to the grill. PIC was made aware of the improper storage order and storage order was corrected. Ensure that staffs are made aware of adequate storage order for food items. Raw foods must always be stored below ready-to-eat foods and meats must be stored according to their internal cooking temperatures. [P]
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The counter surface on left of the dish machine was observed to have been unsealed to the wall disabling the caulking. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the caulking will be redone. Ensure that the gaps between these surfaces and the walls are caulked to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.[C]
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed engaging in food prep without washing hands. The employee recently entered the facility from outdoors and went to the cookline to handle food. Discussed with the PIC proper handwashing and the need of washing hands when entering from outside. Ensure to always wash hands before engaging in food prep if tasks are interrupted.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of raw chicken stored on the counter at room temperature. The PIC mentioned that the employees were going to portion the chicken into smaller batches. Discussed that chicken shall stay in cold holding equipment until it’s ready for use. The tub of chicken was placed inside of the walk in cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods maintain proper cold holding temperatures at 41F or below when not in use.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
comment: The facility prepares and serves sushi in house made with both raw and cooked seafood. There wasn’t a consumer advisory sign posted throughout the facility making consumers aware of the health risks, nor is there a disclaimer on the menu. A consumer advisory sign was posted for customers’ view to correct the violation. Be sure to work on adding a disclaimer to the menu to make consumers aware of the health risks associated with the consumption of raw or undercooked foods.
citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were several mouse dropping on the floor surrounding the water heater in the main kitchen area. Shown to the PIC and the droppings were cleaned to correct the violation. No other droppings were observed throughout the facility. Discussed cleaning in hard to reach areas, as well as areas that don’t get used very often to prevent harboring conditions for pest (in addition to cleaning heavily used areas). Ensure that the premises is free of insects and regularly cleaned to eliminate the presence of unwanted pest.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The containers that the facility uses for storing ready-to-eat (RTE) foods aren’t food grade approved. The containers have many cracks, aren't durable, and will not be able to withstand repeated ware washing. Discussed with the PIC that containers for storing food must be sufficient in thickness and resistant to cracking and tares. In the near future, purchase containers that are food grade approved if using to store food in house. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of the hood system were observed heavily accumulated with dried grease. The facility contracts Steam Power to service their hood system. Discussed with the PIC that baffles should be cleaned in house in between professional cleanings. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor underneath the cook line is in need of a deep cleaning. There was dried food, grease accumulation, and other debris observed behind pieces of cooking equipment. Shown to the PIC. Ensure that floors are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The main cook’s food handler certificate has expired. The PIC mentioned that the facility will have the employee’s certificate renewed. Ensure that any employee who cooks or handles clean dishes obtain either a food handler certificate or a food manager certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
Inspector observed the following items to be stored in improper packaging:
1. Wonton strips stored in a cardboard box on the counter
2. Cooked breaded chicken stored in a cardboard box in the upright  sliding-door cooler.
3. Cooked pork stored in a grocery bag in the upright 2-door cooler.

Food must be stored in either its original packaging or a container which is made for food contact or can be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure these items are stored safely to prevent accidental contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Raw pork stored above cooked chicken
2. Raw duck stored above raw shrimp and noodles
3. Raw beef stored above raw shell eggs

The PIC was informed and these items were moved. There is a storage order flyer posted on the walk-in cooler door with Chinese translation. Ensure staff are following the instructions listed on this flyer.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed an employee wash and rinse multiple dishes without sanitizing. The triple sink was not prepared for proper wash, rinse, and sanitize. The staff member was halted by inspectors. The PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper wash, rinse, sanitize practices. The triple sink was properly prepared during the inspection. A handout with Chinese translation was also provided. Ensure proper wash, rinse, sanitize practices are followed for every dish that is cleaned in the facility.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation.

Inspectors observed no date marking on prepared food containers in the facility. All temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum. The inspector will return on 4/20/2026 to check on date marking at the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed bleach in use at the facility which is not labeled for use on food-contact surfaces. The product appears to be intended for use on laundry, not food-contact surfaces. Bleach must have a label with an EPA number and instructions for food-contact sanitizing. A follow-up will be conducted on April 13, 2026 to ensure proper sanitizer is being used in the facility.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed no stem thermometer present in the facility. An employee was informed and stated that he could not find the thermometer. A follow-up will be conducted on April 20, 2026 to ensure a stem thermometer is readily available for use in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple containers of sugar, flour, corn starch, and MSG to be missing a label. Education was conducted regarding the importance of labeling white powders to prevent accidental misuse. The containers were labeled in Chinese using a Sharpie during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed two dead insects present in the facility during the inspection. One was in the back near the walk-in cooler, and the other was beside the chest freezer. Inspectors also noted rodent droppings present under shelving and on window sills in the facility. Ensure active pest control measures are being taken in the facility to prevent contamination. The facility requires deep cleaning in many spaces of the kitchen that will contribute to pest harborage in the facility. Inspector will spot check for pest control and cleaning during the scheduled follow-up (April 20, 2026).
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed several foods (ex. egg rolls, wontons, chicken wings, crab rangoon) in the clear sliding cooler were not covered during storage. Items were also stored in the 2-door upright cooler and walk-in cooler without protective coverings. Ensure coverings are used for all food in coolers to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed single-service cups stored directly on the floor in the back storage area. Ensure these items are stored at least 15cm off the ground to prevent contamination from splash, dust, or pests.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of food reside in the bottom gaskets of the clear sliding door cooler.
(2) THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of debris inside of the fan above the double door cooler. 
(3)  The prep table in the back of the kitchen was covered in flour/corn starch.
(4) The shelving above the triple sink is rusted and soiled.
(5) The ceiling in the back room and above the chest freezer is heavily soiled/damaged.
(6) The handle of the coolers and chest freezer are soiled with food debris.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed there is a buildup on grease and other debris on the floor underneath the fryer. The fryer should be moved to facilitate cleaning underneath. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the floor is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The inspectors observed the following facility items in need of repair:
(1) The facility is missing coving in many areas of the kitchen. 
(2) The utility sink is damaged and repaired with duct tape.
(3) The triple sink is held up with bare wood between the sink basin and the floor.
(4) The ceiling is damaged with gaps between the seams in the back storage area.
(5) The shelving above the triple sink is heavily rusted and damaged.

Ensure these facility items are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspectors observed significant amounts of water to be leaking/ponding throughout facility. Areas mainly include walk in cooler, dry storage, and dish room. Per CK, kitchen will be closing until a plumber is contacted and leak is serviced.
citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The ice scoop in the bar ice basin was observed to have the handle in contact with the ice. CORRECTED- This was discussed with an employee, who then corrected the scoop handle to be above the ice. Employees use their bare hands to scoop ice using the ice scoop, therefore, the ice scoop should be stored with the handle above the ice to protect the ice from contamination from bare hand contact.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a spoon observed to be in the handwashing sink at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The spoon was removed and an employee was educated that handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use and that they are ONLY used for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were packages of raw beef tenderloin filets in a standing cooler above a container of breadcrumbs. CORRECTED- An employee moved the breadcrumbs to be above the raw beef tenderloin filets. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The ice baffle and the top of the inside of the ice machine were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The ice baffle and the top of the inside of the ice machine were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that the ice machine is being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain it clean. 
2. The pizza cutter was observed to be stored between the back of the table and the wall. This is not a food-contact surface. CORRECTED- The pizza cutter was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are being stored in a manner that protects them from contamination. 

Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There was marinara sauce in a hot holding unit that was probed to be at 122F and 118F. An employee stated that they had recently transferred the sauce from the stove into the steam table. CORRECTED- The marinara sauce was reheated on the stove and this was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that hot holding temperatures are being monitored by employees to make sure that hot holding equipment is properly functioning. Ensure that TCS food is being hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There were reduced oxygen packaged (ROP) halibut and salmon that were observed to still be in their package and thawed in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The ROP salmon and halibut had slits cut in their packages and an employee was educated on this. Ensure that ROP fish is removed from its packaging prior to being thawed under refrigeration or is removed from its packaging immediately after being thawed.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The floor under the soda syrups and next to the water heater is observed to be an accumulation of soil residue on it.
2. The walk-in cooler shelves have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residue.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink to the right of the cook-line is observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 
2. The handwashing sink in the back preparation area of the kitchen is observed to need to be sealed to the wall. 
3. There are holes in the wall above the pizza preparation cooler. Ensure that these holes are sealed. 
4. There are missing coving tiles under the table to the left of the dish machine. Ensure that these coving tiles are replaced. 
5. The table to the left of the dish machine is in need of being sealed to the wall. 
6. FIRST REPEAT- There are missing cove tiles to the left of the mop sink. Ensure that this coving is replaced. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed that the large cooler in the back kitchen area had raw bacon on the top shelf above cheese, potatoes, and other ready-to-eat food items. The PIC was notified, and the raw bacon was moved to the bottom shelf, where it was below these foods. Ensure that raw meats are stored below READY TO EAT foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspectors observed several sauces made in house that were still in the coolers past their date-marking, including a honey mustard dressing that was made in house that should have been discarded 30 March 2026. The PIC and staff were notified, and the out-of-date sauces were voluntarily discarded. It is important that TCS foods, especially ones that are prepared “in house” in an establishment, are discarded after 7 days, with day 1 being the date of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is in need of repair:
(1) The gasket of the left door of the prep cooler in the front kitchen is in disrepair.
(2) The large standing cooler in the back had a dish rag tied around a dripping hose. According to the PIC, this was placed there by the plumber.
The PIC was notified of the issues, and will work on getting them repaired by the next routine inspection.
Ensure that equipment is maintained in good working order that prevents contamination and loss of temperature control.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following surfaces in need of cleaning:
(1) the shelving in the back kitchen standing cooler - there was an accumulation of soil residue on the shelves.
(2) the right side of the front kitchen prep cooler - there was significant accumulation of soil residue - the prep cooler should be moved for cleaning.
The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean these surfaces before the next routine inspection.
It is important that nonfood-contact surfaces be cleaned frequently to prevent the build up of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
(1st Repeat) Inspectors observed that no one present in the facility at the start of the inspection has completed the allergen awareness training. All Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM) must also complete training in basic allergen awareness principles. Ensure that sufficient employees have the allergen certificate by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment:
Multiple incidents of bare hand contact were observed during today’s inspection:
1) The salad tongs at the server station were in contact with the food.
2) The ice scoop was in contact with the ice in the ice machine.
3) A bowl was stored as a scoop in tomato sauce in the walk in cooler. 
CORRECTED- the tongs and ice scoop were moved so that the handle was no longer in contact with the ready to eat (RTE) foods. The bowl was removed from the tomato sauce. Ensure scoops (that have handles) and tongs are stored in such a manner to prevent bare hand contamination. Improper hygiene practices are one of the top five risk factors for food borne illness.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 2 cans of tomato sauce on the bottom of the can storage rack to contain dents within the body and along the seam. CORRECTED- The inspector pointed out the dents to the person in charge (PIC), who stated they will be removed the cans from service to be returned to supplier (currently the cans above create a weight that make them inaccessible). Remind employees to check cans for dents along the seams to prevent the entry and growth of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed ground beef (minimal internal temperature of 155F) stored above whole cuts of beef (minimal internal temperature of 145F). CORRECTED- the ground beef was moved below the whole cuts and education regarding surface area contaminants for ground products was provided. Inspector provided the PIC with a storage order handout. Ensure all animal proteins are stored by increasing internal cooking temperatures to prevent contamination of foods with lower (-no) cooking temperatures.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket near the kitchen entry to have soap, and no measurable concentration of chemical sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket (Chlorine bleach) was remade to 100 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at a frequency to hold the sanitizing concentration of food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm for Chlorine bleach). Do not use soap for chemical sanitation, as the soap and sanitizer combined decrease each product’s intended use.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed raw shelled eggs sitting at an ambient temperature of 86 on wire shelving in the kitchen. The PIC verified the eggs had been out since 10 AM (3.75 hours). CORRECTED- the eggs were discarded. Ensure all  temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F, OR marked to be used or discarded within 4 hours after removing from temperature control to limit the growth of pathogens.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Date marking was absent from nearly all TCS food items through the facility. Items include, but are not limited to: cut tomatoes, cut potatoes, fish, and other animal proteins. CORRECTED- dates or preparation were placed on TCS foods. Ensure all TCS foods are labeled with the date of preparation/ thawing/ opening, to be used or discarded within SEVEN days. The day of preparation/ thawing/ opening counts as day ONE.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a gap in the back door along the bottom and left perimeter, allowing light to enter. This gap may serve as a location for pest to enter the facility. Ensure weather stripping is placed to seal the gap by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed edible taco bowls stored (inverted) on top of the double door cooler nearest to dish machine. CORRECTED- the taco bowls were covered. Ensure all food is stored in a manner to protect from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a wet sanitizer cloth stored on top of single use butter and jams near the kitchen door. CORRECTED- the wet sanitizer cloth was moved to the sanitizer bucket. Ensure all wet sanitizing cloths are stored in a chemical sanitizing solution to prevent the harborage and spread of pathogens with a high water activity.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: The fan grates in the walk in cooler contain a significant amount of dust. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, grease, and other debris. These debris poses a risk to contaminate ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.[C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed an electrical outlet below the kitchen microwave to be lacking plate covers. Place covers on these outlets to prevent the entry of food or other debris, which may enter the wall. Physical facilities should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed boxes of food items stored directly on the floor of the walk-in freezer connected to the main kitchen space. The PIC was informed and pallets/crates will be acquired to lift food items off the ground. Ensure storage is corrected prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspectors observed several items that were being stored past their date-marked discard date. PIC voluntarily disposed of the items. It is important that items not only are properly date-marked with the day of prep being day 1 and day 7 being the date where the item must be used or discarded, but that out-of-date items are then discarded per the written date-mark.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following instances of improper storage:
1) bowls were stored on open shelves upright instead of inverted and were open to falling debris through the shelves;
2) utensils were stored upright instead of inverted in the drying racks.
The PIC was notified of all instances.
1) The shape of the bowls is not conducive to inversion, so the PIC plans to place mats on the above shelves to protect the dishes and prevent falling debris.
2) The utensils were removed and washed and replaced in an inverted position.
It is important that all equipment, utensils, and single-service or single-use articles are kept protected through cover or inversion.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed a build-up of debris in the following locations:
1) (1ST REPEAT) The debris on the floor of the outside shed that stores single-use articles.
2) The debris surrounding the microwave in the front kitchen area.
3) The splashes and debris in the bottom of both milk coolers.
4) The debris surrounding the bread slicer.
The PIC was notified and planned to add it to the cleaning schedule.
It is important that food-contact and non-food contact surfaces are kept free of accumulated dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of black mold and deterioration of caulking near the dish machine and triple sink. PIC was notified and made plans for cleaning and re-caulking. It is important that all physical facilities be maintained and in good repair, and that equipment that cannot be moved is kept sealed to prevent the building of moisture and debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer dispenser in the meat/seafood area appears to not be functioning properly. The sanitizer bucket, as well as the triple sink tested at 0ppm (quat). After changing the chemical’s bag, the solution remained at 0ppm (quat). The facility will utilize the butcher shop’s triple to sink to access sanitizer until the sink can be repaired. Ensure that the sanitizer solution tests at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There were at least 20 boxes observed on the floor of the shared walk in freezer. The boxes were pilled on top of each other and have started to fall onto the floor. An employee started to rearrange the freezer during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- baffles of the hood system above the fryers were observed with dried grease
- floor freezers that holds prepackage foods (breakfast frozen meats & okra) were observed with a significant amount of ice buildup. There is a broken gasket on the door, which might be causing the ice to accumulate 
- the fan grates of the small meat cooler (in deli) and the fan grates of the meat/butcher room are heavily accumulated with dust
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of repair:
- the current caulk on the triple sink in the deli area is starting to pull from the wall and also contains black mold
- the current caulk on the triple seat in the meat/seafood area is starting to pull from the wall
Ensure that sinks are cleaned and recaulked to prevent debris accumulation and assure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: The shared walk in freezer is lacking proper lighting. There was minimal visibility without using flashlights. A light bulb was provided to correct the violation.Ensure that better lighting is provided to the unit.
citation_text: 6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There weren’t any handwashing signs posted at the handwashing sinks in each of the bathrooms. A handwashing sign instructing employees to wash hands before returning to work after a bathroom break should be posted and available in bathrooms. A sign for each bathroom was given to the PIC to post. Ensure that handwashing signs are posted and available for employees.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was mold starting to form on the lid of a container storing a food item (maybe icing). The container was shown to the PIC. There was also a significant amount of mold buildup on the shelves inside of the walk in cooler - see violation #49 for further details. A follow-up to ensure that the shelves, food items, and food packaging are in good condition and are free of mold.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The ice shoots of the soda machine were observed soiled with black debris. Shown and discussed with the PIC. The facility mentioned that the ice shoots will be cleaned in the near future. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation. Will follow-up on 4/13/2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution available along the main cookline. Discussed with the PIC and a sani bucket was prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer solution present if food preparation, food handling, or service is occurring to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The two storage racks inside of the walk in cooler were observed HEAVILY accumulated with mold buildup. Shown and discussed with the PIC. The facility has a plan to deep clean on a day that the facility isn’t in operation. A presence of mold inside of any cold holding equipment poses several health risks to food items, as well as food contact surfaces. Ensure that shelves are taken outdoors and are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold buildup up.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There was a leak coming from the pipe underneath the handwashing sink in the kitchen area. The sink is also being supported by a 2x4 wood plank. The PIC tighten the piping during the inspection as a temporary fix. Because this was also a violation at the July 2025 routine inspection, a follow-up is being scheduled for 4/13/2026 to ensure that the plumbing is repaired by a licensed plumber and is in leakfree condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Overall, the facility is in need of a detail cleaning in many areas of the store - including floors, walls, and ceilings of the cook-line, floors and walls in the back stock area, and underneath and behind large pieces of equipment. Pieces of equipment that aren't stationary shall be pulled from wall so that floors and walls can be thoroughly cleaned. The PIC mentioned that the facility has a plan to deep the facility maybe on a day that the facility isn't in operation. In the meantime, be sure to thoroughly clean the facility during down time to prevent the buildup of splatter, food, and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handwashing sink along the cookline is starting to pull from the wall and has about an 1/2 inch gap between the wall and the sink. This gap allows for unwanted debris to fall and accumulate behind the sink. Ensure that the sink is caulked to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following were observed during today’s inspection,
1. The sanitizer concentration in the dish machine was measured at 0ppm. PIC told inspector that they will use the three compartment sink until the dish machine is fixed.
2. The chlorine sanitizer in the sani bucket in the kitchen was observed to be unreadable. PIC was made aware and a new sani bucket was made. (COS) 
3. There was no sani bucket observed at the bar. Education was carried out. A Sani bucket was made. (COS)
 Ensure that the sanitizer concentration in the sanitizer buckets and dish machine is continuously checked at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following were observed, 
1. The nozzles of the soda guns at the bar were observed with an accumulation of soil. Education was carried out. The nozzles were cleaned immediately. (COS)
2. The baffles of the ice machine were observed with an accumulation of mold. Discussed with PIC. The ice was discarded. PIC assured inspector that a cleaning will be scheduled. Inspector will return on Tuesday (4/6/26) to followup. 
 Ensure that food contact surfaces and utensils are clean at all times.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed a box and several bags of single service items being stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Education as carried out. The single service items were removed to be stored properly in another location.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
REPEAT X2 Inspectors observed the following,
1. An accumulation of grease and dust build up on the side and underneath the fryers including food debris.
2. Soil accumulation observed under the grill and stoves. 
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the above mentioned areas will be clean. Ensure that closed spaces like the above mentioned areas are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: A mop head was observed being stored on the floor in a dirty water in the mop bucket at the beginning and during the inspection. Discussed with PIC and the mop storage was corrected. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: An accumulation of ice and frost were observed in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the accumulation would be cleaned. Ensure that the ice is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a missing ceiling tile above the fryers including the kitchen. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the ceiling tile is replaced sealing the opening.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: The hood ventilation was observed to have an accumulation of soil and grease buildup dangling. PIC was made aware. PIC called the company hired for the routine cleaning and the hood service was scheduled while inspector was present. Ensure that the hood systems is routinely cleaned to avoid the accumulation of grease and soil.
citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Facility was observed to not be in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that they do not have certification however, will be getting the training done soon. Ensure that CFPMs receive allergen training to be in compliance with the LAW. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed jalapeños stored in an open can in the walk in cooler. The person in charge stated the can was opened yesterday. CORRECTED- education about storage of acidic foods in metal cans was conducted, and the jalapeños were transferred to a food safe container. Ensure acidic foods held past the day of opening are stored in a food safe container if held past one day, to ensure no metals leach into the food.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.[P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed one container of cooked ground beef to bear the date 3/27, and another container to have no date in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- the person in charge verified that the beef was cooked on Wednesday (4/1), and wrote the date to reflect. Ensure all temperature control for food safety items are marked with the day of preparation, to be used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation/ thawing/ opening counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed shrimp thawing in a metal container at room temperature. CORRECTED- the person in charge moved food under cold running water, which was later transferred to the prep table, to be cooked today. Ensure use of proper thawing methods, which includes placing the items under cold running water, moving to refrigeration, or cooking to the items to the minimum internal cooking temperature (145F for shrimp).
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F). [Pf]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled container of a white grainy substance. CORRECTED- staff confirmed the item as salt, and placed a label to reflect the containers contents. Ensure foods that may easily be mistaken for other foods and chemicals are labeled after removing from their original container to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) in the facility at the start of the inspection. This was discussed with the PIC. Both operators are CFPMs and they arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were two containers of raw cut chicken breast observed to be above two whole cuts of beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The chicken was moved to a different shelf, where it was not above the beef. Ensure that staff are educated on storage order to protect food from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: There were refried black beans that were probed to be at 121F on the hot holding line. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that the refried black beans were reheated this morning and the black beans were reheated on the stove. The refried black beans were probed to be at 184F on the stove. Ensure that hot food is being held at 135F or above. Ensure that staff are educated to reheat food items to 165F before placing them in hot holding.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were multiple food items in the walk-in cooler and in the preparation coolers in the kitchen that were not date-marked, including a container of beans that was made two days ago, a container of pico de gallo that was made yesterday, and a container of cooked meat. CORRECTED- The food items were date-marked and the PIC educated the staff on proper date-marking. Ensure that staff are date-marking TCS food items that are opened or prepared in-house, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day, if they are held for more than 24 hours. A spot check is scheduled for 4/13/2026 to ensure that staff are properly date-marking TCS food items.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of birria in the walk-in cooler that had a date of 3/21 on it. There were also two containers of salsa that had a date of 3/9 on them. CORRECTED- All of the food items were discarded and the PIC educated the employees that food items made in-house need to be discarded after 7 days. Ensure that TCS food items that are prepared or made in-house are being date-marked and are being discarded by the end of the 7th day. Think day 1 being the date of opening or preparation + 6 days for a total of 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed scooping ice with a single service cup using their bare hands. Education was carried out. The ice was discarded and the container cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that employees are educated and reminded to always use gloves when handling ready to eat food items. Moreover, ensure that employees use the scoop to dip ice from the bins to fill cups for drinks.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The internal surfaces of the coffee and tea makers and the frappe machine were observed with soil accumulations. Discussed with PIC. The tea and coffee makers and frappe machine were immediately cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned above are constantly monitored, cleaned, and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sani buckets were measured at 0 ppm at the beginning of today’s inspection. PIC was made aware. PIC instructed a staff member to remake the sani buckets. The sani buckets were remade and tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that the sanitizer concentration is routinely checked throughout the day.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness.
