A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed mop buckets being stored improperly with dirty water in them as well as the mop heads. PIC was made aware of the proper storing procedures and actions were taken to get this violation corrected. Ensure that staff are aware of the proper procedures for storing mop heads and the disposal wastewater.
citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled. 
1. The internal surface of other coffee maker was observed with an accumulation of soil.
2. The ice machine baffles was observed with an accumulation of pink and black molds.
PIC was made aware. PIC instructed employees to stop using the ice in the ice machine. The coffee maker was also cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. The ice was discarded and PIC commenced cleaning and sanitizing the ice machine. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ice machine baffles and the surface of the coffee makers are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking above the counter top on the right side of the dish machine was observed coming off the wall. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the counter top will be re-caulked to the wall. Ensured that this area is sealed to the wall properly to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: One employee on the cook line was observed to touch their clothes with their gloved hands without washing hands or changing gloves. Inspector witnessed multiple incidences of task changing without hand washing. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all food employees are washing their hands before donning gloves and are changing their gloves after touching body parts.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed multiple cans of marinara dented along the seams. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the cans from service to be returned to the supplier. Ensure cans are frequently checked for dents along the seams to prevent the entry and harborage of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 2 sanitizer buckets and the sanitizer at the bar triple sink to be between 0-100 ppm of quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- buckets were remade at a proper concentration (200 ppm). Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at frequency to maintain the sanitizer concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed both bar soda nozzles and soda gun holders to be soiled. CORRECTED- Employees cleaned and sanitized the food contact surfaces. Ensure soda nozzles and the soda gun holder are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation. Food contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the door between the walk in cooler and walk in freezer to contain a sizable gap, and the gaskets to be loose. The PIC stated a new frame is being ordered. Ensure the door is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIRD REPEAT: The wire shelving in the walk in cooler is soiled and rusted. Inspector discussed getting shelf liners, cleaning/ painting, or replacing shelves. The PIC stated they will be ordering new shelving. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The hood baffles and fire suppression system were observed to contain an accumulation of grease drips and debris. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination to ready to eat (RTE) foods, and can serve as a fire hazard. Ensure the hood vent system and baffles are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods to bare no date. The person in charge (PIC) stated the items were opened (half and half) and prepared (tomato sauce) within the past two days. CORRECTED- the PIC placed the correct dates on the food items. Ensure all TCS items are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days- the day of preparation counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The PIC does not have allergen awareness training. Inspector will email the PIC a website to obtain Allergen training. Obtain training by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed an employee repeatedly tap knife on the surface of the trash can in the midst of prepping avocados. The practice was ceased and corrected on site. The kitchen manager discussed proper food handling with the employee and the knife was sanitized during the visit. Ensure that clean food contact surfaces are sanitized whenever cross contamination occurs.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility is in full operation and no sanitizer buckets were available. Discussed with the person-in-charge and two sanitizer buckets were prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are available at all times if food prep is occurring.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are being frequently tested and changed if not at the label-recommended concentration. It is typically recommended to change sanitizer buckets every two to four hours, depending on how often it is used. Ensure that staff are educated that sanitizer buckets should be made before food preparation or cooking begins.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There were no Quaternary ammonium sanitizer test strips available in the facility. The facility uses Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tablets for their sanitizer buckets. A follow up is scheduled for 4/10/2026 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. Ensure that there are always test strips available for every type of sanitizer used in the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on duty is observed to not have their Allergen awareness training certificate. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on duty who has their Allergen awareness training certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) If used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The blade of the can opener was observed soiled during this inspection. Staff indicated that the item had not been used yet today, indicating that it was left soiled overnight (or longer). The PIC was shown and moved the can opener to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact equipment are cleaned regularly throughout the day (at least every four hours).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Two moist wiping cloths are observed on different surfaces. Education was conducted and the cloths moved to their sani buckets to correct. Ensure that all wiping rags are stored between uses in the relevant sanitizer of sufficient concentration.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following canned foods on the shelves were observed to have dents:
1. La costena refried beans has significant dent on the body.
2. Cheddar cheese sauce has significant dents on the body (x2).
3. Red enchilada sauce has significant dents on the body (x3).
4. Clover valley pinto beans has significant dents on the body and around the seam.
5. Premium cheddar has significant dent on the body.
6. Campbells spaghettios and meat balls has dents around the seam and significantly on the body.
7. County style baked beans has significant dent on the body.
8. Clover valley sliced carrots has significant dent on the body.

CORRECTED - The operator was informed and the dented cans were voluntarily removed from the shelf. Dented cans can have entry and harborage of Botulism, ensure canned foods with dents are removed from the shelves and not sold to customers.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.

citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Under the shelled eggs tray in the third fresh food cooler was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The bottom of the diary cooler at the back storage was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The fan vents in the three fresh food coolers were observed to have dust accumulation. The dust accumulation on the fan vents in the second fresh food cooler are significant and almost covering the vents.
4. The nestle ice cream chest freezer was observed to have significant ice buildup.

The operator was instructed to have those surfaces clean. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of soil and dust accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The employee restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. The inspector instructed the operator to ensure hot water is provided at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. A follow-up (re-inspection) will be conducted on April 13, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Dirty water from mopping was observed in two mop buckets by the mop sink. CORRECTED - The operator was informed and educated by the inspector and the mop buckets were voluntarily emptied. Dirty water from mopping the facility should be discarded when not actively in use.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. comment: Steaks were observed being stored above fish and shrimp in the standing cooler on the far end of the wall right of the cook line. Education was carried out. citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employee was observed not using a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing. PIC was made aware and education carried out. Ensure that employees are reminded to always use a barrier to shut the faucet after handwashing handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

comment: Employee was observed bare handling slices of ready to eat bread and pizza. Education was carried out. Employee donned gloves appropriately. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable about not bare handling ready to eat food items before serving.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed multiple container of white powders on storage shelves in one of the prep area. Inquiries were made and education carried out. The containers were label appropriately. Ensure that containers holding white powders of any kind are properly labeled.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The internal surface of the microwave was observed with an accumulation of soil and food debris. PIC was made aware. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces of equipments that are exposed to splash and spillage are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed eggs to be stored above noodles in cooler. Discussed with PIC, eggs were relocated to the bottom shelf in cooler. Ensure proper storage order is bing maintained to be prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed a container of open single service utensils to have a pen resting inside. Discussed with PIC, education on proper storage of single service utensils was provided. Utensils were discarded and pen was moved to another location. Ensure all single service utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during all hours of operation. Discussed with PIC, manager arrived during inspection. Ensure a certified food manager is present within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.

citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers training to have been completed by staff during inspection. Discussed with PIC, staff will take the steps to have the required food handlers license. Ensure any staff member that handles food has the required food handlers license available within the facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: SECOND REPEAT- The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC stated that the other PIC is currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to use their gloved hands to roll their sleeves of their shirt up and continued to prepare food using the soiled gloves. CORRECTED- Handwashing education was conducted with the PIC and the employee. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable of when to wash their hands and change gloves to avoid contaminating food.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility has failed to obtain in-date test strips. The inspector will continue to schedule follow up inspections until the facility has obtained an in-date test kit to verify proper chemical sanitizing concentration. Fees for scheduled follow up inspections increase with each occurrance.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed a container of onion crunch topping to be stored with no protective covering. The container had package labeling sitting inside of the container contacting the food. The PIC was informed and the item was discarded. Ensure containers remain covered to prevent items from accidentally contaminating food surfaces.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a sanitizing cloth stored directly on the food contact surface of the sushi prep table. The PIC was informed and the cloth was moved to the sanitizer bucket. Ensure wet cloths are stored in sanitizing solution to prevent microbial growth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the condensation catch canister of the rice cooker to be soiled with a pink residue. The PIC was informed and the item was moved to the dish area. Inspector also observed the gaskets of the coolers under the rice cooker to be heavily soiled. Ensure all parts of the rice cooker and coolers are washed and sanitized frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed ice and a dark beverage in the kitchen hand sink. The PIC was informed that hand sinks cannot be used for dumping drinks. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for handwashing only and a utility sink is used for dumping drinks. The sink was rinsed and sanitized during the inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed there is a buildup of debris on the ice machine baffles. The PIC was reminded that food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soil residues. The inspector will follow-up on 10 April 2026 to check that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed that the concentration of the sanitizer bucket (quat) in the right serving area was low (100ppm). The PIC was notified, and inspectors educated that the sanitizer solution (sourced from the triple sink) may need to run for additional time to reach the correct concentration. The PIC remade the sanitizer solution for the bucket and it tested at 200pm (quat). Sanitizing solution should be tested frequently to confirm it is at an effective sanitizing concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed that the caulking behind the chemical dishwasher area and the neighboring triple sink between the equipment and the wall was in disrepair. PIC was informed of the issue, and assured inspectors that the necessary repairs will be done by the next routine inspection. It is important that all food surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple employees don gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED- education about times to wash hands was reviewed with staff. All employees should wash hands prior to donning gloves to engage in food handling, and after engaging in any activity which may contaminate hands to prevent the contamination of foods.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the serving line hand washing sink being used as a dump sink when preparing a new sanitizer buckets (see violation #16). CORRECTED- education was conducted about the usage of hand washing sinks. Ensure all sinks designated for hand washing are used for hand washing ONLY- so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed with no measurable chlorine concentration after 3 runs of the dish machine. The person in charge (PIC) called their service provider and prepared the triple sink for sanitation in the meantime. CORRECTED- The dish machine was observed to dispense 100 ppm Chlorine after the service provider replaced the sanitizer. Ensure staff knows how to change chemical sanitizer. Test the dish machine at least once daily to ensure proper sanitation of food contact surfaces. Due to the history of this dish machine failing to meet sanitation concentrations/ temperatures, inspector highly recommends keeping a log of daily sanitizer concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).  [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The quaternary ammonia sanitizer buckets along the line (used for food contact surfaces) were observed to be at a low concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer buckets were remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia, 50-200 ppm for Chlorine- the active ingredient in bleach).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed the only (2) tubes of quaternary ammonia test strips within the facility to be expired. The facility uses quaternary ammonia for chemical sanitation of food contact surfaces within the triple sink and sanitizer buckets. CORRECTED- the chemical service provider who serviced the dish machine (see violation #16) gave the facility in-date test strips. Ensure chemicals used for sanitation of food contact surfaces have an in-date test kit to verify proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed caulking on the left side of the kitchen’s (first) hand washing sink to be fragmented. Seal the sink to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold by the next routine inspection. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
One employee was observed to have an expired food handler certificate, and multiple other employees on staff during today’s inspection did not have Food Handler Certificates. All employees who participate in any degree of food handling must obtain a Food Handlers Certificate within 30 days of hire, to be maintained every 3 years. The Inspector provided a list of ANSI-approved food handler courses to the PIC. Ensure all staff who have not completed a Certified Food Protection Manager’s course obtain Food Handlers by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Due to this violation being a third repeat violation, this violation is now on compliance conference. A follow up is scheduled on 4/3/2026 to ensure that all employees who are not CFPMs have obtained their food handler certificate, or according to Colleen Kelley, the Director of Environmental Health, the permit for the facility will be suspended. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-102.11(A) Demonstration. The operators present were unaware of many of the nuances associated with safe food handling. In particular, storage order, hand washing, sanitizing, and cleaning seemed to be lacking. The facility will have several opportunities to correct the violations observed during today’s inspection. The follow-up with this violation will occur in over a month to ensure discussions and educations resulting from today are being properly applied to the daily operations. It would be of benefit to have all staff participate in the certified food managers course. The knowledge gained during that course can only help with safe food handling. 


Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [PF]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The operator informed the inspector that the owner of the facility was not available to provide the signed copies. The inspector also gave blank copies to the operator. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 04/06/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
citation_text:
2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. Personal products are being stored throughout the kitchen (see violation #56) but there is a half-used drinking bottle of water on the right side of the preparation cooler. Cease storing personal products in various areas throughout the kitchen (inclusive of clothing and other sundries). See that personal beverages are being stored on the shelf adjacent to the hand sink so that hands may be properly washed after taking a drink. 

An employee may drink from a closed container with a lid and a straw and then return to work. Any other cup, can, or bottle needs to be followed with a hand washing occasion. 
Discussed storage of personal foods. The space should be re-evaluated to account for the minimal space and the volume of personal items present. Use a cup with a lid and straw or store the bottle by the hand sink. 

(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT - 2-301.14 When to Wash. Observed an employee donning gloves without a proper hand washing occasion. The operator was previously in the walk-in cooler and moving boxes of items. Halted the behavior of donning gloves and requested the staff member wash hands. Proper hand washing technique was observed. 
In addition, the operators were later observed changing gloves and moving items at the request of inspectors without washing hands. The scene became hectic as inspectors were requesting information while food was being prepared, but hand washing opportunities should not be missed. 

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. Portion cups are being used as scoops in the seasoning containers by the service counter. See that proper scoops with a handle are available for use. Store the scoop so the handle is presented out of the food. Avoid allowing hands to touch the product. 
Follow-up is occurring on 4/6/26 due to the availability of the inspector. 


(B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed a grocery bag being used to hold seasonings. Grocery bags are not approved for direct food contact and should not be used as a storage device. Cease storing spices in grocery sacks. 
(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed multiple instances of improper storage. The walk-in cooler has chicken over fish. Fish over butter. Chicken over beef. And Chicken over cut green peppers. The walk-in cooler is small for the amount of food present. See that storage is corrected to allow for proper storage: washed and cut produce, over unwashed produce, over fish, beef/pork, chicken, and then personal foods on the bottom. Change storage of foods to prevent the potential for cross-contamination. 


 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Boxes of food are observed being stored on the floor of the walk-in freezer. Operator moved the foods during the inspection. Again, storage and organization must be maintained to keep this small space working properly. 


(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. There was not a sanitizing bucket available to store in-use wiping cloths. A bucket was created during the inspection and test strips were available to check the concentration of the product. See that sani-buckets are available for the operators to store their wet wiping cloths within the solution between uses. 

 A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. The interior of the microwave is observed soiled with food from repeated use. Clean the interior of the microwave. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. A half dozen baked potatoes were observed in a container atop the microwave by the fryers. A potato was probed at 76F. The potato that was probed was discarded. The product is going to be held using TIME AS CONTROL. Discussed with operator the need to identify the time the food was created and then control for FOUR HOURS. The baked potatoes were created at 11am, so they would need to be discarded by 3pm. 

And then, 3:30pm arrived and inspectors returned to the kitchen to see that the potatoes were discarded. The inspectors observed that the potatoes had been discarded by the operator. A discussion was again held with the operators that upgrading to a Class I permit would allow for foods to be cooled and reheated. The ideal handling for the baked potatoes are to cook several, cool, and then store in the preparation cooler. That would eliminate the counter storage. 

The four hours rule is not the best option for a facility that cannot control the time. 


 (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Observed two boxes of chicken wings stored on a counter to the right as you enter the kitchen. Wings were present during the inspection without being addressed. The operators were busy with a steady lunch rush. When questioned, the operators indicated the foods were brought from another store two hours prior. The chicken wings were probed at 56F. The boxes were quickly moved into the walk-in cooler for proper cold holding. Discussed NOT storing foods on the counter for future handling during busy periods. Move foods out of temperature control as they are going to be handled. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. No foods within the facility are noted to have date marking present. There were multiple cooked foods in the walk-in cooler and bulk foods in the preparation cooler that could have potentially carried a date mark. See that foods held longer than 24 hours are dated with the date foods are opened. This includes the cooked gyro meat, sausages and hot dogs, and any prepared foods. 
Raw proteins do NOT need a date marking. 

(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. The available bleach is not approved for food contact surfaces. Discussed using a product that is USEPA registered. Provide a proper chemical for sanitizing. Operator indicated that the kitchen should have one bleach for sanitizing and one for floors, walls, and ceilings. This was not observed. Only one type of bleach was present and it did not meet the requirements. 

Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the walk-in cooler and 2 door cooler by the window. The operator was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each of the coolers to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
citation_text:
3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. The dry storage shelving is full of bulk containers of white powders and other seasonings without common name labeling. Label white powders and clear liquids with common name.

The cheese cake in the dessert cooler is not labeled. Provide ingredient labeling to be available for the general public should they ask for contents. 

Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. Observed several uncovered containers of food in the walk-in cooler contained amongst soiled shelving. Clean the shelving of the walk-in cooler and see that foods are properly covered while in storage.  

(A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(D) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. No sani-bucket was available for wiping cloth storage. Wiping cloths are observed on counters around the kitchen. Sani-bucket was created during the inspection and wiping cloths were told to be stored within the bucket. 

 (D) Dry wiping cloths and the chemical sanitizing solutions specified in Subparagraph (B)(1) of this section in which wet wiping cloths are held between uses shall be free of FOOD debris and visible soil. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. A single-service tin container is observed stored on the bottom shelf of the dry storage rack holding seasonings and spills from the upper shelving. The single-service pan is not inverted and thus is open to storage of all spilled foods. Discard this container. 

(C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Ice accumulation was observed on the plumbing line in the walk-in freezer. The operator was instructed to ensure the plumbing line is cleaned to sight and touch and kept free of ice buildup.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan covers in the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer were observed to have dust accumulation. 
2. The 2-door cooler by window was observed to have soil accumulation
3. SECOND REPEAT - The hood above the fryer and the side of the fryer were observed to have soil and grease accumulation.

The inspector instructed the operator to ensure the non-food contact surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas in the facility were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The ceiling tiles and air return above the drink shelf were observed to have dust accumulation.
2. The floor area beneath the storage table by the water heater was observed to have grease and soil accumulation.
3. Ice buildup was observed on the floor in the walk-in freezer.
4. Food debris was observed on the floor area between the water heater by the mop sink and the storage table.
5. The floor drain was observed to be soiled.
6. The plumbing at the triple sink was observed to be soiled.
7. The wall at the triple was observed to have soil accumulation.
8. The ceiling tiles and air return above the storage table by the water heater were observed to have dust accumulation.

The inspector instructed the operator to ensure these areas are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment:
Pants and coats belonging to employees were observed to be stored on the dry storage rack for spices. The operator was instructed to move the pants and coats away from foods items used for customers in order to prevent contamination.

The inspector also observed the employees’ foods were stored with food items used for customers in the walk-in cooler. The inspector instructed the operator to ensure employee foods are stored at the bottom of the cooler, away from foods for customers.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Two employees handling foods were observed to not have food handlers’ certificates. The operator was instructed to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness notice
comment:
The facility has no allergy notice available. Allergen declaration notice was provided during their inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.08(a). Food Allergy awareness. (a) A restaurant shall display a notice indicating to consumers that any information regarding food allergies must be communicated to an employee of the restaurant. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The blue container for holding ice scoop in the women’s locker was observed to have water and soil accumulation.
2. Dust accumulation was observed in an unsealed opening behind the hood light fixtures.

The inspector instructed the person-in-charge to ensure the non-food contact surfaces are cleaned and kept free of dust, water and soil accumulations.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer solution to test at greater than 200 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bottle was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer solution is available and at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed leak to be present at the bottom of front prep cooler. Discussed with PIC, cooler will be serviced. Ensure equipment is maintained to be working up to the manufactures standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed prep cooler to be soiled with small amounts of food debris accumulation under lid. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler lid will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed triple sink to have a leak present from faucet. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced. Ensure a licensed plumber services triple sink and that no leak is present.
citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(Repeat x2) Observed the following require repairs:

(1) The wall panel holding the paper towel dispenser at the front hand washing sink is lifting up on the left side. The panel needs to be sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

Ensure these locations are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed multiple dented cans to be present in dry storage area. Discussed with PIC, cans were pulled and will be discarded. Ensure facility is checking for dented cans at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a container of milk and multiple containers of nuts to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper dates marking practices. Dates were placed on the milk, and the bags of nuts were discarded. Ensure any TCS item kept longer than 24 hours is properly date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed multiple food items to be stored on the floor in walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, items will be moved to an approved location. Ensure any food item is kept at least 6 inches off of ground to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed shelving unit in dish room to have plates not inverted with no proper covering available. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper equipment/utensil storage. Plates and utensils were run through dish machine, and were then returned to shelf in an inverted manner. Ensure any equipment/utensil being stored in a shelving unit is either covered or inverted to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed 2 sanitizer buckets to be at a concentration of 50 ppm Quat. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer buckets were dumped and remade and tested to be 200 ppm Quat. Ensure all sanitizer buckets are prepared at the proper sanitation level and are being replaced roughly every 4 hours.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the lobby juice dispenser nozzles to be soiled with juice splash/buildup. Discussed with PIC, nozzles will be removed and put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. Ensure food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination/buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair to the right of the dish machine and at the mop sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents caulking from getting damaged.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment:
Repeat Violation

The wiping cloth that was being used to wipe food-contact surfaces was observed to be stored on the counter. This was discussed with the PIC and a bucket was recommended, as they often use the sanitizer from the Schnuck’s deli’s triple sink. CORRECTED- The PIC filled a sanitizer bucket and was educated that the wiping cloth should be stored in chemical sanitizer in between uses to prevent bacteria growth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the utility sink in the sushi area to be pulled away from the wall and leaning. Ensure the sink is repaired and sealed to the wall prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution present in the kitchen during the inspection. PIC was informed and a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure sanitizer is available at all times of food preparation or service.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the ice machine to be soiled with a black residue inside the machine. The interior of the ice machine is considered a food contact surface, and should therefore be clean to sight and touch at all times. A follow-up is scheduled for 4/6/2026 to ensure the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized. Inspector recommends hiring a third party such as AirMasters to deep clean and sanitize the machine.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspectors observed ham and shredded mozzarella cheese to be stored in the white upright cooler without a proper date mark. The PIC was informed and dates were added to the necessary items.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed the scoop of the ice machine to be stored on a surface that is not clean to sight and touch. The PIC was informed and will place scoop on a dish that can be properly ware washed and sanitized in the future. Ensure this scoop is properly stored in the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment:
There has been a history of falsifying pH logs for the acidified sushi rice. See violation #29 for further details. The PIC has continuously falsified data logged within record logs.This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to ensure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. 

PIC has not demonstrated knowledge of food safety practices. PIC has continued to operate without essential equipment (pH meter) or other interim measures in place.
