Operator was noted to have falsified data logged within record logs. This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to insure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. See violations below.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
comment:
It is evident that the PIC is falsifying pH records. The PIC noted two pH recordings, however, one of the recordings had been pre written for a future time (9:59am). Discussed with the PIC that falsifying records is against the facility’s HACCP Plan and also inaccurate record keeping. Ensure that pH records are accurate and never falsified. Will follow-up on April 6, 2026 to ensure that records are being correctly monitored by the PIC. 

Logs and discussion with the PIC indicate sushi rice pH and pH meter logs have been falsified. Logs reflect that the pH meter has been calibrated and sushi pH measured over the last week despite the lack of a functional pH meter in the facility. Staff must record accurate HACCP records. Inspector will follow up to see that accurate logs are maintained.
citation_text: 8-103.12(C) Conformance with Approved Procedures. If the REGULATORY AUTHORITY grants a VARIANCE as specified in § 8-103.10, or a HACCP PLAN is otherwise required as specified under § 8-201.13, the PERMIT HOLDER shall: (C) Maintain and provide to the regulatory authority, upon request, records specified under § 8-201.14 (D) and (E)(3) that demonstrate that the following are routinely employed; (1) Procedures for monitoring the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (2) Monitoring of the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (3) Verification of the effectiveness of the operation or process, and (4) Necessary corrective actions if there is failure at a CRITICAL CONTROL POINT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed prep cooler in the production room to be soiled under the lid behind stored items, the containers holding disposable cutlery to be soiled, and the container for the ice scoops was observed soiled with moisture residue. The PIC was informed and the areas were cleaned with a clean cloth and sanitizer.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed the gasket of the “HB2” cooler to have an accumulation of soil. The PIC was informed and the gasket was cleaned during the inspection. 

Inspectors also observed the hood baffles to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure baffles are cleaned frequently to prevent debris from falling into food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the hand sink in the hot kitchen to be separating from the wall. Ensure this sink is repaired to be sealed to the wall tightly to prevent moisture accumulation between the sink and wall.

The hand sink in the front bathroom was also observed to be missing sealant between the sink and wall. Silicone sealant will prevent moisture accumulation and microbial growth.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, recontaminating the hands in the process. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to refresh hand washing procedures with staff. Ensure proper hand washing takes place at all times in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: No disposable towel or hand drying device was observed in the two restrooms. CORRECTED: The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and paper towels were provided. Ensure paper towels are available in the restrooms at all times for proper hand drying and to allow employees to turn off faucets without recontaminating clean hands. This is the third observation within one month of paper towels not being available in the restrooms (March 6, March 16 and March 26).
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [PF]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizer bucket (quaternary ammonia) for food contact surfaces to be at a low concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer bucket was remade to 400 ppm. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made and tested at a frequency to reach the sanitizing concentration for food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonia).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed the ambient thermometer in the under counter cooler to be broken. Ensure all cooling units holding temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods contain a working ambient thermometer to monitor cold holding temperatures. Obtain an ambient thermometer for this unit by 4/6/26.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: A bin of water was observed in the walk-in cooler on the top shelf directly across from the door. There is a small drip from the vent in the ceiling. Repair the cooler to eliminate the leak. See that condensation drainage is discharged and is not dripping back into the walk-in cooler.
citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the self closer to the men’s restroom to be nonfunctioning. Ensure the self closer is repaired by the next routine inspection. Restrooms should have functioning self closing doors to protect against food contamination.
citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Several physical facilities violations have remained from the pre-opening:
1) 2ND REPEAT: Acoustic tiles were observed above the passageway between the cold line and the kitchen. Eliminate use of acoustic tiles. Replace them with vinyl coated or wipeable tiles.
2) 2ND REPEAT: Replace broken floor tiles by mop sink & grease trap. Broken tiles allow buildup of general debris and water.
3) FIRST REPEAT: Several holes were observed in the wall behind the 3 compartment sink. Fill or patch any holes.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Multiple areas within the physical facilities were observed to have coving separating from the wall:
1) 2ND REPEAT:the wall near the entrance to the kitchen.
2) To the left of the hand washing sink (nearest the register). 
3) To the left of the mop sink
4) On the side counter between the soda machine and self service drink cooler.
Ensure coving is sealed to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a significant accumulation of food and other soil debris on the floor drain beneath the 3 compartment sink. Physical facilities should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Discussed doing an initial deep clean, then maintaining cleanliness every 2 weeks. Floor drains are a significant source of harborage for pests.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspector observed one dim light present in the facility’s walk in cooler. Replace this lightbulb to display an intensity of at least 108 lux by the next routine inspection. Food areas must be adequately lit.
citation_text: 6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning; [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM certificate was not available at the facility. The PIC indicated that several employees had taken the course/test but were unable to provide certificates for verification. The situation was discussed and options for getting the certificates from ServeSafe given. Ensure that certificates are available for the CFPMs/PICs at the facility prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) If used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The blade of the can opener was observed soiled with dry food debris. When asked the PIC indicated that it had not been used that day, indicating that it was not properly cleaned the day before. Education was conducted and the PIC moved the can opener to dish to remedy the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned correctly and often.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be thawed: (A-E) Using an approved method. 

A log of ground beef is observed in standing water in a sink. When asked an employee indicated that it was thawing in cold water for later service. This is not an approved method. The PIC was consulted and education conducted. Ensure that the TCS foods are thawed in a safe manner in the facility. The log was prepared during the inspection to correct.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple ladles stored hanging at the west side of the kitchen were observed soiled with food debris. The PIC indicated that it was likely caused by the pizza racks being stored on the shelf above. This is likely, but the food contact surfaces must be protected from contamination prior to use. Moving the ladles or the racks are both viable options to remedy the situation. The contaminated ladles were moved to dish for cleaning to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are protected from contamination prior to use in the facility.

title: Food handler training
comment:
(REEPAT) 410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Food Handler Certificates were unavailable for multiple employees on staff during today’s inspection. Ensure all food service staff obtain a Food Handler’s certificate to be made available during future inspections. Inspector provided guidance on where to find ANSI-approved Food Handler’s certificate Courses.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed passing through the gap beneath the exit door in the dinning area.The inspector advised the person-in-charge (PIC) to use a weather stripping to seal the gap so as to prevent entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Dust accumulation was observed on the fan covers in both walk-in coolers.
2. Soil accumulation (icy shade) was observed beneath the fan casing in the walk-in coolers by the dish self.

The inspector instructed the PIC to have the fan covers and fan casing cleaned to sight and touch so as to prevent contamination of foods stored in the walk-in cooler.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no soap to be available at bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was brought to hand sink. Ensure hand sinks are properly supplied with soap to prevent ay possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a container of pizza sauce to be held past its 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, sauce was from an old system facility was using. Sauce was discarded and education was provided on date marking policy. Ensure any TCS item kept longer and 7 days is discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed 2 chemical spray bottles to be resting on the same shelf as drinks behind the bar. Discussed with PIC, bottles were relocated to an approved location. Ensure all chemicals are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed ice scoop to be resting on the top of ice machine with a thin layer of dust present. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was put through the wash, rinse, sanitizer process and placed in a clean container. Ensure in use utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(E) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(E) In a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is not time/temperature control for safety food.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set at the bar upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a chemicals sanitizer solution is prepared and available at both the bar and kitchen during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice scoop handle to be in contact with ice in ice machine. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was moved to an approved location. Ensure ice scoop is not in contact with ice to prevent any possible contaminantion.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS foods being kept in walk in cooler that were kept longer than there 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed 2 clean ladles to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, ladles were pulled and put through the wash, rinse, sanitize process. Ensure all utensils are properly cleaned to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop in the bar area was observed with the scoop handle in contact with the ice. This allows for bare hand contact with the Ready-To-Eat (RTE) food (ice) when picking it up. The PIC was notified and moved the scoop to correct. Ensure that all RTE foods are protected from bare hand contact at all times in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: After almost completing the handwashing process, an employee was observed drying his hands with the same paper towel he used to turn off the faucet handles. Educated staff and the employee on proper handwashing to correct the violation. Ensure that a fresh towel is used to dry hands after discarding the hand towel used to operate faucet handles.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was an opened can of ketchup on the top shelf above the preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- An employee switched the ketchup into another container. Educated the employees on transferring highly acid foods to a different can to prevent corrosion after opening, especially if the food item is acidic, such as ketchup or tomato sauce. Ensure that food packages are in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
SECOND REPEAT- The inspectors observed multiple incidents of improper storage order in the facility’s cold holding units:

1. There was a pan of raw shrimp above packages of cooked crawfish in the bottom of a kitchen preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The raw shrimp was placed below the cooked crawfish. 
2. There was a container of marinated raw beef stored above a container of cooked chicken in a standing double-door cooler. CORRECTED- The marinated raw beef was moved to be below the container of cooked chicken. 
3. There was a container of breaded raw fish above a box of ready-to-eat eggrolls in a standing cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The eggrolls were moved to be above the container of breaded raw fish. 
4. There were several containers of raw meats or seafood stored above other raw meats with higher cooking temperatures inside of the walk in cooler. CORRECTED - the containers were rearranged during the visit

Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order. There are multiple storage order handouts posted in the facility.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffle of the ice machine in the sushi area was observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on the outer surface. Discussed with the PIC and the baffle was sanitized to correct the violation. Additionally, the blade of the can opener was observed heavily soiled with dried debris. The can opener was placed through the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that surfaces that come in contact with foods are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizing dispenser at the triple sink wasn't functioning properly. The PIC mentioned that the water isn't pulling through the lines to mix with the quaternary ammonium compound. The facility mostly uses the dish machine to sanitize dishes and bleach is used in their sanitizers buckets, however, the triple sink is sometimes used to sanitize dishes. Ensure that the plumbing is repaired to allow for the water and sanitizer to dispense proportionately. Will follow-up on April 6, 2026 to ensure that the plumbing has been repaired.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was a container of teriyaki sauce by the hibachi cook-line that was observed to be sitting at room temperature. The label states to “Refrigerate After Opening”. The PIC stated that the bottle was opened yesterday, as they typically go through a bottle a day. The PIC and Kitchen Manager were educated that the teriyaki sauce needs to be refrigerated after opening. CORRECTED- The teriyaki sauce was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are being held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed a container of bean sprouts held on an ice bath to be improperly placed on ice. The bottom of the container was stored on the surface of the ice. The inspector demonstrated  how to properly place containers on ice to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Violation corrected on site. Be sure to educate employees on how to effectively create an ice bath for TCS foods to maintain a temperature of 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
The following items were observed in containers different from its original container:
- Teriyaki sauce stored in a 5 gallon bucket that reads “soy sauce”
- Soy sauce in a bucket that reads “teriyaki sauce”

Discussed with PIC that items that are transferred from its original container must clearly state the food product. Be sure to label food with the correct name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: One of the double door coolers in the kitchen is observed to have one missing handle that has a string attached to it to allow them to open the door. The other handle on the cooler is observed to be crushed and in disrepair. Ensure that these handles are properly repaired. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
There was observed to be a scoop that was made from the top of a milk gallon bottle. CORRECTED- The scoop was discarded and the staff was educated that food-contact utensils should be durable, able to withstand repeated warewashing, and are smooth and easily cleanable. The staff were educated to use a proper scoop that is intended for use with food. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The shelves of the double-door cooler (also missing handles) are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. This was shown to the PIC, who stated that they will clean the shelves tonight. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are being cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: There wasn't any hot water available in the men’s bathroom. The PIC mentioned that a knob must’ve been mistakenly switched to stop the flow of hot water. Warm water became available during the inspection. Ensure that hot water is available to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The caulking of the handwashing sink in the hibachi and sushi preparation area is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. Ensure that this caulking is re-done and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. There is a gap between the caulking of the handwashing sink by the main cook-line in the kitchen and the wall. Ensure that this caulking is re-done and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. The handwashing sink in the dish room and the triple sink is in need of recaulking. The current caulk has pulled away from the wall. Ensure that these sinks are recaulked. 
4. There is tape being used as a repair mechanism on the wall behind the hibachi cold-holding. Ensure that the crack in the wall is properly repaired. Tape is not an approved repair mechanism.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several utensils in storage were observed with remaining food debris on them. The PIC confirmed that the storage location should be clean items and moved the entire container back to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage in the facility. It is highly suggested that the employees that conduct dish washing procedures be re-educated to ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage moving forward.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No certified food protection manager (CFPM) was available during the inspection. The inspector advised the person-in-charge (PIC) to get certified in food protection management so that a CFPM is available during all hours of food preparation/operation. The director of the program is certified but shares some time with Nokomis schools. See that more than one person is certified within the facility. Operator present during the inspection has a certificate that just expired on March 2. She intends to retake the course and test sometime within the next week.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. The facility dish machine operator had no knowledge of testing the heat sanitizing dish machine using a maximum registering thermometer. An image of the device was shared with the dish operator. See that the facility purchases and uses (daily) the thermometer to insure the accuracy of the dish machine. Operator knew to check the display to ensure the rinse temperature was at least 180F.
(A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The fan cover in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation. The PIC was informed to ensure the fan cover is cleaned to sight and touch and kept free of dust. Furthermore, the two box fans being used in the facility (dish and kitchen) are also observed soiled. See that these fans are cleaned prior to use. Do not allow soiled air to flow over the kitchen space.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. No food handler cards were available for present staff. Only one employee was recently hired. See that all staff are either certified food managers or food handlers as required. There should be one certified food managers present during all hours of operations. Anyone else should have the food handlers card. 

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a significant accumulation of soil debris on the soda nozzles at both the grill and server station. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Discussed more intensive cleaning process than soaking overnight moving forward. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf[

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed plates in the grill and assisted living area facing upwards without a covering. CORRECTED- plates were moved under a covering or inverted. Ensure food contact surfaces are protected from contamination by storing inverted or under a covering.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following physical facilities in need of cleaning or repair:
1) The caulking to the right of the kitchen’s dish machine is separating. Reseal to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
2) The fans of the walk in cooler contain an accumulation of dust. Dust may travel to contamination nonfood and food contact surfaces.
Ensure these items are cleaned and repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed opened milk containers in both the Reach and Spring kitchen to be missing date marking. The person in charge (PIC) verified that they were opened within the past 1-2 days. CORRECTED- the date the items were opened was placed on the containers. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked if held for over 24 hours. The date of opening/ preparation/ thawing counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed an unmarked bottle of clear liquid in the mop room of the Spring kitchen. The PIC was unable to verify the contents. CORRECTED- the bottle was emptied and brought to the main kitchen for ware washing. Ensure all clear liquids, chemicals, and cleaning products are labeled to prevent potential chemical contamination of foods or food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf[

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility has failed to obtain in-date test strips. The inspector will continue to schedule follow up inspections until the facility has obtained an in-date test kit to verify proper chemical sanitizing concentration. Fees for scheduled follow up inspections increase with each occurrance.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was no hand soap available at the hand sink by the fountain drinks station during the inspection. PIC was made aware. PIC provided a bottle of handwashing soap. Ensure that a type of handwashing cleanser is available at all hand sinks at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels available at the hand sink by the drinks station in the lobby area during today’s inspection. PIC placed a roll of paper towels at the hand sink by sink. Ensure that all hand sinks within the facility have the adequate supply of handwashing accessories at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC. Ensure that hand washing is taking place at all times that it is required in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hand and use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing with staff to ensure that it is taking place correctly at all times.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

1) A container of milk is observed in the walk in cooler without a date marking and mostly empty. The PC was shown and discarded the container to correct as they were unsure when it had been opened. 2) A containers of pasta sauce is observed with a date of 3/11. This would have the discard date located at the end of 3/18. The PIC was shown and discarded the container to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are properly date marked and discarded/used prior to the end of day seven.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Two cans are observed with significant dents in the observable seams. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The cans were separated from the other cans for discarded/credit. Ensure that all can containers are maintained in good condition or separated out to prevent Botolism.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener is observed with dry, accumulated filth. The PIC was shown and cleaned the blade during the inspection to correct. Education conducted. Ensure that all food contact equipment are maintained clean in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not register at effective levels of sanitizer in the solution. The PIC was shown and investigated the situation. It appeared as if the jug of concentrate had off-gassed. A new jug was supplied and the concentration worked its way back up to effective levels during this inspection to correct.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Three sanitizer buckets were observed to be at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The sanitizer buckets were remade and tested to be at 200ppm of sanitizer. citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There is an insect glue trap placed directly above the dish table across from the dish machine. Discussed  with the manager that insect traps shall never be stored above food, food prep area, or above areas where clean dishes are handled and stored. Ensure that insect glue traps are never placed in the above mentioned areas to prevent cross contamination of food items.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There is a significant gap at the bottom of the back door of the establishment. The gap is at least an inch in size. PIC mentioned that the facility will be having the door replaced very soon. Ensure that all outer doors are closed fitting to prevent the entry of unwanted pests and insects.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There was a significant amount of ice build up on the floor, shelves, and packaging of food of the walk in cooler. Shown to the manager and he mentioned that the cooler is suppose to be serviced soon to fix the buildup issue and service the unleveled floor. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed cardboard boxes of food stored directly on the floor of the walk-in freezer. The PIC was informed that items must be stored at least 6 inches off the ground. The PIC acquired plastic pallets and moved items off the floor during the inspection. This violations is now corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee wash hands and turn off the faucet without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- education was conducted and the operator informed the new employee about proper hand washing technique. The employee rewashed their hands, using a barrier to turn off the faucet, and therefore prevent re-contaminating hands. Frequently review proper hand washing technique with all staff.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed single use to-go bowls submerged in a 5 gallon bucket of soy sauce (for use as a scoop). Inspector informed the person in charge (PIC) that scoops in service must have handles to avoid bare hand contact with the ready to eat (RTE) food items. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the soup bowl with a gloved hand. Inspector advised the use of ladles or scoops with handle for the future. Utensils used for RTE foods, ice, and sauces must have a distinction between food contact and hand contact surfaces to prevent bare hands contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed an employee rinsing their personal food in a designated hand washing sink. CORRECTED- education was conducted regarding the use of hand washing sinks. Hand washing sinks are to be used for hand washing ONLY. Cease this practice.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed multiple uncovered foods and sauces in the grill coolers as well as the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- a covering was placed over these items. Ensure all foods stored in cold holding are covered to protect from cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw fish stored over cabbage in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- items were rearranged to reflect proper storage order.  Ensure all RTE food items are always stored above animal proteins to prevent the contamination of RTE foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of biofilm on the soda nozzles nearest the sushi station. CORRECTED- nozzles were removed and brought to the dish area to undergo full ware-washing (wash-rinse-sanitize). Discussed using a brush to clean the nozzles or bringing them for complete ware-washing to remove any soil debris. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items on the cold buffet line to be out of temperature. The PIC verified they had been on the line since the start of service (approximately 2.5 hours):
1) Pork- internal temperature of 45F
2) Crab meat- internal temperature of 50F.
3) Garlic sauce- internal temperature of 47F.
CORRECTED- items were removed from the line and voluntarily discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are cold held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed tuna in reduced oxygen packaging thawing in the sushi cooler. The label indicates that the food must be removed from a reduced oxygen environment upon thawing. CORRECTED- education was conducted and a cut was placed in the package. Ensure all fish in reduced oxygen packaging are vented when moved into thawing to prevent the growth of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Wet cloths were observed stored in an otherwise clean, unused rice cooker. The PIC indicated that these cloths were held for use while storing cooked rice in the rice cooker to help maintain moisture and keep rice from drying out. Discussed wet cloth storage- ensure damp cloths are stored in sanitizer solution, or if used to wipe up a spill, placed in a dirty laundry basket.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of food debris and rust on the shelves of the walk in cooler. Discussed either cleaning/ repainting, or replacing the shelves. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and designed to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.[C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

Seven prepackaged individual bottles of Nesquick were observed with manufacturer’s use by dates of either September 2025 or February 2026. The PIC was shown and discarded the observed items to correct the violation. Ensure that the facility discards TCS products prior to their expiration date.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed 2 coolers to have improper storage order of meats. Eggs and other meats were observed to be stored above salads. Discussed with PIC, meats were relocated to a proper location within cooler. Ensure facility is maintaining proper storage order of meats to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed salt, flour, and rice to be missing the proper labeling being contained outside of original container. Discussed with PIC, labels were placed on each container. Ensure any white substance removed from its original container is properly labeled.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed 2 containers of old, soiled utensils to be stored in contact with clean handing ladles. Discussed with PIC, the old utensils were no longer in use and discarded. The ladles were pulled to be placed in dish machine. Ensure clean utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed small amounts of food splash to be present at the sauce warmer and prep cooler lid. Discussed with PIC, both areas were cleaned during inspection. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: At least five to ten fruit flies were observed on the mesh bags of whole onions in the back kitchen area. The person-in-charge mentioned that the onions are usually used within a week and never are stored for long periods of time. Discussed possibly storing onions in clean trash containers or any type of sealed container to prevent attracting insects. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination and unwanted insects.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine was tested at 0ppm (CL). The machine was cycled several times and still tested at 0ppm. A service technician was contacted during the visit. The machine was later repaired and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were several insect glue traps stored above food prep areas throughout the kitchen area. The traps were filled with dead insects. Discussed and shown to the person-in-charge (PIC). Be sure to remove glue traps from above food prep areas to prevent contamination of food items.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed four dented enchilada cans on the shelves in the dry storage. PIC was made aware. The dented cans were immediately removed and store in a different location. Ensure that dented cans or packaged food items maintain their sealing integrity at all times.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The internal surface of the coffee maker was observed soiled. PIC was made aware. The coffee maker was cleaned and sanitized while inspector was present. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the internal surface of the coffee maker are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The shelvings in the dish room use to store dishes were observed to be rusted. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that the necessary actions will be taken. Ensure that the shelvings are cleaned and painted with anti-rust paint to cover the current surface.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the left counter top of the dish machine was observed in disrepair. PIC was made aware. The counter top was re-caulked while inspector was present. Ensure sealed spaces remain sealed providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Dented cans were observed in dry storage. The observed cans were shown and discussed with the PIC. The cans were removed for discard to correct. Insure package integrity of all cans in the facility moving forward.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: (1) A dirty knife was observed with food debris on the magnetic rack next to the three part sink. (2) A food dicer tool was observed with remaining food debris while stored on top of the ice machine. The PIC was notified and shown both items, and they were moved back to dish to correct. Insure that all food-contact items are completely clean prior to storage to sight and touch at all times.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: A spray bottle with degreaser solution was unlabeled. It is important that all chemicals that are in working containers be labeled to prevent cross contamination or improper use. The PIC was notified and the spray bottle was labeled immediately.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Personal items were stored in a metal cooking pan along with a stem thermometer. PIC was shown and the thermometer was washed to correct. Food contact utensils should be stored so that they are not exposed to sources of contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The underside of the shelf above the steam table was observed to have accumulated debris from old food splashes. The PIC was notified, and made plans to clean it later at the end of the day, and clean it on a regular schedule. It is important that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are maintained clean.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility items in need of cleaning/repair:

1. The ceiling around the lighting in the kitchen has exposed drywall. Ensure these areas are painted or paneled to avoid moisture accumulation

2. The hood system is in need of cleaning

Ensure these items are resolved prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector observed no allergen certification present at the facility. Ensure the CFPM has an allergen certificate prior to the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed jalapeños (stated to have been opened yesterday by the person in charge (PIC)) being stored in the can. CORRECTED- kitchen staff transferred the contents of the can into a food safe container. The original can is not rated to safely hold the food material after opening the can. Ensure acidic food items from cans (such as jalapeños and tomato paste) are transferred (and date marked) into a food safe container if held over 24 hours to prevent contamination of ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed pork stored below chicken in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED-kitchen staff moved the chicken below the pork to reflect correct storage order. Due to the fact that chicken (165F) requires a higher internal cooking temperature than pork (145F), it must be stored below the raw pork. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed an open container of cranberry juice labeled “Refrigerate after opening” sitting at room temperature (internal temperature of 63F) at the bar. CORRECTED- the PIC confirmed the container had not been open for more than 3 hours. The bottle was immediately moved into cold holding. Temperature control for food safety items (TCS) (including those labeled “Refrigerate after opening “ or “Keep refrigerated”) must be cold held at or below 41F, and date marked like all other TCS food items. Read labels of hermetically sealed containers regarding safe storage after opening to prevent temperature abuse and potential food-borne illness.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple TCS foods to be out of the seven day range of date marking:
1) Tamales dated 2/23
2) Cream cheese dated 2/26
3) Salsa dated 3/2 and 3/10
CORRECTED- the tamales and cream cheese were voluntarily discarded. The salsa had the incorrect dates, and was confirmed to have been prepared on 3/13. New dates were applied to reflect the date of preparation. Ensure date stickers are removed during ware washing and items are marked with the date of preparation (day one), to be used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets on the bottom of the protein prep cooler to be separating. Replace gaskets by the next routine inspection to ensure equipment is in proper repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to always wash their hands before donning gloves including in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the servers station to have a build-up of soils on them. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC, and PIC removed the nozzles to clean them immediately. Ensure nozzles are cleaned or replaced frequently enough to keep them free of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: The gravy and cheese sauce were observed not holding the proper temperatures. The cheese sauce was temping at 116 and the gravy at 109. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that one of the wells was not working. The gravy in that well was discarded. The cheese sauce was taken to be reheated. Inspector later reexamined the temperature of the cheese sauce and it was observed at 154F. Ensure that hot holding temperatures are monitored at a regular frequency to avoid spoilage.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding.
