(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed several drain flies in the utility closet and the dish room. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the flies are dealt with using authorized pest control methods. Zappers and fly strips may be hung, but they must not be hung over food. Ensure that pest activities is reduced within the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Several cardboard boxes of cookies were observed being stored on the floor in the serving area. Discussed with PIC. The boxes were placed on crates to keep them off the floor. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protected them from contamination splash.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: There were several wet wiping cloths just laying on multiple counter tops  in the kitchen and prep areas. PIC was made aware. Education was carried out. The wet cloths were taken to get laundered. Ensure that wiping cloths are kept in sanitizer solutions in between use.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Several tongs were observed being stored on the side handle-bar of the hot holding unit on the cook line. The side of the unit is soiled with grease and dust accumulations. Ensure that in-use or between use utensils are stored properly to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The shelvings use to store dishes by the grill was observed with soil and dust accumulations. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the shelvings will be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that the shelving is cleaned and the accumulations removed. Make sure that this shelving is monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-401.11(C) Equipment, Clothes Washers and Dryers, and Storage Cabinets, Contamination Prevention. (C) If a mechanical clothes washer or dryer is provided, it shall be located so that the washer or dryer is protected from contamination and only where there is no exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a build-up of oils and food debris behind the grill and griddle on the line. Ensure that these areas are cleaned regularly enough to mitigate the build-up of oils and food debris. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: A food protection manager was not observed at the facility during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) was advised to either have another employee or all employees certified in food protection management. Ensure there is a certified food protection manager at the facility during all hours of food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT - An employee was observed changing task and not washing hands before putting on gloves. CORRECTED - The employee was instructed to wash hands by the inspector to prevent contamination of food. Ensure hands are washed when tasks are changed and before putting on gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1.The bottom of the front non-functional prep cooler was observed to have food debris accumulation. 
2. The top shelf for storing mushroom in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.
3. The wall above the top shelf for storing mushroom in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.
4. The fan blade cover and fan casing in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.

The PIC was instructed to have the surfaces mentioned above, cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The pipe beneath the handwashing sink in the back area was observed to be leaking and temporarily repaired with duct tape. The PIC was informed that duct tape is not an approved material for permanent repairs in a food establishment as it is not smooth or easily cleanable. The PIC was advised to have the pipe properly repaired and the duct tape removed. Ensure the plumbing is maintained in good repair by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas in the facility were observed to be in need of cove tiles replacements:
1. THIRD REPEAT -  The left side of under the handwashing sink at the back area.
2. The right side of under the three-compartment sink.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the missing wall cove tiles in the areas mentioned above are replaced for smooth and easy cleaning.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B)  Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall above the prep sink on the can opener table was observed to have soil accumulation. The PIC was informed. Ensure the wall is cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
An employee handling food was observed to not have a food handlers’ certificate. The PIC was instructed to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

There was not a CFPM available at the time that the inspection began. The PIC at the time stated that the CFPM was at the other store picking up supplies. About halfway through the inspection Mr. Annerino arrived. This corrected the violation but a CFPM must be present at all times that the facility is operating.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple pans on the shelf over the three part sink were observed with remaining stickers and food debris. The PIC was shown and instructed to ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned when ran through the washing process. 2) (REPEAT) The soda nozzles in the drive thru area are observed soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean them. The nozzles were removed and disassembled and then cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate situation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

During the inspection a moist wiping cloth was observed on a counter and not in current use. The PIC was consulted once they arrived and the cloth moved to a sani bucket to correct. Ensure that all wiping rags are stored between uses in a sanitizer at effective concentration.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

A phone was observed on the table in the back next to equipment and with food nearby. The item was removed prior to the situation being brought to the PICs attention. Ensure that all personal items are stored away from food contact and preparation areas to prevent possible contamination of foods.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine reach a dish plate temperature of 150-154F after running several cycles. Inspector discussed proper heat sanitizing temperatures with the person in charge (PIC). The facility has been directed to utilize the triple sink for chemical sanitation until the machine’s heat boosters have been adjusted to reach a minimum plate temperature of 158F (FDA food codes allows for +/-2 instrument error). Inform the inspector if the machine has been adjusted prior to the follow up date.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to initially be dispensing 0 ppm. Staff stated they had run the dish machine multiple times beforehand- and were therefore unaware of improper sanitizing concentrations. CORRECTED- the dish machine was run again and observed to be dispensing 50 ppm chlorine. Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are frequently tested to verify proper sanitizing concentration per manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed multiple house made sauces in the walk in cooler to be held past the seven day date marking period (3/6). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the sauces to be discarded and remade. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are used to discarded within seven days. The date of preparation, thawing, opening, etc. counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the hinge lid on the salad prep cooler to be loose from its fitting. CORRECTED- the PIC reset the screws during the inspection. Ensure all equipment is maintained in proper repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following canned foods on the shelf were observed to have dents:
1. Always save pineapple chunks was observed to have significant dent on the body.
2. Always save pear halves was observed to have significant dent on the body.
3. Always save fruit mix was observed to have significant dents on the body and along the seam (x4)
4. Bust black beans was observed to have significant dent on the body.

CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and the dented cans were removed from the shelf. Dented cans can have entry and harborage of Botulism, ensure canned foods with dents are removed from the shelf and not sold to customers.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Rodent droppings were observed on and under the snack storage shelves. Food residue (popcorn) and gnawed packaging were also observed, including within a wall opening to the left of the snack shelves, indicating evidence of rodent activity.

The PIC was informed of these findings. The PIC stated that a pest control operator had recently serviced the facility and set traps; however, documentation of the most recent service was not available at the time of inspection.

The PIC was instructed to thoroughly clean and sanitize all affected areas, including on and under the shelves, to remove droppings and food residue. The PIC was also advised to maintain documentation of pest control services on-site. 

A follow-up inspection will be conducted on March 31, 2026 to verify that rodent activity has been addressed and to review pest control service records.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1. Soil accumulation was observed on the lower air intake vents of the center cooler located along the left wall.
2. Soil accumulation was observed on the product display tray for bottled water in the center cooler along the left wall.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the surfaces mentioned above in the center cooler along the left wall side are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Bare wood with a huge opening was observed behind the ice cream freezer. The inspector discussed having the opening closed for smooth and easy cleaning and to prevent hideouts for pests and rodents.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed ice cream scoops fully submerged in the running well. CORRECTED- the well was emptied and cleaned, and the scoops were brought to the dish area for ware washing. Ensure scoops and all food contact surfaces are stored with the handles ABOVE the water to prevent bare hand contamination of the food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed sausage in the kitchen’s under counter cooler to bear the following dates: 2/26 and 3/3. Both of these dates are past the seven day date marking requirements for temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods. CORRECTED- the sausage was voluntarily discarded by kitchen staff. Ensure dates are removed and proper ware washing ensues for all food contact surfaces. Ensure all TCS foods are used or discarded within seven days- the day of preparation/ thawing counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [Pf]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed stir spoons at the barista station in a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- education occurred on in use utensils storage with the PIC. Ensure all in-use utensils are stored in a manner that will prevent bare hand contamination of the food contact surface.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed gaskets at the double door standing cooler (unit #2) in the kitchen to be fraying. All nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that equipment is maintained and in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The floor of the walk-in freezer has an accumulation of chunks of ice and debris on it. 
2. The floor under and around the soda syrups across from the walk-in cooler has an accumulation of debris and soda syrup residue on it. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are cleaned and maintained clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to produce their Certified Food Manager (CFM/ CFPM) certificate during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived on site. Ensure a CFM is present on site at all times food is being cooked or prepared, and maintain files on site for future inspections.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen to contain soap, and no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade to display 200 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are made with ONLY warm water and a chemical sanitizer, as soap interferes with sanitizing ability of chemical.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled white powder in the kitchen. CORRECTED- a kitchen staff member labeled the product as sugar. Ensure any ready to eat (RTE) food products that may be easily mistaken for another is labeled once removed from its original container to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces where observed to be in need of repair or reconditioning:
1) The gaskets at BOTH standing coolers and the standing freezer in the kitchen are fragmenting.
2) One of the microwave handles is loose from the door.
3) Some shelves in the standing cooler directly next to the fryers are rusted. Clean/ reseal/ paint, or replace rusting shelves.
Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are in proper repair to prevent potential contamination of foods. Nonfoodcontact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.[C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The only Allergen certificates available were observed to have been expired. Inspector provided Allergen Awareness training information to the PIC. Ensure CFMs obtain Allergen Awareness training, to be maintained every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the dish machine to measure 0ppm chlorine with a test strip. The PIC contacted a service representative for repair during the inspection. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/20/2026 to ensure the dish machine is repaired. In the mean time, staff will use the triple sink for sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed a container of fresh cut potatoes stored on the counter on the cook line. An employee stated that the potatoes are stored on the counter until cooking. Since the potatoes are cut, they are considered a time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food. Ensure cut potatoes are stored at 41F or less to prevent spoilage or pathogen growth. The potatoes were moved the the cooler during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed cooked pork stored in the prep cooler and corn, green beans, and gravy stored in the walk-in cooler to be missing a proper date mark. These items are considered ready-to-eat (RTE), time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Any RTE TCS foods need to be date marked after opening, preparing, or portioning into a new container. Ensure staff are practicing proper date marking to prevent bacteria accumulation in food. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/20/2026 to ensure proper date marking practices are being conducted in the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed a pork loin thawing in standing water in the triple sink. The faucet was running over another container of thawing chicken. The PIC was informed that thawing must be conducted under running water or refrigeration at all times. The pork was moved to the walk-in cooler during the inspection. Ensure proper thawing practices are followed to prevent pathogen growth.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no quaternary ammonia test strips available in the facility. Quaternary ammonia tablets are used in sanitizing buckets, and chlorine is used in the dish machine. The facility had only chorine test strips available. The PIC was informed and test strips were acquired. Ensure both types of test strips are available at all times to properly monitor sanitizer concentrations.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following structures in the building in need of repair:
1. Walk-in cooler-to-freezer door has exposed foam insulation and raw wood to the right of the frame, as well as rags pressed into the holes of the freezer door
2. The walk-in freezer was observed to have heavy ice accumulation as well as food debris on the floor
3. The fan in the dish area was observed soiled with dust and debris

Ensure the floors, ceilings, and walls of the facility are constructed such that they are smooth and easily cleanable. Untreated wood can be painted or stained. Insulation needs to be covered with silicone or another non-porous material. The holes need to be patched and painted. Rags are not an appropriate material for floors, walls, or ceilings in a food preparation/storage space.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following canned foods on the shelves were observed to have dents:
1. Clover valley cream style corn has dent along the seam.
2. Campbells beef barley soup has dent along the seam.
3. Armour chili no beans has significant dents in the body and along the seam (x6).
4. Clover valley fruit cocktail in light syrup has dent along the seam (x3).
5. Dole pineapple chunks has dent along the seam.

CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and the dented cans were removed from the shelf. Dented cans can have entry and harborage of Botulism, ensure canned foods with dents are removed from the shelf and not sold to customers.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Auto air fresheners were observed hanging over canned tomato basil soups. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the auto air fresheners were moved to a different location. Ensure poisonous or toxic materials are not stored over food.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the back storage cooler and cooler used for hot dogs and eggs. The PIC was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each of the coolers to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each of the coolers to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed to be passing through the middle (left and right) and beneath the emergency exit door at the back storage. The PIC was advised to close the holes at the center of the door and to use weather stripping to tightly seal beneath the door. Ensure the gaps are sealed to prevent potential entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. The PIC was informed. Ensure hot water is provided at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. The inspector will follow-up on March 26, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Bare wood and gaps were observed at the left side of the restroom door by the paper towel holder. The PIC was instructed by the inspector to ensure the bare wood is painted and the gaps closed for easy cleaning and to prevent possible hideout for pests.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The handwashing sink in the first restroom was observed to have no hot water available. The inspector discussed with the person-in-charge to ensure hot water is available at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. The inspector followed up on March 16, 2026 to verify compliance but the violation has not been fixed, so the inspector will be back on March 26, 2026 for a second follow-up to ensure hot water is available in the first restroom.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple pans are observed washed and with remaining stickers on the bottoms. The PIC was instructed to ensure that the stickers are removed prior to or during the washing process to ensure that they do not provide for possible mold growth on the food contact surfaces. The items were moved back to dish to correct. 2) Three knives on the magnetic strip were observed with food debris on them. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned after use and prior to storage in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). 

The coving in the section of the facility where the chest freezers and standing freezer are located was observed with a gap along the top section where it meets the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-seal the coving to the wall prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all coving is correctly sealed to the walls at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

1) Pre-cooked ravioli in the top shelf of the island cooler at the northern end are observed with internal temperatures ranging from 48F-51F. Investigating the situation lead to the conclusion that the noted items were stocked to far out from the cooling location in the unit to be effective. Items behind the second row in from the outside appear to be holding temperature correctly. The items from that point in were allowed to be kept while those from outside of the point were discarded to correct the immediate violation. Education should be conducted with the stockers to ensure that the coolers are not overloaded and the food temperatures maintained at safe ranges. 2) TCS foods on the top shelf of the island cooler on the east side are observed with internal temperatures ranging from 47F-48F. The observed items and the rest of the shelf were discarded to correct the immediate violation. The cooler issue is being managed on the line item #33 of this report.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The top shelf of the island cooler on the east side would not register correct temperatures for the TCS foods observed. Internal temperatures were observed for multiple items throughout the cooler and only items on the top shelf on this side were observed out of compliance. The PIC took the shelf out of service until maintenance could be contacted and arrive. A follow up is being scheduled for 10 days to ensure complaince is attained. Ensure that all coolers are functioning correctly at all times in the facility.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

This facility has begun to use a lactic acid based sanitizer. The facility has not acquired test strips for this chemical by the time of the inspection. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to acquire test strips prior to the follow up in 10 days. Ensure that all sanitizers used for wiping food contact surfaces have appropriate test strips at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine at the Globe to be dispensing 0 ppm sanitizer. The person in charge (PIC) called their service provider to have the machine serviced. Inspector will return on 03/19 or sooner if contacted by the PIC to check for compliance. Dishes produced at the bar must be brought to the kitchen for proper ware washing until the machine is serviced and observed to be dispensing proper chemical sanitizer concentrations. Ensure all dish machines are tested frequently to verify that the machine is reaching the sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a gallon of milk and creamer without date marking at the bar reach in cooler. CORRECTED- the PIC could not guarantee the date these items were opened, and discarded them as a result. Ensure that date marking happens within 24 hours of opening a TCS (time/temperature controlled for safety) food. To identify TCS foods, look for the phrases “refrigerate after opening” or “keep refrigerated” on the item packaging. Additionally, anything prepared in the kitchen that is not shelf-stable must also be date marked within 24 hours of preparation.

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed the hot holding unit at the front of the kitchen to have a piece of duct tape on it, and the gaskets to be in disrepair. The PIC removed the duct tape and stated they will be ordering new gaskets. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the deterioration of equipment into ready to eat foods.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the bar chest-cooler that is used to store beers and juices to be soiled. Specifically, the bottom of the cooler underneath the grates that are used to store beers and juice is soiled. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed a single use 2 oz cup stored in powdered sugar. CORRECTED- the cup was removed and replaced with a scoop that has a handle. Ensure all ready to eat (RTE) foods are handled with gloves, deli paper, or a scoop with a handle- to differentiate between the food contact and hand contact surface moving forward to prevent bare hand contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple soda nozzles in both the lobby and drive-thru to contain an accumulation of biofilm. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the soda nozzles to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda nozzles are both cleaned AND sanitized each night to remove debris that could contaminate RTE beverages. Food contact surfaces must be maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed unlabeled spray bottle beneath the front counter. The PIC verified that the substance was sanitizer. CORRECTED- the PIC labeled the container to display the contents. Ensure all chemicals are properly labeled to prevent food contamination.
citation_text: 7-101.11 Identifying Information, Prominence. Containers of POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS and PERSONAL CARE ITEMS shall bear a legible manufacturer's label. [Pf]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed white powder at the fry station to contain no label. CORRECTED- the PIC identified and labeled the food as powdered sugar. Ensure all RTE foods that may be mistaken for other foods are labeled once removed to from their original container to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair or cleaning:
1) An accumulation of dust and debris on the shelf above the drive through. Clean nonfood contact surfaces at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
2) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the kitchen.
3) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the mens’ restroom.
4) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the womens’ restroom.
5) Caulking along the back and right side border of the triple sink. 
Physical facilities that may not be moved for cleaning must be adhered to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned and repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed a food handler on shift with no Food Handler certificate available. All employees must have food handler certificates to be made available during inspections within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The CFM has not completed Allergen Training. The PIC was able to show the inspector that they have obtained the course and training materials via email. Complete training and test to be made available by the next routine inspection. All High risk establishments should have an Allergen Certified Certified Food Manager within 30 days of employment, to be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed donning gloves without washing their hands in between tasks and cooking. Discussed with PIC. Employees were educated and the behavior was abolished. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable to always wash their hands before donning gloves during food prep.
citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
Inspector observed the following dented cans in the dry storage during today’s inspection. 
1. Four cans of cream of mushroom.
2. Two cans of chunks pineapple.
PIC was made aware. The cans were discarded. Ensure that dented cans are removed from inventory to be returned to distributor or discard to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION Inspector observed  soil accumulation in the soda gun nozzle at the bar. Discussed with PIC and the soda gun nozzle was cleaned immediately. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following were observed during the inspection.
1. There was no sani bucket available in the kitchen during inspection.
2. The sanitizer in the dish machine was unreadable during today’s inspection. 
A staff member was asked to create a bucket at the end of the inspection. PIC replaced the sanitizer in the dish machine.  Both sanitizers were tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that all sanitizers are always made at the appropriate concentration and available during food prep at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: A pan filled with chicken breast was observed being thawed sitting a water in the triple sink. Education on appropriated thawing methods as stated within the 2022 FDA food code was carried out. The chicken breast was later placed under running water to be properly thawed. Ensure that employees are knowledgeable about the appropriate thawing methods to avoid food contamination and spoilage.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple cardboard boxes with food items being stored on the floor in the walk-in cooler by the dry storage. PIC was made aware of the cardboard boxes with food items being stored on the floor. PIC said that they would have them remove from the floor. Ensure that containers and boxes with food items are stored at least 6” above the floor.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
The following were observed.
1. A few knives were observed lodged in a space in the wall above the triple sink.
2. A knife was observed lodged in the space between the prep counter space on the large prep cooler and a cardboard box of single use food storage sheets in the kitchen. 
Education was carried out. The knives were removed and taken to be cleaned. Ensure that in-use or between-use utensils are stored properly.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A THRICE REPEAT VIOLATION. An accumulation of food debris was observed under the fryer in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the surface would get clean. Ensure that closed spaces under equipments are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed dirty mop water sitting in the mop bucket and a wet mop head stored on the floor in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. The dirty mop water was discarded and the mop head stored properly. Ensure that employees are reminded to discard of dirty mop water after mopping and mop heads store in a way that allows them to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Several broken tiles were observed under the fryers. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the necessary would be done. Ensure that the broken tiles are repaired providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: An accumulation of grease and dust were observed dangling from the hood filters in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that the third-party company that usually clean the hood were scheduled to be at the facility a couple days before but canceled due to scheduling conflicts. Hence, they are scheduled to be in the facility within a day.  Ensure that the filters are cleaned to avoid the contamination of food.
citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspector observed an employee food being stored with other food items in the walk-in cooler in the kitchen. Education was carried out. The employee food was removed to be store in another location. Ensure that employee foods are stored separately from other food items to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There was no stem thermometer available for measuring internal foods temperatures. PIC assured inspectors that the thermometer will be present in the future. Ensure that there is always a stem thermometer is available for measuring the internal temperatures of mood items.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was no test strips available during inspection. PIC acquired test strips during the inspection. Ensure that there is always test strips available to monitor the concentration of sanitizers.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment:
Repeat Violation

The operator’s Certified Food Protection Manager certificate is not present. Ensure that there is always a person in charge who is a certified food protection manager.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw beef stored above cooked tortillas in the prep cooler. The PIC was informed and the item was moved to the bottom. Ensure raw meats are never stored above ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no stem thermometer available during inspection. Ensure a stem thermometer is available at all times of food prep. A follow-up will be conducted at the next event to ensure a thermometer is present and in use.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no test strips available on the truck. The PIC was informed and strips were acquired. Ensure test strips are available at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to present the company’s Exclusion and Restriction policy to the inspector. The PIC stated they would send the policy to the inspector, but this did not happen within 24 hours of the investigation, despite a follow up phone call from the inspector. The inspector provided a blank copy of SCDPH’s Employee Health Reporting Agreement to the PIC. Inspector will return on 03/24 to ensure that the PIC has EITHER obtained signed copies of SCDPH’s employee health reporting agreements from employees, OR can show the inspector the company’s exclusion/ restriction policy. All food establishments must have a verifiable manner to confirm reportable illnesses.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed sanitizer buckets throughout the kitchen holding below the concentration required for food contact surfaces (100 ppm quaternary ammonia). CORRECTED- sanitizer buckets were remade to proper concentration. Ensure sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the appropriate concentration for food contact surfaces per the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facilities in need of repair or maintenance:
1) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall is peeling.
2) The floor drain below the drive thru register is missing a floor drain cover.
3) There is no outlet cover on the wall behind the ice cream machine.
4) THIRD REPEAT: There is a missing floor tile in front of the back door. 
Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the entry and microorganisms with high water activity. Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) FIRST REPEAT: There is an accumulation of grease in the hood vent above the fryers. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination on ready to eat (RTE) foods, and also pose a fire risk to the facility. 
2) Food and general debris on the wall and floor beneath the front counter.
3) Dust on the wall behind the drive thru drink machine.
Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for the person-in-charge (PIC) and an employee were not available during the inspection. The inspector provided blank copies for the PIC and employee to complete and sign. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink was observed to be obstructed with lots of ice cubes in it. CORRECTED: The inspector discussed using the handwashing sink for handwashing purpose only. The ice was melted off with hot water and the sink was accessible for handwashing. Ensure the handwashing sink is not used for purposes other than handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [PF]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
The following areas were observed to not have handwashing signs for employees:

1. The male and female restrooms. 
2. The handwashing sink at the bar. CORRECTED: The sign was posted near the handwashing sink during the inspection.

The inspector provided handwashing signs for the two restrooms and the handwashing sink. Ensure the handwashing signs are posted in the restrooms and handwashing sink to notify employees to wash their hands.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The inner wall surface of the ice machine was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The soda guns and soda holsters were observed to have soil accumulation. One of the soda gun and soda holster was observed to have dead bugs in them. The PIC was instructed to clean them by the inspector during the inspection. The PIC cleaned the soda guns and holsters during the inspection, but they were not cleaned to sight and touch, bugs and soil were still observed in them.

Ensure the ice machine, soda guns and soda holsters are cleaned to sight and touch by washing, rinsing and sanitizing them. The inspector will follow-up on March 23, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The following time/temperature for safety (TCS) foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” were observed on the counter at the bar:

1. Blue cheese stuffed greek olives.
2. Deli-sliced hot jalapeño peppers.
3. Maraschino cherries.
4. Caramel flavored topping.

The PIC was informed as well as educated by the inspector and the TCS foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” are kept in the cooler and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: A wet ice scoop was observed to be placed on an absorbent cloth material on the counter by the ice machine. The inspector discussed storing the ice scoop in a non-absorbent container after usage. Ensure the ice scoop is stored in a dry container and not on an absorbent material.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed a used, closed single service bowl to be resting in an in use rice cooker. Discussed with PIC, bowl was removed and rice cooker was emptied and remade. Ensure only rice is placed in rice cookers to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of noodles to be at 50F in cooler. Discussed with PIC, noodles were placed in a way that prevented the cooler air from dispensing evenly. Noodles were moved to bottom of prep cooler and later ran a temperature of 40F. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple in use sauce bottles to be missing date marking. Discussed with PIC, sauce was discarded and bottles were remade with correct dates. Ensure any item removed from its original container is date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 EJ present to monitor the control of roaches within the facility. See additional notes in General Comments. There were no glue traps present during today’s inspection. Two live adults were observed under equipment on the cook line. Ensure glue traps are out and dated at all times to monitor activity. SCDPH will continue to follow-up until no pests are observed.
