This means keeping the glue traps present as a monitoring tool and insuring treatment is curtailing life cycles. 

 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

A tray of raw ground beef is observed stored on a shelf over containers of cooked ground beef used for sandwiches in the reach in cooler across from the hand washing station. The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employee was observed donning gloves without handwashing. PIC was made aware. Ensure that employees are aware and remember to wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114. The concentration of the quaternary ammonia sanitizer in the sani bucket was observed  at 0ppm. PIC was made aware and the sanitizer was remade to correct the violation. Ensure that the sanitizer concentration is monitored and checked at a regular frequency.

(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The thermometers in the large display cooler at the deli were observed not functional. PIC was made aware. A few stem thermometer were placed for temporary use until hanging thermometer are installed. Ensure that thermometers are always present within the cooler.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of food debris under fryer and the oven at the deli. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that it was going to be cleaned. Ensure that staff are aware of the accumulation of food debris under equipment and closed surfaces hence, need to extend cleaning procedures to closed spaces as well. Ensure that closed spaces and surfaces under equipments are routinely monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The coving tiles along the compartmental wall next to the fryers and on the right side of the walk-in cooler were observed broken and missing. PIC assured inspector that the tiles will be replaced. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done to maintain the facility in good repairs.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: The ventilation filters in hood system were observed with accumulated dust and soil. Education was carried out and PIC assured inspector that the filters will be cleaned. Ensure that the hood filters are cleaned to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.14 Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The handwashing sinks in the two restrooms were observed to have no hot water available. The person-in-charge was informed. Ensure hot water is available at the handwashing sinks in the two restrooms at all times. The inspector will follow-up on April 10, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. There is no food protection manager present. The operator (Khalid) did just acquire his food handler’s card. The CFPM was out for the morning. See that a CFPM is present during all hours of operation. The store should have one certified food manager present during all hours of operation. 

 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink.  There is observed a wet wiping cloth stored in the basin of the handsink near the walk-in cooler. Cloth was removed during the inspection. Even though you have hand sinks at either end of the cookline and use primarily the one by the entrance, see that both hand sinks are kept free of debris and stocked with soap and paper toweling. 


(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness.The sani-bucket was not yet set-up and the operator had just opened and begun work in the kitchen. The bucket was created during the inspection and operator knew to create the bucket to 100ppm. Operator then used his test strips to test.  Sani-buckets should be discarded nightly. OR, the bucket should be discarded by the opener as a new bucket is created. The bucket is noted as being cold with soiled water. 
 See that wiping cloths are being stored within a proper sanitizing bucket. The bucket should be sized to hold several cloths and still allow space for a hand to be submerged. The most important part of sanitizing is that a testable residual of sanitizer is present in the bucket. 

Discard buckets at the end of the day or when concentration dips below the allowed amount. 

Keep a sani-bucket, that is holding proper chemical residual, available for holding wet wiping cloths. 

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. The interior of the microwave was observed soiled with food splash. The microwave was cleaned during the inspection. 

UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. The walk-in cooler was observed in excellent condition with raw proteins stored on the bottom shelf and everything covered and date marked. One items of bulk cooked foods was observed from March 4. The food was moved to a personal storage location and marked as such. 

(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. The prep cooler and reach-in freezer are coated with a small amount of frost accumulation. Operator stated he was going to chip away at the ice of the preparation cooler today. See that the reach-in freezer is defrosted and cleaned as well. 


(A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. There remain several areas that need detail cleaning attention: upright two-door cooler and spice containers. An extensive list was hand written and given to the two operators present. Cleaning includes the fronts of all equipment. 

(C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. There is detail cleaning that is observed to be occurring around the center wall. There are some areas where detail cleaning is lacking: around the feet of the fryer, around the floor of the reach-in freezer, and around the seasoning storage shelving. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. Observed several personal items stored adjacent to the pizza oven mixed-in with gloves. Dates, keys, telephone, and other items are stored on the conveyor belt with various gloves and storage bags. Personal items were moved during the inspection. Cease storing personal drinks within food preparation, storage, and serving areas.  

(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. CFPM is not allergen certified. 

 (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following canned foods on the dry shelves were observed to have dents:
1. Hunts pasta sauce has significant dents on the body and along the seam (x6).
2. Sweetened condensed filled milk has dent along the seam.
3. Campbell chunky clam chowder has significant dents on the body (x2).
4. Campbell spicy tomato soup has significant dent on the body.
5. Boiled peanuts has dent along the seam.

CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and educated and the dented cans were removed from the shelves. Dented cans can have entry and harborage of botulism, ensure canned foods with dents are removed from the shelves and not sold to customers.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometer was observed in the cooler across the women’s restroom. The PIC was informed, educated and instructed to provide internal thermometer in the cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure an ambient thermometer is placed in the warmest part of the cooler to accurately monitor internal temperature.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Dead ants were observed on the floor at the far left end corners close to the brown door, under the electrical equipments in the back storage. The PIC was instructed by the inspector to have the dead ants removed from the facility and the floor area cleaned. Ensure the dead insects are removed from the facility and the floor area is cleaned to sight. The inspector will be back on April 10, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 6-501.112 Removing Dead or Trapped Birds, Insects, Rodents, and Other Pests. Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed to be passing beneath the door at the back storage. The PIC was informed, educated and advised to use weather stripping to seal the gap beneath the door. Ensure the gap is sealed to prevent potential entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Significant soil accumulations were observed on the external surfaces of the freezer doors at the back storage.
2. The first standing cooler across the women’s restroom was observed to have soil accumulation on the plastic holes at the bottom of the cooler door.

The PIC was instructed by the inspector to have those surfaces cleaned. Ensure the surfaces of the freezer and standing cooler mentioned above are cleaned and kept free of soil accumulations.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Dirty water and mop heads were observed in the mop bucket at the mop station and in a black bucket in the mop sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and educated on proper air-drying techniques for mop heads; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop heads were placed in the mop sink with the mop heads facing upwards to air-dry since there was no empty wringer basket or hanger. Ensure water from mopping is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The double sink across from the office area is in need of caulking. The gap between the wall and the piece of equipment is large enough to hold a pencil, therefore, the sink shall be caulked to the wall. Ensure that all stationary pieces of equipment are caulked to the wall to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
There were between 5-10 employees working at the time of the inspection. The kitchen manager was able to produce his food manager certificate and 2 other food handler certificates for other employees. Discussed that every employee that handles food and clean dishes shall have a food handler certificate. Ensure that food certificates are printed off and are available for all employees during routine visits. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the handsink along the main cookline. Shown to the PIC and soap was added to the dispenser to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always soap available at every handsink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Various salad dressings, potato salad, cut melon, and desserts were stored inside of a cooler with an ambient temperature of 50F. The foods were probed using several different internal thermometers. All TCS foods were discarded to correct the violation. The items had been stored in the unit since the morning, as far as the manager was aware. Ensure that TCS foods that are intended to be cold held are held at 41F or less. 

Also, ensure that shredded cheese that is being held on ice is changed frequently to avoid cheese from sitting in the temperature danger zone for long periods of time.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The cooler along the cookline that stores salad dressings had an ambient temperature of 50F. The inspector’s probe thermometer, the facility’s internal thermometer (recently placed inside of the unit), and the facility’s probe thermometer all verified an ambient temperature of 50F. The cooler stores salad dressing, uncooked broccoli, potato salad, fruit, and desserts. All time/temperature control(TCS) foods were pulled from the cooler and discarded. Per phone call with the facility’s manager, Don Hubbell, a service technician will be to service the cooler tomorrow morning. Ensure that cold holding equipment is sufficient enough to maintain cold hold temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handsink in the back slicing area is in need of caulking. The sink has pulled away from the wall and shall be recaulked to prevent debris accumulation. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed rice and rice noodles soaking in buckets with no lid stored directly on the floor. The PIC was advised to keep food containers covered at all times as well as at least 6 inches off the ground. Coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container. The PIC placed covers on both buckets and moved them to a counter during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected on site. 

The inspector recommends investing in additional shelving or carts for buckets to avoid this violation in the future.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed knives in the bar area to be stored between the prep cooler and the counter. This are is not accessible for cleaning/sanitizing, and therefore is not safe for utensil storage. The knives were moved to the dish area during the inspection. Ensure the knives are stored on an easily cleanable surface to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review hand washing with staff and conduct oversight as needed. Ensure proper hand washing at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the inspector observed the bar three part sink to have a low concentration in their sanitizing bin. The PIC was notified and strengthened the newly made solution to correctly. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

Multiple employees were observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review when hand washing is required with their staff and conduct oversight as needed. Ensure that hand washing is conducted each time that it is required by the code.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink across form the manager’s office was observed without soap. The PIC was shown and replaced the soap to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several pans on a shelf being stored as clean were observed soiled with remaining food debris and stickers. The PIC was shown and education conducted. They moved the items back to dish for re-cleaning. Reviewing of procedures and oversight of the dish cleaners is suggested to prevent future issues. Ensure that all food contact surfaces re completely cleaned prior to storage and re-use in the facility.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The shelf for storing milk in the walk-in cooler was observed to have soil accumulation from milk deposit. The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed. Ensure the milk shelf is cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Soil accumulation from milk deposit was observed on the floor area under the shelf for storing milk in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed. Ensure the floor area under the milk shelf is regularly cleaned and kept free of milk deposit.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There is observed to be a large pot of rice cooling that is set on a trash can and there is a sheet pan that is being used to prepare salmon that is set on top of another trash can. This was discussed with the PIC. Trash cans should not be used as counters, as they are not clean, sanitized food-contact surfaces. Cease using trash cans as counters and either obtain more preparation tables or use other surfaces in the facility, such as the top of the chest freezer.
citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the front baffle of the ice machine to be soiled. Shown to the kitchen manager and she mentioned that the baffle will be cleaned. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation, as well as contamination of ice.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan vent in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation. 
2. The outer surface area behind the soda nozzles was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The standing freezer by the cook line was observed to have ice buildup.

The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed. Ensure the surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas in the facility were observed to be in need of repair:

1. The space between the wall and handwashing sink by the cook line freezer was observed to be in need of caulking/sealing.
2. The space between the wall and three-compartment sink was observed to be in need of caulking/sealing.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the spaces mentioned above are caulked/sealed for easy cleaning and to prevent water from entering the spaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No certified food protection manager was at facility upon inspector arrival. Ensure that a CFPM is working any time that food is being prepared.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Two cans of tomatillos and two cans of tomatoes purée were observed to be dented and placed on the dry storage shelf. Education was carried out. The dented cans were removed. Ensure that cans of food items are examined to avoid botulism contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw eggs being stored over cooked pulled chicken in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that food is stored in the correct order to prevent contamination. From top to bottom, the correct order is fish, pork and beef, eggs, then poultry (chicken and turkey).  COS PIC switched the foods so that the raw egg could be stored above raw beef.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Knives were observed stored inside the space between the lid of the prep cooler and the hood on each sides. PIC was made aware. Education was carried out. The knives were removed and taken to the dish washing area to get cleaned. Ensure that utensils that are use as food contact surfaces such as knives are monitored, cleaned, sanitized, and stored appropriately.
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled.
1. The nozzles of the soda gun at the bar was observed to be soiled. Education was carried out. A staff member cleaned and sanitized the soda nozzles while inspector was present. (COS)
2. A buildup of soil accumulations within the soda nozzle sockets on the Coca-Cola machine in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC partially cleaned some of the sockets to keep the machine running. The rest will not be used until they have been cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that the reminder of the accumulation buildup is cleaned. A follow-up is scheduled for 03/19/2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: A dead cockroach and several live juvenile roaches were observed in the Coca-Cola machine nozzle socket and dispenser hood. PIC showed invoices of a their pest control company being in the facility for treatment. One of the invoices showed that the technician was present in the facility on 3/6/36. PIC told inspector that they have a two weeks frequency pest treatment routine ongoing. Ensure that pest control comes routinely to eliminate the pest presence. Inspector will return 3/19/2026 to re-inspect for pest presence.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed the gasket of the prep cooler on the far end of the cook line to broken and held together using a white tape. PIC was made aware. make sure that the prep cooler tasted is repaired to prevent food spoilage. Ensure that the appropriate repairs are done to allow the doors of the prep cooler to close properly.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed a leakage in the plumbing lines under the triple sink at the bar. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that this leak is sealed to be in compliance with the LAW.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed multiple instances of missed hand washing opportunities. Discussed with PIC, education was provided to remind staff to always wash hands in between donning new gloves, or coming into contact with soiled surfaces. Inspector observed staff adjust clothing, discarding items directly in contact with gloves into trash, all while no hand washing occurred. Ensure staff is hand washing at a frequency that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed staff members switch between tasks with soiled gloves. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper glove wearing procedures. Staff member removed gloves, rewashed hands, and placed new gloves on. Ensure after use, gloves are not being reused for multiple tasks to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.15(A) Gloves, Use Limitation. (A) If used, single-use gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with ready-to-eat food or with raw animal food, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed in use ice scoop and ice scoop bin to be soiled with red food splash. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop and container were placed through wash, rinse, and sanitize process. Ensure ice scoop are clean and are being stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Observed the following date marking issues:
1) (Repeat) Observed multiple sauce bottles located at the front line, front line cooler, and back sauce prep cooler to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. 
2) Observed a container of jalapeños to be held past date marking maximum date. 
3) In use juice purées at drive thru window observed to be held past date marking maximum date. 
4) In use lemonade observed to be held past date marking maximum date. 
5) In use butter observed to be held past date marking maximum date. 

Discussed with PIC, all items were discarded. PIC claimed items were going to be pulled and discarded, however multiple items were dated to be discarded multiple days ago. Ensure staff is properly date marking any TCS item, and that all TCS items are following the 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed left dipping well to be not turned on upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, dipping well was turned on while inspector was washing hands to start inspection. Ensure any in use dipping wells is turned on during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 3-304.12(D) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (D) In running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist food such as ice cream or mashed potatoes.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following areas to be soiled with food debris:
1) (Repeat) Observed significant food debris accumulation at the chicken prep area, mainly the containers heavily soiled with flour and egg yolk.
2) The sauce holder to the right of front hot holding line.
3) The front line bottom sauce cooler.
4) Freezer to the right of breading station. 

Discussed with PIC, the following locations will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact areas at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure all members of staff that handle food have a valid food handlers license available within facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: (TWICE REPEAT) No employees at the establishment had access to a CFPM license. Ensure that at least one employee has access to their Certified Food Protection Manager credentials at all times food is being prepared. Correct by next routine inspection (at least 90 days from today).
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chlorine sanitizer in the sani bucket was unreadable at the beginning of today’s inspection. PIC was made aware. The sani bucket was remade. The new concentration tested at 100 ppm. Ensure that the sanitizer concentration is monitored at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following were observed soiled. 
1. The nozzles on the soda machine were observed soiled. 
2. The internal surface of the coffee makers were observed soiled.
Education was carried out. The nozzles were removed to be cleaned. The internal surface of the coffee makers were wiped clean and sanitized. Inspector reinspected the soda nozzles and the surface of the coffee makers.  They showed evidence of being cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are routinely monitored, cleaned, and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed the door seals of the prep cooler in the kitchen to be repaired with duct tape. Discussed with PIC and Cook, both informed inspector that the parts are already being looked at to properly repair the unit. Ensure that equipment is smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Duct tape is not considered smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Ensure this is completed by the next routine inspection (at least 90 days from now).

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following facility maintenance and cleaning issues were observed. 
1. (REPEAT x2) Inspector observed the wall above the mops sink splash guard to be crumbling. Ensure this area is repaired and repainted to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface.
2. Grease and soil accumulations were observed beneath the fryers, grill, and stove in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. Ensure that these accumulations are cleaned to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
3. Inspector observed the accumulation of dust and soil on the shelvings in the dish room. Ensure that these accumulations are shelvings are routinely monitored and cleaned.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a leakage and rots in the ceiling on the far end of the dry storage area by the walk-ins in the basement. PIC was made area. PIC informed inspector that a technician is scheduled to come and do the repairs soon. Ensure that this is repair to ensure that the facility is in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector was unable to verify food handler training certification during today’s inspection. PIC said that those documents were locked away and they had no access to them. Inspector told PIC to have copies of certifications in a folder accessible for inspection purposes. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(1) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE (PIC) shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. 

The PIC is not currently a CFPM and is missing critical food safety knowledge at the time of this inspection. Education was given in relation to the observed violations and concerns noted during this inspection. More knowledge is needed and would normally be covered by the CFPM course that is required. While education will be deemed as sufficient at this time other enforcement is likely if this becomes an ongoing issue.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there is not a CFPM available in the facility. The kitchen manager stated that they should be going through the process soon. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all food handling shifts in the facility moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen would not dispense paper towels. Investigation showed that the towels were not fed into the equipment correctly. The PIC was unable to get the equipment functioning correctly. A set of paper towels were set out for hand washing to correct. 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:

The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
citation_text:
3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours. 

A half pan of cooked hamburgers was observed on the front of the grill with internal temperatures of 56F. The pan is not on a hot element for the equipment. The kitchen manager stated that they were letting the items warm up before they would get an order to cook them. This is not a safe practice and would allow for temperature abuse of TCS foods. Education was conducted and the pan moved back to dish to correct. Cease this process immediately. Keep all TCS foods either above 135F or below 41F with a quick change between to the two temperature ranges.

title: Approved thawing methods used.

4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

citation_text: 4-901.11(A) Equipment and Utensils, Air-Drying Required. The PIC was informed and stated that she is training new opening staff that failed to order the cooler correctly. The beef was moved to the bottom of the cooler during the inspection. Ensure staff are educated on proper storage order policy to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed deli beef and deli turkey in the bottom of the cook line prep cooler to be stored past its 7-day date mark. The beef was marked 2/24 and the turkey was marked 2/23. Ensure staff are monitoring coolers daily and discarding any items stored beyond 7 days. The items were discarded during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

comment: The Certified Food Protection Manager left for a meeting during the inspection. Ensure that there are enough Certified Food Protection Managers to cover all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to be sweeping the floor and then use their bare hands to season cooked fries. CORRECTED- The fries were discarded and the employee was educated to never use their bare hands to contact ready-to-eat foods (see violation #9). The employee was also educated that handwashing should always be done when switching tasks, especially when going from sweeping to food preparation or cooking. Ensure that all employees are educated on washing hands when switching tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed to be sweeping, then use their bare hands to season cooked fries. CORRECTED- The fries were discarded. The employee was educated that ready-to-eat food items should never be touched with bare hands and that handwashing is needed when going from sweeping to any type of food preparation or cooking. Ensure that all staff are educated on never using their bare hands to touch ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a pan containing raw bacon above a container of their cooked “Kitchen Sink” dish in the bottom of a preparation cooler on the cook-line. CORRECTED- The storage order of the two items was switched to the “Kitchen Sink” dish being above the pan of raw bacon. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order to make sure that food is being protected during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

comment: There were dishes that had been cleaned and placed with the clean dishes that were observed to still have stickers for date-marking on them.
