citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There was reduced oxygen packaged salmon observed to be in the bottom of the cooler that was still in its packaging. Reduced oxygen packaged salmon should be removed from its reduced oxygen environment before being thawed to reduce the risk of botulism. CORRECTED- The staff were educated on this and the salmon in the cooler drawer all had a slit placed in it. Ensure that staff are educated on proper thawing procedures for reduced oxygen packaged fish.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were rodent droppings observed in the dry storage room next to the cook-line. The facility currently has Sentinel coming every other day, according to the PIC. The facility and their pest control are aware of the pest issue. There were large holes observed to be in the wall of this storage room that would allow entry of rodents into the room. A follow up is scheduled for 3/16/2026 to ensure that the rodent droppings have been cleaned up and that appropriate actions are being taken.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair:

1. There is tape on the missing handle of the left door of the double door cooler. Tape is not an approved repair mechanism. Ensure that this door handle is properly repaired and the tape is removed.
2. FIRST REPEAT- There is a build-up of ice in both of the outside walk-in freezers. One of the walk-in freezer doors has a gasket that is in disrepair. Ensure that both walk-in freezers are repaired to prevent ice build-up and that all existing ice is removed to allow all surfaces to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The outside of the white storage containers in the storage room. 
2. The fan covers of the double-door cooler in the dish area. 
3. The fan covers of the outside walk-in coolers. Both have an accumulation of dust on them. 
4. The light covers above the cook-line are observed to have a slight accumulation of dust on them. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIRD REPEAT- It was observed that the caulk behind the dish line sprayer is cracked and peeling. The PIC stated that this is due to the table being moved when the dish machine was replaced last week. Ensure that the caulk is replaced to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface transition between the dish table and wall. Due to this being a third repeat violation, the PIC stated that they could re-caulk the table to the wall by 3/16/2026. The inspector will follow up on 3/16/2026 to ensure that the caulking has been re-done and that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed washing hands and turning off the faucet without using a barrier. The employee was educated by the inspector on proper handwashing procedures, and the person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to review proper handwashing practices with all employees. Ensure a barrier, such as a paper towel, is used to turn off the faucet after handwashing to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The pizza holder machine was observed to have food debris accumulation from the previous day. CORRECTED: The inspector advised the PIC to always clean the pizza holder machine at the end of the day after food operation hours since it is a food contact surface. The machine was cleaned to sight and touch by an employee during the inspection. Ensure food contact surfaces are kept free of food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A sanitizer bucket was not observed at the facility when the inspector arrived. CORRECTED: The PIC prepared a sanitizer bucket at the start of the inspection. Ensure sanitizer bucket is available and replaced every 2 - 4 hours during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: After two cycles, the dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm. It appeared that the sanitizer bucket was empty. The person-in-charge replaced the bucket and the machine was retested at 100ppm (CL). Violation corrected on site. Be sure to monitor levels of sanitizer buckets to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly, as this helps to maximize the effectiveness against the spread of pathogens.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Both soda guns in the bar area were observed with dried liquid debris on the inner surfaces (inside nozzles). Shown to the PIC and the surfaces were sanitized during the visit to correct the violation. The facility mentioned that the nozzles are cleaned every night. Suggested wiping the surfaces with a sanitizer towel to remove debris from hard to reach places. Ensure that the surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Various Time/Temperature Control (TCS) foods were observed without proper date marking. These items included many white sauces, cooked shrimps, and cheese sauce. Shown to the PIC and the sauces were marked with the preparation date and the shrimps were discarded. Violation corrected. Ensure that all TCS Foods that will be held in house overnight are date marked and discarded if held longer than seven days after preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Upon arrival, there weren’t any sanitizer buckets available throughout the kitchen. The kitchen was in full service and was in the midst of preparing food. Discussed with the PIC and two sanitizer buckets were prepared for both the pizza and grill station. Each bucket tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always available during food prep to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of the double door standing cooler to be in disrepair. Inspector showed the equipment to the person in charge (PIC), who stated they will put a work order in. Ensure gaskets are replaced by the next routine inspection so that all equipment is in proper repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) The dish machine was registering low on the inspector’s and facility’s test strips at the beginning of the inspection. The jug of concentrate had appeared to have off gassed. A new jug was attached to the machine and it was brought up to effective levels to correct. 2) (REPEAT) The sani buckets in the front of the kitchen as well as the bar area were observed low at the beginning of the inspection. These are the other two buckets in the facility from the one noted on the previous routine inspection and are a repeated situation. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets during this inspection to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle of the Cherry Pepsi fountain drink was observed heavily soiled during the inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned/sanitized the nozzle during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

The light in the walk in freezer would not turn on during the inspection. The inspector returned to this location at the end of the inspection as the PIC indicated that it would take a short while for the bulbs to warm up. The room was still dark at the later observation point even thought the light was left on. The inspector also turned the light off and back on and waited a few minutes to no avail. The PIC is instructed to exchange the bulbs (most likely fix) or contact an electrician if new bulbs do not fix the issue prior to the next routine inspection. The freezer must have effective lighting to ensure food and employee safety. Ensure effective lighting at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The internal surface of the coffee maker was observed with a build up of soil. 
PIC was made aware. PIC instructed a staff member to clean and sanitize the coffee maker. After the cleaning and sanitation, inspector inspected the coffee maker to confirm the soil removal and sanitation. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the coffee maker are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility maintenance issues that could impede proper cleaning.
1. (TWICE) Inspector observed broken tiles under the dish machine.
2. The coving along the wall behind the grill and fryers on the cook line. 
3. The wall covering above the pipes beneath the electrical panels was observed missing. 
Discussed with PIC, who assured the inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned areas are cleaned and repaired providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: A staff member was observed not using a barrier after handwashing to shut off the faucet. Education was carried out. The staff member rewashed their hands following the appropriate procedures for drying their hands and shutting the faucet off. Ensure that a barrier is always use to shut off the facet after handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer within the sani buckets were reading at 0ppm during the inspection. Education was carried out. A staff member remade the sani buckets and they tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer concentration are frequently checked to maintain appropriate sanitation of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Handwashing soap was not observed at the handwashing sink in the restroom. The person-in-charged (PIC) was informed by the inspector and handwashing soap was made available. Ensure handwashing soap is always available at the handwashing sink in the restroom.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Disposable towels were not observed in the handwashing sink at the restroom. The PIC was informed by the inspector and disposable paper towels were made available. Ensure disposable paper towels are available at the handwashing sink at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan covers in the walk-in cooler was observed to have dust accumulation.
2. Spilled liquid soap from a Tide laundry detergent bottle was observed behind the shelf in the walk-in cooler. 
3. The shelf in the 3 door cooler for storing milk was observed to have soil accumulation.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the areas mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. The PIC was informed. Ensure hot water is provided at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. The inspector will follow-up on March 16, 2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIRD REPEAT: The following areas were observed to be in need of repairs:

1. The space between the wall and the three-compartment sink was observed to be in need of caulking. Ensure the space is sealed to prevent water from entering and causing mold growth.
2. The ceiling tiles in the hallway behind the walk-in cooler and the hallway leading to the restroom were observed to be missing. Some of the tiles in both areas were also observed to be soggy. The PIC stated the landlord would be renovating the facility, including the ceiling tiles. Ensure the tiles are replaced for easy cleaning.
3. The space between the wall and the handwashing sink in the restroom was observed to be in need of caulking. Ensure the space is sealed to prevent water from entering and causing mold growth. 
4. Broken floor tiles and a sinking floor were observed in the backroom used for storing packs of water and paper towels. Ensure the floor tiles are replaced.
5. Bare wood was observed on the wall across the three-compartment sink. Ensure the bare wood is covered for easy cleaning. 

The followed areas were discussed with the PIC to have them repaired before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Wet mop head was observed inside the three-compartment sink (used as a mop sink) facing downwards. The PIC was informed and educated on proper mop drying technique. Ensure wet mop heads are placed on a wringer basket or hanged up to allows them air-dry properly.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed changing tasks during food preparation without washing hands. The employee was observed preparing coffee, wiping the coffee nozzle with sanitizer, and repeatedly scooping ice from the ice bin to prepare beverages without washing hands between tasks. The person-in-charged (PIC) was informed that this practice may result in contamination, including potential chemical contamination if sanitizer residue remains on hands when handling ice and preparing beverages. CORRECTED: The PIC was instructed by the inspector to review proper handwashing procedures with employees and the employee washed hands before continuing task. Ensure employees wash their hands when changing tasks during food preparation, especially after using sanitizer to wipe the coffee nozzle to prevent food contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The three ice bins at the server station were observed uncovered during the inspection and not all three bins were being used at the same time. Food residue was observed along the top corner edges of each ice bin. CORRECTED: The inspector instructed the PIC to keep the ice bins covered when not actively in use. Ensure ice bins are kept covered when not actively in use to prevent contamination of ice.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the sealant between the counter and wall in the dish machine to be damaged and soiled. Ensure sealant is removed and replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The countertop above the triple sink and the handsink is bare wood. Be sure that bare wood is painted so that the surface is smooth, easily cleanable, and non absorbent. Additionally, there is a soft spot observed on the floor in front of the triple sink. Be sure that floors are free of holes and are always in good condition. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The scoop for sugar in the kitchen was observed to be a cup that did not have a handle on it. Discussed this with the PIC. CORRECTED- The scoop was removed and replaced with a scoop with a handle. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods always have handles on them to prevent contamination from bare-hand contact.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:

Ensure dish machine is working up to the manufactures standards and at the proper concentration (100ppm CL).

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed multiple drawers holding cleaned utensil to have food debris accumulation. Discussed with PIC, drawers will be cleaned and utensil will be put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. Ensure all clean utensil are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at the back triple sink. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. Ensure a licensed plumber services leak and facility to continue to monitor plumbing for any possible leaks.
citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair in the following locations:
1) Black mold was observed to be present at the caulking to the left of the dish machine. 
2) Caulking was observed to be soiled with food debris at the back kitchen hand sink. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the baffles of the ice machine to contain a slight soil accumulation. Discussed proper process to clean/ sanitize machine with the person in charge (PIC). Inspector will return on or by 3/18/26 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed plates at the front counter stored with the food contact surface up. CORRECTED- the PIC inverted plated. Ensure all food contact surfaces are stored in a manner than prevents against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without washing their hands in the kitchen area. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that hand washing is taking place when needed at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The bar dish machine was not observed to have effective levels of CL sanitizer for food contact surfaces during the inspection. The concentrate jug was changed by the PIC and still did not adjust to effective levels. A third jug was brought out and looked significantly more yellow than the previous fresh jug. Once primed this brought the effective concentration up to acceptable levels and corrected the violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The salad prep cooler was observed with internal temperatures for lettuce, cheeses and house made mayo based sauces are observed in the 51F-52F range. These items were brought into this cooler this morning during prep (approximately 5 hours ago). The foods were discarded to correct and the cooler should be monitored moving forward to ensure effective cold holding is taking place.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The egg wash (milk and eggs) on the prep line were observed holding around 60F in its ice bath. The ice is only touching the bottom of the inner pan and the pans are located between the grill and the fryers. The current set up does not allow for ice to surround the egg wash with the current equipment. Education was conducted with the PIC and staff. The current egg wash was discarded and a new set up with a larger ice pan and an egg wash pan that allows for the ice to surround ice will be used moving forward. Ensure that the ice is maintained at a level around the food that is higher than the level of the food. Monitor the egg wash temperatures throughout use times to ensure that effective cold holding is maintained at all times.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. 

A pan of white sauce is observed in the right most prep cooler during the inspection. This pan came from a batch observed earlier in the inspection on a counter cooling and was observed at 60F-80F depending on where the internal temperature was observed. Education was conducted with the PIC. This equipment is not sufficient for cooling hot foods, especially while the cooler is in use for active food preparation. The pan was moved to the walk ins for rapid cooling. Stirring is also suggested because of the temperature gradient observed. Ensure that all foods are cooled effectively at all times in the facility moving forward.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the standing cooler by the handwashing sink and milk cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. The fan vent in the standing cooler by the handwashing sink was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The inner top surface above the coffee filter was observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The outer surface of the juice machine, especially the surface close to the orange juice nozzle was observed to have soil accumulation.

The PIC was instructed to have those surfaces cleaned by the inspector. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are kept free of soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were not signed employee reporting agreements available for any of the employees. The PIC was given copies in both Spanish and English. A follow up is scheduled for 3/13/2026 to ensure that all employees have signed an employee reporting agreement. Ensure that once all employees have signed an agreement, that these are kept in a safe, accessible place to be shown for all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
The following improper storage order was observed in the facility: 

1. A plate of raw chicken over a pan of raw chorizo. CORRECTED- The raw chicken was moved to be below the raw chorizo. 
2. There was a cold holding unit that the PIC stated should be a freezer. The PIC explained that it has not been freezing correctly. The unit was observed to be approximately 31F to 35F during the inspection. There was observed to be raw beef, raw chicken, and raw chorizo above cooked chicken and produce in this cold holding unit. All raw beef chicken, and chorizo items in the unit were moved to be on the bottom shelf to protect the other food items in the unit from contamination. 

Storage order was discussed with the PIC and a handout in both Spanish and English was given to the PIC. Ensure that staff are educated on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The bleach in the facility is observed to not be EPA-Registered and is meant for whitening and brightening laundry. This bleach is being used for their sanitizer buckets. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled for 3/6/2026 to ensure that an EPA-Registered bleach has been obtained for the facility. Bleach that is used for sanitizing food-contact surfaces should be EPA-Registered.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The only probe thermometer that is available in the facility is not meant for checking the temperatures of cold food items. The probe thermometer only starts measuring at 50F and above. A follow up is scheduled for 3/13/2026 to ensure that there is a probe thermometer in the facility that can measure the temperature of cold food items. Ensure that there is always a probe thermometer in the facility that can measure the temperature of both cold and hot food items.
citation_text: 4-204.112(E) Temperature Measuring Devices. (E) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES on WAREWASHING machines shall have a numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1°C or 2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There were salsa bowls and chip baskets that were observed to not be inverted and the food-contact surfaces are exposed to contamination. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that these baskets or bowls are either inverted, have a shelf over them, or are covered to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is a leak coming from the pipes under the handwashing sink in the kitchen and it is allowing waste water to spill onto the floor. A follow up is scheduled for 3/6/2026 to ensure that this leak has been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to prevent waste water from leaking.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There were observed to be personal food items on the middle shelf of a double-door cooler. Discussed getting a tub or bucket and labeling it personal for employees to place their personal items in. This bucket should be on the bottom shelf of the cooler to protect the items for the facility from contamination. Personal storage should be in an area that does not expose food, equipment, linens, and single-service items to contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any hand soap available in the employee bathroom. Discussed with the PIC and hand-soap was provided to correct the violation. Be sure that every hand-sink has a supply of soap to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Several Time/Temperature Control foods (TCS) stored on the steam table were probed between 91F - 96F. These foods included mashed potatoes, green beans, corn, shredded pork, etc. The foods were placed on the steam table no longer than two hours prior to the inspection. Foods were reheated on the stove to at least 165F to correct the violation. The water inside of the steam table was probed to ensure that the table was working properly (probed 175F). Ensure that TCS foods are always hot held at 135F or above to maintain proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was mold observed on a package of dinner rolls. Shown to the PIC and the rolls were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that food items are in good condition and never containing mold.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple incidents of employees switching tasks without washing hands. CORRECTED- inspector discussed times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC). Ensure all employees frequently review required times to wash hands, which includes but is not limited to: after cleaning, after touching personal items, when switching between handling raw and ready to eat food items, etc.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the soap dispenser in the restroom nearest the back door to not be dispensing. CORRECTED, the PIC removed and cleaned the dispenser, to be placed at the sink basin for patrons to dispense themselves. Discussed purchasing a pump soap until the current dispenser is repaired or replaced with the PIC. Ensure all sinks designated for hand washing always have warm running water, paper towels, and soap for proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed the stem thermometer within the facility to be out of calibration. CORRECTED- the PIC calibrated the thermometer using the ice water method. Ensure all stem thermometers are maintained in proper calibration to ensure proper cooking, cooling, and reheating temperatures.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- Metal shelving used for container storage was observed to be rusted. The PIC has cleaned the rust off of some of the shelves, however due to the design of the shelves/ amount of surface area that is currently rusted, replacing them will prevent potential for contamination of the food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No certified food protection manager (CFPM) was observed in the facility at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED: The CFPM showed up later during the inspection. The inspector discussed with the person-in-charge (PIC) to have another employee certified in food protection management, so that a CFPM can be present during hours of operation. Ensure a CFPM is available at the facility during all hours of food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: A stack of plastic containers were observed on the edge of the designated handwashing sink by the three-compartment sink. CORRECTED: The PIC removed the containers after being informed by the inspector. Ensure the handwashing sink is easily accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [PF]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the walk-in and bottom of the pizza prep table coolers. The PIC was informed and instructed to provide internal thermometers in each cooler to allow for proper temperature monitoring, especially in the event of equipment failure. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the warmest part of each cooler to accurately monitor internal temperatures.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall tiles under the soap dispenser, between the handwashing sink and pizza prep table was observed to be breaking from the wall at the top and the surface. The PIC was informed to have the tiles caulked back to the wall. Ensure the wall tiles are replaced for easy cleaning and also to prevent possible hideout for pests.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: A wet mop head was observed stored on the surface of the mop sink with the mop head facing downward.  CORRECTED - The PIC was informed that mop heads must be stored in a manner that allows for proper air-drying. The mop head was placed on the wringer basket by the PIC to facilitate adequate air-drying. Ensure mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
An employee handling food was observed to have an expired food handlers’ certificate (expired 3 years ago). The PIC stated the employee has been scheduled to take the certified food protection manager class on March 4, 2026.  The inspector instructed the PIC to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Hand washing should be taking place regularly and consistently during food operations, and specifically prior to donning gloves and when changing tasks. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with employees to ensure safe practices are always taking place in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted with both current workers. Ensure hand washing is completed correctly at all times, including using a clean barrier to turn off the faucet to protect the freshly cleaned hands from re-contamination.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were not signed employee health reporting agreements for any employees. CORRECTED- The facility only has a total of four employees currently and all employees were present at the time. All employees signed an employee reporting agreement. Ensure that these are kept in a safe, accessible place, as these will need to be shown during all health inspections. Employees should be informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with the law, to the person in charge, information about their health as it relates to diseases that are transmissible through food.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following food was observed to be exposed to contamination due to its packaging:

1. There were observed to be unpackaged tortillas being stored in plastic grocery bags. CORRECTED- The tortillas were voluntarily discarded and the PIC was educated that plastic grocery bags are NOT a food-contact surface. Grocery bags should never be used to directly store unpackaged items into. 
2. There was an opened can of tomato purée in the bottom of the preparation cooler. CORRECTED- The tomato purée was transferred into another container. The PIC was educated that tomatoes are acidic and can erode the can, causing the potential for contamination to the tomato purée. Ensure that cans are never used as a means of storage and that food is always transferred to another container. 

Food packages should always protect the integrity of the contents so that food is not exposed to adulteration or potential contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a package of raw pigs feet observed to be above empanadas in the bottom of the preparation cooler in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The PIC switched the storage order of the items. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzles in the kitchen were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine were both cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that employees are educated to clean both the soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine. Food-contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was an open bottle of Hidden Valley Italian Dressing and an open bottle of Parmesan cheese that both stated to “Refrigerate after opening” that were observed to be on a shelf at room temperature in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they had likely been open for days and voluntarily discarded both bottles. Ensure that staff are educated to read labels and are properly storing Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: There was a bottle of NyQuil observed to be on a shelf in the kitchen next to a package of tortillas. CORRECTED- The PIC voluntarily discarded the NyQuil and was educated that poisonous or toxic materials should never be above or next to food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single service articles. Ensure that food is not being exposed to contamination from poisonous or toxic materials. The inspector also discussed with the PIC to make sure that employees are not working when sick.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There were not ambient thermometers observed to be in either of the bar coolers. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that there are ambient thermometers in all mechanically hot or refrigerated cold holding units.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: There were pots and plastic bins observed to be stored on the floor in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The PIC and an employee moved them onto a shelf that is more than six inches above the floor. Ensure that cleaned equipment and utensils are stored at least six inches above the floor.

(A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The cover on the steam table needs removed to allow it to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. Seal the hole around the plumbing to the left of the bar handwashing sink. Ensure that the sealant that is used is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. If spray foam is used, ensure that it is cut flush and painted to seal it. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- Paint the bare wood above the triple sink in the bar area. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- Seal the wall board to the trim tiles throughout the kitchen.
5. FIRST REPEAT- Seal the holes in the stainless steel wall behind the cook-line. 
6. FIRST REPEAT- Caulk the drain boards in the dish area. 
7. FIRST REPEAT- Repair or provide stoppers for the triple sink to allow the sinks to hold water. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There were rat droppings observed to be in the basement in the area with the water heater and ice machine. The PIC stated that these are old droppings. Ensure that these old droppings are cleaned up to allow for monitoring of any rodents. The basement of the facility has a history of a rodent issue and proper cleaning of this area will allow for monitoring of any rodents. A follow up will be conducted on 3/13/2026 to ensure that the droppings have been cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed small amounts of black mold to be present in ice machine. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be properly cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation. Inspector has scheduled a follow up for 3/11/2026.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed juice dispenser to be soiled with food splash under juice units. Discussed with PIC, are will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There were packages of reduced oxygen packaged tilapia that were observed to be thawed without being removed from their packaging. CORRECTED- The PIC and another club member were educated on ROP fish needing to be removed from packaging immediately after being thawed or prior to thawing. The tilapia was removed from its packaging during the inspection. The ROP fish that is kept in its packaging while thawing leads to a risk for botulism. Ensure that members are educated on this practice.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. The PIC was shown and stated that a bucket was intended for this purpose to allow for running water. The fish was placed into the bucket during this inspection and begun to have running water during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
citation_text:
3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

A knife was observed stored in the small gap between shelving and wall in the northern most prep cooler. The PIC was shown and stated that it was there to help keep the lid open. The knife was removed and observed soled with food debris. It was moved to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that soiled utensils are stored so that they do not contaminate surfaces in the facility that are not easily cleanable. Ensure that items intended to not be food contact surfaces are not used as food contact surfaces.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The cake spatula container in the second drawer of the cake prep area was observed to have debris accumulation. The person-in-charge was informed. Ensure that the container is cleaned and kept free of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival, the handwashing sink was observed obstructed with a cooking pan and dishes. The cooking equipment was removed from the sink to correct the violation. Given that the handwashing sink is used by multiple parties, the kitchen employee is responsible for keeping the sink free of dishes and unobstructed for handwashing purposes. Ensure that handsinks are always available for employees to wash hands.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) The junction between the wall and left side of the sink in the women’s bathroom was observed to have a crack in the caulking that is providing a gap. 2) The caulk around the sink in the men’s bathroom was observed cracking and providing a gap. The PIC was notified and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks have smooth and easily cleanable surfaces sealing them to the walls moving forward.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspectors observed the water inlet from the bun steamer on the cook like to be dripping. Ensure all food equipment is maintained in good repair. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspectors observed personal cell phones on the barista counter as well as on the shelving above the cook line. Personal items must be stored away from areas of food preparation. Cease this practice.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: 3RD REPEAT: An accumulation of pink soil debris/ biofilm was observed on the baffle of the ice machine. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized the baffle of the ice machine. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

comment: Inspector observed the chemical sanitizing dish machine to be dispensing 0 ppm Chlorine. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) primed the dish machine, which was then observed to be dispensing 50 ppm Chlorine. Ensure the dish machine is primed and tested at a frequency to ensure the proper concentration of food contact surfaces- as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the tamarind and tomato sauces at the front counter cooler (identified as being Temperature Control for food Safety- (TCS) by the PIC based on ingredients and processes) to be above 41F (stem thermometer reading of 56F). CORRECTED- the items were moved from the working cooler this morning, and the facility will implement TIME AS A CONTROL until the cooler is serviced. Ensure items are used or discarded within FOUR hours until the cooler is observed to be cold holding food items at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Food items in the walk in cooler were stated to have been prepared in previous days did not have date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC placed dates on the foods and replaced old stickers that did not reflect the date of preparation. Ensure all TCS food items are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days. The day of preparation counts as day one. Date marking must be dated based on the oldest prepared ingredient.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the under counter cooler to have an ambient temperature of 51F, and as such not properly cold holding food items (see violation #22). TCS food items must be held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens that may cause foodborne illness. Inspector will return by 03/06 to ensure the cooler has been serviced or replaced.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.

citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. comment: REPEAT - The front counter sanitizer bucket was observed to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium and the sanitizer bucket by the cook-line was observed to be at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. title: Food handler training
comment:
Some employees handling foods were observed to not have food handlers’ certificates. The PIC was instructed to ensure all employees handling foods are certified in safe food handling. Ensure all food handlers obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

comment:
