2. Canned mandarin oranges (significant dent in body)
3. Canned beans (dent along the seam)

CORRECTED - The person-in-charge was informed and the dented cans were removed from the shelf. Dented cans can have the entry and harborage of Botulism, ensure canned foods with dents are removed from the shelf and not served in meals to the children.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. The kitchen manager who is food manager certified arrived shortly after the inspection began to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always at least one individual who is food manager certified present at all times.
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown 
proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
There are several areas that are in need of cleaning:
- overhead hood baffles are soiled with accumulated grease
- soiled inner surfaces of the prep coolers (food debris)
- the milkshake mixers were accumulated with dried milk debris

Ensure that these surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet during the inspection. Education was conducted with the PIC and they were instructed to review hand washing procedures with employees and provide sufficient oversight to ensure hand washing takes place correctly in the facility. Ensure that hands are not recontaminated at the end step of the hand washing process in the facility.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A container of beef was observed on the floor under shelving in the walk in cooler. A conversation took place with the PIC and the container was moved to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored so that possible contamination is prohibited.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The women’s hand-sink is in need of recaulking. The current caulk is peeling away from the wall. Discussed with the owner and he mentioned that the facility will have the sink recaulked soon. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair to prevent accumulated debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The soda gun holder, as well as the soda gun nozzle in the bar area were observed soiled with dried liquids. The person-in-charge mentioned that the gun holder was recently replaced. Both the nozzle and the holder were sanitized during the visit to correct the violation. 
2. A cutting board was observed to be stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. CORRECTED- The cutting board was pulled to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure that cutting boards are stored in an area away from contamination. 
3. There were knives stored between the preparation cooler and the wall, where the knives were in contact with the wall. The wall and side of the preparation cooler are not food-contact surfaces. CORRECTED- The knives were pulled to be cleaned. Ensure that knives are being stored in a manner that does not expose them to contamination. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
The following food items were observed to be kept past their 7-day date-marking:

1. Two containers of cooked and cooled wings with a date of 2/18.
2. A container of sautéed peppers and onions with a date of 2/18.
3. A container of potato skins with a date of 2/18.
4. A container of cooked chicken with a date of 2/18.

CORRECTED- All of these food items were discarded. Ensure that Time/Temperature control foods are discarded by the end of the 7th day.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The triple sink is observed to not be fully sealed to the wall and the caulking is in a state of disrepair. Ensure that the triple sink is fully sealed to the wall and that the sealing is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. The kitchen manager who is food manager certified arrived shortly after the inspection began to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always at least one individual who is food manager certified present at all times.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The can opener blade was observed soiled with dried food debris. Discussed with the person-in-charge that this surface comes in contact with food and shall be cleaned frequently. The PIC placed the can opener into the dish machine to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation, as well as cross contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were at least three cooked dishes that were stored in the walk in cooler that lacked proper date marking. The dishes included but aren't limited to meatballs, deli meat, shredded beef, etc. The PIC mentioned that the dishes had been stored inside of the unit for a few days. The facility was instructed to date mark each item, however, the PIC voluntarily discarded the dishes to correct the violation. Discussed that if cooked dishes will be stored in house longer than 24 hours, the items must be date marked with the day that it is prepared. Ensure that TCS foods are properly date marked and monitored so that they aren’t stored past seven days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The dish table along the dish machine is in need of recaulking. Discussed with person-in-charge the necessary repairs. Ensure that the dish table is recaulked back to the wall to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on duty at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The owner who is a CFPM arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on duty during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to go outside with gloves on and then return to the cook-line and continue food preparation. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that when engaging in tasks that contaminate gloves, handwashing and changing gloves needs to occur. The employee then proceeded to rinse their hands, without soap, in a non-handwashing sink. The employee was educated on this as well and washed their hands in the handwashing sink. Ensure that food employees are educated on when to wash their hands and change their gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to go outside with gloves on and then return to the cook-line and continue food preparation. The employee was educated that when engaging in tasks that contaminate gloves, handwashing and changing gloves needs to occur. The employee then proceeded to rinse their hands, without soap, in a non-handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The employee was educated on this as well and washed their hands in the handwashing sink. Ensure that all employees are educated that handwashing should only be done in a handwashing sink.
citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The soap dispenser in the women’s bathroom was observed to not be functional and there was no soap at the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The PIC obtained batteries for the soap dispenser and fixed it during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap at every handwashing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Two improper storage orders were observed in the following area:
- Raw chicken wings stored above lemons and other cooked meats inside of the standing cooler (near the back door)
- Raw chicken stored above diced tomatoes and several rolls of raw beef.

Discussed with the person-in-charge that raw chicken has the highest internal cooking temperature of 165F and must always be stored at the bottom shelf of cold holding units. The items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that ready-to-eat RTE foods and ground beef are stored above all raw chicken products to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The employee washing dishes was observed to wash and rinse the dishes, then place them on the clean dish rack without sanitizing. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that after being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils need to be sanitized either manually or through mechanical operations. The triple sink is observed to not have any stoppers that would allow for proper sanitizing in this manner. Stoppers are important to have in case the dish machine is not properly sanitizing. This was discussed with the PIC. The dish machine is properly chemical sanitizing with Chlorine sanitizer and the employee stated that they will be using that for cleaning dishes instead of using the triple sink. Ensure that equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils are being sanitized.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(1) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (1) Except as specified under Subparagraph (C)(2) of this section, a contact time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution specified under 4-501.114(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The Chlorine sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to be at 0ppm. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 150ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are frequently tested and remade if not at a label-recommended concentration. Sanitizer buckets should typically be changed every two to four hours, or sooner if the bucket is heavily used.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The cheese sauce on the steam table was observed to only be at 129F. CORRECTED- An employee reheated the cheese sauce on the stove and the cheese sauce probed to be at 166F. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are being held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were two containers of cooked potatoes that were observed to be cooling within the double-door standing cooler. The potatoes were covered in plastic wrap and probed to be at 67F. The potatoes were date-marked that they had been cooked on 2/25 (today’s date), but the employee was unsure of the exact time the potatoes had been cooked. CORRECTED- The plastic wrap was removed from the top of the potatoes and the potatoes were placed in a standing freezer to allow for more rapid cooling. The potatoes probed to be at 47F at the end of the inspection. The employee was educated that when foods are being cooled, they should be uncovered and there should be less in the pan to allow for more rapid cooling. The potatoes were observed to be mounded in the pan and the employee stated they will place less in the pan going forward. Cooling of foods should be monitored. Foods need to be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours, and then from 70F to under 41F within another four hours, for a total of six hours for cooling.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There was not a probe thermometer observed within the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 3/6/2026 to ensure that a probe thermometer is available and easily accessible in the facility. There should always be a probe thermometer in the facility to allow for measuring the temperature of foods being cooked, cooled, or reheated.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
There was observed to be mashed potatoes in a sour cream container in the bottom of a prep cooler in the kitchen. The facility is observed to be re-using plastic single-use containers for food storage, such as sour cream containers. Food-contact surfaces should be durable, corrosion-resistant, and about to withstand repeated warewashing. Cease re-using these containers for food storage (unless the foods are individually packaged, such as the containers of condiments in the bottom of the server preparation cooler that are being stored in a sour cream container) and obtain containers that are meant to be re-used. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Multiple dishes in the storage area were observed with remaining food debris, oil or a sticky substance still on them. Several of these items are still wet from recent washing. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to dish for recleaning to correct. Ensure that dishes are being completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
citation_text:
3-403.11(A) Reheating for Hot Holding. (A) Except as specified under (B) and (C) and in (E) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the FOOD reach a temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) for 15 seconds. 

A pan of cheese sauce on the prep line was observed at 114F internal temperature during this inspection. Investigation showed that it was pulled from its reheating process to early due to a miscommunication in the kitchen. The cheese was on the cook line approximately 30-45 minutes prior to observation per the cook that pulled it. The pan was allowed to be brought to the stove for rapid reheating to be saved. Another pan was above 165F and moved to the steam table for service to correct. Ensure that the reheating process is completed each time in the facility.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
citation_text:
3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

1) The probe thermometers on the cook line are observed in a cup that is spoiled with food debris and oil accumulation. 2) The knife used at the sandwich perp cooler was observed in the open space between the two cooler lids. This space was cleanable but was not observed clean at the time of the inspection. Both locations were shown to the PIC and the food contact items removed for cleaning. The storage surfaces were also cleaned and sanitized to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact items are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

Three sinks in the facility were observed with leaks at the faucet. The sinks were the bar three part sink, the sprayer faucet by the dish machine and the faucet at the mop sink. The PIC was instructed to have the sinks repaired to remove the leaked prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor under the server drink station is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue and debris on it. A follow up is scheduled for 3/9/2026 to ensure that these floors have been cleaned. Discussed this with the PICs. Ensure that these floors are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Mouse droppings were observed in multiple locations and corners within the kitchen and dry storage areas during today’s inspection. PIC told inspector that they have been having issues with mouse for some time now. However, they are working with maintenance to combat the mouse situation. PIC told inspector that they will continue to monitor and take the necessary measures to eradicate the mouse situation. Ensure that the necessary actions are taken to reduce and eradicate pest activities within the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the paper towel dispenser at the juice hand washing station to be non-operational. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) informed maintenance, who cleared the jam in the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always readily available to complete proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed fragmented caulking behind the hand washing sink of the juice station. Maintain proper repair of physical facilities by resealing the sink to the wall by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) added 2 capfuls of sanitizer, and the sanitizer was observed at 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer used for food contact surfaces is made and tested at a frequency to meet the required concentration as required by the manufacterer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed drawer holding clean utensils to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, utensils were removed and put through the wash, rinse, and sanitize process. While utensils were removed, PIC cleaned and sanitized drawer. Ensure clean utensils are stored in a way that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be showing black mold to the right of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being monitored/replaced as needed to prevent black mold buildup.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment: 410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: REPEAT- The PIC is not a Certified Food Protection Manager. The PIC stated that her son will be working on obtaining their CFPM certificate. Ensure that a CFPM is available to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

A half gallon of half n’ half is observed with an internal temperature of approximately 47F. The air temperature in this cooler was between 47F-49F. The front of house manager was consulted and discarded the dairy product to correct the immediate violation. The plan is to use any of the other coolers in this area moving forward as they were all observed at acceptable temperatures.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple moist rags were observed throughout the facility on counters or shelves. These items should have been held between uses in the nearby sani buckets to prevent pathogenic growth. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. Ensure that all in use rags are stored between uses in buckets of sufficient sanitizer concentration to prevent pathogen growth. The rags were moved during the inspection to their buckets to correct.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT - Inspector observed raw shell egg stored above cut tomato and mushrooms in the top of the prep cooler. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was informed and the eggs were moved to the bottom of the prep cooler

Paper receipt was also observed on the cut tomatoes in the top of the prep cooler. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the receipt was removed. 

Ensure foods are protected from potential contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed to be passing through the back door. The PIC was instructed to have the gap sealed with weather stripping. Ensure the gap is covered to prevent potential entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1. The chest freezer gasket was observed to have soil accumulation.
2. The fan blade covers in the walk-in cooler were observed to have soil accumulation.
3. The non-functional oven in front of the walk-in freezer was observed to have food debris and dust accumulations.
4. Food debris accumulation was observed on clean dishes at the dish area. 

The PIC was informed. Ensure the areas mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The shelves in the walk-in cooler were observed to be rusted. The PIC was instructed to have the shelves coated. Ensure the shelves are kept free of rust by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT - The following areas were observed to be in need of caulking/sealing:

1. Gaps were observed between the walls and the hand washing sinks.
2.  The caulking on the three-compartment sink in the kitchen was observed to be peeling off.

Openings between fixed equipment (sinks) and walls can allow for the entry of water and harborage of mold or bacteria. Ensure the gaps are sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple employees change tasks without hand washing. Discussed the need for ongoing education with the staff regarding times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC). Ensure hands are washed after handling soiled equipment or utensils, after touching cell phones, when switching tasks between handling raw food and ready to eat (RTE) foods, before donning gloves, and after engaging in any tasks that may contaminate the hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed a cup being used as a scoop, submerged in sugar. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the scoop with a gloved hand, and placed a scoop with a handle to be used for scooping sugar in a clean plastic bag. Ensure all ready to eat foods are handled with cleaned gloves hands, or utensils that have a clear differentiation between the hand contact surface and food contact surface.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the heat sanitizing dish machine to reach maximum heat plate temperature of 145, after 4+ cycles. Neither wash or rinse temperature gauges on the outside of the machine were moving during the cycle. Inspector directed the facility to use the triple sink to wash-rinse-sanitize all food contact surfaces until the dish machine has been repaired, and observed sanitizing at a minimum temperature of 160F. Inspector will return on 03/02/26 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple plates and bowls at the serving station stored with the food contact side upwards. CORRECTED- the plates were inverted after the inspector discussed the need for the food contact surfaces to either be covered or inverted when not actively serving to prevent contamination of the food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.[C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact and nonfood contact surfaces in disrepair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Two spatulas hanging in ready to use position on the cook-line were chipped around the perimeter. CORRECTED- spatulas were voluntarily discarded. 
2) The gaskets along the triple door cooler, as well as the warmer (next to the hood system) were frayed or fragmented.
Ensure utensils are checked for integrity to prevent contamination of food. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable. Gaskets should be replaced by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The condensers of the coffee machines contain an accumulation of soil debris.
2) SECOND REPEAT: The black, (3) segmented container holding ready to use utensils at the island across from the hood contains food debris. 
* Line item #2 was previously noted as violation #44, and has since been moved.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket. Inspector discussed proper mop storage with the PIC. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry, to prevent the growth of microorganisms.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair:
1) There is no caulking between the hand washing sink (in front of the office) and the wall.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine contains an accumulation of debris, and is fragmented or absent in multiple areas.
3) Coving between the floor and wall is peeling in the chemical storage closet (directly to the right of the entry).
Fixed equipment should be sealed to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) A tray of cooked dumpling was observed being stored underdressed raw chicken to cool. Education was carried out and the dumpling tray was removed. Ensure that proper storage order is practiced to avoid cross contamination. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Multiple soda nozzles were observed with soil accumulation. PIC was made aware. The nozzles were removed, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed water chestnuts being stored in the can after opening inside the prep cooler. Education was carried out. The chestnuts were placed in the appropriate storage container. Ensure that food items are stored appropriately to avoid contamination. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, therefore recontaminating their hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff. Ensure that the hand washing procedures in the facility protect freshly washed hands from recontamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing prior to food service/handling. Education was conducted and they are instructed to review hand washing with employees. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that it is required in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several items in the storage area used for cleaned dishes are observed with remaining food debris or stickers on them. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to the dish area for re-cleaning to correct. They are instructed to review with all dish washers acceptable levels of cleanliness for the food contact equipment and conduct oversight as needed to ensure that the dishes are cleaned appropriately at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The two display coolers next to the ordering line were observed to be holding TCS foods with internal temperatures of 49F-51F. When discussing with the PIC the items in the coolers were mostly placed into these coolers the day before the inspection in the morning. The only exception were the cannolis which arrived in the cooler approximately 5 hours prior to the inspection. The TCS items observed include multiple containers of ricotta filling, parmesan cheese, roast beef and several slices of cheese cake. The cannolis were allowed to remain until 4pm (six hours) and then be discarded. The remaining TCS items were discarded immediately to correct the violation. The PICs cleaned the filters on the front and back of the coolers to hopefully fix the overall issue. They also stated that they had contacted the owners who were having a company come to ensure that a more in depth maintenance scenario was not needed. The violation is considered corrected at this time with the caveat that the inspector will return in the morning to check if the remedial actions taken during the inspection were sufficient. The PICs are aware that tomorrow’s visit could ensure violations requiring follow ups in the future.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

Two employee cell phones were observed on a counter used for food preparation. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the phones moved to correct the immediate violation. Ensure employee possessions are stored in locations where contamination of foods or food contact surfaces is not a concern.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: There wasn’t any bleach available for responding to a vomit or diarrheal event. Discussed with PIC that bleach should be purchased in order to properly respond to a Norovirus event. The bleach must contain an EPA registration number. Ensure that bleach is purchased and available by the March 2, 2025 followup date.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the dish room lacked paper towels and also hand soap. Discussed with the person-in-charge that every handsink shall be stocked with the essentials for proper handwashing. Ensure that every handsink has warm running water, handsoap, and paper towels at all times. Will follow up on March 2, 2026.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a temperature measuring device available for the heat sanitizing dish machine. A temperature measuring device is necessary for ensuring that the machine is effectively sanitizing food contact surfaces. The person-in-charge mentioned that the facility will purchase thermo stickers in the near future. Ensure that a temperature measuring device is available to monitor sanitizing temperatures. Will follow-up on March 2, 2026.
citation_text: 4-204.115 Warewashing Machines, Temperature Measuring Devices. A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; and (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Various surfaces of the fryer were observed heavily accumulated with grease and food debris. Shown to PIC. The surfaces included inside of the fryer, the outer surface of the fryer, and underneath and around the walls of the fryer. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is an unused steam table stored across from the serving line, as well as an unused cabinet that is stored inside of the dry storage room. Discussed with PIC that items that are no longer needed for operation shall be removed from the premises. Ensure that items are removed, as this may create a harboring environment for unwanted pest and insects.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Food handler training
comment:
None of the employees, other than the only employee who holds a food manager certificate, could produce a copy of their food handler certificate. Discussed with the person-in-charge that all employees who handle clean dishes or food must obtain food handler certificates. Ensure that every employee has a food handler certificate on file by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed four dented cans in the dry storage shelf of the kitchen space. The PIC was informed and the cans were removed from use. In the future, set aside any dented cans and return to distributor. Dented and damaged cans can cause bacterial growth which leads to botulism contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of a cleaning:
1. The interior of the cabinet freezer on the cook line which stores the chicken fried steak.
2. The piping of the hood system above the fryers have accumulated oil and debris which is developing drips.
3. The interior of the hot box has an accumulation of food debris.

Ensure these surfaces are clean to sight and touch during the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
Inspector observed the following freshwater leaks in the facility:
1. The hand sink next to the dish area has a slow leak from the faucet handle.
2. The wall faucet with a hose connected has a considerable leak from the handle.

Ensure these plumbing concerns are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
3rd Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the mop head stored in the bottom of the mop bucket. This storage method does not allow for proper drip drying. The PIC was informed and stated that hanging hooks are located above the mop sink for proper storage. The PIC plans to reeducate staff on proper storage.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed the following areas to be soiled with food debris/soil:
1. The walls of the dish area
2. REPEAT - Floor under ice machines
3. REPEAT - Floor of walk-in freezer
4. Ice accumulation on floors, walls, and ceilings of walk-in freezer

Informed PIC that these areas are in need of a deep clean. Soil accumulation can promote both food-borne pathogen growth as well as potential pest harborage. Ensure floors in facility are cleaned frequently to avoid soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following canned food items were observed to have dents around their seams:
1. Mandarin oranges
2. Whole peeled potatoes x2

CORRECTED - The person-in-charged (PIC) was informed and the dented cans were removed from the shelf. Ensure dented cans are removed from the shelf due to potential contaminants from exposure.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:
1. Bottom of the 3-door cooler at the back storage area has soil accumulation.
2. Shelf for storing clean pots at the walk way has dust accumulation.
3. Shelf for storing clean plate at the salad bar has dust accumulation.

The PIC was informed. Ensure the surfaces mentioned above are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Employee was observed handling non ready to eat food from the prep cooler with their bare hands. CORRECTED- education about times to wash hands was provided. Ensure education about glove usage and  proper hand washing times are reviewed with new staff.
citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Sanitizer for food contact surfaces were observed to be outside of their recommended range in the following locations:
1) FIRST REPEAT The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer at the bar was observed to be at 100 ppm at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the sanitizer was remade and tested to be at 200 ppm of Quaternary ammonium. 
2) The kitchen’s Chlorine bleach sanitizer bucket was observed to be “bleaching out”- indicating too high of a concentration of bleach. CORRECTED- the bucket was diluted to 200 ppm.
Ensure that sanitizer is frequently tested using the facility’s test strips, and remade if not at the label-recommended concentration (200 to 400ppm for Quaternary ammonium and 50-200 ppm Cl for bleach).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed an unlabeled white powder in the dry storage above the mop sink. CORRECTED- the item was identified as baking soda, and labeled accordingly. Ensure white powders (which may be easily mistaken for each other) are labeled once removed from their original container.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the kitchen prep counter. CORRECTED- the cloth was moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of bacteria with high water activity. Dry wiping cloths may be used, as long as there are replaced at least every 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food Handler certificates on file were observed to have been expired. Ensure Food Handler Certificates are renewed every 3 years and maintained on file. New employees should obtain a Food Handler certificate within 30 days of hire. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: There were several packages of cook dinners that lacked proper allergen and ingredient labeling. The dinners were stored in a floor cooler in front of the deli area. Discussed with PIC that all individual dinners will need to list ingredients and allergens. Ensure that packaged food items contain proper allergen and ingredient labeling.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIRD REPEAT- The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.
