citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed multiple dishes to be resting in hand sink. Discussed with PIC, ensure hand sink is solely being used for hand washing. Dished were removed from hand sink.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking behind the kitchen sinks to be cracked. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: FIRST REPEAT - Ambient thermometer was not observed in the walk-in cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to provide an ambient thermometer. Ensure an ambient thermometer is available in the warmest part of the cooler by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The interior white coating of the microwave was observed to be peeling, exposing the underlying material. The PIC was informed. Ensure the microwave is repaired or replaced so that all surfaces are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The surface area around the soda machine nozzles was observed to have soil accumulation. The PIC was informed and instructed to clean the area. Ensure the surface area around the soda nozzles is maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: The restroom handwashing sink was observed to have no hot water available. Corrective Action: The PIC was informed. Ensure hot water is provided at the restroom handwashing sink at all times. The inspector will follow up on 02/23/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. [PF]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The ceiling tile above the mop sink in the dry storage area was observed to be missing. The PIC was informed. Ensure the missing ceiling tile is replaced before next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The ceiling tiles above the three-compartment sink and mop sink at the dry storage area were observed to be soiled. The PIC was informed. Ensure the ceiling tiles are replaced before next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Dirty water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket next to the mop sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure water from mopping is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was an open container of Barbecue sauce that was observed to be on a table in the kitchen and not in refrigeration. This sauce states to “Refrigerate after opening”. CORRECTED- The PIC discarded the Barbecue sauce and was educated to read labels of sauces. Ensure that food items that are Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is a table that has pans holding it up. The PIC stated that the end of the table needs repaired. Ensure that this is repaired. 
2. The dish table to the right of the dish machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in the caulking and needs re-sealed. 
3. The handle of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be broken and is in need of being replaced. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair and that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The small fan in the dish area. CORRECTED- The PIC removed it to be cleaned. 
2. The walk-in cooler fan covers. 
3. The bottom shelf holding sauces and plates across from the pizza oven on the cook-line. There is observed to be an accumulation of dust and soil residue on it. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of pink soil accumulation on the front baffles of the ice machine. Empty the ice machine to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure all food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to have no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding the recommend concentration and process for testing. Sanitizer was observed at a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is made and tested at a frequency to verify the proper concentration for sanitizing food contact surfaces as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed to go to cups of cheese sauce to be hot holding at 119F (verified via stem thermometer). CORRECTED- the 2 cups of cheese sauce were voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Discussed long term solutions with the PIC (either using time as control [foods are used or discarded within 4 hours and marked accordingly], OR filling the bulk container to ensure the warm water is transferring to multiple sides of the container, and then moving it into a to-go container at the time of service. Ensure any temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are hot held at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple TCS food/ drink items without date marking (PIC verified they had been opened or prepared in days prior):
1) Orange juice at bar cooler
2) Salsa at kitchen standing cooler.
CORRECTED- both items were marked with the dates they were opened and prepared. Ensure all TCS foods being held over 24 hours are date marked to be used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed an in-use knife stored between a cutting board and wet cloth. CORRECTED- the knife was brought to the dish area for ware washing. Education about wet wiping cloth/ in use utensil storage was provided. Ensure all in use utensils are stored in a manner that prevents the contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.[C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of debris on multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
1) Rust on the shelves in the walk in cooler 
2) Rust on the shelves to the right of the dish machine.
3) Dust on the monitor cords above the service station in the kitchen.
Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Shelves should be resealed or replaced by the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, which may contaminate ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple instances of coving not sealing to the wall:
1) Cracked tile beneath the dish machine
2) Loose coving on the South wall of the mop room.
Inspector showed these areas to the PIC, and education was provided. Ensure these areas are repaired by the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Dead bugs were observed on the floor close to the emergency exit door and the side of the soda cooler. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated it was due to the gaps in the door at the emergency exit. Ensure the dead bugs are cleaned from the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.112 Removing Dead or Trapped Birds, Insects, Rodents, and Other Pests. Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Light was observed to be passing through the corner of the emergency exit door at the back. The PIC stated an order will be put in to have the door well-fitted. Ensure the gaps are covered or sealed to prevent pests from entering the facility.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handwashing sink in the employee bathroom was observed to have gap between the wall and the handwashing sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the handwashing sink was caulked to the wall during the inspection. Ensure the gap is sealed so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: A zesty orange sauce with “Refrigerate After Opening” was observed on the shelf in the dry storage. CORRECTED - The PIC was educated and the sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are stored in the cooler and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Disinfectant spray and All purpose cleaner with bleach were observed on the ice machine close to the restroom. CORRECTED - The PIC was educated and the chemicals were voluntarily moved to the chemical storage area. Ensure poisonous or toxic materials are not stored above food or food equipment to prevent chemical contamination of food.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Ice buildup was observed in the silver double door cooler. The PIC was instructed to have the cooler defrosted and cleaned to prevent more ice accumulation. Ensure the cooler is defrosted and cleaned to sight and touch by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Dirty water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink at the bar to only dispense cold water- the hot water faucet was nonoperational. All sinks designated for hand washing should be able to reach a minimum temperature of 85F. Inspector will return on 02/24/25 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contact an accumulation of debris:
1) The soda nozzle at the bar banquet room
2) 2 ladles handing in ready to use position with an accumulation of food debris on the food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- items were moved to the dish machine for ware washing. 
3) The water fountain in the hallway contains a significant amount of limescale and biofilm.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods. Inspector will return on 02/24 to check that line items 1 and 3 have been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.  [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple pieces of equipment to be in disrepair:
1) The gaskets along the 3 door refrigerator are frayed.
2) The hinges along the pizza prep cooler are not holding the lid in place.
Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are maintained in proper repair. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in need of physical repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The hand-sink at the (main) bar should be sealed to the wall.
2) FIRST REPEAT: Coving on the West wall of the dry food storage is peeling.
3) FIRST REPEAT: Coving on the wall directly to the right of the entryway of the chemical storage room. Coving is also peeling on the North side behind the water heater.
4) Coving in the Southwest corner of the dry storage is absent.
Items that cannot be moved easily for cleaning should be adhered to the wall. Seal items to wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple cell phones stored on the prep counter of the kitchen. Ensure personal belongings are kept in a designated area, separate from food and nonfood contact surfaces used to serve food to the public to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The sanitizer solution in the sani bucket at the deli bar area was measured at 0 ppm at the beginning of the inspection. Staff was educated and the sani bucket was remade measuring at 200 ppm. Ensure that the sani bucket is monitored and changed at a regular frequency to ensure that food-contact surfaces are appropriately sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed washing hands and turning off the faucet without using a barrier. CORRECTED - The employee was educated by the inspector on proper handwashing procedures, and the person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to review proper handwashing practices with all employees. Ensure a barrier, such as a paper towel, is used to turn off the faucet after handwashing to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Cleaned cooking utensils stored on the dish rack were observed to have food debris remaining on the surfaces. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the utensils were returned to the dish machine for re-washing. Ensure all cooking utensils are properly washed and maintained free of food debris before being stored for use.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [PF]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Chicken in batter (a time/temperature control for safety [TCS] food) was observed in the walk-in cooler with date marking exceeding the maximum allowable holding time of 7 days. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the product was voluntarily discarded. Ensure date marks on TCS foods are routinely monitored and all TCS foods are discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood-contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning:

1. Food debris accumulation was observed in the corners inside the cappuccino machine.
3. Food debris accumulation was observed at the bottom of the container used to store customers’ knives at the server station. CORRECTED - An employee placed the container in the dish machine for cleaning.
5. Soil accumulation was observed on the surface around the juice machine nozzles. CORRECTED - The surface was cleaned during the inspection.
7. Food residue accumulation was observed on the interior top surface of the middle microwave (of three stacked microwaves) across the cook line. CORRECTED - The microwave was cleaned during the inspection.
8. Food debris accumulation was observed on the top surface of the dish machine.

The PIC was informed and instructed to ensure the remaining areas are cleaned prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood-contact surfaces are routinely cleaned and maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to be in need of repairs:

1. The left side of the handwashing sink at the order station needs to be caulked.
2. The bottom of the wooden shelf across the juice machine is bare and needs to be covered. 

The PIC was informed of the areas mentioned above. Ensure the areas mentioned above are repaired so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During the inspection a CFPM was not available in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have a CFPM available at all times that the facility is in operation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

The only hand sink in the bar area was observed with a pitcher in it as well as a pair of blenders in front of it preventing access and use. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain the hand sinks in the facility accessible at all times. The items were moved to correct.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The faucet to the triple sink had a plastic bag wrapped around it to prevent a leak from spraying out. This is not an approved method to repair plumbing. The PIC was instructed to have a plumber repair the faucet prior to the scheduled follow-up. The follow up was pushed back from the usual three days because of the weekend and holiday.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) (REPEAT x2) On arrival the dish machine would not register on the inspector’s CL test strips. The quat test strips showed a little color change but was not sufficient for quat sanitizing either. The PIC was consulted and replaced the jug of quat concentrate with a CL concentrate jug. Once primed the registered correctly on both the inspector’s and facility’s test strips. 2) On arrival the sani bucket would not register correctly on the inspector’s test strips. The bucket was remade by staff to correct. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are at effective levels at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed multiple dead adult roaches on the floor in dry storage. PIC stated the Pest Control Log is in the main office. Advise updating log for Pest Control Provider. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned in their entirety to better monitor pest activity.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated that employees will sign the forms. The inspector provided blank copies to the PIC for each employee to sign. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 02/20/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
comment: The facility juices their orange juice themselves and bottles it. There is observed to not be a Consumer Advisory directly on the bottle. The label only states that the juice is unpasteurized. This was discussed with the PIC that juicing requirements are that if the juice is bottled, there needs to be a Consumer Advisory on the bottle. CORRECTED- The PIC made labels that included the Consumer Advisory and will place these on all future bottles. Ensure that all unpasteurized juice that is bottled includes a Consumer Advisory directly on the packaging.
citation_text: 3-404.11(B) Treating Juice. Juice packaged in a food establishment shall be: (B) Labeled, if not treated to yield a 5-log reduction of the most resistant microorganism of public health significance: (1) As specified under § 3-602.11, and (2) As specified in 21 CFR 101.17(g) Food labeling, warning, notice, and safe handling statements, JUICES that have not been specifically processed to prevent, reduce, or eliminate the presence of pathogens with the following, “WARNING: This product has not been pasteurized and, therefore, may contain harmful bacteria that can cause serious illness in children, the elderly, and persons with weakened immune systems.”

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following areas were observed to have low sanitizer concentration:

The PIC remade the bucket and the triple sink sanitizer which tested at 100 ppm (Cl). The inspector reminded the PIC and employees that sanitizer buckets must be changed on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizer concentration levels are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-200 ppm).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.

[C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed dairy milk, oat milk, and strawberry topping to be opened in the standing cooler without date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC stated the items were opened within the past 2 days. A date was placed on the items. Ensure all Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) foods that are not used within TWENTY FOUR HOURS are date marked. Date marked items must be used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment:
It was observed that the operator was unable to properly communicate basic food handling safety as related to the nature of the operations. The facility is acidifying rice, using time as control, and serving raw fish. These are incredibly high risk food handling behaviors that can quickly cause a food-borne illness outbreak if not properly controlled. Staff should be aware of cold and hot holding temperatures. Staff should be able to acknowledge that foods held at room temperature should be used or discarded within four hours. There should be documentation of the prior handling of sushi fish so that everyone is aware of parasite destruction prior to use. Operator should also be able to demonstrate basic hand washing and control how staff wash hands. 
Proper hand washing should be demonstrated by all staff at the follow-up inspection. 
Staff should be aware of safe food handling strategies such as time as control, parasite destruction, and proper cold/hot holding.
citation_text: 2-101.11(C) Assignment. (C) This section does not apply to certain types of FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS deemed by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY to pose minimal risk of causing, or contributing to, foodborne illness based on the nature of the operation and extent of the FOOD preparation. [Pf]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to provide Employee Health Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. Inspector provided blank employee health reporting agreements during today’s inspection. Ensure all employees read and sign employee health reporting agreements to be maintained on file (at the facility) for future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).[Pf]

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: Inspector observed no bodily fluid cleanup policy within the facility. CORRECTED- Norovirus paperwork was provided during today’s inspection, and bleach is available. Ensure this policy is maintained on file for future inspections. Each food establishment must have a written policy for the cleanup/ disinfection of vomit and diarrhea to prevent the spread of Norovirus.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: The operator was observed beginning to prepare customer foods without washing their hands. Operator was previously in the lobby eating their lunch and handling other facility equipment. CORRECTED- The operator was paused from donning gloves to have a hand washing opportunity.
citation_text: 2-301.11 Clean Condition. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The operator was halted from donning gloves in-order to wash hands. The hand washing process was halted multiple times in-order to achieve proper procedure. Initially, the operator simply rinsed their fingers and turned off the faucet and called that a hand washing. The operator then used soap for a two second scrub before turning off the faucet and reaching for paper towel. Finally, inspector interfered to demonstrate proper hand washing using a scrubbing timeframe of 10-15 seconds, rinse, dry with a paper towel, and used the towel to turn-off the faucet. SCDPH will be performing spot checks and education throughout the year to ensure proper hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon entering the facility, inspector attempted to wash hands but the hand sink basin was filled with a large bulk of steel wool. CORRECTED- the steel wool was moved to an adjacent counter to allow for proper hand washing. Sinks designated for hand washing must always be made accessible for hand washing ONLY. The sushi is rolled with gloved hands and hands should be washed prior to donning gloves.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink.  (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
comment: The facility purchases sushi fish from Martinez (Sacramento Dr., Chicago). The facility does not have letters of guarantee for the parasite destruction. Martinez was contacted during the inspection and was aware of what paperwork needed to be sent. CK e-mail was given for records to be e-mailed. During the inspection, no documents were provided. Facility will receive a copy as SCDPH is provided.
citation_text: 3-402.11(A) Parasite Destruction. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before service or sale in READY TO-EAT form, raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH shall be: (1) Frozen and stored at a temperature of -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 168 hours (7 days) in a freezer; (2) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -35°C (-31°F) or below for a minimum of 15 hours; or (3) Frozen at -35°C (-31°F) or below until solid and stored at -20°C (-4°F) or below for a minimum of 24 hours. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the wait station to display no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade and observed at a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. comment: The facility is using time as control for the sushi rice but had some product from 10am the previous day. CORRECTED- Some of the product was kept for personal use, the remainder was discarded. The sushi rice is not controlled using a pH meter and thus should be discarded or used within FOUR HOURS. Time As Control for food Safety (TAC) paperwork was completed during today’s inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed various in-house mayo-based sauces sitting on the counter at room temperature (Spicy Miso Mayo and Chili Spicy Mayo). Previously,  the operator mentioned keeping the sauces on the counter for lunch and then put the sauces back inside of the cooler after lunch. The inspector educated about the danger of leaving temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods at room temperature for long periods of time and then putting them back inside of the cooler for future use. Previously, the recommended solution of using a time-as-control system where only small amount of sauce are brought out of the cooler and any leftover sauce are discarded after four hours was discussed. 
Today, sauces were again left on the counter and initially no one was quite aware of how long sauces stayed on the counter. Ensure that staff (there are only three) are educated on the proper time-as-control policy for house made sauces, spoons in water, tempura batter, and dry cloth on preparation counter. 
The aforementioned items should be removed/discarded and fresh created every FOUR HOURS. A Time As Control policy was created during the inspection. Discussed the bulk storage of sauces in the back cooler and movement of bulk product over 7 days.
Store homemade sauces, tempura batter, water and spoons, and dry cloth at room temperature for only FOUR HOURS.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed salmon in the standing double door cooler to be lacking date marking. The PIC stated the salmon was thawing. Thawing under refrigeration is an approved practice, however items should be date marked when brought into thawing. CORRECTED- the PIC stated they will be placing dates on the salmon. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are marked with the date they are brought into thawing in the future.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
comment: The facility does not have a consumer advisory posted on the facility wall or within the menu. CORRECTED- inspectors provided a consumer advisory sign during the inspection. Ensure a consumer advisory is included in future menu prints. Facilities serving raw or undercooked animal foods must disclose associated risks of food-borne illness to the public.
citation_text: 3-603.11(C) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens.  (C) REMINDER shall include asterisking the animal-derived FOODS requiring DISCLOSURE to a footnote that states: (1) Regarding the safety of these items, written information is available upon request; (2) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness; or (3) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no stem thermometers present in the establishment during today’s inspection. The facility cools and reheats food, and therefore must have a stem thermometer to verify proper internal temperatures of foods to verify proper cooling and cooking temperatures. Ensure a stem thermometer is purchased and made available by 02/17/26.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed multiple white powders with no label. CORRECTED- the containers were labeled as sugar and salt. Ensure foods that may be commonly mistaken for other foods are labeled with their common name once they are removed from their container.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility was unable to provide Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. All employee who handle are serve food are required to obtain a Food Handler’s certificate within 30 days of hire. Inspectors provided a list of ANSI-approved programs that offer Food Handlers courses. Ensure all employees obtain a Food Handler Certificate by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed that the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility has not completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the CFPM completes the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

citation_text:

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed not using an adequate amount of soap and not properly rubbing hands together before rinsing and drying. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was educated and instructed to review proper handwashing procedures with employees. Ensure sufficient soap is used during handwashing and hands are vigorously rubbed together for at least 10 to 15 seconds before rinsing and drying with a single-use paper towel. Employees must also use a paper towel to turn off the faucet to prevent recontamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. [P]

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

The standing cooler behind the registers is observed to be holding TCS foods between 48F and 52F internal temperatures. Multiple items were checked using a probe thermometer that were representative of the coolers functionality. TCS items were then discarded and included: 1) a containers of goat cheese; 2) two containers of sour cream; 3) a container of macaroni salad; 4) three quarter pans of sliced tomatoes; 5) three containers of Greek yogurt; 6) three quarter pans of house made avocado spread and; 7) a container of potato salad. Cooked eggs and bacon were recently placed into this cooler after preparation this morning and were allowed to be moved to other coolers in the facility. Many other items such as pre-packaged salad dressings and alcohol are not considered TCS foods and were allowed to remain in this cooler. As the TCS foods were discarded the violation is being considered CORRECTED at this time. The cooler functionality is being managed under line item #33 of this report.
