The probe thermometer in the facility is observed approximately 6F - 10F off of accurate during this inspection. The thermometer was checked using ice water and registered in the mid 20s Fahrenheit. Education was conducted for calibrating this type thermometer and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all thermometers are correctly calibrated at all times.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
citation_text:
3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers. 

The packages used for Fed Kitchen do not have cooking temperature requirements as per the HACCP plan and previous conversations with the PIC. The situation was discussed with multiple PICs and new labels are in the works for the next batch to be prepared. Ensure that all labeling requirements are met on the food packaging and per the HACCP plan at al times.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during this inspection is unaware of any completed allergen trainings at this facility. They recalled a previous conversation. They are instructed to have all CFPMs at the facility complete an ANSI accredited allergen training and maintain copies of the certificates at the facility moving forward.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The signed employee health reporting agreement forms for each employee were not available during the inspection. The person-in-charge (PIC) stated that employees will sign the forms when the owner is available at the facility. The inspector offered to provide blank copies for the facility to complete. Ensure all employees sign and maintain employee health reporting agreement forms on-site. The inspector will follow up on 02/17/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [PF]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The sanitizer test strips at the facility were observed to be wet and unusable. The PIC stated the test strips were accidentally dropped in water over the weekend and new test strips have been ordered. Ensure sanitizer test strips are available and usable at the facility at all times. The inspector will follow up on 02/17/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas were observed to have accumulations of dust and soil:

1. FIRST REPEAT - Dust accumulation was observed on the fan guard in the walk-in cooler.
2. Debris accumulation was observed on the walk-in cooler floor, especially under the food shelving.
3. Debris accumulation was observed in the corner area near the thermostats under the pizza oven.
4. Soil accumulation was observed on the food shelving in the walk-in cooler.
5. Food debris accumulation was observed inside the utensil holder container located by the three-compartment sink.
6. Food debris accumulation was observed inside the container used to store pizza cutters for customers at the server station.
7. Food debris accumulation was observed on the top surface of the oven. 
8. FIRST REPEAT - Soil accumulation was observed on the inside of the ice machine baffles.
9. Soil accumulation was observed on the soda gun holster.

The PIC was informed of the above conditions and instructed to clean the listed areas to sight and touch. Ensure all nonfood-contact surfaces are routinely cleaned and maintained free of dust, soil, and food debris accumulation to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Ice accumulation was observed on the walk-in freezer floor and behind the fan casing. The PIC was informed and instructed to remove the ice buildup to prevent further accumulation. Ensure all ice buildup is cleared and the walk-in freezer is maintained free of ice accumulation by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC during this inspection did not have a CFPM and did not know of any others in the area that did. The normal person that does have one was off that day. Ensure that there are enough CFPM’s available to cover all shifts.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with all employees. Ensure that the hand washing procedure in the facility does not allow for recontaminating the hands at the end of the process.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. The PIC was consulted and instructed to review when to wash hands with all employees. Ensure that hand washing takes place before donning gloves.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The only sani bucket observed in the kitchen during the inspection did not register on either the inspector's or facility’s test strips. The PIC was consulted and stated that the bucket was made around 11 in the morning. The bucket was remade to correct concentration during the inspection. Ensure that the sanitizers are refreshed often enough so that they are maintained at effective concentrations at all times.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 2 cans of olives and tomato sauce to be dented along the seams. CORRECTED- the cans were separated from cans from service to be returned to food supplier. Ensure cans are checked for any dents along the seams, and sizable dents along the body when stocking. Dented cans may allow for the entry and growth of Botulism.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed light entering the facility along the perimeter of the back door. A sizable gap (about 1-2cm) exists in the upper right corner. Ensure the door is repaired by the next routine inspection to protect against the entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed paper plates used for catering service stored with their food contact surface facing upwards in the dry storage. CORRECTED- education about protecting food contact surfaces from potential contamination was provided. The PIC stated they would place the single service articles in a bag. Ensure all food contact surfaces are stored in a position that protects from potential contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the physical facility in need of repair.
1) FIRST REPEAT: The wall in the kitchen is missing caulking behind the rinse and wash portions of the triple sink. Ensure the sink is resealed to the wall to allow for a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The backsplash of the sink in the women’s restroom was bare wood. Paint or seal the bare wood so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
3) A gap exists between the mop sink and the wall directly to the left. Re-adhere the sink basin to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in proper repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed the hand contact surface of tongs touching a baguette. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the tongs into a separate container and discarded the baguette. Ensure all utensils are stored in a manner that prevents bare hand contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple pieces of equipment to be in disrepair:
1) Cooler drawer of cook-line facing dining room.
2) Cooler drawer of cook-line facing back of house.
3) Cooler drawer of drive thru sandwich prep cooler. A piece of metal on the right side is loose and able to obscure the ability of a drawer to close.
4) The top interior of the microwave on the cook-line.
Ensure all equipment is maintained in proper repair. Repair or replace equipment by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a significant accumulation of debris on the floor and wall directly beneath the triple sink. Ensure the physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a broken tile on the coving between the bakery room and drive thru area. Ensure repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the kitchen is observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. The PIC indicated that it was likely from last night and had not been changed today. This is not a sufficient concentration to effectively sanitize foods contact surfaces. Education was conducted and the bucket remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility. Change them as needed.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
citation_text:
3-403.11(D) Reheating for Hot Holding. (D) Reheating for hot holding as specified under (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 5C (41F) and the temperatures specified under (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours. 

The gyro meat on the spit is observed with internal temperatures ranging from 28F-47F during this inspection. Per the PIC the spit was pulled from the freezer approximately two hours ago and not heated up immediately. Items on the spit should be cooked through completely in one process and the extra cooled and stored accordingly. The item was cooked during this inspection to correct the immediate violation.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

Cooked rice in portioned containers are observed in the reach in cooler across from the gyro spit. They are without date marking or tracking of any kind and were prepared yesterday (per the PIC). Education was conducted and multiple option (tracking the batches via white board, tracking dates on the individual containers, tracking batches with cycling the product, ect) given and the inspector will check what the decision for a process is at the scheduled follow up. Ensure that all TCS foods in the facility are marked for seven day date marking at all times.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The hand sink in the kitchen area does not have functioning cold water. The only option is hot water at this sink and the water reaches scalding within 10-15 seconds. This does not promote adequate or safe hand washing practices. Per department head CK this could be a closing violation and needs to be remedied immediately. A follow up is being scheduled for 24 hours to ensure that a repair is completed. If it is not completed at that time the PIC is aware that closure will follow.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. 

An employee phone was observed on that table in front of the three part sink where food preparation takes place. Education took place and the phone removed to correct the immediate violation. The table was re-sanitized as well. Ensure that employee belongings are stored so that they are not a concern for contamination of food contact surfaces or foods.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspector observed a wastewater leak from underneath the right basin of the triple sink. A leak or ponding water was not observed at the start of the inspection. The leak seems to have occurred during the inspection. The PIC was notified of the leak and the triple sink was drained. The dish machine in the facility is currently under maintenance, so the triple sink is the facility's sole method of washing and sanitizing. The accommodate their needs, the right basin will be converted to the “rinse” basin with no water held. The facility will wash in the left basin, rinse with running water in the right basin, and sanitize in the center. This is a temporary solution until the sink can be repaired. If the leak worsens and the sink cannot be used at all, the facility has large bins that can be utilized as a temporary triple sink. Staff is educated on preparing temporary washing/sanitizing systems. A follow-up will be conducted on Friday, February 6th to ensure the sink has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following facility items are in need of repair:

1. The cove base under the triple sink is peeling from the wall. Ensure floor/wall junctions are sealed to prevent moisture damage or mold accumulation.

2. The sealant between the triple sink and the wall was observed soiled and damaged. The sealant (typically silicone) needs to be removed and replaced.

Ensure these facility repairs are completed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure education trickles down to all employees and that they are conducting correct procedures at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

1) In two locations the hand sinks are blocked by equipment. Locations include the produce walk in cooler and the sink at the end of the oven line. The PICs were shown and moved the blocking items to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote regulate and consistent use.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The three part sink was observed being remade during this inspection. The employee was mixing hot water with the pre-metered solution. The solution was tested and did not register on the inspector’s test strips. Education was conducted. The dispenser is designed and adjusted so that the solution coming out of the equipment is at the correct concentration and diluting it reduces its efficacy to ineffective levels. The sink was remade to correct. Ensure that education is trickled down and that all staff can use the relevant equipment correctly in the facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Beef and chicken in the Asian Market are observed on the counter of the prep cooler out of temperature control. It was found that the items were removed from the cooler approximately an hour before observation. Internal temperatures were observed at 60F. Education was conducted and the items allowed to be moved back into the cooler. Ensure that foods are not left out for prolonged periods of time without temperature control.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

At several locations in this facility employee related foods and drink were observed intermixed with foods and ingredients intended for consumers. The locations were shown to the PIC and they were instructed to designate a place for employee foods to be stored so that they would not be a concern for contaminating consumer foods. The items were moved during this inspection to correct. Drinks in the facility should be in a cups that have lids and straws as well.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. This was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff. Ensure hand washing takes place correctly at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and:(H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to move from taking an order and donned gloves prior to food handling. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to review hand washing with staff and monitor hand washing to ensure it takes place at all times that it is needed. Ensure hand washing is taking place at all required times in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

Raw eggs are observed over cheese in the front prep cooler in the facility. The PIC was shown and moved the items to correct. Ensure that foods are stored according to their cooking orders in coolers at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani buckets in the facility are observed low on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and replaced the buckets during this inspection to correct. Ensure all sanitizers are maintained at effective concentrations at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas of the facility were observed to be in need of repair:

1.) Wall tiles in the back booth area were observed to have gaps at the top where sealing is needed. The person-in-charge (PIC) was instructed to caulk the top of the wall tiles to ensure they are properly sealed and to prevent potential harborage for pests.

2.) Floor tiles beneath the automated drive-through soda machine were observed to be broken, with water accumulation present.

3.) A floor tile beneath the smoothie cooler was observed to be partially broken, with water accumulation present.

The PIC was informed to have all damaged or unsealed floor and wall tiles repaired or sealed prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure floors and walls are maintained in good repair and are smooth, sealed, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT - Dirty mop water and the mop head were observed in the mop bucket next to the mop sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed; the dirty water was discarded, and the mop head was placed in the wringer basket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use and mop heads are properly stored by placing them in the wringer basket or hanging them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The inspector observed the triple sink to be missing its sealant at the back of the sink. The sink needs to be sealed to the wall to prevent water and microbial accumulation. The PIC was informed and stated that maintenance was performed on the sink over the summer. The PIC has plans to submit a work order for repair. Ensure this repair is complete prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee rinse hands with water only for less than 5 seconds. Education was conducted at the hand sink. The employee was instructed to wash for a minimum of 20 seconds with soap and water. Although eduction was attempted, the employee did not  respond to education or repeat hand washing. A follow-up is scheduled for Thursday, February 5th to ensure staff are practicing proper hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. The handles of the faucet are considered soiled, as they are handled with dirty hands. To prevent recontamination of newly cleaned hands, ensure staff are using a paper towel to turn off the hand sink. A follow-up will be conducted on Thursday, February 5th to ensure proper handwashing practices are taking place in the facility.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning new gloves. Donning gloves with soiled hands poses a cross-contamination risk. Education was attempted with the individual, but the inspector was ignored. The PIC was informed and plans to conduct further education with staff. A follow-up is scheduled for Thursday, February 5th to ensure proper hand washing practices are followed in the facility.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the food preparation line to contain only 50ppm quaternary ammonia sanitizer. CORRECTED- sanitizer was remade to a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are monitoring sanitizer concentrations with test strips and swapping out the buckets frequently. The active ingredient in the sanitizer solution evaporates over time, which will cause the concentration to decrease.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed two pots in the back dish area soiled with standing water. The pots were hanging on the clean dishes racks facing the dish area. The PIC was informed and the dishes were moved be re-washed and sanitized. Ensure clean dishes are protected from soil and contamination during storage.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspectors observed the prep table on the service line to be damaged and temporarily protected with tape. The broken edge of the prep table is very sharp, and poses a hazard to staff. However, the tape is not food-safe and therefore cannot remain on the surface. Ensure the prep table is replaced to prevent food safety or employee safety hazards. 

Inspectors observed the triple sink in the food preparation space to be damaged and tipping away from the wall. Due to the incorrect angle of the sink basin, water is collecting and standing in the basin. Ensure this is repaired to prevent water retention in the sink. 

REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspector also observed the triple sink to be cracked between two basins. This allows water to leak from the sink to the floor. The PIC is aware of the issue. 

Ensure these items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed interior of coolers to be soiled with food debris. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspectors observed the front service hand sink to have a steady freshwater leak. This water is being surveyed directly to the drain within the sink basin. Ensure this leak is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspectors observed waste water leaking onto the floor under the triple sink. The plumbing is propped up with a crate and a sodden rag. The flooring of the dish area was heavily soiled with waste water. The PIC stated that staff have to squeegee the floors every hour to prevent further accumulation. Wastewater accumulation poses a risk of cross-contamination with clean dishes and food items stored in the area. A follow-up is scheduled for Thursday, February 5th to ensure the plumbing is repaired.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the following areas in need of a deep cleaning:
1. Floor under stoves and fryers
2. Floors of dish area
3. Floors of walk-in cooler
4. Walls around dish area
5. Plumbing under triple sink
6. Walls around cooking station

 Ensure facility has been deep cleaned prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food-contact surfaces in the facility to be in need of repair:
1. REPEAT VIOLATION- The shelving holding clean dishes, single-service containers, and the selves above the triple sink were observed rusted and in need of repair/replacement.
2. There are two holes under the triple sink on the right wall. Ensure these holes are patched to prevent moisture from accumulating in the walls.  

These areas which are not smooth and easily cleanable pose a hazard for bacterial accumulation and food-borne illness transmission. Ensure these areas are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A soiled pair of scissors is observed in storage alongside spoons ready for customer service. Discussion revealed that it is used for cutting the milks bags in the Prairie Farms dispenser. This means that the observed soilage is residual milk and should not be in contact with the spoons. A server removed the scissors to correct. Ensure that all cleaned food contact surfaces are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) A long drip is observed on the hood system over the fryers. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The drip was removed to correct. 2) Food debris (and possible mold) is observed on the wire shelving in the standing cooler across from the steam table. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean to prevent possible contamination of the foods beneath. Ensure that all locations are maintained clean when they are in proximity to containers of food. 3) (REPEAT) Wire shelving in the standing cooler across from the steam table in the kitchen is chipping/rusting. This poses a concern for physical contaminations in the foods beneath. The PIC is instructed to reseal and/or replace prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

The PIC during the majority of this inspection does not currently have a completed allergen training certificate. The situation was discussed and they are instructed to complete a course and maintain a certificate moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Accumulated food debris was observed on the floors underneath the cookline line. Shown to PIC. Ensure that floors are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed an insect glue trap stored in very close contact with a stack of clean pans (in cabinet across from triple sink). Shown to the PIC and the trap was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that insect traps are never stored in areas where food or food contact surfaces can be exposed to contamination.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: No designated person in charge (PIC) was present during the majority of today’s inspection. The kitchen was left unattended for a short period of time, during which time a resident or guest could have entered the kitchen and contaminated food intended for service. During today’s inspection multiple priority and priority foundation violations were cited. These violations include, but are not limited to, no date marking, improper hand washing and times to wash hands, improper concentration of sanitizer and lack of education regarding use of sanitizer. The inspector will return on 02/12/26 to ensure all priority and priority foundation violations have been corrected.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/CFPM) present during the majority of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived towards the end of the inspection. The presence of a CFM oversees and educates staff on safe food handling practices, and helps reduce the incidence of food-borne illnesses. Ensure a CFM is present during ALL times at which food is being handled or prepared.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple incidents of food handlers switching tasks and donning gloves without handwashing. CORRECTED- Education was conducted with the PIC regarding appropriate times to wash hands per the food code. Review times to wash hands with all staff who handle food.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) [P].

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed a food handler wash hands, and then turn off the faucet without the use of a barrier. CORRECTED- education about the importance of a barrier was provided and the individual rewashed their hands, using a barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure all food handlers use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid recontaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a dish in the basin of the sink in the Memory Care kitchenette. CORRECTED- the dish was removed from the basin and education about hand washing sink usage was provided. The PIC stated that all dishes are to be brought back to the main kitchen for ware washing. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing ONLY, so as not to deter frequent hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) The food contact surface (blade) of the facility’s can opener. CORRECTED-the can opened was pulled to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized
2) The internal surfaces and the baffles of the ice machine contain soil debris and limescale. Inspector will return on 02/12/26 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket used for wiping food contact surfaces was observed to have no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade to 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. The staff member was making a sanitizer bucket from an incorrect dispenser, and education was provided. Ensure ongoing education about the proper use of sanitizers occurs frequently.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed no date marking within the facility. CORRECTED- the PIC applied dates to food opened or prepared within the past seven days. Food that had an unknown date or preparation, or that was prepared over seven days ago was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Education was provided regarding which items should be date marked. This violation will be spot checked during the 02/12/26 reinspection.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed two probe thermometers to be out of calibration. CORRECTED- the inspector demonstrated how to calibrate a stem thermometer using the ice water method. Both thermometers were calibrated during today’s inspection. Ensure stem thermometers are maintained in good repair to check proper internal cooking temperatures.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed 6 cans of green beans stored on the floor of dry storage. Ensure all food and food contact surfaces are stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to be in improper storage:
1) Forks and spoons in Memory Care were stored with a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- the utensils were rearranged with a gloved hand so that only the hand contact surfaces were available to be dispensed.
2) Plates in the kitchen were stored with an exposed food contact surface. Plates should be inverted or stored under a covering during storage.
Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a manner to prevent potential bare hand or environmental contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the handle of the single standing cooler in the kitchen to be deteriorated and contain duct tape to hold it in place. All nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure equipment is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed the facility’s heat measuring dish puck to be nonoperational. Inspector will return on 02/12/26 to ensure the heat registering dish puck is working to verify proper sanitizing temperatures for heat sanitizing dish machine.
citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed multiple drawers storing food utensils to contain debris. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Two damp mop heads were observed stored in the basin of the mop sink and mop bucket during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the PIC moved to the mops to the top of the mop buckets, so that they may air dry. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows for air drying moving forward.
citation_text: 6-501.16 After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Caulking is missing behind triple sink to the right of the dish machine. Areas that are not easily moved for cleaning must be sealed to the wall. Seal the space between the wall and the sink prior to next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold and bacteria with a high water activity.
citation_text: 6-501.11 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) The merchandiser grates within the open display cooler on the food island was observed to have the accumulation of dangling soil and dust. Discussed with PIC.  Ensure that the dangling soil and dust is removed to prevent soil accumulation and possible contamination. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed a to-go soup bowl submerged in the soy sauce. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the bowl to be discarded, and replaced with a ladel. Education occurred regarding the need for a scoop with a handle to prevent potential bare hand contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The soap in the back hand washing sink was observed to be not properly dispensing. CORRECTED- a hand soap pump was brought to the hand washing sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are always supplied with accessible soap for proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: A total of four cans (a mixture of soy sauce and oyster sauce) were observed to contain dents along the seams. CORRECTED- The PIC voluntarily used post-it notes to mark the dented cans with a large “X” to be sent back to their supplier. The PIC stated the kitchen manager stocks the shelves, and communicated this new procedure to them. Ensure seams of cans are not dented to prevent the entry and growth of Botulism. Mark and move these cans aside in the future.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed wet wiping cloths out in the front area as well as in the kitchen. CORRECTED- Person in charge moved cloth to sanitizer bucket before inspector was able to discuss item. Ensure wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer buckets in between uses to prevent the growth and harborage of bacteria.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed shelves within the walk in cooler to contain an accumulation of rust and other debris. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris. Ensure shelves are either cleaned painted/sealed (made to be smooth and easily cleanable) or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There are mouse droppings observed to be in multiple areas throughout the dry storage area in the basement. These areas include, but are not limited to, a metal bowl, a metal container, on the lid of a rice cooker, on a plastic bag, and in ceramic bowls. An employee was shown these areas and where the mouse droppings are. It was discussed to make sure that all equipment that is brought upstairs to be used is washed, rinsed, and sanitized before use. A follow up will occur on 2/9/2026 to ensure that these mouse droppings have been cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to not use a barrier to turn off faucet after washing their hands. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was educated on proper handwashing procedure and the employee was instructed to wash their hands again. Ensure a barrier such as paper towel is used to turn off the faucet after handwashing in order to prevent re-contamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A crate of egg was observed to be stored above ready-to-eat foods in the standing cooler. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the eggs were moved to a different cooler. Ensure that raw foods are not stored about ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: An Italian dressing that is produced in-house has been stored in the cooler for 3 days without the container being date marked after 24 hours. The PIC was educated on date marking sauces that are produced in-house and stored after 24 hours because it is a time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food. Ensure that TCS foods are date marked after 24 hours before storing in the refrigerator and discarded after 7 days. The inspector will follow-up on 02/09/2026 to ensure the facility is in compliance.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [PF]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Effective Pest Control: The facility has seen a sudden surge of pests related to outside source. Orkin has been called to complete a six month intensive service. The facility has several glue traps around the back storage area. Glue traps are observed to be filled with over a dozen pests of various life stages. The concern is being addressed, but the problem seems to be fairly extensive (all life stages observed). See violation #55 for maintenance items to address to support pest control. The facility is in good operating order in-terms of cleaning. Concerns to address are pest treatment and maintenance. The inspector will spot check the facility on 02/28/2026 to inspect pest activity.
citation_text: 6-202.16 Exterior Walls and Roofs, Protective Barrier. Perimeter walls and roofs of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall effectively protect the establishment from the weather and the entry of insects, rodents, and other animals.  [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility did not have sanitizer test strips available at the time of inspection. The PIC was instructed to obtain and maintain sanitizer test strips on site. Ensure test strips are available at all times for testing sanitizer concentration levels. The inspector will follow up on 02/09/2026 to verify compliance.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [PF]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The backup make-table cooler opposite the triple sink has accumulation of food debris. The PIC was informed and instructed to clean the cooler to sight and touch before the next routine inspection. Ensure coolers are kept free of food debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. The facility is managing a sudden pest problem. Traditionally, all these surface concerns would not be addressed, but when pests are involved, maintenance and cleaning are addressed in a more detailed manner. The recommendation of SCDPH is always to eliminate cardboard from the facility, acquire proper pest control (done), and work to insure walls are sealed to prevent movement between walls and kitchen. The following surfaces need maintenance attention:

1) The wall to the right (by the hand sink) as you enter the kitchen is pulled from the wall. See that wallboard is firmly secured to the wall.
2) There is a gap around the relief line from the grease trap into the wall. Use a foam caulking to eliminate this gap. 
3) There are multiple holes in the dry storage room ceiling and around the back door. Again, spray foam, cut flush will help eliminate gaps.
4) the corner trim to the left of the triple sink is damaged. Repair the damaged trim.
5) The 2x4s under the windows of the dry storage area/preparation area are unsealed. Seal any bare wood,
6) Walk around the back storage area and pull equipment away from the walls. Clean and secure cove base to the wall. There are several areas where there is gaping of cove base.
7) Finally, there are a few floor tiles that are observed damaged. Replace the damaged floor tiles. 
8) The wall paint by the mop sink at the mop station is peeling off and the wall needs to be repainted.

Now is a good time to address ongoing maintenance concerns in the facility. The building is old and Head West has been present for several decades. Revisiting painting and surface maintenance is appropriate at this time.

comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. The individual that holds a food manager certificate arrived in the midst of the inspection. Ensure that there are more employees that are food manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The facility could not produce any employee health reporting forms. A copy of an employee health form was given to the manager for employees to sign and complete. The employee working at the time of the inspection signed the form during the visit. Ensure that all employees sign employee health forms and be sure that they’re conveniently located for future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Two containers of waffle batter were observed at room temperature in the service area. The employees planned to keep the leftover batter from breakfast, however, instructions on the waffle mix stated that batter must either be used within 4 hours or discarded (if not cold held during service) or kept at 41F or below at all times. Discussed with the employees that if there are plans to keep the batter for another day of service, the batter must stay cold held at 41F or below. If batter remains at room temperature, then the batter will need to be discarded after 4 hours. The batter was voluntarily discarded by the facility to correct the violation. Be sure to follow the manufacturer's instructions regarding Time/Temperature control foods to ensure safety of food items.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was a container of cream cheese spreads observed at room temperature in the service station. The packaging stated to keep items refrigerated. PIC mentioned that the containers are normally placed in the freezer overnight and are expected to keep the spreads cold through breakfast hours. Suggested switching out containers half way through breakfast to ensure that the spreads are maintaining proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Ensure that all food handlers have been notified in a verifiable manner their responsibility to report foodborne illness related symptoms.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.

An employee was observed to move from washing dishes to donning gloves for food preparation. As the inspector was at the only hand sink in that area no hand washing took place during this procedure. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing with the food handlers in the facility. Ensure hand washing takes place at all times that it is required in the facility.

The bar hand sink was without a hand drying system at the time of this inspection. The paper towels that are normally at this location were found and brought back to their location to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.
