comment: There isn’t any hot water available at the kitchen’s handsink. Employees mentioned that there was hot water available earlier in the day. The water was left running for a few minutes and never came available. Hot water was available at every other sink in the facility, however, hot water shall be available at each handsink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly. Will follow-up on 2/6/2026.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The cove base underneath the triple sink is pulling away from the wall. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that cove base is secured to the wall to avoid accumulated debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The follow areas are in need of recaulking:
- the handsink in the men’s bathroom 
- the triple sink inside of the meat room

In addition, the cove base is pulling away from the wall (right of kitchen’s handsink). Ensure that sinks are recaulked and that the cove base is resealed to prevent accumulated debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the soda nozzle at the wait station has soil accumulation. The person in charge (PIC) was informed and he stated the nozzles would be cleaned by the close of work. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid soil or mold build up.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed light passing through the door by the triple sink. The PIC was informed and educated on the risk of pests entering the facility through gaps. Ensure all outer openings are sealed to prevent entry of insects and rodents.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspectors observed food debris in the knife storage container. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the container was transferred to the triple sink for washing. Ensure all equipments and utensils are stored in a location free of soil.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
1st REPEAT - Observed the handle of the cook line freezer is in a state of disrepair. A portion of the plastic has broken off exposing the soft, absorbent material underneath. The handle must either be replaced or repaired so that the absorbent material is not exposed. Ensure that the handle is a smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent surface by the next routine inspection. PIC discussed plans to cover the inset handle and install another handle above. Ensure repairs are smooth and easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: 1st REPEAT - Inspectors observed grease build-up on the wall and floor behind the grills on the cook line. The PIC was informed, he stated cleaning is done every 4-6 months and would be cleaning those areas very soon. Ensure the wall and floor behind the grills on the cook line is cleaned before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed gap between the wall and floor titles under the triple sink. The PIC was instructed to seal the gap so that from the wall to the floor is smooth, easily cleanable and prevents water accumulation. Ensure the gap is sealed by next routine inspection to prevent water accumulation and also a hideout location for potential insects.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a spoon present in the basin of the hand washing sink. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the spoon to be taken to the dish room. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for handwashing only to incentivize frequent hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed light entering the facility through the back kitchen door (along the bottom perimeter). Discussed this area as a point of potential entry for pests with the PIC. Replace weather stripping by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: No temperature measurement device for heat sanitation was available during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that a new heat dish puck has been ordered, and delayed in shipping. Ensure a heat measuring device for sanitation is made available by 02/06/26 to ensure proper heat sanitation temperatures in a verifiable manner.
citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The person in charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/ CFPM). They stated they are scheduled to take the exam in one week. Ensure the facility is under the supervision of a CFM any time food is being prepared or served.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The PIC was unable to present Employee Health Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. The inspector provided an English language handout and will be emailing a Spanish language handout to the PIC. Ensure all staff who handle food read and sign Employee Health Reporting Agreements. Inspector will return on 02/06/26 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Multiple Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items were observed above 41F.
1) FIRST REPEAT: Individual cream cheese portions from both the top and bottom of the storage canisters were probed to have internal temperatures between 58-62F.
2) Strawberry topping was probed to have an internal temperature of 63F. 
CORRECTED- The PIC stated and will be discarded after today’s breakfast service. The PIC will check with upper management moving forward regarding either keeping these items on an ice bath, or using Time as a Control for Food Safety (TAC).
Inspector will spot check cold holding during the 02/06/26 follow up.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed yogurt, orange juice, and apple juice in the self service dispensers to lack date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC placed dates on the aforementioned items. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked when opened, to be used or discarded within seven days. The day the item is opened counts as DAY ONE.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed individual cream cheese packets stored on top of an ice pack at the breakfast counter. These ice packs are unable to provide sufficient cooling for TCS foods (which should be held at or below 41F). See violation #22 for details. PIC will inform inspector on or by 02/06/26 weather the facility will move forward using ice baths to cold hold TCS foods, or use TAC.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. [Pf]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed single service knives and spoons positioned in a mixed orientation at the breakfast counter. CORRECTED- the PIC rearranged the single service items with gloved hands so that the hand-contact surface is positioned outward. Ensure this practice continues moving forward to prevent the bare-hand contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: No sanitizer bucket was available at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the PIC made a sanitizer bucket and education occurred regarding availability. Ensure a sanitizer bucket is ready and available during all times in which food is being prepared or served.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of food debris on the bottom of the kitchen’s standing cooler. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces and equipment are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) in the facility at the start of the inspection and there was food preparation and serving taking place. CORRECTED- A CFPM arrived at the end of the inspection and they were educated on this. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of food preparation, cooking, and serving.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels at the handwashing sink at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The employee replaced the paper towels. Ensure that there is always a supply of individual, disposable towels at all handwashing sinks to allow for the proper use of a barrier during the handwashing process.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There are no Chlorine test strips available to test the concentration of the Chlorine sanitizer in the dish machine. A follow up is scheduled for 2/5/2026 to ensure that Chlorine test strips have been obtained. There should always be test strips for every type of sanitizer that is being used in a facility to ensure that food-contact surfaces are being sanitized at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The faucet of the triple sink in the kitchen is observed to have a dripping leak coming from it. Ensure that this leak is repaired. All plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The server station on the east side of the facility was observed to not have paper towels at the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and paper towels were placed at the sink. Ensure that all handwashing sinks in the facility are supplied with individual, disposable towels to allow for proper handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The facility is observed to have soil residue and mold accumulation on the shelves in the walk-in cooler and on the wall in the back right corner of the walk-in cooler. A follow up is scheduled for 2/5/2026 to ensure that these shelves and the wall has been cleaned. Ensure that equipment is being cleaned to protect food from contamination, as any uncovered food could have potentially been exposed to the mold.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food-contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The soda nozzles at the east server station were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in them. Ensure that these are being taken apart when cleaning them and are being cleaned regularly. 
2. THIRD REPEAT- The top of the inside of the ice machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue. The PIC stated that Pepsi was here two days ago to clean it. Ensure that the ice machine is being checked regularly to make sure it is being cleaned sufficiently. 

A follow up is scheduled on 2/5/2026 to ensure that these food-contact surfaces have been cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are being maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The facility uses ice baths during lunch for TCS food items on the cook-line. The ice bath for sauces only reached a quarter of the way up the bottles of sauces. The ice bath for burger toppings (lettuce, tomatoes, and pickles) and other food items, such as coleslaw, was only ice and only touched the bottom of the container. Coleslaw probed to be at 51.9F and ranch probed to be at 52F. The burger toppings probed to be at 49F. These ice baths had been made at 11am. The PIC stated that they checked the temperatures of the food items at 12pm and that they were under 41F. The PIC stated that the sauces and coleslaw are discarded after four hours and that the other items are placed back in the cooler. Ensure that ice baths are properly submerging the bottom of the containers and are a mixture of both ice and water to allow for proper cold holding. These TCS food items need to be maintained at 41F or below unless they will be under Time as Control and discarded after four hours. CORRECTED- A proper ice bath was discussed with the PIC and the TCS items on the line were placed under Time as Control. These items were discarded at 4pm. Ensure that TCS food items are being properly cold held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The back door by the chemicals is observed to have a gap in the bottom of it that allows an entryway for insects and rodents. Discussed weatherstripping the door with the PIC. Ensure that this gap is closed to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The faucet of the mop sink is observed to have a dripping leak coming from it. Ensure that this is repaired and maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair: 

1. The dish area is in need of being resealed. The current caulking is observed to be in disrepair and has an accumulation of soil residue on it. 
2. The gasket of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this gasket is replaced. 
3. The standing freezer that is used for glasses is observed to have a cracked gasket. Ensure that this gasket is replaced. 
4. The trim to the right of the handwashing sink in the kitchen is separating from the wall. Ensure that this is resealed. 
5. The caulking on the handwashing sink on the cook-line is observed to be in disrepair. Ensure that this is resealed. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: A drain in front of the fryers in the kitchen is observed to be not draining. CORRECTED- The facility had a plumbing company come repair the drain. The facility was closed during this process. The drain is repaired and the facility opened later that day. Educate staff to keep drain covers on drains and to prevent grease from going down the drain to avoid future back-ups or cloggings.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at back kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure staff is monitoring facility to prevent any possible leaks.
citation_text: 5-201.11 Approved. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM and hoses conveying water shall be constructed and repaired with APPROVED materials according to LAW. (B) A water filter shall be made of SAFE MATERIALS.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the silicone sealant to the left of the dish machine to be damaged. The PIC was informed and plans to submit a work order for repair. Ensure this repair is complete prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspectors observed an opened roasted garlic Parmesan sauce labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” stored on the kitchen counter and in a serving bowl. CORRECTED - The PIC was instructed that time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” must be stored under refrigeration for safety purposes. The sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure all TCS sauces are refrigerated after opening and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following non-food contact surfaces to have crevice and broken parts:

- The kitchen handwashing sink’s caulking is peeling off and needs to be re-sealed.
- The deep reach-in silver freezer cover is partially broken and needs to be replaced.

The PIC was informed and the areas mentioned above would be repaired before the next routine inspection. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are free of crevices or broken parts to allow for easy cleaning.
citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspectors observed soil accumulation on the caulking around the triple sink in the dry storage area and the handwashing sink at the ice cream station. The PIC was informed that the caulking must be cleaned prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are regularly cleaned and maintained free of soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following areas of the facility to be in need of repair:

- The back door does not remain closed properly, and light is visible through the bottom right side of the door, which may allow the entry of pests and insects.
- Floor tiles are missing beneath the triple sink.
- Wall tiles at the mop station are loose and separating from the wall.

The PIC was informed, and the issues listed above are to be corrected prior to the next routine inspection. The physical facility must be maintained in good repair at all times.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

There is not a CFPM available at the facility during this inspection. The rules were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have a CFPM available at all times of operation moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector for the ice machine has a small amount of pink slime build up observed during this inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean and sanitized at all times in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee operate faucet handles with bare hands after the handwashing process. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing procedures. Ensure that employees are using barriers to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm (quat). The PIC mentioned that the sani bucket was mistakenly filled with plain water. Quaternary ammonia was added to the solution and was tested at 400ppm to correct the violation.

There was one sanitizer bucket on the cook-line that tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium and one sanitizer bucket in the back preparation area that tested to be at 100ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Both sanitizer buckets were remade and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. 

Ensure that all sanitizer buckets are testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The fan guards of the walk in cooler were observed accumulated with dust. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed sour cream, tartar sauce, and ranch dressing being held above 41F in the facility’s counter top cooler. Items were probed between 54-56F. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) stated the items had been in the unit for less than four hours. All items were moved to a working cooler. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are held 41F, or time as control (TAC) is implemented, with the items to be used or discarded within 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the counter top cooler to have ambient temperatures ranging between 52-56. This is not a safe cold holding range for TCS foods, as noted by violation #22. The PIC stated the new unit is capable of cooling and freezing foods. PIC called their equipment service provider during the inspection to eliminate the defrost cycle, and ensure ambient temperatures of 41F and below. The PIC stated they will call inspector when the unit is serviced and can be observed to be properly cold holding TCS items.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed walls and some shelving of the walk-in cooler to have bare wood. The paint on the door of the walk-in is damaged exposing bare wood, and the wood below the ventilation system in the walk-in appears to be untreated/uncoated. Ensure these wood surfaces are sealed to prevent moisture absorption and mold/bacterial accumulation.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was an empty sanitizer bucket observed to be in the handwashing sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The inspectors removed the bucket and discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use and that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The soda gun nozzle and holder were observed to have slight soil residue accumulation on them. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned the nozzle and holder during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was not a sanitizer bucket made and available in the kitchen. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at a proper concentration of 400ppm. Ensure that there is always sanitizer made and available for use in the kitchen during all hours of food preparation and cooking.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor under the dish machine is observed to be in need of cleaning. There was a dead roach, along with an accumulation of food debris and soil residue, under the dish machine. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was an open can of ketchup observed to be being used on the cook-line. CORRECTED- The ketchup was moved into another container. The PIC was educated that ketchup is an acidic food and should immediately be transferred to another container after being opened if it is canned. Ensure that cans are not being used for a storage method, especially for acidic foods, to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- There was a tub of raw chicken over a tub of raw beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The chicken was moved to be below the beef and the PIC was educated on proper storage order. Ensure that proper storage order is always as follows: 
1. Ready-to-Eat foods.
2. Unwashed Fruits and Vegetables.
3. Partially Cooked Foods (Ex: par-cooked chicken).
4. Seafood and shell eggs. 
5. Beef and pork.
6. Chicken. 
Ensure that food is always protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FOURTH REPEAT- There are multiple containers of sauces in the walk-in cooler and containers of food in the bottom of the preparation cooler that were observed to be uncovered. This was discussed with the PIC. All food should be covered in open-air coolers to protect the food from contamination. Ensure that food is stored in packages, in covered containers, or in wrappings to protect the food from contamination. Due to this violation being a fourth repeat, multiple spot checks and educational visits will occur before next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT - Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. CORRECTED - The person-in-charge (PIC) was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed a trash can was obstructing easy access to the handwashing sink. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed and the trash can was moved to a different location. Ensure the handwashing sink is easily accessible at all times for employees.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [PF]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the quaternary ammonium sanitizer on the dough prep table was testing at 50 ppm. CORRECTED - The PIC was informed, and the sanitizer was remade to achieve a concentration level of 200 ppm. Ensure the sanitizer concentration level is maintained between 200 - 400 ppm at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following time/temperature for safety (TCS) foods labeled “Refrigerate After Opening” stored on a dry storage shelf in the kitchen:

- “Barbecue sauce in refill bottles.”
- “Grated Parmesan cheese.”

CORRECTED - PIC was informed, and the foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are stored under refrigeration and maintained at 5°C (41°F) or less after opening.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION - Inspectors observed the shelves holding clean dishes across from the triple sink to be soiled with debris. 

Inspectors also observed the shelf across the serving area holding disposable plates to have accumulation of grease deposits.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned regularly to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspectors observed an employee working does not have food handler training certificate. PIC was informed to ensure all employees who do not have a CFPM certificate must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all employees obtain a food handlers certificate by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There is soil residue observed under the racks where sausage is stored in the display cooler. This was discussed with the PIC. The PIC instructed an employee to clean this area. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present within facility. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspectors observed an opened bottle of stir fry sauce with “Refrigerate After Opening” on the label in the dry storage. The person-in-charge was reminded of this violation from the previous routine inspection conducted on January 12, 2026 and the sauce was voluntarily discarded today. Ensure time/temperature for safety foods are stored at 5°C (41°F) or less after opening.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. Observed an employee touching face and ears before returning to work without hand washing. Discussed with operator the need to wash hands. 
FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed the scoop for the cooked white rice did not have a handle. The PIC replaced the scoop with a handled scoop during the inspection. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods always have a handle to avoid bare hand contact with the food.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw seafood stored over cut onions in the walk-in cooler. The raw seafood was moved onto the bottom shelf during the inspection. Ensure that raw seafood is always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces are not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The debris on the can opener blade.

(2) The debris on the container holding egg rolls in the sliding door cooler.

(3) The soiled knives on the magnetic knife holder. 

Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soil residues. The inspector will follow-up on 2/2/2026 to check that the above referenced are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. The facility is observed to be ware washing without soap and sanitizing. The operator was going to simply rinse a spatula between uses. Halted the behavior and discussed operator use of soap and sanitizing agent. Proper ware washing occurred. 


A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a spray bottle containing fryer cleaner was not labeled. The spray bottle was labeled during the inspection. Ensure that toxic materials removed from the bulk supply are labeled with the common name of the material.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The dust on the interior sliding cooler fan. 

(2) The food debris on the sliding cooler door track.

(3) The food debris and spills in the freezer. 

(4) The debris where the handle meets the scoop in the broccoli container. 

(5) The plumbing beneath the triple sink is observed to be soiled with accumulated grease and food debris. Clean the plumbing and the floor drain. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at time of inspection. The PIC stated that the food manager will arrive later in the day. Ensure there is a CFPM present during all times of food preparation and service.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employee improperly hand wash before donning new gloves. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are using hand soap to wash and washing for a minimum of 20 seconds every time they need to don new gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed a tray of pulled pork dated 1/12 in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed that the pork was held beyond its 7-day date mark. The tray was discarded. Ensure staff are monitoring food in the walk-in cooler and discarding at the end of day 7.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed caulking to be missing/in a state of disrepair in the following locations:
1. To the right of the dish machine

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure staff is checking caulking regularly.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The inspector observed a small freshwater leak at the mop sink as well as a leak at the dish area hand sink. The PIC was informed and maintenance will be scheduled for the plumbing concerns. Ensure these repairs are completed prior to the next routine inspection (at least 90 days).
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

At the time of this inspection none of the employees have completed a Reporting Agreement or similar paperwork verifying their knowledge of their responsibility to report illnesses. The PIC had blank copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement available and education was conducted. The PIC is instructed to make copies and have all employees sign one prior to the follow up.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink next to the ice machine only has hand sanitizer available. The container was replaced during this inspection with soap to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

To-go containers and their lids are observed with the food contact surfaces face up/exposed next to the ovens. Education was conducted and the items flipped over to correct. Ensure that all single service food contact surfaces are stored so that the food contact surfaces are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

Raw eggs are observed over lettuce and cooked pasta in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-arrange the items. They did and the violation is considered corrected at this time. Ensure that foods are stored according to their cooking temperatures so that cross contamination is not a concern moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The dish machine would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Investigation showed the jug of concentrate was empty and another is not available in the facility at the time of this inspection. The PIC called the general manager and they stated that they would pick up a new jug on the way in today. The facility will avoid doing dishes until the GM arrives with the new jug to simplify the situation. The facility does have the ability to use the three compartment sink and sanitizer is available for this process. The procedures for that were reviewed with the inspector during this inspection. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are maintained at effective use at all times. The inspector will SPOT CHECK tomorrow to vrerify that the sanitizer is in use as stated. Violations may be added tomorrow if not.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) If used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The potato slicer in the middle hallway is observed with dried on potato remains during this inspection, including the top of the last potato sliced. The PIC was consulted and stated that this equipment was used last this morning around 9:30 AM and would not likely be used again today. This equipment should be cleaned after use each morning. It was disassembled by staff and moved to dish for cleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned after use and at least every four hours while in use.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Five pans of rice and two quarter pans of pork in the hot holding unit in the middle hallway are observed with internal temperatures of 103F to 128F. The PIC was consulted and voluntarily discarded the items to correct the immediate violation. They stated that the equipment has been having issues for a while and a work order has been put in for maintenance. Multiple suggestions were given by the inspector with the simplest being to use the spare steam well as well as the bottom tray of the hot holding unit at the corner of the service counter. The hot holding unit should not be used for hot holding TCS foods until maintenance can be inducted. Because these foods are being discarded the immediate violation is being considered corrected at this time. The inspector may spot check in the coming weeks to ensure that TCS foods are properly hot held moving forward.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

A container of cooked macaroni noodles in the walk in cooler is without date marking. When asked, the PIC believed that the noodles were prepared one or two days ago. Education was conducted. To correct the immediate violation a date mark was placed on the noodles container. Ensure that all TCS foods are properly date marked at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

Multiple locations throughout the back two hallways and in the walk in cooler need the floors swept and mopped. These areas are primarily under the shelving and counters. The PIC was told and instructed to clean these locations regularly and consistently to prevent accumulation of filth. Ensure the facility is cleaned regularly and consistently.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Observed mouse droppings at the facility. There were a few droppings in the dry storage area, but there was a larger accumulation of droppings to the right of the double door cooler on the cookline. Inspector spoke with the custodian. They are having a small mouse issue throughout the building that started recently. Pest control is performed by AAA Springfield Terminate once a month. They are setting sticky straps throughout the kitchen. The following actions must be taken to eliminate pests at the facility:

- Cleaning must be a priority at the facility, especially deep cleaning under equipment and other hard to reach areas. Remove the current droppings to better monitor the issue moving forward. Communicate where they are seeing droppings appear with the custodian and pest control operator. 
- Seal all possible entry points with steal wool. Inspector observed a hole in the far right corner of the dry storage area with what appeared to be discarded steel wool on the ground. The custodian re-sealed the hole with more steel wool during the inspection. Any other possible entry points into the facility must be sealed. 
- The custodian placed more traps during the inspection in the areas where droppings were observed. Continue to utilize traps to manage pest population. 
- Store boxes at least 6-inches above the ground.
- Remove excess food, cardboard boxes, and other equipment from the facility.
- Food containers must be kept closed to eliminate food sources; especially overnight. 
- Communicate pest sightings and possible entrance points to the custodian and pest control operator. Inspector also suggests increasing the frequency of visits with the pest control company. 

An inspector will return in two weeks (2/4/2026) to check on progress to eliminate pests at the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of mouse droppings in the dry storage area. There was also a young dead mouse on a sticky trap underneath dry storage shelving. The kitchen manager noticed the issue about a month ago, but it has gotten worse in the last two weeks. The inspector was informed that the issue is throughout the entire school. Pest control is performed by AAA Springfield Terminate every two weeks to a month. They are setting traps (i.e., buckets, sticky pads, spring traps), but the custodians are not aware of any spraying. They have having some success with trapping, particularly with young mice.

The following actions must be taken to eliminate pests:

- The dry storage area must be cleaned to remove the current droppings. Removing the droppings will allow the facility to better monitor the issue moving forward. They must communicate where they are seeing droppings appear with the pest control operator.
- The northeast corner of the dry storage room has the largest accumulation of droppings; including droppings on top of food storage containers. Upon the inspectors request, the kitchen manager removed all boxes from this area to allow better visibility. The ceiling tile above the corner also has what appears to be chew marks. The custodian present was notified about the potential entrance point and will be communicating with the pest control operator.
- The boxes in the dry storage area must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground. 
- Excess containers, food, and cardboard must be removed from the dry storage area. 
- Food throughout the kitchen must be kept closed to eliminate food sources; especially overnight. 
- The large holes underneath the dish machine must be sealed (ex. install a piece of plastic or metal over the holes). Additionally, seal any other holes (using steel wool) to prevent pests from entering the facility. 
- Communicate with the pest control operator about pest sightings and entrance points. Inspector suggests a more frequent schedule for visits. 

The kitchen manager had a conversation with Springfield School District 186 manager Megan McMillan during the inspection. They were also provided with SCDPH Environmental Health Director Colleen Kelly’s card for communication moving forward. An inspector will return in two weeks (1/30/2026) to check on progress to eliminate pests at the facility.

CORRECTED- the items that had been in the temperature danger zone for over 4 hours were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. The packaging for the cream cheese, ham, and american cheese were labeled “refrigerate after opening.” The ham that had been in the cooler for 2 hours was moved to the working prep cooler to quickly cool to 41F or below. Ensure TCS foods are held at 41F or below.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. There is no sanitizing bucket present.  Not having an available sani-bucket is a completely unacceptable practice and one that has been discussed at length throughout the last several months. Sani-buckets should be discarded nightly. OR, the bucket should be discarded by the opener as a new bucket is created. The bucket is noted as being cold with soiled water. 
 See that wiping cloths are being stored within a proper sanitizing bucket. The bucket should be sized to hold several cloths and still allow space for a hand to be submerged. The most important part of sanitizing is that a testable residual of sanitizer is present in the bucket. 

Discard buckets at the end of the day or when concentration dips below the allowed amount. 

Keep a sani-bucket, that is holding proper chemical residual, available for holding wet wiping cloths. 

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. Ensure that required foods are always properly date marked.

The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspectors observed some of the employees food handlers certificates to have expired. PIC was informed. Ensure all employees handling foods obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-102.11(A) Demonstration.The kitchen has not been properly run since opening. Today marks the sixth follow-up to monitor the operations since the kitchen was closed and then allowed to reopen (earlier this year). The facility needs to educate staff on proper safe food handling as well as raise expectations in terms of how a properly cleaned facility should appear. The kitchen continues to have areas where cleaning is missed (see violations #49 and 55). Furthermore, the facility continues to have concerns regarding cooling, date marking, and overall maintenance of the walk-in cooler. 
Today’s visit was an expensive one. This marks the highest cost for a follow-up ($300) as well as a 50% increase in the permit fee for the following year. The financial incentive to improve operations is not yielding results. The next consideration for compliance will include suspension of permit for three days, then five days, and then possible complete suspension of permit. 
The next few visits indicate what next steps SCDPH will follow. SCDPH will visit in the afternoon (after 3pm) for the next visits in-order to capture all facility employees and properly educate. As there is only one operator in the store at a time, it is pivotal that all tasks are intentionally and properly completed. If the store is not closed properly, then the store cannot open properly. If cost isn’t given to labor, then cleaning and maintenance will never occur. 

In addition to the follow-up, a health educator will be asked to come and educate once or twice a month. The educator is free and will focus on one task per visit. 


 Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. The sanitizing bucket is observed from last night. A completely unacceptable practice and one that has been discussed at length. Sani-buckets should be discarded nightly. OR, the bucket should be discarded by the opener as a new bucket is created. The bucket is noted as being cold with soiled water. 
 See that wiping cloths are being stored within a proper sanitizing bucket. The bucket should be sized to hold several cloths and still allow space for a hand to be submerged. The most important part of sanitizing is that a testable residual of sanitizer is present in the bucket. 

Discard buckets at the end of the day or when concentration dips below the allowed amount. 

Keep a sani-bucket, that is holding proper chemical residual, available for holding wet wiping cloths. 

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.
