(1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There weren’t any quaternary ammonia test strips available at the facility. The owner mentioned that the facility used the last of their test strips. Quat test strips were provided to the facility to correct the violation. Ensure that quat test strips are available to be sure that concentrations are at the manufacturer’s recommendation.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Food handler training
comment:
There are currently two employees hired to operate the bar area. One employee has a food handler certificate, while the other employee does not have a food handler certificate. Discussed with the owner that anyone that handles ice will need to obtain food handler certificates. Ensure that all bartenders are food handler certified. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspectors observed 5 live, fast-moving roaches, 1 live, slow-moving roach, and 1 dead roach in the facility. The PIC stated that the last pest control visit was 12/16. The visits are bi-weekly. There were no glue traps observed placed throughout the facility. The PIC claims that another employee has been removing the glue traps. Ensure dated glue traps are placed throughout the dining room, bathrooms, service line, kitchen, dish room, and dry storage areas. Ensure that cardboard is removed from areas where pest concerns are known, as cardboard can both harbor and feed pests. Clean areas (especially drains) as frequently as possible to reduce food and water sources. A follow-up will be conducted on January 14, 2026 to ensure the presence of pests in the facility is declining. 

***Ensure receipts are kept in facility for all pest control visits***
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the coving (trim at floor/wall junction) to be damaged or missing. Ensure coving is replaced our repaired throughout the entire facility to prevent the movement of pests.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

The floors are in need of a general deep cleaning throughout the kitchen and service line. Ensure equipment is pulled away from the wall and the floors are cleaned thoroughly. The floors need to be kept clean to ensure pests are not sustaining on food debris left overnight in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on January 14, 2025 to ensure cleaning has been conducted in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
There was improper storage order in the following prep coolers in the kitchen area:
- Two containers of raw chicken were stored above sliced cheeses and lettuce heads 
- A container of raw beef was observed directly above dressings and other sauces

Discussed with the person-in-charge and the raw meats were rearranged in a manner that protects against contamination of RTE (ready-to-eat) foods. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below RTE foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There were sliced tomatoes stored along the serving line that were observed at room temperature. The PIC mentioned that the food items used as toppings are normally cold held over ice to control the safety of the food item. The items include shredded parmesan cheese, sliced tomatoes, cut onions, etc. The items were replaced to correct the violation. Discussed the need to either use temperature control or time control for the sliced tomatoes and Parmesan cheese. Be sure that all employees are on one accord regarding which safety measure is used. If using temperature control, be sure that TCS foods are properly placed on ice so that all sides of the containers are covered. If using time control, be sure that TCS are held for no longer than four hours before being switched.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a jug of pickled products stored inside of the walk in cooler that exceeded the seven day date marking. The mixture included but not limited to cut onions, pickles, and other veggies. The date listed on the jug was 12/15/2025. Discussed that any products pickled in house must not exceed the seven day rule, as they are considered TCS after preparation.  Ensure that pickled items aren’t held longer than seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There were several reduced oxygen packaged salmon stored in the drawer cooler along the cook-line. The salmon packages were thawed and the label mentioned to remove fish from packaging before thawing or keep frozen. The employees were instructed to slice a small opening into the packaging to remove the packed air to correct the violation. Ensure that ROP fish are removed from packaging before thawing occurs if the fish isn't going to be cooked immediately. Thawing food in ROP creates a perfect environment for bacteria to grow.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket on the cook-line was observed to be at 50ppm of Quaternary ammonium. The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at 0ppm of Quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade by the PIC and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that the sanitizer dispenser knob is being fully turned when filling up a sanitizer bucket. These buckets should be changed at least every two to four hours (more if they are heavily used) and should be frequently tested to ensure that they are at a label-recommended concentration. Staff should be trained on how to properly make a sanitizer bucket, how to test it, and how often to change them.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using a cell phone and then proceeded to don gloves and engage in food handling. Be sure to educate employees on when to wash hands when tasks are interrupted. citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The facility could not produce any valid food handler certificates for employees. Discussed with the owners that employees who handle pizza and ice shall obtain food handler certificates. A food handler reference sheet was given to the facility. Ensure that all employees obtain food handlers certificates. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

comment: Inspector observed there to be no sanitizer buckets available in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC, and PIC made sanitizer buckets immediately. Ensure that there is always sanitizer solution available to staff when food is being handled.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed some TCS foods in a prep table to not be at proper cold-holding temperatures. Items were: two trays of cotija cheese (51F), a tray of diced tomato (47F), cups of salsa verde (66F), mayonnaise (49F), chicken broth (47F), various sauces (60F, 60F, 60F,61F, 66F, 54F), Parmesan cheese (55F), Eggs (52F), vinaigrette (60F), and mashed potatoes (47F). All foods were discarded voluntarily. Ensure that food is always stored at 41F or below. Discarding the food makes this violation corrected on site. Inspector will still return for violation 33.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed there to be several foods without date marks in various kitchen coolers. Discussed with PIC, and pic could confirm that all items were made within the last seven days. Ensure that all TCS items are marked with a date mark within 24 hours of opening or production of food. Never keep this food longer than 7 days after date marking. Inspector will return 12/22 to re-inspect date marking practices.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed two bleach spray bottles without a label on them. Upon discussion, PIC had the bottles labeled with the common name of the cleaner. Ensure that all toxic chemicals in the kitchen are labeled.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the large lidless prep cooler on the kitchen line to be failing to hold temperature. For temperatures, see violation 22. Ensure that all cold-holding units being used to store food are capable of holding food at 41F or below. Inspector will return 12/22 to re-inspect the cooler.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) on-duty today did not have an allergen certification. Ensure that all CFPMs have valid allergen certifications.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the inside bottom surface of the prep cooler to have an accumulation of food debris. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to preclude accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM/CFM) certificate of the person in charge (PIC) expired earlier this year. Discussed retesting and inspector provided a list of ANSI-approved courses to test through. Ensure CFM certificates are renewed every 5 years.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed no paper towel present at the back hand sink. The PIC was informed and paper towels were supplied. Ensure disposable towels are available at all times to promote proper handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following food-contact surfaces to be soiled and in need of cleaning:
1. REPEAT VIOLATION ice machine is soiled with mold on interior baffles
2. Interior of pizza ovens
3. Pizza cutters kept on exterior of ovens
4. Interior and exterior of popcorn machine

Ensure these food-contact surfaces are cleaned as frequently as necessary to prevent an accumulation of soil. A follow-up will be conducted on 12/29/2025 to ensure these items are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed the seasoning shaker for the popcorn to be stored open under employee coats and personal items. The popcorn kernel bin under the machine in the cabinet was also observed left open. Ensure these containers are kept away from sources of contamination and sealed tightly when not in use.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspectors observed the door to the popcorn machine to be damaged and repaired with duct tape. The PIC was informed that duct tape is not a smooth, easily cleanable surface and therefore cannot be used on food-contact surfaces. Ensure the door to the machine is repaired with an approved material.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspectors observed a small freshwater leak in a copper pipe near the back triple sink. This pipe previously supplied water to a dish machine. This machine has since been removed and the pipe is no longer needed. The PIC has plans to cap off and remove the unnecessary plumbing. Ensure these repairs are completed prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed the coving around the bar to be peeling from the wall. Ensure the coving is sealed or replaced to prevent moisture accumulation in the wall. 

Inspectors also noted mold accumulating on the wall and floor below the freshwater leak mentioned in violation #51. Ensure the flooring and wall is cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One Food handler’s license was observed to have expired last month. The PIC stated the employee was on staff today, and that the individual will complete their food handler’s course through a preferred service, paid for by the facility. Ensure all food handler’s maintain their food handler’s license by retaking the course every three years.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Overall, the facility could use some deep cleaning. Floors throughout the facility were observed with general debris in the walk in cooler, behind the counter, and the storage areas. Can rings, card board boxes, empty soda cans, and various waste products that appear to have been incorrectly discarded were observed on the floors of the facility. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained in a manner that prevents debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed uncovered salsa verde and tomato sauces in the walk-in-cooler. Ensure ready-to-eat (RTE) foods are covered during storage to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed two bags of onions and tortillas in the rest room. CORRECTED- the PIC was informed and the onions and tortillas will be moved to a different location as soon as additional staff arrive. Ensure food is not stored in rest rooms to prevent contamination of foods.
citation_text: 3-305.12(B) Food Storage, Prohibited Areas. Toilet Rooms. FOOD may not be stored: (B) In toilet rooms. [Pf]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspectors observed the triple sink faucet to be dripping water. Ensure leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. (C)

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no hand soap to be available at bar hand washing sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was available at the back hand sink that was moved to the bar hand washing station. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped with hand soap.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no paper towels to be available at the back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are properly equipped for paper towels.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed a trash can to be blocking the bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, trash can was moved away from hand sink. Ensure all hand sinks are easily accessible.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice machine to be soiled with a layer of black mold. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be cleaned. Ensure ice is removed and wash, rinse, and sanitize the basin and baffle lip.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following facility repairs in need:
1) The triple sink needs re-attached to the wall and caulked. 
2) The coving is missing around the perimeter where the ice machine is and next to the drink shelving unit. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure repairs are completed before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be available during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure any employee working longer than 30 days has completed the required food handlers license and license is available within facility during all hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, facility has multiple CFM’s however none were available during inspection. Ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed member of staff to not use a barrier when turning off handwashing faucet. Discussed with employee, education on proper hand washing was provided and employee rewashed hands. Ensure staff is properly washing hands to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Various violations involving improper handwashing procedures observed today, as well as during previous routine inspections. It is extremely important that proper handwashing is regularly communicated to employees, as it is crucial to food safety and reducing the spread of food borne illness. Improper hand washing is a leading contributor to food borne illness. Employees have been observed washing hands in dump sinks, not using barriers to operate faucet handles after washing hands, and missed opportunities for washing hands after touching body parts with gloved hands. There are two hand-sinks in the kitchen area, however, employees are only utilizing the hand-sink in the dish area. The sink across from the cook-line is used a as dump sink. Discussed converting the dump sink to a handwashing sink, as it is conveniently located for employees to frequently wash hands. A follow-up will be scheduled for 12/26/205 to ensure that hand-sink is proper converted.
citation_text: 2-103.11(D) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (D) EMPLOYEES are effectively cleaning their hands, by routinely monitoring the EMPLOYEES' handwashing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: At least two employees were observed using bare hands to turn off the faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with the PIC. Educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. When cleaning hands, be sure to follow the following procedures: 1.)  rinse hands with warm running water 2.) apply soap and later hands and arms for at least 10 seconds 3.) rinse soap from hands under running water 4.) use a disposable towel to dry hands (before turning off faucet handles) 4.) use the disposable towel to operate faucet handles to shut off water. Ensure that these cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The ice scoop’s handle in the bar area was observed in direct contact with the ice. Discussed with PIC that ice scoops should always be stored with the handle faced upward and never in direct contact with ice. Ensure that ice scoops are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The designated handsink in the bar area was observed with a stainless steel container in the basin area. The facility uses the sink as a dump sink, as well as a handwashing sink. Discussed the need to only use the sink as a handwashing sink. A handwashing sign was given to the PIC to place on the sink. The PIC placed the sign on the sink to correct the violation. Ensure that hand-sinks remain unobstructed to allow proper access for employees to wash hands when necessary. Also be sure that the handwashing sink isn't used as a dump sink.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm (CL). The bucket contained soap and water. The bucket was re-prepared and bleach was added to the solution (tested at 100ppm CL). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize surfaces.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda gun holder in the bar area was observed heavily soiled with dried liquids and insects on the food contact surface. Shown to the PIC and the holder was taken apart and cleaned during the inspection. The facility wasn't aware that the holder was able to separate for cleaning purposes. Ensure that soda gun holders are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: There was a container of white rice stored on the counter of the cookline. The facility uses time control to control the safety of the food item, however, the rice exceeded its four hour timeframe. The person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that the rice was placed on the counter at 11am and the rice was probed at 75F at 3pm. Discussed with PIC that the rice had exceeded its four hour timeframe. The rice was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that foods that are used as time control never exceeds four hours at room temperature. Also discussed keeping track of when food its prepared.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(1) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (1) Except as specified in (B)(2), the FOOD shall have an initial temperature of 5°C (41F) or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 57°C (135°F) or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Various food items were stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and freezer. These items include but aren’t limited to shrimp, carrots, frozen meats, etc. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against cross contamination and is at least six inches above the floor at all times.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There isn’t any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerator units to allow visibility for food service workers.
citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed baklava cakes to be removed from original packaging without a date marking available. Discussed with PIC, education on proper date marking was provided and stickers were placed on baklava. Ensure any TCS item removed from its original packaging is properly date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed black mold to be present at the caulking at mop sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure staff is monitoring caulking to prevent any possible mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer solution to be at 300 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bottle was remade and tested at 100pm CL. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared at the proper sanitization level.
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspectors observed no food protection manager (CFPM) present during food preparation and service. The PIC was informed that a CFPM needs to present at all times of food prep or service. Ensure staff have certification prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed two sanitizer buckets in the kitchen measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The dispenser was tested as well, measuring 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The inspectors discovered that the detergent and sanitizer were swapped in the dispenser. Due to this mistake, the buckets were filled with a detergent solution rather than sanitizer. The bottles were swapped and the dispenser was flushed. The dispenser then measured 150ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. Ensure staff are measuring the concentration of sanitizer buckets frequently to catch when these mistakes happen and correct them. Test strips are kept at the bar for safe keeping.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed a stainless steel cup and scoop next to the server’s ice bin to be soiled and retaining old water. The PIC was informed and the cup and scoop were moved to the dish area. Ensure staff are washing and sanitizing these items frequently to prevent cross-contamination with ice.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspectors observed large containers of commercial teriyaki and sweet chili to be stored on a shelf in the kitchen. These containers stated “refrigerate after opening” on the manufacturer’s label. The PIC was informed and these containers were discarded. Ensure refrigeration requirements from the manufacturer are followed at all times. 

***Labels stating “for best flavor, refrigerate after opening” does not state a requirement. This is for flavor and quality, not safety.***
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspectors noted the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to be missing a date mark:
1. Beef sticks in walk-in
2. Cubed cheese in walk-in
3. Celery in walk-in
