title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. A supporting worker is present without a food handler certificate.  Provide food handler training for all employees. More knowledgeable staff can only help support safe food handling. 

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. CFPM is not allergen certified. 

 (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was dried food debris in the basin of the kitchen’s handwashing sink. Discussed with person-in-charge (PIC) that hand sinks are to only be used for handwashing purposes. Ensure hand sinks are never used for warewashing or as a dump sink. Be sure to educate employees on proper use of handsinks.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There are several insect devices that are located directly above food prep areas. There is a hanging glue trap (with many dead flies) placed above the prep cooler along the cookline. Discussed moving the trap further from the prep cooler or an area where food prep doesn’t occur. There is also a sticky trap stored near a holding rack where fried chicken is dumped after being fried. The PIC mentioned that Plunkett’s, the facility’s pest control company, placed the trap in that specific area. Discussed that insect traps are to never be stored in a manner where it can contaminate food or food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There are at least three baking sheet pans used to catch leaking blood from raw animal protein. These sheets are placed underneath storage racks inside of the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC that sheets are to be replaced at the end of each night if soiled with animal liquids. Ensure that sheet pans are cleaned at a frequency to preclude accumulation and unwanted odors.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Overall, the facility is in need of a detail cleaning in many areas of the store - including floors, walls, and ceilings of the cook-line and the bakery area, floor of the walk in cooler, floors and walls in the back stock area, and underneath and behind large pieces of equipment. PIC mentioned that the facility is in the process of a transition and that they are planning to perform a deep cleaning soon. In the meantime, be sure to thoroughly clean the facility during down time to prevent the buildup of splatter and food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the upright white cooler closest to the door if the kitchen to measure 50F with the infrared probe. This cooler failure must be a recent occurrence, as the yogurt within the cooler measured 41F with a probe thermometer. All TCS foods within the cooler was transferred to an alternative cold holding unit. PIC was made aware of the failure and plans to contact maintenance. Since the facility has adequate cold holding equipment aside from the cooler that failed, this violation is considered corrected on site with no follow-up needed. Inspector will call occasionally to spot check cooler repair process.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed no food handler’s certificates available at the facility. The PIC was informed and has an action plan to certify all kitchen staff. The PIC currently operating the kitchen as a CFPM from previous employment. Ensure all kitchen staff have food handler’s or food manager’s by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-102.11(A) Demonstration. The certified food manager was present in the morning. They began opening operations and then felt sick and left. There is currently no one with food safety knowledge in the store. The foods being prepared were left out on the counter as the operator left for home. During the inspection, the gentleman present stated that the operator would return presently, however, when a phone call was placed, a friend answered and stated the operator was sleeping. The facility is in a poor state of condition due to lack of active managerial control that occurred well beyond today. The owner and a new operator were present for a spot check about one month ago. At that time, SCDPH was assured that safe food handling knowledge would be applied to the facility and conditions would change. The kitchen has not been properly run since opening. Today, the facility is closed until the owner can clean, conduct appropriate repairs, and prove that the staff is able to safely handle food. 


 Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. There is no food protection manager present. The operator present has no basic knowledge of safe food handling. The store should have one certified food manager present during all hours of operation. 

 (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. The handwashing sink is observed to have a plastic container within the basin. Thus obstructing the use of the sink. Discussed with the operator that the handwashing sink should always be left available for use. Remove the plastic container so the sink is accessible. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability.  There is no soap observed in the bathroom handwashing sink. Provide soap for the bathroom. 

Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Neither the kitchen handwashing sink nor the bathroom handwashing sink was supplied with paper toweling. Provide a supply of drying towels for handsinks. 

 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. There are observed containers of spices in the dry storage area that are unopened. Above them is a slew of possible sources of cross-contamination. The foil used to line the shelving is ripped with pieces falling onto the shelf below. There are crumbs from other spices and nuts on the torn foil shelf, and there are half used water bottles (personal beverages) scattered throughout the shelf. The water bottles were discarded. The shelf is still in a state of disrepair and there is potential for spices, nuts, and soil to fall into the opened containers below. See that the spices are properly covered, shelving is cleaned, and shelving is maintained in sound repair. 

 FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(7) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. There is observed molded cucumbers in the walk-in cooler within a bulk box of produce. Also, there is observed a half dozen or more soft, green, and sprouted potatoes in the dry storage room. Finally, sprouted garlic is observed, apparently forgotten, under the grill line. The potatoes were discarded. Cease use of molded and old food. Use food that is in sound condition. Discard molded food from the facility. 

 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (7) Storing damaged, spoiled, or recalled food being held in the food establishment as specified under § 6-404.11.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed a container of raw animal protein with added grilled onions to be sitting on the counter. The operator was sick and left for home. The food is observed at 71F. The food should have been replaced in the walk-in cooler prior to leaving. SCDPH asked for the food to be discarded as the operator could not provide the time animal protein was removed from walk-in cooler. Ensure any raw TCS food item is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination. 

Also, observed an old chicken box to be used to hold clean utensils. Cease use of animal protein boxes for any storage other than the original contents. This strategy for storage presents a huge potential for cross contamination. 


 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed an open tub of raw ground beef to be stored on the top shelf of the walk-in cooler over fresh vegetables. Remove raw proteins to shelving below the produce.  

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed a bag of onions being stored on the soiled floor of the dry storage area. The floors are observed coated with soil and grease. Keep unprotected produce off the floor to prevent cross contamination from mopping activities and soil. 

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. Storage shall occur at least six inches above the floor.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. The sanitizing bucket is a shallow metal tin with cold water that tested at 0ppm Cl. The container appears to have never been used and is from a previous day’s creation. There are dry cloths around the kitchen. See that wiping cloths are being stored within a proper sanitizing bucket. The bucket should be sized to hold several cloths and still allow space for a hand to be submerged. The most important part of sanitizing is that a testable residual of sanitizer is present in the bucket. Discard buckets at the end of the day or when concentration dips below the allowed amount. 
Keep a sani-bucket, that is holding proper chemical residual, available for holding wet wiping cloths. 

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. Observed utensils left in-use from a possible previous day. The operator left for the day and remaining on the counters was a spoon with old rice debris and a cutting board and knife with old food debris present. Also, the triple sink is observed filled with old dishes that are coated in food. The dishes are not being done nightly. Failure to complete dishes at the end of the day provides a possible food source for pests. Dishes should be done nightly to prevent the accumulation of bacteria growth throughout the evening too. 

Also, there is an upright meat slicer in the back room with a soiled blade, soiled pushing blade, and soiled cutting table. 

Leave the store ready for the next day’s use. Clean dishes nightly. 


(C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. There is observed a rice steamer holding rice at 90F. The rice is from yesterday. Rice was asked to be discarded. 


 (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. There is a container of raw animal proteins on the counter in-front of the grill. The food is temped at 68F. The food was discussed to have been pulled from the cooler, had cooked onion added, and then left as the sick employee left for home. The food should have been returned to the cooler as the operator was leaving or discarded depending on symptoms and prior food handling practices. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Of the dozens of containers of cooked foods noted in the walk-in cooler, only three or four were date marked. Most of the foods observed in the walk-in cooler were barely covered with foil and lacking a date mark. Properly mark cooked foods with the date they are created at the end of the service day. Again, proper closing procedures lends to a proper opening. 


(A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. A container of cooked animal protein is observed in the walk-in cooler with a date of November 5. Food was well beyond the allowed seven days. Food is observed with an apparent film of slime mold. Discard TCS food left in the cooler longer than seven days. 

 (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: 
Observed several ROP containers of salmon to be thawed in the walk-in cooler without the packaging being cut. The labeling on the salmon indicates that the packaging should be cut prior to thawing in the refrigerator. The salmon packages were cut during the inspection. 


(E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. There is observed containers of spices without a lid to protect from overhead contamination. Covered during the inspection. 

 (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-802.11(E) Specifications. Dry wiping cloths are observed stored, unfolded, atop single-service, on the side of the cook line, on a roll rack by the handwashing sink, and on various counters of the kitchen. Store clean linens in a specific area where they are not subject to splash and cross-contamination. 

(E) Dry wiping cloths shall be laundered as necessary to prevent contamination of FOOD and clean serving UTENSILS.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. There is observed an old knife box, that is soiled with grease accumulation and spilled spices, holding portion cups and lids. Discard the portion cups and the box. The portion cups have become soiled with grease and contents of the box. 

Observed single-service boxes of cups and to-go etc on the floor of the front cashier space. Store single-service articles at least 6” off the floor to allow for proper cleaning and prevent cross-contamination. 

(C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

title: Gloves used properly.
citation_text: 3-304.15(B) Gloves, Use Limitations: Observed old gloves (inverted as if pulled-off and some pulled from the tips as if for possible reuse) stored around the kitchen. Gloves should be for single-use only and not saved for possible reuse. Discard gloves after one use. Discarded during the inspection.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. Observed the foil wrapped shelving to be damaged and broken. Cease use of foil to line the shelving if it is unable to be properly maintained. 

(A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. Multiple surfaces throughout the kitchen are noted to be soiled with old food debris and grease. Most notably is the interior of the microwave which is observed thickly encrusted with multiple days use. Also, observed tongs stored as clean over the triple sink to be soiled with old food debris. Containers on the storage rack adjacent to the triple sink are observed coated with grease and crumbs. 

 (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) The faucet at the back preparation sink is loose. There has been a repair, but it has been insufficient. Repair the faucet. 

A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
citation_text:
5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. The facility has mop water remaining from yesterday’s cleaning. Leaving soiled water present overnight is a potential source of water-borne pathogens as well as a water source for pests. Empty mop water nightly. Emptied during the inspection. 

 Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.18 Cleaning of Plumbing Fixtures. The bathroom is coated with soil from use. Clean the bathroom immediately.  

PLUMBING FIXTURES such as HANDWASHING SINKS, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing.  Observed a ceiling tile to the left of the hood to be bubbled from possible water damage. Replace the ceiling tile. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. The wall behind the cook line is observed thickly coated with soil and grease. Also, observed the corner of the dry storage area to have an accumulation of what appears to be dead gnats. Finally, the floor in-front of the triple sink and around the meat slicer is thickly coated with grease, soil, and blood. Clean the floor immediately after each use of the meat slicer. 


(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. Observed at least five bottles of water and one coffee cup stored within cooking equipment and food storage. Bottles of water are all half-opened. Multiple bottles are observed resting on their side. Discarded the water bottles during the inspection. Cease storing personal drinks within food preparation, storage, and serving areas.  

(A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. Present party is neither CFPM nor food handler qualified. Provide food handler training for all participating employees. More knowledgeable staff can only help support safe food handling. 

(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. CFPM is not allergen certified. 

 (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- An employee was observed to not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. CORRECTED- The employee was educated on the proper handwashing procedure and was later observed to use the proper handwashing procedure. Ensure that all staff are educated on proper handwashing and are using a barrier when turning off the faucet to avoid re-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There is observed to be ice in a basin that is uncovered. Ice should be covered when not in use to prevent contamination. Ensure that a cover is provided when ice is not actively being used. A follow up is scheduled for 12/19/2025 to ensure that there is a cover over the ice to protect the ice from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine in the bar area is observed to be sanitizing at 0ppm of Chlorine. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that staff are not using this dish machine to wash, rinse, and sanitize dishes. If the dish machine is used, the dishes need to be sanitized in the triple sink after being ran through the dish machine. A follow up is scheduled for 12/15/2025 to ensure that the dish machine has been repaired and is properly sanitizing at a label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There are single-use straws that are observed to be in a container on the bar counter that are unwrapped. Single-service articles should be wrapped to protect them from contamination. The straw being unwrapped exposes it to contamination, as the employee either needs to grab the straw to place it in the drink or the consumer will need to grab the straw and could potentially contaminate the other straws in the container. Ensure that straws that are wrapped are obtained to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility is observed to be using Purell sanitizer spray to sanitize surfaces, but does not have a test strip for this sanitizer. A test strip is necessary to ensure that the sanitizer is at the correct concentration. Ensure that a test strip is obtained for Purell sanitizer spray or cease use of it and use the Quaternary ammonium sanitizer to wipe down food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- There is an accumulation of popcorn and food debris on the floor under the equipment across from the popcorn machine. 
2. The nonfood contact surfaces of the slushy machines were observed to have an accumulation of dust on them. 

This was shown to the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is a drip leak observed to be coming from under the triple sink in the kitchen. A follow up is scheduled for 12/15/2025 to ensure that the leak has been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to allow for proper disposal of sewage.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food handler training
comment: Food handler cards for all staff not certified. * No sense of cheating with this-take the course/test as a group.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: prep cooler lid has broken right side bucket holding up thawing shelf in walk in cooler will need a non busy day to remove products & see if bucket is holding the shelf. Facility will repair in 2026.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the non-food contact surfaces equipment on the line to have a build-up of oils and food debris. Ensure that equipment is cleaned frequently enough to keep it clean. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a build-up of oils behind the grill and griddle on the line. Ensure that these areas are cleaned regularly enough to mitigate the build-up of oils. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There were several dented cans observed to be for sale on the shelf, including, but not limited to, mixed vegetables, sliced mangos, beef barley soup, fruit cocktail, and evaporated milk. CORRECTED- These items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. It is important to remove dented cans from being sold, as dents in cans exposes the food to contamination from bacteria growth. Ensure that any dented cans are discarded of or returned to the distributor.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There was not an ambient thermometer observed to be in the walk-in cooler/freezer. An ambient thermometer is necessary, as the digital thermometer should not be relied on. Ensure that there is an ambient thermometer placed in the warmest part of the unit (closest to the door) by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a floor drain cover missing on the drain in front of the mop sink. This drain also appears to be on the verge of backing up. Ensure that this is kept an eye on and that the drain cover is replaced. A drain cover is important due to it blocking items from going into the drain, potentially causing a sewage back-up. Ensure that this drain cover is replaced by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspector observed Medium-risk food class behaviors (hot holding) during today’s inspection. None of the staff at today’s inspection were Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPMs). Class II facilities must have a CFPM present to oversee proper food handling practices and temperatures for ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure a CFPM is present at all times during which food is being handled or hot held to mitigate the risk foodborne illnesses.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: No employee reporting agreements were available at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- all staff who were present signed the Employee Reporting Agreements. Ensure Employee Reporting Agreements are signed by all staff and maintained on file for future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed an opened package of hotdogs (used for roller dogs) unlabeled and stored in the standing retail cooler. CORRECTED- package was moved to a cooler in the back of the store. Open packages of food for the public allow for a risk of contamination and adulteration. Cease this practice.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
All Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items in the facility’s open air cooler were observed to contain an ambient temperature of 52F, and have internal temperatures between 46-53F. The PIC stated that the items had been in the cold holding unit for over 4 hours. CORRECTED: the following items were TCS OR labeled as “Keep Refrigerated”, and voluntarily removed from service, to be returned to the food supplier:
Cookie dough (X12), Chobani yogurt( X4), Pudding cups (X4), Sub sandwiches (X5), fruit cups (X3), grilled cheese sandwiches (X12), Italian wraps (X2), beef and cheddar sticks (X22), cheddar and salami sticks (X10), cheddar cheese curds (X3), Colby jack string cheese (X20), mozzarella and salami (X7), pepperoni and mozzarella (X7), mozzarella string cheese (X13), chocolate cake (X5), pickles (X12), banana cake (X8), strawberry cake (X5), birthday cake (X9), carrot cake (X4).
Ensure all TCS foods (as well as foods labeled “Keep Refrigerated”) are stored in cooling units that are at or below 41F. Inspector will do a spot check and bring temperature logs to maintain once the open air cooler is observed at or below 41F. Until that time utilize standing retail coolers for TCS foods.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The open air cooler was observed holding TCS foods between 46-53F. The unit contained a stem thermometer to monitor ambient temperatures, which initially read at 52F. During today’s inspection a myriad of TCS foods had to be discarded (see violation #22), and the open air cooler was unplugged and turned back on. The temperature of the unit was observed to be going down, but ensure the unit has either been serviced, or observed be able to hold foods at or below 41F before putting TCS foods back into this unit. The inspector will return by 12/22/25 to check the cold holding temperatures of this unit.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The facility’s stem thermometer was observed to be 8F higher than the inspector’s thermometer. CORRECTED- Education was provided and all stem thermometers were calibrated using the ice water method. Ensure all cold holding units contain accurate thermometers to monitor temperatures for food safety.
citation_text: 4-502.11(B) Good Repair and Calibration. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be calibrated in accordance with manufacturer's specifications as necessary to ensure their accuracy. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The drink divider racks in the facilities cooler were observed to contain an accumulation of mold. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of any soil debris. Inspector and the PIC discussed rotating which racks get deep cleaned on a regular basis. Deep clean these nonfood contact surfaces by the next routine inspection.
* This violation was noted as #55 at the pre-opening, and has since been reclassified.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The faucets at the facility’s triple sink were observed to be leaking. Ensure all plumbing is repaired by a licensed plumber 
* This violation was noted as #55 at the pre-opening, and has since been reclassified.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The following physical facilities noted during the pre-opening are still in need of repair:
-Replace wood shelves over the 3 compartment sink with something smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
-Eliminate tape in the mop sink. Fill holes in the wall.
Physical facilities should be made to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
None of the staff were able to produce a Food Handler’s certificate during today’s inspection. Ensure all staff take an ANSI-approved Food Handler course, and print to maintain on file for future inspections. Inspector will provide a list of courses to the PIC when returning on 12/22. Ensure all staff members, and new staff obtain a Food Handler’s license within 30 days of hire.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was a severely dented can of campbell’s soup on a shelf in the grocery section. The dents were on the side seam of the can and there was a point at the top seam. The can was pulled from the shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that packaging of food items are in dent free condition.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a bottle of glass cleaner stored on a shelf directly above the triple sink. Discussed with PIC and the bottle was removed. Ensure that toxic chemicals are stored in a manner that prevents contamination of clean dishes.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed stagnant waste water inside of the mop sink in the back-stock area. The person-in-charge (PIC) mentioned that a work order will be placed to have the sink serviced so that waste water is able to drain properly. Stagnant waste water can attract unwanted pest and insects.  Ensure that waste water is never stagnant and is able to drain in an appropriate sanitary manner.
citation_text: 5-402.15 Flushing a Waste Retention Tank. A tank for liquid waste retention shall be thoroughly flushed and drained in a sanitary manner during the servicing operation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival, there wasn't a certified food protection manager available. A CFPM arrived shortly after the start of the inspection to correct the violation. Person-in-charge mentioned that the facility will work to get the main cook food manager certified. Ensure that there is always at least one employee who is food manager certified during operating hours.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer solution available while food prep was occurring. Discussed with PIC and a sanitizer bucket was created. Demonstrated how to properly test sanitizer solutions using (CL)test strips. Ensure that there is ALWAYS a sanitizer bucket available during hours of operation (including the shack where food is being cooked and held).
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed a loaded cart obstructing the hand sink. Discussed with PIC and the cart was removed to ensure an accessible hand sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are accessible at all time for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed  soil accumulation in the soda gun nozzle. Discussed with PIC and the soda gun nozzle was cleaned immediately. Ensure that food contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION. An accumulation of food debris was observed under the fryer in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the surface would get clean. Ensure that closed spaces under equipments are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking along the triple sink was observed to be wearing out. Inspector also observed a broken tile with settle water under the foot of the grill. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that accessory equipments in facility are monitored, cleaned, and in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspectors observed facility not being in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the person with the CFPM certification will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure that at least one certified food protection manager at the facility obtain a basic allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The person in charge (PIC) was unable to produce employee reporting agreements. Inspector gave the PIC a blank employee reporting agreement. Have employees review and sign agreement to maintain on file for future inspections. Inspector will return on 12/19/25 to check for compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple food handlers wash their hands, and turn off the faucet without a barrier. CORRECTED- education occurred with the food handlers regarding proper hand washing/ drying procedures. Frequently review proper hand washing procedures with all employees to prevent the recontamination of clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw meat stored above milk in the kitchen’s double door cooler. CORRECTED- kitchen staff rearranged the raw meat below the milk to reflect proper storage order. Inspector provided the PIC with storage order chart to review with employees, or post on a cooling unit. Ensure animal proteins are always stored below ready to eat (RTE) foods, and animal proteins are stored by increasing cooking temperatures. Items that require the highest internal cooking temperatures should be stored at the bottom of cooling units to prevent the contamination of foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed multiple Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) foods to be out of temperature. Milk in the mini fridge on the counter was initially observed at 45F, and multiple desserts in the display cooler were observed to have an ambient temperature between 45-51F. After turning down the cooling units, the following items were observed above 41F: 2 cherry pies (45F internal temperature), 1 chocolate cream pie (45 internal temperature), and 1 cinnamon roll with cream cheese icing (46F). CORRECTED- the food items listed were removed from the cooling unit to be discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are maintained at or below 41F by frequent monitoring of ambient thermometers.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The dessert display cooler and mini fridge at the server station were both observed to have ambient temperatures between 45-51. CORRECTED- units were turned down. Ensure all cold holding units are holding TCS foods at or below 41F. Monitor with ambient thermometers.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: A container of shredded cheese in the walk in cooler was observed without a lid. CORRECTED-a pizza pan was placed over the container. Ensure that all foods are protected from contaminants at all applicable times.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan has an accumulation of dust. 
2. The shelves holding the dry storage items between the walk-in cooler and walk-in freezer. 
3. The floor under the triple sink. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food Handler Certificates were unavailable for multiple employees on staff during today’s inspection. Ensure all food service staff obtain a Food Handler’s certificate to be made available during future inspections. Inspector provided guidance on where to find ANSI-approved Food Handler’s certificate Courses.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
No Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPMs) on site during today’s inspection had completed Allergen Training. Inspector provided literature on Allergen training to the PIC. Ensure CFPMs complete Allergen Training, and maintain on file for future inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed there was not paper towels at the hand washing sink next to the ice machine. During the inspection paper towels were brought to the hand washing sink. Ensure there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed utensils and food debris in the hand washing sink basin by the ice machine. The PIC was educated that hand washing sinks cannot be used for purposes other than hand washing. Ensure that hand washing sinks are only used for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: Facility bags ice on-site from their ice machine, but is not equipped with the necessary equipment to handle ice in a sanitary manner. There is no 3 compartment sink on-site for use to wash, rinse, and sanitize the ice scoop. Facility voluntarily discarded all ice that has already been bagged, and will need to cease handling of ice until a 3 compartment sink is installed in the facility.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed shell eggs stored over milk inside the cooler at the back of the store. During the inspection an employee moved the eggs onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Facility’s 3 compartment sink has been removed, leaving the facility with no way to wash, rinse, and sanitize their ice scoop. Facility cannot handle any food (including ice) without a 3 compartment sink. Inspector will follow up on December 22, 2025 to discuss facility’s plans moving forward. In the meantime, facility must stop handling all food (including ice).
citation_text: 4-301.12(B) Manual Warewashing, Sink Compartment Requirements. (B) Sink compartments shall be large enough to accommodate immersion of the largest EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. If EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS are too large for the WAREWASHING sink, a WAREWASHING machine or alternative EQUIPMENT as specified in (C) of this section shall be used. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of debris on the shelves holding drinks in the walk-in cooler. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were packages of raw shelled eggs on a container of cut onions and above a bowl of salad mix. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the eggs onto another shelf and proper storage order was discussed. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is a drip leak coming from the pipes under the triple sink in the kitchen. The PIC has a plumber coming to repair the issue tomorrow. A follow up is scheduled on 12/12/2025 to ensure that the leak has been repaired. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair to allow sewage to be properly disposed of.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the bleach spray bottle in the kitchen to be too strong. Solution in the spray bottle was beaching out test strips. CORRECTED Inspector and PIC mixed a new bleach solution at 100PPM. Ensure that bleach solutions are no higher than 100PPM. Facility has test strips.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No employees at the establishment had access to a CFPM license. Ensure that at least one employee has access to their Certified Food Protection Manager credentials at all times food is being prepared. Correct by next routine inspection (at least 90 days from today).
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed the door seals of the prep cooler in the kitchen to be repaired with duct tape. Discussed with PIC and Cook, both informed inspector that the parts are already being looked at to properly repair the unit. Ensure that equipment is smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Duct tape is not considered smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. Ensure this is completed by the next routine inspection (at least 90 days from now).

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT X2) Inspector observed the wall across the hall from the mop sink to need painted. It has been repaired, but still lacks paint. A coat of paint will render the wall smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. 

Inspector also observed the wall above the mop sink guard to be soiled and crumbling. Ensure this area is repaired. The nature of soils may require Kilz or another anti microbial paint to mitigate future damage from soils.

Correct by next routine inspection (at least 90 days from today).
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
(REPEAT X3) Ensure that all CFPMs are allergen certified once they are able to obtain their certified food protection manager license. Correct by next routine inspection (at least 90 days from today).

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed the faucets of both hand washing sinks on the front line to be dripping. Ensure the leaks are repaired by the next routine inspection. Plumbing shall be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed caulking on the left side of the kitchen’s (first) hand washing sink to be fragmented. Seal the sink to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold by the next routine inspection. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor drains in the kitchen and the floors under the hot kitchen line were observed to contain an accumulation of debris. Periodically move equipment to deep clean. Floors should be cleaned.at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed several dead roaches underneath equipment throughout the entire facility. Prioritize pulling out equipment to clean underneath. The inspector will check on cleaning at the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A)  Inspectors observed multiple food items including but not limited to chicken, beans, and pork in stainless steel food containers stored in the walk-in cooler and the stainless steel double doors standing cooler in the kitchen. Inspectors also saw a container of chicken that was dated12/25/25 but the used by date had expired. PIC told inspectors that the food items were made the day before. PIC discarded the container of chicken dated 12/25/25 as a corrective action. PIC also instructed a staff member to properly date the food items that were not properly dated marked. Ensure that food items that are prepared and being stored for more than 24-hours are properly date marked and stored. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket connected to the bar dish machine was empty when the inspector arrived. During the inspection the empty bucket was switched with a new one and the dish machine re-tested at 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that food contact surfaces are always properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the bar hand washing sink is not sealed to the wall. Ensure that the hand washing sink is sealed to the wall (ex. caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is not cove base along the wall in the ware washing room behind the triple sink and ice machine. There are several cracks along the wall seam that are accumulating dirt and other debris. Ensure that there is cove base present by the next routine inspection.
