title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the handwashing sink to be obstructed by a sanitizer bucket. Discussed with PIC, and bucket was removed from the sink to allow for easy hand washing. Ensure that hand sinks are not obstructed during service.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen to have too much bleach in it. It was bleaching out the strips. Inspector dumped sanitizer bucket and mixed a new bucket at 50PPM of chlorine sanitizer. Ensure sanitizer is made at the correct concentration. Facility has test strips.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The bleach available isn’t an EPA approved chemical for sanitizing food contact surfaces. The chemical is low splash and can’t be used for sanitizing purposes. Discussed purchasing EPA regulated bleach with the person-in-charge (PIC). Ensure that bleach used for sanitizing is EPA registered (not low splash or scented).
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed shrimp being thawed in the basin of the hand washing sink next to the kitchen office. CORRECTED- shrimp was removed from the sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for no other purpose than hand washing, so as to not deter hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas in the facility needing repair:
1) FIRST REPEAT: Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The bar hand-sink needs caulked to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to be made smooth and easily cleanable.
3) There are tiles underneath the dry storage along the north wall of the kitchen have separated from the wall.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: None of the facility’s Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPM)s have allergen awareness certificates. Allergen Awareness information (given during the previous inspection) is in black binder with the other paperwork. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training in Class I facilities. Certificates must be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.[C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Facility's quaternary ammonia test strips were observed to be nonfunctional. CORRECTED- functioning test strips were obtained during the inspection. Ensure functioning test strips (that correspond with sanitizer) are always available.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed there was not soap at the front hand washing sink. During the inspection the PIC brought a bottle of soap to the hand washing sink. Ensure that there is always soap available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (quat). During the inspection the sanitizer bucket was re-made testing at 200 ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration (200-400 ppm for quat).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPAT VIOLATION FROM THE PRE-OPENING:

Observed the cove base to the left of the triple sink is peeling away from the wall. Ensure that the cove base is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No CFPM was present at time of inspection. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that a CFPM is present at the facility whenever food is being prepped and handled.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw chicken feet being stored over raw beef in the WIC. Discussed with PIC, and PIC moved the chicken below the beef. Ensure that meats are stored in the correct order to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Two workers were observed to not have food handler certifications. Discussed with PIC and PIC stated they would get them soon. Ensure all people handling food in establishment are licensed. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed facility to have no sanitizer bucket set up during inspection. (CORRECTED) Discussed with PIC, and PIC mixed a sanitizer bucket at 400PPM of quaternary ammonium sanitizer. Ensure that kitchen staff have access to a prepared sanitizer bucket whenever food preparation is taking place.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility when the inspector arrived. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. The inspector suggests more employees taking the CFPM class to ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Observed that the employee health reporting agreements were not signed by all employees. During the inspection all employees signed the agreement. Ensure that new employees sign the agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. During the inspection the sanitizer bucket was re-made testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizing concentrations are always testing at the correct concentration (50-200 ppm (Cl)).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the rice cooker on the counter was hot holding rice between 125-130F. The PIC stated that the rice was cooked at 12 pm. The rice was put under a time-as-control policy and any leftover rice will be discarded at 4 pm. The PIC was instructed to closely monitor the temperature of the rice cooker to ensure that it is functioning properly. The inspector will return on 12/8/2025 to check that the rice is being hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed the facility was using Always Save Bleach that does not have an EPA registration. The PIC was educated that bleach must have an EPA registration indicating that it is safe for food contact surfaces. During the inspection Chlorox bleach with an EPA registration was brought to the facility. Ensure that bleach for sanitizing solutions always has an EPA registration.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee handling raw bacon and then proceeded to grab sandwich bread from the toaster wearing the same gloves. The employee was educated about the importance of removing gloves, washing hands, and donning new gloves when switching between handling raw meats to ready-to-eat foods. The bread was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that hands are always clean to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed an employee grab sandwich bread with their bare hands. The employee was educated that ready-to-eat foods must always be handed with a barrier (i.e., single-use gloves, utensils, or deli tissue). The bread was discarded during the inspection and the employee donned gloves to grab a new piece of bread. Ensure that employees always use a barrier when handling ready-it-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed the scoop for the sugar container does not have a handle. The inspector educated that all scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of the food to avoid bare hands contacting the food. Ensure that the sugar container has a proper scoop by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the ice machine baffles have an accumulation debris. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The PIC and inspector discussed creating a routine cleaning schedule and posting a log by the ice machine to ensure that it is being cleaned regularly. The inspector will follow-up on 12/16/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles has been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed sugar by the large prep cooler and flour by the fryers were stored unpackaged in containers without labeling. All easily mistakable foods (ex. white powders) not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. The salt and flour containers were properly labeled during the inspection. Ensure that easily mistaken foods removed from original packaging are always labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The bottom shelf of the double cooler has an accumulation of food debris.

(2) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The inside of the microwave has an accumulation of debris.

(3) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The bar soda nozzle holder has an acclimation of debris on the bottom. 

(4) The accumulation of soda syrup on the shelving above the soda machine.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:

(1) Paint the cabinets in the server station.

(2) Replace the wood top counter under the pass-thru window in the kitchen with stainless steel. 

(3) Replace rotted cabinets underneath the hand washing sink in the kitchen. 

(4) Replace the table that holds the meat slicer. 

(5) Replace the wooden shelves by the large (salad) prep cooler in the kitchen with stainless steel shelving. 

(6) Replace the missing electrical outlet cover on the wall behind the fryers. 

(7) Replace the old mop sink with the new mop sink that was purchased. 

(8) Replace the wood shelving above the triple sink with stainless shelving. 

Ensure that the above referenced physical facilities are repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed single use to-go bowls submerged in 5 gallon buckets of vinegar as well as soy sauce (for use as a scoop). Inspector informed the person in charge (PIC) that scoops in service must have handles to avoid bare hand contact with the ready to eat (RTE) food items. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the soup bowls. Inspector advised the use of ladles or scoops with handle for the future. Utensils used for RTE foods, ice, and sauces must have a distinction between food contact and hand contact surfaces.
* This violation was previously noted as violation #43, but has been moved to a #9.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed soap and steel wool in the basin of the hand washing sink at the sushi station. CORRECTED- soap and steel wool were moved to the dump sink. Discussion was had regarding the availability of hand washing sink. The hand washing sink must be available for hand washing ONLY at all times. If the sink is being cleaned, the supplies used to clean the sink should only be brought over at that time, from the dish area, and immediately returned. Cleaning the sink must be a separate task from washing hands, so as not to contaminate hands. Cease this practice.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed three cans in the facility’s dry storage to contain significant dents. Two cans of soy sauce contained large dents along the body, and one can of water chestnuts contained a large dent along the top seam. CORRECTED- cans were moved into a cardboard box to be returned to the supplier. PIC stated this should be standard practice (checking for dented cans and moving to cardboard box to receive credit from food supplier). Remind kitchen staff of this practice. Inspector provided dented can infographic to the PIC, and will spot check for dented cans with the employee health educator before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw chicken stored above RTE sauce in the sliding grill cooler (against the wall). CORRECTED- chicken was moved to the bottom shelf on the other side of the cooler. Ensure all RTE food items are always stored above animal proteins to prevent the contamination of RTE foods and sauces.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Two sanitizers bucket at the grill contained a low concentration of Chlorine bleach sanitizer (0 and 10 ppm respectively).
CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizer buckets to (0->100 ppm [bucket behind grill] and 10->200 ppm Cl [bucket across hot holding]) an acceptable sanitizing concentration. Monitor sanitizer concentration with facility’s test strips. Ensure sanitizer is at the concentration recommended by the manufacture’s label, and made ONLY with EPA-labeled bleach and water.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no ambient thermometer in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC moved an ambient thermometer from the walk in freezer to the walk in cooler- near the door. Ensure all cooling units contain ambient thermometers near the warmest part of the unit to monitor proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a fly strip above covered soy sauce and a box of unwashed produce on the cookline. Discussion took place with the PIC regarding proper placement of fly strips (away from areas of food preparation and food storage). Ensure insect control devices are placed in locations that prevent the possible contamination of ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: A leak was observed from the plumbing under the hand washing sink in the dish area. CORRECTED- PIC tightened a fitting, and the pipe was observed to no longer be leaking. Ensure all plumbing is maintained to prevent leaks and convey wastewater out of the facility.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas of the physical facility in need of repair:
1) The caulking on the wall to the right of the dish machine is fragmented. 
2) There are a few small holes from previous shelving on the wall to the right of the dish machine.
3) The hand washing sink nearest the walk in cooler is beginning to separate from the wall (on the left side).
Ensure all surfaces are sealed and repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection to prevent the entry of water and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed ice accumulation under the fan unit in the walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, unit will be serviced. Ensure staff is checking equipment at a frequency that prevents ice accumulation.
citation_text: 4-201.11 Equipment and Utensils. EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the containers holding clean utensils have an accumulation of food debris on the bottom. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food debris. Ensure that the containers are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed washing hands without using a barrier to turn off faucet handles. Discussed with person-in-charge proper handwashing procedures. When washing hands, be sure to educate employees on using barriers to turn off faucet handles to avoid recontaminating freshly washed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
There was improper storage order in the following cold holding equipment:
- Raw chicken stored above produce and seafood items in the walk in cooler
- Raw chicken stored above seafood and ready-to-eat foods in the kitchen prep cooler

Items were rearranged to correct the violation. Ensure that chicken is always stored below any RTE foods or foods with lower cooking temperature to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

On arrival the inspector observed a box on top of the kitchen hand sink. The box was removed to correct. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation (C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sanitizer bucket in the kitchen is observed with a concentration of 0 ppm CL. The PIC was shown and had the bucket remade to correct. They also stated that the bucket was likely from lunch service and had not been changed since this morning. Ensure that all sanitizers in the facility are changed when needed so that they are maintained at effective concentration.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

1) The left side of the mop sink has a gap forming and needs to be resealed to the wall. 2) The baseboard/coving to the right of the three part sink are observed pulling away from the wall. Re-seal to the wall. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair/reseal prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The soda nozzles in the drive thru area are observed soiled. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean them. The nozzles were removed and disassembled and then cleaned during this inspection to correct the immediate situation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared and ready for use. A solution was prepared during this inspection to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use in the facility at all times that foods and food contact surfaces are handled.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

A brown cigarette is observed wrapped in plastic wrap and stored in the standing cooler in the kitchen. It is above and next to foods intended for consumers. The PIC was shown and instructed to remove the item. They did so to correct the violation. Ensure that employee personal items are stored separated from foods intended for consumers.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The soap dispenser at the handwashing sink next to the preparation area in the kitchen is observed to be broken and there is no hand soap available at the sink. CORRECTED- The PIC placed hand soap at the handwashing sink and plans on fixing the soap dispenser. Ensure that all handwashing sinks always have a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were pans of raw steaks above pans of potatoes in the Banquet Walk-In Cooler. CORRECTED- The PIC corrected the storage order and the steaks were moved below the potatoes. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The dish machine in the kitchen was observed to have Laundry Chlorine Bleach hooked up to it and was only heat sanitizing at 146F. The PIC called EcoLab regarding this issue. The EcoLab representative has ordered a part to repair the dish machine, as it is not properly reaching a heat sanitizing temperature of 165F or above. The Laundry Chlorine Bleach was disconnected from the machine, as this was the wrong chemical delivered by US Foods. The EcoLab representative explained that the dish machine does not always properly reach the heat sanitizing temperature needed due to heavy usage and not having a booster directly on the machine, therefore, there is an ultra-sanitizer chemical hooked up to the machine to ensure that it is sanitizing dishes. The PIC will be obtaining this chemical to ensure that it is sanitizing. Ensure that this dish machine is not used until this chemical is obtained and is properly sanitizing at the label-recommended concentration. 

The Chlorine sanitizing dish machine in the bar area is observed to have an “Out of Order” sign on it and a part has been ordered for it. The facility has been bringing the bar dishes to the kitchen to be cleaned. 

A follow up is scheduled on 12/8/2025 to ensure that the kitchen dish machine has been repaired and is properly sanitizing. A spot check will be conducted when the bar dish machine has been repaired to ensure that it is properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
There were multiple food items in the walk-in cooler that were observed to be held past the 7 days allotted for date-marking: 

1. Red onions with a date of 11/20. All pickled items made in-house should be discarded after 7 days. 
2. Two containers of cooked and cooled cauliflower with a date of 11/22. 
3. A pan of mashed potatoes with a date of 11/26. 

CORRECTED- All items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are date-marked, with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of day 7.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair: 

1. There is a cracked tile that is pooling water next to the drain in the dish area. 
2. The coving behind the dish machine has caulking that is in disrepair. Ensure that this is re-sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
3. The Nudo board behind the warmers in the doorway to the dish area is observed to be coming away from the wall. Ensure that this is re-sealed.
4. THIRD REPEAT- The coving/wall across from the dish machine in the kitchen is in disrepair. 
5. SECOND REPEAT- The cabinet under the coffee machine in the coffee bar has tape on it as a repair mechanism. An operator stated that they plan on replacing the cabinets. Ensure that these cabinets are repaired. 
6. SECOND REPEAT- The dish area caulking is in a state of disrepair and is in need of being re-sealed. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The floor under the preparation area in the banquet area of the kitchen is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. Ensure that this is being regularly cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soil residues. Physical facilities should be cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was an egg shell observed in the kitchen’s hand-sink. Discussed with person-in-charge (PIC) and the shell was discarded. Ensure that hand-sinks are only used for handwashing purposes and never food prep or as a dump sink.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were several sliced deli meats that lacked date marking inside of the kitchen prep cooler. Discussed proper date marking with the PIC and date marking labels were provided to the food items. Ensure that all sliced deli meats are date marked if being held in house longer than 24 hours. Be sure to discard if seven days are exceeded.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: There was a spray bottle of a cleaning chemical stored on the bottom shelf of the prep table. There was also single service items and equipment used for cooking stored on the shelf. Discussed with PIC and the bottle was moved to the storage area where other hazardous chemicals are stored. Ensure that hazardous chemicals are never stored with food or items that will come in contact with food to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: There were several utensils and dishes with dried food debris in a container on a storage rack (in the kitchen area). Discussed and shown to PIC. Be sure to clean dishes at a frequency to preclude debris accumulation during storage.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: Observed no hot water to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, hot water was being serviced during inspection. Inspector will spot check facility within the following days to confirm hot water is available. Ensure facility has hot water available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed several dented cans on the shelves. The cans were removed from service and the PIC was educated. Ensure that food packages are in good condition to protect the integrity of the food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) The debris underneath the glass portion behind the Jolly Rancher frozen beverage machine nozzles.

(2) The debris behind the slushy machine nozzles.

(3) The dust and other debris on the shelves inside the walk-in drink cooler. 

(4) The debris behind the cappuccino machine nozzles. 

(5) The surface above the coffee pot. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris, dust, and other residues. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a leak at the triple sink faucet. Ensure that the leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there is not a covered waste receptacle in the female toilet room for sanitary napkins. Ensure that the female toilet room has a covered waste receptacle by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION:
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions.  The facility is observed to have soiled floors and shelving due to a previous mouse infestation. Originally noted in the 2023 inspection, evidence of current presence was observed throughout the facility. During today’s inspection, there is observed mouse droppings throughout the entire back storage area (from around the soda service station to the opposite alcohol and office space). There are not any large numbers. And droppings appear to be old. There was also an old dead mouse under the soda boxes. This is a cleaning issue. Cleaning will need to be extensive and thorough. Remove all the bulk boxes of sundries from the back storage space and clean the floor. SCDPH will allow thirty days for compliance to allow for detail cleaning. As part of cleaning, see that the walls around the soda syrup storage shelf are cleaned and painted as required. Soda splash is observed around the wall behind the syrup boxes and on the ceiling above the shelf. 
Finally, the floor drain of the hand sink behind the soda service station is observed soiled with mold growth.
Clean the aforementioned areas paying particular attention to the soda syrup storage area. 

 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. The back room is observed to have damage to several ceiling tiles directly over the soda syrup box shelf. The ceiling tiles should be replaced and best practice would be to use a vinyl coated tile - to allow for proper cleaning. In addition to the cleaning to address the previous pest problem (see other 55 violation) maintenance should be conducted to insure surfaces are properly sealed to prevent entrance of pests. There are observed several holes in walls around the alcohol storage across from the office space and around the soda syrup boxes. As you clean, seal any observed holes with steel wool. The use of spray foam is allowed, but mice will chew through this material. 
Furthermore, several of the acoustic tiles in the back storage room are observed water stained from water damage. Replace the ceiling tiles with ones that are in good repair.

The wall holding the shelving with mouse droppings is observed to have mold and mildew damage. Discussed using a Kilz or similar product to seal the wall to prevent further growth. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed several dented cans in the dry storage area. The dented cans were removed from service and the PIC was educated. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of the food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets were testing at 0-452 ppm (Lactic Acid; Sink and Surface Cleaner). The sanitizer buckets were remade testing at 704 ppm (Lactic Acid) during the inspection. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 152-153F with a maximum registering thermometer. The facility will be washing and rinsing items inside the dish machine and sanitizing in the tripe sink until the dish machine is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 12/15/2025 to check that the dish machine is properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed single-use utensils stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. During the inspection the utensils were moved into an upright container with the handles sticking outwards to limit students touching the food contact portions. Ensure the utensils are always stored to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed the internal surface of the coffee machine to be soiled. PIC was made aware. A staff member was instructed to clean the internal surface of the coffee machine. Inspector later reexamine the area mentioned and it was cleaned to sight of touch. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the internal surface of the coffee machine are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.


Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

citation_text:

 Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Inspector observed a build up of ice at the door of the meat walk-in freezer that is adjoining the meat walk-in cooler in the basement. PIC was made aware. Ensure that the ice accumulation is cleaned up providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge including section 1-17).

The PIC was not showing active managerial control in relation to the cold holding situation related to the walk in cooler (refer to line item number 22). The PIC was aware of an issue and maintained use of a failing cold holding unit, even allowing for new product to be put into the cooler after admitting to knowing that it was not functioning correctly. The managerial staff is also having ongoing issues with CFPM certificates. One was available at the end of today’s inspection, but was not here when the inspection began. Having all managerial staff with this certification would ensure that food safety concerns are understood at all times. Education was conducted and possible procedures for future situations were discussed with the PIC during this inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available in the facility. Mrs. McLemore arrived during this inspection to correct. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts/all times that foods are being handled or prepared. She stated that the CFPM that should have been there was having car trouble and she was needed to acquire stock from another store due to discarding the items from the walk in cooler (refer to line item number 22).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

Multiple employees were observed throughout the inspection to wash their hands and then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff and monitor hand washing moving forward in order to promote safe practices.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Inside of the ice machine is a piece hanging down behind the defector shield. Today it is observed with possible rust residue. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain this equipment clean moving forward. The items was cleaned during this inspection to correct.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Multiple TCS items in the walk in cooler are observed with internal temperatures between 48F-50F. The PIC was told and stated that they knew the cooler was having issues at 9 am this morning. They put in a work order at that time. Several of the TCS foods were prepared today, but were placed into the cooler to long ago (per the PIC) for them to be safe at these temperatures. The foods are all observed with internal temperatures within the range of the coolers ambient temperature. All of these items were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Items discarded include sliced tomatoes (7 quarter pans), mayonnaise (out of the package and portioned) (5 quarter pans), diced/cooked chicken (3 quarter pans), maple honey butter (labeled as refrigerate after thawing) (three containers), chopped lettuce (one large tub, six cases), 16 premade salads and multiple cheeses. Two containers of beef were placed into the cooler approximately an hour prior to observation. These were allowed to be moved to a correctly functioning cooler and saved. Ensure that all TCS foods are maintained at effective temperatures at all times in the facility.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

Multiple items in the walk in the walk in cooler appear to be incorrectly date marked. Per the employee the items (chopped lettuce, sliced tomatoes and sliced onions) were all prepared this morning. These items are all showing preparation dates ranging over the past three days. The PIC was shown and instructed to review and re-educate use of the label maker for future items. These items were discarded due to temperature abuse during this inspection (refer to line item #22).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The walk in cooler in the facility is not effectively holding foods at safe temperatures (refer to line item number 22). The maintenance tech arrived during this inspection to fix it. Per him, stop leak was added to the system and then more Freon was added. By the end of the inspection the cooler is observed at effective cold holding temperatures. Ensure that all coolers are maintained in effective states at all times.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.

5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The three part sink in the dish area is observed with a leak coming from the faucet. The PIC was shown and stated that a work order had already been put in and the maintenance person was scheduled to be at the facility today. He arrived and ordered a part for overnight delivery. This is confirmed via messages noted on the closing manager’s phone with the district manager. A follow up is being set for Friday to ensure that the repair is completed.

The PIC was shown and directed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

The walk in freezer off of the walk in cooler is observed with a thick accumulation of ice on a majority of the floor as well as major frost accumulation throughout the freezer. The PIC was instructed to remove the ice/frost and maintain the floor clean moving forward. Ensure that the facilities are maintained clean at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall behind where the instapot is being stored has a soft surface. Walls in areas where food prep occurs shall be smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. Ensure to replace wall surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed dust strings hanging from the ceiling above the cook-line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that dust strings are cleaned from the ceiling. They present a cross-contamination hazard, as they could easily be dislodged from the ceiling and contact food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the servers’ station to be encrusted with soils. Discussed with PIC, and PIC had them cleaned immediately. Ensure these nozzles are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

comment: Inspector observed a build-up of ice in both of the walk-in freezers. The south outside freezer had build-up on food boxes and strip curtains. The north outside freezer has built-up ice on the walls and strip curtains. Both machines appear to have problems sealing around the doors. Along with this, ice was observed below and behind the fans in the coolers. Ensure these machines are serviced to prevent ice build-up, as ice is not seen as a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector observed the CFPM to not have an allergen certification. Ensure all CFPMs have valid allergen certifications. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: A sanitizer bucket wasn’t available during food preparation in the popcorn area. Discussed with person in charge (PIC) that a sanitizer solution must be available if food prep is occurring. The facility only prepares popcorn in this particular area of the store. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the food preparation line to contain no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- sanitizer was remade to a concentration of 150 ppm quaternary ammonia. The person in charge (PIC) showed the Qdoba safety and sanitation manual to the inspector, which stated that quaternary ammonia sanitizers should be made to contain 150-400 ppm. The PIC emailed this manual to their inspector, as well as the inspector on site today. Inspectors will confirm if this is acceptable with supervisors, and will continue communication with the facility.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: It was observed that no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM/CFM) was on site during today’s inspection. The only employee present had a Food Handler’s card. All Class II facilities must have a CFM present during all times at which food is handled or prepared. The presence of a CFM helps to decrease the risk of food-borne illness by overseeing safe food handling practices, and ensuring temperatures of all Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items are within their required range (below 41F or above 135F) to prevent the growth of harmful pathogens.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The inspector observed a gap between the floor and wall between the soda machine and standing drink cooler. This gap may allow for the collection of food and other debris. Debris may attract pests. Reseal coving by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple live nymphs along the wall of the back storage room, between the soda boxes and standing coolers. Multiple dead and live roaches (in various sages of development) were observed on glue traps today. A dead roach was also observed directly beneath the soda lid holders (in an area the inspector noted was in need of cleaning during the last inspection).
Glue traps have either NOT been date marked, or not REPLACED since the last follow up inspection. Today is the third follow up inspection since 09/15 original inspection, and the proliferation of roaches has gotten worse. 
Roach sightings are being logged in a blue Steritech binder, however only two sightings have been noted since the last follow up. The facility has increased the frequency at which pest control services the establishment to biweekly, however the presence of nymphs indicates that the adults are breeding.
Facility must coordinate cleaning efforts with maintenance (to fill and seal holes/ gaps which may be harboring roaches), as well as their pest control operator to ensure the elimination and of harborage conditions, and to stop the proliferation of roaches.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed some of the under counter cabinets at the concession stand to contain large holes between the cabinets, which may be prime conditions for pest harborage. Coordinate with maintenance to ensure these holes are filled. All nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Inspector will check that these physical facilities have been sealed on 12/17.
citation_text: 4-402.11(A) Fixed Equipment, Spacing or Sealing. (A) EQUIPMENT that is fixed because it is not EASILY MOVABLE shall be installed so that it is: (1) Spaced to allow access for cleaning along the sides, behind, and above the EQUIPMENT; (2) Spaced from adjoining EQUIPMENT, walls, and ceilings a distance of not more than 1 millimeter or one thirty-second inch; or (3) SEALED to adjoining EQUIPMENT or walls, if the EQUIPMENT is exposed to spillage or seepage. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed food debris throughout the facility, including significant films of grease in some under counter cabinets. There is signifcant soiling of the cabinets directly underneath the soda lid holders on the back side of the service counter. 
Food contact and nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. The facility requires increased managerial oversight to ensure conditions for pest harborage (see violation #38) are eliminated. Managers that open the facility must communicate with managers that close the facility, and coordinate cleaning schedules. Establish cleaning schedules and encourage cleaning during lapses between customers. Inspector will return on 12/08/25 to check cleaning.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Multiple physical facilities are observed to contain a significant accumulation of food and other soil debris:
1) The floor and drainage pipe next to the soda boxes contain liquid pooling, and a significant amount of soil accumulation.
2) The floor and wall on the East wall behind the soda boxes in the food storage room.
3) Behind the water heater.
 Ensure floors and walls are cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil accumulation. Inspector will return on 12/08 to checking cleaning.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Inspector observed the facility to be repackaging and selling ice in cups. Facility is not permitted to handle food. Ensure this practice is ceased or that the permit is upgraded to a medium risk. Inspector will return 12/04/2025 to re-inspect permit-level activities.
citation_text: 2-103.11(Q) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (Q) Written procedures and plans, where specified by this Code and as developed by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, are maintained and implemented as required.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed the facility to have no dedicated hand sink. There is a sink that is used as a dump sink and for hands. Ensure that the facility either installs a new sink for hand washing, or uses this sink only for hand washing. Inspector will return 12/04/2025 to re-inspect the hand sink.
citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Facility does not have a dedicated hand sink where ice is packaged. Follow-up on 12/04/2025
citation_text: 5-204.11 Handwashing Sinks. A HANDWASHING SINK shall be located: (A) To allow convenient use by EMPLOYEES in FOOD preparation, FOOD dispensing, and WAREWASHING areas; and (B) In, or immediately adjacent to, toilet rooms.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: Facility is repackaging ice into cups to be sold. Cups are unlabeled, and come from a source not meant to be repackaged and sold. Ensure that this practice stops. Inspector will return 12/04/2025 to re-inspect ice packaging process.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

citation_text: 7-301.11 Separation. POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored and displayed for retail sale so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were several different time/temperature control (TCS) foods stored in the standing coolers and the pizza cooler that lacked proper date marking. These TCS foods include sliced deli meats, soft cheeses, tomato sauces, etc. Discussed the need of date marking for TCS foods held in house longer than 24 hours. Ensure that TCS foods that will be cold held longer than 24 hours are date marked with the date that it is opened or prepared. Be sure to discard if not used within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. Ensure that single service items are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Floors and walls throughout the facility is in need of deep cleaning. Observed food debris along the back wall behind where pizza dough is prepped and also underneath pieces of equipment and prep tables. Discussed with PIC. When time permits, be sure to pull pieces of equipment from walls to wipe down floors and walls.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
