citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the steam table in the back corner of the kitchen to be holding food at 125F. Discussed with. PIC, and figured out that the hot-holding unit was turned down too low. Food was reheated for holding at 10AM according to kitchen staff, and service is over at 2pm. In this instance, discard the food after service. Food is allowed to be held at ambient temp for up to 4 hours before being discarded. Corrected: PIC turned the hot holding on a warmer setting, inspector probed at 135F before leaving. Ensure hot holding units are kept at 135F or above and checked regularly.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared and available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The person in charge (PIC) at today’s inspection had a Certified Food Protection Manager Certificate (CFPM) which had expired in February 2025. The CFPM exam must be retaken every 5 years. Ensure all CFPM certificates are maintained up to date, and available by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The PIC could not produce Employee Health Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. All employees in facilities that handle food must read and sign an Employee Health Reporting Agreement within 30 days of hire. Inspector provided blank agreement for the PIC to make copies. Ensure agreements are signed by staff to be made available for inspection by 12/01/25.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed the grate of the pizza oven to contain a heavy accumulation of grease and food debris. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the grate to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure all equipment is cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may contaminate ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-602.12 Cooking and Baking Equipment. (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. (B) The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed a bottle containing red liquid to bear no label. CORRECTED- the liquid was identified as quaternary ammonia sanitizer, and the bottle was labeled accordingly. Ensure all containers holding chemicals are labeled once removed from their original container.
citation_text: 7-101.11 Identifying Information, Prominence. Containers of POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS and PERSONAL CARE ITEMS shall bear a legible manufacturer's label. [Pf]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a large hole on top of the beer cooler. This hole may allow for the accumulation of soil debris. Fill hole so that nonfood contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility’s Chlorine bleach test strips were soiled and unable to be used to test sanitizer concentration. The facility also has quaternary ammonia to sanitize food contact surfaces, but no corresponding test strips. CORRECTED- quat test strips were acquired. Ensure the facility always has test strips available that correspond with the sanitizer being used for food contact surfaces at the facility to ensure proper sanitizing concentrations are being reached according to the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soil debris on the lid of the chest freezer. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris- which may contaminate RTE foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the ice machine interior has an accumulation of debris. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 12/1/2025 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the women’s restroom does not have a covered waste receptacle for sanitary napkins. Ensure that the women’s restroom has a covered waste receptacle by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The person in charge (PIC) at today’s inspection was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). Medium risk establishments must have a CFPM present in the building during all times during which food is being handled to oversee proper food handling and safe temperatures. Inspector provided information on ANSI-approved courses to obtain a CFPM certificate. Ensure a CFPM is always available during times of food handling.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed raw ground pork stored above mandarin oranges in the standing cooler during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- oranges were moved above the raw meat. Inspector provided a storage order infographic to the PIC. Ensure all ready to eat (RTE) foods are stored above raw foods to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC stated that the other PIC is currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: One of the PICs was observed to prepare spring rolls using their bare hands and the PIC stated that the spring rolls will not be cooked before being served. CORRECTED- The spring rolls that were prepared were discarded and the PIC was educated that ready-to-eat foods should not be handled with bare hands. Bare hand contact with ready-to-eat foods can lead to foodborne illness. Ready-to-eat foods should be handled with utensils or gloved hands (with the hands being washed prior to gloves being donned.)
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a lemon in the handwashing sink and the ice machine was observed to be draining into this handwashing sink as well. The lemon was removed and this was discussed with the PIC. Handwashing sinks should ONLY be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. A follow up is scheduled for 12/5/2025 to ensure that the ice machine is draining into another sink or bucket.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The facility has par-cooked chicken in a foil pan that was observed to not be in cold or hot holding. The PIC stated that they make more of the chicken as they run out and they cook it before serving. The PIC stated that they do not always go through it within the four hours that is allotted under Time as Control. This was discussed with the PIC, as this should either be hot held, cold held, or placed under Time as Control. CORRECTED- The chicken had only been there since 12pm, when the facility opened, and was placed under Time as Control. The operator stated that they will begin putting it in the cooler and cold holding it. A spot check will be conducted on 12/5/2025 to ensure that the chicken is being cold held after it is cooked.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There were containers of sauces that were cooked and then cooled that did not have date-marking on them. CORRECTED- The items were date-marked during the inspection. All Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods that are opened or prepared in an establishment should be date-marked with day 1 being the date of opening and day 7 being the date the item is discarded. A spot check will be conducted on 12/5/2025 to ensure that TCS items that are held for over 24 hours are being date-marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: The facility uses a container of water to hold their rice-scoop in between uses. The PIC stated that they change the rice-scoop water a few times throughout the day, but there was no written indication or standard operating procedure of when this rice-scoop water is changed. Ensure that there is a written indication of when items that are under Time as Control were made to make sure they are being discarded of after 4 hours. A follow up is scheduled for 12/5/2025 to ensure that the time is being recorded for the rice-scoop water.
citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There are dishes and single-service containers throughout the kitchen that have their food-contact surfaces exposed to contamination. This was discussed with the PICs. Ensure that these items are inverted to protect the food-contact surfaces from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was not a prepared sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen for sanitizing food-contact surfaces. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. The PICs were educated that there should always be a sanitizer bucket available in the kitchen, before food preparation or cooking even begins. It is essential to have a prepared sanitizer bucket that is at a label-recommended concentration to clean food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation
Upon arrival, PIC informed inspectors that the dish machine was also programmed for chemical sanitization, but the machine tested 0ppm with a chlorine test strip twice. The dish machine was observed with a final rinse temperature of 150.4F with the dish puck. The inspectors informed the PIC that the sanitizer bucket was empty and therefore not supplying the machine with chlorine for sanitization. The final rinse temperature observed is also insufficient to achieve sanitation. The chemical bucket was replaced during the inspection, but the machine failed to pull the sanitizer through the system via the pump. A follow-up is scheduled for 11/21/2025 to ensure Ecolab services and repairs the dish machine.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the lactic acid sanitizer dispenser in the dish room to measure 0ppm lactic acid with a test strip. The dispenser’s sanitizer source jug was observed to be nearly empty. If the tubing is not long enough, the sanitizer dispenser can fail before the container is fully emptied. Ensure staff are testing the dispensed sanitizer frequently and monitoring the fill level on the chemical jug. The PIC was informed of the issue and the jug was replaced, measuring 700ppm lactic acid.
citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
Inspectors observed the plumbing under the “wash” basin of the triple sink to have a significant leak. The other two basins had a failure in the stopper system that prevented them from holding water. The inspectors recommended purchasing additional drain stoppers as a temporary fix until the plumbing can be repaired. Temporary ware-washing will include washing and rinsing in the dish machine, and a final sanitizing step in the left two sink basins. 

A follow-up will be conducted on 11/21/2025 to ensure the plumbing has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw chicken and beef stored above cooked potatoes in the corner prep cooler. The PIC was informed and the items were rearranged. Ensure staff are storing raw meat below ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility when the inspector arrived. During the inspection a CFPM arrived at the facility. The inspector suggests more employees getting CFPM certificates. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of food preparation and handling.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee used their bare hands to operate the faucets after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucets to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPART VIOLATION: Observed the hand washing sink was blocked with a sanitizer bucket when the inspector arrived at the facility. The bucket was removed and the employee was educated. Ensure that the hand washing sink is maintained accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bottom right gasket of the freezer is in a state of disrepair partially unattached. The gasket must be either repaired or replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the gasket is fixed by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the employee working does not have a food handler certificate. Ensure that all employees who do not have CFPM certificates complete the food handler training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following require repairs:

(1) The mop sink must be sealed to the wall. 

(2) The bathroom ceiling and door trim must be sealed to the wall (eliminate the large gaps). 

Ensure that the above referenced are sealed to the wall to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of debris on the baffles of the ice machine. The PIC stated that the ice machine baffles were cleaned recently, however there is debris on the sides indicating that these spots were missed in the last cleaning. The inspector will follow-up on 12/1/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The facility could not produce any food manager certificates. The only Certified Food Manager on file wasn’t available during the visit. PIC mentioned that the certificates were locked in the office room and the employees did not have a key to access the documents at the time of the inspection. Ensure that there is always a certified food protection manager present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: The employee who normally handles food was observed processing transactions at the register and engaging in food prep without washing hands. Discussed with PIC the need to wash hands before handling food since there was an interruption of tasks. Ensure that employees wash hands in between changing tasks to avoid cross contaminating food.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: The PIC mentioned that employees normally wash hands in the ware-washing sink where dishes are cleaned. Discussed with PIC that handwashing should only occur in the handwashing sink. The triple sink shall only be used for cleaning dishes. Ensure that hands are washed in the designated hand sink only.
citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: The facility is serving yogurt dipped grapes. When asked the source of the grapes, the PIC wasn’t aware of where the grapes are being made. Discussed that food sold for public consumption must be made in an approved permitted kitchen. The facility was instructed to not serve the grapes to the public. Will follow-up on November 24, 2025 to gather more information about the food source.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There are several missing ceiling tiles in the back storage area where single service items, bottled drinks, and the ice machine are stored. PIC was able to replace one ceiling tile, however, the facility is still expected to replace the remaining missing tiles. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a certified food protection manager present at the start of the inspection. A CFPM arrived shortly afterwards. Discussed the need of having at least two employees who are manager certified. The person in charge mentioned that another employee is in the process of getting food manager certified. Ensure that there is always a CFPM available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
There were a few items inside of the grab & go cooler that lack proper labeling. These items included protein products made in house. Discussed with PIC the need to label each food items with the common food name, any possible allergens, and date marking (if applicable). Ensure that food items include proper labeling. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed two sani buckets at the facility to be below acceptable levels of sanitizer. The sanitizer near the order window measured 0PPM and the sanitizer in the kitchen measured 100PPM of Quaternary Ammonium sanitizer. Facility has test strips, ensure they are used to regularly check sanitizer concentration. Sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at 300-400 PPM of quat. Ensure sanitizers are refreshed regularly enough to keep them at the right concentration. PIC refilled the sanitizers from the dispenser.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the can opener to have a build-up of soils on the blade. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the blade of the can opener is cleaned and sanitized regularly enough to keep it clean. Inspector will return 12/01/2025 to re-inspect the can opener blade for cleanliness.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed all chef’s coolers (drawer coolers) to be holding chicken, cheese, and beef at 44-45F (probed). There were 8 trays in total that were moved to the standing cooler at the facility. The facility was able to move them to a standing cooler to cool them back to acceptable temperature ranges; food at 45F or below does not need to be discarded if it can be cooled back to 41F. Ensure that no food is stored in these coolers until they can be repaired.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed two drawer coolers to be holding foods at 44-45F. See violation 22 for foods. Ensure that the machines are serviced so that they holds foods at 41F or below. Inspector will return 12/1/2025 to re-inspect coolers’ cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the back-of-house area where dry storage is located to be in need of cleaning. The ice machine exterior, and floor around and behind the ice machine have accumulated soils. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that surfaces in this area are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed multiple soup containers being reused as scoops in ready to eat (RTE) foods (including but not limited to a sushi vinegar marinade and sugar). CORRECTED- the PIC removed the soup containers and replaced them with scoops with handles. Any utensils used with RTE foods must have a food contact surface as well as a hand contact surface to prevent bare hand contamination of food. 
* This violation was previously noted as violation #43 during the last routine inspection, and has since been moved to #9.*
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed 2 sponges and 1 steel wool in the basin of the hand washing sink near the West sushi prep station. The person in charge (PIC) indicated that the sponges are at the sink to clean the sink. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the sponges and steel wool to the dish area. If sponges are used to clean the sink they should ONLY be brought over for that purpose and then immediately returned to the dish area. All hand washing sinks should be used for hand washing only. Using hand washing sinks for other purposes may deter hand washing for food handlers.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed improper storage order in the facility’s walk in cooler. Shrimp was stored over vegetables- including but not limited to jalapeños. CORRECTED- the PIC rearranged ready to eat (RTE) food items to be stored over animal proteins. Inspector gave PIC storage order handouts in English, Spanish, and Mandarin to be hung around the facility. Ensure RTE food items are always stored above animal proteins, and animal proteins are stored by increasing internal cooking temperatures (items with the highest internal cooking temperatures should be stored at the bottom) to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The facility’s dish machine was run 3 separate times and each time was observed to have a sanitizing concentration of 0 ppm. The PIC called their service provider to have the machine serviced. CORRECTED- While the inspector was writing the report the service provider was able to examine the machine and verify that the dish machine was reaching the appropriate sanitizing concentration (200 ppm). Facility should use test strips at least once a day to ensure that the dish machine is reaching proper sanitizing concentrations.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed no measurable concentration of sanitizer at the rotary bar sanitation bucket. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bucket was remade to have a concentration of 200 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made and checked (with the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to contain the correct concentration of sanitizer as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed items in the dessert cooler to be marked with times of preparation which had not passed yet (12:30pm time observed at 11:20am). The PIC indicated that the items were prepared at that time the day before. CORRECTED- the desserts were also labeled with the day they were prepared. Ensure all Time and Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) items being held for more than one day are marked with the day of preparation or thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple incidents of wet sanitizing cloths being stored on the counters of food preparation areas. CORRECTED- the wet cloths were moved to a sanitizer bucket. Ensure sanitizing cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between use to prevent the growth and harborage of microorganisms.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).[C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a leak from base of the faucet at the hand washing sink behind the West sushi station. CORRECTED-The sink was removed from the wall to tighten the fitting during the inspection. Ensure that all plumbing systems at the facility are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the time of this inspection there is not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts. A CFPM arrived during this inspection to correct the immediate concern. Hand outs were given for local CFPM courses as well as the CFPM courses provided by SCDPH in the coming year.

4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can open is observed soiled with dried on debris. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain clean moving forward. The item was moved to dish for cleaning during this inspection to correct.

comment: Observed the bar ice scoops stored with the handles touching the ice. The PIC was educated and the ice scoops were moved outside of the bins during the inspection. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to prevent bare hand contact with the food.
