title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is an accumulation of debris inside the ice machine. The ice machine must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 12/1/2025 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on counters at the bar. The wiping cloths were moved into the sanitizer portion of the triple sink during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dust on the metal wire shelving in the kitchen (i.e., above the prep cooler, between the oven and freezer, and between the triple sink and kitchen entrance door). Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the table in the back of the kitchen (near the ice machine) holding various coffee/tea machines and the spray nozzle sink is not properly sealed to the wall. The caulking is deteriorating in quality and pulled away from the wall. Since the table is not easily removable from the wall the current caulking must be removed and the table re-caulked to the wall. Ensure that the table is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels at the handwashing sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand-sinks are supplied with paper towels to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A banana stored in the cooler near the tripe sink was observed in a decaying condition. The banana had turned completely black, losing its natural yellow color. Shown to PIC and the banana was discarded. Ensure that food intended for public consumption is always in good condition.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The facility was observed using a plastic grocery bag to store cut sweet potatoes in a prep cooler. Although the sweet potatoes a fried before being served, the practice of storing food items in plastic grocery bags isn’t ideal. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned and sanitized. The potatoes were transferred to an appropriate container to correct the violation. Ensure that foods are stored in food grade products and never in plastic bags.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of both fryers were observed with a significant amount of dried grease debris. PIC mentioned that the facility cleans the baffles manually in the triple sink. Discussed contacting an outside company to service the duct work of the overhead hood system. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed kitchen line ice bath to be cold holding chicken at 47F. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper ice baths and water was added to the ice. Inspector observed chicken to later be at 41F. Ensure all ice baths are properly cold holding any TCS food at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: (Repeatx2) Observed the top of the back dish machine to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris and accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was relocated to the strainer portion of bucket. Ensure mops after use are placed in a position that allows them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: The wiping cloth that was being used to wipe food-contact surfaces was observed to be stored on the counter. This was discussed with the PIC and a bucket was recommended, as they often use the sanitizer from the Schnuck’s deli’s triple sink. CORRECTED- The PIC filled a sanitizer bucket and was educated that the wiping cloth should be stored in chemical sanitizer in between uses to prevent bacteria growth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment:
Facility has several repeat violations this inspection. This demonstrates that staff has not been adequately informed of safe food handling practices. Along with this, no manager was present upon inspection. Ensure that repeat violations are corrected and that staff are educated on proper food handling techniques. See repeat violations. Inspector will return 11/26/2025 to re-inspect active managerial control.

2-101.11(A) Assignment. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, the PERMIT HOLDER shall be the PERSON IN CHARGE or shall designate a PERSON IN CHARGE and shall ensure that a PERSON IN CHARGE is present at the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-103.11(Q) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (Q) Written procedures and plans, where specified by this Code and as developed by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, are maintained and implemented as required.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No certified food protection manager was at facility upon inspector arrival. Ensure that a CFPM is working any time that food is being prepared.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed beef being stored over cut bell peppers in a prep cooler in the kitchen. Ensure that food is stored in the correct order to prevent contamination. From top to bottom, the correct order is fish, pork and beef, eggs, then poultry (chicken and turkey).  COS PIC switched the foods so that the raw beef was stored below the peppers.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
(REPEAT x3) Inspector observed tortillas and cheese being stored in a grocery bag on cook line. There was also meat being stored in a grocery bag in the walk-in cooler. Use of grocery bags as a food-storage device has increased since previous inspections. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that foods are stored in food-grade containers at all times. Inspector will return 11/26/2025 to re-inspect food storage.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed the packed salsa in the salsa cooler to not be date marked. Ensure that prepared foods are date marked within 24 hours of preparation and kept for no longer than 7 days. Inspector will return 11/26 to re-inspect date marking practices.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed several dead cockroaches at the bar as well as in storage areas in the back. Along with this, inspector found a live cockroach at the bar hiding under the margarita syrups. Ensure that pest control comes regularly. During the previous spot checks, inspector was shown multiple invoices for Bacon pest control, however they could not be found today. Ensure that pest control comes routinely to eliminate the pest presence. Inspector will return 11/26/2025 to re-inspect for pest presence.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed several areas in need of cleaning or repair in the facility. 
-The first area is the wall behind the soda syrups. The wall has a large opening. Ensure that this opening is sealed to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. It is okay to have the hoses run through the wall, but the wall must be closed around the hoses.
-The second area is on the right side of the bar. There is a large hole that opens to an air conditioner unit. This hole must be closed either by adding a door to service the air conditioner, or sealing off the wall.
-The third area is the back room in the kitchen with standing coolers and a chest freezer. Inspector observed this area to be soiled along the edges of the walls. Ensure these areas are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.
-Facility could also benefit from a general cleaning since pest presence has been observed for a while now. 

Ensure all of these violations are corrected by the next routine inspection in 2026.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: The facility does not have a designated person in charge (PIC) to exhibit managerial duties such as ensuring that employees are educated on proper food safety and understanding the risks of unsafe food handling practices. The designated PIC should be available to assist inspectors during routine food inspections.The facility has a history of improperly cold holding TCS foods, incorrect storage order, inadequate equipment for temperature control, lacking records for time controlled items, incorrect handwashing, etc. Based on the various priority and priority foundation violations observed during routine visits, SCPDH will continue to issue follow-ups and monitor the progress of the facility’s understanding of food safety. Ensure that there is always a PIC present during operational hours.
citation_text: 2-101.11(A) Assignment. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, the PERMIT HOLDER shall be the PERSON IN CHARGE or shall designate a PERSON IN CHARGE and shall ensure that a PERSON IN CHARGE is present at the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT during all hours of operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed washing hands without using proper handwashing procedures. The employee was observed rinsing hands without using soap. The activity was ceased and corrected on site. The employee was instructed to wash hands at a different hand-sink using the following steps: rinse hands under warm running water, apply soap and lather hands for at least ten seconds, rinse hands under running water until soap is completely removed, use a single service towel to dry hands, turn faucet handles off with the same paper towel to avoid recontaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a hand washing sink in the kitchen (across from the dish machine) to not have soap. Education was provided to the person in charge regarding stocking all hand washing sinks. CORRECTED- employees were instructed by the PIC to wash hands at one of the other hand washing sinks in the kitchen for the time being. All hand washing must be supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels. Inspector will check that all hand washing sinks are appropriately stocked during 12/01/25 follow up inspection.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple incidents of improper storage order in the facility’s cold holding units:
1) In the walk in cooler there was raw chicken stored over scallops.
2) In a kitchen prep cooler raw chicken was being stored over ready-to-eat (RTE) sauces.
3) In a kitchen prep cooler red meat was being stored above crayfish.
CORRECTED- all items were moved to reflect proper storage order.  Inspectors provided multiple handouts in Mandarin that show correct storage order. Ensure all animal proteins are stored BELOW ready-to-eat (RTE) food items, by increasing internal cooking temperatures- items with higher temperatures should be stored at the bottom of the cooling unit to prevent cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) A significant amount of soil debris was observed on the front and back baffles of the facility’s ice machines. Inspector will return on 12/01/25 to ensure the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized.
2) The can opener in the kitchen. CORRECTED- item was moved to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of RTE foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Several TCS foods stored on the salad station and the floor dessert case were observed with an internal temperature between 45F-57F. These items included but aren't limited to cut lettuce, tomatoes, dairy based dressing, cheeses, pasta salads, cheesecakes, and other desserts. PIC mentioned that TCS foods were placed in the cold table at 11:00am. PIC also mentioned that facility adds water to the table, which then freezes and is expected to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. The facility was instructed to discard TCS items. Foods were discarded voluntarily. Ice was added to the cold table to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: The facility has a Time as Public Health Control (TAC) policy for the sushi area (rolls and sushi rice). There were no markings or system present to indicate the time the food items were put out during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the time each of the foods under TAC were put out were marked with stickers on the buffet glass. Ensure all TAC items are marked to indicate the time of preparation. Foods held out of temperature for over four hours allow for the growth of harmful pathogens, which may cause foodborne illness.
citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The hibachi cold line, the salad cold line, and the floor dessert case aren’t maintaining proper cold holding temperatures for TCS foods. See violations #22. Foods were probed between 45F-57F. Shown to discussed to PIC and TCS foods were discarded. The facility adds ice to the cold-well to help maintain temperatures. The inspectors observed the ice levels to be extremely low. Employees added more ice to the cold well. Ensure that the unit is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed a gap in the bottom right corner of the kitchen back door. Openings between the indoors and outdoors of food establishments may allow for the entry of pests. Replace weather stripping by next routine inspection to close all gaps.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple wet wiping cloths being stored on counters during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- inspector provided education to the PIC. Wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer solution in between uses. Moist sanitizer cloths sitting out may allow for the growth and harborage of harmful microorganisms.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).[C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The heat puck used to measure the dish machine’s surface temperature was observed without batteries. Discussed with PIC. The facility mentioned purchasing batteries to power the device. Ensure that all temperature measuring devices are available and properly functioning to be sure that dishes are getting sanitized correctly.
citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple physical facilities in need of repair:
1) The tiles in front of meat walk in cooler.
2) Two hand washing sinks IN the kitchen (near the dish machine and along the cook-line) contain gaps between the sink and wall.
These spaces may allow for the entry of food debris, and moisture. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There were several missing light bulbs inside of the two-door coolers along the cook-line. The coolers are stored across from the fryers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that lighting is available in all cold holding equipment.
citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the handle of the cookline freezer is in a state of disrepair. A portion of the plastic has broken off exposing the soft, absorbent material underneath. The handle must either be replaced or repaired so that the absorbent material is not exposed. Ensure that the handle is a smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) The interior of the microwave by the kitchen entrance (near the spices/seasonings).

(2) The dust on the metal wire dish drying rack near the dish machine.

(3) The dust and other debris on the walk-in cooler fans. 

(4) The grease build-up on the wall behind the grills on the cookline. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no hand washing signs to be available in employee restrooms within facility. Discussed with PIC, bathrooms were recently renovated and signage was never replaced. Inspector provided facility with the necessary hand washing signage. Ensure all employee bathrooms have hand washing signs available.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Observed no thermometers to be present within reach in coolers throughout facility. Discussed with PIC, thermometers will be purchased and placed within coolers. Ensure a temperature reading device is available within all cold holding equipment.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed the exterior door to have light shining from below the door. Discussed with PIC, the door will serviced and leak will be sealed. Ensure staff is monitoring all outer openings to prevent any possible pest infestation.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed walk in cooler to have an ambient temperature of 45F-47F. Discussed with PIC, walk in cooler will be serviced. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple sandwiches to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, sandwiches were pulled and discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed door to walk in cooler to be in a state of disrepair. Multiple holes were observed and pieces of the door are missing. Discussed with PIC, walk in cooler issues are believed to be separate from door issues, however PIC will look into replacing door. Ensure equipment is working up to the manufactures standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is made and at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There is a gap under the emergency exit door right outside of the receiving area. Ensure all gaps around exterior doors are sealed to prevent the entry of pests. Discussed with PIC.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wood paneling around the walk-in coolers and freezers in the receiving area must be sealed to the units with silicone caulk to allow them to be easily cleaned. Discussed with PIC.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there was an accumulation of debris in the soda gun holders at the bar. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The PIC began the process of washing, rinsing, and sanitizing the holders during the inspection. Ensure that the soda gun holders remain clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) The faucet at the back preparation sink is loose. There has been a repair, but it has been insufficient. Repair the faucet. 

A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. 
Observed a ceiling tile to the left of the hood to be bubbled from possible water damage. Replace the ceiling tile. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up in fish fry station. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine are in need of cleaning. There was debris accumulation on the surfaces that are in direct contact with ice. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The fan guards of the cold room’s cooler were observed heavily accumulated with dust. The fans are above the table where food preparation occurs. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that fan guards are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent possible food contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

comment:
There were several missing floor tiles in the following areas:
- a couple of missing floor tiles around the mop sink
- a missing tile near the back door
- a missing tile near the pieces of laundry equipment 

Ensure that missing floor tiles are replaced to prevent ponding water or debris accumulation in the above mentioned areas.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not any sanitizer available for use while drinks were being served. The PIC setup the triple sink testing at 400 ppm (quat) during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a sanitizing solution available during all hours of operation.

(B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following require cleaning:

(1) The accumulation of debris on the metal shelving in the kitchen by the entrance door (storing the microwave and other equipment/utensils).

(2) The accumulation of debris on the shelves inside of the cooler in the cooler/freezer storage room across from the kitchen entrance (storing various drinks). 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the cove base has peeled off the wall in the following locations:

(1) Behind the bar hand washing sink.

(2) To the left of the cooler in the cooler/freezer storage room across from the entrance kitchen. 

Ensure that the cove base is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed storage order violations within the coolers:

(1) Various raw meats over cooked chicken in the silver double door cooler. 

(2) Raw chicken over shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. 

The above referenced violations were corrected during the inspection. Ensure that raw meats are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods, and raw meats and shell eggs are stored according to internal cooking temperatures.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed several foods (ex. egg rolls, wontons, chicken wings, crab rangoon) in the clear sliding cooler were not covered during storage. The foods were covered with saran wrap during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always covered when not being used.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the counter. The wiping cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival at the facility and throughout the inspection, there was no CFPM present. Discussed with PIC and it was acknowledged that the individual with CFPM certification were out. There was no other person with an active certified food protection manager certification present in the facility. Inspector gave a few flyers containing information about acquiring CFPM certification. Ensure that at least one person with CFPM certification is present at all time during facility operation. [C]
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Inspector observe the two hand sinks with in the facility to be obstructed. The hand sink in the kitchen was observed to be obstructed by the mop bucket. And the hand sink in the serving area was observed to be obstructed by a tray of serviettes and other single service items. PIC was made aware and the various item obstructing the hand sinks mentioned were removed. Ensure that hand sinks within the facility remains accessible at all times for proper handwashing.

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed the following food-contact surfaces to be soiled.
1. The internal surface of the coffee maker was observed with a build up of soil. 
2. Inspector observed the dispenser of the ice cream machine with a build up of soil.
3. An accumulation of soil build up was observed inside the nozzles of the soda machine. 
PIC was made aware. PIC instructed a staff member to commence the cleaning of the above mentioned surfaces. After the mentioned food-contact surfaces were cleaned, inspector inspected them to confirm the soil removal and sanitation. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed a jug of milk in the chest cooler in the serving area not properly date marked. Discussed with PIC. PIC confirm that the milk jug was open the day prior (11/12/2025). PIC instructed a staff member to date mark the milk jug. Education was carried out. Ensure that ready to eat food and TCS food are properly date marked if they are going to be store for more than 24 hours after opening or prep. 

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Inspector observed the screen door at the back exit to not be tightly fitted to the frame. Inspector observed visible light passing through the top of the screen door. PIC was made aware. Ensure that this door is repaired to be tightly fitting to properly seal off the doorway at the back exit in order to discourage the entry of pests.

5-205.15(B) Inspector observed the faucet next to the dish machine to leaking. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. 

System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
citation_text:
5-402.13 Inspector observed the urinal in the men’s bathroom to be leaking and a bowl sitting beneath the piping to catch the dripping wastewater. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. A follow up has been issued. Inspector will return on 11/18/25 to follow up on the repairs. Ensure that this leakage in the wastewater line is repaired accordingly to be in compliance with the Law.

Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility maintenance issues that could impede proper cleaning.
1. An accumulation of grease build up underneath and on the sides of the fryers and grill. Inspector will return on 11/21/25 to follow up on cleaning as this relates to complaint #25-0597.
2. (TWICE REPEAT) Few broken tiles under the fryers in the kitchen area. Inspector also observed broken tiles under the dish machine.
3. The caulking between the counter top on the left of the dish machine and right of the dump sink was observed in disrepair.
4. Inspector observed a build up of soil on the shelving in the walk-in cooler. 
Discussed with PIC, who assured the inspector that the relevant cleaning and repairs will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned areas are cleaned and repaired providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Facility was observed to be out of compliance with food allergen awareness training. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the training will be done. Ensure that facility is compliant with this law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

Inspectors suggest more staff obtain their CFPM to ensure a CFPM is present at ALL TIMES food is being prepared or served.

citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed a significant amount of soil accumulation on the front baffles of the ice machine. Inspector will return in ten days to ensure the ice machine has been emptied, cleaned, and sanitized. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed a gap in the back door along the bottom and left perimeter, allowing light to enter. This gap may serve as a location for pest to enter the facility. Ensure weather stripping is placed to seal the gap by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple single service containers and plates throughout the facility facing upwards. CORRECTED- single service containers and plates were flipped. Ensure single service containers are stored either under a cover or inverted to prevent the contamination of the food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the handle on the double door cooler (nearest the dish machine) to be in disrepair. Ensure all equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspectors observed no sanitizer buckets available in the kitchen at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the PIC made a sanitizer bucket at a concentration of 100 ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizer is available in the kitchen during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces in the facility in need of cleaning:
1) FIRST REPEAT: The fans in the walk in cooler contain a significant amount of dust. 
2) The fans in the double door cooler next to the dish machine contain an accumulation of dust.
3) The handles of the double door cooler next to the dish machine contain a significant amount of food debris.
4) There was a significant amount of grease accumulated in the space between the grill and the grill coolers.
5) A significant amount of food splash was observed on the wall behind the cook line.

Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, grease, and other debris. These debris poses a risk to contaminate ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.[C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed 2 electrical outlets in the kitchen to be lacking plate covers. Both of these were on either side of the steam table; one was underneath the microwave, and the other was to the right of the steam table on the cook-line. Place covers on these outlets to prevent the entry of food or other debris, which may enter the wall. Walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival only one employee has a signed reporting agreement. Per the PIC there are approximately 10 employees currently working at the facility. A pair of blank copies were given to the PIC at today’s inspection and they are instructed to make copies and have all food handlers sign one prior to the follow up in 10 days.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

On arrival, test strips were not available for the sanitizers used in the facility. The PIC was unable to provide any during this inspection and a follow up is being scheduled for 10 days.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

An employee’s phone is observed on the counter next to where food preparation is taking place. Education was conducted. Phones should be stored with employee belongings or in pocket and should not be stored where contamination of foods/ food contact items can be contaminated. The phone was moved to correct.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
citation_text:
2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result. 

An employee was observed to be eating a bowl of soup on the prep line as the inspector arrived. The PIC halted the consumption and discarded the bowl prior to inspector intervention. Ensure that consuming of foods in the facility does not pose a concern of contaminating foods and/or food contact surfaces in the facility.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

Mold is observed on cheese in a container in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and discarded the container during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all foods remain free from spoilage in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw fish is stored over cooked pasta in the prep cooler to the west of the prep line. Education was conducted with the PIC and the containers moved to correct. Ensure that staff knows how to store foods in the coolers to prevent possible cross contamination in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Coffee: Observed an employee turned off the faucets with their bare hands after hand washing. The employee was educated that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Coffee: Observed multiple wet wiping cloths stored on the counter. The employee working was educated and the wiping cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wiping cloths are always held in sanitizing solutions between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION.

Coffee: Observed powders for drinks stored with the scoop handles in direct contact with the powder. The employee was educated that all scoops for ready-to-eat foods must be stored to prevent contamination. The inspector suggests storing the scoops outside of the container. Ensure that scoops are stored with the handles above the top of the powder by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Back area: Observed the shelving in the back area walk-in cooler (connected to the dairy display coolers) have an accumulation of debris on the shelves for the dairy display cases. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Bakery: Observed the walk-in freezer floors have an accumulation of food residue underneath the shelving. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the floors are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to enter the kitchen from the dining room and don gloves without washing their hands. Another employee on the cook line was observed to touch their clothes with their gloved hands without washing hands or changing gloves. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all food employees are washing their hands before donning gloves and are changing their gloves after touching body parts.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed uncut avocado sitting directly on top of raw shelled eggs in the cook line prep cooler. CORRECTED- the avocado was moved into a separate container, and the eggs were moved below. Ensure raw animal proteins are kept separate from ready to eat (RTE) food items.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Multiple food contact items were observed to contain an accumulation of debris during today’s inspection:
1) FIRST REPEAT: A knife on the magnetic strip next to the salad prep station. CORRECTED: The knife was brought to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
2)  FIRST REPEAT: The ice baffle on the North ice machine was observed to contain a slight accumulation of debris. The PIC stated the machine was serviced 3 days ago. CORRECTED- overall cleaning of the ice baffles has improved. PIC stated the machines will be cleaned at an increased frequency.
3) Vegetable chopper contained food debris in the upper portion of the equipment. CORRECTED- equipment was brought to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of RTE foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed 3 sanitizer buckets to be between 0-100 ppm of quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- buckets were remade at a proper concentration (200-400 ppm). Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at frequency to maintain the sanitizer concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple items to be held past their seven day date mark (gyro meat- 10/31, salsa ranch- 10/27, and chipotle BBQ-10/27). CORRECTED- the gyro meat was discarded, and the PIC stated the other sauces had been remade since the sticker date, and the items were re-stickered with the correct dates. Ensure all Time/Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) food items are marked with the date they are prepared, and are used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation or thawing counts as day one. To help ensure this practice takes place, ensure sauces are placed into a new container that has been clean and sanitized.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed insect stun light above single service articles at the entry of the kitchen. Ensure that insect control devices are stored away from single service items to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: There were multiple wiping cloths that were observed to be stored on the counter in between uses, rather than being stored in the sanitizer bucket. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored in the sanitizer bucket in between uses to prevent bacterial growth on the cloths.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The top of the dish machine contains a layer of debris.
2) The shelf liners in the dry storage contained an accumulation of dust.
3) SECOND REPEAT: The wire shelving in the walk in cooler is soiled and rusted. Inspector discussed getting shelf liners, cleaning/ painting, or replacing shelves.
4) SECOND REPEAT: The shelving on the cook line contains an accumulation of dust. 
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation or dust or debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Multiple physical facilities were observed to be in need of repair:
1) THIRD REPEAT: The triple sink and table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The hand sink in the south men’s bathroom was not adhered to the wall. There is also not a large enough gap to easily clean between the sink and the wall. The sink should be sealed to the wall to be smooth and easily cleanable.
Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The PIC stated their Allergen Awareness Certificate had expired, and they were unable to produce Allergen Awareness certificates for any Certified Food Protection Managers (CFM/CFPM). Inspector provided Allergen Awareness literature to the PIC, which included a web address to ANSI-accredited institutes. Ensure all CFMs obtain an Allergen Awareness certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the back of the house tested at 0ppm (quat). There are two different sanitizer dispensers and the PIC used the dispenser that was connected to an almost empty bucket. The bucket was reprepared and tested at 400ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are tested after they are prepared to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(2) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPAregistered label use instructions by providing: (2) A contact time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50 MG/L that has a PH of 10 or less and a temperature of at least 38°C 100°F) or a PH of 8 or less and a temperature of at least 24°C (75°F).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Several different TCS foods such as but not limited to cheeses and meats lacked proper date marking. These items were stored inside of the prep cooler in the pizza room. Discussed with PIC and the date of preparation was added to the food items. Ensure that TCS foods are date marked if being cold held for longer than 24 hours. Items must be discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of a deep cleaning:
- Surfaces inside and outside of the dish machine
- Each basin of the triple sink has dried food debris
- Floors underneath, around, and behind pieces of equipment inside of the dish room

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A)  There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. There was however one person with a food handler who is currently enrolled and in the process of writing the exam. Ensure that there is at least one food protection manager present during operation at all times. 

 Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(C) There was no sanitizer observed in the kitchen and at the bar. PIC was made aware and sani buckets were made. The quaternary ammonium sanitizer buckets tested at 300 ppm. Ensure that there is always sanitizer solution available during food prep and food handling. 


 Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available. Corrected - The PIC borrowed a neighboring trucks sanitizer and created a bucket testing at 200 ppm (quat).
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed there was not a triple sink available (serving drinks with ice and cutting fruit). Corrected - Using the neighboring trucks triple sink for today and inspector will spot check tomorrow.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed milk in walk in cooler to be less than 6 inches above floor. Discussed with PIC, a truck had come in this morning delivering the milk. Milk will be placed in a location that is 6 inches above ground, ensure all food items are kept 6 inches above flooring
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: There are cold sandwiches and wraps that are prepared in house and stored in a grab & go cooler near the front entrance. The products lacked proper allergen labeling. Discussed with PIC the need to list allergens on food products so that consumers are aware of potential allergens.
citation_text: 3-602.12 Other Forms of Information. (A) If required by LAW, CONSUMER warnings shall be provided. (B) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or manufacturers' dating information on FOODS may not be concealed or altered. (C) The PERMIT HOLDER shall notify CONSUMERS by written notification of the presence of MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS as an ingredient in unPACKAGED FOOD items that are served or sold to the CONSUMER.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following areas were observed with debris accumulation:
- Fan guard of the walk in cooler accumulated with dust
- Fan guard above the triple sink where clean dishes are stored (accumulated with dust)

Ensure that fan guards are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent the build up of dust and contaminating food and/or food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The following food contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning:
