1. The top of the dispenser of the Bunn coffee machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue. 
2. The holder for the ice scoop is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue. 

The PIC cleaned both food contact surfaces and was educated on the importance of frequently cleaning them. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were single-service plates and containers by the Mac and cheese and nacho station that were observed to not be inverted. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all single-service articles are inverted or covered to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of sealing (caulking):

1. The back preparation sink in the kitchen of Ginna’s Cafe is observed to have mold growth in the caulking. Ensure that this is re-sealed. 
2. The handwashing sink and triple sink in Fuzzi-Wigs are observed to not be sealed to the wall. Ensure that these are sealed to the wall. 
3. There are holes above and around the handwashing sink and paper towel dispenser in the back of Fuzzi-Wigs. Ensure that these holes are sealed. 

Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. 

Two gallons of milk in the standing cooler in the kitchen are observed partially used and without date marking. Per the PIC they were opened yesterday. Date marking was discussed and dates added to the jugs to correct. Ensure proper date marking is taking place in the facility at all times.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Multiple rags are observed on counters around the kitchen and are moist. Placing them in sanitizer of correct concentration between uses was discussed and they were moved to a freshly prepared bucket to correct. Ensure that the sani rags are stored between uses in sanitizer.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared and ready for use on the food contact surfaces in the facility. Education was conducted and a bucket made to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer is prepared and ready for use at all times that foods and food contact items are being handled in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to change gloves without washing hands. Education was conducted. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times that hand washing is required when handling foods.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

The hand sink next to the three part sink has a small spray that comes out from the faucet when on. The PIC was aware of this and stated that the new area manager was planning on remedying the situation in the near future. Ensure that all plumbing in the facility is maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the mop sink is not sealed to the wall. Ensure that the mop sink is sealed to the wall (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC could not provide any form of verification that the employees were informed of their responsibility to report foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis. Blank copies of the SCDPH reporting agreements were found while searching for documentation and signed by the employees during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Maintain this documentation at the facility moving forward.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Hand washing should be taking place regularly and consistently during food operations, and specifically prior to donning gloves and when changing tasks. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with employees to ensure safe practices are always taking place in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

On arrival, a bowl and utensils are observed in the hand sink, preventing use until they were removed. The items were removed as the inspector was starting the inspection and prior to being addressed by them. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained easily accessible at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives on the magnetic rack are observed with remaining food debris. These items were shown to the PIC and the items move to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are fully cleaned prior to storage.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

On arrival, containers of prepared noddles and rice are observed stored at room temperature. Per the PIC they came out of the coolers approximately an hour ago. They were allowed to move the items back into the cooler for today to correct. The importance of temperature control was emphasized to the PIC once these items are hydrated/cooked. Ensure that all TCS items are stored in temperature control at all times in the facility.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a prepared sanitizer in the facility. When asked the PIC prepared a bucket using bleach (CL) to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer is available at all times that the facility is in operation.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

The hand sink as you enter the facility is observed with a leak coming out of the piping at the bottom. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair and did so during this inspection. Ensure that the plumbing in the facility is maintained in proper repair at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 


Multiple locations in the building used for storage are observed with rodent droppings scattered about. No rodents are observed and no chewing is observed on any packaging at this time. Cleaning was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean up the droppings from the facility. If they notice more droppings appearing after the clean-up they should contact pest control for maintenance. Ensure that the facility is cleaned regularly and thoroughly to prevent accumulation of filth.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed the PIC did not wash hands before putting on gloves to prepare foods. The PIC was reminded that hands must be washed before initiating a task that involves working with food, changing gloves, after contaminating hands (ex. touching your clothes, making a sanitizer bucket, touching your phone), and upon re-entering the kitchen. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order:

(1) Raw beef on the top shelf of the clear double door cooler over various ready-to-eat foods (ex. bread, vegetables, sauces)

(2) Shell eggs on the middle shelf of the Coca-Cola cooler above various ready-to-eat foods (ex. vegetables, sauces).

The storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. Ensure that raw meat and shell eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces were not clean to sight and touch:

(1) The accumulation of debris inside of the ice machine. 

(2) The accumulation of debris on the soda machine nozzles. 

(3) The knife stored in the gap between the prep cooler and shelving (not a cleaned and sanitized surface) - CORRECTED; removed to be washed/rinsed/sanitized during the inspection.

(4) The cutting board stored behind the faucets of the dump sink - CORRECTED; moved onto the shelving during the inspection. 

(5) The soiled plastic containers holding various dry foods - CORRECTED; soiled containers discarded and the food was moved into new containers during the inspection. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. The inspector will follow-up on 11/13/2025 to ensure that the ice machine and soda nozzles have been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the ice scoop at the server area stored with the handle directly touching the ice. The PIC was educated about proper utensil storage. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored with the handle above the top of the food to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived at the facility. The PIC made a sanitizer bucket testing at 150 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. Ensure there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed an accumulation of foods debris on the bottom of several coolers and freezes in the kitchen (i.e., clear double door cooler, silver freezer, large white freezer). Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the bottom of the coolers and freezers are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the facility mopped this morning and the dirty water was still in the mop bucket when the inspector arrived at the facility at 4:30 pm. The PIC dumped the mop water during the inspection. Ensure that mop water is always dumped after use.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: Observed an opened energy drink can stored on the top shelf of the cookline prep cooler. The drink was moved away from the cookline during the inspection. Ensure that drinks are stored in a location where they cannot contaminate food and food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee rinsed hands for about five seconds with soap and used their bare hands to turn off the faucets. The inspector demonstrated the proper hand washing procedure and afterwards the employee correctly washed their hands. After the education the employee and PIC were observed using the proper hand washing procedure throughout the inspection (i.e., rinsing hands under water, scrubbing hands with soap for 10-15 seconds, drying hands with paper towel, using a barrier to turn off the faucets). Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of grease on the hood system causing drips. The facility must clean the hood system more frequently. The inspector will follow-up on 11/13/2025 to ensure that the hood system has been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed various foods throughout the kitchen coolers (prepared/cut produce, cooked chicken, eggs rolls, wontons, rice etc.) were not covered during storage. Ensure that foods are always covered when not being used.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee bring a knife to the triple sink for cleaning and only rinse the utensil under running water. Also observed the same employee only wash and rinse the can opener blade. The inspector used the assistance of a translator on a phone call to explain the wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure, and the triple sink was properly setup during the inspection. The inspector also provided a handout to post above the triple sink for reference. The inspector will follow-up on 11/13/2025 to check on cleaning procedures.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl). The PIC dumped and remade the bucket testing at 100 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the can opener had a large accumulation of debris on the blade. During the inspection the blade was cleaned.  Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the can opener blade remains clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a large container of cooked fried rice stored at room temperature without marking indicating when it must be discarded. The facility uses a time-as-control (TAC) procedure for the cooked rice. The translator on the phone call explained the proper TAC procedures to the PIC during the inspection. The TAC window must be written down to ensure that any leftover rice is discarded after four hours. The inspector will follow-up on 11/13/2025 to check on TAC procedures for the fried rice.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed fortune cookies stored in cardboard boxes on the floor by the cash register. The fortune cookies were moved during the inspection. Ensure that food is always stored at least 6-inches above the ground.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on counters in the kitchen. The wiping cloths were moved into the sanitizer buckets during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizer solutions between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned:

(1) The accumulation of food reside in the bottom gaskets of the clear sliding door cooler.

(2) THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulation of debris inside of the fan above the double door cooler. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIFITH REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the chest freezer in the back dry storage area has a lid that is in a state of extreme disrepair held together with duct tape. Duct tape is not easily cleanable or an appropriate repair. The PIC previously stated they cannot find a replacement lid and will purchase a new freezer when they have enough money. Ensure repairs or replacements by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there is a buildup on grease and other debris on the floor underneath the fryer. The fryer should be moved to facilitate cleaning underneath. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the floor is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no one present at the facility has an allergen awareness certificate. Ensure sufficient employees have allergen awareness certificates by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
citation_text:
3-501.14(A) Cooling. The facility has bulk containers of food in the walk-in cooler that are cooked foods from previous days service. The bulk containers show no signs of proper cooling: covered, large amounts, and no date marking. The facility is unable to properly discuss cooling with SCDPH staff. Today, again, cooling practices were discussed at length. 

COOLING: KEEP ON COUNTER UNTIL PRODUCT IS 135F (USE PROBE THERMOMETER TO MONITOR TEMPERATURE). 
ONCE 135F, START ACTIVELY COOLING: 1) USE AN ICE BATH; 2) LEAVE UNCOVERED; 3) SMALLER PORTIONS/SHALLOW PANS; AND 4) PORTIONS IN THE FREEZER TO KNOCK DOWN HEAT BEFORE MOVING TO COOLER. 

(A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Thawing. Full tub of raw, frozen chicken is observed thawing on a counter in the back room. Discussed thawing under running water, in refrigerator, or as part of cooking. Chicken was placed under running water at the triple sink. SCDPH will continue to monitor thawing practices to insure education is gained.


Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Gloves used properly.
citation_text:
3-304.15(C) Gloves, Use Limitation. The facility is observed donning gloves without a proper hand washing. Also, it appears that gloves are being used to protect hands and not food as the staff are observed touching multiple surfaces with gloved hands without changing. Discussed glove use at length. The facility will have this education included in the ongoing training that will occur over the next few months.  


(C) Slash-resistant gloves may be used with READY-TO-EAT FOOD that will not be subsequently cooked if the slash-resistant gloves have a SMOOTH, durable, and nonabsorbent outer surface; or if the slash-resistant gloves are covered with a SMOOTH, durable, nonabsorbent glove, or a SINGLE-USE glove.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-401.11(A)(1) and (A)(3)-(8) Equipment, Clothes Washers and Dryers, and Storage Cabinets, Contamination Prevention. 

There is immediate concern over the lack of cleaning in this facility and the potential for cross-contamination. As a bare minimum, safe food handling should include a routine cleaning schedule that maintains surfaces clean. A follow-up for the following surfaces will be conducted in two weeks: 

1) Fryer, flat top, steamer, and vertical broiler are observed thickly coated with accumulated grease. This appears to be a potential fire hazard. Clean the cooking surfaces.
2) Throughout the facility, in-use cooking utensils are not being removed every four hours for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. There were observed soiled knives and peelers under the prep cooler from previous days use. Discussed cleaning. This is one of the topics that will be covered in future educationals. Staff appeared to be unaware as to proper wash, rinse, and sanitizing practices. 
3) Preparation cooler interior and exterior is observed soiled with accumulated food debris. 

Clean the aforementioned surfaces paying attention to maintaining these surfaces clean once the initial task is completed.  


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, EQUIPMENT, a cabinet used for the storage of FOOD, or a cabinet that is used to store cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be located: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed used mops to be resting directly on the floor near mop sink. Discussed with PIC, mops will be relocated to a hanging location or to top of mop buckets. Ensure all mops are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: An employee dumped a glass of water and ice into the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC, who educated the employees that handwashing sinks should not be used for dumping. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There is a handwashing sink to the left of the preparation cooler. This cooler is directly next to the handwashing sink and the handwashing sink has no splash guard around it. An employee was observed to wash their hands and water splashed onto the side of the preparation cooler. If the lid is left open on the preparation cooler, the food would be exposed to contamination. A follow up is scheduled 12/4/2025 to ensure that the preparation cooler is either moved away from the handwashing sink or that a splash guard is placed around the handwashing sink to protect the food in the preparation cooler from contamination.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- A shelf in the walk-in cooler was observed to have mold accumulation on it. CORRECTED- An employee cleaned the shelf during the inspection. Ensure that these shelves are being routinely cleaned to prevent mold accumulation. Mold spores travel and have the potential to contaminate food in open-air coolers.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were two containers holding clean dishes that were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in them. CORRECTED- The PIC had an employee clean them during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- There are single-use boats sitting above the fryer and fry containers above the hot holding line with their food contact surfaces exposed to contamination. Discussed proper single service storage. CORRECTED- The PIC inverted these during the contamination. Ensure that all single-service utensils and articles are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: There was a container that is used for hot holding chicken that is observed to have a crack in the bottom of it. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that equipment or utensils that are in disrepair are discarded.
citation_text: 4-502.11(A) Good Repair and Calibration. (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. There is a bucket holding up the thawing shelf in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that this is repaired or replaced to eliminate the need for the bucket to hold it up. 
2. The preparation cooler lid is observed to be coming off. There is a screw missing on the left side of the lid. Ensure that this is repaired. 

Equipment should be maintained in good repair or replaced as needed.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The chub warmer is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall. 
2. FIRST REPEAT- The table that holds the lemonade and soda machine in the drive through area is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- The triple sink is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall, especially to the left of the triple sink and directly above the left side. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The batter station is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall. 
5. FIRST REPEAT- The dish shelves across from the ice machine are rusted. They need to be sealed to prevent contamination to clean dishes. 

Ensure all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. FIRST REPEAT- The floor underneath the fryers. 
2. The ceiling above the fryers is starting to have an accumulation of flour on it. Ensure that this is being regularly cleaned. 
3. There is ice build up in the walk-in freezer on the pipes behind the fans and on the floor underneath shelving. Ensure that this is scraped off and cleaned. 

Physical facilities should be maintained clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food handler training
comment:
SECOND REPEAT- The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: An opened container of barbecue sauce manufactured by Little Caesars was observed stored at room temperature on a storage rack. The label of the bottle stated to refrigerate after opening. Shown to PIC and the sauce was voluntarily discarded. Ensure to properly follow the label instructions on food packaging to ensure safety of foods.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The baking sheet pans stored on the storage rack near the pizza line are starting to chip and are no longer in good condition for baking. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that he would purchase new baking sheets soon. Be sure that food contact surfaces are always in good condition and never chipping to ensure the prevention of contaminating food items. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The storage shelf to the right inside of the walk in cooler was observed with a significant amount of dust and other debris. Shown to PIC. When time permits, pull the shelf from the cooler and power-wash or either wipe with a sanitizer towel. Ensure that pieces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There was a leak observed at the bottom pipe of the hand-sink near the employee bathroom. There is a blue bucket placed under the sink to catch the leak. PIC mentioned that he would contact a technician to service the leaking pipe. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Employees working at the time of the inspection could not show proof of food handler certificates. All employees that handle food and are not food manager certified will need to obtain a food handler certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Inspector observed raw chicken being stored above raw shell eggs in the walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware. PIC removed the raw chicken and stored it appropriately. Ensure that proper storage order is observed at all times to avoid cross contamination of food items. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) The following food contact surfaces were observed with a buildup of soil.
1. The internal dispensing surface of the ice cream machine was observed with an accumulation of soil.
2. The internal surface of the coffee machine was observed with a buildup of soil. 
3. A few cooking utensils (3 soup dippers) were observed rusted. PIC discarded them immediately. A sifter was observed soiled. 

The above mentioned food-contact surfaces were immediately cleaned to sight of touch. PIC discarded the rusted soup dippers as a corrective action. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at all times.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12  Inspector observed an accumulation of soil under the grill and the hot holding unit. Discussed with PIC. PIC assured inspector that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that these areas are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. This action will keep these areas free from the accumulation of food debris and soil. 

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12  Inspector observed an accumulation of grease and food debris under the fryers. PIC was made aware. Ensure that surfaces such as the ones mentioned are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency. 

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

Containers of bleach and cleaning agents are observed on shelves above drinks intended for consumers. The PIC was shown and the location discussed. The shelves were re-arranged during this inspection to correct. Ensure safe storage locations in the facility moving forward.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed a ready to eat (RTE) bagel sitting on the counter at the drive through at the end of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed a need for food grade container or packaging with the PIC. The bagel was removed from service. Ensure all RTE foods are only in contact with sanitized utensils, clean gloved hands, single service containers, or napkins to prevent the contamination of foods.
citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM/ CFPM) was on site at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- CFM arrived about 15 minutes into the inspection. A CFM must be present at all times food is being prepared or served. Inspector provided the PIC a list of ANAB-accredited Certified Food Protection Manager Courses, which includes tests that are available in Spanish. Ensure a CFM is always present during the facility’s hours of operation to oversee proper food handling and temperatures.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed tomato paste and jalapeños being stored in their original container after opening. CORRECTED- kitchen staff transferred the contents of the cans into a food safe container. The original can is not rated to safely hold the food material after opening the can. Ensure food items from cans are transferred (and date marked) into a food safe container to prevent contamination of ready to eat foods.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed partially cooked chicken nuggets stored below raw scallops and shrimp in the double door freezer in the facility’s back room. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) directed staff to move chicken nuggets to the top. Ensure any partially cooked animal proteins are stored above raw animal proteins to prevent contamination of food. Ready to eat foods should be stored at the top of a cooling unit, followed by animals proteins that require increasing cooking temperatures- with the protein requiring the highest cooking temperature at the bottom.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.  [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the dish washing machine to not be dispensing a chemical sanitizer (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- PIC called their service provider to obtain more sanitizer. The sanitizer was replaced and observed to be properly dispensing sanitizer (100 ppm Cl). Ensure frequent testing of sanitizer solution using the facility’s test strips. Dish machines that sanitize chemically should be dispense 50-200 ppm Cl bleach to properly sanitizer food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed multiple time/temperature control for food safety (TCS) items to be without date marking. Items included, but are not limited to, cheese sauce, salsa verde, salsa, onion, cilantro, cheese, and tamales. CORRECTED- PIC marked each item with the day they were prepared or thawed. Ensure all TCS foods being held at the facility for over 24 hours are date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed light entering the facility along the left side of the back door. Ensure all outer openings are protected from the entry of pests. Apply new weather stripping by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed cups lacking handles being stored in the sugar tub underneath the chip area prep table. CORRECTED- The person in charge removed cups from food storage container. Discussed proper utensil storage for in-use utensils with the person in charge. Ensure the usage of scoops with HANDLES sticking outwards to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed one Food Handler Certificate to have been expired since September, and two wait staff to not have their Food Handler’s Certificates. Ensure all employees handling food or ice obtain their Food Handler’s Certificates within 30 days of hire. Food Handlers must renew their certificate every three years to ensure safe food handling practices.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
It has been observed that the facility’s CFM has allowed their Allergen training to expire. Ensure all CFMs have their Allergen Awareness Training, and renew this certificate every three years. Inspector provided literature regarding Allergen Awareness requirements, which includes a link to ANSI-approved Allergen awareness training programs.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed an employee washing their hands in the triple sink. Corrective education was provided for employees. Ensure hands are only washed in the hand sink.
citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed at least two leaks dripping from the faucets of the triple sink. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that she would contact the facility’s internal maintenance team to repair the leaks. Ensure that faucets are maintained in leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: At the start of the inspection, a drink pitcher was observed inside of the bar’s hand-sink. Discussed with the PIC and the pitcher was removed. Ensure that hand-sinks are never obstructed and are available at all times for employees to wash hands.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine in the back storage room were observed with a significant amount of black mold and other debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that a service technician will be contacted to service the machine. Discussed cleaning the baffles in house in between professional services or having the technician company service the machine more frequently. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent mold build up and possible contamination of food items.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There are several pieces of unused equipment stored in the back storage room. The PIC is in the process of having the unused equipment removed from the premises. Discussed with PIC that unnecessary pieces of equipment can be seen as litter and act as a harboring environment for unwanted insects and pests. Continue to make progress regarding cleaning and the removal of pieces that are no longer necessary for operation.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand washing sink in the infant room to contain a paintbrush in the sink basin. CORRECTED- the paint brush was removed from the sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing only. A blocked sink/ a sink used for other purposes may deter frequent hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed ambient thermometer to be missing from the refrigerator in the infant room. CORRECTED- an ambient thermometer was placed in the door. Ensure all cold holding units contain an ambient thermometer placed in the warmest part of the unit to ensure temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are held at or below 41F.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The standing freezer in the kitchen has a large accumulation of ice observed. The PIC was shown and instructed to remove the ice. It is highly suggested that a pan be placed under the condenser unit so that the ice accumulation can be caught and the food packages protected from possible contaminants. Ensure that the ice is managed moving forward.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed a gallon of whole milk at an ambient temperature of 50F in one of the infant room refrigerators. The gallon of milk (which had been in the room for over 24 hours), as well as an individual bottle of milk (brought in 2 hours ago) probed at an internal temperature of 47F. CORRECTED- the gallon of milk was voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). Milk bottles were moved into refrigerators observed to be properly cold holding. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Refrigerator in an infant room was observed at an ambient temperature between 48-50F. Inspector turned down the cooling setting from 1-.05. Unit was observed to be at the same temperature 20 minutes later. The equipment is failing to hold TCS items at or below 41F (see violation #22). Ensure TCS items are held in working cooling units until this item is serviced. Inspector will return on 11/12/25 to ensure the refrigerator has been serviced to cold hold at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed one cooling unit in an infant room to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- PIC moved a thermometer into the cold holding unit. Ensure all cold holding units holding TCS items contain an ambient thermometer, placed in the warmest part of the unit, to monitor cold holding temperatures. Staff should monitor cold holding units to be at or below 41F.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
One Food Handler card was observed to have been expired 11 days ago. Ensure all staff obtain a Food Handler’s license within 30 days of hire, and maintain this certificate to be renewed every 3 years. A Food Handler’s course helps to ensures safe food handling practices.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed mops being dried in mop bucket basin. Discussed proper mop drying procedures with PIC. Ensure that mops are hung to dry, either over the wringer basket or on the wall. CORRECTED PIC placed the mops so that the mop heads were hanging over the wringer basket.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food. The facility is observed to have prepared produce in the walk-in cooler that is not covered. Also observed containers of chicken, onions, cabbage, and broccoli on the cookline are not covered while not being used (lunch rush had not started yet; no customers during the inspection). Follow-up on 11/6/2025. 

Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. Observed wet wiping cloths sitting by the triple sink. Corrected on site - wiping cloths moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wiping cloths are held in sanitizing solutions between uses. 

(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A)  Inspector observed an accumulation of soil inside the nozzles of the self-serving soda machines in the lobby. PIC was made aware. One of the machines was cleaned and sanitized. The other soda machine will have out of order posted on them until the nozzles are cleaned to sight of touch. Ensure that the internal surface of the soda machine nozzles are monitored and cleaned thoroughly to prevent contamination. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Inspector observed an accumulation of grease, food debris and soil build up under the grill and the fryers. PIC informed inspector that the grease trap is leaking beneath the grill and the fish and poultry fryers. PIC assured inspector that the grease trap is scheduled to be cleaned on Friday 10/31/25. Ensure that the build up is cleaned and sanitized to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 


Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Person in charge (PIC) did not have allergen awareness training. Inspector provided literature regarding allergen ANSI-approved awareness training courses for all Certified Food Protection Manager (CFMs). Obtain training by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the kitchen area of the facility is without paper towels during this inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced the empty dispenser during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

1) Raw chicken is observed over Ready-To-Eat (RTE) turkey and cooked beef in the walk in cooler. 2) Raw ground turkey is observed over RTE ground beef in the walk in cooler. Both items were shown to the PIC and they adjusted the storage locations to correct. Education should be regular and consistent in relation to storage orders in the coolers moving forward. Ensure foods are stored correctly in relation to their cooking temperatures in the coolers.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An open can of mountain dew was observed on the wire shelf in the dry storage room intermixed with foods intended for consumers. Before the PIC could be shown the can was removed by staff. The situation was discussed with the PIC. They asked for suggestions and the inspector stated that personal drinks should be stored “low and/or away” from items intended for consumers.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed one dead roach in a cabinet. CORRECTED. Education was provided to the person in charge (PIC) regarding reduction of pest harborage. The area was cleaned up, with the roach removed. Continue cleaning areas where food debris or grease may be harbored. Reduce moisture and check dark spaces for harborage conditions, as roaches are nocturnal pests.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee turned off the faucets after hand washing with their bare hands. The employee was educated that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucets to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Educational hand washing handouts were provided and the inspector suggests posting above the hand sinks. Ensure that the proper hand washing procedure is always used.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order:

(1) Raw meat stored on the shelf above onions in the walk-in cooler.

(2) Raw eggs stored on the shelf above various sauces in the double door cooler on the cookline. 

The storage order violations were correct during the inspection. Educational handouts were provided and the inspector suggests posting them in the kitchen. Ensure that raw meats and eggs are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed a large amount of cooked beans cooling in a deep, covered container on the counter at room temperature. The PIC stated that the beans had been cooling for about an hour. The inspector probed the beans and the internal temperature was 105F. The PIC was reminded that the beans must get below 70F in two hours. The beans were immediately separated into multiple uncovered containers to allow air flow through more of the food and moved into the walk-in cooler. The PIC was educated about the importance of using proper cooling methods and educational handouts were provided. The inspector will follow-up on 11/7/2025 to check on cooling practices at the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
