comment: Observed raw fish that bears a label indicating that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing was thawing inside of the packaging in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was educated and an employee removed the fish from the packaging during the inspection. Ensure that required foods are always removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the counter in the server area. The PIC was educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizing solutions between uses. The wiping cloth was removed for laundering during the inspection. Ensure that wiping cloths are always held in chemical sanitizer when not in use.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sugar container in the dry storage area has a bowl for a scoop. All scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of the food to avoid contamination. Ensure that the sugar container has a scoop with a handle by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The accumulation of dust and other debris on the walk-in cooler fans. 

(2) The accumulation of food debris in the container holding clean utensils on the storage shelves by the dish machine. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-103.11(O) Person In Charge. All of the portion of Code applying to knowledge of person-in-charge are applicable at this facility. The manager has a certified food protection certificate, however, is unable to demonstrate proper safe food handling and cannot impart knowledge onto staff. While language is a concern, the evidence of proper knowledge should be able to be seen in the cleaning and general maintenance of the facility. Overall, there is no apparent effort to maintain food as required in the Food Code. SCDPH has discussed the future operations of this facility and has the following solutions: 1) the facility will be upgraded to a Class I facility to insure multiple visits throughout the year; 2) the facility will be on a two week rotation of inspection by the director of EH and facility inspector to insure compliance with Code and that knowledge is being gained and applied; and 3) following a few months of follow-ups, the facility will be routinely visited by the SCDPH health educator to fill education gaps and to insure safe food handling between SCDPH visits. Inability to observe improvement will result in a suspension of permit until knowledge of proper food handling can be demonstrated. 
The food manager class is great education for all involved in the operations. Having multiple employees complete the training can only benefit Almadina operations. Please see that those employees that work any amount of time in the kitchen are at least food handler trained. But ideally food manager certificates should be obtained for employees. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (O) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD safety, including FOOD allergy awareness, as it relates to their assigned duties. FOOD allergy awareness includes describing FOODS identified as MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS and the symptoms that a MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN could cause in a sensitive individual who has an allergic reaction.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. Observed staff to not be able to demonstrate proper hand washing. As previously documented, the staff does not understand how to properly wash hands, when to wash hands, and how to properly use gloves. Gloved hands were observed being washed today. The tasks was identified as improper, halted, and corrected. Employees in the facility were not using a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing hands. Discussed with operator and employee and demonstrated proper technique. The employee interacting with SCDPH was on his phone at least five times during this educational meeting. Discussed washing hands after answering phone calls and handling food. Continue to educate available staff on proper technique. 

 (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Observed no paper towels to available at hand sink to left of the cookline. The staff indicated this handsink is not being used, however, as it is present, the sink should be properly supplied.

CEASE USING THE HANDSINK TO FILL PANS. HANDSINK IS FOR HANDWASHING ONLY. 

 Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure paper towels are available at all hand sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. The facility is not wiping off the lids of containers and that results in crusted foods. One crusted bottle was discarded, the other should be cleaned. 

FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
citation_text:
3-501.14(A) Cooling. The facility has bulk containers of food in the walk-in cooler that are cooked foods from previous days service. The bulk containers show no signs of proper cooling: covered, large amounts, and no date marking. The facility is unable to properly discuss cooling with SCDPH staff. Today, again, cooling practices were discussed at length. The staff does not have a stem thermometer to monitor temperatures and remains unaware of proper cooling practices. 

COOLING: KEEP ON COUNTER UNTIL PRODUCT IS 135F (USE PROBE THERMOMETER TO MONITOR TEMPERATURE). 
ONCE 135F, START ACTIVELY COOLING: 1) USE AN ICE BATH; 2) LEAVE UNCOVERED; 3) SMALLER PORTIONS/SHALLOW PANS; AND 4) PORTIONS IN THE FREEZER TO KNOCK DOWN HEAT BEFORE MOVING TO COOLER. 

(A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. Half of the kitchen foods are date marked. The walk-in cooler was one of the specific reasons for returning today, and only half of the present foods were properly date marked. The preparation cooler had date markings on everything, despite that not necessarily being required. Discussed date marking with two staff members. Date mark as food is placed within the coolers. There are multiple containers of rice and proteins cooked prior to today, without a proper date mark. If nothing is date marked, then the facility cannot know when to discard foods after seven days. Date mark prepared foods once created and date mark TCS foods once opened.



(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Thawing. Full tub of raw, frozen chicken is observed thawing on a counter in the back room. Discussed thawing under running water, in refrigerator, or as part of cooking. During the inspection, chicken was placed under running water at the triple sink. SCDPH will continue to monitor thawing practices to insure education is gained.


Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. The facility STILL does not have a probe thermometer available. A probe style thermometer shall be provided to allow for the proper cooling, reheating, and cooking of foods within the facility. Provide a stem thermometer and learn how to use and calibrate the thermometer. 

(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Gloves used properly.
citation_text:
3-304.15(C) Gloves, Use Limitation. The facility is observed donning gloves without a proper hand washing. Also, it appears that gloves are being used to protect hands and not food as the staff are observed touching multiple surfaces with gloved hands without changing. Discussed glove use at length. The facility will have this education included in the ongoing training that will occur over the next few months.  


(C) Slash-resistant gloves may be used with READY-TO-EAT FOOD that will not be subsequently cooked if the slash-resistant gloves have a SMOOTH, durable, and nonabsorbent outer surface; or if the slash-resistant gloves are covered with a SMOOTH, durable, nonabsorbent glove, or a SINGLE-USE glove.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-401.11(A)(1) and (A)(3)-(8) Equipment, Clothes Washers and Dryers, and Storage Cabinets, Contamination Prevention. 

Cleaning is not being properly conducted. Raise the standards on cleaning. The floor was asked to be cleaned, but corners were missed. Shelving was asked to be cleaned, but the soiled walk-in cooler shelving remains soiled. 

There is immediate concern over the lack of cleaning in this facility and the potential for cross-contamination. As a bare minimum, safe food handling should include a routine cleaning schedule that maintains surfaces clean. The facility does not have a single surface that is observed free of accumulated grease and soil. A follow-up for the following surfaces will be conducted in two weeks:
1) hood system - the hood has not been serviced since 2023. The baffles are observed coated with grease and ready to drip onto the food of the cook line - clean the baffles, the Ansul system, and service the hood.
2) Shelving in the walk-in cooler is coated with food debris and mold. The shelving should be removed and power washed to remove all access grease and soil. 
3) The dry storage shelving is observed coated with a dusting of powder from the various spices held on the shelves. The side brace is nearly yellow from powder from spices.
4) Fryer, flat top, steamer, and vertical broiler are observed thickly coated with accumulated grease. This appears to be a potential fire hazard. Clean the cooking surfaces.
5) Throughout the facility, in-use cooking utensils are not being removed every four hours for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. There were observed soiled knives and peelers under the prep cooler from previous days use. Discussed cleaning. This is one of the topics that will be covered in future educationals. Staff appeared to be unaware as to proper wash, rinse, and sanitizing practices. 
6) preparation cooler interior and exterior is observed soiled with accumulated food debris. 

Clean the aforementioned surfaces paying attention to maintaining these surfaces clean once the initial task is completed.  


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, EQUIPMENT, a cabinet used for the storage of FOOD, or a cabinet that is used to store cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be located: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. The facility needs maintenance attention to the following areas:
1) the ceiling tile of the corner of the cookline is bubbled from a previous water leak. Replace the damaged ceiling tile.
2) the faucet of the prep sink is loose and not secure. Replace the faucet. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed one dead, and one live fly during today’s spot check. Obtain pest control provider by next routine inspection. Pest control devices (such as fly strips) may be purchased to manage pests, just ensure they are away from food storage.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a bottle of bleach to be on the same shelf as in use dressing. Discussed with PIC, bleach was moved to a location away from dressing. Ensure any toxic material is stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following areas to be soiled with food debris:
1) The interior of nacho cheese dispenser to be soiled with food accumulation. 
2) The drive thru microwave.

Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at triple sink and to the right of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, areas will be caulked. Ensure staff is monitoring caulking and replacing as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The person in charge (PIC) did not have test strips to verify sanitizing solution concentration for food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- PIC obtained test strips. Ensure the use of test strips to verify concentration of sanitizer used for food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

title: Food handler training
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: PIC has not completed Food Handler Training. Anyone handling food or ice must obtain Food Handler Training (every 3 years). The attainment and retention of Food Handler’s certificates ensures safe handling practices. Keep certificates printed and available for review during health inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) There was no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present during today’s inspection. PIC was Made aware. PIC assured inspector that they will proceed with the process of getting a CFPM on site at all times during operation. Ensure that there is at least one CFPM present in the facility during operation at all times. 

 Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Inspector observed the following food items being stored on the floor during inspection. 
1. Multiple lotus containers in cardboard boxes stored directly on the floor next to the double doors standing milk cooler in the back.
2. Multiple boxes of smoothie mix in cardboard boxes stored on the floor at the entrance of the dry storage area. 

PIC was made aware. PIC told inspector that they are currently overstock at the moment however, they would ensure that the above mentioned food items would be stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect them from splash, pest, and other forms of contaminations. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed mold accumulation to be present at the wall behind soda dispensing nozzles. Discussed with PIC, area will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevent mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present upon arrival. DIscussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager to present within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the back room was observed to have a container of graffiti remover in it. CORRECTED- The inspector removed the graffiti remover from the sink basin and educated the PIC that handwashing sinks should always be maintained accessible at all times for employee use. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times and are only used for their intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink in the back room was observed to not have any paper towels at it. CORRECTED- An employee placed paper towels at the handwashing sink and the PIC was educated that all handwashing sinks should always have paper towels at them. Paper towels are necessary to allow for proper handwashing and the use of a barrier when turning off the faucet.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: The facility is observed to be selling hot dogs and tornadoes on roller grills during today’s inspection. The facility does not have a grease trap and the current one is concreted in. A new grease trap would need to be put in and the facility would need to be moved to a Medium Risk to allow these roller grill items to be served in the facility. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they will cease selling the hot dogs and they were all discarded during today’s inspection. A spot check will be conducted in the future to ensure that the equipment has been removed from the facility and that these roller grill items are no longer being sold.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the inside of the Bunn coffee machine is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. A follow up is scheduled on 11/3/2025 to ensure that the top of the inside of the Bunn coffee machine has been cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are frequently cleaned and are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- There were pre-packaged sandwiches that were observed to be in the cooler that did not bear any date-marking on them. This was discussed with the PIC. The PIC stated that the sandwiches arrive frozen and that they are placed into the cooler upon arrival. The PIC stated that these items were placed in the cooler on Tuesday. It was discussed with the PIC that these must be date-marked when put out and discarded if not sold within 7 days. CORRECTED- The sandwiches were date-marked during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: There were bottles of a bleach cleaning spray observed to be above boxes of cereal. CORRECTED- These boxes of cereal were moved to another shelf, where they were not exposed to contamination. Ensure that chemicals are never stored above food items. Food items should be protected from contamination during storage and display.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The bleach that the facility is observed to be using for food-contact surfaces does not have an EPA Registration Number. A follow up is scheduled for 10/27/2025 to ensure that the facility has obtained an EPA-Registered Bleach. This was discussed with the PIC.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There were single-service forks and knives that were observed to be in cups with their food-contact surface being exposed to contamination. CORRECTED- The utensils were inverted by an employee and the PIC was educated that these should be displayed inverted to protect them from contamination. Ensure that single service articles and utensils are handled, displayed, and dispensed to protect the food-contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility is observed to be using bleach as a sanitizer, but did not have any Chlorine test strips. This was discussed with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled on 11/3/2025 to ensure that Chlorine test strips have been obtained.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The walk-in cooler fan covers are observed to have an accumulation of dust on them. 
2. The shelf the microwave is on is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Follow-up for cleaning under the cookline, ceiling tiles over steamer, mop sink tiles.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Follow-up to insure management is maintaining the facility clean and maintained.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not register on the inspector test strips (CL sanitizer). The concentrate jug was observed empty and replaced. The new jug would not register on the test strips either, even when the jug itself was tested. A third jug was attached to the machine and then produced the needed concentration of CL in solution for effective sanitization of dishes. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are at effective levels at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is an accumulation of debris on the ice machine baffles. The PIC stated they get the ice machine professionally cleaned every six months, but the inspector suggests a more frequent cleaning schedule. The inspector will return on 11/3/2025 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned to sight and touch. The inspector will call the PIC on 11/3/2025 to schedule a time for the follow-up.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the kitchen freezer has a large accumulation of frost. The inspector recommends increasing the frequency that it is defrosted. Ensure that the freezer is defrosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of food residue inside of the pizza ovens. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The pizza ovens that are broken or not used frequently must also be maintained cleaned. Ensure that the pizza ovens are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the water/tea bar soda gun to be soiled with black mold. Discussed with PIC, soda gun will be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda guns are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed kitchen prep cooler to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, prep cooler will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevent food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bottle was set up and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer soulition is prepared at the proper sanitization level during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the ice machine baffle to be soiled on the corners. Discussed with the PIC, and PIC immediately cleaned and sanitized the baffle. Ensure that baffles are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed pasta salad on an ice bath to be probed at 49F. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) stated the serving had been sitting out for approximately one hour, so the item was moved into a cooler. Education about ice baths occurred with PIC. Ensure items moved out during busy periods are either; held at or below 41F, are in an ice bath which surrounds the bottom and sides of the container, or time as control for food safety (TAC) is used.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items without date marking (caramel iced latte, milk, and sour cream). CORRECTED- the caramel iced latte is not currently being used, but education about date marking occurred. Milk and sour cream were both opened or prepared yesterday, and were marked with the corresponding date. Ensure all TCS items are date marked with the date they are opened, prepared, or thawed, and used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed insect control device over foods in hot holding. CORRECTED- PIC moved the light away from food storage. Ensure all pest control devices are installed away from areas of food storage and preparation to prevent insects from contaminating food.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed multiple wet sanitizer cloths being stored on counters in both the bar area and the kitchen. CORRECTED- education occurred with PIC and staff. Ensure wet sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution when not in use to prevent the growth of pathogens on the cloth.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector observed Certified Food Protection Manager’s (CFPM/CFM) Allergen awareness training to be expired. Allergen awareness training must be maintained and renewed every 3 years for facility’s CFMs. Ensure CFMs receive Allergen Awareness training by ANSI accredited program by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: The leak coming from the pipes under the triple sink is still present and has not been repaired. The PIC stated that they have a company coming this week to repair the leak. A follow up is scheduled for 10/24/2025 to ensure that the leak has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employees on the cookline were not washing hands between removing gloves and putting on new ones. The employees on the cookline were educated that hands must be washed before donning gloves to initiate tasks that involve working with food. The PIC will be continuing to educated employees about the proper procedure. Ensure that employees always wash hands when switching gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the sushi hand washing sink was blocked with a container of vegetables. The employees at the sushi station were educated that the hand washing sink must always be accessible. During the inspection the container was removed from across the hand washing sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are always maintained accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed plastic containers holding various sauces and seasonings on the cookline were soiled with debris. The PIC discarded the soiled plastic containers and replaced them with new containers during the inspection. They were reminded that the plastic containers must be replaced on a regular basis to avoid soil accumulation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed glass cleaner re-packaged from the original container into spray bottles were not labeled. During the inspection the glass cleaner at the sushi station and by the mop sink were labeled with the common name. Ensure that toxic materials taken from bulk supply are always clearly labeled with the common name of the material.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Observed there are not ambient air thermometers inside of the coolers at the sushi station and the main kitchen. There are thermometers inside the walk-in coolers. The ambient air thermometers must be placed at the warmest part of the cooler (i.e., next to the door). Ensure that every cooler has an ambient air thermometer by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed that the bar hand washing sink is not sealed to the wall. Ensure that the hand sink is sealed to the wall (ex. caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: The accumulated debris behind the nozzles of the server soda machine. 

(2) The dust on the fans of the single door cooler by the kitchen entrance. 

(3) The dust, drink spills, and other debris inside of the clear door cooler under the back counter at the bar. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the cove base has fallen off the wall to the right of the kitchen back door and on the corner to the left of the front walk-in cooler. Ensure the cove base is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the mop head stored on the mop sink basin. The PIC and employees were educated that mops must be stored in a position that allows the head to air-dry. The mop was hung on the rack during the inspection. Ensure that mop heads are always stored to facilitate air-drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the ceiling in the alcohol storage room (also stores single-use articles and food contact surfaces) at the back of the kitchen is damaged in the back right corner. Ensure that the ceiling is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the seal on the back hand sink to be cracked and damaged. Ensure sealant is replaced before next routine inspection to prevent moisture and bacterial growth.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 22 cans to be rusted, severely dented, or dented along a seam. Discussed with PIC, and all cans were disposed of immediately. Ensure that dented (sharp dent or seam dent), rusted, or bulged cans are thrown away and not sold to customers.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed 4 papayas and several yellow summer squashes to be molding on the retail shelf. Discussed with PIC and all moldy foods were discarded. Ensure that moldy food is removed from shelves and not sold to customers.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed soda nozzle on Coca-Cola machine next to the UPS store to have a build up of soils. Discussed with PIC. PIC cleaned the nozzles and internal surface of the Coca Cola soda dispenser machine as a corrective action.. Ensure soda machine nozzle is cleaned regularly to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION:
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food. The facility is observed to have a number of foods, stored from the previous days’ operation, to be uncovered (egg rolls and cooked chicken in the drink cooler; fried chips next to the fryers; bulk rice, bulk potato starch, and bulk dry noodles in the back; egg rolls and various prepared produce in the walk-in cooler). title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed the hood system beginning to drip grease due to lack of cleaning. Maintain the hood system clean so that accumulated grease does not drip onto food being cooked beneath (THIS IS A FOUR TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION). Also, observed the fans of the walk-in cooler to be coated with dust and grease. Clean the fans to prevent soiled air from moving through kitchen. Follow-up on 10/30/25
