title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils.  Observed soiled tongs in the fryer basket from yesterday’s service. Also, observed a silver pan scoop used to put vegetables into the wok soiled with grease and food debris. Finally, the tumble mixer being stored by the hand sink is left uncovered and is soiled with various dried produce pieces. See that the tumbler is cleaned and then stored to prevent food contact surface from being soiled. Also, see that the tongs and scoop are cleaned every night after closing. Follow-up on 10/30/2025.

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Observed fried rice stored in a steamer from yesterday. The steamer was turned-off overnight and the food was temped at 50F today. Owner stated that he was going to discard the product, however, the facility should remove old food at the end of the night. Close properly to allow for proper opening. Leaving food overnight is a potential concern for pests. Leaving the old food also means the steamer may not be cleaned properly before being reintroduced to service. During the inspection, the rice was discarded.  
SCDPH will continue to spot check so this behavior of overnight storage is corrected. 
Food code does allow you to store hot food (over 135F) for an indefinite period of time (until quality becomes a concern). Either remove the food and clean containers nightly, or store at temperatures of 135F or above. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION:
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. Observed a whisk and a lid for a pan being stored held against the wall by the plumbing of the water heater. Cease using this back room to store clean utensils. Utensils to be used for kitchen use/food contact should be properly stored on a clean surface within the kitchen space. 

FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION:
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. Observed single-service items in the back dry storage room stored on the floor. Cease storing single-service items on the floor. Ensure that single-service items are stored 6-inches off the ground to avoid contamination. 

(A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Observed ketchup being stored in the can after a days use. Ketchup is an acidic food and will damage the can if not moved to a more appropriate container after opening. See that ketchup and other acidic foods (pineapple) are properly stored in a different container after the can is opened. The can of ketchup also was observed barely covered with plastic wrap and with pieces of onion on the surface. This ties in with violation #15 (see above) that addresses proper storage of items to prevent cross contamination. Keep containers covered to prevent cross-contact with other items.  

Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. Observed a large accumulation of grease and food debris on the floor underneath the fryers. The floor must be cleaned to sight and touch. Follow-up on 10/30/2025.
Also, observed old mouse droppings around the back door of the facility. No large accumulation and nothing that appeared new. Clean the back storage area.
Finally, observed the light shield in the walk-in cooler to be coated with accumulated grease and dust. Remove and clean the walk-in cooler light shield. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. Observed cove base peeling off the wall to the right of the sliding drink cooler and to the left of the drive through window. Ensure that the cove base is sealed to the wall. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FOUR TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. Ceiling tiles in the dry storage area by the back door are starting to show signs of ware from leaks. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed sanitizer at the bar’s triple sink to not be reaching the sanitizing concentration benchmark set by the manufacturer’s label (200-400 ppm of quaternary ammonia). CORRECTED- PIC made bleach water sanitizer at a concentration of 200 ppm. Inspector will return on 10/30/25 to check one of two solutions:
1) The facility has adjusted the water heater to reach 75F to allow quaternary ammonia sanitizer tablets to dissolve.
2) Facility has obtained unscented bleach (with an EPA registration number and label indicating use for food contact surfaces) to use as sanitizer. Facility has test strips for both sanitizers, so either are acceptable means of sanitation for food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed two temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items (orange juice and heavy whipping cream) to be without date marking in the facility. CORRECTED- the heavy whipping cream was voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC), and the orange juice was labeled with a date. Ensure all TCS food and drinks are marked with a date once opened; the day the item is opened counts as “day one”. Use or discard within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed container holding multiple food contact utensils at the bar to be soiled with debris. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized cup holding utensils. Ensure all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, which may transfer to food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Fan covers in the walk in cooler were observed to be soiled with dust and ice. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the buildup of debris. Clean fans during defrost. Inspector will check the cleaning of the fans during a spot check on 10/30/25.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC for this facility has not completed and acquired a CFPM certificate. A hand out was given with current local options for the course/test. They are instructed to acquire a CFPM prior tot he next routine inspection.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC could not provide verification of employees being notified of their responsibility to report. The PIC called the food manager and they could not direct them to them either. Fresh copies of the SCDPH Reporting Agreements were given to be signed prior to the follow-up scheduled for 10/27/25.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
(REPEAT x2)6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The hand sink next to the three part sink is without paper towels at the start of this inspection. Paper towels were supplied to correct.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

A package of raw sausage is observed over containers of Ready-To-Eat sauces in a standing cooler. The PIC was shown and educated. The package was moved to the bottom cooler to correct.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

The deflector shield in the ice machine is observed with slime/mold growth. The PIC was shown and cleaned the location to correct.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC was unaware of any reporting agreements or similar paperwork that had been filled out or signed by food handlers. The PIC called the food manager who stated correct procedures but stated that they had not known that verification/paperwork was required. Blank copies were found in the public health folder in the filing cabinet. Fresh copies of the SCDPH reporting agreements were given during this inspection and a follow up scheduled for 10 days to ensure compliance with the code. Ensure that all needed paperwork is available at all times in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
(REREAT) 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

On arrival the hand sink next to the three part sink is observed blocked with a hand cart. As the inspector and PIC walked into the space the PIC moved the cart into the walk in cooler prior to inspector prompting. This shows that they know that it should not be in this location normally. The situation was discussed with the PIC during this inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks remain accessible at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice scoop handle to be in contact with ice at drive thru window. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was removed and placed in a way that handle is not in contact with ice. Ensure ice scoop handle is not in contact with ice.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed confetti cake toppings to be held past their 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, item was pulled and disposed of. Ensure staff is monitoring date marking and is posing of any TCS food held longer than 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure staff is monitoring caulking at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of grease on the hood baffles in the back section of the kitchen. This build up could serve as an ignition source for a kitchen fire. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease or other debris. Clean by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM/ CFM) was present during today's inspection. A CFM is required at all establishments serving unpackaged food to oversee food handling, proper hot and cold holding temperatures for temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods, as well as proper sanitation procedures and concentrations. Ensure a CFM is acquired and present for future inspections.
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN 
CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed an employee dumping dirty water down the hand washing sink. The PIC was reminded that hand washing sinks cannot be used for any purpose other than hand washing. The PIC will be educating employees about proper sink usage. Ensure that hand washing sinks are only used for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed several dented cans stored on the storage rack by the walk-in cooler. There was also an open ketchup can in the bottom of the cookline prep cooler that had a severe dent along the seam. The opened ketchup can was voluntary discarded during the inspection and the other dented cans from the storage rack were removed from service. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket on the cookline was testing at 0 ppm (Cl). The PIC remade the bucket which tested at 100 ppm (Cl). The inspector reminded that PIC and employees that sanitizer buckets must be changed on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-200 ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that plastic containers storing various powders/seasonings and the spoons for dispensing on the cookline were heavily soiled. The PIC discarded the heavily soiled containers and spoons during the inspection. The inspector educated that the containers and spoons must be changed regularly to avoid the accumulation of soil resides. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a cutting board drying behind the faucet of the utility sink by the back door. The sink was being used by an employee while the cutting board was drying. The PIC was educated that the cutting board could become contaminated by dirty water splashes, food residue, or other debris stored in this location. During the inspection the cutting board was removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized before stored in another location. Ensure that food contact surfaces always remain clean to sight and touch during storage.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a large container of rice was stored on the cookline with an internal temperature of 50F. The PIC stated that the rice was removed from the cooler at 11 AM. When asked, the employees on the cookline stated that they were planning to put the rice back inside the cooler after lunch ended. The inspector explained the importance to the PIC and employees of keeping rice outside of the temperature danger zone (41-135F). They cannot leave large quantities of rice at room temperature for several hours and then put the unused rice back inside of the cooler for future use. The rice was put under a time-as-control policy and was discarded at 3 pm. The PIC and inspector discussed removing smaller quantities of rice that can be used during the lunch rush in the future. The inspector will follow-up on 10/21/2025 to check that only small quantities of rice are being removed from the cooler during lunch.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed ketchup and pineapple stored inside of opened cans. Ketchup and pineapple are an acidic food and will damage the can if they are not moved to a more appropriate container after opening. The ketchup was voluntarily discarded (can was also dented; see violation #13) and the pineapple was moved into a plastic container during the inspection. Ensure that ketchup, pineapple, and other acidic foods are property stored after opening. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The food debris in the interior of the sushi prep area microwave. 

(2) The debris inside of the bar soda gun holder. 

(3) The debris accumulation on top of the dish washing machine. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the bar hand washing sink is not sealed to the wall. The sink must be sealed to the wall (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed a personal drink stored on the shelf above the cookline prep cooler. The PIC was educated that personal drinks must be stored away from food preparation areas to avoid contamination. The drink was moved away from the cookline during the inspection. Ensure that personal items are kept in designated areas for employee storage.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. The facility is in the process of cleaning and maintenance. The store has started to undergo a deep cleaning starting at the back door and moving on the perimeter (the walk-ins on the left and the ice machine to the dish machine on the right). There remains multiple pieces of equipment (and floors, walls, ceilings) that need more detailed cleaning attention. The facility is of the understanding that the cleaning is not nearly complete and there are multiple areas that need detailed attention. Inspector will be following-up on what has been started on November 10, 2025. 
A power washer is available and should continue to be used on bulk equipment and physical facilities that can  withstand. 
NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
4-301.14 Ventilation Hood Systems, Adequacy. The piece of steaming equipment that is in the back room puts out enough steam that is appears the ceiling tiles overhead are either experiencing condensation drips resulting is peeled ceiling tile surface and possible mold growth. Either way, the steam should be contained to avoid damage to ceiling and walls. The immediate solution was suggested to have the ceiling tiles replaced. This may be a temporary erasure of the condensation problem, but if the ceiling is not continuously wiped/dried, the ceiling tiles will become soiled/damaged again. 

Ventilation hood systems and devices shall be sufficient in number and capacity to prevent grease or condensation from collecting on walls and ceilings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shell egg stored above cut tomato and mushrooms in the top of the prep cooler. The PIC was informed and the eggs were moved to the bottom of the prep cooler
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed no sanitizer available in the kitchen during food prep. PIC was informed and added chlorine bleach to a  bucket of water in the kitchen, measuring 100ppm chlorine. Ensure staff have sanitizer available at all times of food preparation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
comment: Inspectors observed breaded chicken cooling on the counter in the kitchen. The PIC informed inspectors that the chicken had been prepared “this morning.” The chicken measured 90F with the infrared thermometer. The inspector discussed proper cooling with the PIC and the chicken was placed in the walk-in cooler. Ensure items are kept on the counter to cool ONLY until they reach 135F. At that time, items need to be transferred to a cooler to complete cooling within the required time-frame.
citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: No ambient thermometers were observed in the facility’s cooling units. Ambient thermometers help the facility monitor cold holding temperatures, to ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are at the correct temperature (41F and below) to mitigate the growth of pathogens. Ensure the facility obtains ambient thermometers in cooling units (with freezers being an exception) to monitor cold holding temperatures by the next routine inspection. Place ambient thermometers in the warmest part of the cooling unit (towards the front).
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspectors observed a knife stored in the seam between the prep cooler and the adjoining counter. This seam is not easily cleanable, and is therefore not an acceptable storage location for in-use utensils. The PIC was informed and the knife was moved to the dish area. Inspector recommends investing in a magnetic knife strip for the prep area.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed gaps between the walls and the hand washing sinks and triple sink in the kitchen. Openings between fixed equipment (sinks) and walls can allow for the entry of water and harborage of mold or bacteria. Seal gaps by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The inspector observed one of the soda machine nozzles to have soil accumulation on the soda machine dispenser. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned the nozzle and the inside of the machine. The PIC stated that they clean the nozzles daily and wipe the dispenser part of the machine. The other nozzles were observed to be clean. Ensure that staff are adequately cleaning the nozzles and the soda machine. Food-contact surfaces and utensils should be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple dead roaches on insect traps, as well as in the under-counter cabinetry. Live roaches were also observed on the traps, from adult to larval stages. Employees are currently logging pest sightings in a blue “Steritech” binder. Nine roach sightings have been reported during the past month in the binder in areas including the bar, near the water heater, in the manager office, as well as in areas where ready-to-eat food is held. On 10/07/25 the pest control technician noted that the areas in the pest log had been chemically treated, and gel bait was applied.

 If dead roaches are spotted they should be immediately removed, and the area they were in should be cleaned. Remove all conditions for harborage, including spilt food and beverages, as well as cardboard. Write the date on glue traps to better monitor pests. The frequency at which pest control is providing services to the facility is currently inadequate. Increase services to biweekly treatments. The inspector will return on 10/29/25 to check pest control management. Ensure the facility has proof of service available as well as a minimum six month contract with a pest control provider to show during the follow up inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. [C]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-103.11(O) Person In Charge. All of the portion of Code applying to knowledge of person-in-charge are applicable at this facility. The manager has a certified food protection certificate, however, is unable to demonstrate proper safe food handling and cannot impart knowledge onto staff. While language is a concern, the evidence of proper knowledge should be able to be seen in the cleaning and general maintenance of the facility. Overall, there is no apparent effort to maintain food as required in the Food Code. SCDPH has discussed the future operations of this facility and has the following solutions: 1) the facility will be upgraded to a Class I facility to insure multiple visits throughout the year; 2) the facility will be on a two week rotation of inspection by the director of EH and facility inspector to insure compliance with Code and that knowledge is being gained and applied; and 3) following a few months of follow-ups, the facility will be routinely visited by the SCDPH health educator to fill education gaps and to insure safe food handling between SCDPH visits. Inability to observe improvement will result in a suspension of permit until knowledge of proper food handling can be demonstrated. 
The food manager class is great education for all involved in the operations. Having multiple employees complete the training can only benefit Almadina operations. Please see that those employees that work any amount of time in the kitchen are at least food handler trained. But ideally food manager certificates should be obtained for employees. 


The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (O) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD safety, including FOOD allergy awareness, as it relates to their assigned duties. FOOD allergy awareness includes describing FOODS identified as MAJOR FOOD ALLERGENS and the symptoms that a MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN could cause in a sensitive individual who has an allergic reaction.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. Observed staff to not be able to demonstrate proper hand washing. Employees in the facility were not using a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing hands. Discussed with operator and employee and demonstrated proper technique. The employee interacting with SCDPH was on his phone at least five times during this educational meeting. Discussed washing hands after answering phone calls and handling food. Continue to educate available staff on proper technique. 

 (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
citation_text:
3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. The facility is observed cooling and reheating almost every protein served at the facility. As a Class II facility, the act of cooling/reheating is not allowed. As the kitchen is cooling over eight different items, the upgrade to Class I will occur. Furthermore, the facility is struggling to demonstrate safe food handling. The inability of the facility to proper clean, maintain, and handle foods dictates the upgrade. 


(A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. Observed a covered container of cooked/cooled potatoes to be molded. Potatoes were discarded during the inspection. 

FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
citation_text:
3-501.14(A) Cooling. The facility has bulk containers of food in the walk-in cooler that are cooked foods from previous days service. The bulk containers show no signs of proper cooling: covered, large amounts, and no date marking. The chicken on the counter is temped at 90F which implies possible improper cooling and the obvious improper reheating/hot holding (see violation #21). 

COOLING: KEEP ON COUNTER UNTIL PRODUCT IS 135F (USE PROBE THERMOMETER TO MONITOR TEMPERATURE). 
ONCE 135F, START ACTIVELY COOLING: 1) USE AN ICE BATH; 2) LEAVE UNCOVERED; 3) SMALLER PORTIONS/SHALLOW PANS; AND 4) PORTIONS IN THE FREEZER TO KNOCK DOWN HEAT BEFORE MOVING TO COOLER. 

(A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. There are multiple items being held on counters and not in proper hot holding units. The facility has a hot holding display, a steam table, and a warmer available. None of these items are in-use today. During the inspection, chicken (cooked yesterday) was observed on the counter at 90ish F. The operator could not immediately explain why food from yesterday and just brought to the counter within the last 15 minutes was temping at 90F. See violation #20. The proper hot holding of foods was discussed as was the proper reheating behavior. A warmer was plugged-in and made available for use. 

HOLD FOODS AT 135F OR ABOVE ONCE COOKED.

REHEAT FROM COLD TEMPERATURE TO 165F WITHIN TWO HOURS. 

USE A PROBE THERMOMETER TO INSURE THIS PROCESS IS PROPERLY CONDUCTED. 
This hot holding practice will be monitored by SCDPH staff over the next few weeks to insure proper education to staff. 

(A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. Nothing in the kitchen bares a date mark. There are multiple containers of rice and proteins cooked prior to today, without a proper date mark. If nothing is date marked, then the facility cannot know when to discard foods after seven days. Date mark prepared foods once created and date mark TCS foods once opened.



(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(B) Thawing. Full tub of raw, frozen chicken is observed thawing on a counter in the back room. Discussed thawing under running water, in refrigerator, or as part of cooking. During the inspection, chicken was placed under running water at the triple sink. SCDPH will continue to monitor thawing practices to insure education is gained.


Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. The facility does not have a probe thermometer available. A probe style thermometer shall be provided to allow for the proper cooling, reheating, and cooking of foods within the facility. Provide a stem thermometer and learn how to use and calibrate the thermometer. 

(A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(A) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. There were no sani-cloths being stored in the available sanitizing solution. Cloths were observed on various counters around the kitchen. The available sani-bucket was shallow. A larger bucket was created - use a bucket that can fit your hands and the available cloths. 

(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills from TABLEWARE and carry-out containers that occur as FOOD is being served shall be: (1) Maintained dry; and (2) Used for no other purpose.

title: Gloves used properly.
citation_text:
3-304.15(C) Gloves, Use Limitation. The facility is observed donning gloves without a proper hand washing. Also, it appears that gloves are being used to protect hands and not food as the staff are observed touching multiple surfaces with gloved hands without changing. Discussed glove use at length. The facility will have this education included in the ongoing training that will occur over the next few months.  


(C) Slash-resistant gloves may be used with READY-TO-EAT FOOD that will not be subsequently cooked if the slash-resistant gloves have a SMOOTH, durable, and nonabsorbent outer surface; or if the slash-resistant gloves are covered with a SMOOTH, durable, nonabsorbent glove, or a SINGLE-USE glove.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-401.11(A)(1) and (A)(3)-(8) Equipment, Clothes Washers and Dryers, and Storage Cabinets, Contamination Prevention. 

There is immediate concern over the lack of cleaning in this facility and the potential for cross-contamination. As a bare minimum, safe food handling should include a routine cleaning schedule that maintains surfaces clean. The facility does not have a single surface that is observed free of accumulated grease and soil. A follow-up for the following surfaces will be conducted in two weeks:
1) hood system - the hood has not been serviced since 2023. The baffles are observed coated with grease and ready to drip onto the food of the cook line - clean the baffles, the Ansul system, and service the hood.
2) Shelving in the walk-in cooler is coated with food debris and mold. The shelving should be removed and power washed to remove all access grease and soil. 
3) The dry storage shelving is observed coated with a dusting of powder from the various spices held on the shelves. The side brace is nearly yellow from powder from spices.
4) Fryer, flat top, steamer, and vertical broiler are observed thickly coated with accumulated grease. This appears to be a potential fire hazard. Clean the cooking surfaces.
5) Throughout the facility, in-use cooking utensils are not being removed every four hours for wash, rinse, and sanitizing. There were observed soiled knives and peelers under the prep cooler from previous days use. Discussed cleaning. This is one of the topics that will be covered in future educationals. Staff appeared to be unaware as to proper wash, rinse, and sanitizing practices. 
6) preparation cooler interior and exterior is observed soiled with accumulated food debris. 

Clean the aforementioned surfaces paying attention to maintaining these surfaces clean once the initial task is completed.  


(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, EQUIPMENT, a cabinet used for the storage of FOOD, or a cabinet that is used to store cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be located: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-501.17 Warewashing Equipment, Cleaning Agents.  The facility is observed using a window cleaner to clean a rice steamer. Also, there was no knowledge of how a triple sink was to be properly created and used. Discussed sanitizing at the moment. Steamer was cleaned-in-place using a bleach solution to complete. Will continue to educate on future inspections. 


When used for WAREWASHING, the wash compartment of a sink, mechanical warewasher, or wash receptacle of alternative manual WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT as specified in 4-301.12(C), shall contain a wash solution of soap, detergent, acid cleaner, alkaline cleaner, degreaser, abrasive cleaner, or other cleaning agent according to the cleaning agent manufacturer's label instructions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, See food contact surfaces violation. The facility is in danger of creating a cross-potential situation due to the lack of cleaning and potential of molds and soil to move from surfaces to food. Continue to clean so that surfaces are maintained free of accumulated soil. 

Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
citation_text:
5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. The facility had mop water remaining from yesterday’s cleaning. Leaving soiled water resent overnight is a potential source of water borne pathogens as well as a water source for pests. Empty mop water nightly. Emptied during the inspection. 

 Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. The facility needs maintenance attention to the following areas:
1) the ceiling tile of the corner of the cookline is bubbled from a previous water leak. Replace the damaged ceiling tile.
2) the faucet of the prep sink is loose and not secure. Replace the faucet. 

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. Floors throughout the facility are observed soiled with a heavy accumulation of soil. Areas of concern are under and behind equipment (especially around the back door).
Clean the floors throughout paying attention to clean around equipment. 


(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed the internal surface of the smoothie blender to be soiled. PIC was made aware. PIC immediately cleaned the internal surface of the blender. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the internal surface of the blender are monitored, cleaned, and sanitized at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer available in the kitchen during food preparation. An employee was informed of the requirement for sanitizer availability and a spray bottle was prepared, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is available at all times of food preparation and service.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the soda gun nozzle at the bar had an accumulation of debris. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The PIC cleaned the nozzle during the inspection. Ensure that the soda gun nozzle remains clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the stainless steel shelf above the three compartment sink is rusted. The shelf must either be replaced or pained and sealed. Ensure that the shelf is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.  

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces require cleaning:

(1) The grease on the floor and on the side of the fryer and oven. 

(2) The food debris on the gaskets of the freezer by the fryers. 

(3) The dust behind the juice machine nozzles.

(4) The debris on the bottom of the ice scoop holder at the bar. 

(5) The dust and other debris on the shelf holding milk and creamer in the walk-in cooler. 

(6) The debris on the bottom of the black containers holding clean dishes next to the walk-in freezer. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Observed the following lacked date marking when the inspector arrived at the facility:

(1) Rice that was cooked yesterday morning in the silver triple door cooler.
(2) Rice that was cooked yesterday morning in the walk-in cooler. 
(2) Gyro meat that was cooked and cooled on Sunday in the walk-in cooler. 

During the inspection the above referenced foods were correctly date marked. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one; food is discarded after six additional days). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed bare wood planks on the wall behind the slushy machines by the cash register. The bare wood must be sealed (ex.painted) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there was an accumulation of food debris and grease on the table surface underneath the grill. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. The PIC began the process of cleaning the surface during the inspection. Ensure that underneath the grills remains clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there is a missing cover on the light switch to the left of the mop sink closet. Ensure that the missing cover is replaced to maintain physical facilities in good repair by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed a personal drink stored on the shelf above the prep cooler on the cookline. The drink was removed from the shelf during the inspection. Ensure that personal drinks are stored away from food preparation areas to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training expired in May 2025. The PIC will be renewing their certificate. Ensure that all CFPM’s have training in allergen awareness principles by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed soda nozzle on Coca-Cola machine next to the UPS store to have a build up of soils. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that they will have the machine marked out of order until it is able to be cleaned. Ensure soda machine nozzle is cleaned regularly to avoid contamination.
Inspector will return on 10/21/25 for a followup
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

Ensure that the surface identified is clear to sight of touch.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.

3-305.11(A) Inspector observed a few dairy food items being store on the floor in the dairy walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware and PIC immediately remove the items and stored them appropriately. Ensure that food items stored at least 6 inches from the floor to protect them from splash, dust, and other contaminants. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Inspector observed a mop head being stored on the floor in the produce aisle. PIC was made aware and the mop head was removed to be store properly. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a position that allows them to air dry. 

Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

 Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed liquid cheese sauce to have an ambient temperature of 125F, and was probed to have an internal temperature of 126F. CORRECTED- the liquid cheese was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Liquid cheese was moved to used time as a control for food safety (TAC). The outside of the container was marked with a discard time 4 hours past when the bag was opened. Other options may include using a ladle for liquid cheese until the hot holding unit is serviced or replaced. Hot holding units for hot TCS items must be maintained at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the Ortega Liquid cheese dispenser to be inadequately holding hot temperatures- see violations #21. Hot holding units must reach temperatures to hold TCS foods at or above 135F. Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to check that the unit is properly hot holding foods. Repair or replace unit.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple incidents of improper utensils storage:
1) Both the chopped tomatoes and onions contained single service bowls with no handles in the food.
2) The ice scoop handle was touching the ice in the drive-thru.
CORRECTED. The single service bowls in the produce were discarded, and the ice scoop was moved to its holder. Scoops with handles should be stored so that the nonfood contact surfaces (the handle, which is touched) is stored above or separate from the food to prevent bare-hand contamination. Do not reuse bowls as scoops, as there is no differentiation between the food-contact surface and the hand contact surface. Either Immediately discard bowl after use, or obtain scoops with handles for produce.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed a significant accumulation of burnt food debris on the interior of the quesadilla grill, and grease on the outside of the quesadilla grill. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Old food debris could serve as a source of contamination for RTE foods. Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to inspect quesadilla grill cleaning.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of dust on the fans in the walk in cooler. Clean fans at a frequency to prevent potential contamination of foods in storage of the walk in cooler (see violation #15).
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
PIC did not have Allergen training available. They stated they’ve passed it before, but had trouble printing. Allergen training expires every 3 years. Ensure all CFMs take allergen awareness training every 3 years. Maintain records on file to be available upon request during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed rusting on the shelves of the kitchen’s standing freezer. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth, and easily cleanable. Reseal or replace shelving by the next routine inspection.

citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Two sections of the salad prep cooler are observed with the lids wedged open by items inside. Internal temperatures for lettuce and house made mayo based sauces are observed in the 51F-52F range. These items were brought into this section approximately 4 hours ago.
