title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no paper towels at the hand washing sink. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed paper towels at the hand washing sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for handwashing only, and are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed facility’s sanitizer bottle “bleaching out”- meaning the concentration of Chlorine bleach in the bottle was at a concentration greater than 200ppm. CORRECTED- the bottle was diluted to an approved concentration of 200ppm. Ensure sanitizing solutions intended for food contact surfaces are at a concentration recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm in the case of Cl bleach).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed an open container of half and half creamer with no date marking. The PIC did not know when the container was opened. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the half and half. Ensure all temperature control for food safety items (TCS) are marked with the date they are open are prepared. TCS items must be used or discarded within seven days after opening; with the day they are opened counted as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed a bottle containing a clear liquid to have no label. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the bottle as “bleach.” Ensure bottle containing clear liquids are labeled with their contents if they are taken from their original container to avoid potential contamination of food items.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed after properly washing hands the PIC turned off the faucet with their bare hands and dried their hands using a multi-use wiping cloth. The PIC was instructed to dry hands with single-use paper towels and use the paper towel as a barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure that employees always wash hands according to the correct hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed a carton of raw eggs stored over cucumbers in the standing double door cooler. The PIC was educated and the eggs were moved onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below any ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Sanitizer solution at the three compartment sink was observed to have a concentration of less than 50ppm (Cl). The sanitizer solution also contained soap. CORRECTED- Provided education to the food employee, who remade the sanitizer solution to a concentration of 100ppm (Cl). Ensure sanitizer solutions are prepared using only sanitizer (chlorine) and water- no soap.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed various in-house mayo-based sauces sitting on the counter at room temperature. The PIC said that they keep the sauces on the counter for lunch and then put the sauces back inside of the cooler after lunch. The inspector educated about the danger of leaving temperature control for safety (TCS) foods at room temperature for long periods of time and then putting them back inside of the cooler for future use. The inspectors and PIC discussed possible solutions. The recommended solution is using a time-as-control system where only small amount of sauce are brought out of the cooler and any leftover sauce are discarded after four hours. This system allows the sauces to be left on the counter for convenient use during preparation. The inspectors will return on 10/15/2025 to check that the TCS sauces are being stored correctly.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed several prepared foods (i.e, various seafood salads) were observed in the prep cooler bottom without proper date marking. The PIC stated that the foods had been prepared yesterday and they will be used for several days. During the inspection the salads were date marked. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum (the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1, food is discarded after 6 additional days).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several roaches alive (slow moving) and dead at the facility. The number of roaches has significantly decreased from the last routine inspection; however, the PIC must continue to prioritize cleaning, covering foods, eliminating pest entrance points, and other pest control methods. They should also continue with routine visits from their pest control provider. The inspector will spot check the facility before the next routine inspection to ensure that the facility is taking proper pest control methods.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed utensils at the wait station stored with the food contact surfaces facing outwards. The waitress was educated and the utensils were inverted so the handles faced outwards. Ensure that utensils are always stored to prevent the contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 

(1) The debris inside of the sushi prep cooler bottom (currently not-functioning). 

(2) The debris inside of the mini cooler below the sushi prep station. 

(3) The debris on the trays holding clean dishes by the triple sink. 

(4) The buildup of grease and other debris on the handle of the toaster oven. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) at the facility has not completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the CFPM completes the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items were out of proper cold holding temperature. The ambient temperature of the open air cooler was initially observed at 51F, and went down to 41F (no indication of defrost on cooler). As a result, multiple TCS items were probed for internal temperatures:
1) Three cheeseburgers were probed at temperatures of 48(X2) and 45F.
2) Three Chobani yogurts were probed at 48(X2) and 47F.
3) Two steak and jalapeno burritos were probed at 49 and 51F.
4) Two beef and bean burritos were probed at 48 and 46F.
5) One country fried chicken was probed at 47F.
6) One smoked ham and turkey club was probed at 48F.
7) Two smoked ham and swiss sandwiches were both probed at 48F. 
8) Two egg and sausage burritos were probed at 50 and 51F.
9) One Italian wrap was probed at 48F.
10) One chicken and Ceasar wrap was probed at 47F.
11) One buffalo chicken wrap was probed at 47F.
12) Two packaged of creamer in the dispenser were also observed to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Creamers were voluntarily discarded.

Three items not listed in numbers 1-11 were probed from the open air cooler and had internal temperatures below 41F. CORRECTED- due to all of the previously mentioned foods being prepackaged, they had to be discarded to be probed. The inspector notified the person in charge (PIC) of the need to probe and discard foods due to high temperature readings. The PIC stated they check cooler temperatures at the end of the shift daily. Inspector encourages use of a daily temperature log to monitor temperatures for cold holding units. Ensure TCS foods are kept at or below 41F to prevent the growth of microorganisms that may cause foodborne-illnesses.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed the creamers at the dispenser to not contain date marking. The PIC stated they were not certain when they were last refilled, but it is likely that it has been over seven days. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded creamers. Ensure TCS foods that require opening are marked with the date they are opened, and used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed multiple chemicals (washer fluid, glass cleaner, and exhaust fluid) being stored over drinks in the back storage. Chemicals should be stored under or away from food products to prevent potential contamination of foods. Inspector will return on 10/14/25 to ensure chemicals are stored below or away from foods.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Multiple flies (both dead and live) were observed throughout the facility. Flies were observed near the front register, soda machines, and on the shelving of the open air cooler. The PIC was unsure of who the facility uses for pest control. Flies pose a risk of contaminating food sources. If the facility uses a pest control operator, reach out to schedule an appointment, or obtain pest control devices. If there is no Pest Control Operator, ensure one is obtained. Inspector will return on 10/23/25 to check how the flies are being managed.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed single service cups stored on the ground. Single service articles should be stored at least 6 inches above the ground to protect food contacts surfaces from contamination, and also prevent the attraction of pests. Ensure all single service items are stored on facilities’ shelving.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of debris: 
1) Mold is growing and accumulating on the sides and back of the self-dispensing soda machines.
2) Mold was observed along the individual line shelving of the drink coolers. 
Clean and sanitize nonfood contact surfaces at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of mold, or other contaminants. Items may be wiped with a clean sanitizer cloth, power washed, or washed in the facility’s three compartment sink.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspector observed water pooling on the floor behind the soda machines. The source of the leak appeared to be a carbonator below the soda machines. Contact supplier to service the connection line to prevent leakage. Pooling water may attract pest and allow for the growth and harborage of microorganisms that thrive in high levels of water activity.
citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed two wet mops on the floor. Discussion between the PIC and inspector occurred regarding storage of mops. Mops should be stored in a position that allows air drying to occur. Mops that are unable to air dry harbor bacteria that feed on the fats broken down by soaps and detergents. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows for air drying in the future.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a square hold about 10”x10” to the right of the mop sink, as well as a circular hole in the wall to the right of the soda machines in the back. The hole next to the mop sink allows for access to water shut off. Exposed drywall or wood should be painted or sealed to prevent the entry of water. Cover circular opening, and obtain a door or seal/ paint the drywall next to the mop sink. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair. Ensure repairs are made with nonabsorbent materials; smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of soda splash and debris in the wall behind and floor below the soda boxes. This sugar rich debris attracts and helps to harbor pests (see violation #38). Facility should clean at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Two containers of ground beef were observed in the walk-in cooler at 46F and 48F, probed. Both PIC and a food employee indicated that all foods in the walk-in cooler had been there since yesterday and that no foods prepared today had been placed in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the out of temperature ground beef. Ensure time/temperature controlled for safety foods are held at 41F or below at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The walk in cooler was observed with an ambient temperature of 45F using inspector’s probe thermometer. Ground beef was observed at 47 and 48F and was voluntarily discarded. Other foods were observed at 42-45F (tomato sauces, pizza dough, broth). PIC stated that the cooler is approximately 40F when he arrives in the morning, but based on inspectors observations the cooler struggles to maintain that temperature when the door is opened frequently during the day. The walk-in cooler needs to be serviced. Inspectors will follow up on 10/15/25 to see that the cooler is maintaining foods at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Food handler training
comment:
There were two employees working at the time of the inspection, one employee was a certified food protection manager and the other employee did not have any food certificates. Discussed the need of at least a food handler certificate if handling food, drinks, or clean dishes. Be sure that all employees obtain a food handler certificate within 30 days of hire if not already a certified food protection manager. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed interior of the ice machine to be soiled with debris. Ensure staff clean and sanitize interior of the ice machine as frequently as necessary to prevent a buildup of debris. A follow-up will be conducted on 10/14/2025 (accounting for the weekend and holiday) to ensure the ice machine has been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed bottled beer stored in ice used as food. Inspector discussed the risk of cross-contamination with PIC, and beer was removed. The ice in the chest will be removed and replaced prior to use. Ensure beers are stored in available coolers/freezers or in designated ice baths NOT to be used as food.
citation_text: 3-303.11 Ice Used as Exterior Coolant, Prohibited as Ingredient. After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed the food handler’s certificate on file for the present employee to be expired as of 2022. Ensure all employees have a valid food handler’s certificate at all times of operation behind the bar. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. 

The bathrooms in the facility do not have self closing doors. The items were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to install self closers prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure all restroom are self closing in this facility.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The facility is observed to be in a poor state of cleanliness and is continuing to worsen - many of the violations present during today’s inspection are REPEAT violations. There does not seem to be a cleaning schedule in place that is being followed. Floors, walls, drains, and equipment are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. There are a number of cleaning repeat violations that have not been corrected since previous inspections. Attention to cleaning is needed in the facility. The poor state of cleanliness has caused soil and molds to accumulate throughout food storage and preparation locations and this poses a threat of contamination to food. A follow-up is scheduled for 11/10/2025 to ensure that cleaning is being done, the facility is improving in cleanliness, and that a regular cleaning schedule has been implemented and is being FOLLOWED.
citation_text: 2-102.11(C)(8) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (C) Responding correctly to the inspector's questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include: (8) Describing the relationship between the prevention of foodborne illness and the management and control of the following: (a) Cross contamination, (b) Hand contact with READY-TO-EAT FOODS, (c) Handwashing, and (d) Maintaining the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT in a clean condition and in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee turn off the faucet with their bare hands after handwashing. CORRECTED- A discussion occurred with the person in charge (PIC) to review proper hand washing procedures with all employees. Failure to use a barrier to turn off the faucet recontaminates hands. Ensure all food handlers use a barrier to turn off faucets after hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed the handwashing sink in the back kitchen prep area to be out of soap. CORRECTED- The PIC replaced the soap and was educated that all handwashing sinks should be supplied with soap at all times. Ensure all sinks used for hand washing are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels for proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed a blender in the basin of the hand washing sink at the bar. CORRECTED- The blender was moved and education with the PIC occurred over hand washing sink usage. Handwashing sinks should only ever be used for their intended purpose of handwashing. Ensure handwashing sinks are available at all times for hand washing to incentivize employees to wash their hands.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The racks in the walk-in cooler holding various food items were observed to have mold accumulation and dead flies on them. A follow up is scheduled for 10/17/2025 to ensure that these racks have been cleaned. Food should be protected from cross contamination by cleaning equipment and utensils.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- There were opened containers of food in the bottom of the prep coolers and the standing cooler in the kitchen. The fan in the standing cooler is observed to be soiled, which could contaminate the container of uncovered food. All food should be protected from contamination when in an open-air cooler by being covered.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The facility is in a poor state of cleanliness. Floors, walls, equipment, and drains are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. A follow up is scheduled for 10/17/2025 to make sure that cleaning is happening in the facility. The lack of cleaning and build up of soil residue on floors, walls, and equipment is posing a risk of contamination to food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

comment: Inspector observed the multi-use drink dispensing nozzle at the server station to contain an accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- The nozzle was removed to be cleaned and sanitized by kitchen staff. citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The facility has a prep cooler that is not working and they are currently using an ice bath to keep items in cold holding. A follow up is scheduled for 10/17/2025 to ensure that the cooler has been repaired. Ensure that an ice bath is used for cold holding and that the temperatures of the food are regularly checked to make sure they are being properly held at 41F or under until the cooler is repaired.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
There are a number of nonfood contact surfaces that are observed to be in need of cleaning in the facility. More attention is needed to cleaning. The following nonfood contact surfaces are in need of cleaning:

citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

comment: The dispenser parts of the soda machine were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(2) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT,UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (2) In toilet rooms.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility is observed to be using a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer and does not have test strips for it. Every sanitizer that is used in a facility should have test strips for it. A follow up is scheduled for 10/17/2025 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The rubber seal on the front side of the chest freezer in the baking room is observed with black mold growth beginning. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The location was cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was an accumulation of a pink substance on the outer baffles of the ice machine in the new kitchen space. Shown to the PIC and the baffles were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that baffles of the ice machine are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handler licenses to be present upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, staff will all take steps to get licenses . Ensure all members of staff that handle food have the required food handlers license. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: No bleach or biohazard kit was available during today’s inspection. Norovirus signage is posted above the hand washing sink, however no spill kit is available for cleanup. Obtain a biohazard spill kit, or simple bleach (no “non-splash” or scented) with an EPA registration number by 10/17/25.
citation_text: 2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.

The back door also is allowing strips of light enter along the left perimeter of the door. Ensure all gaps and repaired or closed by the next routine inspection to protect against the entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is a leak observed to be coming from under the triple sink. It is currently leaking into a bin. Due to the inspector’s availability and the facility’s hours, a follow up is scheduled for 10/14/2025 to ensure that the leak has been repaired. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: The only Certified Food Protection Manager, also the only employee who handles food, isn’t performing duties as necessary. The individual isn't properly educated on ware-washing (including wash, rinse, sanitize), date marking, prevention of cross contamination, creation of sanitizer buckets, handwashing, etc. During the visit, the inspector demonstrated how to create sanitizer solutions and how to accurately test the concentration. Overall, the CFPM failed to demonstrate basic knowledge of food safety. The inspector will bring helpful handouts for the facility to use as reference for preventing the spread of food borne-illness on the follow date of 10/16/2025.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

comment: Inspector observed a slight accumulation of soil debris on the interior of the ice machine located in the facility’s basement. Food contact surfaces should be maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of foods (ice). Ensure ice machine is emptied and the interior is cleaned and sanitized by 10/15/25.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed two opened containers of creamer without date marking. CORRECTED- the PIC knew when the creamer downstairs was opened and placed the corresponding date on the container. The creamer upstairs was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) items are marked with their opening date if held for more than one day. Use or discard TCS items within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector and PIC observed multiple ants on the soda nozzle in the upstairs satellite bar. CORRECTED- the PIC cleaned and sanitized the soda nozzle, and stated that it should have been soaking. Ensure pest control is obtained (or verified) and monitored to prevent the contamination of drinks and garnishes.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed neither of the upstairs bathroom doors to contain self-closers. Provide self closers on all restroom doors to prevent the contamination of potable beverages.
citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: (SECOND REPEAT) Inspector observed the floor at the back walk-in-cooler to contain spots of bare wood, as well as chipping into the surface of the floor near the door. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Wood is highly absorbent and may allow for the entry and harborage of mold. Seal or repair floors by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers certificates during today’s inspection. All employees who handle food or drinks must obtain a Food Handlers card; and renew it every three years. Course completion reviews safe food handling practices and cold holding temperatures, among other important food safety standards. Ensure all bar tenders obtain a Food Handlers certificate, and maintain a copy on file to be made available during future routine inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: (Repeatx2) Observed mold accumulation to be present on the caulking to the right of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being checked regularly for black mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employee turn off faucet without using a barrier. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing techique, employee rehashed hands. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off faucet to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
citation_text:
3-201.11(B) Compliance with Food Law. (B) FOOD prepared in a private home may not be used or offered for human consumption in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

This facility is licensed as a Class-III (low risk) facility. The complaint stated that they were serving food prepared at home to customers. This was confirmed by the PIC during this inspection who appeared unaware that this is not allowed. The distinction between a private event and serving to the public was made. Education was conducted and they are instructed to either upgrade their risk classification to Class-II (medium risk) or pull temporary event permits moving forward. In either situation the food would need to be prepared on site. This situation is considered corrected with education to the PIC. The current practice is being ceased at this time.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There were a couple leaks dripping from a pipe above the right table of the dish machine. The facility is aware of the leaks and is in the process of repairing the leaks. The facility mentioned that the ice machine on the second floor is causing the leaks in the kitchen area. In the meantime, the facility is instructed to place a bucket underneath the drip to catch contaminated water. A follow-up will be scheduled for 10/8/2025 to ensure that leak is repaired and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The spray bottle in the meat room would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation showed that the dispensing machine was not dispensing at correct concentration. The bottle was refilled from a different machine in the facility to correct the immediate violation. A check of the machine will be conducted on the scheduled follow up in ten days related to flies in the facility (refer to line item #38).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives in the produce prep area are observed with remaining food debris on them and in storage in the knife rack. Per the PICs these knives are damaged (observed chipped) and are being discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are thoroughly cleaned and sanitized prior to storage in the facility.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple locations in the facility are observed with gnats/fruit flies/drain flies. Locations include: 1) the dairy mop sink; 2) the trash can in the produce area; 3) the mop sink by the back receiving door. The PICs were shown and instructed to contact pest control for maintenance. Ensure that all pests are removed from the facility and the facility is maintained free of pests moving forward.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment:
(REEPAT) 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple partially consumed drinks are observed throughout the stock areas of the facility. The PICs were shown and discarded the items during this inspection to correct. Ensure that employee foods are only consumed in areas that do not allow for possible food contamination.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspectors observed the Certified Food Manager Certificate (CFM) on file to have expired in March of this year. The person in charge (PIC) stated that they have not retaken the test since then. Inspector provided PIC with a handout on accredited institutes through which they may retake the exam. A CFM must be on site at all times during which food is being prepared or handled. The presence of a CFM helps to oversee proper food handling and cold holding temperatures to ensure facility is in compliance with safe food handling and preparation. Retake the test by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The PIC was unable to produce signed Employee Reporting Agreements during today’s inspection. The inspector provided the PIC with a blank copy of Sangamon County Department of Public Health’s Employee Reporting Agreement. The inspector will return on 10/16/25 to ensure all employees have signed and read the agreement. Ensure these documents are kept on file to be produced during inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed multiple items (pork belly, Mackerel, Tilapia) to have torn packaging, or be outside of their packaging in the sliding chest coolers & freezers. CORRECTED- items were re-wrapped. Ensure all temperature control for safety (TCS) food items that are packaged on site retain their seal to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.[Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspectors observed the sliding chest cooler in front of the food prep area to not contain an ambient thermometer. CORRECTED- the PIC added an ambient thermometer to the cooling unit. Ensure all cooling units contain an ambient thermometer to measure the temperature at the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility ensure all cooling units are working properly to hold items at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: 1) Inspectors observed mouse droppings on the floor and between boxes in the back dry storage area (shipping container). 
2) Inspector also observed a dead bug on a noodle package on the top shelf of the open air cooler. CORRECTED- this item was removed from service by the PIC.

The facility uses Sonny Adams for Pest Control once monthly. Droppings should be cleaned up, but large pallets of food will need to be moved to properly clean. Contact pest control operator, and monitor the area for evidence of pest after clean up, and check shipments for pests during delivery.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspectors observed a significant amount of brown rice being stored in a cardboard box, with an open top in the back dry storage area. Foods in dry storage should be completely covered in a food-grade package or container to prevent the contamination of food. This storage method also may attract pests (see violation #38). Ensure foods are protected from contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed a bare wood countertop over the triple sink. Wood is highly absorbent and may allow for the entry and harborage of mold. Seal or paint this shelving unit to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
The PIC was unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates during today’s inspection. Three people were observed to be packaging food during today’s inspection. Ensure all workers who handle or prepare food have and maintain their Food Handler’s Certificate every 3 years. Food Handler’s must have a certificate on file within 30 days of hire. Ensure these documents are available upon request during future inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket along the cook-line tested below 100ppm (quat). The sani solution was changed and retested at 200ppm to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are testing at the manufacturer's recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The gap in between the triple sink and the wall is need of recaulking. The current caulk is filled with debris and must be repaired. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are sealed to avoid buildup of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of the hood system above the fryers were observed with a buildup of grease debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. In between professional cleanings, be sure to manually clean baffles as often as necessary to avoid buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning in the following areas:
- Floors throughout the kitchen (underneath and behind equipment)
- Outer surfaces of equipment
- Walls and ceilings throughout the entire facility
When time permits, be sure to clean physical facilities at a frequency to prevent buildup of grease and food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Inspectors observed a build up of ice in the walk-in cooler at the bottom of the door of the walk-in freezer. A build up of ice was also observed behind the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspectors that the building up will be cleaned. Ensure that the build up is clean to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

 Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Inspector observed a staff member shutting off the sink without using a barrier after handwashing. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff members remember to use a barrier after to shut off the faucet in order to avoid recontaminating their hands. 


Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A THRICE REPEAT VIOLATION. There was no sanitizer bucket (s) available on the cook line at the beginning of today’s inspection. Discussed with PIC. The sani bucket was made immediately. The final measured of the sanitizer concentration was 200 ppm. Ensure that sani buckets are made at the appropriate temperature at all times during food prep.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector observed several food items in the walk-in cooler not properly date marked. Some of the items are but not limited to an opened jug of milk, sauces, dumplings fillings, cooked meat, and etc. PIC was made aware and education was carried out. Ensure that all food items are properly dated when they are being stored for future use. 


Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION.The caulking on the handwashing sink by the pass through window at the front of the cook line was observed in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned handwashing sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.113 Inspector observed multiple mop heads stored improperly in the utility sink. Education was carried out and the mop heads were stored properly. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a way that allows them to air dry and discourage the growth of bacterial cultures.

Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the handwashing sink by the standing freezer in the back area is observed in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned handwashing sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The back door of the establishment was observed propped open upon arrival. The PIC mentioned that the facility baked cookies earlier in the morning and the door was propped open to allow fresh air inside. The door was closed to correct the violation. Ensure that outer doors are never propped open, unless there are effective methods to prevent the entry of unwanted pests and insects.
citation_text: 6-202.15(D) Outer Openings, Protected. (D) Except as specified in (B) and (E) of this section, if the windows or doors of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, or of a larger structure within which a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT is located, are kept open for ventilation or other purposes or a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT is not provided with windows and doors as specified under (A) of this section, the openings shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) 16 mesh to 25.4 mm (16 mesh to 1 inch) screens; (2) Properly designed and installed air curtains to control flying insects; or (3) Other effective means.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no hand soap to be present at bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was refilled. Ensure soap is present at all hand sink to ensure proper hand washing is practiced.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be kept past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled and discarded. Ensure any TCS item is kept no longer than 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed employee bare hand lettuce going onto a cooked pizza. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper glove wear practices. Ensure any ready to eat foods are properly handled by employees.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed tubing to be in contact with ice at bar. Discussed with PIC, plans are in place to move hose unit to one ice bin so the other can be used. Facility will be using a separate ice bin for ice at the bar. Ensure tubing is not in contact with ice.
citation_text: 4-204.16 Beverage Tubing, Separation. Except for cold plates that are constructed integrally with an ice storage bin, BEVERAGE tubing and cold-plate BEVERAGE cooling devices may not be installed in contact with stored ice.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up at bar or kitchen. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer buckets were set up and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure sanitizer solution is set up and available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

1) Both bathrooms have ceiling tiles of the acoustic type. These are not smooth and easily cleanable and need to either be replaced with smooth and easily cleanable tiles or made smooth and easily cleanable via paint or a sealant. Do this prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces in the facilities where moisture can accumulate. 2) The hand sink in the left bathroom is pulling away from the wall and exposing a gap. Previous inspections had this as having a work order in approximately two years ago. This situation needs to be remedied prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a strainer and lemon in the handwashing sink- indicating that it’s being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- the strainer was moved. Cease this practice. Rinse sink may be emptied and used for this purpose, or the facility can use a bucket. Hand washing sinks should be used for handwashing only. A blocked hand washing sink is likely to deter hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces soiled with debris:
1) The front baffles of the ice machine
2) The holder for both soda nozzles at the bar. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) cleaned and sanitized both soda gun holders. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch.
- A follow up will occur on 10/15 to check the ice machine.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer compartment of the bar’s triple sink to be measuring at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia (quat). CORRECTED- PIC remade sink to a concentration of 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer solution is made at a frequency to maintain the concentration of sanitizer as recommended by the manufacturer's label. Until violation #50 is corrected, let the sanitizer water cool before adding quat tablets.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
