comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of food debris and splash on the interior sides and top of the facility’s microwave. Nonfood contact surfaces can serve as a source of contamination for ready to eat foods. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of food debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: After observing a hot water temperature at the sanitizing sink, the inspector noted the cold water faucet on the right hand side of the bar’s triple sink to not be dispensing cold water. The water in the rinse and sanitize basins was probed at 140F and 132F respectively. Skin submerged in water that is 132F+ could cause a 3rd degree burn within 15 seconds, and water that is 140F+ could cause 3rd degree burn within 5 seconds. The lack of cold water poses a safety risk to food handlers. The high water temperature also increases the rate at which sanitizer dissipates, making it harder for sanitizing solution to hold a proper concentration of 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia. A follow up will occur on 10/15/25 to ensure the water heater and plumbing have been inspected and repaired by a LICENSED plumber.
citation_text: 5-104.11 System. Water shall be received from the source through the use of: (A) An APPROVED public water main; or (B) One or more of the following that shall be constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW:  (1) Nonpublic water main, water pumps, pipes, hoses, connections, and other appurtenances, (2) Water transport vehicles, or (3) Water containers. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Multiple surfaces in the kitchen were observed to contain gaps and exposed bare wood:
1) The East wall has no dry wall, and is entirely made of exposed bare wood. 
2) There is a gap between the North and East walls (next to the light switch). 
3) The West side of the bar (under the counter) contains bare wood. 
Paint or seal these areas to prevent the entry and harborage of microorganisms, which may contaminate food. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Gaps between the wall and coving exist on the Southern wall of the kitchen. There is NO coving on either the North or West walls of the kitchen. Reseal and provide coving/ trim to these areas to prevent the growth and harborage of mold by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no soap available at the bar handwashing sink at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) placed hand soap at the sink. Ensure hand washing sinks are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels (or a high velocity hand dryer) to incentivize proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no probe thermometer available at the facility. CORRECTED- PIC found a probe thermometer during inspection. All facilities heating temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods should have a probe thermometer available to measure internal temperature of foods to ensure foods are reaching temperature benchmarks.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed staff going through coolers disposing off TCS items held past 7 day date marking maximum, Discussed with PIC, date marking education was provided and remaining TCS items were pulled and discarded. Ensure all TCS items are properly date marked and pulled after their 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed multiple food items kept in walk in cooler and freezer to be resting on a pan on floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were moved to at least 6 inches off floor. Ensure all food items are stored at least 6 inches off of floor.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice machine to be soiled with black mold. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be emptied and properly cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, items were moved to stove and reheated to 165F. Ensure all TCS foods being hot held are kept at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the 2 prep coolers in the pizza prep area have significant food splash running down the cooler doors. Discussed with PIC, areas will be cleaned. Ensure facility is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to need replaced in the following areas:
1) Triple sink to the right of dish machine. (Repeat)
2) Mop sink. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring caulking.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to don gloves without washing their hands. CORRECTED- The employee and PIC were educated that proper handwashing needs to be done prior to putting gloves on. Ensure that employees are following the proper handwashing procedure prior to putting gloves on.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The water to the mobile unit was not plugged in and water was not accessible at the sinks at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The PIC plugged the pump in and stated that it is usually plugged in, but that he had to move the truck. The PIC was educated that the mobile unit cannot operate without running water and that the pump ALWAYS needs to be plugged in.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was not a sanitizer bucket made at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- A Chlorine sanitizer bucket was made and tested at the correct concentration of 100ppm. The PIC was educated that there must always be ready-to-use sanitizer during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: The PIC stated that he drains his waste water in the storm drains or at a restaurant in New Berlin. CORRECTED- The PIC was educated that waste water needs to be drained at an approved sewage drainage facility. Ensure that waste water is properly disposed of.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector probed heavy cream in the beverage cooler of the facility. Heavy cream probed at 50F. It and another carton of half and half were discarded immediately by the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are always kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
Inspector observed the beverage cooler to not be holding food at 41F or below. See violation 22 for foods. Inspector originally observed the cooler holding food at ~50F. Inspector watched PIC discard food, and then had the cooler closed and left until the end of the inspection. At the end of the inspection, the cooler was holding ~49F. Ensure cooler is serviced so that it holds food at or below 41F.

Inspector will return 10/09/2025 to re-inspect cooler.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated on the importance of the proper hand washing procedure to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning a new pair of gloves. The employee had just finished handling a bleach solution that was too strong for food contact surfaces. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Ensure employees always wash their hands prior to donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee spraying cutting boards and other food contact surfaces with an unlabeled bottle of bleach solution. The solution was tested, and “bleached out” the test strip. Bleaching out the strip is an indicator that the solution is far stronger than the maximum indication of the strip, which is 200ppm. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer was far too strong and should not be used on food-contact surfaces. Quaternary ammonia tablets were used to prepare a new sanitizer solution. Ensure staff use test strips to measure the concentration of a sanitizing solution prior to spraying on food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple containers in the walk-in cooler (including cooked beef) to be missing a date mark. All time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must be marked with a date mark and discarded within 7 days of opening/preparation. Ensure all foods are marked prior to storing overnight in the walk-in cooler. A follow-up will be conducted on October 10, 2025 to ensure facility is in compliance for date marking.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
comment: Inspector observed skirt steak on the menu which is served undercooked. The menu had no consumer advisory statement, and there was no statement posted visibly in the facility. The PIC was informed of the need for a consumer advisory statement and signage was provided. Ensure this disclaimer is visible to the public at all times of undercooked or raw food service.
citation_text: 3-603.11(A) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (A) Except as specified in 3-401.11(C) and Subparagraph 3-401.11(D)(4) and under 3-801.11(C), if an animal FOOD such as beef, EGGS, FISH, lamb, milk, pork, POULTRY, or shellfish is served or sold raw, undercooked, or without otherwise being processed to eliminate pathogens, either in READY-TO-EAT form or as an ingredient in another READY-TO-EAT FOOD, the PERMIT HOLDER shall inform CONSUMERS of the significantly increased RISK of consuming such FOODS by way of a DISCLOSURE and REMINDER, as specified in (B) and (C) of this section using brochures, deli case or menu advisories, label statements, table tents, placards, or other effective written means.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed a spray bottle containing a bleach solution to be unlabeled. Education was conducted regarding labeling requirements for toxic materials and the bottle was labeled during the inspection. Ensure all toxic materials bear a legible label to avoid improper use.
citation_text: 7-101.11 Identifying Information, Prominence. Containers of POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS and PERSONAL CARE ITEMS shall bear a legible manufacturer's label.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspectors observed salmon in the walk-in cooler to be thawed in its original reduced oxygen packaging. The packaging bore a label indicating that the packaging had to be opened prior to thawing. Education was conducted regarding the risks of thawing fish in reduced oxygen packaging. The packages were opened during the inspection. Ensure staff are opening the packaging prior to thawing to prevent the growth of clostridium botulinum, the organism that causes botulism toxicity.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspectors observed a significant buildup of ice in the walk-in freezer on the ceilings, as well a slight accumulation on the air curtains and floors. The walk-in freezer must be de-frosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the walk-in freezer frost is removed by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspectors observed no chlorine test strips available in the facility. There was a chlorine sanitizer bottle in use which was far too strong for food contact surfaces. To prevent the misuse of toxic materials on food-contact surfaces, ensure there are test strips available and in use in the facility at all times. A follow-up will be conducted on October 10, 2025 to ensure the facility has all necessary test strips.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the interior of the microwave to be soiled with food debris. The hood system above the fryers was also observed to be soiled with grease and food debris. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the ceiling of the walk-in cooler to have a slow drip of water and an accumulation of mold in the seams of the paneling. Ensure the ceiling of the walk-in cooler is cleaned and repaired to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: One employee who was present during today’s inspection did not have a signed Reporting Agreement on file. CORRECTED- employee read and signed reporting agreement. All employees should read and sign an Employee Health Reporting Agreement within 30 days of hire to ensure that employee understands their responsibilities regarding reporting illnesses, or symptoms that could lead to Food-borne Illness. Ensure all employees have read and signed the Employee Health Reporting Agreement within 30 days of hire.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: At the start of today’s inspection, the handwashing sink at the bar was observed to be lacking paper towels. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) obtained paper towels. Ensure warm running water, soap, and paper towels are always available at hand washing sinks to ensure proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed chicken being stored above milk in the walk in cooler. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the chicken below the milk. Milk is considered a “ready to eat” (RTE) food item, which should always be stored above animal proteins to avoid cross contamination. Items should be stored according to cooking temperatures; with the items requiring the highest cooking temperature stored below items that require lower cooking temperatures to- no cooking.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of pink and black soil debris on the front baffles of the ice machine. PIC contacted the individual who works on their HVAC system to service the ice machine on 10/06. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of food items.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Multiple temperature control for food safety (TCS) items were observed to be cold holing over 41F. Items include chopped lettuce, sliced tomatoes, and onions- all of which probed at 47F. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded lettuce, tomatoes, and onions. The prep cooler is not holding TCS items at or below 41F, so PIC and inspector discussed using time as a control for food safety (TAC), or cold holding items on ice, until the prep cooler is serviced (see violation #33). Inspector discussed proper methods for cold holding on ice, as well as the 4 hour limit for TAC.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed two containers of marinara being held past their seven day limit (items were dated 08/27 and 09/20). CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded both containers of marinara. Ensure all TCS foods are used or discarded within seven days. The day items are prepared or thawed counts as day one.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the prep cooler to have an ambient temperature of 47F. PIC was notified, and a work order was placed to have the unit serviced. Ensure cold holding units are able to hold food items at or below 41F.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Multiple coolers throughout the facility were observed without ambient thermometers. CORRECTED- PIC moved extra thermometers into units lacking ambient thermometers. When placed correctly, ambient thermometers measure the temperature in the warmest part of the cooling unit. This helps the facility identify early on when cold holding units are out of temperature. Ensure all coolers (freezers do not require ambient thermometers as long as food is observed to be frozen solid) contain ambient thermometers, placed towards the front of the unit.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed multiple single service storage containers being stored on the floor in the dry storage area in the banquet room. PIC stated that shelving has been ordered to keep single service items off of the floor. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored at least 6 inches above the floor.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Nozzles of the fountain drink machine are observed soiled during this inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced all nozzles during this inspection with the back ups to correct. Per the PIC the nozzles are cleaned weekly. This should be more often as the needs of the facility require. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch at all times in the facility.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

The ambient air thermometer in the prep cooler is observed broken and non-functioning at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and placed another thermometer in the cooler to correct the violation. Ensure that all coolers have a correctly functioning thermometer available in them at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

1) Major ice and frost accumulation is observed in the walk in freezer. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and to clean often enough to maintain the area free of frost and ice. 2) The floor in the walk in cooler has filth accumulation in corners that needs to be clean more thoroughly. The PIC was shown and instructed review cleaning procedures and ensure that cleaning is taking place thoroughly and regularly moving forward.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Overall, the facility has significant improved with date marking. Staff appear to mostly monitor date marking of TCS foods, however, there were a few items that were past the seven day timeframe (date marked 9/17 and 9/18). These items include buffalo dip, various in house made sauces, sloppy joe, etc. Discussed with PIC and items were discarded. Ensure that any TCS foods that are held in house for longer than seven days are dated marked and discarded if not used within seven days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There were two packages of raw beef thawing at room temperature inside of the triple sink in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC proper thawing methods. The beefs were placed under running cool water, allowing for the water to cycle and drain off loose particles. When thawing in sinks, ensure that items are placed under running cool water and are completely submerged.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: An insect glue trap was observed hanging from the ceiling in the dish machine area. The glue trap was not directly placed over clean dishes, however, the trap contained a significant amount of dead flies and could possibly contaminate clean dishes during the warewashing process. Ensure that insect traps are placed in areas where food and/or food contact surfaces aren’t exposed to contamination.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a mini cooler to the left of the of the triple and a drawer cooler in the kitchen area that are no longer in service. The kitchen employees mentioned that the facility has no future plans to use the pieces of equipment. If pieces of equipment aren’t functioning properly and there’s no plan for usage in the future, then be sure to remove equipment from facility, as they can be considered as litter.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were several containers of uncovered items in the walk in cooler such as but not limited to meats, tomato sauce, broths, etc. All foods stored in coolers must bear a covering to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The chemical sanitizing dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The chemical bucket was changed and cycled at least 6 times before testing at 100ppm (CL).  Ensure that the dish machine tests at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Overall, the facility lacks proper date marking for TCS foods in the walk in cooler. These items include but aren’t limited to items containing cooked beef, pasta sauces, cooked noodles, and other various items. Discussed with PIC proper date marking and items were date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that any TCS foods held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: A container of cooked ground beef was dated 9/10/25 in the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC that all TCS foods can only be cold held for up to seven days before needing to be discarded. The PIC mentioned that the meat was prepared two days prior to the inspection. The proper date sticker was added to the container to correct the violation. Ensure that cooked meats are never held in house longer than 7 days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The ambient temperature of the walk in cooler was observed at 45F. Discussed having the walk in cooler serviced due to alarming ambient temperature. Ambient temperatures for cold holding should be 41F or below. PIC mentioned that the door of the cooler had been opened and closed recently, which has caused the cooler to increase in temperature. Ensure that cold holding equipment is capable of maintaining proper cold holding temperatures. Will follow-up on 10/9/2025.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The only allergen certificate available in house has expired (7/2025). Ensure that an allergen certificate is obtained and available by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11 Inspector observed the calking on the hand sink in the back room to be in disrepair. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspector tor that the sink will be caulked to the wall properly. Ensure that the caulking is done in a manner that provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Inspector observed a staff member not washing their hands at the hand sink before donning gloves and starting food prep. Staff had just come out of the bathroom and touched the door handle with their bare hands. Education was carried out and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff practice adequate handwashing before donning gloves during food prep. 


When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 Insoector observed mice droppings in the following locations. 
1. Under the shelves in the dry storage.
2. Droppings observed on top of the plastic covering of the single service containers in the dry storage.
3. Droppings observed on the floor behind the double doors cooler in the kitchen.
There were pest traps observed but no other signs of rodent presence. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the droppings would be cleaned and they will be on the lookout for any rodent or other pest activities. Ensure that the facility is checked on a regular basis to evaluate and eliminate the presence of any pest. 

(A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple cold held temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods in the open air cooler to have an internal temperature above 41F:
1) Hard boiled eggs had an ambient temperature of 51F, and probed at 45F. Three total packages of hard boiled eggs (two were in compliance) were probed for internal temperatures and voluntarily discarded by the person in charge (PIC). 
2) Two containers of Chobani yogurt were probed and one had an internal temperatures of 45F (the other had an internal temperature that was in compliance). Both containers were voluntarily discarded by the PIC.
3) Egg and dill salad sandwich and carrot cake had ambient temperatures of 48F. When probed they had internal temperature that were in compliance, however were discarded to be probed.
CORRECTED- probed items were discarded, and items in the open air cooler were pushed backwards. Ambient thermometers in the cooling unit show proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure all TCS items are monitored to be cold holding at 41F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed caulking around mop sink to contain an accumulation of black soil debris. Ensure caulking is cleaned and replace by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple employees switch tasks between food prep and handling monetary transactions or touching their sides without hand washing. CORRECTED- inspector modeled and discussed appropriate times to wash hands with the person in charge (PIC) and food handlers. A failure to wash hands before donning gloves allows contaminants on one’s bare hands to transfer to the food contact surfaces of the otherwise clean gloves. Ensure employees always wash hands before donning gloves and in between tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the front counter to have a concentration of 100 ppm quaternary ammonia (quat). CORRECTED- the PIC remade the sanitizer to a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary. Ensure sanitizing solutions are made at a frequency to hold the proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed strawberries and blueberries on the “toast line” to be out of temperature (strawberries probed at 61.8F and blueberries probed at 60F). PIC stated that both the strawberries and blueberries had been placed on the line around 8am (inspection began at 1pm- 5 hours past the items were taken from the cooler), and held on ice packs. CORRECTED- the blueberries and strawberries were voluntarily discarded by the operator. Inspector and PIC discussed using a different method for cold holding items on the toast line in the future- either ice, or implementing time as control (TAC). If TAC were implemented, items would be used or discarded every 4 hours. If using ice for cold holding, it is recommended that that be refreshed every 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: The handles of multiple in-use scoops at the smoothie prep station were observed touching the food powder. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the handles above the surface with a clean, gloved hand, and reminded food handlers to keep the handles above the food. Ensure that food with handles are always stored with the food contact surfaces in the food, and the handles are stored above the food to avoid bare hand contamination of food.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets on the double door cooler to be separating. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Replace or repair gaskets by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
1) Inspector observed food debris in the prep cooler as well as the standing freezer in the kitchen.
2) Inspector observed a significant accumulation of ice in the chest freezer. Routinely clean during defrost cycles.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer solution prepared in the facility during food preparation or service. Education was conducted and a spray bottle was prepared measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no available stem thermometer for confirming proper cook temperature for TCS foods. Education was conducted an a stem thermometer was acquired. Ensure thermometers are available at all times of food prep and service.
citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer prepared in the facility during food preparation and service. Education was conducted on sanitizer requirements and a spray bottle was prepared, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure a spray bottle is prepared at all times to ensure proper sanitization of food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no test strips available in the facility. Education was conducted and test strips were acquired. Ensure tests strips are available at all times to ensure proper sanitizer concentration.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Food handler stated the facility has been using the dish machine to sanitize dishes and other food contact surfaces. The facility was instructed to utilize the triple sink to wash and sanitize food contact surfaces until the heat sanitizing dish machine was serviced, AND the facility had a way to verify proper sanitizing temperatures are being reached until the dish machine. CORRECTED- Education occurred with the PIC, who was reminded that the dish machine is not to be used until proper heat sanitizing temperatures are reached, and the facility is able to verify proper sanitizing temperatures. The heat sanitizing dish machine took over 1 hour to heat up during the inspection. Ensure employees utilize the triple sink for sanitation OR wait until the dish machine reaches a minimum wash temperature of 160, and minimum rinse temperature of 180 to use the dish machine for heat sanitation.
citation_text: 2-103.11(L) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The designated person in charge (PIC) was unable to locate heat test strips during today’s re-inspection. They have ordered strips, and they have an invoice stating they have been delivered, but the facility could not produce the heat temperature test strips. Facilities that use heat for sanitation need heat test strips or a surface temperature dish plate to verify that the machine is reaching proper sanitizing temperatures.
citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The person in charge (PIC) had an expired Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) Certificate. Ensure CFPM is renewed and maintained every 5 years. A CFPM should be present during all times during which food is being handled or prepared.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The inspector observed the hand washing sink to contain a scoop and lid. CORRECTED- the inspector moved the items to wash hands. Education occurred with the Person in Charge (PIC) regarding hand sink availability. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing only, to incentivize hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: The iced coffee bags were observed without date marking. CORRECTED- the inspector asked the PIC when the coffee bags were opened. PIC stated they were opened when the new shipment came in on 09/22, and marked the bags with the corresponding date. Once temperature control for food safety (TCS) cold held items are opened, they must bear date mark to be used or discarded within 7 days time.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed ice machine cleaner to be stored over soda boxes in the back storage room. CORRECTED- the cleaner was moved away from the food products. Ensure chemicals are always stored below or away from food products to prevent a contamination of foods.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The PIC verified that the facility does not have ambient thermometers. Ambient thermometers (when properly positioned) display the temperature of the warmest part of the cold holding unit, which help the facility identify when the cold holding units are not properly working. Obtain ambient thermometers for cold holding units housing TCS foods (milk, cheese, eggs, meats) by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed multiple single service boxes to be stored on the ground; including cups, straws, and trays. CORRECTED- PIC moved single service boxes onto other boxes that were neither foods or food contact surfaces. Ensure single service articles are stored at least 6 inches above the ground to prevent potential contamination of food contact surfaces at all times.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the gaskets of multiple standing coolers to be in disrepair. The following coolers need their gaskets repaired or replaced. Those housing: water, Gatorade, Celsius, Ghost, Monster, and Mountain Dew. Ensure these repairs take place by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Facility is currently using Purell sanitizing wipes to clean food contact surfaces. To continue using Purell to sanitize food contact surfaces, the facility must obtain Purell test strips to verify that the solution is holding the proper sanitizing concentration. Either buy quaternary ammonia to sanitize food contact surfaces  (which the facility has test strips for), OR obtain and use Purell test strips.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed an accumulation of milk residue on the floor beneath the milk in the retail cooler. Increase the frequency at which this area is being cleaned to prevent the contamination of food contact and nonfood contact surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The facility only had a small amount of handwashing soap left and had no more available on the truck. CORRECTED- The PIC went to the store and obtained more handwashing soap. Ensure that there is always soap available at the handwashing sink to allow for proper handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was no soap available to wash dishes on the mobile unit. The PIC stated that they scrub the dishes using water and a scrub pad and then sanitize them. CORRECTED- The PIC was educated that the proper way to wash dishes is to wash, rinse, and then sanitize. They were educated that soap always needs to be available and is a crucial part of the warewashing process. Soap was obtained by the PIC to correct the issue. The sinks in the mobile unit are labeled wash, rinse, and sanitize. Ensure that there is always soap on the mobile unit and that dishes are being washed properly.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed a bag of hot dogs in the chest cooler to not be date marked. Discussed with PIC, and PIC date marked the bag of hot dogs. Ensure opened food items are date marked within 24 hours of opening and kept for only 7 days thereafter.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: At least two employees were observed touching faucet handles with bare hands after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with the PIC. Ensure that a barrier (paper towel) is used to operate faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee handling phone with gloved hands and then proceeded to handle food without changing gloves. Discussed with PIC. PIC ceased activity to correct the violation. If changing activities with gloved hands, be sure to switch to a fresh set of gloves and wash hands before doing so to prevent possible contamination of food items.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The bottom inner surface of a cooler along the cook-line was observed with soiled towels and also a strong odor due to spilled liquids. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspector observed the only employee present during today’s inspection to not have a Certified Food Protection Manager’s (CFPM) Certificate. CORRECTED- an additional employee with their CFPM arrived. A CFPM should be present at all times food is being prepared or served. Ensure a CFPM is present at all times food (that is not prepackaged) is being served.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Employees were unable to locate Employee Reporting Agreements, but did state they had signed them. Inspector will return on 10/07/25 to view Employee Reporting Agreements. Ensure they are on file and available at any time a future inspection may occur.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).[Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a biofilm accumulated around the soda nozzles. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) replaced the soda nozzles and took the ones that had been on the machine to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil residues, and to prevent contamination of ready to eat (RTE) food and drinks.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector and employees could not locate test strips that correspond with the sanitizer in the facility. The facility is using quaternary ammonia as their sanitizing solution, but have Chlorine test strips. Inspector will return on or before (if the facility obtains them before the follow up date) 10/07/25 to ensure that facility has test strips that correspond with their sanitizer solution.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the coving that seals the floor to the wall peeling from the wall underneath the electrical panel in the stock room. Reseal the coving to the wall to prevent entry of water, which could harbor mold.
2) Inspector observed a large hole cut in the drywall behind the soda boxes in the stock room. This hole exposes drywall edges and bare wood. Cover or repair this wall so that it is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed cracked and missing floor tiles in front of the self service soda station, as well as in the men’s restroom. Repair or replace tiles by the next routine inspection, so that surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen is obsrerved without soap (only hand sanitizer available). The PIC stated that when food handling was taking place that hand washing was taking place in the bathroom. Education was conducted and soap provided to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen is observed without paper towels. The PIC stated that when food handling was taking place that hand washing was taking place in the bathroom. Education was conducted and paper towels provided to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain food debris or chipping/ pitting:
1) 2 knives were stored in a ready to use position with food debris on them. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the knives to be cleaned and sanitized.
2) One spatula was chipped and contained pitting. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the item.
Ensure food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch, to prevent contaminating ready to eat (RTE) foods items. Equipment that contains pitting or breakage could potentially contaminate RTE foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed 2 bottles of milk in the Newborn room mini-fridge to be above recommended cold holding temperatures. Milk was probed at 48F.  Classroom teacher stated that the milk was brought in by the parent one hour prior to the temperature being taken. CORRECTED- Milk was moved into working refrigerator in the cafeteria. Ensure all TCS foods are held in units that are being cold held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the cold holding unit in the Newborn room to have an ambient temperature of 51F. Inspector will return on 10/07/25 to ensure that the cold holding unit has been repaired or replaced. Do not store TCS items in this mini-fridge until the food items can hold an internal temperature of 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed the cold holding units in the newborn and toddler rooms to not have ambient thermometers. CORRECTED- the PIC placed ambient thermometers in the front of the cold holding units. Ensure all cold holding units that contain TCS foods have an ambient thermometer in the warmest region to monitor the temperature of the unit.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed 3 doors to have a sizable gap in the bottom left corner. These doors are located at the kitchen loading zone, the cafeteria, and south hallway door between the classrooms and the cafeteria. These openings could allow for the entry of pests. Extend or replace door sweeps by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected.
