(A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed 2 different Food Handlers Certificates to be expired. Ensure Food Handlers Certificates are acquired within 30 days of hire, and renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the downstairs ice machine has an accumulation of debris inside. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The PIC stated that they clean the ice machine every six months, but the inspector suggests a more frequent cleaning schedule. The inspector will return on 10/6/2025 to check that the ice machine has been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not sanitizer available when the inspector arrived at the facility. During the inspection the triple sink was filled with sanitizer testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizing solutions are available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the ice scoop holder by the downstairs ice machine had an accumulation of soil residues. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The PIC began the process of cleaning the ice scoop holder during the inspection. Ensure that the ice scoop holder is always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that the employees either did not have food handler certificates or they are expired. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection (from an ANSI accredited program).

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed several ceiling tiles throughout the store are either missing or showing signs of water damage. Ensure that the missing or damaged ceiling tiles are replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to handle bread rolls. Discussed the need of glove usage when handling RTE (ready-to-eat) foods. The activity was ceased and correct on site. Ensure that gloves are always worn when handling RTE foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A box of shelled eggs was stored above cut tomatoes and sliced onions in the walk in cooler. Discussed and shown to PIC. The PIC placed the shelled eggs underneath the RTE foods (Ready-to-eat) to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored beneath RTE items to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm quat. Inspectors AM and SM prepared a sani bucket and tested it at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommendation to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Two containers of meat sauces stored in the warmer were probed at 118F and 104F. The PIC mentioned  that the sauces were placed in the warmer an hour and a half prior to the inspection. The facility was instructed to reheat the meat sauces (on stovetop) to the proper reheating temperature (at least 165F). Be sure that TCS food items are always held at 135F to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: The drinking straws in the bar area were observed unwrapped and stored in close proximity to consumers. Discussed with PIC proper storage for unwrapped straws. Ensure that unwrapped straws are either stored behind the counter where they area controlled by employees or purchase wrapped straws for consumers.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of re-caulking and repair: 
- missing floor tiles in front of dish machine 
- cove base along the bottom of the walls near the mop sink
- caulking along the back of the hand-sink along the cook-line

Ensure that these areas are maintained in good condition.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed a bowl of chicken in the WIC to be stored over ground beef. Cross contamination does not appear to have occurred. Discussed with PIC, and PIC moved the chicken below the ground beef. Facility has a storage order handout posted on the outside of the WIC. Ensure that food is stored in the correct order to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn’t any paper towels available at the handwashing in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Ensure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
(REEPAT) 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the bathroom is without acceptable soap options. The PIC was notified and stated that the bathroom was not for customers. title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

The fountain drink machine in the facility is not currently in use. The nozzles are still heavily soiled however and need cleaned. The PIC was notified and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all equipment is maintained clean at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Numerous ceiling tiles throughout the facility are missing and several more have water damage. The PIC indicated that they were in the process of repairing these items. title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) The baseboards in the bathroom are either missing or peeling away from the wall. Dust and mold are observed on the fan covers, ceiling and walls of the walk in cooler. The PIC is instructed to clean and to maintain it clean at all times moving forward. Ensure that the facilities are maintained clean at all times

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed ice in the basin of the hand washing sink at the start of today’s inspection- indicating that it was being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- the ice went down the drain as the inspector washed their hands. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing only, to incentivize hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Bare wood trim and walls were observed in the ice machine room. Floors, walls, and ceilings must be made smooth, and easily cleanable. Seal or paint bare wood to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed volunteers rinsing dishes and filling up buckets inside of the designated hand washing sink. The PIC was informed and will be educating all volunteers about proper sink usage. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the inside of the ice machine had an accumulation of debris. The PIC cleaned the ice machine to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residue and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed the facility did not have test strips available. The inspector provided the facility with chlorine test strips during the inspection. Ensure that test kits are always available to measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12. There was no active certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. PIC was the only employee with a CFPM certificate however, it had expired a couple weeks prior. PIC assured inspector that they would get enroll to get re-certify. Ensure that there is at least one active certified food protection manager present in facility during operation at all times. 

(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-201.11 Facility did not have any employee heath reporting agreement available during inspection. PIC said that the facility owner has the paperwork and was unable to be present. The facility owner later brought copies for the employees to sign. Ensure that every employee sign the employee health agreement to be in compliance with the law. 


(A)(1) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person In Charge, and Conditional Employees. Reportable Symptoms. (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. A FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE shall report the information in a manner that allows the PERSON IN CHARGE to reduce the RISK of foodborne disease transmission, including providing necessary additional information, such as the date of onset of symptoms and an illness, or of a diagnosis without symptoms, if the FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE: (1) Has any of the following symptoms: (a) Vomiting, (b) Diarrhea, (c) Jaundice, (d) Sore throat with fever, or (e) A lesion containing pus such as a boil or infected wound that is open or draining and is: (i) On the hands or wrists, unless an impermeable cover such as a finger cot or stall protects the lesion and a SINGLEUSE glove is worn over the impermeable cover, (ii) On exposed portions of the arms, unless the lesion is protected by an impermeable cover, or (iii) On other parts of the body, unless the lesion is covered by a dry, durable, tight-fitting bandage.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 There was no paper towels available at the hand sink on the cook line. PIC was made aware and the paper towel dispenser was refilled. Ensure that there are paper towels available at the hand sink at all times to ensure adequate handwashing is practiced.

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17 Inspector observed the following food items in the standing cooler without proper date marking. 
1. The proportioned oxtails in the standing cooler.
2. Beans and rice mix in the standing cooler.
PIC was made aware. PIC informed inspector that the food items mentioned were prep on Saturday 09/20 but due to the rush, they forgot to date the food items. PIC instructed one of the employees to properly date mark the food items. Ensure that any food items not used within 24 hours must be date marked appropriately. 

(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11 Inspector observed the following from the pre-opening. 
1. Unseal wood around the triple sink in the kitchen. 
2. Caulking on the triple sink is observed in disrepair.
3. The acoustic ceiling tiles above the mop sink has not been replaced from the previous-opening. 
Ensure that the relevant correction are made to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(h). There was no one within the facility that is a manager observed to have allergen training completed. PIC was educated that as a high risk establishment, at least one Certified food protection manager is required to have allergen training completed within the facility during operation. Ensure that the allergen training is completed to be in compliance with the law.


Allergen awareness training. (h) Any and all documents, materials, or information related to a restaurant or business allergen awareness training module is confidential and shall not be open to public inspection or dissemination and is exempt from disclosure under Section 7 of the Freedom of Information Act. Training may be conducted by any means available, including, but not limited to, online, computer, classroom, live trainers, remote trainers, and food service sanitation managers who have successfully completed an approved allergen training. Nothing in this subsection (h) shall be construed to require a proctor. Proof that a food service sanitation manager has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed a carton of eggs stored above a shelf of ready-to-eat foods (i.e., pizza sauce, ham, cooked meatballs) in the kitchen triple door cooler. The PIC was educated that eggs are a raw food and therefore must be stored below any ready-to-eat foods. The eggs were moved onto the bottom shelf during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always stored to protect against cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is a buildup of frost inside the downstairs freezers. The PIC was instructed to defrost the freezers to remove the buildup of frost. Ensure that the freezers are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a hand washing sink blocked by food trays. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the trays. Ensure handwashing sinks are available for use at all times to incentivize hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed a food handler who did not have a Food Handler Certificate. The PIC stated the employee has been here for 7 months. Ensure all employees who are handling or preparing food/ drinks at the facility obtain a Food Handler’s Certificate from an accredited institute within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The person in charge’s (PIC) Certified Food Protection Manger (CFPM) certificate has expired, as of this May. The PIC is scheduled to take their CFPM exam next month. Ensure a CFPM is present at all times food is being prepared or handled.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop sitting wet on floor of mop sink. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC, and mop was moved to proper storage hook on wall. Ensure that after use, mops are stored such that they can effectively drip-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food-contact surfaces in the facility to be in need of repair:
1. The shelving holding clean dishes, single-service containers, and the selves above the triple sink were observed rusted and in need of repair/replacement.
2. The triple sink ledge between the first and second sink basin was observed cracked and separated. The crevice which is created by the break is not easily cleanable. 

These areas which are not smooth and easily cleanable pose a hazard for bacterial accumulation and food-borne illness transmission. Ensure these areas are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

Inspector discussed repairs with PIC. The triple sink has an existing service ticket for repairs. Ensure all areas are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following areas in need of a deep cleaning:
1. Floor under stoves and fryers
2. Floors of dish area
3. Floors of walk-in cooler
4. Walls around dish area
5. Plumbing under triple sink

Facility is under new management. The new management has reached out for a quote to hire someone to deep clean the facility. Inspector recommends closing the facility for a day to move and clean around/under all equipment. Ensure facility has been deep cleaned prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the triple sink is not fully sealed to the wall. Ensure that the triple sink is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the small cooler on the counter storing walking taco toppings was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The cooler uses frozen ice and was not sufficiently cold holding during the inspection. The foods inside the cooler were shredded lettuce, marble cheese, sour cream, and salsa. The toppings were observed to have internal temperatures between 60-62F. They were put inside the cooler over four fours ago and therefore were voluntarily discarded during the inspection. The inspector and PIC discussed using a time-as-control (TAC) method for the walking tacos topping since they only require a small amount throughout the day. The PIC will be keeping the toppings for four hours and discarding any leftovers after the four hour TAC window ends. The inspector reminded the PIC that they must use a time keeping method to record the time when the food must be discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a significant amount of syrup and biofilm accumulated around the multi-drink nozzles at both the server station and the drive thru. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the outer portion of the nozzles to be cleaned and wiped with a sanitizer cloth. Due to the affixed nature of the nozzles, inspector recommends brushing the multi-drink nozzles with a cleaning and sanitizing solution nightly. Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch to prevent the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the strawberries in the drive thru cold holding well to be out of temperature. Strawberries had an ambient temperature of 50F, and probed at 47F. Their sticker time indicated they had been on an ice bath for 6+ hours. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the strawberries. Ensure TCS foods are cold held at or below 41F to prevent the growth of pathogens. Out of temperature items must be used or discarded within 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed 2 wet sanitizer cloths to be on the counter at the drive thru, as well as at the ice cream station’s triple sink. CORRECTED- PIC moved sanitizing cloths to sanitizer buckets. Wet textiles can allow for the growth and harborage of mold and other microorganisms. Ensure wet sanitizing cloths are stored in a sanitizer solution in between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
1) Inspector observed a significant amount of grease and food debris on the baffles and fire suppression systems of the hood vents above the fryers. Grease drips pose a threat on contamination on RTE foods, and also pose a fire hazard to the facility. Steam Power cleans the facility’s hood vent system quarterly. PIC stated the baffles are cleaned on a weekly basis.
2) The racks in standing “fryer cooking” cooler contain grease accumulation and rust. Paint/ seal, or replace the nonfood contacts surfaces by next routine inspection.
Ensure nonfood contacts surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: PIC was unable to produce Food Handler certificates for employees during today’s inspection. Employees should obtain their Food Handler’s Certificate within 30 days of hire, and renew their certificates every 3 years. Ensure all employees complete food handler’s certificate training, and retain records on file for verification during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed on two different occasions rinsing hands in the hand-sink without following proper handwashing procedures. The activity was ceased and a discussion was had on proper handwashing procedures to correct the violation. When washing hands, be sure to rinse hands first, then add soap and lather hands for at least 10-15 seconds, rinse hands again, dry hands with a disposable towel, and then use towel to turn off faucet handles. Ensure that proper cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Observed several TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) foods stored in a prep cooler (and standing cooler) without proper dating marking. These items include crab meat, crushed tuna, cream cheese, shrimp, spicy mayonnaise, etc. PIC mentioned that items were prepared yesterday and will be discarded today. Discussed with PIC that these TCS foods must be date marked if held in house over night. 
Day 1 counts as the day that the items are made. There are 6 additional days that the items can be held in house before it must be discarded. At the end of day 7, the items must be discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The PIC was beginning to food prep without having a sanitizer bucket available. The activity was ceased and the PIC was asked to create a sanitizer bucket. After preparing the bucket, the solution was tested at 200ppm(quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There was a glue insect trap placed directly over the triple, exposing clean dishes to possible contamination. There were at least five dead flies present on the trap. Discussed the need to place the trap in a different location to prevent insect fragments from falling onto clean dishes. Ensure that insects traps are placed in a manner that prevents contamination of food, food contact surfaces, dishes, and utensils.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn't a sanitizer solution available while food preparation was occurring. Discussed with PIC and a solution was created and tested at 400ppm (quat). Be sure that a sanitizer solution is available if food preparation is occurring to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

comment:
Several areas in the kitchen were observed accumulated with grease and/or food debris:
- floors and drains underneath the rotisserie ovens
- floors around both chicken fryers
- Sides of fryers

Ensure that cleaning occurs in these areas as frequent as necessary to prevent build up of grease and food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine was observed testing at 0ppm (CL). The facility was instructed to use the triple sink until the machine is functioning correctly. A follow-up is scheduled for 9/24/2025. Be sure that the dish machine is maintained at the proper concentration to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized effectively.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There were a couple leaks dripping from a pipe above the right table of the dish machine. The facility is aware of the leaks and is in the process of repairing the leaks. The facility mentioned that the ice machine on the second floor is causing the leaks in the kitchen area. PIC expects to have the leaks repaired tomorrow. In the meantime, the facility is instructed to place a bucket underneath the drip to catch contaminated water. A follow-up will be scheduled for 9/19/2025 to ensure that leak is repaired and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of pizza sauce and a container of sausages dated 8/30/2025 in the walk in cooler. Items considered Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food (TCS) are to only be held in house for 7 days and discarded if 7 days are exceeded. PIC discarded items to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS are never held in house for longer than 7 days.
