The facility has CFB Steam Power for servicing the hood system, however, the baffles are able to be cleaned manually in a ware-washing sink or dish machine. Ensure that hood baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to avoid grease buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall behind the wash sink (across from fryers) is in need of re-caulking. The old caulk was observed pulling from the wall. Ensure that gaps are caulked properly to prevent debris buildup in hard to reach places.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: A ground beef roll was observed thawing in a sink with plugged water. The PIC unplugged the sink and provided running water to correct the violation. If using the running water method for thawing, be sure to never plug sink so that water is never at a stand still and continuously flowing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of the hood system (above the fryers) were observed heavily accumulated with grease debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. The facility has CFB Steam Power for servicing the hood system, however, the baffles are able to be cleaned manually in a ware-washing sink or dish machine. Ensure that hood baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to avoid grease buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: A wiping cloth intended for sanitizing food contact surfaces was observed hanging from the side of the sani bucket. Discussed with PIC and the cloth was placed inside of the sanitizer solution. Ensure that wiping cloths intended for sanitizing are always stored inside of the solution and never hanging from the sides of the bucket.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Multiple items were observed in the retail coolers to be held past their best by date. CORRECTED- one package of cream cheese (expired 4/25), and 2 cinnamon roll packaged (expired 7/25) were voluntarily removed from service by the person in charge (PIC). 
Other non-TCS items in the retail space were recommended to be removed from service for quality purposes. These items include baked beans (X5), green beans (X2), chicken noodle soup (X2), taco seasoning(X6), gravy mix (X2), Ritz crackers (X2), and Vanilla Wafers (X2). The PIC voluntarily discarded all of the aforementioned items. 
Ensure that unopened temperature for food safety items (TCS) are removed from service after they expire, or used or discarded within 7 days of opening.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed 2 dead adult cockroaches behind cold holding units in the back of the facility. CORRECTED- Discussion removed the dead roaches, and cleaned the areas where they were seen. PIC stated they will notify their pest control operator to increase frequency. Eliminate conditions that allow for the harborage of pests by removing cardboard from floors and frequent cleaning.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.[C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of food debris in the bottom portion of the prep cooler, as well as the interior of the adjacent cabinet. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris, and harborage of pests.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed bare wood above the bar hand washing sink. Bare wood is porous, that therefore provides a surface that may harbor the growth and harborage of mold. Ensure bare wood surface is painted by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspectors observed several cockroaches in the kitchen. Cockroaches were concentrated under the triple sink. Both adults and nymphs were observed. Pest control has greatly reduced the number of cockroaches, but small populations still persist. Alternative pest control methods may be needed to eradicate the pests completely.

There is a hole in the wall behind the triple sink that needs to be sealed as well. Inspectors recommend using spray foam to seal the hole. Once spray foam is used, shave foam flush with the wall and paint it to make it smooth, durable, and easily cleanable. 

Ensure door sweeps allow no light to pass under the door.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: REPEAT- The PIC is the only employee present and is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC has their food handler certificate, but was educated that there always needs to be at least one CFPM in the facility during all hours of food preparation and serving. Ensure that there are enough Certified Food Protection Managers to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There was a mop bucket of used mop water next to the mop sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC who was educated that the waste water needs to be dumped in the mop sink immediately after use, as this prevents pest harborage conditions. Ensure that waste water is dumped immediately after use.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking at the handwashing sink to the right of the ovens is observed to be in disrepair. Discussed re-caulking this by next routine inspection. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: REPEAT- There was a container of food for an employee in the top of the cooler containing hot dogs to the left of the ovens. CORRECTED- The PIC removed the food from the cooler and was educated that the food needs to be in a bottom shelf in a bin labeled personal. Ensure that food intended for employees is kept separate from food for consumers to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizer dispenser (sink and surface sanitizer; lactic acid) was not dispensing at the correct concentration. The district manager contacted EcoLab to schedule repairs during the inspection. The PIC will be making the sanitizer buckets manually until it is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 9/22/2025 to check that the sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dirt, outside residue, and other debris on the floor underneath the triple freezer by the back exit door. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the floor is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. All employees who do not have the CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present at the facility. The PIC will be taking the CFPM class. Ensure there is a CFPM present during all hours of operation by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee turned off the faucets with their bare hands after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. All employees who do not have the CFPM certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed a broken floor tile in front of the back door. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure tiles are repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of grease in the hood vent above the fryers. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination on ready to eat (RTE) foods, and also pose a fire risk to the facility. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: Inspector observed no ambient thermometers in the cold holding units (walk in cooler and prep coolers) at the facility. Ambient thermometers should be placed toward the warmest part of the cooling unit to ensure temperature control for food safety (TCS) food items are cold held at or below 41F. Obtain and place ambient thermometers by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-204.112(B) Temperature Measuring Devices. (B) Except as specified in (C) of this section, cold or hot holding EQUIPMENT used for TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. [C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There was a major leaking coming from the faucet handle of the kitchen’s handwashing sink. The PIC mentioned that a plumber will be to service the sink very soon. Ensure that faucet handles are maintained in good repair and always in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed heat dish plate for the facility’s heat sanitizing dish machine to reach a surface temperature of 150F, after 3 wash and rinse cycles. Person in charge (PIC) placed a work order for the dish machine. Facility is instructed to utilize the 3 compartment sink for sanitizing food contact services until the dish machine is serviced. Dish machines that use heat for sanitation must reach a minimum temperature of 165F.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed no device to test the temperature of the heat sanitizing dish machine. PIC and other staff members were unable to locate the strips during this inspection. Obtain test strips to ensure that heat sanitizing dish machine is reaching minimum required sanitation temperatures.
citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: There’s clean dishes stored in the dish machine that appear to be from breakfast earlier in the day. Discussed with PIC that dishes must be properly air dried and not left in the machine over night. Dishes left over night in the dish machine can be exposed to extreme moisture, possibly creating an environment where mold can grow. Ensure to place clean dishes on shelves or in a manner where they are able to air dry.
citation_text: 4-901.11(A) Equipment and Utensils, Air-Drying Required. After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) Shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining as specified in the first paragraph of 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (food-contact surface SANITIZING solutions), before contact with FOOD.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There were a couple leaks dripping from a pipe above the right table of the dish machine. The facility is aware of the leaks and is in the process of repairing the leaks. The facility mentioned that the ice machine on the second floor is causing the leaks in the kitchen area. PIC expects to have the leaks repaired tomorrow. In the meantime, the facility is instructed to place a bucket underneath the drip to catch contaminated water. A follow-up will be scheduled for 9/19/2025 to ensure that leak is repaired and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: A mop was observed in the basin of the storage bucket (also storing waste water). After mopping floors, be sure to store mop heads in a manner that allows for them to properly air dry. Ensure that mop heads are never stored in dirty waste water over night. This may attract unwanted insects and pests in the kitchen area. Waste water must also be dumped at the end of the shift and never left overnight.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed there were dented cans on the dry storage shelf in the back of the kitchen. The PIC stated that employees should be putting any dented cans they find when stocking shelves in the office. During the inspection the cans were removed from service and brought to the office. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect food from exposure to potential contaminants.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer dispenser (sink and surface sanitizer; lactic acid) at the triple sink in the back of the kitchen is not pulling any sanitizer through the line and only dispensing water. During the inspection the PIC manually made a sanitizer bucket testing at the correct concentration. The inspector will follow-up on 9/22/2025 to ensure that the sanitizer dispenser is dispensing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of frost inside the white standing freezer in the back of the kitchen. The freezer must be de-frosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the cove base behind the dish washing machine is missing or peeling off the wall. The missing cove base must be replaced and the peeling cove base must be sealed to the wall. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

Numerous dead bugs are observed around the inside rim of the display chest freezer in front of the register. The PIC is instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mop is observed being stored in dirty mop water in the bathroom. The PIC was notified and instructed to stored so that it can drip dry when not in use. Ensure proper storage moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed food contact sanitizer bottle reading 0 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the sanitizer bottle was remade to have a concentration of 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is made (and tested using the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to hold the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed soil accumulation on the soda nozzles at the bar, as well as inside the nozzle holder. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved the nozzles to be cleaned and sanitized, and wiped the nozzle holder with a clean sanitizing cloth. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Nacho cheese containers on the south hold holding unit were observed to have ambient temperatures ranging from 115-120. The PIC stated the cheeses had been there at least since yesterday. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded 28 containers of nacho cheese, and a probe thermometer was placed in the hot holding unit to monitor ambient temperatures. Ensure all hold holding units allow internal temperatures of temperature control for safety (TCS) foods to reach 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed 1 dead adult cockroach under the north hot holding chips and nacho cheese unit. Staff should eliminate harborage conditions by frequent cleaning (see violation #49) and check incoming shipments for pests. Continue to utilize pest control operator, and eliminate conditions for harborage.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed pretzel trays to be stored with the food contact surfaces facing upwards. CORRECTED- PIC inverted the trays. Ensure ongoing education occurs with staff regarding the storage of food contact surfaces to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris in the following areas:
1) The hinges around the artisan popcorn contain an accumulation of dust and food debris.
2) The gaskets of the hotdog under counter cooler contain an accumulation of mold.
3) Soil accumulation behind the un-adhered board underneath the pick up station. 
4) Counter above the lid drawers (behind northern most register). 
5) Underneath the lid pop out storage directly to the left of the northernmost register.
Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulking at hand washing sink (directly next to the triple sink) to be fragmented and separating from the wall. Fixed facilities  that cannot be moved for cleaning should be sealed to the wall to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor and drainage pipe next to the soda boxes contains liquid pooling, and a significant amount of soil accumulation. Ensure floors and walls are cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine’s sanitizing temperatures were recorded between 124F-153F after at least 6 cycles. The dish machine was tested using several different measuring devices (heat puck and thermo stickers). See that the dish machine is serviced and its sanitizing temperature is at least 160F. Facility is instructed to wash, rinse, sanitize in triple sink until the machine is functioning properly. Will follow up 9/18/2025.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

The front screen door to the facility is observed to not completely close at the time of this inspection. The latch is jammed in the open position and does not allow for complete closing. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection. Provide for tight fitting outer openings of the facility in order to prevent the entrance of pests.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture.

The hand sink in the women’s bathroom is currently pulling away from the wall and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-seal prior to the next routine insepction. Ensure that all areas subject to moisture are maintained with smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
comment: Observed soup to be cooling at 100F after 1.5 hours. Discussed with PIC, soup will be constantly stirred and moved to walk in cooler to drop temperature quicker. Ensure all TCS foods being cooled are at 70F after 2 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed precooked sausages to be hot held at 90F. Discussed with PIC, TCS items were pulled from hot holding and cooked to 165F before returning to hot holding. Ensure any TCS food being hot held to be kept at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed soup to be cooling at 100F in ambient air temperature. Discussed with PIC, inspector provided education regarding proper cooling techniques. Ensure staff is properly monitoring cooling.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed ice scoop to be resting on soda dispensing surface. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was put through wash, rinse, and sanitize process and placed within ice with the handle outside of ice. Ensure all in use utensil are properly stored to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed sanitizer bucket to be at 0ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was remade and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure all sanitizer buckets are at the proper sanitation level.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the temporary hand sink to be missing soap and paper towels. These items are vital to ensuring proper handwashing and preventing cross-contamination during food handling. The PIC was informed and soap and paper towels were acquired from a neighboring stand.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspectors observed shredded cheese to be held above the maximum cold holding temperature for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. The cheese was being stored in a cooler with ice, but the container was sitting atop the ice rather than fully submerged. Education was conducted on how to properly prepare an ice bath and the violation was corrected-on-site.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed boxes of single-use articles (i.e., cups, lids) stored directly on the ground in the storage closet outside of the kitchen. The PIC was educated that all single-use articles must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination. Ensure proper storage by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The corner wall next to the refrigerators is observed with the corner cover and Nudo board pulling away at the bottom. The PIC is instructed to repair/reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that the facilities are maintained in good repair at all times to prevent possible contaminants and pest issues.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility does not have a way to verify the sanitizing temperature of the dish machine at the time of this inspection. Both test strips as well as a maximum registering thermometer were discussed and a follow up is being set for 10 days to verify compliance. The PIC tried showing the probe thermometer effectiveness for this situation but it could not be verified in that manner and the digital one in the facility normally used for this would not turn on. A follow up is being scheduled for 10 days.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine’s sanitizing temperature was recorded between 151F - 154F. The PIC mentioned that the dish machine’s last service was about eight months prior to the inspection. Discussed with PIC that the minimum sanitizing temperature must be 160F to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces. Ensure that the dish machine is serviced to maintain a sanitizing surface temperature of at least 160F. Will follow-up on 9/17/2025.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is an ice cream machine that is currently not in use in the kitchen area. The PIC mentioned that the facility does not plan to use the machine in the future. Remove any unused pieces of equipment if there is no plan for use in the future.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: The Road Ranger did not have a designated person in charge (PIC) who has knowledge about safe food handling practices present during today’s inspection. Multiple priority and priority foundation violations were observed during today’s inspection. Violations 3, 23, 24, and 28 could all contribute to food-borne illness. Ensure all staff handling and preparing food have food safety education. A follow up inspection will occur on 09/22/25 to ensure priority and priority foundation violations have been corrected.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.[10]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Employees were unable to produce employee reporting agreements. A blank copy will be emailed to the PIC on Monday, 09/15/25. Ensure all employees handling or serving food items read and sign agreements by 09/22/25.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
SECOND REPEAT (for all items): The following temperature control for food safety items were observed without date marking:
1) Creamer, whole milk, and half and half in the creamer dispenser
2) Pizza sauce in the prep cooler.- CORRECTED. The employee who prepares pizza arrived and marked the sauce with the day it was removed from its container. 
All TCS items must contain date marking. The day of preparation or thawing counts as day one. Items must be used or discarded within 7 days,
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Paperwork (verification and procedures) for time as public health control (TAC) used for pizza was unable to be presented to the inspector at this time. Facilities using TAC must have verifiable procedures and written records available at the inspectors request. Inspector will return to the facility on 09/22 to verify TAC paperwork with PIC.
citation_text: 3-501.19(A) Time as a Public Health Control. (A) Except as specified under (D) of this section, if time without temperature control is used as the public health control for a working supply of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD before cooking, or for READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is displayed or held for sale or service: (1) Written procedures shall be prepared in advance, maintained in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and made available to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY upon request that specify:  (a) Methods of compliance with Subparagraphs (B)(1)-(4) or (C)(1)-(5) of this section.; and (b) Methods of compliance with § 3-501.14 for FOOD that is prepared, cooked, and refrigerated before time is used as a public health control. [Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed engine lubricant and coolant being stored over prepackaged juices and soda in the facilities dry storage area (near the walk in cooler). Food items cannot be stored underneath toxic substances. Ensure toxic substances are stored away or underneath food items to prevent the contamination of RTE (ready to eat) food items.
citation_text: 7-301.11 Separation. POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored and displayed for retail sale so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple cold holding units missing ambient air thermometers in the following locations:
1) Standing cooler #1 (dairy)
2) Standing deli cooler
3) Standing double door cooler in the pizza prep room
Cold holding units intended for the storage of TCS food items must contain an easily readable ambient thermometer in the warmest part of the cooler. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in the aforementioned locations.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed single service food boats in the pizza prep area to be stored with their food contact surface facing up. CORRECTED- Food Handler inverted the trays. Ensure food contact surfaces are protected from contamination by storing them under a covering, or in an inverted position.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C}

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Single service articles (cups, lids, to go containers, and food trays) were observed to be stored on the floor in the dry storage area of the triple sink room, as well as the pizza prep room. Single service containers must be stored at least 6 inches above the ground to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed the gaskets of several standing coolers to be in disrepair. Coolers are in the following locations:
1) Standing cooler #8 (Red Bull)
2) Standing cooler #9 (Celsius)
3) Standing cooler #11 (Pepsi)
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Gaskets should be repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the gaskets on the creamer dispenser to be soiled with mold accumulation. Ensure gaskets and all nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the caulking around the hand washing sink (in the triple sink room) to contain a biofilm, and to be separating from the wall. Clean and replace the caulking to prevent the growth and harborage of microorganisms. This repair will also provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIRD REPEAT: The floor under the milk storage shelving in the walk in cooler was observed to contain a significant amount of soil debris and splash. Ensure the physical facility is cleaned at a frequency to prevent the buildup of soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Staff members were unable to produce Food Handlers Certificates at the inspector’s request. Ensure that all employees who handle or prepare RTE food have a Food Handler’s Certificate available at the inspector’s request. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed hand washing sink to have no paper towels. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) replaced paper towels. Ensure all hand washing sinks have warm running water, soap, and paper towels at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dust in the following locations: (1) walk-in cooler fans; and (2) ceiling vent above the storage shelves between the double door cooler and oven in the kitchen. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the fans and vent are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no soap to be present at bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was brought and placed at handsink. Ensure all hand sinks a re properly equipped to encourage hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed a pot of sauce to be cooling on the floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and pot was moved to at least 6 inches off the ground. Ensure all food are kept at or above 6 inches from the ground.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed clean plates to not be inverted in shelving unit. Discussed with PIC, PIC will invert plates today and order plastic covering for shelves. Ensure all clean plates are inverted or stored in a way that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a small gap on the lower right edge of the back door. Gaps in outer openings of the facility may allow for the entry of pests. Corrected by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: The ice bin was observed to be stored in ready to use position with the food contact surface facing upwards. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) inverted the ice bin. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored in a position to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed rust along the shelves of the standing cooler towards the back of the store. Nonfood contact surfaces should be free of rust and any debris that may pose a potential to contaminate food items. Ensure shelves are replaced, or cleaned and repainted by the next routine inspection to have a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no measurable concentration in sanitizer bucket. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) remade sanitizer bucket to a concentration of 100 ppm Chlorine bleach. Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at a frequency to sustain the concentration as reccomended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: REPEAT- There were raw beef patties observed to be over milk, raw shelled eggs, jalapeños, and a container of dressing. This was discussed with the PIC and a handout on storage order was provided. CORRECTED- The raw beef patties were moved to be below these items. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There were reduced oxygen packages of salmon that were observed to be thawed and in the cooler. These packages of salmon state to remove from packaging prior to thawing and had not been removed from the packaging. This was discussed with the PIC who was informed that this fish either needs to be removed entirely from the packaging or a cut needs to be placed in the packaging prior to being thawed. CORRECTED- A cut was placed in each packaging of fish to correct the violation. Ensure that all reduced oxygen packaged fish is removed from the reduced oxygen environment prior to thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The handwashing sink in the kitchen, the triple sink in the kitchen, and the table next to the dish machine are all observed to need to be caulked to the wall. 
2. There are cracked gaskets on a cooler and a freezer in the kitchen. This was discussed with the PIC who stated that they have ordered more gaskets and will be replacing them soon. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
REPEAT- The floors, walls, ceiling, and vent covers throughout the facility are in need of a deep cleaning. The walls, ceilings, and vent covers above the steam table, pizza oven, and the dish area were observed to have dust accumulation. The walls in the kitchen have built-up food splatter on them. Ensure that these physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned. 

The coolers/freezers and gaskets of them are in need of cleaning in the kitchen. This was discussed with the PIC as well. Ensure that these are cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed freezers 1, 4, and 5 in the storage area to have a build up of ice on the inside. Discussed defrosting with PIC. Ensure these units are defrosted regularly enough to remove the ice. Ice is not considered smooth, durable, or easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Several cucumbers stored in cooler #4 were observed covered in mold. Discussed and shown to PIC and the cucumbers were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that all food items are maintained in good condition and never moldy. If food is observed moldy, be sure to never serve and discard items immediately.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine’s sanitizing temperature was recorded at 148.6F. The dish machine was run four times and the temperature remained the same. The PIC mentioned that MJ Kellner was suppose to visit the facility again to service the machine but hasn’t. PIC made a call to have a technician service the facility as soon as possible. The dish machine’s sanitizing temperature should always be recorded at least 160F to ensure effective sanitizing of food contact surfaces. Until the machine is functioning properly, the facility was instructed to sanitize dishes in triple sink using the available chemicals (bleach or quaternary ammonia).  Will follow-up on 9/15/2025.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Cut tomatoes stored in cooler #1 were observed with an exceeded time/temperature control for safety of food. The cut tomatoes were dated August 18, 2025, which is past the required seven day time frame for cold holding. Discussed with PIC proper date marking and to never hold TCS items in house longer than seven days. The tomatoes were also observed moldy. The PIC discarded the cut tomatoes. Ensure that TCS foods prepared in house are held no longer than seven days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The hand sink by the three part sink in the C-store is without soap at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and refilled the dispenser to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. On arrival the sani bucket in the Caribou Coffee shop did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and had the bucket remade during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all in use sanitizers are maintained at effective concentration at all times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed facility to be using quaternary ammonium sanitizer, but facility only had test strips for chlorine sanitizers. Discussed what strips to buy and where to get them with PIC. These strips can be purchased from food distributors or online. The strips will be for measuring the concentration of quaternary ammonium concentrations. They’re commonly called QAC strips. They come in rolls and also individual sticks. Inspector will return 09/22/2025 to check if facility has gotten the strips.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sink by the back office desk is not sealed to the wall. The sink must be sealed (ex.caulking) to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the sink is sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed there was sausages on the roller grill but there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) present during the inspection. Ensure there is always a CFPM present during food preparation by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the glass portions on the slushy machine around the nozzles have an accumulation of soil residues underneath. The glass portions should be removed to facilitate cleaning. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the slushy machine is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was present at the facility during today’s inspection. The presence of a CFPM helps to ensure safe food handling practices, and decreases the risk of Food borne illnesses by overseeing facilities and educating food handlers. Ensure there is a CFPM present at the facility any time food is being served.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Signed employee reporting agreements were not available upon request. CORRECTED- the inspector provided the person in charge (PIC) with SCDPH employee health reporting agreements. A spot check will occur on 09/19/25 to check that the PIC has signed forms from the facilities volunteers.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer available at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the inspector demonstrated how to prepare the sanitizer compartment of the triple sink- per the label’s instructions. Sanitizer was observed at 200 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is available for food contact surfaces on days where food assembly is required (i.e.- Taco Tuesdays where volunteers assemble tacos).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no measurable concentration of sanitizer in the sanitizer bucket at the start of today’s inspection. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) remade sanitizer to an approved concentration (400 ppm quaternary ammonia). Ensure sanitizer is made (and tested using facility’s test strips) at a frequency to have the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a wet sanitizing cloth on the prep table. Wet textiles left out may lead to the growth and harborage of microorganisms. Ensure sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizing solution in between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed the facility to be lacking sanitizer test strips that correspond with the solution used for sanitizing. Chlorine (Cl) test strips were found in the facility, however quaternary ammonia (quat) is the sanitizing solution currently being utilized. The facility should either use Chlorine bleach as a sanitizer, or obtain quat test strips, to ensure sanitizer can be tested for the correct concentration. The inspector gave some quat strips to the facility, however a spot check will occur on 09/22/25 to ensure the facility has obtained their own.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device. [Pf]

comment: Inspector observed the freezer drawers to contain a significant amount of food debris. Debris on nonfood contact surfaces poses a potential to contaminate ready to eat (RTE) food items. Ensure the drawers are cleaned routinely to prevent cross contamination of RTE food items.
