title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
The dish room cooler at the facility is not holding temperature. Inspector measured temperatures of food in the cooler to be between 48 and 52F. Food must be held at 41F or below. Discussed with PIC, and PIC called for service immediately. Inspector will return 09/19/2025 to re-inspect the temperature holding capabilities of the cooler. 

See violation 22 for food in the cooler.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee in the bar area was observed rinsing hands in the ware washing sink. Educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. When cleaning hands, be sure to follow the following procedures: 1.)  rinse hands with warm running water 2.) apply soap and later hands and arms for at least 10 seconds 3.) rinse soap from hands under running water 4.) use a disposable towel to dry hands (before turning off faucet handles) 4.) use the disposable towel to operate faucet handles to shut off water. Ensure that these cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed touching body parts with gloved hands. The employee was getting ready to engage in food handling before the activity was ceased and corrected. The employee was instructed to wash hands and change gloves to correct the violation. Educate employees on proper glove usage and when to wash hands when contamination occurs.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a stainless steel container in the basin of the handwashing sink in the bar area. Shown to PIC and the container was removed to correct the violation. Ensure that hand-sinks remain unobstructed to allow proper access for employees to wash hands when necessary.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A container of raw steak was observed above various sauces in the cooler across from the cook-line. Discussed with PIC and the steak was moved to the bottom shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored beneath ready-to-eat foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
A cutting board that’s being used in the kitchen was observed with several chips on the top surface. Discussed and shown to PIC. PIC mentioned that more cutting boards will be purchased. Ensure that food contact surfaces are maintained in good condition and never with chips or scratches to prevent possibly contaminating food items. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment:
There were leaks observed at the following sinks and dripping into the sink basins: 
- A leak coming from the faucet of the handwashing sink in the kitchen area
- Leaks coming from both faucet heads of the triple sink in the kitchen area

Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that sink faucets are maintained in good repair and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There wasn't any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerator units to allow visibility for food service workers
citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility could not produce food handler certificates for cooks and other employees that handle food and clean dishes. Employees who are not manager certified must obtain a food handler’s certification if handling food and clean dishes.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Two aluminum cans stored in the dry storage area were observed with deep dents around the body of the can. The cans were shown to the PIC and pulled from the shelf to correct the violation. Ensure that aluminum cans are maintained in good condition and are never dented to prevent possibly contaminating food items.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

1. There is a broken piece of coving to the left of the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Ensure that this is repaired. 
2. The facility has a new handwashing sink in the kitchen. There needs to be caulking around the handwashing sink to seal it to the wall. 
3. The plate under the handwashing sink in the kitchen is observed to be coming away from the wall. Ensure that this is sealed. 

Ensure all physical facilities are repaired and maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

comment: The taco meat in the warmer was observed to only be holding at 131F (probed). The PIC stated that the warmer was turned down lower than it should be at due to them not wanting the plastic of the cups to melt. CORRECTED- The PIC reheated the taco meat to 165F and turned the warmer up to hold at 135F and above. Ensure that hot food is holding at 135F and above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed two areas to have soiled food-contact surfaces. Both areas were at the detached Globe Tavern. The first area is the drain-tube connected to the soda gun holder. The tube has a build-up of soils in the tube. A reusable straw brush could be a good tool for cleaning this. The second area is the ice scoop holder at the bar. The scoop holder has a build-up of soils along the bottom edges. The scoop comes directly into contact with these soils when the scoop is inserted in the holder. Ensure both of these areas are cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. They also require regular sanitization, as they are a food-contact surface (ice and soda are both considered food).

Inspector will return 09/18/25 to re-inspect the condition of these areas.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Inspector noticed several juices that needed date marks in the bar cooler. One of the bottles was bloated, and was thrown away immediately. Inspector discussed date marking the rest of the juices with the PIC. Ensure that date marking happens within 24 hours of opening a TCS (time/temperature controlled for safety) food. To identify TCS foods, look for the phrases “refrigerate after opening” or “keep refrigerated” on the item packaging. Additionally, anything prepared in the kitchen that is not shelf-stable must also be date marked within 24 hours of preparation. Should staff have any date-marking questions, call me at (217) 341-2603.

Inspector will return 09/18/25 to re-inspect date marking practices.

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector noticed a build-up of ice in the walk-in freezer (K-41). This build up is occurring mostly near the bottom left edge of the door, but there is still a uniform frosting of every surface in the freezer. Discussed the situation with the PIC. Ensure that maintenance is done on the cooler to prevent this build-up of ice and frost.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Inspector observed the bar chest-cooler that is used to store beers and juices to be soiled. Specifically, the bottom of the cooler underneath the grates that are used to store beers and juice is soiled. The soils are not affecting the items being stored in the cooler, but still must be removed. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the bottom of the cooler is cleaned out regularly enough to keep it clean. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Inspector observed the secondary dish machine table to not be sealed to the wall. It is not far enough from the wall to be cleaned manually, so it must be sealed to the wall to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the table is sealed to the wall.

Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed the food handler fail to wash hands when switching tasks between handling monetary transactions and preparing food. CORRECTED- the food handler washed their hands between tasks at the inspector’s bequest. Wash hands before donning gloves to prevent transferring pathogens from bare hands to gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: No sanitizer bucket was available at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) made a sanitizer bucket of quaternary ammonia at a concentration of 200 ppm. Sanitizer must be available for food contacts surfaces at all times food is being prepared or handled. Make sanitizer each day before food is handled or prepared, and remake throughout the day to maintain the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: An accumulation of soil debris was observed around the drainage line in the walk in cooler. Routine cleaning should take place to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a small floor tile missing right of the triple and mop sinks, as well as coving peeling from the wall (in the same area). Surfaces around floors and walls should be maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure these repairs occur before the next routine inspection to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Inspector observed evidence of the hand sink at the bar being use as a dump sink. PIC was made aware about the hand sink serving only for the purpose of handwashing. The hand sink was created and staff was educated, Ensure that designated sinks for handwashing be use solely for handwashing and nothing else. 

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Inspector observed there to be no hand soap available at the handwashing sink in the back by the triple sink. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the soap will be refilled. Ensure that there is hand soap available at all hand sinks to enable proper handwashing at all times. 

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Inspector observed bottles stored in the handwashing sink in the back by the triple sink. Discussed with PIC and the bottles were removed. Ensure that hand sinks are free and accessible at all times for handwashing. Handwashing sinks shall not be used for storage or any other purpose other than their designated purpose for handwashing.


Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed the soda nozzles  to be soiled. Discussed with PIC. PIC ensured inspector that the soda nozzles will be cleaned. Inspector will return on 09/12/25 to follow up. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the soda nozzles are monitored  and cleaned at a regular frequency. 

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Inspector observed an accumulation of dust and soil build-up on the fans of the refrigeration unit in the walk-in cooler. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspector that the accumulation will be cleaned. Ensure that this accumulation is clean to sight of touch to avoid possible contamination.


Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and that the PIC is instructed to ensure that employees are correctly educated in relation to hand washing procedures. Ensure that a clean barrier is used to maintain the freshly washed hands in a clean state.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to pass on this relevant information to employees and ensure that hand washing is taking place WHEN required at all times in the facility. Ensure hand washing happens at all times required.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans of foods are observed with significant dents. Education was conducted with the PIC and the noted cans separated out for discard/credit. Ensure that all food packaging is in good condition until use. This is not a repeat at this time, but this situation has been noted earlier this year. Ensure that education is passed on to employees and procedures are consistently in alignment with food safety standards.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw shrimp is observed over Ready-To-Eat (RTE) beef in the front standing cooler. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-arranged during this inspection to correct. Education conducted. Ensure that safe storage order and separation of raw/Ready-To-Eat items in the coolers is taking place to prevent possible cross contamination. Store raw meats under RTE foods as well as according to their cooking temperatures.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

On arrival the cloth used for wiping counters in the front of the facility is observed being left on the counter between uses. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to store the cloth between uses in a sanitizer of sufficient concentration to maintain food safety standards. The rag was moved to the bucket to correct. It was also suggested to maintain an extra bucket in the front preparation area to allow for a more convenient safe storage location.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There were no active Certified Food Protection Managers (CFPMs) present at today’s inspection. One employee had an expired CFPM, and no one else at the facility had taken the class. A CFPM must be present during all hours in which food is being prepared or handled. The inspector shared a list of approved CFPM courses to the person in charge (PIC). Ensure multiple employees obtain or renew their CFPMs to ensure the PIC has a wide breath of food safety knowledge they can share with other staff members.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed no paper towels in the all gender restroom. CORRECTED- a staff member replaced the paper towels. Ensure all handwashing sinks are stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels to decrease the risk of food-borne illnesses.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket to have 50 ppm of quaternary ammonia at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the PIC remade the sanitizer to 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed (and checked with the facility’s test strips) at a frequency to maintain the proper sanitizing concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A knife in ready-to-use position (on the prep tables’s magnetic strip) was observed to contain an accumulation of food debris. CORRECTED- the knife was taken to the facility’s triple sink to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Multiple foods were observed to be above the accepted cold holding value of 41F (tomatoes- probed at 45.9F, red onions- probed at 46F, and cucumbers- probed at 46.4F, spinach- probed at 45.1) on the west prep line cooler during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that the items were prepared at the start of the day- over 4 hours ago. CORRECTED- the PIC voluntarily discarded the aforementioned ready to eat (RTE) food items. Close cooler lids when not in use, and routinely probe RTE items to ensure they are holding internal temperatures below 41F. RTE foods must not be left in the “Temperature Danger Zone” (41-135) for more than 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of food debris during today’s inspection:
1) Food pan areas of prep coolers
2) Along the back hinges of the prep coolers
3) Under the cookie display box.
4) All interior walls of the microwave.
5) Magnetic knife strip over the kitchen prep table.
To prevent the contamination of RTE foods, nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of food debris. Encourage staff to clean during slower times when food preparation is not occurring.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Multiple areas in the physical facility were observed to be in need of repair:
1) The caulking along the triple sink was observed to be discolored and fragmented. The current caulking should be removed and replaced.
2) The caulking behind the meat slicer was incomplete. Complete caulking this area.
Counters, plumbing, and other items that are fixed in place (and cannot be moved for cleaning) should be sealed to the wall to prevent the harborage of mold, and provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food Handler certificates were not able to be produced for all employees present at today’s inspection. To ensure safe food handling practices, all employees must obtain and be able to produce a Food Handler’s Card within 30 days of hire. Ensure all employees have their Food Handler’s Cards by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.[C]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed multiple items (sandwiches and cut vegetables) in the double door standing cooler nearest the cafeteria to be without date marking. When the inspector asked the date the items were prepped it was stated that the items were prepared on Tuesday (09/02). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed dates on the items. Food being cold held for more than 24 hours must be used or discarded within seven days. Date marking helps to prevent foods from being held past an unsafe date. Educate all employees about date marking requirements.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Inspector observed the two dish plates in the facility to not be operational. The PIC has communicated with maintenance to obtain new batteries for the temperature measuring devices. Inspector will return on 09/15/25 to check that the batteries in both heat plates have been replaced, and both devices are working. When a facility is using heat for sanitation purposes there must be heat detection plates. Facility should use plates on a regular basis to ensure the proper sanitizing temperature is being reached (160F+).
citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of repair:
- Hand sink in kitchen area is pulling from wall. Caulk hand-sink back to wall
- Parts of the wall in between the triple sink and hand-sink are starting peel. Repaint affected areas.

See that areas are repaired. Physical facilities must be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employee cough into hand and continue prepping cooler. Discussed with PIC, employee rewashed hands and education was provided. Ensure staff members are washing hands at a frequency that prevents contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed multiple TCS food items to be kept at room temperature. Discussed with PIC, items were prepared this morning. Inspector provided education in regard to cold holding TCS foods, ice baths were created for sauces, and larger items were placed in cooler. Ensure all TCS foods being cold held are kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS foods to not have date marking available. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and dates were placed on TCS foods. Ensure all foods kept longer than 24 hours are properly date marked and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed multiple in use cloths not being stored in sanitizer solution. Discussed with PIC, cloths were moved to sanitizer bucket. Ensure any in use rag is kept in a sanitized solution.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking at mop sink to be in a state of disrepair. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents disrepair from occurring.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed three areas to have soiled food-contact surfaces. 

The first two areas were the bar soda nozzles. Discussed with PIC at bar. Ensure that soda nozzles are taken apart and cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. 

The third area was the ice machine baffle. The front of the baffle was clean except for the edges near where it attaches to the ice bin. These edges are holding soils. Discussed with PIC at bar. Ensure that the baffle is cleaned thoroughly enough to remove soils from all parts of the baffle. 

Inspector will return 09/15/2025 to re-inspect these food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed a bottle of juice and two containers of coffee creamer to not be date marked at the bar. Discussed with bar PIC. Ensure that all items labeled “refrigerate after opening” are date marked within 24 hours of opening and kept for no longer than 7 days. Inspector will return 09/15/2025 to re-inspect date marking practices.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspector noticed two areas that cockroaches could be entering the facility. 

The first area is the event room door to the outdoor seating area. There is a gap under this door that must be sealed to prevent pest entry.

The second area is the bar door to the outdoor seating area. There is a gap under this door as well that could allow pests in the building.

Ensure these gaps are sealed to prevent pest entry, this is especially important given the pest presence in the kitchen.

Inspector will return 9/15/2025 to ensure gaps have been sealed.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed cockroaches in the kitchen. Both adults and nymphs were observed. 5-10 were seen free roaming in the kitchen and a large amount were seen on sticky traps. Facility is keeping up with cleaning, the only area in the kitchen that could use more cleaning is behind the dish machine. All other areas were observed to be clean. There are also no gaps or holes observed in the kitchen where cockroaches could be getting in. All food is being stored protected in plastic containers or cold-holding units. Inspector will return 9/15/2025 to re-inspect pest presence. Ensure that pest control comes and pest presence is reduced before this visit.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The bar freezer containing just pizzas was observed to have a build-up of ice. Ice is not considered smooth, nonabsorbent, or corrosion resistant. Discussed with PIC. Ensure freezer is defrosted regularly enough to keep it free of ice.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the bar cooler being used to chill glasses to contain debris. The bottom of the unit is lined with wire mesh, and underneath is dirty. Discussed with bar PIC. Ensure this area is cleaned regularly enough to keep it free of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that no one at the facility has completed the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) training. The PIC is working on finding a translator for the test. Ensure that there is a CFPM present at the faculty during all hours of operation by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived at the facility. The PIC was educated and they made a sanitizer bucket testing at 150 ppm (Cl). Ensure there are always sanitizing solutions available whenever food preparation is occurring.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) was on the premises during today’s inspection. A CFPM is required to be present during all times food is being prepared or served. Inspector suggests an additional food handler obtains their CFPM so that there is a CFPM on site at all times. The presence of a CFPM ensures safe food handling and decreases the incidence of improper food handling and the risk of food-borne illness.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- No paper towels were available at the kitchen hand-sink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- Upon request, paper towels were provided at the kitchen handwashing sink. Ensure warm running water, soap, and paper towels are always available at handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There is a 2 basin sink in the kitchen area. When the inspector asked the food handler where they wash their hands they stated in the restroom. The restroom is set to close, and therefore poses a risk of contamination freshly cleaned hands. The kitchen sink is used for hand washing and cleaning employee dishes CORRECTED- Inspector spoke with the person in charge (PIC), who will educate employees that handwashing before food prep or service should take place in the right basin of the kitchen sink. Teacher dishes were moved from the right basin to the left basin. Hand washing sinks are designated for hand washing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the sink in the men’s restroom to be out of soap. CORRECTED- the PIC was notified and the soap was refilled. Ensure all handwashing sinks are always stocked with warm running water, soap, and paper towels (or another means to dry hands).
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed multiple pieces of fruit to be resting in bar ice machine. Discussed with PIC, fruit items were removed ice. Ensure ice is being protected from ant possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed dish machine to be testing a 0ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be serviced. Inspecotr instructed facility to use triple sink for all dish washing until dish machine is serviced.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed bar ice scoop to be resting in contact with ice. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was removed from ice and placed in a sanitized location. Ensure ice scoop is kept out of contact with ice to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed both ice scoops to be resting on unsanitized surfaces. Discussed with PIC, ice scoops will be cleaned ad placed on a sanitized surface in between use. Ensure in use utensils are stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The ice machine in the back area used by multiple departments (including bakery) has globs of black slime/mold observed around the internal chute opening. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean at all times. The equipment was cleaned/sanitized during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Multiple areas in the facility are observed to have multiple fruit flies/gnats/drain flies. Areas include: 1) the bakery dish area; 2) the drain next to the seasoning mixer in the bakery area; 3) the back-stock storage area directly behind the bakery; 4) the chemical room in the back-stock area and; 5) in the room next to the chemical room in the back-stock area. The PIC stated that EcoLab had already been to the facility recently but that they would be contacting them for another visit for the noted areas. A follow up is being set f to check for compliance.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink next to the walk in freezer in the bakery area is pulling away from the wall exposing a gap/crack that needs repaired. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces throughout the facility, and especially around areas regularly exposed to moisture.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. A CFPM arrived shortly into the Inspection to correct. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to have one at the facility at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area/front was without a hand drying provision. Paper towels were supplied during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote good hand washing practices in the facility.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The facility does not have a way to verify the sanitizing temperature of the dish machine at the time of this inspection. Both test strips as well as a maximum registering thermometer were discussed and a follow up is being set for 10 days to verify compliance.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared and ready for use on the surfaces in the facility. The PIC had a sani bucket prepared using quat to correct. Ensure that there is a sanitizer available for use at all times in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: ... (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

Employees are observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet during this inspection. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to trickle down the needed information. They should also be monitoring the hand washing practices in the facility to ensure that they are being conducted correctly at all times. Ensure proper hand washing takes place at all times in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

1) Employees are observed to not wash hands prior to donning gloves. 2) Employees are observed to change tasks without hand washing or changing gloves. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to re-educate employees about glove changing and hand washing practices. They should also be aware of ongoing practices and enforce safe practices. Ensure hand washing is taking place WHEN it should be in the facility.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

A tray used for hot holding cooked chicken prior to service is observed with encrusted grease deposits and in use. The inspector scraped their fingernail on the item to ensure that it was encrusted grease and not a stain. The PIC was shown and instructed to scrub the trays in order to provide a smooth and easily cleanable (as well as clean) surface for food contact moving forward. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained free of encrusted grease and other contaminants in the facility at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The space above the fries/tater tots hot holding station is heavily soiled with food debris and oil. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all physical facilities are maintained clean at all times.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The ice scoop in the coffee bar is observed to have a broken handle and an employee was observed to use the scoop part of it to scoop the ice with their bare hand. Due to there being no handle on the scoop and ice being a ready-to-eat food, the scoop will come into contact with the ice and the employee’s hand. This allows for contamination to the ice from the scoop. CORRECTED- The PIC provided a new scoop for the coffee bar and discarded the current one. Ensure that all scoops have a handle on them to prevent contamination to food.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: REPEAT- There is no signage observed indicating which sink is the handwashing sink in the bar. There is soap and napkins at one sink that is supposed to be designated as the handwashing sink, but does not have signage indicating it is one. There is also a strainer in this sink that allows for easier dumping of drinks for employees. Handwashing sinks should only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. There needs to be a sign or poster that notifies employees to wash their hands at that handwashing sink. Signs were provided at the last inspection and were once again provided during the inspection today.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzles in the kitchen were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in them. CORRECTED- The PIC had these cleaned during the inspection. An employee stated that they clean these every Tuesday. It is recommended to clean them more often than is currently occurring. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: REPEAT- The top of the inside of the ice machine next to the banquet walk-in cooler is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue. CORRECTED- The PIC had this cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that ice machines are regularly cleaned to prevent this accumulation from occurring.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: REPEAT- The dish machine in the bar area is observed to be reading at 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- EcoLab arrived during the inspection and found that the Chlorine in use was expired. The chemical had gassed off, which is why it was reading at 0ppm of Chlorine. New Chlorine sanitizer was obtained and the PIC was educated by EcoLab on when to change the Chlorine sanitizer. The dish machine read at 100ppm after switching the sanitizer that was in use. Ensure that the dish machine is regularly tested to make sure that it is sanitizing at the label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was a squeeze bottle with mayonnaise in it along the cook line that was observed to be sitting at room temperature among other sauces that are not TCS. Mayonnaise is a TCS food item and should be held at 41F and under. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that he took it out of the cooler this morning and voluntarily discarded it. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety Foods are held at 41F and under.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: REPEAT- There are no ambient thermometers observed to be in four of the coolers (three along the cook line and the cooler on the buffet line). This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that there are thermometers placed inside all mechanically refrigerated or hot food storage units.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: There is observed to be no allergen labeling present on the buffet items in the facility. This was discussed with the PIC. Any buffet/bulk item that the consumer serves themself needs to have Allergen labeling on it. This can be done through a poster, a QR code, images of the allergens, or allergens listed next to each item. Information on this will be provided to the PIC.
citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: REPEAT- The plates in the buffet area are observed to be stored with the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are stored inverted or covered to protect the food- and lip-contact surfaces from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The walk-in freezer is observed to have ice accumulation on the fans and on the ground under the fans. Ensure that the issue causing the accumulation is repaired and that the ice is removed to allow the surfaces to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: There is bare wood exposed in the cabinet under the new triple sink in the coffee bar and under the counters of the coffee bar. This bare wood needs to be sealed due to it being exposed to splash, spillage, and other food soiling. Ensure that this is sealed or painted by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The covers of the fans in the walk-in cooler next to the preparation area in the kitchen have an accumulation of dust on them and are in need of cleaning. 
2. REPEAT- The dish shelves were observed to have an accumulation of dust on them. CORRECTED- These shelves were cleaned during the inspection. 
3. The floor under the preparation area in the banquet area of the kitchen is observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on it. Ensure that this is cleaned. 

Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained clean.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. REPEAT- The coving/wall across from the dish machine is in disrepair. 
2. REPEAT- The cabinet under the coffee machine in the coffee bar appears to be warped and needs to be repaired. In this same area, they are using tape as a repair mechanism for the counter. Tape is not an approved repair mechanism and the cabinet and door need to be properly repaired. 
3. REPEAT- The dish area caulking is in a state of disrepair and needs to be re-caulked. 
4. There is broken coving under the right triple sink across from the mop area that is in need of repair. 

Ensure that all physical facilities are repaired and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was a phone observed to be on a food contact surface in the kitchen. CORRECTED- The employee removed the phone and the table was sanitized. Phones hold a significant amount of bacteria and should never be in contact with a food contact surface. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The gasket of the clear door cooler in the kitchen is observed to be in a state of disrepair. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that this gasket is repaired or replaced by next routine inspection. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was no sanitizer observed to be made in the kitchen at the start of the inspection. The employees were preparing and cooking food. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was made and tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Ensure that sanitizer is made and available during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A pot of potatoes was stored on a crate directly underneath the handwashing sink in the kitchen area. Shown to PIC and the potatoes were moved. Food shall never be stored on the floor or in a manner where they are exposed to contamination.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Cooked breakfast sausages stored on the kitchen’s steam table were probed at 72F. PIC mentioned that the sausages were cooked earlier in the morning around 6am. Discussed the need to either keep the sausages hot held or on time control. PIC will use the steam table from now on to maintain the safety of the food. The sausages were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS (time/temperature control) foods are held at 135F or above to maintain proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Overall, the facility has mostly date marked TCS foods that are stored in house longer than 24 hours, however, a few food items lacked date marking in coolers throughout the facility. Sliced meats, cooked meats, and sauces stored in the back coolers and in the prep coolers along the cook-line were observed without date marking. Ensure that TCS foods stored in house overnight are date marked and used with 7 days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A container of the gravy was observed on the counter at room temperature. PIC mentioned that gravy was cooked earlier in the morning and was placed on the counter to cool. Discussed proper cooling procedures for TCS food items. The gravy was placed into the back standing cooler to finish the cooling process. Be sure that TCS foods are never cooled at room temperature. Instead, place food in cold holding equipment, on ice, or any other effective method of cooling to ensure safety of food.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the facility hot holding various food items in plastic containers on the hot line such as cheese sauces, gravies, and other sauces. Discussed with PIC that the containers are not approved to hold hot foods, nor are they sufficient enough to withstand repeat ware-washings. Instructed the facility to use stainless steel containers to hold hot foods. Ensure that materials used for hot holding are food safety approved, durable, and long lasting. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available along the kitchen’s cook-line. A sanitizer solution was prepared and tested at 100ppm (CL) to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are available in all areas where food prep occurs, including the cook-line and the service station.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed a member of staff put on gloves without washing hands before. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper glove wear. Staff member rewashed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no paper towels to be present at one of the kitchen hand sinks. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand washing sink. Ensure all hand washing sinks are properly equipped with paper towels.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a container of ham located in walk in cooler to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, ham was discarded and education was provided on proper date marking procedure. Ensure all TCS foods kept past their 7 day date marking maximum are discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition.
