(A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair to the right of the dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure caulking is being replaced at a frequency that prevents caulking from getting damaged.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed on two different occasions rinsing hands in the sink without proper soap or using a barrier to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with PIC. When washing hands, be sure to rinse hands first, then add soap and lather hands for at least 10-15 seconds, rinse, dry hands with a disposal towel, and turn off handles using paper towel before discarding.  Ensure that proper cleaning procedures are followed when washing hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed a coffee machine and a tea machine to have soiled grounds in the baskets. This was in a separate area for staging dinners, not in the main kitchen. The dispensers were NOT in use, the food remnants were from a previous service. Discussed with PIC, and the PIC emptied the containers and took them to the dish room. Ensure that all food served to customers is safe. These dispenser baskets can soil fast, ensure they are cleaned out as needed.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed spilled milk at the bottom of the kitchen's reach in milk cooler. Person in charge (PIC) stated that the cooler is cleaned on a weekly basis, but had missed it’s cleaning last week. Continue cleaning schedule and clean spills as they occur.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed multiple white powders throughout the facility (one on the cook-line, and 2 in dry storage) with no label. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed a label on the items. Ensure items that may easily confused with others are labeled once removed from their original packaging to prevent the risk of contaminating food.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: FOURTH REPEAT: The restroom door is not self-closing. A restroom without a self-closer poses a risk of contamination of food products.  Add a self-closer to the restroom door.
citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
5th REPEAT: Mop sink room is mostly unfinished. The following repairs/maintenance activities are needed in the mop room:
-Surfaces surrounding the sink should be smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable. See that the wall to floor is covered/baseboard.
-See that walls are smooth and painted with a semi-gloss paint.
-Caulk sink to wall.
-Ceiling should be smooth and easily cleanable at least over the mop sink area.

A discussion regarding planned reconstruction took place between the inspector and the PIC. PIC stated that the facility has recently merged ownership with their building-mates. Both PICs are balancing assets. A quote for construction has been placed on the room. Further communication will occur between the operator and SCDPH regarding the reconstruction.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 4th REPEAT: Trim tiles along the wall under the 3 compartment sink and dish machine are not sealed to the wall, creating a gap between the tile and the wall. Openings between the floor and wall can allow for the harborage of mold. Seal the wall to floor and eliminate the gap.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
The Food Handler Certificate of one of the kitchen staff was observed to have expired in 2024. PIC is aware of the lapse in certification and has posted a list of companies by which the staff member may renew their certificate. Ensure all staff members have an active Food Handlers card by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the surface to the right of the dish machine is not fully sealed to the wall. The caulking has peeled off creating a gap between the surface and the wall. Ensure that the caulking is properly sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

The hand sink next to the three part sink was observed blocked by a towel container in front and a spray bottle inside of it at the start of the inspection. The items were removed by the inspector to allow for hand washing to correct. The PIC was notified of the situation and instructed to ensure that all hand sinks are accessible at all times in the facility.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The hand sinks in the food preparation area as well as next to the three part sink are without paper towels at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC was shown and replaced the towels to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The spout of the ice chute on the fountain drink machine is observed with pink growth around the lip where ice comes out. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean regularly along with the fountain drink machine nozzles. The item was cleaned during this inspection to correct.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed bar soda gun to be soiled with mold accumulation. Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff is cleaning soda guns at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: At least two employees were observed using bare hands to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. To ensure that hands are getting washed properly, a barrier must be used to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. Be sure to educate all employees on proper handwashing procedures.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed handling a cellular device in the dish room. The employee the reached to handle clean dishes without washing hands. The activity was ceased and the employee was instructed to wash hands before handling clean dishes. Ensure to educate employees on proper phone usage and when to wash hands when contamination occurs.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The dish machine in the dish room was tested at 0ppm CL. The dish machine was cycled several times before contacting a technician to service the machine. A tube was replaced on the dish machine during the inspection and tested again at 100ppm CL to correct the violation. Ensure that chemical sanitizing dish machines test at the manufacturer's recommended concentration to be sure that dishes are getting sanitized properly. 

Also, the sanitizer bucket along the cookline was tested at 0ppm (Quat). Discussed with PIC and the bucket was recreated and tested at 200ppm (quat). Ensure that chemical sanitizers are maintained to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The floor of the walk in freezer was observed with chunks of ice build up. Ensure that the freezer floor is maintained as often as necessary to prevent ice accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: A leak was observed at the faucet of the triple sink stored in the dish room. The leak was dripping from the faucet into the basin of the triple sink. Ensure that faucets are maintained in good repair and in a leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: A cellular phone was stored inside of a drawer filled with clean utensils (various knives) in the kitchen area. Ensure that phones are stored in manner that prevents contamination of clean dishes and utensils.
citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Employee reporting agreements were observed to not be signed. CORRECTED- All present employees signed one and there are only a few other employees. The PIC stated that they will have the other employees sign when they come to work. Ensure that these are kept in a safe space, as they will need to be accessed for all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available in the facility. Mrs. McLemore arrived during this inspection to correct. Ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts/all times that foods are being handled or prepared.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

On arrival the sani bucket anlong the A prep line is observed to registered low on the inspector’s test strips. The PICs were shown and remade the bucket during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The wall behind the drive thru frosty machine has a large section or nudo board that has been damaged and is falling away from the wall. The PIC was shown and directed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

The walk in freezer off of the walk in cooler is observed with a thick accumulation of ice on a majority of the floor. The PIC was instructed to remove the ice and maintain the floor clean moving forward. Ensure that the facilities are maintained clean at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to take their gloves off and then don a new pair of gloves without washing their hands. CORRECTED- The employee was educated that even when only switching gloves, you must wash your hands. Handwashing should be done before putting on gloves and when switching gloves. Ensure that food employees are washing their hands before engaging in food preparation.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a sanitizer bucket on the serving line to be at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- kitchen staff remade sanitizer bucket to a concentration of 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are remade and tested at a frequency to hold the proper concentration- as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed 2 dead insects in a cabinet on the serving line. The PIC is in communication with maintenance- who oversees pest control operations. Inspector will follow up on 09/10/25 to check that the facility has no pests.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed multiple wet sanitizer rags sitting on the counter at the kitchen service counter. CORRECTED- the sanitizer rags were moved into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure wiping cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Observed clean utensils in the drawers of the island facing the cook line to be stored in black bins which were soiled with food debris. PIC was informed and bins were moved to dish area. Ensure staff are cleaning bins frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed multiple plates and bowls being stored with the food contact side up, and uncovered. CORRECTED- the PIC inverted the plates and bowls or moved them under coverings. Ensure food contact surfaces are stored under coverings or inverted to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.[C[

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Inspector observed 2 spatulas hanging in ready to use position on the cook-line to be in disrepair. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) voluntarily discarded the two spatulas. Ensure utensils are checked for integrity to prevent contamination of food. Food contact surfaces should be maintained smooth and easily cleanable.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of dirt, wood chips, and insect droppings in a cabinet at the serving line. While there were no items in storage in this cabinet, nonfood contact surfaces in the facility should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the harborage of pests- see violation #38. A follow up will occur on 09/10/25 to ensure routine cleaning of nonfood contact surfaces is occurring.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket. CORRECTED- the mop was moved to the top to air dry. Ensure mops are stored in a position that allows them to air dry, to prevent the growth of microorganisms.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.

Ensure ongoing education on proper handwashing occurs- including using a barrier to turn off the faucet to prevent food handlers from re-contaminating their hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the handwashing sink at the bar to be out of paper towels. CORRECTED- PIC replaced paper towels. Ensure all sinks designated for handwashing are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels.

Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. comment: Inspector observed open containers of milk and orange juice at the bar without date marking. CORRECTED- The PIC stated the items were opened yesterday and labeled them accordingly. Ensure temperature control for safety (TCS) foods being held over 24 hours are labeled with the date they are opened, and are used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: A spray bottle of clean linen air freshener was observed over clean plates next to the sushi station (nearest the restrooms). CORRECTED- PIC removed the spray bottle from the kitchen. Ensure chemicals are clearly identified and stored away from and under food or food contact surfaces to avoid contaminating food.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: When asked, the PIC indicated that there were no probe thermometers present in the facility. CORRECTED- A second PIC brought two probe thermometers to be used within the facility. Inspector demonstrated thermometer calibration using the ice water method. Ensure probe thermometers are available and calibrated to measure the internal temperatures of TCS foods.
citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use. [Pf]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed three (two in dry storage, and one over the prep cooler on the cook line) containers of white powders lacking a label. CORRECTED- the PIC labeled the items as sugar and salt. Ensure items that may be easily mistaken for other items are labeled with their name to avoid potential contamination of food.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed fly strips hanging throughout areas of food preparation in the kitchen. CORRECTED- PIC had kitchen staff remove the fly strips. Ensure insect control devices are not located over areas of food preparation to prevent contamination of food.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple instances of improper in-use utensil storage:
1) Soup containers were being used as scoops submerged in soy sauce and sugar containers. CORRECTED- PIC removed the containers or replaced them with a ladle. There is no clear hand contact surface on soup containers, which poses a risk of bare hand contamination of food.
2) The handle of the ice scoop at the server station was touching ice. CORRECTED- PIC removed the ice and placed the ice scoop in a cup. 

Ensure ready to eat (RTE) food items (that require no further processing or cooking) contain scoops with handles. Ensure the handle is sticking outward and the food contact surface is in the food to prevent cross contamination from bare hand contact.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed leaks from base of two faucets in the kitchen (on the cookline and in the dish area). Per discussion with PICs, the sinks will need to be removed from the wall to tighten the fitting. See that the leaks are repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Multiple personal items, such as personal drinks, personal food, hats, and first aid supplies were observed throughout the kitchen during today’s inspection. CORRECTED- PIC moved the personal items to an area away from food for service. Inspector recommends setting a designated space for personal items that is separate and below foods intended for service, to protect foods for service from contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observed more food handlers at the facility than there are food handler certificates (inspector was provided with 4 food handler’s cards). All kitchen staff, bar tenders, and wait staff are required to obtain a food handler’s card within 30 days of hire. Ensure all employees have a food handler’s card by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The three employees at the facility are without reporting agreements or other versions at the time of this inspection. Clean copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement were given and filled out during this inspection to correct. Ensure that reporting agreements are maintained for all food handlers at the facility at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen was without paper towels. The PIC refilled the dispenser during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are fully and correctly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The fry slicer is observed soiled at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several fruit flies/gnats are observed in the vicinity of the fry slicer in the kitchen during this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact pest control for maintenance. A follow-up is being scheduled for 10 days to ensure that the situation has been brought into compliance.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice machine to have a build up of bacteria/mold to be present. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning ice machine at a frequency that prevents build up.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed multiple boxes of food to be in contact with an icicle forming under fan unit in walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, items within boxes are sealed. Upon inspection, TCS items within boxes were untouched by ice. PIC relocated boxes and walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure any food item being stored is protected from any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed walk in freezer to have excessive amounts of ice accumulation forming under fan unit. Discussed with PIC, walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure equipment is maintained and working up to manufacter’s standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Sanitizer bucket tested at 0 ppm during inspection. PIC was made aware and PIC had the Sani bucket remade. Ensure that the sanitizer in the sani bucket is tested at a regular frequency to ensure that sanitizer remain at the appropriate concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket in the sushi and asian market area is observed to not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was shown and replaced the buckets during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at correct concentration at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The pineapple slicer in the area to the west side of the hot line is observed with dry food debris on it. When asked the nearby employee stated that they were not sure the last time that it had been used as it wasted a lot of pineapple and they have been slicing by hand for some time. This leads to the conclusion that it was not properly cleaned when it was put away and left soiled for a long period of time. 2) Multiple large buckets are used for preparing tea (per the PIC) and are stored on the shelves with remaining tea residue on them. They are also still partially wet from cleaning. The PIC had the items cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The display cooler used for cake slices along the service line is observed with a holding temperature of 57F. Most items in this cooler are not TCS foods and so are not a concern. There is a box of sour cream packets in the container though that bares a label requiring refrigeration. This was discussed with the PIC and the sour cream packets discarded to correct the immediate concern. The PIC indicated that they would be putting in a work order for the cooler moving forward.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several flies (at least 8-10) are observed by the mop sink and adjacent tanks. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency (EcoLab) for maintinance. They did mention that EcoLab had already been planning on starting a fly based plan in the facility. This should probably be pushed forward and implemented immediately. The normal follow-up schedule would land on a weekend and will be pushed back to the following Monday.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Multiple rags used for wiping counters are observed stored on the counters in the facility. These items were pointed out to the PIC and discussed. They should be stored between uses in their sani buckets that are maintained at proper concentration. The rags were moved to the sani buckets to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink in the produce walk in cooler/prep area is observed with a gap forming in the caulking sealing it to the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to reseal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure a that all facilities are smooth and easily cleanable where water and moisture is consistently in abundance.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

One of the doors on the employee side of the display cooler used for pasta salad has several pieces of duck tape being used as a repair medium. Duck tape is not an approved method of making repairs as it allows for mold/pathogen growth. The location was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair properly prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day.

1) Two opened gallons of milk in the standing cooler at the end of the prep line are observed without date marking. Neither the PIC or the worker knew when the containers had been opened. 2) A gallon of milk is partially used and bares a date marking of 8/20. This indicates that it should have been discarded at the end of last night at the latest. All three containers of milk were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Education should trickle down to the employees working in this area to ensure that this situation does not repeat in the future.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several flies (at least 8-10) are observed by the mop sink and adjacent tanks. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency (EcoLab) for maintinance. They did mention that EcoLab had already been planning on starting a fly based plan in the facility. This should probably be pushed forward and implemented immediately. The normal follow-up schedule would land on a weekend and will be pushed back to the following Monday.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

A piece of equipment next to the grill is observed with encrusted food residue in the gaps/crack provided by cracked aluminum tape. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and then re-seal the spaces prior to the next routine inspection. The PIC then indicated that this equipment was unused and a leftover from when Wahlburger’s was here. He stated that it would be discarded prior to the next inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink next to the mop sink is observed pulling away from the wall, which is producing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facility equipment is maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The owner’s Food Protection Manager Certification has expired. The owner is currently in the process of renewing her managers license. Ensure that there is at least 2 employees that are manager certified to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.Q

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off faucet handles after the handwashing process. Discussed proper handwashing procedures with PIC. Ensure that a barrier (paper towel) is used to operate faucet handles after washing hands to avoid recontaminating freshly washed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Cooked tater tots were observed at room temperature and was tempted at 94F. Discussed with PIC that cooked potatoes are considered TCS (time/temperature control for safety) and will need to be hot held. PIC placed tater tots and fries under a heat lamp to correct the violation. Be sure that TCS foods are maintained at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available for the bar area. Discussed with the PIC and a bucket was prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat). Ensure there is a sani bucket present in both the bar and kitchen area during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of a deep cleaning: 
- floors and walls around/behind pieces of equipment
- shelves of kitchen equipment
-outer surfaces of table top cooking equipment

Ensure that non food contact surfaces and physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup of food and grease debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed plates at the sushi station and in the kitchen to be face up. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) moved some of the plates underneath the counter at the kitchen, and inverted those that didn’t fit. Plates at the sushi station were moved to a lower rack, so that they could be under a cover. Ensure this practice continues to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the ice machine baffles have an accumulation of debris. The ice machine must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 9/8/2025 to check that the ice baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the ice machine scoop was stored with the handle touching the ice. The PIC was informed and the ice scoop was moved during the inspection. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are stored with the handles above the top of food to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is a gap between the hand washing sink and the wall. Ensure that the hand washing sink is sealed to the wall (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed both water fountains to contain an accumulation of mineral buildup and limescale. A follow up will occur on 09/09/25 to check that the water fountain has been cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the buildup of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: SECOND REPEAT- A gap that is approximately 1 cubic centimeter in area was observed at the bottom left corner along the threshold of the emergency exit door near the restrooms. A small gap could allow for the entrance of pests into the facility. Ensure the gap is sealed to eliminate a potential entry point for pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed debris along multiple nonfood contact surfaces:
1) The last triple cooler labeled “cold drinks”
2) The “Fresh Foods” cooler
3) The first triple freezer labeled “Frozen foods”
4) The third triple freezer labeled “Frozen foods”
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Gaps were observed in the coving (covering between the floor and wall) in the back storage area, as well as where two walls meet about 20’ away from the office. Seal gaps to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Gaps between surfaces that expose bare wood or dry wall can harbor mold or other microorganisms. Ensure gaps are sealed or covered by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed employee to be washing cups/dumping liquids down hand sink. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and practice will be stopped. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a container of juice concentrate in use to be held past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, item was pulled and discarded. Ensure all TCS items are discarded after their 7 day date marking maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the microwave above batter station to be soiled with food debris/splash. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands in the three part sink as they entered the unit after having lunch. Education was conduced with the PIC and they are instructed to review with all employees as applicable. Always wash hands correctly and in a designated hand sink.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
(REEPAT x2) 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

1) There are tears in the mesh door used for entering the unit by employees. 2) The roof grate has a mesh covering that has come loose and is no longer preventing pest entry. 3) The fan at the back wall of the unit in the corner away from the door is not functioning while the vent is open. These items are allowing for the entrance of pests and should be fixed. These items will be re-evaluated at the follow-up being scheduled in 10 days.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

1) Several flies of both the house and fruit/gnat variations are observed in the mobile unit while it is in operation. Several fly strips are observed in use at this time but do not appear to be sufficient for the current needs. 2) Several gnats/fruit flies are observed in the storage shed in the vicinity of the bags of onions. Both situations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to remedy them prior to the follow-up. Ten days lands on a Saturday, therefore the follow-up is being scheduled for the following Monday.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is a buildup of frost on the white reach-in freezers in the downstairs main kitchen. The freezers must be defrosted at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of frost. Ensure that the freezers are defrosted to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of dust on the walk-in cooler fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed multiple TCS foods being kept in walk in cooler that were kept longer than there 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were discarded. Ensure all TCS foods are date marked and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed street corn dip to be thawing in the basin of the triple sink. Discussed with PIC, inspector provided proper thawing education and dip was submerged under running water. Ensure when thawing items are kept submerged under running water or in a cooler.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the soda nozzle holder at the bar to contain an accumulation of soil debris. Person in charge (PIC) stated the facility switched from Coke to Pepsi, and they may have left an older nozzle holder. CORRECTED- PIC wiped the area with a clean sanitizer rag. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed dried food splash and other food debris accumulated in the microwave’s interior. CORRECTED- PIC wiped the interior of the microwave with a clean sanitizing rag. An accumulation of debris on nonfood contact surfaces may serve as a source of contamination for ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed handle of salad tong to be resting in contact with salad within cooler. Discussed with PIC, tong was relocated to a plate near salad cooler. Ensure only food contact surfaces of utensils are in contact with food.
citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed prep cooler next to salad dispenser to be cold holding at 52F. Discussed with PIC, inspector will follow up on cooler on September 1, 2025. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed bar soda gun to be soiled with black mold. Discussed with PIC, soda gun was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda gun nozzles are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents mold buildup.
citation_text: 4-101.11(A) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (A) Safe.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non food contact areas to be soiled with food splash:
1) Inside doors of freezer to the right of hood system.
2) Inside doors of prep cooler across from hood system. 
3) Microwave above pizza prep cooler. 

Discussed with PIC, the following areas will be cleaned. Ensure non-food contact areas are being kept at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the caulking at the back kitchen handsink to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be cleaned and replaced. Ensure staff is monitoring and replacing caulking throughout facility regularly.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT-Bar hand sink is not caulked to the wall. Discussed with PIC, and PIC said she would have it caulked to the wall as soon as possible. Ensure this is caulked to the wall so that the surface transition is smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw shell eggs stored above buttermilk and bleu cheese dressing in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was informed and the items were switched on the shelves. Ensure raw shell eggs are never stored above ready-to-eat (RTE) foods to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: FIRST REPEAT: All Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificates have expired. Discussed CFPM course and proctoring with person in charge (PIC). The PIC had 2 of the same educational sheet regarding accredited programs from the Sangamon County Department of Public Health from previous inspectors. All facilities serving food are required to have a CFPM on staff and scheduled during all shifts. CFPMs decrease the incidence of a food-borne illnesses, decrease the number of critical violations, and demonstrate proper food safety practices to their staff.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the soap dispenser at the back handwashing sink (across from the triple sink) to not be working during today’s inspection. PIC is waiting on a new dispenser to be delivered. Ensure all food handlers are using one of the two hand sinks that are fully supplied and working until the back hand sink is stocked and in working order. A follow up will occur on 09/08/25 to ensure all sinks are fully supplied and are in working order.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The paper towel dispenser at the back handwashing sink (across from the triple sink) was not working during today’s inspection. PIC stated a new battery had been ordered for the dispenser and will be delivered soon. Ensure all hand washing sinks are always supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels. A follow up is scheduled for 09/08/25 to ensure today’s violation is corrected.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed two sanitizer buckets located at the barista station to be tested at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- PIC remade and tested sanitizer buckets to a proper concentration of 200 ppm. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed (and checked with facility’s test strips) at a frequency to maintain the proper concentration as recommended the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: Inspector observed the caulking between the splashguards and the sink at the donut prep hank sink to be deteriorated. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent the harborage of mold and other microorganisms. Clean and re-caulk this surface before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas to be soiled with debris:
1) The floor on the North side of the drive through station (under the register).
2) The floor under the triple sink.
Inspector discussed the areas that need cleaning with the PIC. Floors should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the build up of soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Shelves of the prep table in the middle of the kitchen and floors behind equipment and underneath the triple sink were observed with accumulated food debris. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent build up of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The facility could not locate any signed employee health forms. Blank forms were provided to the facility for employees to complete. The forms were signed to correct the violation. Ensure that health forms are available and accessible for future routine inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: A personal drink was observed stored on top of the dish machine. Discussed with PIC the potential for cross contamination of clean dishes. Ensure that personal drinks are never stored in manner that can contaminate food items, single service items, or food contact surfaces. The drink was removed to correct the violation.
citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: An employee moved a trash can with gloved hands and then proceeded to handling food without switching gloves. The activity was ceased and corrected. Ensure that single service gloves are limited to one task and if tasks are interrupted, be sure to remove gloves, wash hands, and don new gloves.
citation_text: 3-304.15(A) Gloves, Use Limitation. (A) If used, single-use gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with ready-to-eat food or with raw animal food, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
