comment: The soda gun in the bar area was observed soiled with dried liquids. Discussed and shown to PIC. The soda gun was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent build up.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: A pan of gravy stored on the stovetop was observed at room temperature. PIC mentioned that the facility planned to reheat the gravy later in the day. Discussed with PIC that TCS (temperature/time control) foods must be either cold held or hot held to ensure safety of food items. PIC mentioned that he got distracted and that the gravy was mistakenly left at room temperature from the early morning. The gravy was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that foods that are hot held are maintained at 135F or above and never held at room temperature.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A large container of cooked chicken broth was observed actively cooling at room temperature (with lid on container). Discussed with PIC proper methods for cooling TCS foods. A cooling handout was given to the facility as reference. The broth was portioned into shallow pans to allow for the broth to cool quickly and efficiently. If using the shallow pan method for cooling, ensure that TCS foods are placed in smaller portions and in shallow pans to allow for the item to cool within the proper timeframe for safety.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The standing Pepsi cooler in the service area was observed with an ambient temperature of 50F. A container of cream cheese was probed at 46F. The facility adjusted the temperature knob to a higher number that is sufficient enough for properly cold hold. The temperature of the cooler was observed at 41F after adjusting the temperature knob. Be sure that cold holding equipment is maintained at 41F or below in order to ensure proper cold holding temperatures for TCS foods.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Portions of cooked rice were observed in the walk in cooler in plastic bags. Discussed and shown to PIC. The bags of rice were discarded. Ensure that foods are never stored in plastic bags, as it is not an approved food contact surface, nor is it durable and sufficient enough to withstand repeated ware-washing.  

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed 2 chlorinated bleach bottles, as well as the dispenser on the wall to be at 0 ppm Cl. Chlorine sanitizer must be measured between 50-200 ppm Cl to effectively sanitize food contact surfaces. A follow up inspection will occur on 08/29/25 to ensure that the chlorine sanitizer dispenser is dispensing sanitizer solution at an appropriate concentration. Use quaternary ammonia solution to clean food contact surfaces until the chlorine dispenser is serviced and observed dispensing the appropriate concentration of sanitizer.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: An accumulation of grease was observed on the hood, baffles, and fire suppression nozzles of the hood vent system over the facility’s fryer. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination on ready to eat foods, and also pose a fire risk to the facility. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease or other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a significant amount of debris and soil accumulation underneath the soda boxes in the facility’s dry storage area. The harborage of soil accumulation may attract pests. Facilities should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the build up of soil debris. Ensure shelving is being moved to clean the floors.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee at the grill station used their barehand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed knives at the deli stored with the blade in the gap between the prep cooler and prep counter. The PIC and deli employees were informed that the knives could become contaminated stored inside the gap. The knives were moved into a new location during the inspection. Ensure that in-use utensils are stored in a location that is routinely cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The particle board holding utensils on the wall outside the main walk-in cooler and the wall by the prep cooler in the on-the-go room must be sealed (ex. painted). 

(2) The plastic cornering in the small dish washing room (near the tray line kitchen) by the entrance and the large dish washing room by the dish machine have fallen off the wall and must be replaced/repaired.

Ensure that all the above referenced are repaired/replaced/sealed to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the internal fans in the grill double door cooler have an accumulation of dust and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed there is a leak in the hand washing sink in the small dish washing room (near to the tray line kitchen). Ensure that the leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of soil debris and a biolfilm:
1) The back of the baffles of the ice machine.
2) Dr. Pepper, Diet Coke, Coke, Tea, and Mellow Yellow soda nozzles at the server station.
3) Soda nozzle at the bar.
4) Soda nozzle inlet at the bar.
CORRECTED- all of the items mentioned above were cleaned and sanitized. The ice baffles and soda nozzle inlet at the bar were wiped with a clean sanitation rag. The soda nozzles were taken to the triple sink to be washed and sanitized. These surfaces are considered food contact surfaces and could serve as a source of contamination.  Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of biofilms and soil debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Consumer advisory provided for raw/undercooked food.
comment: Inspector observed no consumer advisory in the menu. A discussion occurred with the person in charge (PIC), and while most burgers are fully cooked, some customers do request to have their hamburgers not fully cooked. Inspector left consumer advisory guidelines with the PIC. The next time the menu is printed the facility must include a disclosure (using words such as “raw” or undercooked”, or an asterisk that leads to the reminder), and a reminder regarding the increased risk of food-borne illness associated with consuming undercooked animal proteins. Correct by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-603.11(C) Consumption of Animal Foods that are Raw, Undercooked, or Not Otherwise Processed to Eliminate Pathogens. (C) REMINDER shall include asterisking the animal-derived FOODS requiring DISCLOSURE to a footnote that states: (1) Regarding the safety of these items, written information is available upon request; (2) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness; or (3) Consuming raw or undercooked MEATS, POULTRY, seafood, shellfish, or EGGS may increase your RISK of foodborne illness, especially if you have certain medical conditions. [C]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a wet sanitizer rag on the bar counter at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- the sanitizer rag was moved to the sanitizer bucket. Wet sanitizer rags left out may allow for the growth and harborage of bacteria. Ensure wet sanitizer cloths are stored in a sanitizer bucket in between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Observed microwave above hot holding station to be soiled with food splash. CORRECTED- the PIC wiped the interior of the microwave with a wet sanitizer cloth. Nonfood contact surfaces that contain an accumulation of soil debris can allow for the contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure staff is cleaning non-food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the basin of the hand washing sink within the ware washing room is rusting. Ensure that the hand washing sink is replaced or the rust removed to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee used their barehand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were sanitizer buckets observed to be in the kitchen handwashing sink and in the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- The PIC moved both of them out of the sink into their respective places. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for anything other than the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of cooked penne dated 8/14 and a container of coleslaw dated 8/16. CORRECTED- Both food items were discarded due to being past the 7 day date-marking rule. The PICs were educated that any item that is prepared or cooked needs to be date-marked and discarded after seven days (day 1 being the date of opening or preparation).
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a container of breaded raw eel and a container of raw shrimp that were observed to be above a container of cut ginger in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The ginger was moved over to avoid being under the raw eel and raw shrimp. The PIC was educated on proper storage order and appeared to be educated on it. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The dish shelf is observed to have slight soil residue accumulation on it. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that these are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Food handler training
comment:
There are three employees other than the PIC, who is a Certified Food Protection Manager, that are observed to not have a food handler certificate. This was discussed with the PIC who was educated that all employees who are handling food need to have their food handler certificate. Ensure that all food handling employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria at all times. 

Multiple buckets of sanitizer in the facility are observed with low concentrations on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was unaware of the last time that the buckets had been remade and replaced the buckets during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at correct concentrations at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Containers of whipped topping and half n’ half are observed at room temperature next to the rack used for storing prepared sandwiches. An internal temperature was taken and showed 71.5 F. All three observed containers had manufacturer labeling indicating the refrigeration is required for these products at all times. The items were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. The PIC stated that these items were normally stored in the cooler under this location. Ensure that these items are stored correctly in temperature control at all times moving forward.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple food contact single service storage locations around the kitchen are observed with dust and debris in contact with the single service items. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the locations and to keep the locations cleaned moving forward. Ensure that all single service items are stored in such a way as to be protected from contamination prior to use.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
citation_text:
5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. 

The drain under the customer service shelving is observed backed up and believed to be clogged. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the drain unclogged prior to the follow up in three days. Ensure that all drains are maintained a state where they remain functional at al times.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed chicken being stored in plastic grocery bags in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC and PIC removed chicken from grocery bag. Ensure that meat is stored in food safe bags.
citation_text: 3-302.11 Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Observed there was not signed employee health reporting agreements at the facility. The PIC was provided with blank copies for employees to sign. The inspector will follow-up on 9/3/2025 to check that all employees have signed the reporting agreements.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed the PIC used their bare hand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw beef stored over milk in the kitchen cooler and raw beef stored over various packaged pastries in the storage shed cooler. The PIC was educated and the raw beef was moved onto the bottom shelves during the inspection. Ensure that raw meat is always stored below ready-to eat foods to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The frost accumulation in the kitchen reach-in freezer and storage shed ice cream freezer - the freezers must be defrosted. 

(2) The gap between the mop sink and the wall - the mop sink must be sealed to the wall (ex. caulking).

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that there is a significant buildup of grease and dust on the kitchen fan stored on top of the ice machine. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the fan is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the basin of the  handwashing sink at the facility’s bar to be obstructed by a container of Clorox wipes. CORRECTED- the wipes were removed. Ensure handwashing sinks are made available for handwashing only at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.[Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Multiple food contact surfaces were found to contain an accumulation of soil debris:
1) Back of the ice baffles in the large server prep room.
2) Soda nozzles of the bar server station.
CORRECTED- the ice machine was emptied and wiped with a clean sanitizer rag. The soda nozzles were removed to be cleaned, brushed, and sanitized.
Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris. This frequency may need to increase with use and variable outdoor temperatures.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiples areas in the facility needing repair:
1) Under the left side of the sink at the dish machine there are multiple tiles that have come loose from the wall.
2) The walls on either side of the mop sink contain exposed wood. Ensure the walls are covered with a smooth, easily cleanable surface to prevent the harborage of mold. 
3) The bar hand-sink needs caulked to the wall. Facilities that cannot be moved for cleaning should be adhered to the wall to be made smooth and easily cleanable.
Ensure repairs are made by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
None of the facility’s CFMs have allergen awareness certificates. Discussion was had between inspector and PIC, and inspector gave the PIC a list of accredited institutes for allergen awareness training. Certified Food Protection Managers are required to obtain allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.[C]

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11 Inspector observed raw pork being stored over cooked food. Discussed with PIC, and (CORRECTED) PIC moved the raw pork underneath the cooked food. Ensure that meat is stored in correct order to prevent cross-contamination. 

(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Three areas were observed in need of painting or refinishing:

-The ramp on the floor going into the kitchen area needs repainted. The old paint has worn away, allowing the bare wood underneath to show.

-The cart in the kitchen is rusted and dirty. Ensure the cart is cleaned and repainted to keep the surface clean, smooth, and durable.

-One side of the triple sink has a rusted metal plate on it. Ensure this area is cleaned and refinished or repainted to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. The shelf above the sink needs cleaned as well.

-The triple sink now has several gaps where caulking is needed. Ensure that all gaps in the metal on the triple sink are caulked.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Several ceiling tiles in the northwest corner of the kitchen are falling from the ceiling, one was observed broken. Discussed with PIC. Ensure these tiles are repaired so that the ceiling is smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Inspector observed the servers station soda nozzles to contain a small amount of soils. Ensure these nozzles are cleaned frequently enough to keep them clean. If soaking doesn’t remove soils, scrubbing may be necessary. CORRECTED PIC took off nozzles, had them scrubbed and sanitized, and replaced on to the machine.

Inspector observed the can opener on the line to have a build-up of food debris. Discussed with PIC and (CORRECTED) PIC had the can opener washed in the dish machine immediately. Ensure the can opener is cleaned frequently enough to keep it clean, or every 4 hours during use.

Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-703.11(C)(1) Inspector observed the bar dish machine to be dispensing 0ppm of chlorine sanitizer. Inspector primed the machine for 30s and ran it again. Chlorine was still measuring around 0ppm. Ensure this machine is serviced so that it can properly dispense sanitizer. Use the triple sink at the bar to sanitize dishes until the machine can be serviced and tested again. Inspector will return Thursday, 8/28/2025, to re-test the machine.

Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (1) Except as specified under Subparagraph (C)(2) of this section, a contact time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution specified under 4-501.114(A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Inspector observed a plastic service container of orange juice being stored in the water cooler to be 48.7F (Probed). Container was labeled 8/30/2025, which means it was prepared two days ago. PIC voluntarily threw out the orange juice. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored at 41F or below.

Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 Inspector observed 10-15 flies in the dry storage area. Ensure that all food-storage areas are kept free of pests. Discussed with PIC. Facility can use fly strips or stunning lights as long as they are not stored directly over food or utinsels. Inspector will check again during the Thursday, 8/28 follow-up. If pest presence is not dealt with by then, inspector will spot check later on.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulk behind the dish table to be cracked and peeling. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the caulk is replaced to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface transition between the dish table and wall.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Metal shelving used for container storage in dry storage was observed to be rusted. Shelving will need to be painted or replaced so that the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed there was quat sanitizer spray bottles that were not labeled. The PIC labeled the bottles during the inspection. Ensure that containers for toxic materials removed from the bulk supplies are always labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the unused cooler drawers under the grill have an accumulation of debris. The PIC was reminded that unused equipment must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the drawers are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Two cheesecakes were observed in the sliding cooler without date marking. Education occurred about date marking requirements- items taken from freezing to cooling must be marked with the date that they are moved into thawing. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) marked the items with the date the items were moved into refrigeration. Ensure items moved into thawing are marked with the original date they were moved into thawing. Those food items must be used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- The probe thermometer in the facility’s hot holding was observed to be broken. CORRECTED- the PIC brought out a working probe thermometer to be used and the broken thermometer was voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 4-203.11 Temperature Measuring Devices, Food. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±1°C in the intended range of use. (B) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand sink in the kitchen to have no available soap or paper towel for proper handwashing. The PIC was informed that proper handwashing is vital for safe food handling. citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation
