citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the ice machine baffles to have visible mold accumulation. PIC was informed that these baffles directly contact ice, which poses a cross-contamination concern. A follow-up will be conducted on September 9, 2025 to ensure the ice machine has been deep cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
Inspector observed house flies present in the kitchen near the triple sink. There was a bin of soiled wash cloths stored on the floor which seemed to be attracting the flies. Inspector suggests sealing soiled cloths in bags each night to prevent pest development. 

Inspector also observed a small swarm of gnats/drain flies present underneath the bar near the hand sink. The floors were damp and heavily soiled, which may be contributing to pest development. See violation #55 for floor cleaning details. 

A follow-up will be conducted on September 9th, 2025 to ensure the presence of pests has reduced and professional pest control has been conducted in the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

Observed floors in kitchen underneath fryers to be heavily soiled with grease residue. The floors behind the bar were also observed heavily soiled. Clean floors in kitchen and bar.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment:
Inspector observed a low risk establishment selling cut melon, cut pumpkin, and samosas. The samosas were not packaged, and set so that customers could self serve with tongs into a to-go clam shell container.  Due to the fact that the facility is only permitted as a low risk establishment, there is to be no food handling.
CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) removed the aforementioned items from service. If the facility is interested in increasing their risk classification permit, they must have a pre-opening with the Food Program Manager of Sangamon County Department of Public Health. Any facility handling food is required to have a hand sink for hand washing, and a triple sink so that utensils can be appropriately washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
citation_text: 3-201.11(A) Compliance with Food Law. (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(D) The facility triple sink had a sanitizing concentration lower than 50ppm. The water for the faucet was too hot and the chemical was off-gassing. Concentration was tested at a proper 200ppm as the water temperature was lowered. Hands should be able to be submerged in the dish water (keep under 110F). 

Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 Inspector observed employees donning gloves without handwashing in between tasks. Education was carried out and PIC was made aware about washing hands before donning gloves.  Ensure that hands are washed properly before donning gloves when switching in between tasks.  

When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.16(B)  (REPEAT X2) Inspector observed the coving under the handwashing sink in the back prep area to be coming off the wall. Discussed with PIC. PIC ensured inspector that the coving will be resealed to the wall.  Ensure that this coving is resealed to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 


Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-501.14 Inspector observed the accumulation of mold and soil in the ventilation duct above the dry storage area. PIC was made aware of the mold buildup. PIC ensured inspector that the duct would be clean appropriately. Ensure that the vent duct is monitored and clean at a regular frequency to avoid contamination of foods items. 

Cleaning Ventilation Systems, Nuisance and Discharge Prohibition. (A) Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. (B) If vented to the outside, ventilation systems may not create a public health HAZARD or nuisance or unLAWful discharge.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
comment: On arrival there is not a procedure available for cleaning up vomit/diarrheal events. A new copy of the procedure given by this department was distributed to correct.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: On arrival the CL based sanitizer in the unit are far to strong for safe use around food. The solution was diluted during this inspection to acceptable levels to correct.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the PIC could not locate the signed employee health reporting agreements. The PIC was provided with blank copies for all employees to sign today. The signed agreements should be stored in a location where they are always available upon request. The inspector will follow-up on 9/2/2025 to check that the employee health reporting agreements have been signed by all employees.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of debris inside of the ice machine (THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION) and ice bucket at the bar. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. The inspector will follow-up on 9/2/2025 to check that the ice machine and ice bucket have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed there are a significant number of flies at the facility within the kitchen. The facility grills outside and flies enter the facility when the door is opened and closed. The inspector suggested various solutions, such as fly strips near the doorway (must be placed away from food contact surfaces), air curtains, mesh netting over the door, and contacting a pest control company for more recommendations. The inspector will follow-up on 9/2/2025 to check on flies in the kitchen.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 

(1) The food debris on the bottom shelf of the freezer in the kitchen and single door freezer in the outside dry-storage shed. 

(2) The dust on the shelves holding clean dishes above the triple sink. 

(3) The dust and grease on the vent in the kitchen ceiling. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that the PIC could not locate food handler certificates for all employees. Ensure that all employees have basic food handler training and certificates are kept at the facility by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: SECOND REPEAT: An accumulation of soil debris was observed on the baffle of the ice machine. CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) cleaned and sanitized the baffle of the ice machine. Clean the ice machine as often as necessary to prevent growth of microorganisms.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed salmon in the walk in cooler still in its reduced oxygen packaging. Salmon packages contained a label to remove from the reduced oxygen environment upon thawing. CORRECTED- the PIC placed small cuts in the packages to take the food out of a potentially harmful environment.Ensure salmon and other packages that are in a reduced oxygen environment are opened for proper thawing to prevent the growth of Clostridium botulinum- the causative agent of Botulism
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed soil accumulation in multiple nonfood contact surfaces in the facility:
1) The inside of the microwave on the cook-line contained an accumulation of food debris.
2) A container holding clean utensils contained food debris and grease. CORRECTED- the bin holding the utensils was brought to the triple sink to be clean and sanitation.
Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of food debris, to prevent contamination of ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the kitchen floors underneath the fryers in the kitchen to contain a significant amount of grease and soil accumulation. Accumulations of grease could contribute to pest harborage and contamination. Ensure the physical facility is cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- No food handler certificate is available for the food employees during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Inspector provided website to receive Food Handler certificates on the back of their business card. Keep food handler certificates available on file for review during inspections.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the baffles of the ice machine to contain a small accumulation of soil debris. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) wiped the ice baffles cleaned, and stated they are cleaned on a weekly basis. Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch. The frequency of cleaning may need adjusted with increased use and temperatures outside.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the top of the microwave’s interior to contain an accumulation of food debris. CORRECTED- the PIC was informed of the accumulation and wiped the area with a clean sanitizer cloth. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation or food debris, or other materials that may contaminate ready to eat (RTE) foods.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The Person-In-Charge (PIC) is not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). The PIC stated that the other PIC is currently working on getting their certificate. Information on classes was provided. Ensure that there are multiple CFPMs to cover all hours of operation and food preparation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM on site during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The PIC did not have signed employee reporting agreements for any of the three employees currently working at the facility. This was discussed with the operator and copies were provided. A follow up will be conducted on 9/2/2025 to ensure that there is a signed employee reporting agreement for all employees.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was a container of raw chicken skewers above containers of peanut sauce. CORRECTED- These were moved to the bottom shelf next to the other raw chicken in the cooler and education was conducted regarding storage order. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during preparation, holding, storage, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were clean cutting boards stored behind the faucets of the triple sink in the kitchen. CORRECTED- These cutting boards were cleaned and moved onto a dish shelf to be stored. This was discussed with the PIC and they were educated that the wall and faucet the cutting boards were touching are not clean surfaces. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The facility holds their bean sprouts on an ice bath due to lack of cooler space. The bean sprouts are in water in a container, which is sitting on ice. The ice bath did not sufficiently submerge the bottom of the container of the bean sprouts to allow for proper cold holding. The bean sprouts were probed to be at 60F at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The PIC was educated on how to properly make an ice bath to allow for proper cold holding. The ice bath needs to submerge the sides of the container. The ice bath was corrected and the sprouts were probed to be at 41F. Ensure that TCS foods are cold held at 41F and below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There is not a probe thermometer available in the facility. It is important to have a probe thermometer to ensure that food is being cooked to the correct temperature. A follow up is scheduled for 9/2/2025 to ensure that a probe thermometer is obtained. Education for calibration of the thermometer will be conducted as well.
citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility does not have test strips for the sanitizer that they are using. They are currently using a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer and need to have Quaternary ammonium test strips available to check the concentration of the sanitizer. If using another type of sanitizer (such as Lactic Acid or bleach (Chlorine)), you also need test strips for that type of sanitizer. The PIC was educated on this and was shown photos of what the test strips look like. A follow up is scheduled for 9/2/2025 to ensure that test strips have been obtained for the sanitizers used within the facility.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT- The stainless steel wall covering to the wall left of the wok is observed to be in need of being sealed to the wall. Ensure that this is sealed and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed a handwashing sink in the kitchen (sushi bar side) to be blocked by two stacked 5 gallon sanitizer buckets at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) moved the sanitizer buckets aside. Ensure handwashing sinks are accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the handwashing sink in the middle line of the kitchen (nearest the walk in cooler and freezer) to be out of soap. CORRECTED- the inspector notified the PIC, who refilled the soap. Ensure hand washing sinks are supplied with warm running water, soap, and paper towels at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed four dented cans (baby corn, oyster sauce, ketchup, and water chestnuts) in dry storage. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the dented cans to a separate area to be returned to their distributor. Ensure staff who are accepting deliveries check for dents in cans (particularly along the 3 seams of the can) and integrity of food items. Dented cans can lead to bacterial growth and food contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There was an open container of carrots and an open container of sprouts that were observed to be stored under the fan unit in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and they were educated on the risk for contamination that this poses. All food items should be covered in coolers. Lids were placed on both containers. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by being stored in a package, in a covered container, or a wrapping.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a significant amount of soil debris accumulation on the soda nozzles in the kitchen (near the sliding class cooler). CORRECTED- PIC removed the soda nozzles to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitation buckets at the grill contained no observable sanitizer concentration- 0 ppm Cl. CORRECTED- PIC remade sanitizer buckets to 50 ppm (bucket behind grill) and 200 ppm Cl (bucket by kitchen door). Monitor sanitizer concentration with facility’s test strips. Ensure sanitizer is at the concentration recommended by the manufacture’s label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
There were multiple instances where TCS food is not being held at 41F and under: 

1. There was a container of spicy mayo by the sushi bar. This is a sauce that is made in-house and is made with mayonnaise. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that this has likely been sitting out for days and voluntarily discarded it. All sauces made in-house should be held at 41F and under (and should be date marked). 
2. The walk-in cooler was observed to have an ambient temperature of 48F. The PIC stated that there was a company that fixed the fans yesterday. Upon further investigation, the walk-in cooler had been set this high since yesterday. CORRECTED- The PIC re-set the temperature to 37F and the temperature dropped down to under 41F. The following items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC that had been in the cooler since yesterday: 5 containers of 5 pounds of peeled garlic (probed at 46.5F, 46.4F, 47.4, 46.6, and 46.4), approximately 1300 eggs (8 containers of 180 eggs that probed at 48.3F, 47F, 47F, 47F, 49.7F, 46.4F, 46.9F, and 47.6F), and 56 containers of tofu (5 boxes each containing 12 blocks of tofu that probed to be at 46.4F, 46.3F, 46.5F, 46.3F, and 46.5F). All other items were allowed to be kept due to being delivered today, prepped today, or were sauces that were acidic enough to inhibit bacterial growth.
Ensure that TCS items are held at 41F or under.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The cold holding buffet line is observed to not be properly holding TCS items at 41F and under. On the line, the following items were probed: pork (52.9F), octopus (48F), crab (53F), sprouts (52F), and noodles (49F). CORRECTED- The noodles and sprouts were replaced on the line. The pork, octopus, and crab were placed on Time as Control and the PIC was told to use them within four hours. The operators stated that items are frequently rotated on the line with fresh product. It was recommended to fill the bottom of the cold holding unit with ice and water to allow the items to reach under 41F until the line can be repaired. 

Ensure that TCS items are held at 41F or under.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed no date marking in the facility. When the inspector inquired the dates that the TCS foods were prepared they were told by the PIC that the foods were either prepared today or yesterday. Education occurred about date marking requirements with the PIC. TCS and ready to eat (RTE) foods and sauces being held after the day of service are required to be marked with the date, and used or discarded within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: An employee was observed to thaw shrimp in still water in the kitchen preparation area. CORRECTED- The shrimp were placed in a container and were put under cold running water. The PIC and employee were educated that the only proper forms of thawing are through refrigeration, under cold running water that allows the food to remain at 41F and under, or through the cooking process.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F). [Pf]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed single use to-go bowl submerged in a 5 gallon soy sauce bucket being used as a scoop. Inspector informed PIC that scoops in service must have handles to avoid bare hand contact with the food item. Inspector advised the use of ladles or scoops with handle for the future.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment:
There were multiple instances where single-service articles and utensils were exposed to contamination: 

1. The small spoons used for sampling are not all facing the same way and are for consumers to grab themselves. Ensure that these are all placed to be facing the same way- with handles out to prevent bare hand contact with food surfaces.
2. Bowls next to the soup hot holding were not inverted. CORRECTED- The PIC inverted these to protect them from contamination. 
3. The foam single-service cups were not inverted. CORRECTED- The PIC inverted these as well. 

Ensure that all single service articles and utensils, including bowls and plates, are inverted or placed under a shelf to protect the food contact surface from contamination. Utensils used for customer self service should be arranged so that the handle is facing outward.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
There were two milk jugs observed to be cut and in use as rice scoops. This was discussed with the operators and they were educated that scoops used for food should be durable, corrosion-resistant, and able to withstand repeated warewashing. Ensure that these scoops are replaced with proper scoops that are sufficient to be used as a food contact surface. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspector observed at least 8 dented cans in the facility. PIC was informed that cans that are dented on the top, bottom, or side seams or cans that are dented such that the dents come to a pointed edge pose the risk of botulism growth and food-borne illness transmission. The PIC will remove the dented cans when time allows, for he is the only employee currently present at the facility.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the handwashing sink in the Assisted Living Dining Room being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- Education occurred between the inspector and Person in Charge (PIC). Handwashing sinks are to be used only for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw chicken being stored over raw ground beef in a cooler (to the left of the handwashing sink) in the Grill area of the facility. CORRECTED- the PIC moved the chicken to be stored on the bottom shelf, and notified staff that animal proteins should be stored so that items requiring higher internal temperatures for cooking are stored below other items (proteins requiring a lower internal temperature and ready to eat [RTE] foods). Ensure storage order education occurs with all food handlers on a routine basis.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The saniziter bucket in the main kitchen was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- kitchen staff remade sanitizer bucket to an acceptable value (200 ppm quaternary ammonia). Ensure sanitizer buckets are made and checked (using facility’s test strips) at a frequency to maintain the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed breakage in the gaskets of the main kitchen’s standing freezer (to the left of the hood vent system). Inspector showed the PIC the gaskets, which they added to their repair order list. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are maintained to be smooth and easily cleanable to prevent contamination of foods.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: The kitchen sanitizer bucket in the “Winter” wing was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer bucket was remade and observed to be at a proper concentration of 400ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed at a frequency to hold proper concentration levels as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration of 200-400 ppm and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed food debris or dust in the following locations:
1) Food debris in the silverware divider in “Spring” kitchen
2) Food debris in the silverware divider in “Winter” kitchen
3) Dust and soil accumulation on top of the Care Center dish machine. 
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, soil, and food debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed a leak on the front right edge of the Care Center’s dish machine during the rinse cycle. The person in charge (PIC) was notified and will be making a call to EcoLab to have the machine serviced. Ensure plumbing systems are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector and PIC observed holes in the walls (appeared as through shelving units had been relocated) of the mop sink rooms in each branch of the Care Center. The PIC noted the repairs to be made by maintenance. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Overall, the facility could use some education on the importance of chemical sanitizer. This includes how to properly test sani solutions, knowing the recommended concentration for effectively sanitizing, being aware when sanitizer is low, where test strips are located, and how often to change sani solutions during operations. See violations #16 and #48 for further details. The kitchen employees were not aware that the chemical dispensing bucket was extremely low and that the buckets did not contain the proper concentration for effective sanitation. The inspector discussed the importance of sanitizer and the need for education with the executive director of the facility. Be sure that all staff are trained on food sanitation to ensure the safety of residents.
citation_text: 2-103.11(L) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Both sanitizer buckets in the kitchen area tested at 0ppm (quat). The dispensing bucket was almost empty, however, there was enough chemical left to recreate both sanitizer buckets. Both sani buckets tested at 400ppm (quat) to correct the violation. More quaternary ammonia was also purchased. Be sure to maintain sanitizer solutions to ensure that food contact surfaces are properly getting sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine in the kitchen area appeared to have an accumulation of black debris on the outer surfaces. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent buildup and contamination of the ice.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: A container of thousand island dressing stored on a counter in the kitchen area was observed at room temperature. The package label stated that the dressing should be refrigerated after opening. The dressing had been opened prior to the inspection and left on the counter. Discussed with the CFPM and the dressing was placed into the walk in cooler. Ensure that TCS food items that must be cold held are kept at 41F or below and be sure to follow the manufacturer’s instructions for maintaining safety of food items.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Upon arrival, the inspector observed all sanitizer buckets to test at 0ppm (quat). Quaternary ammonia is being used as sanitizer and the dispensing bottle appeared empty. Discussed with the executive director that staff members that handle food or clean dishes must be trained on how to properly test sanitizer solutions to ensure that the chemical is working effectively. The inspector demonstrated how to correctly test sanitizer solutions and what range of concentrations are appropriate for sanitizing food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the kitchen sanitizer solution was at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector tested the bucket. The PIC was informed and they dumped and remade the bucket which tested at 150 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the can opener blade had an accumulation of debris. The PIC cleaned the blade to sight and touch during the inspection. The inspector educated that the can opener blade must be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after every use. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the walk-in cooler fans have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in cooler fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any hand soap available at the handsink in the front of the house. It appeared that the soap dispenser was empty. PIC replaced the dispenser with a new bag of soap to correct the violation. Be sure that hand soap is available at all handsinks to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Upon arrival, there wasn’t a sanitizer bucket available. Discussed with PIC and a sanitizer solution was created and tested at 300ppm (quat). Be sure that a sanitizer solution is available during all hours of operation to ensure that food contact surfaces are getting properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed no sanitizer present at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- person in charge (PIC) made sanitizer at triple sink. Ensure sanitizer solution is available and holding the correct concentration (with facility’s test strips) during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed debris accumulation on the soda nozzle at the bar. CORRECTED- PIC removed nozzle to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the build up of soil or debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash their hands and use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. This was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff. Ensure hand washing takes place correctly at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

A floor tile is damaged/missing between the fryers and adjacent freezer near to the wall. Grease and food debris is observed in this location at this time. This location needs repaired to allow for effective cleaning. Repair/replace the tile prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that the facility is maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the knife holder in the deli department was observed to be have food debris and soil residue on it. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned it during the inspection and was educated on the importance of maintaining this clean. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There were single service containers in the deli that were observed to not be inverted. CORRECTED- The PIC inverted the containers and was educating on keeping single service articles and utensils inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent contamination to food and lip-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The bottom of the deli freezer is observed to have a build up of food debris. 
2. The deli walk-in cooler fans are observed to have a build up of dust and soil residue. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employees were not using a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC was informed and they will be educating employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employees were removing gloves and donning new gloves to engage in food preparation without hand washing in between. The PIC was informed and they will be educating employees about the proper hand washing frequency. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with food.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed that the caulking sealing the triple sink to the wall is degrading in quality. Ensure that the caulking is removed and replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

On arrival there was not a CFPM available at the facility. The situation was discussed and someone who said that they had a CFPM arrived during this inspection, however a certification was not available for this person at the facility. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs working at the facility to ensure that all shifts are covered when food handling is taking place.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

There is not currently a verification method available at the facility for employees acknowledging their responsibility to report food safety symptoms and diagnosis. A fresh copy of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreement was given to the PIC. They are instructed to make copies and have all employees sign a copy prior to the follow up in 10 day.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

A food handler was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to review hand washing procedures with all employees and enforce safe food handling practices at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the facility is without soap. Soap was provided to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks in the facility are supplied with soap at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT X2) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Large accumulations of mold are observed on the baffle in the ice machine. Education conducted and this items will be checked at the follow-up being conducted in 10 days. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained cleaned and sanitized at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REEPAT) 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). 

On arrival the spray bottle labeled for sanitizer did not register on the inspector’s test strips. The PIC was consulted and was instructed to remake the solution. A bucket was made using CL/bleach instead. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times that food handling is taking place in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

An employee was observed to use a dry wiping cloth on the cutting board and knife used for sandwich preparation during this inspection. This should have been a sani rag stored in solution between uses to prevent the growth of pathogenic organisms. Education was conducted and the rag moved to the newly created sani bucket to correct.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

Degreaser and window cleaner are observed in spray bottles without labels. The PIC was shown and instructed to add labels to the containers. Labels were added to correct.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips were not available for the sanitizer used in the facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to acquire test strips effective for the sanitizers used in the facility prior to the follow-up in 10 days.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Food handler cards are not available for the staff at this facility at the time of this inspection. The situation was discussed and the PIC instructed to ensure that food handler cards are maintained at the facility for all food handlers in the facility at all times.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The food debris and grease on the floor underneath the front grill and steam table. 

(2) The dust on the wall vent behind the front steam table. 

(3) The food debris and grease on the floor underneath the kitchen fryers - THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed there is a leak at the kitchen hand washing sink from the faucet spout. Ensure that the leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop stored with the wet head directly on the ground. The PIC hung the mop inverted during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored with the mop head in a position that facilitates air drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:

title: Food handler training
comment:
An employee is observed to not have their food handler certificate. Ensure that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the following storage order violations in the facility:

4. Raw shell eggs stored above cut tomatoes (standing 2-door cooler)

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

A follow-up is scheduled for 8/14/2025 to ensure the ice machine has been cleaned and sanitized. Inspector recommends hiring a third party such as AirMasters to deep clean and sanitize the machine.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

comment: Inspector observed single-service forks on the cook-line and in the bakery to be displayed in a mixed orientation. CORRECTED- The single service forks were rearranged so that the food contact surface will be facing away from the food handler. Ensure that all single service utensils are displayed in a manner that will prevent contamination of the food contact surface.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation or food residue or dust during today’s inspection.
1) FIRST REPEAT The dry storage shelving to the left of the ice machine was observed to be soiled with dust. 
2) THIRD REPEAT: Food debris was observed inside drawer coolers in the drive thru salad station and the under-counter coolers on the main cook-line.
Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as needed to prevent accumulation of food debris, dust, and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple nonfood contact surfaces to contain an accumulation of debris;
1) There was an accumulation of soil debris around the outlets of the decaf and light roasts coffee makers in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge wiped the outlets with a clean sanitizer rag to remove debris. 
2) The microwave (particularly the top of the interior) contained an accumulation of grease and food debris. Education was provided to the person in charge (PIC) regarding the need to include cleaning and sanitizing the entire interior of the microwave on a regular basis. 
Nonfood contact surfaces and equipment should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspectors observed the outer surface of the door to the walk-in cooler to be rusted and corroded. Rust and corrosion is not considered a smooth, easily cleanable surface, and is therefore at risk of cross-contamination. Ensure the walls and door of the walk-in cooler are repaired (recommend sanding and repainting) prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- Multiple food handler’s certificates for onsite employees were observed to be expired. The person in charge (PIC) was informed that the certificates need to be renewed. Ensure all employees have a valid food handler’s certification prior to next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet, therefore recontaminating their hands. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing procedures with all staff. Ensure that the hand washing procedures in the facility protect freshly washed hands from recontamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) Painters tape is being used to hold a pair of sinks together in the dish room. The tape is observed heavily soiled and is not a good material for this area. The PIC was notified and instructed to remove the tape. If needed use a smooth and easily cleanable material for this contraction point. 2) The metal counter is pulling away from the wall to the right of the dish machine. This is exposing a gap. Re-adjust and/or re-seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facilities near moisture are sealed with materials that are smooth and easily cleanable.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

An employee cell phone was observed on a counter next to foods being handled. The situation was discussed with the employee, and latter PIC, and the phone moved to correct the immediate violation. Ensure employee possessions are stored in locations where contamination of foods or food contact surfaces is not a concern.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed ice in both the kitchen and bar hand sink. The PIC was informed that hand sinks may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. Ensure staff are dumping ice and drinks in dump sinks and never the hand sinks.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw ground beef stored above barbecue and buffalo sauce in the prep cooler. The PIC was informed and the beef was moved to the bottom shelf. Ensure raw ingredients are stored below ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the potato slicer to be soiled with food debris. The PIC was informed, and the potato sliced was washed/sanitized. Ensure the slicer is cleaned frequently to prevent and accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed bleu cheese and cooked pork stored in coolers in the kitchen without a proper date mark. Cooked pork and bleu cheese are both considered ready-to-eat (RTE), time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Any RTE TCS foods need to be date marked after opening, preparing, or portioning into a new container. These food items need to be discarded 7 days following the initial date on the marking.
