Since these food items had an unknown date of preparation, they were discarded. Ensure staff are practicing proper date marking to prevent bacteria accumulation in food.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed the ice scoop stored inside the ice machine with the handle in contact with ice for the consumer. The PIC was informed and the scoop was removed. Ensure staff are using the clean steel bin to store ice scoops to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(E) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(E) In a clean, protected location if the utensils, such as ice scoops, are used only with a food that is not time/temperature control for safety food.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed bowls stored on a shelf in the kitchen exposed to splash, dust, and/or other sources of contamination. The PIC was informed to invert the bowls on a clean surface to prevent contamination. Ensure the bowls are stored properly during the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed the shelving next to triple sink holding clean equipment to be soiled with dust/debris. The PIC was informed that the shelves need to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff are cleaning the shelves with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soil and dust.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled with dust/debris:
1. Small freezer in front of fryers
2. Gaskets/seals of all cabinet-style coolers/freezers

Ensure these surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent the accumulation of soil/debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The backup probe thermometer is stored in a pan mixed in with scrapers used for the chicken baking equipment. This poses a possible contamination source for the food contact parts of the probe thermometer and this practice should cease moving forward. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they had the probe sanitized and moved to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they remain clean/sanitized prior to use.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11 Inspector observed a build up of accumulated ice above the shelves on the left of the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the accumulated ice will be cleaned. Ensure that this build up of ice accumulation is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 

(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine is observed to have slight soil residue accumulation on it. CORRECTED- The PIC cleaned this during the inspection and was educated on the importance of maintaining it clean. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility has recently obtained a dish machine and is observed to not have an irreversible registering thermometer to check the heat sanitizing temperature of the machine. CORRECTED- The PIC ordered one during the inspection and it should be at the facility within a couple of days. A spot check will be conducted on 8/19/2025 to ensure that it arrived to the facility. Ensure that there is always a thermometer available to measure the temperature of the dish machine.
citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. The PIC was informed and they immediately remade the bucket. After being remade the bucket was too strong but after adding more water it tested at 150 ppm (Cl). The inspector educated that buckets must be checked on a regular basis using test strips and they cannot have any dish soap inside. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the can opener blade had an accumulation of debris. The PIC was notified and the blade was cleaned during the inspection. The can opener should be cleaned and sanitized after every use. Ensure that the can opener blade is always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the mop was stored with the head on the floor during the inspection. The PIC was educated and the mop head was moved into the drying portion of the mop bucket. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the ceiling tiles in the room with the ware washing and fryers are deteriorating. There are portions of the ceiling tiles that are peeling off over food preparation areas. The ceiling tiles must be repaired/replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Inspector observed the walk-in cooler fail to maintain proper cooling temperatures during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that the door to the walk-in was kept open during food preparation. While the cooler was able to recover and restore proper cold holding, fluctuations outside of the safe holding parameters should be avoided. Ensure that the PIC is monitoring cold holding temperatures and preventing improper cold holding in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on August 11th to ensure the cooler is being properly monitored.
citation_text: 2-103.11(I) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (I) EMPLOYEES are properly maintaining the temperatures of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOODS during hot and cold holding through daily oversight of the EMPLOYEES’ routine monitoring of FOOD temperatures.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed the following food items to be above the maximum safe cold holding temperature in the walk-in cooler (all probed):
1. Chili (50.8F)
2. Two large containers of raw chicken (50.8F)
4. Taco meat (48.7F)

CORRECTED: Inspector waited at facility and confirmed that walk-in cooler reached safe cold-holding temperatures relatively quickly. PIC stated that the door of the cooler was open for an extended period during food prep. Ensure the door remains closed as much as possible to ensure proper cold holding. Discussed maintaining cooler temperature logs to aid in temperature monitoring.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed upright freezer in the dry storage area to have an accumulation of food debris and ice at the bottom of the freezer. Ensure freezers are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled with dust/debris:
1. Above and around ventilation in the walk-in cooler
2. Baffles of the hood system

Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to prevent an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed walls and some shelving of the walk-in cooler to have bare wood. The paint on the door of the walk-in is damaged exposing bare wood, and the wood below the ventilation system in the walk-in appears to be untreated/uncoated. Ensure these wood surfaces are sealed to prevent moisture absorption and mold/bacterial accumulation.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed 4 items to not be date-marked. The items were marinara sauce cups, sliced American cheese, raw beef patties, and cut tomatoes. Discussed with PIC and PIC added date marks to all items without them. Ensure all items are date marked within 24 hours of opening or preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed a bowl of shrimp in water in the standing cooler in the back of the kitchen. Discussed proper cooling methods with PIC. Ensure that frozen foods are thawed under refrigeration, or in running cool water at 70F or below. Food must not be thawed in standing water. PIC drained the water from the bowl and continued thawing shrimp under refrigeration.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed 4 physical facilities in need of maintenance.

-The first place was the seal on the wall behind the fryers. The seal between NUDO boards is pulling from the wall. Ensure that it is repaired or replaced to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface.

-A light has recently been replaced in the kitchen, ensure the ceiling around the light is repainted to cover the drywall above. Drywall is absorbent, and surfaces in the kitchen must be nonabsorbent.

-There was an accumulation of flour and dust on dry storage shelves as well as the vent above them. Ensure these areas are cleared of debris, and cleaned regularly enough to keep them clean. Along with this, the floor under the shelves held some food debris. Ensure this area is swept regularly to prevent the build-up of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the front of the kitchen to have approximately 10PPM of chlorine sanitizer. Discussed with PIC, and PIC had the sanitizer changed immediately for fresh sanitizer measuring 100PPM of chlorine. Ensure the sanitizers are remade as often as needed to maintain sanitizer levels at or above 50PPM.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(2) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPAregistered label use instructions by providing: (2) A contact time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50 MG/L that has a PH of 10 or less and a temperature of at least 38°C 100°F) or a PH of 8 or less and a temperature of at least 24°C (75°F).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a build-up of ice in the WIF. The ice in the WIF is all over the ceiling in frozen droplets. Discussed cleaning out the ice with PIC. Ice build-up of this fashion could indicate a problem with the unit. Ensure that the ice is removed from the ceiling often enough to make the surface nonabsorbent and smooth.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed several cracked or broken tiles underneath the soda rack in the basement. Discussed with PIC, and PIC stated that a work request would be put in. Ensure these areas are repaired to make them smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a Certified FOOD Protection Manager (CFPM) who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The CFPM at the beginning of the inspection needed to leave without a replacement CFPM available to cover the shift. They stated that the night manager was in the process of trying for the certification but had not yet attained it. Ensure that there is always at least 1 CFPM present during all hours of operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and:(H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

1) Employees are observed to don gloves without washing hands. 2) An employee was observed to adjust their pants and then don gloves and handle food without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that when to conduct hand washing is reviewed with staff and enforced in the facility. Ensure hand washing is taking place prior to donning gloves and at any time that hands may have become contaminated prior to food handling.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

A crate in the walk in cooler used to store a sauce container off of the floor is observed with major white mold growth on it. The PIC was shown and removed the item for cleaning. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean in the facility at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

There is a crack in the seal along the top junction of the roof/wall in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all areas subject to moisture remain sealed and with a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A pair of employee beverages (sodas) are observed in a box in the walk in cooler that also contains sliced deli meats. This box is on the top shelf of the wire shelving racks. The situation was discussed with the PIC and the drinks removed to correct. Ensure that employee drinks/foods are stored below and/or away from foods intended for consumers. A cooler in the front of the area is observed with other drinks in it and would be a far better location for storing these items moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed there was not paper towels at the bar hand washing sink. The sink was provided with paper towels during the inspection. Ensure that there are always paper towels available at every hand washing sink for the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces are not clean to sight and touch: 

(1) The baffles of the ice machine have an accumulation of soil residues. 

(2) The can opener blade has an accumulation of debris. 

Food contact surfaces must always be clean to sight and touch. The inspector will follow-up on 8/14/2025 (delayed due to inspector being at the Illinois State Fair) to check that the ice machine baffles and can opener blade have been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a jug of milk that was opened on Monday in the double cooler lacked date marking. The milk was properly date marked during the inspection. Ensure that temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are always date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day one).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed salt and sugar by the salad prep cooler and flour by the fryers stored unpackaged in containers without labeling. All easily mistakable foods (ex. white powders) not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that the salt, sugar, and flour containers are properly labeled with the common name by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:

(1) The bottom shelf of the double cooler and cookline prep cooler have an accumulation of food residue and other debris.

(2) The inside of the microwave has an accumulation of soil residues.

(3) The bar soda nozzle holder has an acclimation of soil residues on the bottom. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPAT VIOLATION (from the pre-opening) 

Observed the following physical facilities are not maintained in good repair:

(1) Seal hand sink at the bar to the wall.
 
(2) Repair the damage on the inside of the men’s restroom door. 

(3) Paint the cabinets in the server station.

(4) Add cove base to the wall at the gap in the server cabinets. 

(5) Replace the wood top counter under the pass-thru window in the kitchen with stainless steel. 

(6) Replace rotted cabinets underneath the hand washing sink in the kitchen. 

(7) Repair the hole in the wall behind the meat slicer.

(8) Replace the table that holds the meat slicer. 

(9) Replace the wooden shelves by the salad prep cooler in the kitchen with stainless steel shelving. 

(10) Repair the hole in the wall behind the ovens. 

(11) Replace the missing electrical outlet cover in the wall behind the fryers. 

(12) Replace the old mop sink with the new mop sink that was purchased. 

(13) Repair the door trim by the mop sink. 

(14) Replace the wood shelving above the triple sink with stainless shelving. 

(15) The reach-in freezer lid in the back of the ware washing room is in a state of disrepair  **this violation is not a repeat from the pre-opening.

Ensure that the above referenced physical facilities are repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: FIRST REPEAT The bar sanitizer bucket was observed to have a low on concentration (50 ppm quaternary ammonia). CORRECTED- staff member remade sanitizer bucket, and new concentration was observed at 200 ppm. Ensure that all sanitizer buckets and solution meets the appropriate concentration as instructed by the label.
citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling (200-400ppm). [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the coffee dispenser in the kitchen to contain a significant amount of residue around the water outlet. CORRECTED- the outlet was wiped with a clean sanitizer rag. Ensure all food-contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of residue and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed wet sanitizer rags at the bottom of the reach in cooler at the bar in the banquet room. Education occurred with the person in charge. If clean sanitizer rags are being used to hold condensation, they should be changed everyday.
citation_text: 3-304.14(A) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills from TABLEWARE and carry-out containers that occur as FOOD is being served shall be: (1) Maintained dry; and (2) Used for no other purpose. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in need of physical repair;
1) The hand-sink at the (main) bar is loose.
2) Caulking to the left of the dish machine in the kitchen has turned black and appears fragmented.
3) Coving on the West wall of the dry food storage had began peeling off.
4) Coving on the wall directly to the right of the entryway of the chemical storage room. Coving is also peeling on the North side behind the water heater.
Items that cannot be moved easily for cleaning should be adhered to the wall. Seal items to wall to prevent degradation of physical facilities.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
FIRST REPEAT- The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soils.
1. The heat lamp was observed to have an accumulation of soil coating.
2. The grill and fryers was observed to have an accumulation of soil and grease underneath and on the sides.

The person in charge (PIC) was made aware of the soil accumulation in the areas mentioned. PIC said that cleaning schedule will increase in frequency from biweekly to weekly. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned frequently enough to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Inspector observed a personal backpack hanging at the drying rack opposite of the dish machine in the kitchen. CORRECTED- the person in charge moved the backpack to the designated storage area in the chemical room. Ensure personal belongings are kept in a designated area, separate from food and nonfood contact surfaces used to serve food to the public to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed a prep cooler that had raw chorizo being stored next to eggs, and the eggs above raw beef. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC, and PIC had the had the cooler rearranged so that the pork and beef were on the same shelf above the eggs. Inspector provided storage order handout in Spanish for the facility.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
(Repeat x2) Inspector observed the facility to be storing pork in a grocery bag in the back chest freezer. Discussed with PIC and PIC had the meat removed from the grocery bag and placed into food-safe ziplock bags. The PIC also informed the inspector that the meat was from Sysco, and the package had been damaged during receiving. Ensure that food is always stored in food-grade containers.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build-up of soils on the ice machine baffle. Discussed with PIC and PIC had the baffle cleaned and sanitized immediately. Ensure the baffle is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clean. Soils accumulate fast in this area, so more frequent cleanings are needed.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed none of the salsa containers in the salsa cooler to be date marked, and a gallon of milk in a standing cooler to not be date marked. Discussed proper date marking procedures with PIC, and PIC had the salsas and the milk date marked. Ensure that date marks are placed on food packages within 24 hours of opening or preparation, and the food is not kept longer than 7 days after.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector noted several live cockroaches on glue traps around the facility. All glue traps were observed to have some amount of cockroaches on them. PIC informed inspector that pest control comes once a week on Mondays. This indicates that pest control alone is not enough to keep the cockroach population down. Inspector recommends a deep cleaning of all dark and unused areas, as well as behind and inside equipment. Cockroaches can hide in these places and maintain a pest presence in the kitchen even when pest control is active. Ensure the cockroaches are eradicated to maintain clean and sanitary food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector observed the CFPM to not have an allergen certification. Talked with the CFPM about allergen certifications and provided the class handout. Ensure that all CFPMs on staff receive allergen training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspector observed 3 instances of a #16 violation.

-The first instance observed was the can opener blade. Inspector observed the blade to be soiled with food residue. CORRECTED discussed with PIC and PIC had the blade removed from the assembly. Ensure the blade of the can opener is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clean.

-The second instance was a stock pot with pasta dried to the inside. Ensure that all dishes are washed appropriately after each use. Dishes must be clean to sight and touch. CORRECTED PIC had the pot washed, rinsed, and sanitized.

-The third instance was the ice machine baffle. Inspector observed there to be a build-up of soils on the ice machine baffle. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the baffle is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build-up of soils.

Inspector will return 08/04/2025 to re-inspect the baffle.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
comment: Inspector observed the facility to be using steam tables to reheat food. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that all food is brought up to 165 for 15 seconds before going in to hot-holding. Inspector will return 08/04/2025 to re-inspect reheating procedures.
citation_text: 3-403.11(A) Reheating for Hot Holding. (A) Except as specified under (B) and (C) and in (E) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the FOOD reach a temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) for 15 seconds.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: REPEAT- There was a package of raw bacon on the top shelf above containers of cut vegetables in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- An employee moved the bacon below the vegetables and in the proper storage order. Proper storage order was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: REPEAT- There was salmon in reduced oxygen packaging in the top of the preparation cooler and on a shelf by the cook line that was observed to still be in its original packaging. The label and packaging states to remove from packaging prior to thawing. The packages of salmon that were on the shelf by the cook line were observed to be being thawed at room temperature. Proper thawing procedures were discussed with the staff. Reduced oxygen packaged salmon needs to be removed from the packaging or have the packaging cut before it can be thawed. Thawing should only be done through refrigeration, the cooking process, or under cold running water to prevent bacteria growth. CORRECTED- The salmon that was being thawed at room temperature was moved to the cooler (it had only been out for an hour) and all packages of reduced oxygen packaged salmon that were thawed or currently being thawed had their package cut. Ensure that staff are educated on proper thawing procedures.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The dish shelves are lined with a liner that is not smooth and easily cleanable. Clean dishes are directly set on this liner. Switch to a liner that is smooth and easily cleanable or cease using a liner altogether. Nonfood contact surfaces should be smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The gasket of the standing freezer in the kitchen is observed to be in a state of disrepair. Ensure that this gasket is repaired or replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The walk-in cooler fan cover is observed to have an accumulation of dust build up. Ensure that this is regularly cleaned. Nonfood contact surfaces should be cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There was a bucket of used mop water that was observed to not have been dumped after use by the mop sink. CORRECTED- The bucket of waste water was dumped and the PIC was educated on ensuring that this is dumped after use. Waste water should be dumped immediately to prevent pest harborage conditions.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area was without paper towels. The PIC was asked about paper towels and then replaced them during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the bar area would not register on inspector test strips. The machine was in use prior to observation by the inspector. The bar manager worked on the machine for a few minutes and the machine registered correctly afterwards. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inside of the spout for the soda gun at the left side of the bar has a black substance built up. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent soilage.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

A pan of portioned cooked spaghetti in the walk in cooler has a date marking of 7/17/25. Today is day 13 when the items should have been used or discarded by the end of day seven. The PIC checked the bags and agreed that they were old and discarded them during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods are used or discarded by the end of day seven where the day of preparation is day one.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed sanitizer bucket measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC was informed and the bucket was remade, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure buckets are replaced frequently and the sanitizer concentration is monitored with test strips to ensure proper sanitization of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of mold on the rubber gasket seal of the milk dispensing cooler. PIC was informed and will clean/sanitize the gasket. Inspector recommends replacing the gasket if it cannot be thoroughly cleaned. Ensure the gasket is cleaned or replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a pizza pan and cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The PIC was educated that food contact surfaces can become contaminated by water splashes, food residue, or other debris stored in this position. After education the PIC moved the pizza pan and cutting board into a new location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always stored in a position that allows them to remain clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the scoop inside the salt bin does not have a handle. Scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have handles that are stored above the top of food to avoid contamination. Ensure that the salt bin has a scoop with a handle by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observe there are two small holes in the wall above the pizza station where a hook was moved. The PIC was educated that walls must always be smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. Ensure that the holes are sealed (ex. caulking) by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have completed the food handler training. The PIC was educated that all employees who do not have a CFPM (Certified Food Protection Manager) certificate must have food handler certificates. Ensure that all required employees complete the food handler training and copies of the certificates are kept at the facility by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed 3 soup ladles hanging in ready to use position behind cheese sauce hot holding in kitchen to contain soil accumulation. CORRECTED- ladles were taken to the triple sink to be cleaned and sanitized before use. Ensure utensils that are stored in ready to use position are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil debris.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspector observed a contained of white powder (identified as flour) above the pizza station at the end of the kitchen. CORRECTED-person in charge was notified and the flour was voluntarily discarded. Ensure white powders and other items that can be mistaken for others are labeled after they are removed from their original container.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed a 2 oz. plastic container submerged in flour being stored on the shelf above the pizza station. CORRECTED- person in charge discarded the contents of the entire container (see violation #37). Use scoops with handles directed outwards, outside of the food to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed the handle of the double door standing cooler upstairs to be in disrepair. The handle had been broken off and replaced with a pool noodle and scotch tape. Inspector notified the person in charge so that the equipment can be repaired. Ensure equipment is maintained in repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed soil accumulation along the gasket perimeter of the chest freezers upstairs. CORRECTED- the person in charge wiped the gaskets with a clean sanitizer rag. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed multiple items in the facility in need of physical repair;
1) There is a hole in the ceiling upstairs above the soda boxes. This may be indicative of water damage. The inspector notified the person in charge of this damage, so that it may be repaired by the next routine inspection.
2) The mop sink at the entry of the kitchen was observed to have degraded caulking between the sink and the wall. The area between the mop sink basin and wall should be cleaned and either repaired or replaced.
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good condition.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice machine to be soiled with pink substance. Discussed with PIC, ice machine will be properly cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents build up.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed date marking to be missing on multiple TCS item within facility. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper date marking procedure. Date marking stickers were placed on TCS items, ensure any TCS items that are opened and kept longer than 24 hours are date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed coffee machine to be soiled with rust. Discussed with PIC, coffee machine will be cleaned. Ensure food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents rust from forming.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was moved to strainer portion of mop bucket. Ensure after use, mops are placed in a position that allows them to air dry without soiling walls.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed black mold to be present at triple sink caulking in kitchen. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/ replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed multiple pests to be present during inspection. Discussed with PIC, pest control unit will be called to service facility. Ensure facility is kept pest free.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed black mold to be present at the caulking on the triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring caulking to prevent any black mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed both hand washing sinks in the deli and the back hand washing sink at the meat department did not have paper towels. During the inspection paper towel rolls were brought to the hand washing sinks. Ensure that paper towels are always available at every hand washing sink for the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed the following in the deli walk-in cooler were missing date marking: (1) Container of taco meat cooked on Saturday; and (2) Container of pasta salad prepared on Thursday. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was prepared/opened being day one).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed a large container of unpackaged flour in the deli was not labeled. All easily mistakable foods (ex. white powders) not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that the flour container is properly labeled by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the caulking at the spay nozzle sink in the deli (directly to the right of the fryers) is deteriorating. The sink must be re-caulked to remove the gap between the sink and the wall. Ensure that the spray nozzle sink is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the floor underneath the fryers in the deli has an accumulation of food debris and grease. The equipment should be pulled out to facilitate deep cleaning underneath. Ensure that underneath the fryers is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed the PIC remade a sanitizer bucket and opened door handles and then proceeded to test sushi acidic levels wearing the same gloves. The PIC was educated during the inspection that after any potential contamination occurs they must remove gloves, wash hands, and put on new gloves before continuing to handle food. Ensure that hands are washed and new gloves are donned after engaging in any activity that can contaminate hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0-10 ppm (quat) when the inspector arrived. During the inspection the bucket was remade and it tested at 200 ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizing concentrations are always testing at the correct concentration (200-400 ppm for quat).
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Active CFPM retired. PIC at store was provided information regarding classes in the area. Ensure a CFPM is present on staff during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed the facility to be using a sauce cup with no handle to scoop sugar. Discussed with PIC, and PIC removed the sauce cup and started using a spoon. Ensure that all utensils used to scoop RTE food have handles to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed rodent poison stored over the single service bulk items in the basement. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC and PIC had it moved to the bottom shelf immediately. Ensure that poisonous items are not stored above food-service items.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the sides and front of the fryers to be soiled with grease. Discussed cleaning with PIC. Ensure that fryers and surrounding equipment are cleaned frequently enough to prevent the build-up of grease.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the wall above the mops sink splash guard to be crumbling. Ensure this area is repaired and repainted to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface. The wall in the back hallway is also missing some paint. Ensure this is painted to render the surface smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
REPEAT Inspector observed no employees to have an allergen training. Ensure that all CFPMs on staff receive an allergen training. Allergen handouts were provided to PIC.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

One of the containers (re-used from previous sauces) of house made sauce is observed with mold colonies inside of the container. The PIC was shown and discarded the container to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all foods are stored in clean containers and that they are protected from pathogenic growth at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several knives and pans in storage as clean and ready for use are observed with food debris remaining. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to dish to correct the immediate violation. They should review dish washing procedures with employees and ensure that all food contact surfaces are being completely cleaned each time that they are washed.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A)TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

On arrival, several TCS items in the standing cooler in the bathroom hallway are observed with internal temperatures between 56F and 61F. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they stated that employees were probably in an out regularly, increasing the temperature. The inspector stated that, while that would increase the ambient air temperature of the cooler, the foods should not be out of temperature long enough for the internal temperatures to rise to these levels. The TCS foods in this cooler were discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Foods discarded include cooked rice, cooked pork chop, sausage, sauces labeled “refrigerate after opening” and house made sauces including oil and garlic in their ingredients. A check of the cooler will take place to ensure the cooler is repaired/adjusted to function correctly (refer to line item #33).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The standing cooler in the bathroom hallway is observed to not be functioning correctly (refer to line item #22). The cooler needs maintenance/ adjustment to esnure safe food storage. Ensure that the cooler is functioning correctly prior to the follow-up in ten days.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: Ina a manner that is considered safe under the food code. Section (B) allows for TCS foods to be thawed completely submerged under running water.

On inspector arrival large blocks of frozen chicken are observed in standing water in the three part sink. Prior to discussion the primary manager arrived at the facility and corrected the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink in the kitchen is observed pulling away from the wall and exposing a large gap to the right of the sink. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair. Repair/seal the location to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface moving forward.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there was not signed employee health reporting agreements at the facility. The PIC was provided with agreements today and all present employees signed copies. Ensure that all employees who handle food sign the employee health reporting agreement and the signed agreements remain at the facility.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the scoop for the ice machine in the back storage area was stored with the handle within the ice. The PIC was educated and the scoop handle was moved outside of the ice during the inspection. Since the ice scoop is touched by bare hands the handle must be stored above the top of food to avoid contamination. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored properly.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following physical facilities are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The missing piece of cove base to the left of the bar triple sink - cove base must be added to this location.

(2) The hole in the floor infront of the bar sliding drink cooler - the hole must be sealed.

(3) The holes in the wall throughout the back area, specifically behind the reach-in freezer, behind the table to the left of the reach-in freezer, and underneath the back triple sink - the holes must be sealed.

(4) The back hand washing sink that is not sealed to the wall - since the sink is not easily removable it must be sealed to the wall (ex. caulking).

Ensure that the above referenced physical facilities subject to food and/or moisture are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was no Certified Food Protection Manager (CFM) present at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- a CFM arrived towards the end of the inspection. Ensure that there is a CFM present at all times food is being prepared or handled.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The concentration of the prepared sanitizer bucket was initially reading at 0 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- inspector instructed staff member to add a quat tablet to the sanitizer bucket. The sanitizer bucket met the 200 ppm criteria. Use test strips to ensure the correct concentration of sanitizer solution so that that food contact surfaces are properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed spatula that was cracked along the perimeter of the food-contact surface. CORRECTED- inspector notified staff member about the condition of the spatula and it was voluntarily discarded. Ensure that food contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-202.11(A) Food-Contact Surfaces. (A) Multiuse FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be: (1) Smooth; (2) Free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections; (3) Free of sharp internal angles, corners, and crevices. [Pf]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: No sanitizer bucket was observed in the facility at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket was being prepared by a kitchen staff member as the inspectors entered the kitchen.
