This sanitizer bucket was observed at 0 ppm (see violation #16), and no alternative sanitization method was available. Ensure sanitizer solutions are prepared at the start of a shift where food is being handled.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Two areas at the physical facility were observed to be in need of repair. 
1) The southwest ceiling corner above the soda boxes contains a hole about 3” by 3” in area. Ensure the ceiling tile is moved or the gap is filled to prevent against pest harborage. 
2) The orange splash guard behind the mop sink is not adhered to the wall. Water is present between the splash guard and wall, which could allow for the growth and harborage of mold or bacteria. 
Ensure physical facilities are maintained and repairs are made by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

A container of pre-cooked chicken is observed in the bottom of the cooler next to the back chili steam well with internal temperatures of 55F. The PIC was shown and stated that it was placed in the cooler this morning. The chicken was discarded to correct. Per the PIC this cooler will no longer be used for storing of TCS foods. They also stated that it normally only holds clean trays/pans. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored so that they maintain temperatures of 41F or less at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Inspectors observed multiple food contact surfaces to contain soil accumulation or food debris.
1) A slight amount of soil was observed on the ice machine. CORRECTED- the person in charge immediately wiped the soil area with a clean sanitizer wipe.
2) The ice outlets at the self service station in the lobby contained a slight amount of soil accumulation. CORRECTED- employee wiped the food contact surfaces with a clean sanitizer wipe.
3) A slight amount of food debris was observed on a spatula hanging in a ready-to-use position in the kitchen prep area. CORRECTED- the spatula was taken to the dish washing station to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure are food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspectors observed a soil accumulation along the perimeter of the walk-in cooler door. PARTIALLY CORRECTED- employee wiped the gaskets clean with a sanitizer solution. A small amount of soil debris was still present on the wall sealant on the side of the door hinge. A replacement sealant is recommended by the next routine inspection.
Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil or debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed some physical facilities in need or replacement or repair:
1) A tile on the left side of the mop sink is coming loose.
2) Multiple tiles underneath the dry storage (to the left of the walk-in cooler) were observed to be broken. Broken tiles pose a risk of cross-contamination and improper cleaning. 
3) A hole was observed in the wall underneath the dish machine (by PVC plumbing to sink).
Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed dipping well to be turned off upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, dipping wells were turned on. After dipping wells were turned on, a leak became present from the left dipping well. Discussed with PIC, left dipping well will be serviced. All utensils will be moved to the right dipping well. Ensure dipping wells are turned on and running up to manufacturers standards during hours of operation.
citation_text: 3-304.12(D) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (D) In running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist food such as ice cream or mashed potatoes.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at back kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure staff is monitoring facility to prevent any possible leaks.
citation_text: 5-201.11 Approved. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM and hoses conveying water shall be constructed and repaired with APPROVED materials according to LAW. (B) A water filter shall be made of SAFE MATERIALS.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff to turn off the faucet with their bare hands after washing hands. CORRECTED- Education occurred regarding hand washing procedures. Inspector provided a hand washing infographic in both English and Spanish to the facility. Ensure a clean barrier is used after washing hands to turn off the faucet to prevent recontaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed two incidents of handwashing at sinks not intended for hand washing. Hand washing was observed at the bar triple sink, as well as at the kitchen triple sink.Discussion was had with food handlers about the usage of hand sinks to be the only location of hand washing. CORRECTED- hand washing sinks will be the only place where staff wash hands. Hand washing signs were provided to the operator.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: FIRST REPEAT- Inspector observed raw chicken being stored above beef in the walk-in cooler. Due to the fact that chicken requires a higher cooker temperature than beef, it must be stored below the raw beef. CORRECTED-kitchen staff moved the chicken below the beef to reflect correct storage order. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw beef above partially cooked tamales and fried peppers in the double door freezer (in the ice machine room). CORRECTED- kitchen staff moved raw items below the partially cooked items. Animal protein must be stored beneath partially cooked items, raw produce, and any ready-to-eat food items. Ensure facility is practicing correct storage order to prevent cross-contamination. Spanish language literature about storage order was provided to the person in charge.

FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Inspector observed the accumulation of soil on the hood of the fryer including the accumulation of grease on the side of the fryer. Discussed with PIC. PIC ensured inspector that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that this accumulation of soil and grease are cleaned appropriately. 

Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11. Inspector observed staff cutting raw ready to eat vegetables with bare hands. PIC was made aware of the incident. Staff was educated and the food in question was discarded. Staff proceeded to wash their hands and don gloves to continue the task. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable to don gloves during food prep to avoid contamination.

(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths sitting on prep counters within the kitchen. The PIC was notified and the cloths were moved into the sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizing solutions between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed dirty water inside the mop bucket stored in the closet. The PIC stated that they last mopped this morning. During the inspection the water was dumped down the mop sink. Ensure that dirty mop water is always dumped after use.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at back kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure staff is monitoring facility to prevent any possible leaks.
citation_text: 5-201.11 Approved. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM and hoses conveying water shall be constructed and repaired with APPROVED materials according to LAW. (B) A water filter shall be made of SAFE MATERIALS.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed ice bath sink to be leaking. Discussed with PIC, leak will be serviced. Ensure ice bath is serviced so no leak is present.
citation_text: 5-201.11 Approved. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM and hoses conveying water shall be constructed and repaired with APPROVED materials according to LAW. (B) A water filter shall be made of SAFE MATERIALS.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. The facility does have two CFPM’s on staff, but one alternates between locations and the other was away taking some children from the daycare on a field trip. The PIC was informed that a CFPM must be present at all times of food preparation. Ensure more staff members receive certification prior to next routine inspection to accommodate for trips/illness/unexpected staffing complications.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed shredded cheese, hotdogs, sliced cheese, and deli meat to be stored in the facility longer than 24 hours without a date mark. The PIC was informed and date marking was added to these items. No items were kept longer than 7 days. Ensure all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are marked with the date of opening and discarded after 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspector observed plastic serving plates stored without protective covering on a high shelf in the kitchen. To protect the food contact surfaces of these items, ensure the plates are inverted (face-down on the clean shelf) to prevent contamination from dust, splash, or other debris.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

When asked, the PIC was unable to provide effective Norovirus clean-up procedures in the facility. A fresh copy of the procedures distributed by SCDPH was given to correct. Ensure that all needed paperwork is available in the facility at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The dish machine in the facility is not properly sanitizing dishes at the time of this inspection. The machine appears to be attempting to function but sanitizer is not dispensing from the tube into solution correctly. The PIC was consulted and contacted MJ Kelner for maintenance during this inspection. Both the three part sink and the dish machine are used for dishes in the facility. A follow-up is being set for Friday to ensure that the equipment is functioning correctly in complaince with the code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. The bottle’s instructions as well as the use of test strips was discussed and the more tablets were added to bring the solution up to effective concentrations to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers int he facility are prepared and maintained at effective concentrations at all times moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The corner to the left of the walk in cooler is observed with the wall pulling away from the corner and exposing a gap. The PIC is instructed to have the location repaired prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that the physical facilities are maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. 

1) An employee phone is observed on the prep counter near foods being prepared. 2) A cold neck band is observed on the top wire shelf of the standing freezer over open containers of food. The PIC was shown and instructed to store employee items so that contamination of food items is removed. The neck band was move into a bucket and onto the bottom shelf while the phone was removed to correct.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employees miss several hand washing opportunities; including but not limited too, before donning gloves, switching between tasks, and upon re-entering the kitchen. Reminder that employees must wash hands after any source of contamination. The PIC will be educating employees regarding the need for an increased frequency in hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A THIRD REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order: (1) Raw chicken stored above raw beef in the double cooler; and (2) Eggs stored on the top shelf above various ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in cooler. The storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. Raw meats and eggs must be stored below ready-to-eat foods, and raw meats must be stored according to internal cooking temperatures (reminder that raw chicken has a higher cooking temperature than raw beef and thus raw chicken must be stored below). The inspector will follow-up on 7/31/2025 to check on storage order at the facility.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of grease on the hood system causing drips. The drips pose the risk of contaminating food cooking below. The inspector will follow-up on 7/31/2025 to ensure that the hood system has been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces are not cleaned to sight and touch:

(1) The plastic container holding seeds above the steam table was severely soiled with residues and food debris. The PIC moved the seeds into a clean plastic container and discarded the old container during the inspection. 

(2) The broccoli scoop is soiled with various residues, especially near the handle and edges of the scoop. The PIC was instructed to wash, rinse, and sanitize the broccoli scoop. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed an employee bring a whisk to the triple sink for cleaning and only rinse the utensil under running water. All utensils, dishes, and other food contact equipment must be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized during cleaning. The PIC will be educating employees about proper cleaning procedures. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always washed, rinsed, and sanitized during cleaning.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed the following were not properly date marked: (1) egg rolls prepared yesterday in the clear sliding cooler; (2) wantons prepared Saturday in the clear sliding cooler; and (3) noodles cooked yesterday in the prep cooler bottom. All temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum. The inspector will return on 7/31/2025 to check on date marking at the facility.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed a large container of cooked fried rice stored at room temperature without marking indicating when it must be discarded. The PIC stated they take the rice out when it’s busy and put it back inside the cooler when it’s not busy. The inspector educated about temperature abuse and the importance of either using time-as-control (TAC) or only bringing out small amounts of food that can be used during lunch/dinner rushes. The PIC stated that the rice was cooked at 12 pm and thus must be discarded at 4 pm. The inspector will follow-up on 7/31/2025 to ensure that the facility is marking the four hour window for TAC or only pulling out small amounts of cooked fried rice that can be used within lunch/dinner rushes.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed there was chicken and shrimp thawing at room temperature when the inspector arrived. The PIC stated that the chicken and shrimp were recently removed from the freezer. The chicken and shrimp were immediately moved into the walk-in cooler. Temperature control for safety (TCS) foods must always be thawed according to an approved method: (1) Within a cooler at 41F or less; (2) Under continuous running water; (3) In the microwave; or (4) As part of the cooking process. Ensure that TCS foods are always thawed properly to maintain food safety.
citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the scoop for the cooked fried rice did not have a handle. Scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of food to avoid contamination. The scoop was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods always have a handle to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the front reach-in freezer has a significant buildup of frost. The freezer must be defrosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the front reach-in freezer is de-frosted by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable, or non-absorbent materials: 

(1) The takeout menus used a liners for a tray wontons in the clear sliding cooler and a bowl of cooked chicken on the counter - the menus must be removed. 

(2) The cardboard used as a shelf liner in the clear sliding cooler - the cardboard must be removed. 

(3) The ketchup stored in an opened can (acidic foods cannot be stored in open cans) - the ketchup must be stored in a different container after opening. 

Ensure that all materials at the facility are smooth, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent by the next routine inspection. 

4101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the inside of the fan above the double cooler has a significant accumulation of debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the inside of the fan is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of grease and food debris on the floor to the left of the fryers. The PIC was shown the location of the grease and food buildup during the inspection. Ensure that the fryers and surrounding area are cleaned by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there are missing ceiling tiles in the area above the front reach-in freezer. The ceiling tiles must be replaced to ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FOURTH REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the chest freezer in the back dry storage area has a lid that is in a state of extreme disrepair held together with duct tape. Duct tape is not easily cleanable or an appropriate repair. The PIC stated they cannot find a replacement lid and will purchase a new freezer when they have enough money. Ensure repairs or replacements by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed a cell phone and car keys stored on a prep counter where an employee was cutting onions. The cell phone and car keys were moved below the prep counter during the inspection. Ensure that personal items are stored in designated areas away from food and food contact surfaces to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that one of the employees food handler certificate is expired. All employees that handle food at the establishment (and do not have a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate) must have basic food handler training. Ensure that all required employees have a food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

During this inspection there was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility. It is suggested that the night manager acquire a CFPM moving forward.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

A can is observed in storage with major dents in both the top and bottom seams. The PIC was shown and damage to the packages discussed. The can was separated out for credit to correct. Ensure that all packages are checked as product is received.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Several utensils throughout the storage racks in the facility are observed with food residue still evident. The PIC was shown and moved the items back o dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17 Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

1) A spray bottle in the kitchen is without a legible label. The PIC indicated that it is water and a label was re-applied to correct. 2) The same type of bottle was observed in the bar area and contains sanitizer. The bar manager was consulted and added a label to correct. Ensure that all chemicals containers are labeled correctly at all times in the facility to ensure that they are not accidentally used for purposes that they were not intended for.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Two containers of cheese sauce int he walk in cooler are observed without lids. The PIC was consulted and added lids to the containers to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are protected from contaminants at all applicable times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

On arrival there is not test strips available for the quat based sanitizer used in the bar area of the facility. The situation was discussed with the bar manager and test strips will need to be acquired prior to the follow up in 10 days.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

Ensure that there is always a chemical sanitizer made and available to be able to sanitize food contact surfaces during all hours of food preparation.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

The owner and operator had a discussion with the Director of Environmental Health, and the operator will be taking the test to receive their CFM at the end of August.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed eggs being stored above butter- which is classified as a ready-to-eat (RTE) food. CORRECTED- The inspector notified the operator and they moved eggs below the butter and other RTE items. Eggs must be stored below RTE foods to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed mop submerged in the basin of the mop bucket in the kitchen. CORRECTED- operator moved mop to the upper portion of the mop bucket to allow for air drying. Mops should be placed in a position to allow for air drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

When inspection began there was no certified food program manager (CFM) present. CORRECTED- a person with a CFM arrived halfway through the inspection. Ensure there is a CFM present at all times food is being handled.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

The dish machine was observed to be dispensing 0 ppm Cl. The person in charge was notified and will be making a call to have the machine serviced. Use the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is observed to be dispensing 200 ppm. A follow up inspection is scheduled for 07/28/25 (3 days would be Saturday 07/26/25) to check the dish machine.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed two stacks of sliced cheese wrapped in plastic wrap that did not bear a date mark. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC and PIC had the cheese date marked immediately. Ensure that all TCS items are date marked 24 hours after opening.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed there to be two bottles of lime juice that were past-date in the walk-in cooler. COREECTED PIC threw the lime juice away. Ensure that no items are kept past the manufacturer’s due date.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed wire shelves in the dish room to be soiled and rusted in some places. Discussed repairs/replacements with PIC. Ensure these shelves are repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer set up to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was set up and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is set up during all hours of operations.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The triple sink sanitizer solution in the kitchen was observed measuring at 100 ppm quaternary ammonium. CORRECTED- The person in charge was notified and the sanitizer dispenser was observed to be dispensing the appropriate amount of sanitizer (200 ppm). Test sanitizer solution and bucket regularly to ensure sanitizer solutions are effective at sanitizing food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Multiple surfaces were observed to be soiled:
1) Soda nozzles at self service station. CORRECTED- person in charge wiped soda dispenser surfaces and replaced nozzles with a second set so that the first set may be cleaned and sanitized.
2) The plastic wall-mounted knife holder was soiled. CORRECTED- person in charge cleaned the knife holder.
3) The ice machine was observed to have a build up of water residue around the power inlet. CORRECTED- person in charge emptied and cleaned the ice machine.

Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil, food, or water residue.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) REPEAT: There were gaps observed between the front hand sink and the wall. Clean off existing caulking and re-seal the front hand sink to the wall.
2) REPEAT: There is a horizontal gash in the wall above the front hand sink. Fill in or patch the damaged wall.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee remove gloves and put on new gloves without hand washing. The PIC will be educating staff about proper glove use. Additionally, the inspector will be reaching out to the PIC in about two weeks to schedule hand washing education with the SCDPH health educator and Spanish translator. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC will be educating staff about the proper hand washing procedure. Additionally, the inspector will be reaching out to the PIC in about two weeks to schedule hand washing education with the SCDPH health educator and Spanish translator. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. The PIC scheduled service for the dish machine. Until the dish machine is serviced the facility will be washing and rinsing in the dish machine but sanitizing in the triple sink. The inspector will follow-up on 7/24/2025 to check that the dish machine is properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the ice machine baffles have an accumulation of soil residues. Food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. The inspector will follow-up on 7/31/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets on the cookline and bar were testing at 0 ppm (Cl). The PIC was informed and the sanitizer buckets were changed during the inspection. The inspector suggests increasing the frequency that sanitizer buckets are changed throughout the day. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-200 ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of queso sitting on top of the containers inside the steam table with an internal temperature of 81F. The queso container has a label indicating that is was prepared at 7:30 AM. The inspector asked the PIC about the queso and they stated that it should have been put inside the steam table. The PIC voluntarily discarded the queso during the inspection. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following foods stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination: (1) Uncovered containers of chips, tortilla bowls, and taco shells on the cookline by the entrance door; and (2) Uncovered deserts on the top shelf of the double cooler. The inspector educated that foods must be protected from contamination during storage when not being used. Ensure that foods are properly covered during stoarge by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the ice scoop in the server area stored with the handle within the ice. An employee was notified and the ice scoop was moved into the holder during the inspection. Since the handle is touched by bare hands it must be stored above the top of food. Ensure that scoops for ready-to-eat foods are always stored to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: (1) The food residue on the floor beneath the grill on the cookline; and (2) The debris on the magnetic knife holder above the steam table on the cookline. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The preparation cooler was observed to be holding at 70F (cut tomatoes). CORRECTED- The prep cooler was unplugged and the PIC plugged it back in. The prep cooler lowered to under 41F and the food had only been in there for around 30 minutes. Ensure food is kept at 41F or below if it is a TCS food.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The PIC was using a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer spray bottle (a premade solution) but only had Chlorine test strips. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and he stated that he will cease using the Quat sanitizer and use the Clorox bleach they have on the mobile unit. Ensure that there are always test strips available for all types of sanitizers that are being used.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: REPEAT- The floor is observed to not be caulked to the wall and trim. Ensure that this is caulked/sealed to the wall and trim. This was discussed with the PIC. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand sink at the bar being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- employee moved the dump tray to the triple sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are being used for hand washing only.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw meat was observed to be stored on top of a ranch container in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC moved the raw meat beneath the ranch. Ensure that raw food is stored beneath ready-to-eat food.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
1) FIRST REPEAT- Both bar soda nozzles were observed to be soiled. CORRECTED- Employees cleaned the soda nozzles. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
2) Knives on the magnetic strip in the kitchen were observed to contain food debris. CORRECTED- person in charge moved the knives to be cleaned and sanitized. All food contact surfaces that will be used on ready-to-eat foods must be clean to sight and touch.
3) Magnetic strip for the knives contained grease and debris. Non-food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch. A follow up inspection will occur on 07/28/25 to ensure that the knife strip are cleaned or sanitized. 
3) Ice baffles at both the north and south ice machines were observed to contain a significant amount of soil accumulation behind the door hinges. Food-contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch. A follow up inspection will occur on 07/28/25 to ensure that baffles are cleaned or sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
comment: Inspector observed chicken cooling in the walk in freezer to be stacked in a tub. Education occurred with the person in charge regarding the need for shallow pans for food to have the surface area to properly cool. In it’s current configuration the chicken will not reach cooling temperature benchmarks in the required time.
citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Lime juice and whipping cream located at the bar reach in cooler did not have date marking. CORRECTED- Education occurred about date marking and dates were placed on the whipping cream and lime juice. Ensure items being held for more than 24 hours are marked with the date the container was opened, so that they may be used or discarded within seven days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed insect stun light above single service articles at the entry of the kitchen. Ensure that insect control devices are stored away from single service items to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed chicken bouillon with an open lid to be located on the floor of the dry storage area. All food items should remain covered when not in use, and must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect items from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
1) FIRST REPEAT- Wire shelving in the walk-in cooler is soiled or rusted (straight across from the door and to the left when you walk in the cooler). Wire shelving over the prep counter (above the under-counter freezer) is dusty. Clean dusty/dirty shelves. Replace rusted shelves that are no longer smooth/easily cleanable.
2)  Significant amounts of food debris were observed on the floors in the walk in freezer and throughout the kitchen. 
3) The floors of the walk-in freezer and bar walk-in cooler were wet from the cooling system dripping.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
1) 2nd REPEAT: The triple sink and table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked.
2) 1st REPEAT: There are holes in the wall above the hand-sink and the triple sink that need caulked.
3) 1st REPEAT: The kitchen handwashing sink needs re-caulked.
4) A hole was observed in the east wall of the dry storage above the water heater.
5) The hand sink in the south men’s bathroom was not adhered to the wall. There is also not a large enough gap to easily clean between the sink and the wall. The sink should be sealed to the wall to be smooth and easily cleanable.
6) Both walk-in coolers appeared to be dripping water from their compressors (see violation #49). The bar walk in cooler contained several ready-to-eat items, including cut fruit, red peppers flakes, parmesan cheese, and milk. This provides an opportunity for cross contamination. 

Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
The CFM was unable to show inspectors allergen awareness training certificate. All CFMs must obtain allergen awareness training within 30 days of employment. Inspector gave allergen certification information to the CFM.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink after washing hands. PIC was informed that a barrier such as a paper towel should be used to turn off the hand sink to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure all staff members are properly hand washing at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed an employee fail to wash their hands before donning new gloves to portion food for the dessert bar. The PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper handwashing. Ensure staff are washing their hands before putting on new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed knives and a pair of scissors stored inside of counters or equipment which is not considered easily cleanable. Ensure utensils are stored in designated areas to avoid contamination. The PIC was informed and the utensils were sent to the dish area.
citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (1) In locker rooms; (3) In garbage rooms; (4) In mechanical rooms; (5) Under sewer lines that are not shielded to intercept potential drips; (6) Under leaking water lines including leaking automatic fire sprinkler heads or under lines on which water has condensed; (7) Under open stairwells; or (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Inspector observed the triple sink in the dish washing area to be leaking from the drainage plumbing. PIC was informed that waste water must be properly conveyed and plumbing must be maintained in good repair. A follow-up will be conducted on July 24, 2025 to ensure the plumbing has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
citation_text:
2-103.11(I) Inspector observed multiple priority and priority foundation violations during this inspection. See violations below. Staff education is needed regarding cold holding temperatures, handwashing procedures, and other safe food handling practices.

Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (I) EMPLOYEES are properly maintaining the temperatures of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOODS during hot and cold holding through daily oversight of the EMPLOYEES’ routine monitoring of FOOD temperatures.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(A) Inspector observed an employee using the triple sink to wash hands. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that employees only use the handwashing sink to wash hands. This helps to prevent cross contamination. Inspector will return 7/24/2025 to reevaluate hand-washing procedures.

Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
