title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the can-opener at the facility to have a soiled blade. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the can opener blade is cleaned regularly enough to keep it free of food soils and debris. Inspector will return 07/31/2025 to reevaluate the condition of the can opener.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed many of the foods in the walk-in cooler to be above 41F. Foods probed include: Carnitas (50F), Cheese Sauce (50F), Consommé (51F), Raw Beef (51F), Raw Hamburger (50F), Cheese Sauce x2 (52F), Bacon (51F), Refried Beans (51F), Milk (51F), Raw Beef (52F), Cheese Sauce x3 (54F), Sour Cream (48F), Cut Lettuce (53F), Egg Rolls (53F). All out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Ensure that TCS foods are kept at 41F or below. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate cold-holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the drawer coolers under the griddle to not be holding temperatures below 41F. Items in coolers are as follows: Raw Chicken (53.5F), Raw Beef (52F), Raw Marinated Chicken (51.5F), and shredded cheese (55F). All items were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are kept at or below 41F. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate reevaluate cooler temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed 3 TCS items being stored out of refrigeration. The items were: Barbecue Sauce (Ambient temperature), mayonnaise (75F), feta (54F). All were voluntarily thrown away. The barbecue sauce was open on a shelf at room temp, and had been there for a while. Facility was attempting to store the mayo and feta in an ice bath. When preparing an ice bath, ensure that food containers are submerged to the top of the container in ice. Ice must then be replenished as needed to keep foods at or below 41F. Inspector will return 07/24/2025 to reevaluate the cold holding of these items.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
Inspector observed the walk-in cooler at the facility to be failing. Multiple foods inside the cooler probed at above 41F. See violation 22  regarding the walk-in cooler for more information. Ensure cooler is repaired or replaced. Inspector will return 07/31/2025 to reevaluate the cooler’s ability to hold temperatures at 41F or below.

Inspector observed the drawer coolers at the facility to be failing. Multiple foods inside the cooler probed at above 41F. See violation 22 regarding drawer coolers for more information. Ensure cooler is repaired or replaced. Inspector will return 07/31/2025 to reevaluate the cooler’s ability to hold temperatures at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Inspector observed a spatula being used to scoop carnitas in the walk-in cooler to be stored improperly. The spatula was sitting on the shelving in the cooler next to the carnitas. Ensure that while utensils are in use they are stored in the food being served with the handle sticking up. Alternatively, utensils may also be stored on a clean and sanitized work surface while not in use.

3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed 2 utensils in need of repair or replacement in the kitchen. The first utensil in need of replacement or repair was the juicer. The paint on the juicer is flaking from the surface. The second utensil is the fine mesh strainer hanging in front of the ice machine. Loose wires are sticking off the side of the strainer basket. Ensure these items are repaired or replaced.
citation_text: 4-502.11(A) Good Repair and Calibration. (A) UTENSILS shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed several instances of a #55 violation at the establishment.

1) The floor of the kitchen was covered in water and food debris upon the inspector’s arrival. Ensure that the floor is kept free of large amounts of water and food debris.

2) The cold-water outlets in the floor behind the sink have been sealed into the floor with a material that is not smooth and easily cleanable. The material was observed to hold food debris and soils. Ensure this material is either smoothed or replaced to make it easily cleanable.

3) The walk-in cooler compressor is leaking water on the floor of the walk-in cooler and possibly foods inside. Ensure this is repaired to prevent the contamination of other surfaces and items in the cooler.

Ensure these areas are maintained and kept in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The nozzle used for root beer on the fountain drink machine is observed heavily soiled on the inner surface during his inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned the nozzle during this inspection to correct. He stated that they are soaked regularly. This helps but routine cleaning is still needed to maintain safe standards. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times in the facility.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-303.11 Ice Used as Exterior Coolant, Prohibited as Ingredient. After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of FOOD such as melons or FISH, PACKAGED FOODS such as canned BEVERAGES, or cooling coils and tubes of EQUIPMENT, ice may not be used as FOOD. 

A gallon of tea is observed stored in the ice in the ice machine during this inspection. The PIC was shown and removed the item during this inspection to correct. Ensure that ice used for drinks is not used as a cooling or cold holding medium.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the caulking to be missing to the right of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure staff is checking caulking regularly.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food manager to be present upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, ensure a certified food manager is present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the bottom of the sandwich prep cooler to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, cooler will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact areas are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at mop sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking as needed.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw eggs stored over horchata (prepared ready-to-eat drink) and various sauces in the double door cooler. The PIC was educated and the eggs were moved onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw eggs are always stored below ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl). Dishes and other equipment can still be washed and rinsed in the dish machine; however, they must be sanitized in the triple sink until the dish machine is properly sanitizing. During the inspection the triple sink was setup with sanitizer. The inspector will follow-up on 7/21/2025 to check that the dish machine is properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed there is a buildup of debris on the ice machine baffles and the can opener blade. The PIC was reminded that food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soil residues. The inspector will follow-up on 7/28/2025 to check that the ice machine baffles and can opener blade have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed a jug of milk that was opened yesterday and a container of horchata (ready-to-eat milk based drink) that was prepared yesterday were not date marked. The PIC was educated and the milk and horchata were date marked during the inspection. All temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods held at the establishment for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed various foods stored uncovered in the white reach-in freezer and uncovered taco shells on the cookline. The PIC was educated that all foods must be covered to avoid contamination. Ensure that foods are properly covered during storage by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed cooked rice and pico de gallo in the left prep cooler had bowls for scoops. All scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of the food to avoid contamination. During the inspection the PIC removed the bowls. Ensure that all ready-to-eat foods have scoops with a handle that are stored properly by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the ice scoop holder is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed raw eggs stored over lettuce in the walk-in cooler. PIC was informed and the eggs were moved. Ensure raw ingredients are stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employee to not use a barrier when turning off hand washing faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper handwashing technique, and the employee rewashed their hands. Ensure proper handwashing practices are followed.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the front display prep cooler to be cold holding TCS items at 50F. Discussed with PIC, TCS item kept in prep cooler were all prepped 2 hours before service. A time as control procedure has been set for TCS items kept in cooler. During inspection, items within cooler dropped to below 41F, COS. Inspector will spot check cooler in the following days to ensure cooler is correctly working. Ensure any TCS item being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Caulking behind the triple sink and at the fryer sink was observed to be in disrepair. Surfaces that cannot be moved for cleaning should be sealed to the wall, so that they are smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure sinks are adhered to wall by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-402.11(A) Fixed Equipment, Spacing or Sealing. (A) EQUIPMENT that is fixed because it is not EASILY MOVABLE shall be installed so that it is: (3) SEALED to adjoining EQUIPMENT or walls, if the EQUIPMENT is exposed to spillage or seepage.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: FIRST REPEAT: There is ice accumulation in the walk-in freezer on a pipe, on walls, and on shelving. Clean to remove ice build-up. Repair the walk-in freezer to prevent ice accumulation. Facility is aware of the issue.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed significant accumulation of mold and soda syrup on the wall underneath the soda machine. Non-food contact surfaces should be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of mold or debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed two different employees donning gloves without washing hands. CORRECTED- Inspector educated employees about the need to wash hands before donning gloves, and they washed hands before putting on new pairs of gloves. Ensure employees wash hands before donning gloves and having contact with food.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed an employee use the hand washing sink behind the service counter to clean slushee catch tray. CORRECTED- Inspector informed employee that hand washing sinks should not be used to clean dishes. Ensure that designated hand washing sinks are used only for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

Use the triple sink to sanitize by hand until the machine is serviced and observed to dispensing the appropriate amount of sanitizer.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning. [P]

comment:
The following food contact surfaces were observed to be soiled:
1) The container holding drink stirring spoons at the cafe station- CORRECTED- employee took container and spoons to be cleaned and sanitized.
2) Ice baffles were observed to have slight mold. A follow up is scheduled on 07/28/25 to ensure the ice baffles are clean to sight and touch.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed pasta salad and cut melon in prep cooler without date marking. CORRECTED- inspector notified the person in charge, and they stated the items were both prepared yesterday. The operator put dates on both items. Ensure that all items prepared at the facility and being held for more than twenty four hours are marked with the date of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed several items (mushroom, gravy, mixed peppers, sauteed onions, chimi sc, and cream cheese) to be stored and used past the 7 day date requirement. CORRECTED- person in charge was notified and voluntarily discarded items that had been prepared over seven days ago. Ensure that all items are used or discarded within seven days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The tongs stored in the cooked rice along the buffet line was observed with the handle touching cooked noodles (directly behind the rice). The handle of the tongs is used by the consumer. Be sure that employees monitor utensils that are being stored on the buffet line to prevent the contamination of other food items.
citation_text: 3-306.13(C) Consumer Self-Service Operations. (C) CONSUMER self-service operations such as buffets and salad bars shall be monitored by FOOD EMPLOYEES trained in safe operating procedures.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment:
THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: 2-103.11(L) The operators are knowledgeable of the food code but are struggling to apply these safe food handling practices. New staff is not being trained on proper hand washing. And the practices of general cleaning, maintenance, and storage have lapsed. See that education to staff is completed prior to them starting to cook and handle food. See that staff does not forget to practice the knowledge known for safe food handling. Will revisit safe food handling during the ten day follow-up. 


Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure.  Observed new employee to be nearly unable to understand how to properly wash hands. Demonstration of proper hand washing occurred multiple times, the staff member was asked to wash hands, and it took nearly five attempts to observe a successful handwashing. The lack of knowledge was discussed with the owner. The owner was encouraged to have an education session with the employee (see violation #1). The employee speaks Spanish and language is a barrier. SCDPH will bring a Spanish-speaking interpreter to facilitate education. Employee was present for five days. 


(B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision.  The mens toilet room is observed to not be supplied with paper toweling. Supplied with paper toweling during the inspection.

Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food. The facility is observed to have a number of foods, stored from the previous days’ operation, to be uncovered (cooked beef and peanut sauce in the double door cooler is nearly freeze-dried, and multiple foods in the preparation cooler base). Covered during the inspection. 


Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION for storage order violations (i.e., raw meats being stored over ready to eat foods, raw meats not being stored according to internal cooking temperatures).
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation.  Observed raw beef to be stored in direct contact with bok choy. There was a moment where the beef was momentarily moved to a new location while bok choy was discarded. Eventually, the owner discarded the beef and pulled the veggie container to be cleaned and refilled. Corrected on site. 

Raw beef over raw shrimp observed in the walk-in cooler. Discussed storage order with the owner. See that staff is educated on proper storage order. Corrected on site. 

Observed a container of mayonnaise in a metal dish stored in direct contact with a container of veggies. The mayo container was moved and the top layer of the veggies was removed. Corrected on site. 


(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION. 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. Observed the hood to beginning to drip grease due to lack of cleaning. Maintain the hood system clean so that accumulated grease does not drip into food being cooked beneath. 

(A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils.  Observed soiled knives to be soiled on a soiled magnetic strip. The knives were pulled for cleaning during the inspection. The magnetic strip should be cleaned in-place. Also observed the can opener was soiled with grease (THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION). The can opener should be cleaned after every use. 




(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. The back door has a broken self-closer (that will be ordered/owner is aware). Also, there is some daylight visible along the middle of the right side of the door (even when the door is closed). See that door is able to self-close and that daylight is eliminated from around the door. 

(A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION. 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. Observed multiple foods being stored on the floor in the back storage space (foods include sauces, chili peppers, bags of uncooked rice). 

FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. Observed two whisks and a lid for a pan being stored held against the wall by the plumbing of the water heater. The utensils were removed for proper cleaning and then storage during the inspection. Cease using this back room to store clean utensils. Utensils to be used for kitchen use/food contact should be properly stored on a clean surface within the kitchen space. 


FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
citation_text:
3-304.12(B) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. Observed the scoop of the sugar to be stored within the product. The scoop was properly stored with the handle extended out of the food during the inspection. Cease allowing scoops to fall into foods that may require no further cooking. 


During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(B) In food that is not time/temperature control for safety food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment:
THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION. 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. Observed single-service items in the back dry storage room stored on the floor. Cease storing single-service items on the floor. Ensure that single-service items are stored 6-inches off the ground to avoid contamination. 

(A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. The following surfaces need maintenance attention: 1) both of the freezers in the back storage space are observed thickly coated with frost (inches worth!); 2) there is observed duct tape on the side of a pitcher (discarded the pitcher during the inspection) (THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION); 3) the double door cooler holding soda is observed to have a peeling piece of weather stripping (repair the weather stripping); and 4) grey tub holding chicken on the top shelf of the walk-in cooler is observed to have a cut in the bottom corner  (discarded during the inspection). Repair the aforementioned surfaces so they are smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable. 

Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. Observed the following surfaces to be soiled: 1) the shelves above the triple sink; 2) food debris on the bottom of the double door freezer; 3) walk-in cooler shelves are observed thickly coated with food debris; 4) lid of the prep cooler; 5) the shelves of the soda-holding cooler. Items that are observed soiled need to be cleaned at frequency that allows surfaces to be maintained clean. Clean the aforementioned items. 



(B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 REPEAT VIOLATION. There is an acoustic ceiling tile that is water damaged in-front of the woks. The tile is pulled to the side (possibly broken) and allowing for AC unit drips to fall onto the floor in-front of the woks.

THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION. Ceiling tiles in the dry storage area by the back door are starting to show signs of ware from leaks. 


Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12.The floor of the walk-in cooler is observed soiled with accumulated food debris (especially around the storage racks and corners). Also, the walls around the wok (including the wok) and the wall behind the preparation area by the prep cooler are soiled with accumulated foods.    

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. There is a strong odor around the grease trap in the kitchen. Owner acknowledged that the trap hasn’t been cleaned in over six months. The grease trap should be serviced soon in-order to prevent the facility from having a plumbing back-up. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. Observed owner’s personal items to be migrating throughout the facility. See that personal items are maintained in one or two locations of the facility. 


(B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were a few dishes that were observed to be soiled on the clean dish shelf during the inspection today. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the dishes were placed in the dish area to be cleaned again. The employees washing dishes need to ensure that they are fully cleaned before placing them with the clean dishes. Food contact surfaces need to be clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. 

Multiple employees are observed to wash their hands in the three part sink in the main concession stand. Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that proper hand washing procedures are enforced at the facility. Food handlers should only wash their hands in the designated hand washing sinks.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

The hand sink in the third base concession stand is without paper towels on inspector arrival. The PIC was notified and supplied paper towels to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote correct hand washing.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

1) Plastic spoons are observed at the stand alone ice cream stand in a cup with the handles and food/lip contact surfaces intermixed and exposed. The PIC was shown and instructed to arrange them so that the handles are up/exposed to correct. (REPEAT) 2) Food boats are observed throughout the the main concession stand with the food contact surfaces up/exposed. Education was conducted and the stacks of boats flipped over to correct. Ensure that all single service items are protected from contamination prior to use/service.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer ready for use in the facility. Buckets were made during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that sanitizers are available and ready for use at al times that foods are being handled in the facility.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Several cans in the dry storage room are observed with major dents. The PIC was shown and removed the items for credit during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the package integrity is maintained at all times for the stored foods in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

1) Raw fish is observed over raw beef in the standing cooler to the left of the fryers. 2) Raw sausage is observed over Ready-To-Eat (RTE) deli meats in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown both locations and adjusted the storage to correct. Ensure that items in a cooler are stored with the RTE items on top, then raw vegetables, raw sea food, raw beef/pork and raw chicken on the bottom to prevent contamination based on the relative cooking temperatures of the items.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The container used for storing Dixie cups along the prep and service lines is observed soiled. The PIC was shown and had the container washed and items replaced to correct. Ensure that single service items are protected from contamination until use.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

All of the Allergen training certificates available at the facility have expired at the end of last year. The PIC was notified and instructed to have the current CFPMs retake the course/renew the certification. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility maintain current allergen training certifications at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed food handler donning gloves before handling food. CORRECTED- education was provided regarding the need to wash hands prior to donning gloves. Ensure all employees wash hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Sanitizer bottles were observed on the same shelf as the sampling orange juice on the cart. CORRECTED- employee moved the sampling juice to the counter. Education was provided regarding the need to separate toxic substances from ready to eat (RTE) food items. Ensure chemicals are stored away from RTE items to prevent potential contamination of food.
citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed worn out caulking behind wash section of triple sink in HMS room. Discussed with PIC and he put in a repair order to have the caulking replaced. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair. Re-caulk sink by next routine inspection. [C]
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed the single-use utensils at the front customer counter were stored with the food contact surfaces facing upwards. The PIC was educated and the utensils were inverted during the inspection. Ensure that single-use utensils are always stored with the handles facing outwards to avoid contaminating food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the containers holding clean dishes on the shelving across from the dish machine had an accumulation of food residue and other debris on the bottom. The PIC was informed and the containers were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed various white powders (ex. sugar, flour, salt) in the kitchen that had been removed from the original packaging and moved into large containers but were not labeled. All easily mistakable foods not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. Ensure that any white powder re-packaged into storage containers are labeled with the common name of the food by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed a large container of cream filling stored with the scoop handle directly touching the filling. The PIC was informed and they removed the scoop from the container. They stated that the company policy is that scoops should not be stored within food containers. The PIC will be educating employees about the proper procedure. Ensure that scoop handles for ready-to-eat foods are always stored above food to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the cove base underneath the front triple sink is not attached to the wall. The cove base must be sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the cove base is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed the facility was preparing donuts during the inspection but there was not a sanitizer bucket available. The PIC was informed and they made a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a significant buildup of dust on the walk-in freezer fans. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in freezer fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the utility sink was observed coming apart. PIC was made aware. PIC ensured inspector that a ticket will be put in for the caulking repairs on the utility sink. Ensure that the utility sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at back kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure staff is monitoring facility to prevent any possible leaks.
citation_text: 5-201.11 Approved. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM and hoses conveying water shall be constructed and repaired with APPROVED materials according to LAW. (B) A water filter shall be made of SAFE MATERIALS.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The caulking on the back of house coffee table is disconnected on the right side causing a gap between the wall and table. The table must be properly caulked because it cannot be removed from the wall for cleaning. The caulking on the right side must be replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

(2) There are several small holes in the wall within the dish washing room. The holes are from shelving that was removed. The holes must be filled (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The accumulation of soil debris behind the soda nozzles on the drive through and customer drink dispensers. 

(2) The dust on the shelves holding clean dishes and equipment above the non-functioning prep coolers in the dish washing room. 

(3) The debris on the floor of the outside shed that stores single-use articles.

citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: PIC has not demonstrated knowledge of food safety practices. PIC has continued to operate without essential equipment (pH meter) or other interim measures in place. Operator was noted to have falsified data logged within record logs. This violation alone will warrant a number of additional spot checks to insure staff is properly trained and understands the importance of monitoring and logging. See violations below.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection. [Pf]

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Sushi rice is not acidified, nor is a Time as a Control policy in place to maintain food safety while rice is held on the countertop to make sushi rolls. Discussed the use of Time as a Control with PIC. If sushi rice used from cooking, rolls created from that rice need to be created and sold within 4 hours of rice being removed from the rice cooker. If sushi rice is cooled to 41F within 6 hours (and logs are maintained), sushi rolls created from that rice need to be sold within 6 hours of the rice being removed from cold-holding. Sushi packages need to be labeled to indicate the time that they should be consumed by.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control. [Pf]

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
comment: Facility does not have a functional pH meter. The pH meter was not functional during the previous inspection. PIC indicated during this inspection that the pH meter has not been used since the previous inspection. Facility must have functional equipment to measure sushi rice pH and use it regularly. PIC has ordered a new pH meter. Inspector will follow up to see that a new pH meter is provided and verify PIC’s ability to use said meter.
citation_text: 8-103.12(C) Conformance with Approved Procedures. If the REGULATORY AUTHORITY grants a VARIANCE as specified in § 8-103.10, or a HACCP PLAN is otherwise required as specified under § 8-201.13, the PERMIT HOLDER shall: (C) Maintain and provide to the regulatory authority, upon request, records specified under § 8-201.14 (D) and (E)(3) that demonstrate that the following are routinely employed; (1) Procedures for monitoring the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (2) Monitoring of the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (3) Verification of the effectiveness of the operation or process, and (4) Necessary corrective actions if there is failure at a CRITICAL CONTROL POINT.

title: Compliance with variance/specialized process/HACCP.
comment: Logs and discussion with the PIC indicate sushi rice pH and pH meter logs have been falsified. Logs reflect that the pH meter has been calibrated and sushi pH measured over the last week despite the lack of a functional pH meter in the facility. Staff must record accurate HACCP records. Inspector will follow up to see that accurate logs are maintained.
citation_text: 8-103.12(C) Conformance with Approved Procedures. If the REGULATORY AUTHORITY grants a VARIANCE as specified in § 8-103.10, or a HACCP PLAN is otherwise required as specified under § 8-201.13, the PERMIT HOLDER shall: (C) Maintain and provide to the regulatory authority, upon request, records specified under § 8-201.14 (D) and (E)(3) that demonstrate that the following are routinely employed; (1) Procedures for monitoring the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (2) Monitoring of the CRITICAL CONTROL POINTS, (3) Verification of the effectiveness of the operation or process, and (4) Necessary corrective actions if there is failure at a CRITICAL CONTROL POINT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: A build up of food debris was observed in the drain of the kitchen hand-sink. Discussed proper usage of hand-sink with PIC to educate employees. Ensure that handwashing sinks are only used for handwashing. Never use hand-sink for rinsing dishes or other food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A total of 4 ketchup cans were observed to have dents along the seams of the cans. CORRECTED- Person in charge voluntarily removed can and will send back to supplier. Ensure seams of cans are not dented to prevent bacterial growth.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed food debris on ready to use vegetable chopper. CORRECTED- Person in charge removed utensil to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure utensils are cleaned after each use and are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the counter near the front hand sink. CORRECTED- Person in charge moved cloth to sanitizer bucket before inspector was able to discuss item. Ensure wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer buckets in between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspector observed knife on the kitchen prep table (near rice) to be suspended between two tables. CORRECTED- Person in charge removed the knife to be cleaned and sanitized. Food contact surfaces should be stored in such a manner to protect from contamination while in use.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed utensils storage container to contain food debris. CORRECTED- Person in charge removed utensil storage container to be cleaned and sanitized. Non-food contact surfaces should be cleaned at frequency to prevent accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination. [C]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler next to the grill in the kitchen was observed to be inoperable during today’s inspection. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored in the cooler are being monitored with time as a control until the cooler is repaired. Ensure TCS foods in the cooler are kept for no longer than 4 hours. Items kept in the cooler for 4 hours must be discarded; they cannot be cooled and reused. A follow-up is scheduled for July 25th to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the servers station to have a build-up of soils on them. CORRECTED Discussed with PIC, and PIC had the nozzles changed out for clean nozzles immediately. Ensure nozzles are cleaned or replaced frequently enough to keep them free of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed 4-5 flies in the first aisle of the dry-storage room. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the flies are dealt with using authorized pest control methods. Zappers and fly strips may be hung, but they must not be hung over food.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed there to be clean utensils and baking equipment stored on a shelf behind a prep area in the back of the kitchen. These clean, stored utensils were observed to have food debris on them, likely from food prep at the prep table. Discussed more regularly cleaning with PIC. Ensure these cleaned utensils are kept covered, or cleaned regularly enough that they do not accumulate soils.
citation_text: 4-903.12(A)(1) and A(3)-(8) Prohibitions. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, cleaned and SANITIZED EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES may not be stored: (8) Under other sources of contamination.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed there to be several areas in the kitchen in need of a general cleaning. Areas include:

1) The kitchen floors, especially behind and around equipment.
2) Walls behind prep areas, they are especially susceptible to soil build-up.
3) Dry storage rack in kitchen has lots of flour and other debris on it.
4) The dry storage room has some items spilling on to the floor, as well as some flour and other food debris. 
5) Under the crock pot that is currently not in use.

Ensure these areas are cleaned regularly to prevent soil build-up.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the dump sink in the mop room to be pulling away from the wall. Discussed sink maintenance with the PIC. Ensure that the sink is re-caulked to the wall to create a smooth transition between surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There wasn’t any signed employee health forms on file for any of the employees working at the time of the inspection. Provided copies of employee health forms to the PIC (both in Spanish & English). Ensure that all employees have signed and completed health forms and be sure that they are readily available for future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There wasn’t any quaternary ammonium test strips available for the sanitizer solutions. Discussed with PIC. The facility has chlorine test strips for the chemical sanitizing dish machine(in the back of the house), however, they were observed soiled and no longer functional. Ensure to have test strips for each chemical that is being used to sanitize dishes and food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There was a significant amount of ice buildup on the top inner surface of the Coca Cola cooler (near tortilla chip station). Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure to maintain non-food contact surfaces of coolers to prevent the accumulation of ice buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.
