In this case, the facility must use a scoop with a handle to scoop the sugar to ensure no contact between human hands and RTE foods. CORRECTED PIC replaced the cup with a scoop with a handle.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a build-up of food debris behind the shelves in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that cooler is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build-up of food debris in hard-to-reach areas.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed dipping well to be turned off upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, dipping wells were turned on. Ensure dipping wells are turned on and running water during hours of operation.
citation_text: 3-304.12(D) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (D) In running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist food such as ice cream or mashed potatoes.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed a leak to be present at back kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, sink will be serviced by a licensed plumber. Ensure staff is monitoring facility to prevent any possible leaks.
citation_text: 5-201.11 Approved. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM and hoses conveying water shall be constructed and repaired with APPROVED materials according to LAW. (B) A water filter shall be made of SAFE MATERIALS.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the can opener blade had an accumulation of debris and other soil residues. The PIC was reminded that the blade should be cleaned and sanitized after every use. During the inspection the can opener blade was cleaned to sight and touch. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The food debris inside the right pizza prep cooler.

(2) The food splashes and debris inside the microwave. 

(3) The dust and other soil residues on the shelves holding dishes, equipment, and packaged food in-between the dish washing area and prep counter.

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food reside, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple incidents of food handlers donning gloves without washing hands. CORRECTED- Education was conducted with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that hands are washed at each time that it is required per code. Ensure that hand washing takes place prior to donning gloves in the facility.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) [P].

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Hand sink in Memory Care was lacking paper towels. CORRECTED- PIC resupplied hand sink. All hand sinks must be supplied with paper towels at all times.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel. [Pf].

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
REPEAT
Numerous dented cans were observed throughout the dry storage area. Ensure cans that are dented along the top, bottom, or side seams are discarded, as are any cans with significant dents that create sharp edges. CORRECTED- Dented cans were pulled aside to be returned to the supplier or voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
1) Two knives on the magnetic knife strip were observed to have food debris on them. 
2) Scoop holder for ice machine was observed to contain floating debris.

Utensils and utensil holder were pulled to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned after each use and are maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
REPEAT
Food debris or soil accumulation was observed under the 3 door cooler and freezer. Discussed with PIC the need to clean under equipment. Ensure facility is cleaned at a frequency to avoid accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
REPEAT
Damp mop heads were observed stored in the basin of the mop sink. Education was provided to PIC about proper mop storage to prevent growth of bacteria. Ensure mops are stored correctly between uses moving forward.
citation_text: 6-501.16 After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Caulking is missing behind triple sink to the right of the dish machine. Areas that are not easily moved for cleaning must be sealed to the wall. Seal the space between the wall and the sink prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The fan covers of the walk in cooler (behind meat & seafood) were observed with a significant amount dust accumulation. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that cleaning of the fan covers occurs as often as necessary to prevent buildup and contamination of food items.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The faucet of the triple sink in the butcher room was observed with a few leaks. There was water leaking from the faucet into the basin of the sink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that sink faucets are maintained in good repair and never in leaking condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There was a significant amount of ice buildup on the floor of the walk in freezer in the butcher shop. Ice buildup was observed on the floor underneath the storage shelf(to the right of the door). Discussed with PIC. Ensure that cleaning of walk in units occur as often as necessary to prevent ice buildup.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed rice and rice noodles soaking in buckets with no lid. Advised to keep food containers covered at all times. Coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container.  The PIC placed covers on both buckets during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed riceice and rice noodles soaking in water in buckets on the floor. Advised to store elsewhere on a shelf or table. Never store open containers of food on the floor to prevent contamination. Staff moved rice and noodles off floor during the inspection. This violation is considered corrected-on-site.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed bacon cooked yesterday in walk in cooler was not date marked. CORRECTED- PIC placed label on cooked bacon. Ensure that all temperature controlled ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum holding time. [Pf]
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed accumulation of dust on multiple kitchen ceiling vents. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that ceiling vents are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection. [C]
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: None of the employees working at the time of the inspection were certified food protection managers. PIC mentioned that two more employees are in the process of getting food manager certified. Ensure that there is at least one employee who is food manager certified present at the facility all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: There was a significant amount of ice build-up on the shelves stored in the walk in freezer. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure to maintain non-food contact surfaces of equipment as frequent as necessary to prevent ice build-up.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There was a leak observed at the faucet handles of the produce washing sink. PIC mentioned that a work order will be placed as soon as possible. Ensure that faucets are maintained in good repair and are in leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: The additional employee (second to PIC) did not have a signed employee health reporting form. PIC mentioned that she will have the employee sign and complete the form as soon as possible. Ensure that every employee has a signed employee health form on file at the facility.
citation_text: 2-201.11(A)(2) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person In Charge, and Conditional Employees. Reportable Diagnosis. (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. A FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE shall report the information in a manner that allows the PERSON IN CHARGE to reduce the RISK of foodborne disease transmission, including providing necessary additional information, such as the date of onset of symptoms and an illness, or of a diagnosis without symptoms, if the FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE: (2) Has an illness diagnosed by a HEALTH PRACTITIONER due to: (a) Norovirus, (b) Hepatitis A virus, (c) Shigella spp., (d) Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli, (e) Typhoid fever (caused by Salmonella Typhi) or (f) Salmonella (nontyphoidal).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was quiche being stored in an unrefrigerated display case. PIC isn't using time or temperature control to ensure safety for food item. Discussed the need to have quiche on temperature or time control. PIC will use temperature control for most quiche pieces and leave a single piece of quiche on display. The display piece will never be served for consumption. Be sure that TCS foods are either used as temperature/time control to ensure safety of food items.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a package of sliced deli meat stored in the storage room cooler that lacked proper date marking. Discussed proper date marking with PIC and the deli meat was date marked to correct the violation. Ensure that deli meats are date marked if being stored in house longer than 24 hours. Be sure to discard meats if not used within 7 days of opening.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There was a leak observed at the bottom pipe of the triple sink. A bucket was placed underneath the sink to catch the contaminated water. PIC mentioned that the building owner is working to get the leak repaired. Ensure that pipes are maintained in good repair and never in leaking condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

Discussed with PIC and it was acknowledged that the individual with CFPM certification were out and wouldn’t return till later. There was no other person with an active certified food protection manager certification present in the facility. citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A buildup of soil and food debris were observed within the top portion of the prep cooler opposite of the grill along the cook line. Discussed with PIC. citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a few flies in the kitchen and the dry storage areas respectively. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that he necessary action will be taken. Ensure that facility is maintained free of insects and other pests to avoid possible contamination.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the following facility maintenance issues that could impede proper cleaning.
1. A buildup of frost on the refrigeration unit and fan in the walk-in cooler.
2. Few broken tiles under the fryers in the kitchen area. 
3. Dust accumulation hanging off the fan on the floor on the cook line in the kitchen.
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that the above mentioned areas are cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Facility was observed to be out of compliance with food allergen awareness training. PIC was made aware and PIC had no knowledge of the possible location of the certification if any was available. Ensure that facility is compliant with this law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the three compartment sink without caulking. PIC was made aware and PIC ensured inspector that the three compartment sink will have the necessary caulking done.  Ensure that the three compartment sink is caulked to the wall providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Inspector observe that there was only one employee with proof of food handler certification at the facility during the inspection. PIC said that everyone else does have valid food handler certifications however, was unable to provide proof as they may have been locked in a cabinet that is not accessible to them. PIC does not have access to the digital copies either. PIC ensured inspector that they will have the certifications printed out  making them available when needed. Ensure that all employees with the exception of those of the certified food protection manager certification acquired their food handler certification within 30 days of employment.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid recontaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the double door cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was about 55-60F and the following internal temperatures were recorded: shredded cheese 56F, colby jack cheese 55F, mozzarella cheese 55F, cheese slices 54F, cream cheese x3 50-54F, sour cream 53F, ground beef 57F, mayo 55F, salami 58F, sausage 49F, beef 55F, cooked vegetables 55F, ham x3 55-50F, ranch 56F, cheese sauce 55F, and cheddar cheese 58F. All foods has been inside the cooler for over four hours. During the inspection all temperature control for safety (TCS) were voluntary discarded by the PIC (the above mentioned were the TCS foods discarded). There was a package of sausage, steak, and multiple pizzas that were recently purchased that had temperatures below 41F; these were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. The non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (ex. unopened ranch, unopened mayo, uncut tomatoes, cucumbers, lettuce in the harvest cut, and bread). The PIC was instructed that they cannot store any TCS foods inside the cooler until it is cold holing foods at 41F or below. The inspector suggests immediate service for the cooler. The inspector will follow-up on 7/14/2025 to check that the cooler is functioning properly.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The buildup of frost on the standing freezer fans - the freezer must be defrosted. 

(2) The buildup of frost on the reach-in freezers - the freezers must be defrosted.

(3) The cardboard lining the shelf above the sushi prep cooler - the cardboard must be removed. 

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The food debris on the bottom of the standing freezer. 

(2) The grease and food debris on the wall and floor to the right of the fryers. 

(3) The debris on the silver shelves above the prep cooler. 

(4) The debris on the white shelves surrounding the kitchen triple sink. 

(5) The dust on the hood system. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, grease, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the mop was stored with the head in the mop sink basin. The employee working in the kitchen was informed and they hung the mop during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to airdry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the double door cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was between 50-60F and the following internal temperatures were recorded: parmesan cheese 54F, mozzarella cheese 51F, caesar dressing 53F, cut tomatoes 49F, and cream cheese 47F. The temperature control for safety (TCS) foods inside the temperature danger zone were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. There were several TCS foods recently brought to the double cooler from the walk-in cooler that had internal temperatures below 41F and these foods were immediately moved back into the walk-in cooler. All non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC was instructed that they cannot store TCS foods inside the cooler until it is cold holding foods at 41F or less. The inspector suggests getting immediate service for the double cooler. The inspector will return on 7/14/2025 to check on the temperature of the double cooler.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed insect trap placed above clean dish ware (on storage rack between office and mop sink). PIC was notified to have pest control company move trap away from food-contact surfaces to prevent contamination. Insect control devices should not be located over areas where food is being prepared, or where clean equipment is being stored. [C]
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Inspector observed ice bucket faced upwards towards the ceiling- where the food contact surface can be exposed to contaminants.  CORRECTED- Education was provided to the PIC regarding potential contamination of food contact surfaces. Ice bucket was inverted. Food contact surfaces should be stored where they are not exposed to contamination. [C]
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

Multiple employees were observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to actuate the paper towel dispensers. Multiple options were discussed with the PIC for handling this situation but the primary idea is that the bare hands should not be used to actuate this machine. Education conducted to correct. Ensure safe hand washing procedures are used at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

The soap dispenser in the men’s bathroom is observed empty during this inspection. The dispenser was replaced during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times in the facility.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sinks in both bathrooms are observed pulling away from the wall and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair (re-caulk) prior to the next routine inspection and to maintain the surfaces smooth and easily cleanable at all times. Ensure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces at all times in areas subject to foods or moisture.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the left sink at the sushi station that is used for hand washing did not have hand washing signage. The right sink that is used for dumping was labeled with hand washing signage. The signage was removed from the designated dump sink and the PIC was given new hand washing signage for the designed hand washing sink. Ensure that signage that notifies employees to wash hands before returning to work is available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the dump sink (to the left of the reach-in freezer). Stored behind the faucets the cutting board can be contaminated by water splashes, food residue, and other debris dumped into the sink. The cutting board was moved to a different location for storage during the inspection Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. The employee working the dish machine drained the water and the dish machine tested at 100 ppm (Cl) afterwards. The PIC stated that the dish machine repair company suggested draining the water every two hours at the last visit. The inspector reminded that PIC that the dish machine must be tested regularly to make sure that it is functioning correctly (test strips are stored on top of the dish machine). Ensure that the dish machine is always properly sanitizing.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the fried rice in the warmer across from the dish machine had an internal temperature of about 125F. The PIC stated that the rice was put inside the warmer at 11 am when the facility opened. During the inspection the temperature of the warmer was turned up and the rice had an internal temperature of 178F when the inspector re-checked. A time-as-control policy was implemented for the rice. The facility closes at 2:30 pm and any leftover rice will be discarded at this time. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are maintained at 135F or higher.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several pans of cooked rice in the back walk-in cooler stacked together that did not all have date marking. Each item must be individually labeled in case the pans are separated. Ensure that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the seven day maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed the large containers holding various un-packaged white powders were not properly labeled. The containers did not have labels that matched the food inside (ex. flour was in the container labeled corn starch). The PIC stated they will be removing the old labels and creating new labels that match. Ensure that all easily mistaken foods not in the original container are properly labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment:
Observed the following foods stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination:

(1) Uncovered fried tempura on the sushi prep line; the lid was put onto the container during the inspection. 

(2) Uncovered cut vegetables in the walk-in cooler; saran wrap was put on to cover the containers during the inspection. 

(3) A hammer stored on top of foods in the dry storage area; the hammer was moved into the personal storage bin. 

The PIC was reminded that foods not being used must be covered to prevent the risk of contamination and that personal items must be stored away from food. Ensure that foods are always protected from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the silver commercial refrigerator at the end of the cookline (next to the prep cooler) had a plastic wrap that was peeling off. The PIC was informed and an employee removed the plastic wrap during the inspection. Ensure that surfaces are always smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the surface behind the nozzles of the soda machine has an accumulation of soil resides. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the surface behind the soda nozzles are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bottom portion of the walk-in freezer door is in a state of disrepair. The disrepair is causing a build-up of ice on the air curtains and floor by the door. The PIC stated they are still working on finding a company to complete the repairs within their budget. Ensure that materials are properly attached to that they are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to drop a bottle of mayonnaise on the ground, pick it up, and then continue preparing food. CORRECTED- The inspector instructed the employee to sanitize the bottle of mayonnaise, wash his hands, and then don gloves to continue preparing the food. The employee was educated on when to wash his hands. Ensure that food employees are washing their hands and exposed portions of arms after engaging in activities that contaminate their hands.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The walk-in cooler shelves. One walk-in cooler shelf was observed to have an accumulation of mold on it. The others were observed to be in need of cleaning. 
2. The container lids go into in the drive through was observed to have an accumulation of debris in it. 
3. The racks that are used to drop food in the chub warmer were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 

Ensure that these pieces of equipment are cleaned regularly to prevent this accumulation. A follow up is scheduled for 7/16/2025 to ensure these items have been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There were dishes that were observed to still be soiled after being washed that were being placed on the rack with the clean dishes. Ensure that dishes are thoroughly washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The individual washing the dishes should be checking the dishes to ensure they are properly cleaned before they are placed on the rack with the other clean dishes. A follow up is scheduled on 7/16/2025 to ensure that dishes are being thoroughly cleaned before being placed with the clean dishes.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: There was a bottle of regular mayonnaise and a bottle of spicy mayonnaise that were observed to be held on the table next to the preparation cooler, where they were out of cold holding. The PICs thought they could be left out of cold holding. CORRECTED- The guidelines were read by one of the PICs for the mayonnaise and they stated that they can either be at ambient temperature for four hours (Time as Control) or kept in cold holding. The bottles had been made at 11am and had only been out for around thirty minutes during a rush. The bottles were placed back in the preparation cooler and the PICs were educated to make sure that they are being either cold held or left out for four hours and then discarded. Ensure that Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are held at 41F and under.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: REPEAT- There are single-use boats sitting above the fryer with the food contact surface exposed to contamination. Discussed proper single service storage. Ensure that these boats, along with all other single-service utensils and articles, are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: REPEAT- The walk-in cooler door handle is observed to be cracked and missing a part. Ensure that this is repaired or replaced. Equipment should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The shelf holding the soda syrups and the lines to the soda syrups are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue on them. 
2. REPEAT- The chicken hot holding unit next to the bun toaster. 
3. The bottom of the hot holding unit across from the fryers and the catcher part of it that catches the steam moisture. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The chub warmer is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall. 
2. The table that holds the lemonade and soda machine in the drive through area is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall. 
3. The triple sink is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall, especially to the left of the triple sink and directly above the left side. 
4. The batter station is observed to be in need of being re-caulked to the wall. 
5. The grouting around the batter stations and fryers is observed to be low and is allowing food debris and water to collect. Ensure that this area is re-grouted and is made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
6. REPEAT- The dish shelves across from the ice machine are rusted. They need to be sealed to prevent contamination to clean dishes.
7. REPEAT- The plate to the entrance of the walk-in freezer needs to be repaired to be secure to avoid any debris from being trapped under it. 
8. REPEAT- There is a chipped coving tile by the back door that needs repaired. 
9. REPEAT- There is a frost issue in the walk-in freezer that is causing frost and ice to build up. Ensure that the ice and frost are removed and this issue is repaired to prevent it from occurring. 

Ensure all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The floor underneath the fryers. 
2. The wall above the hood system is observed to have an accumulation of dust on it. 
3. REPEAT- The walk-in freezer floor. There is a chunk of ice that needs to be scraped off as well. 

Ensure that all of these areas are cleaned and maintained cleaned. Physical facilities should be cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There was a bottle of water that was in the standing freezer across from the cook line. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the PIC and the bottle of water was discarded. There is already an area for employee storage in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that staff are educated that employee’s items are not mixed with items for the restaurant to protect food, equipment, linens, and single service articles from contamination.

title: Food handler training
comment:
REPEAT- The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Inspector observed fish stored directly under beef and pork in the bottom of the kitchen prep cooler. PIC was informed, and the fish was moved to the freezer. Ensure proper storage order practices are followed to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the prep cooler was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The hanging internal thermometer was reading at about 55F. The following internal temperatures were recorded: jalapeños 53F, chicken 51F, turkey 50F, ham 53F, burger patty 49F, chorizo 49F, parmesan cheese 52F, monterey jack cheese 55F, southwest sauce 56F, spicy mayo 58F, sour cream cups 58F, and salsa cups 53F. Non-temperature control for safety (TCS) foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (ex. onions, jalapeños, pickles, various non-dairy based sauce, strawberries, corn mix, avocados). Some of the TCS foods were put inside the cooler at 8:30 am and other TCS foods has been inside the cooler since last night. The following TCS foods had been inside the cooler since last night and were voluntarily discarded: turkey, ham, feta cheese, parmesan cheese, burger patties, dairy bases sauces (southwest, spicy mayo, and mayo), sour cream cups, and salsa cups. The following TCS foods had been inside the cooler since 8:30 am and were put under time-as-control (TAC) to be discarded at 12:30 pm: lettuce, cut tomato, all cheeses, chicken, and chorizo. The PIC wrote down and posted above the prep cooler the foods that must be discarded and the time they will be discarded. The PIC also mentioned that they are not busy today and will most likely close at 12:30 pm. The PIC spoke with Koady Hawkins who stated they will be scheduling service for the cooler. They will be putting small amounts of TCS foods that can be used within four hours inside the prep cooler until it is serviced. They were reminded that they cannot store TCS foods inside the cooler without TAC until it is cold holding foods at 41F or below. For information about the cooler, see violation #33.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order: 

(1) The raw beef stored over various ready-to-eat foods in the double cooler to the left of the cookline (near the dish machine). During the inspection the raw beef was moved onto a bottom shelf. 

(2) Multiple containers of raw chicken stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler. During the inspection the raw chicken was moved onto a bottom shelf. The facility stores all raw meat in the back left corner of the walk-in cooler and the inspector suggests labeling the bottom shelf for chicken storage only. 

Ensure that raw foods are stored below ready-to eat-foods and raw meats are stored according to internal cooking temperatures. Due to the amount of repeat violations the health educator will be reaching out to schedule food storage education at the facility.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed the prep cooler on the cookline is currently not functioning. The PIC was aware that the cooler was not functioning and prior to the inspection implemented a time-as-control (TAC) policy for temperature control for safety foods inside the cooler (cut tomatoes, lettuce, mayo, and cheese). The majority of the foods had already been removed from the cooler and only condiments and cut vegetables were being stored in the top. While they had implemented a TAC policy they were not writing down the time when food must be discarded. The PIC was aware of the time the foods were put into the cooler and during the inspection a note pad was brought to the prep table and the foods in temperature control were recorded. The PIC stated that a new part has already been ordered to fix the cooler, but until it is serviced they will continue to use TAC. The inspector will follow-up on 7/10/2025 to check on either the TAC procedure or that the cooler is properly functioning. Ensure that foods are properly marked to indicate the four hour TAC window until the cooler is cold holding foods at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspectors observed facility not being in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the person with the CFPM certification will get the training done as soon as possible. Ensure that at least one certified food protection manager at the facility obtain a basic allergen awareness training. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani buckets in the facility would barely register a change on the inspector’s tests trips. The buckets were remade during this inspection to effective concentration to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels at all times in the facility.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A)  TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained: (2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

The tuna poke in the cold holding well on the front prep line is observed with internal temperatures of 66F. The PIC was shown and discarded the container to correct. A deeper well was acquired to help with future storage options. Ensure that all TCS foods are stored at safe temperatures at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed multiple food service employees fail to wash hands before donning a new pair of gloves. PIC was informed and education was conducted regarding proper hand washing practices. Ensure staff are washing hands before donning new gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler next to the grill in the kitchen was observed to be inoperable during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that the cooler failed overnight and all food items in the cooler were discarded. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored in the cooler are being monitored with time as a control until the cooler is repaired. Ensure TCS foods in the cooler are kept for no longer than 4 hours. Items kept in the cooler for 4 hours must be discarded; they cannot be cooled and reused. A follow-up is scheduled for July 11th to ensure the cooler has been repaired.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The upright freezer in the kitchen was observed to have an accumulation of ice. The ice accumulation is at risk of contacting food in the freezer, resulting in cross-contamination. The PIC is aware of the issue and is storing food such that it does not contact the ice in the freezer. Ensure the freezer is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to operate the faucet handles after the handwashing process. Be sure to educate employees on proper handwashing procedures. After washing hands, make sure to use a barrier to operate faucet handles to prevent contaminating freshly washed hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [C]

The pitcher was removed from the handwashing sink and the employee was educated. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not used for any other purpose than the intended purpose of handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: REPEAT- The handwashing sink at the bar was observed to not have any paper towels at it. CORRECTED- An operator placed paper towels at the handwashing sink. The PICs were educated on the importance of ensuring that every handwashing sink has paper towels and soap at it to allow for proper handwashing. Paper towels are a necessity to have a barrier to turn off the handwashing sink after washing your hands.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A Quaternary ammonium sanitizer bucket was observed to only be at 100ppm. The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer dispenser was tested and was also observed to only be at 100ppm. CORRECTED- The PIC adjusted the water pressure and the sanitizer was tested again. The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tested to be at 200ppm. Ensure that sanitizer is always at the label-recommended concentration to allow for proper sanitizing of food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

comment: The cheese sauce on the hot holding line was observed to only be at 126F. This was discussed with the employee who stated that the hot line had been on for a while. The knob was discovered to be at a lower temperature and the employee turned it up. CORRECTED- The cheese sauce was discarded by the PIC and was replaced. The new cheese sauce was probed to be at 135F after it had been on the line for a sufficient amount of time. Ensure that hot food is held at 135F or higher.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed the back storage room off the kitchen (water heater storage closet) to have bagged flour and boxed powdered foods to be stored in the unfinished space. The ceiling is not tiled and the floor is not coved. There is slight water seepage occurring around the floor. The room was previously observed with mouse droppings around the floor. Today, no droppings are observed, however, the space should have no food stored within or should have food protected if it is going to be used for food storage. Use large plastic storage tubs if you are going to continue to use the space for food storage. Provide storage bins that can be contained and are plastic or change the storage location of powdered foods.

Several food contact surfaces in the kitchen are thickly coated with accumulated dust and grease. The baffles of the hood system are coated in a layer of dust (baffles over the chicken broaster units). The broaster units themselves are observed to be coated with accumulated grease as is the surrounding floor and wall. See that the baffles are being routinely cleaned at a frequency that allows them to be maintained free of accumulated dust and grease.  After the baffles are clean, see that the baffles are cleaned a single one at a time and then moved down so that they maintain them clean. Clean the area surrounding the broaster (wall, floor, and attached plumbing).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

Detail cleaning on most of the equipment is lacking (roll cart adjacent to the broaster is thickly coated with accumulated grease). title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

Several ants are observed on the wall, windowsill and counters along the drive thru wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agency for remediation. Cleaning and sealing wall junctions was discussed. Ensure that all pests are removed from the facility prior to the follow up. The follow up is being set for one month to allow pest control time to manage the situation.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

1) A Starbucks drink is observed in the walk in freezer next to foods intended for consumers. 2) A personal drink is observed on a shelf next to and over clean dishes in the back area. Both items were shown to the PIC and the items discarded to correct. Ensure that personal foods are stored separately from foods and food contact items intended for consumer foods.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple employee drinks uncovered sitting on the table next to the hard shell fried ice cream waffles in the kitchen. Staff were educated to only have closed beverages and to handle them in a way that prevents contamination. Ensure that personal drinks in that kitchen are covered with a lid and have straw inserted and stored in a way that prevents contamination of food items.
citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
