The container was relocated to the appropriate location and the staff was educated by the PIC to remember to have the hand-sink free and accessible. Ensure that handwashing sink is easily accessible at all times. [Pf]
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was not sanitizer bucket (s) observed during inspection today at the facility. PIC was made aware about the absence of a sani bucket and staff was instructed to make one. PIC was informed that there needs to be a sani bucket made and available during food preparation at all times in the facility. Ensure that there is sanitizer in sani bucket (s) during food preparation at all times.
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda gun nozzle at the bars was observed to be soiled. Discussed with PIC and the soda gun nozzle was removed and replaced to be cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the soda gun nozzle is monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspectors observed a jug of milk in the prep cooler opposite of the hot holding in the kitchen not date marked after opening. Staff said that the milk has been open two days prior (06/25/2025) to today’s inspection but forgot to date mark the container. Education was carried out and the jug of milk was dated marked properly. Ensure that food items are dated marked properly if not used within 24 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspectors observed shrimp stored in a bucket of water sitting on the floor on the right side of the hand sink thawing. An education was carried out about appropriate thawing method for food items and the bucket of shrimp was placed under running water to be thawed properly.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The soda machine next to the tea station was observed to have an accumulation of soil behind the nozzles and on the levers. PIC was made aware and the machine was cleaned before the end of the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces and equipments are constantly monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency. [C]
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Three locations have temperature violations observed at this time. 1) The drink prep cooler in the front section of the facility is holding milk at 51F. The PIC was shown and discarded the milk to correct. The cooler should either be turned down or (because it is the only TCS item in this cooler) the milk should be moved to another cooler moving forward. 2) The walk in cooler closest to the dish area is observed with items at 45-50 internal temperatures. 410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

Numerous TCS foods in the walk in cooler are observed with internal temperatures between 46F-51F. Items discarded include: turkey, chili, prime rib, filets, ground beef (5 5lb logs), cooked rice, sliced cheddar cheese, sliced Swiss cheese, shredded cheddar cheese, milk, half n’ half, sour cream, cottage cheese, heavy cream, and alfredo sauce. title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.

4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop at the drive thru window is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. This allows for bare hand contact with the ice when the scoop is picked up. The issue was discussed with the PIC and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that the utensils are handled in ways where there is not a concern of contaminating the foods they are intended to handle.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

White mold is observed on diced tomatoes in a container in the bottom of one of the prep coolers. The PIC was shown and discarded the food to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are maintained in a safe stated through service.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield of the ice machine was observed with pink, green and black mold growth along the bottom edge. The location was discussed with the PIC and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the facility would not register a sanitizer concentration on the inspector’s test strips over multiple attempts. While investigating it appears that the container of concentrate has off gassed and diluted itself naturally. This was discussed with the PIC and a new jug attached to the machine in an attempt to resolve the situation. Once primed the machine began dispensing chemical at acceptable levels. Ensure that the sanitizers used in the facility are maintained at effective levels at all times.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

1) A squeeze bottle in one of the prep coolers has a marked date of 5/11-5/18. The PIC indicated that it should be 6/11-6/18 and replaced the label to correct. 2) Sliced tomatoes in the bottom section of another prep coolers have a marked date of 6/-6/12. This container was discarded during this inspection to correct. 3) A different container of diced tomatoes is without any date marking. This container was discarded due to observed mold growth (refer to line item # 13 for write up). Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are correctly marked for seven day date marking at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There is a gap that runs along the entire bottom of the walk in cooler door. The PIC was shown and discussed the situation. The owner latter asked for suggestions as this has been an ongoing issue with the delivery drivers. The walk in cooler is located outside of the back door at this facility and several issues could develop due to this in the future, but have not appeared yet. The current concern is that pests have easy entrance into the walk in cooler from outside. There are not pests currently observed at this time. Ensure that the door is repaired prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all outer openings to the facility are sealed to protect against pest entry.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival and throughout the walk through sani buckets or other sanitizing methods were not available for use in the food preparation and handling areas. The PIC was notified and  sani buckets were prepared for both the front and back preparation areas to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use at all times in the facility that foods are being handled/prepared.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch). 

Under the hand sink in the dish area the coving has come undone from the wall exposing a gap between the wall and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to re-cove the location to prevent moisture or detritus accumulation. Ensure that all wall/floor junctions are closed to allow for effective cleaning.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

The caulking between the three part sink and the wall is observed completely black along most of the strip. The PIC was shown and instructed to replace the caulking with new prior to the next routine inspection and to maintain it clean moving forward.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The display cooler in the customer area of the facility is holding foods at 46F internal temperature. The only items in this cooler that are a Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food are individually packaged cheesecakes. Per the PIC these items were removed from the freezer in the back approximately three hours ago. The items were allowed to be placed back into the freezer for rapid re-cooling and retention. The PIC dissassembled the cooler’s cover and cleaned the vent during this inspection. The cooler reduced its temperature almost immediately and the violation is considered corrected at this time. Ensure that all coolers are operating correctly at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

1) A package of onions is observed on the floor in the back corner of the walk in cooler. 2) A stack of boxes of food are observed in the back corner of the walk in freezer with the bottom box directly on the floor. The PIC was notified and instructed to store all foods off of the ground at all times, including in the walk in cooler/freezer. Ensure that all food items are stored off of the floor at all times in the facility. A similar situation was observed and noted on the previous routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

There is a gap observed between the sink and the wall in the bathroom. The PIC was notified and instructed to re-seal the location so that it is smooth and easily cleanable prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces subject to moisture and/or foods are sealed so that they are smooth and easily cleanable.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

A food handler is observed to wash their hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. The PIC was notified and instructed to review hand washing with staff to ensure safe hand washing moving forward. Education conducted to correct. Ensure that all hand washing is completed in a safe manner at all times in the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the ice baffles have an accumulation of soil residues. The ice baffles must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. The inspector will follow-up on 7/1/2025 to check that the ice baffles have been cleaned to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the cooler at the front service area (by the cash register) was not cold holding foods at 41F or below. The ambient air was about 50-60F, the internal thermometer was reading at 60F, and the opened jug of milk had an internal temperature of 55F. The PIC voluntary discarded all temperature control for safety (TCS) foods during the inspection: multiple jugs of milk, an opened container of oat milk, and orange juice. Non-TCS foods were kept inside the cooler. The PIC serviced the cooler and noticed a large buildup on the filters. The filters were cleaned but before the inspector left the internal thermometer was observed still at 60F. The cooler may require time for the temperature to come down after cleaning the filters; however, they cannot store any TCS foods inside the cooler until it is below 41F. They should schedule maintenance if the cooler temperature does not drop below 41F. The inspector will follow-up on 6/24/2025 to check on the temperature of the cooler.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following have an accumulation of dust:

(1) The shelves holding mixer equipment in the production room - cleaned during the inspection (COS).
(2) The top shelf between the prep cooler and prep counter in the hot kitchen. 
(3) The dust on the hood system in the hot kitchen. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust. Ensure that the above referenced locations are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Dish machine was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration after running three cycles. CORRECTED- Maintenance was on-site and able to reset the machine. Sanitizer was then observed at 200ppm Cl. Ensure test strips are used to monitor dish machine sanitizer. Discussed 3 compartment sink use in the absence of the dish machine.

[P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.

(A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

comment: Peeling paint was observed on the wall behind the 3 compartment sink/dish machine. Repair the wall so the surface is smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Employee foods were observed intermixed with foods for service in the vertical cooler and freezer. CORRECTED- PIC designated the bottom shelf of the vertical cooler for storage of employee foods. Ensure employee foods are stored away from foods for service.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket stored along the coffee line tested at 0ppm. The PIC remade the bucket with a fresh solution and it tested at 200ppm (q). Ensure that sanitizer buckets are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration and changed at least every 4 hours in order for the chemical to properly sanitize food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: The ice scoop’s handle was observed directly touching ice in the machine stored in the back of the house. Discussed with PIC and the ice scoop was placed inside of a bucket designated for ice scoops when not in use. Ensure that ice scoops are stored in manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed there was not soap at the bar hand washing sink. Additionally, the soap dispenser at the hand washing sink by the triple sink is broken and not dispensing any soap. The PIC stated they are having issues with the automatic soap dispensers but repairs are scheduled. The PIC purchased soap during the inspection for the required hand washing sinks. Ensure that hand washing sinks always have soap readily available for the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
comment: Observed the PIC did not have letters of parasite destruction from food suppliers. The PIC receives raw fish for sushi from True World, Great Wall Seafood, and Martinez. During the inspection the PIC contacted True World and Great Wall Seafood and they sent letters immediately. The PIC found proof that Martinez complies for parasite destruction; however, he will still contact them for an official letter. Ensure that letters for parasite destruction are always available for every required supplier.
citation_text: 3-402.12(C) Records, Creation and Retention. (C) If raw, raw-marinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH are served or sold in READY-TO-EAT form, and the FISH are raised and fed as specified in Subparagraph 3-402.11(B)(4), a written agreement or statement from the supplier or aquaculturist stipulating that the FISH were raised and fed as specified in Subparagraph 3-402.11(B)(4) shall be obtained by the PERSON IN CHARGE and retained in the records of the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale of the FISH.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed on the cookline some of the plastic containers storing various powders and seasonings and the spoons for dispensing are heavily soiled. The PIC discarded the heavily soiled containers and spoons during the inspection. The inspector educated that the containers and spoons must be changed regularly to avoid the accumulation of soil resides. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a large container of rice was stored on the cookline with a temperature of 70F. The PIC stated that an employee had taken the rice out for lunch at 12 pm and forgotten to put the rice back inside the cooler. The PIC and inspector discussed removing smaller quantities of rice that can be used during the lunch rush in the future. The PIC agreed to use time-as-control for the rice that was in the temperature danger zone and 4 pm was written down on the rice container for the discard time. Ensure that time/temperature control for safety foods are always maintained at 41F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed fish in a reduced oxygen environment that bears a label indicating that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing was thawing inside the package in the walk-in cooler. citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several white powders (flour, corn starch, sugar, and tempura batter) stored in large containers (not the original packaging) without a label. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on a prep table. The PIC was notified and they moved the wiping cloth into a sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

comment:

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was no certified food protection manager present during today’s inspection. Ensure that there is at least one staff member that is a certified food protection manager in the facility during operational hours at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed multiple boxes of food in the back storage area and front service area to be stored directly on the floor. PIC was informed that food items need to be stored a minimum of 6 inches off the ground to prevent contamination. Ensure food is stored off the floor before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code.

In the walk in freezer, stacks of food in boxes are observed with the bottom boxes on the floor. These bottom boxes are saturated in ice and the dyes from the boxes appear to have soaked into the observable ice coating them. This leads to the conclusion that the food inside of these containers has been contaminated and should not be used. The PIC was notified and discarded the bottom containers of food to correct the immediate violation. The remaining boxes were then placed on milk cartons to correct the future concerns of this situation (refer to line item #39 for write up). Ensure that all foods are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Two stacks of boxes containing food are observed with the bottom boxes stored on the floor of the walk in freezer. The PIC was shown and placed the stacks on top of crates to correct. The bottom boxes were discarded (refer to line item #15 for write up). Ensure that all foods are stored at least six inches above the floor at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

A thick accumulation of frost and ice is observed in the walk in freezer on the shelves and floor. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean often enough to prevent accumulation moving forward. This issue may be resolved when the planned door replacement takes place, however it should be managed at all times regardless.  Ensure that all food areas are maintained clean at all times.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers (CFPM) employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The only allergen certificate currently available at the facility is held by an employee without a CFPM. None of the available CFPMs have an allergen training certificate. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all CFPMs at the facility have completed allergen training prior to the next routine inspection and that the certificates are maintained at the facility moving forward. Ensure that all CFPMs have allergen training completed at all times.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspector observed staff barehandling ready to eat food items during food prep. Discussed with PIC and an education was carried out to correct the behavior. Ensure that staff are aware to don gloves after handwashing before prepping ready to eat food at all times.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed to the sani bucket on the cook line by the grill measuring low concentration at 0 ppm. Discussed with PIC and the sani bucket was remade. The new solution tested at 200 ppm. Ensure that the sani buckets are monitored and tested at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the hot holding unit to not be holding temperature within the appropriate temperature range. Discussed with PIC and the hot holding unit was switched with a better performing unit. PIC mention that the unit in question sometimes malfunction with temperature holding. They will work on getting an upgrade to a more function unit. Ensure that this unit is repair and calibrated to constantly hold the appropriate temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil and food debris within the gasket of the stainless steel four compartment cooler on the cook line opposite the fryers. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the gasket of the cooler would be cleaned. Ensure that non food-contract surfaces such as the gasket of the cooler rare cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface to prevent future malfunction to the equipment.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspectors observed soiled mop water being stored in a mop bucket and a wet mop head stored on the floor of the utility closet. Discussed with PIC. PIC drained mop bucket in the mop sink and the wet mop head was stored properly. Ensure mop water is disposed of properly after each use.
citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the PIC’s Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) certificate expired in February 2025. The PIC was reminded that someone with a CFPM certificate must be present during all hours of operation. Ensure that the PIC renews their CFPM certificate by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. The PIC added bleach to the sanitizer bucket and it re-tested at 150 ppm (Cl). The PIC was reminded that sanitizer concentrations must be tested regularly with test strips. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the rubber spatula in the utensil holder next to the oven is starting to deteriorate. If the spatula deteriorates further it could pose the risk of small pieces breaking off into food. The PIC was instructed to throw away the spatula and purchase a new one. Ensure that all utensils are smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The walk-in cover fans were still observed to be soiled during today’s inspection. A follow up is scheduled for 7/16/2025 to ensure that they have been cleaned. The PIC stated that the dust accumulation is on the inside of the fan cover and that they are unsure if they can take the cover off to clean them. A solution needs to be found to ensure that these can be cleaned and are being regularly cleaned.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floor under equipment in the bar area is observed to still be soiled during today’s inspection. This violation is at the compliance conference step of being a repeat violation. A follow-up is scheduled for 6/30/2025 to ensure that this has been cleaned and has been placed on a cleaning schedule.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: The inspector observed staff handling diced tomatoes with bare hands. Discussed with PIC, and the tomatoes in question were discarded. Ensure that staff are made aware to wear gloves during food preparation at all times.
citation_text: 3-301.11(E)(2) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE POPULATION may contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands if: (2) Written procedures are maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request that include: (a) For each bare hand contact procedure, a listing of the specific READY-TO-EAT FOODS that are touched by bare hands, (b) Diagrams and other information showing that handwashing facilities, installed, located, equipped, and maintained as specified under §§ 5-203.11, 5-204.11, 5-205.11, 6-301.11, 6-301.12, and 6-301.14, are in an easily accessible location and in close proximity to the work station where the bare hand contact procedure is conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The inspector observed chicken being stored over fish in the double-door stainless steel cooler in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC, and the fish was removed to correct the storage order violation. Ensure that raw food items are stored properly to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffles of the ice machine were observed with a build-up of soil. Discussed with PIC, who ensured the inspector that the ice machine baffles will be cleaned in the coming week. Ensure that food-contact surfaces, such as the baffles of the ice machine, are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-202.11(A) Restriction. (A) Only those POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS that are required for the operation and maintenance of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as for the cleaning and SANITIZING of EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS and the control of insects and rodents, shall be allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

A couple chemical canisters were observed to be improperly stored over food items. 
-1 stainless steel refrigerator cleaner canister
-1 glass cleaner canister 
Discussed with PIC, and the canisters were removed and stored away properly. Ensure that staff are aware of the storage order of toxic chemicals and food items to avoid food contamination.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulking on the countertop on the right of the dish machine to be in disrepair. Discussed with PIC, who ensured the inspector that the necessary repairs will be done. Ensure that the countertop is re-caulked to the wall, providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed no handwashing to be set up upon arrival, Discussed with PIC, hand washing was being done at church nearby. A temporary hand washing station was prepared. Ensure hand washing is available on site.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no test strips available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, test strips will be grabbed from church.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer to be set up upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was set up and tested at 100 ppm CL.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employees that were cleaning (or doing other tasks) put on gloves to prepare foods without handwashing first. The PIC was instructed to educate employees about washing hands before donning gloves to engage in food preparation. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the front hand washing sink and customer bathrooms do not have ‘employees must wash hands before returning to work’ signs. The inspector provided signage to the PIC. Ensure that all hand washing sinks always have proper signage that notify employees to wash hands.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed eggs stored on the top shelf of the double cooler over various ready-to-eat foods. The PIC was notified and they moved the eggs onto the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) The dusty ceiling vent above the double cooler. 

(2) The shelves drying clean dishes next to the triple sink. 

Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the ceiling vent and drying racks are to cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following require repairs:

(1) The facility installed a new soda machine and the old soda line holes have not been covered. The holes are located on the wall near the ground by the front hand washing sink and the oven in the prep room. The holes need to be covered to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. 

(2) The wall panel holding the paper towel dispenser at the front hand washing sink is lifting up on the left side. The panel needs to be sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

Ensure these locations are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
The following food items were observed with damaged packaging on the dry goods shelf :
 - There were at least 3 boxes of cereal with broken packaging
- There was an unidentifiable aluminum can without proper labeling of the food item

The items were shown to the PIC and pulled from the shelves. Ensure that the packaging of all food items are in good
condition and not exposed to any contaminants.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the
FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer buckets were testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. An employee added a capful of bleach and the bucket tested at 150 ppm (Cl) afterwards. The PIC was reminded that sanitizer solutions must be checked on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration (Cl = 50-150ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed there were some large containers of cooked rice and noodles prepared yesterday in the front walk-in cooler that were not date marked. The majority of the containers were date marked; however a couple were missing date marks. The containers were properly date marked during the inspection. Ensure that all ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a large bag of cooked sausage stored in a steam table unit that was turned off. The PIC stated that the sausage was taken out of the cooler about 15 minutes ago. The inspector explained they need to either: (1) Turn on the steam table and keep them above 135F; (2) Leave them inside the cooler at 41F or below; or (3) Use time-as-control (if this method is used, than the time the sausage was removed from the cooler must be written down to indicate the four hour time-as-control window). The PIC decided to put the sausages inside the cooler. There is also cooked bacon stored in the turned off steam table; however, cooked bacon is temperature stable and is allowed to remain. Ensure that foods are always stored to maintain food safety.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the cookline prep table. The employee cooking was educated and they moved the wiping cloth into the sanitizer bucket. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Observed the following utensils stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination:

(1) A knife on the cookline stored with the blade in the gap in between the prep cooler and freezer. The gap is not a clean and sanitized surface so it poses the risk of contamination. The knife was moved to another location during the inspection.

(2) A knife stored with the handle in contact with cooling gyro meat shaved from the spinning spit. The knife handle is touched by bare hands and poses the risk of contamination. The knife was removed from the gyro meat during the inspection. 

(3) The sugar scoop stored with the handle in contact with the sugar. The sugar scoop handle is touched by bare hands and poses the risk of contamination. The sugar scoop was removed from the bag during the inspection. 

Ensure that utensils are always stored properly to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the shelves above the triple sink used for drying clean dishes are soiled with debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FISRT REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the caulking behind the spray nozzle table to the left of the dish machine has been removed and not replaced. The spray nozzle table must be sealed to the wall. Due to the area being subject to high amounts of moisture the caulking must be repaired/replaced frequently. Ensure that the caulking is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the pizza prep cooler to be soiled with food splash. Discussed with PIC, cooler will be cleaned. Ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is a buildup of dust on the hood system and portions of the ceiling. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris. Ensure that the hood system and ceiling do not have an accumulation of dust by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were raw shell eggs observed to be above containers of taco meat that had been cooked and cooled and other various food items. CORRECTED- These eggs were moved onto the shelf that holds other raw fish. Storage order was discussed with the PIC and another handout on storage order was provided. Ensure that food is protected from cross contamination during storage, holding, preparation, and display.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine was observed to have slight soil residue accumulation. CORRECTED- This was cleaned during the inspection by the PIC. Ensure that this is cleaned regularly. Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment:
There were multiple single-service articles that were not being displayed correctly throughout the kitchen, including, but not limited to, the following: 

1. The to-go containers above the cook line. 
2. The plastic boats with parchment paper in them above the cook line. 
3. The bowls with parchment paper in them above the fryer area. 
4. The plates by the soup station. 

All single-service articles and utensils need to be inverted or stored directly under a shelf to protect them from contamination. This was discussed with the PIC.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The gasket of the pizza preparation cooler is observed to be in need of cleaning due to an accumulation of soil residue. 
2. The dish shelves next to the dish machine are observed to have soil accumulation and are in need of cleaning. 
3. The air vent above the dish area is observed to have an accumulation of dust and is in need of cleaning. 
4. The floor under the grills along the cook line in the kitchen. There is an accumulation of debris and soil residue. 
5. The bottom shelf of the table along the cook line in the kitchen. 
6. The wall behind the grills along the cook line in the kitchen. 
7. The floor of the walk-in freezer. It was discussed with the PIC to scrape off the built-up soil residue on the floor. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to maintain them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: REPEAT- The only employee working was not a Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). Ensure that there is always a CFPM in the facility during all hours of operation and food preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: There were no available signed employee reporting agreements during the inspection. The owner and the employee both stated that they were unsure of where they were. Blank copies were provided and a follow up is scheduled for 6/18/2025 to ensure that they have been signed. Ensure that these are kept in a safe place where they are accessible for all future inspections.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: There were no thermometers observed to be in any of the refrigerators in the facility. This was discussed with the owner. Ensure that there is always a temperature measuring device in all cold and hot holding units.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
The facility has packages of pre-scooped double scoops available for sale in a cooler. These containers need to be labeled or have an ingredient list posted next to them due to the scoops being packaged for consumers to grab and go. The label information or the list should include the common name of the food, a list of ingredients and sub ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, the name and place of the business, and any major allergens. Ensure that there is either an ingredient list with the required information posted next to the items or there are labels with the required information on each individual package. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: The trash can in the women’s restroom is observed to not have a lid on it. Ensure that in every toilet room that is used by females there is a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The bare wood under the legs of the triple sink needs to be sealed.
2. REPEAT- The mop sink needs to be caulked to the wall. 
3. REPEAT- The wall in back room needs to either be caulked or coved to the floor. 
4. REPEAT- The triple sink needs to be sealed to the wall to eliminate the gap. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Staff was observed donning new gloves without handwashing. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Ensure staff are washing hands before donning a new pair of gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Handwashing was unavailable at the time of inspector's arrival. The installed hand sink was not functional. A free-flowing portable hand sink was delivered during the inspection.
citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs would be done in the summer. Ensure that the floors are repaired/broken tiles replaced so that the floor is smooth and easily cleanable.

Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the following time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods above the safe maximum cold holding temperature in the 2-door cooler:
1. Cottage cheese
2. Sour cream
3. Coleslaw
4. Tavern cheese
5. Cut lettuce
6. Cut tomato
7. Caesar dressing
8. Ranch dressing
9. Shredded cheese

These items all measured roughly 50-60 degrees with the infrared thermometer. The digital thermometer for the cooler read 43F. The PIC was informed and chose to discard all TCS foods in the cooler. The PIC called and scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Since the items were discarded, this violation is considered corrected-on-site.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Due to the failure of the cooler, these items were voluntarily discarded. Education was conducted with the PIC regarding proper date marking procedure and a handout was provided.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The 2-door standing cooler was observed to measure 50-60F with the infrared probe. The interior of the cooler was not cold to the touch. The PIC was informed and determined that the cooler was not operational. Maintenance on the cooler was scheduled during the inspection. A follow-up will be conducted on 6/20/2025 to ensure the cooler has been repaired. In the meantime, the 2-door standing cooler cannot be used to store TCS foods. The walk-in will be used until the service is completed.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The scoop used for ice at the ice machine is observed buried in the ice in the machine. The PIC was shown and the scoop moved to correct. Ensure that ice scoops are stored so that the handles are not in contact with the ice/hand contact area moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

On arrival the hand sink in the women’s bathroom was without soap. The dispenser was refilled during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels. 

The hand sink in the bar area is without paper towels at the beginning of this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and napkins provided for the short term. They did mention that a cloth rag was being used and changed out hourly as the current procedure. A dispenser is being acquired for this location moving forward. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips were not available for the quat sanitizer used in the sani buckets for the facility. The PIC stated that more were already ordered and should be arriving soon. A follow-up is being set for 10 days.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING X3) 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

Walk-in cooler/freezer: 1) replace molded shelving; 2) replace rusting shelving.
Dish Area: 1) repair/replace damaged floor tiles.

Repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed the facility had dented cans on the shelf. The inspector removed the dented cans from the shelf during the inspection. The PIC was instructed to remind employees about the importance of removing dented cans. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw chicken stored over raw beef in the meat walk-in cooler. The PIC was shown the incorrect storage order during the inspection and they moved the raw chicken onto a bottom shelf. The PIC mentioned labeling the bottom shelf for chicken storage only. Additionally a storage order handout was provided for further education. Ensure that raw meats are always stored according to internal cooking temperatures to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The top of the inside of the ice machine was observed to have slight soil residue accumulation. CORRECTED- The top of the inside of the ice machine was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
