comment:

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: The bulk dispensers of cereal and the clear display case containing breads, muffins, bagels, etc. are both observed to not have proper allergen labeling. The facility has placed the Notice to Consumer Allergen poster in both areas, but this is not sufficient. There needs to be either a placard, labels, a poster, or some other method that clearly indicates the allergens that are in each item for consumers to be able to easily view. Bulk food that is available for consumer self-dispensing needs to have allergen labeling posted for consumers.
citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Inspector observed the front-line sliding-door cooler to be out of temperature. Items discarded include Silk almond milk 06/06/2025
(Probed 55.5F), Planet Oat oat milk (Probed at 52.5), and two open containers of whipped cream that could not be probed.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure that this cooler is serviced so that it maintains proper temperatures for food safety. Inspector will
return Friday, 06/06/2025 to re-asses cooler temperature.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR
SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the floor in front of the ice machine to be missing grout between the floor tiles, as noted during the Next Routine Insp
pre-opening inspection. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that more grout is added between tiles to create a smooth, durable, and
easily cleanable surface.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and
ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where
FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a buildup of accumulated ice and frost behind the refrigeration unit and the ceiling of the walk-in freezer. Discussed with PIC and PIC informed inspector that they are aware of the build up and would get it cleaned. Ensure that the accumulated ice is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and this was corrected. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable about using a barrier to shut off the faucet after washing their hands to avoid recontaminating their hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: There was a dented can of oyster sauce that was observed to be in the bottom of the preparation cooler. The can was dented along the bottom seam and oyster sauce was being stored in it to be used. CORRECTED- The can and oyster sauce in it were both voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Education was conducted regarding dented cans. Dented cans should never be used and should be set apart from all other food. These dented cans can be returned to the distributor. Dents in cans means that the integrity of the can has been compromised and the food is exposed to contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: REPEAT- There were two containers of sauces in the walk-in cooler that were observed to be uncovered. CORRECTED- A lid was placed on both containers and the PIC was educated. Food should never be uncovered, especially in a walk-in cooler where there is constant air-flow. Ensure that food is stored in packages, in covered containers, or in wrappings to protect the food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was a phone that was observed to be on the preparation table in the kitchen. CORRECTED- This phone was removed and the table was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure that phones are never placed on a food contact surface. Phones harbor a significant amount of bacteria and can easily contaminate food. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a container of cooked meat observed to not have a date on it in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Date-marking was discussed with the PIC. The PIC stated that the meat was cooked yesterday and a date was placed on it by the PIC. Ensure that all Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are date-marked with day one being the date of opening or preparation and the item being discarded by the end of the seventh day.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: The bleach that is being used to make sanitizer in the facility is observed to not have an EPA Registration Number. This was discussed with the PIC and education was conducted on the correct type to get. It is important that the bleach has the EPA Registration Number on it to ensure that it is safe to be used on food contact surfaces and is properly sanitizing food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- The PIC obtained bleach with an EPA Registration Number during the inspection.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The standing clear single-door cooler in the small room with the soda syrups was observed to not have a thermometer in it. CORRECTED- The PIC placed a thermometer in the unit and was educated on the importance of having them in all hot and cold holding units. Ensure that in all mechanically refrigerated or hot food storage units there is a temperature measuring device located to measure the air temperature of the unit.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The chest freezer in the room with the soda syrups is observed to need defrosted and cleaned due to an accumulation of soil residue. 
2. The shelves in the dry storage room are observed to have an accumulation of soil residue and are in need of cleaning. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed there to be soil build-up on the blade of the can opener. Discussed with PIC. PIC had the can opener cleaned immediately in the dish machine. Ensure the can opener is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clean. COS
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build-up of soils on the ice machine baffle. Discussed with PIC. PIC immediately cleaned and sanitized baffle. Ensure baffle is cleaned enough to keep soil from accumulating.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a crack running the length of the underside of the larger chest freezer lid. Discussed with PIC. Ensure this area is repaired to be smooth, durable, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present during the inspection. Ensure that there is at least one CFPM present during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Several TCS foods stored in the prep cooler next to the drive thru window lacked proper date marking. These items include but aren't limited to sauces, sliced cheeses, and deli meats. Discussed with PIC and proper date marking was added. Ensure that TCS foods stored in house longer than 24 hours after opening are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: A sanitizer bucket was being stored directly next to the meatballs on the steam table. Discussed with PIC and the sani bucket was moved to a different location. Ensure that chemicals are never stored in a manner that can contaminate food items.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The bottom shelf of the prep cooler near the drive thru window was heavily accumulated with food debris and spilled liquids. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Two soda machines that appear to be in disrepair are being stored in the lobby next to the service station. The pieces of equipment are leaking syrups onto the floor, which can also attract unwanted pest and insects. Remove soda machines if they are no longer serving a purpose to the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed the waitress making a drink at the bar placed an ice cube into a drink with their bare hands. The employee was instructed to dump the drink and re-make it when the action was observed. The PIC was informed and they showed the waitress the location of the tongs that are used to transfer ice to the drinks. Ensure that ready-to-eat foods are never handled with bare hands.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the fry station prep cooler was holding foods above 41F. The following internal temperatures were recorded: lettuce 53F, spring mix 50F, lettuce 49F, mozzarella cheese 47F, cooked chicken 50F, diced tomatoes 48F, sausage 48F, raw chicken 47F, and raw fish 47F. The internal hanging thermometer was reading at about 50F. When the temperatures were originally observed out of range the inspector gave the cooler 30 minutes to cool down after lunch. However, after 30 minutes the cooler was still above 41F. The PIC stated that all foods had been inside the cooler for over four hours. All temperature control for safety (TCS) foods were voluntarily discarded during the inspection (foods referenced above). There was two containers of tofu that were within the safety range and moved immediately to a functioning cooler. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain inside the cooler (pickles, onions, lemons, bread etc.). During the inspection the PIC called to schedule service. The PIC was instructed that TCS foods cannot be stored inside the cooler until it is functioning. The facility will be either using time-as-control or ice baths until it is serviced. The inspector will follow-up on 6/10/2205 (the facility is closed on Mondays) to check on the temperature of the cooler.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the underside of the shelves above the prep cooler in the fry station have an accumulation of grease, food debris, and other residues. The PIC was shown the location that needs to be cleaned. Ensure that the underside of the shelves are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Observed the following storage order violations in the facility:
1. Raw shell eggs stored above cooked pulled pork (prep cooler bottom)
2. Raw hamburger stored above ketchup and mustard (prep cooler bottom)
3. Raw hamburger stored above margarine (walk-in cooler)
4. Raw shell egg stored above produce (walk-in cooler)

The PIC was informed and the raw items were moved. A handout was also provided for the purposes of educating staff. Ensure staff are never storing raw meat (including egg) above ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a buildup of grease on the floor behind the cookline where the fryers and flat top grills are being stored. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that floors, walls, and ceilings are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease buildup.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: A food employee was observed wearing gloves to deliver food to customers in the dining room, return to the kitchen, and return to food preparation without washing hands or changing gloves. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will review when to wash hands with employees. Ensure employees wash hands upon entering the kitchen prior to engaging in food preparation without washing.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: A food employee was observed rinsing a milkshake cup in the front counter handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will review handsink use with employees. Ensure handsinks are ONLY used for handwashing, no other purpose.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Sticky fly strips were observed installed in several locations around the 3 compartment sink and clean dish storage. CORRECTED- PIC removed the fly strips and relocated them to use in the dry storage area. Fly strips may be put up overnight when no food is open in the kitchen.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Both the 3 compartment sink and the cookline handsink have leaks from the faucets. Repair sinks to eliminate the leaks.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) Spray foam near the mop sink and walk-in freezer/back door needs to be cut flush and painted to leave the surface smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Broken floor tiles in front of the fryer need to be replaced.
3) Holes in the wall behind the 3 compartment sink need to be filled.
Repair physical facilities to eliminate gaps and create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
1st REPEAT: Current food handler certificates were not available for either of the two non-CFM employees present during this inspection (one is on file, but expired). Long John Silver’s is on the list of Illinois-approved food handler certificates, but PIC was unaware of this internal training and was unsure if staff have completed the course. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire, whether internally through Long John Silver’s or through another approved provider. 
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Several locations throughout the facility are in need of minor repairs. Locations include: 1) the end of the bar on the salad prep cooler has a ball of tape being used as a safety measure; 2) the wall siding to the right of the front prep cooler is pulling away and exposing a gap that is not easily cleanable; 3) multiple small holes are observed in the wall above the mop sink; 4) several small holes on the side of the walk in cooler; 5) the paint on the wall next to the CFPM certificates is observed with a pair of bald spots where a rough surface is exposed. These locations were discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all surfaces around food and moisture are maintained in a smooth and easily cleanable state at all times.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths being stored on table in kitchen. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and cloths were placed in bucket. Ensure any wiping cloths in use are being stored in a sanitized solution.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed ice accumulation to be present in walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, ice will be removed and walk in freezer will be serviced. Ensure facility is monitoring walk in freezer at a frequency that prevents ice accumulation.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be prepared upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizing solution is prepared at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to have mold accumulation present in the following locations:
1) To the right of dish machine. 
2) At mop sink. 

Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring caulking at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A SECOND REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The PIC was educated that the cutting board could become contaminated by dirty water splashes stored in this position. The PIC removed the cutting board from behind the faucet and moved it to another location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always stored away from sources of contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The bare wood planks on the wall by the cash register behind the slushy machines. The bare wood must be sealed (ex.painted) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

(2) The gap between the order window in the customer area and the kitchen is filled with foam. The gap must be filled to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface.

Ensure that the above referenced are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following must be cleaned: 

(1) THIIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION - Observed there were drips on the hood system above the grills and fryers. These drips pose a risk of contaminating food cooking below. The portions of the hood system over the grills and fryers must be cleaned often enough to avoid the accumulation of drips. The PIC cleaned the drips during the inspection (COS).

(2) The shelves for drying clean dishes over the triple sink have an accumulation of grease from the adjacent grills and fryers. The dirty shelves pose the risk of contaminating clean dishes. The shelves must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease. 

Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch by at next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Inspector observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at the start of today’s inspection. A CFPM did arrive during the inspection today. Ensure there are enough CFPM’s on staff to ensure at least one CFPM is present at all times of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed interior of coolers and bins containing condiment cups to be soiled with food debris. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil. Coolers were cleaned during the inspection, and bins were moved to the dish area.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a fly strip above the prep table in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and staff. Fly strip was removed immediately. Ensure fly strips are kept away from food-preparation areas.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulk behind the dish-line sprayer to be soiled. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that caulk is either cleaned or replaced.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. Laminate flooring is being used to line thin shelf board. Cease use of the laminate flooring as a shelf liner.

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in Fuzzi Wigs was observed to be in the basin of the handwashing sink. CORRECTED- This was discussed with the employees and the sanitizer bucket was removed. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained accessible at all times for employee use and are not used for any other purpose than handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A bucket of pickles inside the walk-in cooler was observed to be uncovered underneath the fan unit of the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The PIC was educated on the importance of making sure that all food is covered, especially in the walk-in cooler where there is constant air flow. There is also the potential for contamination from the fan unit of the walk-in cooler. The bucket was covered during the inspection. Ensure that food is protected from contamination by being stored in packages, in covered containers, or wrappings.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. comment:

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
There are clear, packaged containers of bagels, muffins, and other food items in the facility that do not have any labels on them. All items that are packaged for the consumer need to have labels on them. This label must include the common name of the food, a list of ingredients and sub ingredients in descending order of predominance by weight (if made of two or more ingredients), including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD, all major allergens, an accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents, and the name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor. This was discussed with the PIC. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: The scoop in the flour container in the dry storage area was observed to have the handle in direct contact with the flour. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that all scoops that are stored in the food container are stored with the handle above the top of the food.

During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(B) In food that is not time/temperature control for safety food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon.

comment:

1. The single service boats to the right of the hot holding soups. 
2. The to-go containers to the left of the soups. 
3. The small cups next to the dippin’ dots chest freezer. 

All single-service articles need to be inverted or covered to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

comment:

A cup is not a sufficient scoop, as it is not durable, easily cleanable, and does not have a handle. Ensure that the plastic cup is replaced with a proper scoop with a handle. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

comment: Observed an employee don a new pair of gloves without handwashing. Education was conducted regarding proper hand washing. Ensure staff are hand washing before donning a new pair of gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that not all employees have food handler certificates. The PIC was reminded that all employees must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).

citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

(A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

 Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Several TCS foods stored on the hibachi cold table were observed with an internal temperature between 48F-55F (probed). PIC mentioned that TCS foods were placed in the cold table at 11am. PIC mentioned that facility adds water to the table, which then freezes and is expected to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. The facility was instructed to discard TCS items which included cooked rice, crab meat, cooked sausage, and cooked noodles. Ice was added to the cold table to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Several TCS food items such as but not limited to salad dressings, cut tomatoes, and cut lettuces were probed between 47F-55F along the salad buffet line. PIC mentioned that TCS foods were placed in the cold table at 11am. PIC mentioned that facility adds water to the table, which then freezes and is supposed to maintain proper cold holding temperatures. The facility was instructed to discard TCS food items. Ice was added to the cold table to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at 41F or less. 

In addition, several containers of cheesecakes stored in the floor dessert case were probed at 63F. The cheesecakes were also discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: A bottle of WD-40 was stored above a prep table across from the cookline. Discussed and shown to PIC and bottle was removed. Ensure that toxic chemicals are stored in a manner that protects against food contamination.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: A giant pot of mashed potatoes was observed to be in the process of cooling after being cooked. PIC mentioned that the potatoes had been cooling for no longer than an hour. The facility was instructed to place the pot of mashed potatoes into the walk in cooler and uncover the pot in order to cool properly. The mashed potatoes were probed at 128F. Be sure to use proper cooling methods to ensure that TCS foods are getting cooled properly and reduce the amount of time that food is in the temperature danger zone.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The hibachi cold well isn’t maintaining proper cold holding temperatures for TCS foods. See violations #22. Foods were probed between 47F-55F and discarded. A follow-up is scheduled for June 11, 2025 to ensure that the unit is sufficient enough to maintain proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: At least 3 packages of fish were observed thawing in the original packaging under refrigeration. According to the packaging’s label, reduced oxygen packaged fish must be taken out of the package first before being thawed. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that ROP food is never thawed in its packaging.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Several white powders stored in containers in the dry storage area lacked proper labeling. These items consisted of flour, sugar, and other breading mixes. Ensure that white powders are properly labeled with the name of the food item so that they aren’t mistakenly used.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
There were several acidic foods being stored in their original containers in many areas of the facility including but not limited to dry storages areas and coolers. Due to the acidity of these food products (soy sauce, ketchup, oyster, hoisin, etc), the containers can become damaged if the food sits for long periods of time. Ensure that acidic foods are transferred to a more appropriate container after opening. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A significant amount of mold buildup was observed on the bag of mozzarella cheese stored in the main kitchen’s 2 door cooler. Discussed and shown to PIC. The molded cheese was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that food is always safe for consumption and never containing mold or any other contaminant.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of cleaning:
- There was loose food debris observed on the floor of the dry storage area (underneath racks storing dry goods).
- There was a significant amount of ice buildup (and food debris) on the floor of the indoor walk in freezer 
Ensure that these areas are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil with in the dish machine. PIC was made aware of the soil build up and PIC immediately got it cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the dish machine are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed a few jugs of milk that had been opened a couple days prior without being date marked. Discussed with PIC and PIC wrote the “opened dates” on the jugs and ensured inspector that they will continue to monitor the date marking on food items. PIC ensured inspector that they will inform staff to observe date marking as well. Ensure that food items are clearly date marked if not used within 24 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspector observed a wet mop head and a rag being store on the floor in the mop sink. PIC was shown the wet mop head and rag. PIC removed them and took them away to be stored properly. A warning notice will be sent to facility reminding them that this was observed during the previous routine inspection on 02/05/2025. Ensure that mop is store in a position that allows it to air dry limiting the growth of bacteria cultures.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Accumulated ice was observed behind the refrigeration unit in the walk-in freezer. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that there accumulated ice will be cleaned out. Ensure that the accumulated ice is cleaned to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff’s failure to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and this behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are aware to use a barrier to shut off the faucet after handwashing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the hand sink to be obstructed with a garbage bin. Discussed with PIC and the bin was removed allowing access to the hand sink. Ensure that the hand sink is accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspector observed the sanitizer bucket at the food island to be at zero ppm of Quat. This sanitizer is pulled from Taco john’s dispenser. Ensure that the dispenser is tested daily. The bucket was dumped and replenished with sanitizer from the same dispenser. This violation is here by marked corrected on site.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Accumulated ice and frost were observed behind and under the refrigeration unit, on the floor, and door of the walk-in freezer. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the accumulated ice and frost will be cleaned. Ensure that the accumulated ice and frost is cleaned to avoid the contamination of food items.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzles and the dispenser parts of the soda machine were observed to still have an accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- The operators cleaned the dispensers and the nozzles during the inspection today. It was discussed with the operators to make sure that the dispensers and the nozzles are being cleaned and scrubbed daily. It was recommended to have a second set of nozzles to allow for more time for cleaning or to get clear nozzles which allow any soil accumulation to be seen better. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: THIS IS A FISRT REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the facility did not have signed employee health reporting agreements. During the inspection all employees signed a copy and the PIC filed the signed agreements in the office. Ensure that the signed copies remain at the facility and new employees sign the agreement.
citation_text: 2-201.11(E) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person In Charge, and Conditional Employees. Responsibility of food employees and conditional employees to report. (E) A FOOD EMPLOYEE or CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEE shall report to the PERSON IN CHARGE the information as specified under (A) of this section.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not wash hands before putting on gloves to begin preparing food. When the action was observed the employee was instructed to wash hands. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: Observed the facility was selling packaged desserts that were prepared in a private home kitchen. When asked about the source of the desserts the PIC pointed out each dessert that was prepared in the home kitchen. The inspector educated that foods prepared in private home kitchens cannot be sold at the facility. The required desserts were removed from the cooler during the inspection. Ensure that foods always come from an approved source.
citation_text: 3-201.11(B) Compliance with Food Law. (B) FOOD prepared in a private home may not be used or offered for human consumption in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following foods stored in the incorrect storage order: (1) Raw meat stored over cooked meat in the clear double door cooler; and (2) Raw eggs stored over various sauces in the prep cooler bottom. During the inspection the raw meat was moved below the cooked meat and the raw eggs were moved below the sauces. The PIC was educated that raw foods must always be stored below ready-to-eat foods. The inspector will follow-up on 6/2/2025 to check on storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed that the facility uses time-as-control (TAC) for the lettuce by the taco station at the cash register but they were not marking times. The PIC was educated that they must either record the time the food entered TAC (i.e., when the lettuce was removed from the cooler) or when it must be discarded. During the inspection the PIC filled out a TAC policy where they indicated they will use labels to track the time. The inspector will follow-up 6/2/2025 to check that the lettuce is being marked with the 4-hour TAC window.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed that ground beef was thawing submerged with water in the triple sink when the inspector arrived. The PIC was educated that food must be completely submerged and under running water to be properly thawed. The PIC turned on the faucet after being educated about the proper procedure. Ensure that foods are always thawed according to an approved method.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the prep table. The PIC was educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizing solutions between uses. The PIC moved the wiping cloth into the sanitizer bucket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer when not in use.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed the box of utensils by the taco station at the cash register is stored with the handles and food contact portions intermixed. The PIC and inspector discussed possible solutions. The inspector suggests moving the utensils into another container where they can be stored with the handles facing outwards. Ensure that utensils are always stored in a position that prevents contamination of food contact potions.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. The PIC stated that the bucket had been recently dumped. They were reminded that sanitizer buckets must be available whenever food preparation is occurring. When asked to make the sanitizer bucket the PIC first added dish soap to the bucket. The inspector educated that sanitizer buckets should only contain sanitizer and water (ex. bleach (about a capful) and water testing between 50-150ppm). The soap was rinsed out and the bucket was made correctly. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned: 

(1) The silver drying rack holding clean dishes across from the triple sink. 
(2) The floor underneath the dry storage racks.  
(3) The white drink shelves in the walk-in cooler. 

Ensure that the above referenced non-food contact surfaces are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is a missing electrical outlet behind the ice cream freezer in the kitchen. The electrical outlet must be replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil in the soda nozzles of the Coca Cola soda machine. PIC was made aware of the soiled nozzles and the nozzles were removed, replaced, and cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the nozzles of the soda machine are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The refrigeration in the walk-in cooler was observed with a loose screw causing the condenser water output unit to leak water in the walk-in. The unit appeared functional and the temperatures are stable. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. PIC has a plastic container under the refrigeration unit to catch the water for the time being until the appropriate repairs are done.  Ensure that the appropriate repairs are done accordingly to prevent any malfunctions.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

The PIC was unable to provide a procedure during this inspection related to cleaning up vomit/diarrheal events. A copy of the one given out by Sangamon County was given to correct. Another will be sent via email tomorrow. Ensure that all written procedures required by code are maintained at the facility at all times.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

The ice scoop in the ice bin behind the bar is observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Education was conducted with the PIC and the scoop removed to correct.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

At the beginning of the inspection the bar hand sink is observers to be without paper towels. When asked paper towels were provided to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are correctly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

On arrival the ice machine is observed to have black mold growth around the inside of the equipment. The PIC was notified and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. The PIC cleaned the item during this inspection to correct.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Inspector observed staff donning gloves without washing their hands. Discussed with PIC and the behavior as corrected.
Ensure that staff area knowledgeable about washing their hands before donning gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed staff failure to use a barrie to shut the faucet after washing their hands. PIC was made aware of the observed behavior and the appropriate correction was made. Ensure that staff are knowledgeable on proper handwashing etiquette.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observe a few live flies in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensure inspector that the adequate actions will be taken. Ensure that the facility is free of insects or other pest to eliminate harborage.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The facility is observed to have a down ice machine being store in the back by the first drive-through windows. Discussed with PIC and PIC told inspector that they had previously put in for the repairs of  the Ice machine in question. However, they were told by management that they will get a new one soon. Ensure that this equipment is remove from the facility if it is not being used or if there are no plans in motion to get it repair.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed bin of flour in back utility room to be left open between uses. The utility room contains pest which can easily contaminate the flour without proper coverings. Ensure the flour bin is closed between uses.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw chicken livers with no protective coverings to be stored above ready-to-eat pouches of cheese sauce. PIC was informed of proper storage order practices and the items were rearranged. Ensure staff are educated on proper storage order. Raw meat should never be stored above ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat Violation

The dish machine was observed to measure 0ppm chlorine during today’s inspection. The PIC was informed and trouble-shot the machine. The PIC discovered that the tubing was not placed deep enough into the sanitizer bucket to reach the liquid level. The tubing was adjusted and the machine was primed. The dish machine then measured 50ppm chlorine. PIC was informed to monitor the dish machine more frequently with test strips and ensure there are additional buckets of sanitizer available in the facility when the level in the bucket is low.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed plastic bin containing clean utensils to be soiled with food debris. Bins holding clean utensils need to be cleaned frequently to prevent cross-contamination. A follow-up will be conducted on June 6th, 2025 to ensure compliance.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed the exterior door in the kitchen to have a damaged door seal. Incomplete door seals can promote the encroachment of pests in a facility. Ensure the seal is replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

comment: Observed a deceased mouse and mouse droppings in the back and front utility room in the kitchen. title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed foods in the clear door sliding cooler had internal temperatures above 41F. The following temperatures were recorded with a probe thermometer: humus 48F, humus cups 50F, feta-cheese spinach pie 49F, cut leafy greens 54F, gyro sauce (sour cream base) 54F, feta cheese 51F, kasseri cheese 51F, and mozzarella cheese 51F. There were hamburger patties that had an internal temperature of 44F that were immediately moved into another cooler. All foods had been inside the cooler since at least 11am this morning (some of the foods had been inside the cooler overnight) meaning the 4 hour time-as-control window had passed when the foods were discarded after 3pm. All temperature control for safety (TCS) foods (other than the hamburger patties) were discarded during the inspection. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain in the cooler (such as non-TCS vegetables and sauces). The PIC will be scheduling service for the cooler. Until the cooler is serviced and functioning properly the cooler will not be used to store TCS foods. The inspector will follow-up on 5/30/2025 to ensure that the sliding cooler is functioning properly.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

Ensure that handles for ready-to-eat foods are always stored above food to avoid contamination.
citation_text:
3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the 
container.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics.
