title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee filled a sanitizer bucket and then proceeded to put on gloves to handle food without washing hands in-between. The employee was instructed to hand wash when the action was observed. The employee and PIC were educated that hands must be washed after filling up sanitizer buckets (and after other sources of contamination) and before donning gloves. Ensure than foods employees always wash hands properly.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(B) In food that is not time/temperature control for safety food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Milk containers observed in the front reach in cooler are observed open and partially empty without date marking. Per conversations with the PIC one of them was opened this morning and another was opened a couple days ago. Education was conducted. Once milk is opened/unsealed it required seven day date marking and to be used or discarded by the end of day seven. The PIC was notified and placed dates on the unsealed containers to correct.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
This location is attempting to sample the juices without any form of hand washing available at the stand. The sampling was discontinued for the event. A follow-up should be conducted at next weeks market to ensure proper sampling procedures are taking place. Multiple suggestions were given including setting up a temporary hand washing station and pre-packaging the samples in the store prior to transporting to the market.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
There were two containers of baked goods that were observed to not have any labeling on them other than the name. Labeling was discussed with the operator. The operator stated that the baked goods come in frozen and they package them into the clear, plastic containers in the store. The baked goods need to have labels with all of the required components on them. Information regarding this was provided. A follow up is scheduled for 5/31/2025 to ensure that all food items have proper labeling on them. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.

comment:

citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility could not provide proof of food handler certifications for employees. Ensure that employees who are not manager certified obtain a food handler certification if handling food and clean dishes.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

comment: Observed the sanitizer in use on the truck to measure less than 50ppm chlorine. PIC was informed that sanitizer solution was too low, and sanitizer was remade, measuring 100ppm chlorine. Ensure staff monitor the concentration of the sanitizer frequently and replace as needed.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the triple-door prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. All items in prep cooler were probed and voluntarily thrown away. Items probed include: Raw Pork (49.5 F), Cooked Pasta (47.5 F), Raw Steak (47F), Raw Lobster Tail (47F), Raw Salmon (46F), and a house made sauce (47F). PIC stated that all items were stored in the cooler last night, which exceeds the 6 hour time allotment that foods can be between 46-55F. Food is likely out of temperature due to a faulty cooler. Discussed with PIC. PIC has scheduled maintenance on the cooler. Inspector will return 05/20/2025 to re-asses violation.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Inspector observed the 3-door prep cooler on the line to not be holding temperature. Discussed with PIC and PIC has maintenance scheduled for the cooler. For temperatures within the cooler, reference violation 22. Inspector will return 05/22/2025 to reassess violation.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Inspector observed salmon being thawed in reduced oxygen packaging in two coolers in the kitchen. The packaging bears a sticker that says to thaw outside of the package. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that fish is thawed according to packaging guidelines. Inspector will return 05/23/2025 to reassess violation.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Inspector observed the active CFPM in the facility to not have an allergen training. The facility has multiple certified CFPMs with allergen trainings. Ensure that the active CFPM in the establishment has an allergen training.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The potato slicer is observed with soiled with food debris. Per the PIC this equipment has not been used today. he equipment was disassembled and cleaned during this inspection to correct.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There was a case of soda and a box of single service articles observed to be stored on the floor. Discussed this with the PIC and recommended putting a pallet or milk crate under these items. Ensure that all single service articles and food is stored at least six inches off of the ground.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned     EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: The facility is observed to be in a poor state of cleaning and is observed to have a number of priority violations. A follow up is scheduled on 5/27/2025 to ensure that a plan is being implemented to improve cleaning and that the priority violations that are observed to be occurring in the facility have been corrected. Staff should be educated on the importance of cleaning and food safety.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The paper towel dispenser at the handwashing sink near the entrance to the kitchen was observed to be out of paper towels at the start of the inspection. CORRECTED- The PIC replaced the paper towel roll and was educated on the important of ensuring that all handwashing sinks are appropriately stocked with paper towels and soap to allow for proper handwashing. Ensure that all handwashing sinks are provided with individual, disposable towels to allow for the use of a barrier during handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: The racks and the sheet pans in the walk-in cooler holding various food items were observed to have mold accumulation. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2025 to ensure that these racks and pans have been cleaned. Food should be protected from cross contamination by cleaning equipment and utensils.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: REPEAT- There were containers of lettuce observed in a standing cooler that did not have a lid on them. The fan in this cooler was observed to be soiled. Ensure that all food is protected from cross contamination by being in a covered container, a wrapper, or stored in its original, closed package. CORRECTED- Lids were placed on these containers during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The Lactic Acid sanitizer buckets were observed to have 0 ppm concentration of Lactic Acid in them. The facility’s sanitizer dispenser was observed to have little to no sanitizer left in the bucket and the PIC stated that someone is on the way from Jacksonville with more sanitizer. CORRECTED- The facility was able to borrow more Lactic Acid sanitizer from IHOP until more can be brought in from the other store and buckets were remade. All sanitizer concentrations were observed to be at the correct concentration (272 ppm). Ensure that there is ALWAYS sanitizer available in the store to ensure that food contact surfaces are able to be properly sanitized.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: An employee was observed to have their phone on a prep table. CORRECTED- The PIC had the employee remove the phone and sanitize the table. The employee and PIC were both educated. Phones carry a significant amount of bacteria and should NEVER be in contact with a food contact surface. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food contact surfaces are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The top of the Bunn coffee dispenser. 
2. Two of the microwaves (the two in the middle to the left) along the cook line were observed to have food accumulation. 

A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2025 to ensure that these food contact surfaces have been cleaned. Ensure that these food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The front prep cooler was observed to be holding cold items at between 45F and 49F. A container of butter was probed to be at 46F and a container of ranch was probed to be at 49F. The PIC stated that the air had just been fixed and that the cooler had been having issues due to the warmer temperatures. An ice bath was created under the cold holding items. The cooler was checked at the end and was observed to be holding items at 41F and under. This will be spot checked at the 5/27/2025 follow up. Discussed making sure all ice baths are completely submerging the bottoms of pans to allow for proper cold holding.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The facility has a prep cooler that is not currently working and they are having to use an ice bath to keep items in cold holding. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2025 to ensure that this cooler has been repaired. The facility should have a sufficient number of equipment for both hot and cold holding.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: There are plates and bowls on top of the cook line that are observed to have their food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all of these single service items are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following equipment is observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The gaskets on the prep coolers along the cook line. They are observed to either be in need of being replaced or cleaned. 
2. The door on the ice cream freezer is observed to be broken and easily comes off. Ensure that this is repaired. 

Ensure that equipment is maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility was observed to not have an irreversible registering thermometer for the heat sanitizing dish machine. A follow up is scheduled for 5/27/2025 to ensure that the facility has obtained an irreversible registering thermometer. Discussed with the PIC the options for an irreversible registering thermometer.
citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
There are a number of nonfood contact surfaces that are observed to be in need of cleaning in the facility. More attention is needed to cleaning. The following nonfood contact surfaces are in need of cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The fan of the standing cooler that contains the salad mixes. 
2. REPEAT- The bottom of the standing cooler that contains the salad mixes. 
3. REPEAT- The fan covers in the walk-in cooler. 
4. REPEAT- The bottom of the bar cooler. 
5. The outside of the door and handles of the standing freezer and standing cooler. 
6. The bar cooler walk-in fan covers. 
7. The top of the dish machine. 

A follow up is scheduled for 6/16/2025 to ensure that these nonfood contact surfaces have been cleaned and that cleaning has been improved in the facility.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The facility is observed to be in a poor state of cleanliness. The following areas are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The baffles of the hood system. 
2. The walls behind the fryer. There are observed to be drips coming from the baffles. 
3. The floor under and behind the fryers is observed to have grease accumulation. 
4. The floor under the ice machine. 
5. The inside of a prep cooler along the cook line is observed to have an accumulation of water and food debris. 
6. REPEAT- The floor under equipment in the bar area. 
7. The floor drain under the handwashing sink in the bar area. 
8. Both drains in the dish area are observed to be in need of cleaning. 
9. REPEAT- The walk-in freezer floor. 
10. The wall behind the dish machine. 
11. REPEAT- The floor under the cook line. 
12. REPEAT- The floors underneath the back prep area/sink.
13. REPEAT- The floors under the drink station. 

The facility as a whole is in need of attention to cleaning. It is highly recommended to move equipment out and clean floors and walls. A follow up is scheduled on 6/16/2025 to ensure that there is more attention to cleaning and these items have been cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. REPEAT- There is broken coving to the left of the dish area. 
2. REPEAT- There is a piece of broken coving in the walk-in freezer next to the door. 
3. REPEAT- There is broken coving to the right of the walk-in cooler entrance. 
4. The dish area needs re-caulked. 
5. There are two cracked tiles in the mop sink that need repaired. 
6. The coving needs re-sealed to the left of the bar walk-in cooler. 
7. There are broken tiles around a drain in the dish area that is allowing water to pool. 
8. Behind the steamer needs re-caulked. The condensation is creating soil accumulation in the caulking. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The mops in the mop sink were observed to be placed in the bottom of the mop sink, rather than being placed on the hooks to allow for air drying. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that mops are hung to allow for air drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: REPEAT- The facility is observed to be using a steamer that does not have proper ventilation for it and it is creating condensation on the wall and ceiling above it. This is creating mold accumulation in the caulking. This complaint is being referred to the city due to the lack of ventilation. Ensure that a ventilation hood system is provided to prevent condensation from occurring.
citation_text: 4-202.18 Ventilation Hood Systems, Filters. Filters or other grease extracting EQUIPMENT shall be designed to be readily removable for cleaning and replacement if not designed to be cleaned in place.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The green shelving in the pizza dough prep double doors prep cooler was observed with accumulated soil. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspector that the shelving will be cleaned adequately. Ensure that these shelves are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current accumulation of soil build up, cleaned and sanitized to remove at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed in disrepair.
1. There are holes along the wall above the front counter of the dish machine.
2. The coving tile near the delivery driver door is broken creating room for soil accumulation.
Ensure these location area cleaned and repaired to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There was no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present during today’s inspection. At the end of the inspection, the manager with a CFPM arrived. PIC was made aware that there needs to be at least one certified food protection manager present during the facility’s operational hours at all times. PIC ensured inspector that come next inspection, there will be a certified food protection manager present.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The the sanitizer in the sanitizer buckets were not measurable. The readings collected were 0ppm. Discussed with PIC and the buckets were remade to correct this violation. Ensure that these sanitizer in the sani buckets are monitored at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of mold in the ice dispenser of the polar pop soda machine. PIC was made aware of the mold build up and the ice dispenser was cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to avoid food contamination.
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed visible light from the back exit door. Discussed with pic and pic said that they are currently working on getting the gap seal by management. Ensure the necessary repairs are done to seal the gaps to avoid the entry of rodents and other pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(E) Outer Openings, Protected. (E) Paragraph (D) of this section does not apply if flying insects and other pests are absent due to the location of the establishment, the weather, or other limiting condition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed dirty water being stored in mop bucket with the mop head stored in it. PIC was made aware of the appropriate procedure for storing mop heads and the mop wastewater disposal. Ensure that wastewater after mopping are disposed properly and mop heads are stored appropriately to discourage pathogen distribution and growth.
citation_text: 6-501.15 Cleaning Maintenance Tools, Preventing Contamination. FOOD preparation sinks, HANDWASHING SINKS, and WAREWASHING EQUIPMENT may not be used for the cleaning of maintenance tools, the preparation or holding of maintenance materials, or the disposal of mop water and similar liquid wastes.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer bucket in kitchen to have a quaternary ammonia concentration of roughly 50ppm. PIC was informed and replaced the bucket, measuring 200ppm. It seemed like there were three working rags in the same bucket. Intensive use of the bucket can cause the sanitizer concentration to dilute quickly. PIC was advised to use more buckets if necessary to keep up with sanitizing demand.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed cheerios and waffle mix to be stored directly on the floor in the 2nd floor dry storage closet. PIC was informed that food items need to be stored a minimum of 6 inches off the floor to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure food is stored at least 6 inches off the floor by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed personal food items stored in the cooler with food for the facility. PIC was informed that personal food items pose a cross-contamination hazard for food for the consumer. Personal food items can be stored in the cooler, but they need to be stored either on the bottom shelf of the cooler or in a solid container to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure personal items are properly stored by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

TCS foods in the prep cooler are observed with internal temperatures ranging from 46F-50F. The ambient air temperature is also observed at 50F. The PIC was consulted and the situation investigated. TCS items were discarded to correct the immediate violation and include sliced ham, chicken, shrimp, goat cheese, mozzarella cheese and lettuce. Sliced tomatoes and pre-made/packaged hard boiled eggs were moved to the adjacent standing cooler as they had just been prepared. Refer to line item #33 for the follow up on cooler functionality.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The prep cooler in the kitchen is not correctly holding food temperatures during this inspection. The cooler is being temporarily taken out of service as a short term solution and maintenance shall be conducted to repair/ adjust. Follow up in ten days to ensure that the maintinance is conducted and effective.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival and throughout the walk through a sanitizer was not observed ready for use in the kitchen. The PIC was asked about this and made a new bucket for the kitchen. Food preparation was taking place at all times during this inspection. Ensure that there are sanitizers ready for use at all times that foods are being handled and/or prepared.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

An employee was observed to wash hands and then use their bare hands to turn off the faucet. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to ensure proper hand washing is taking place at all times moving forward. A clean barrier should be used after hand washing to prevent recontamination of the hands prior to food service.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw chicken and beef are observed over opened containers of mayo, ketchup and mustard in the bottom section of the prep cooler. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-arranged during this inspection to correct. Education conducted. Ensure that safe storage order and separation of raw/Ready-To-Eat items in the coolers is taking place to prevent possible cross contamination.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

A package of hot dogs is observed in the standing cooler next to the prep-cooler in the kitchen open and without a date marking. The PIC stated that the package was opened yesterday. Education was conducted and a date marking added to the package during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all Ready-To-Eat (RTE) foods in the facility are date marked after opening of their packages or preparation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING x2) 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

Ceiling tiles above the bathroom, sink, mop sink and prep areas are of the acoustic type and are not acceptable for food preparation or moist locations. The PIC was consulted and will be replacing as able moving forward.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed employees working do not have food handler training. All employees who do not have a CFPM certificate must obtain training in basic food handling principles. Ensure that all required employees obtain a food handlers certificate by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspector observed employee don gloves without proper handwashing. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that hands are properly washed when switching tasks before putting on new gloves at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility was observed not in compliance with food handler training. Discussed with PIC, who ensured inspector that employee completed the food handler training however, the certification was at employee residence. PIC said that they will get the employee to bring a copy of their certificate in order to have it on file. Ensure that all staff without a certified food manager certification obtain their food handler training certification to be in compliance with the LAW. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion.
comment: Observed restriction and exclusion paperwork to not be available upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, inspector provided facility with required paperwork. Ensure restriction and exclusion paperwork is kept within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-201.11(D) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person in Charge, and Conditional Employees. Responsibility of the Person In Charge to Exclude or Restrict. (D) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that a FOOD EMPLOYEE who exhibits or reports a symptom, or who reports a diagnosed illness or a history of exposure as specified under Subparagraphs (A)(1) - (5) of this section is: (1) EXCLUDED as specified under 2-201.12 (A) - (C), and Subparagraphs (D)(1), (E)(1), (F)(1), or (H)(1) and in compliance with the provisions specified under 2-201.13(A) - (H); or (2) RESTRICTED as specified under Subparagraphs 2-201.12 (D)(2), (E)(2), (F)(2), (G), (H)(2), or 2-201.12(I) or (J) and in compliance with the provisions specified under 2-201.13(D) - (J).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employee turn off hand sink without using a proper barrier. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing technique, and employee rewashed hands. Ensure staff is properly hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed multiple employees put on glove without first washing hands. Wash hands before putting on new gloves. Discussed proper hand washing technique and glove use with employee.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed knife sanitizer at prep line to measure inadequate quaternary ammonia concentration. Ensure sanitizer tablets are fully dissolved so that concentration is adequate and knives are properly sanitized. The sanitizer was replaced during the inspection.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

Ensure that all deli meats contain proper date marking if being held in house longer than 24 hours. Discard if time exceeds 7 days of opening.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.

Be sure to get rid of unnecessary equipment to maintain premises and the accumulation of food debris.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Hot dogs on the hot dog rollers are observed with internal temperatures of 78F-84F. Ambient air temperature is observed as 74F by the same thermometer. The PIC was unaware of any warming that had taken place yet today. Investigation showed that an employee had partially warmed the items recently and then turned off the equipment. Education was conducted in relation to warming and hot holding. The hot dogs were discarded at noon as that was the safest estimate for a four hour pathogen growth curve. Ensure that all hot foods are maintained above 135F at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the mop sink caulking is molding and starting to deteriorate. The caulking must be replaced/repaired to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the mop sink caulking is smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the blue container holding clean utensils by the sandwich prep cooler has an accumulation of food debris on the bottom. The container must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid contaminating food contact surfaces. The PIC removed the container to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that the container is maintained clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that there is an accumulation of dust on the drink shelves in the walk-in cooler. The shelves must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust and other debris. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there are small holes in the wall in the following locations: (1) Around the hand sink across from the sandwich prep cooler; (2) To the right of the triple sink; and (3) Around the hand sink by the kitchen entrance. Ensure that the holes are filled to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.

(A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: (Repeat x2) Inspector observed there to be an unused ice machine and prep cooler in the facility. The facility has been asked to remove machinery during the past two inspections. Ensure this machinery is removed from the facility to prevent pest harborage conditions.
citation_text: 6-501.114 Maintaining Premises, Unnecessary Items and Litter. The PREMISES shall be free of: (A) Items that are unnecessary to the operation or maintenance of the establishment such as EQUIPMENT that is nonfunctional or no longer used; and (B) Litter.

title: Proper use of restriction and exclusion.
comment: Observed no restriction or exclusion paperwork to be present within facility. Discussed with PIC, paperwork was provided by inspector. Ensure restriction and exclusion paperwork is available within facility during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-201.11(D) Responsibility of Permit Holder, Person in Charge, and Conditional Employees. Responsibility of the Person In Charge to Exclude or Restrict. (D) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that a FOOD EMPLOYEE who exhibits or reports a symptom, or who reports a diagnosed illness or a history of exposure as specified under Subparagraphs (A)(1) - (5) of this section is: (1) EXCLUDED as specified under 2-201.12 (A) - (C), and Subparagraphs (D)(1), (E)(1), (F)(1), or (H)(1) and in compliance with the provisions specified under 2-201.13(A) - (H); or (2) RESTRICTED as specified under Subparagraphs 2-201.12 (D)(2), (E)(2), (F)(2), (G), (H)(2), or 2-201.12(I) or (J) and in compliance with the provisions specified under 2-201.13(D) - (J).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed santizer solution to test at 0 ppm CL upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, santizer solution was remade and tested at 100ppm CL. Ensure sanitizer solution is prepared and at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed multiple TCS food items to be kept at room temperature. Discussed with PIC, items were prepared this morning. Inspector provided education in regard to cold holding TCS foods, ice baths were created for sauces, and larger items were placed in cooler. Ensure all TCS foods being cold held are kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed staff use the sanitizer wiping cloth to clean a surface then did not wash their hands before donning gloves for food prep. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are aware that they need to wash their hands whenever they change tasks.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

comment:
The following cold holdings were observed in disrepair.

comment:
The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soil and food debris:
1. prep coolers adjacent to the grill
2. under the grill
3. under the prep coolers opposite the grill
4. under the countertop adjoining the register
5. under the dish machine and adjoining countertops

citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: At the start of the inspection, the wasn't a Certified Food Protection Manager available. Food preparation was occurring during the inspection. Shortly afterwards, a CFPM arrived to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always a CFPM available whenever food preparation is occurring.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Several sanitizer bottles throughout the facility were testing at 0ppm (q). The PIC mentioned that the sani bottles were prepared using the dispenser in the bakery’s dish room. The chemical directly dispensing from the dispenser was also testing at 0ppm (q). The facility was instructed to use sanitizer from the chemical dispenser in the other dish room (deli). PIC refilled each sani bottle and the chemical tested at 200ppm (q) to correct the violation.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed handling a cell phone and then donning gloves without washing hands. Discussed proper handwashing techniques when switching tasks in between food handling. When handling cell phones, be sure to wash hands before putting on gloves to avoid contaminating food.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed a container of sushi rice to be left on the counter overnight at room temperature for at least 12 hours. The facility acidifies white rice by adding vinegar to control bacteria growth. PIC mentioned that the rice can be held on the counter for 48 hours. According to the HACCP plan for the sushi rice, rice must be discarded if held longer than 10 hours. PIC also mentions that he mixes leftover rice with freshly made rice for the next morning. Never mix leftover rice with freshly cooked rice. Discussed proper holding for sushi rice. Sushi rice can only be kept up to 10 hours at a time and should be discarded if time exceeds. The leftover sushi rice was discarded by the PIC.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: The in house spicy mayonnaise stored in the prep cooler was observed without date marking at the start of the inspection. PIC provided date marking during the inspection with today’s date (4/30/2025). The mayo appeared to be prepared days prior. Discussed with PIC proper date marking. Spicy mayonnaise can only be held in house for no longer than 7 days. Day 1 counts as the day that the mayonnaise is made. There are 6 additional days that the sauce can be held in house before it shall be discarded. At the end of day 7, the sauce must be discarded. The correct date marking was added to the mayonnaise to correct the violation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: A personal drink cup was stored on a shelf directly above clean dishes along the dish table of the dish machine. Discussed and shown to PIC. The drink cup was discarded. Be sure to educate employees on proper drink storage. Ensure that personal drinks are never stored above clean dishes to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 2-401.11(A) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, an EMPLOYEE shall eat, drink, or use any form of TOBACCO PRODUCTS only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; or other items needing protection can not result.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There were several ceiling tiles that were out of place in many areas of the kitchen. These areas include, but aren’t limited to, the dry storage closet (over single service items & food), in the dish room (over clean dishes), and in the back storage room (over clean utensils). Discussed and shown to PIC. The facility mentioned that the ceiling tiles were popped out of place to allow heat to travel to the pipes to prevent them from freezing during harsh temperatures. The ceiling tiles were put back in place during the inspection to correct the violation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: There isn’t hot water available at any of the hand-sinks throughout the establishment. The owner stated the water heater that’s responsible for supplying hot water to the sinks is down. The operator stated that they are waiting on parts to repair the hot water heater. Ensure that there is always hot water available to be sure that hands are getting washed properly. A follow up is scheduled for 5/8/2025 to ensure that the hot water heater has been repaired.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

Educated PIC that there needs to be a certified food protection manager during operation hours at all times. Ensure that a certified food protection manager is present at the facility during operational hours.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The back entrance of the facility has visible light gaps present when the door is closed.  These gaps allow for the entrance of insects and other pests. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the necessary repairs will be done.  Ensure that repairs are made to protect the outer opening of the establishment from pests entry.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw pork stored above tomato sauce, and raw eggs stored over sauces in the upright kitchen cooler. PIC was informed of proper storage order in the coolers and the food items were rearranged. Ensure staff are storing raw foods under ready-to-eat foods to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

comment:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employee was observed donning gloves without washing their hands while preparing food. Discussed with PIC and employee was educated about proper handwashing procedures. Ensure that hands are washed in between tasks before changing gloves at all times during food prep.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: THIS IS A 1st REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed various fish thawing at room temperature. Some of the fish was still frozen (at 41F or under); however some of the fish was observed above 41F. The fish above 41F was discarded during the inspection (four pieces of fish with internal temperatures between 50F and 56F). The PIC was reminded to thaw fish according to an approved method: (1) In a cooler at 41F or lower; (2) Under continuous running water; (3) As part of the cooking process; and (4) In the microwave. Ensure that fish is always thawed according to an approved method.
citation_text: 3-501.12 Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Slacking. Frozen TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is slacked to moderate the temperature shall be held: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less; or (B) At any temperature if the FOOD remains frozen.

comment: Observed roaches at the facility. Currently the pest control company (Adams) only services the facility twice a month. The PIC should contact Adams and schedule more frequent visits. They should prioritize cleaning, especially hards to reach areas. They should also make sure that foods are covered and at least 6-inches off the floor. The inspector will follow-up on 5/1/2025 to check that the facility is taking steps to eliminate the pests.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.
