title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The accumulation of Ice behind the fan and on the floor in the walk in freezers in the back storage area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the ice will be cleaned up. Ensure that the the ice is removed to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The accumulation of soils and food items were observed under shelves. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the accumulation of soils and food items will be cleaned during their inventory inspection. Ensure that shelves in the facility is monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to prevent the accumulation of soil and food items under shelves for a prolonged period of time .
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated on the importance of the proper hand washing procedure to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine is testing at 0 ppm (Cl). The PIC will be scheduling service for the dish machine. Until the dish machine is serviced they will be washing and rinsing in the dish machine but sanitizing in the triple sink. The inspector will follow-up on 4/24/2025 to ensure that the dish machine is testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed tongs stored hanging on the oven handle that were touching the trash can. The PIC removed the tongs to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. The PIC and inspector discussed either storing the trash can or the tongs in a different location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth stored on the prep counter. The employee was notified and they moved the wiping cloth into a sanitizer bucket. The PIC will be educating employees about proper wiping cloth storage. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in sanitizer between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is a significant buildup of ice in the walk-in freezer on the ceilings, as well a slight accumulation on the air curtains and floors. The walk-in freezer must be de-frosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the walk-in freezer frost is removed by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is a buildup of dust and other debris on the white shelves above the triple sink. Non food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food reside, and other debris. Ensure that the shelves above the triple sink are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed mushrooms in the prep cooler to be stored in their original can after opening. PIC was informed that food must be transferred to a new container after opening. The can’s integrity is not maintained after opening, and thus poses a cross-contamination hazard for the contents of the can. The mushrooms were transferred to a new container during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw eggs were observed to be stored above mashed potatoes, and raw beef was observed to be stored directly atop cooked chili. PIC was informed of proper storage order practices. Storing raw ingredients above ready-to-eat ingredients can result in cross-contamination.  A follow-up will be conducted on Friday, April 25th to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution prepared in the kitchen, although there was cooking taking place in the kitchen. Although there were no customers present and no dishes being prepared, ensure there is a sanitizer solution available at all times during food preparation, cooking, or service. A follow-up will be conducted on April 25th to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed chili in the walk-in cooler to bear a date exceeding 7 days (marked 4/6). The chili was actively in use in a warmer for service. Sliced tomatoes stored in the prep cooler were also exceeding the 7 days mark on their label (marked 4/15). PIC was informed of improper date marking, and the items were discarded. Date marking practices will be spot checked during the follow-up scheduled for April 25th.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed cut tomatoes and cut lettuce in the prep cooler bottom to be missing appropriate date marks. Cut tomato and cut lettuce are considered time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. TCS foods must be marked with a date mark if stored longer than 24 hours after preparation and discarded after 7 days. A follow-up will be conducted on May 2nd to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed bags of raw chicken thawing in the triple sink. The faucet was on over the thawing chicken, but the drip was inadequate to agitate and float off loose particles. PIC was informed that thawing methods were inadequate, and the water pressure was increased from the faucet. Ensure proper thawing methods are utilized to prevent the accumulation of bacteria in the chicken, resulting in food-borne illness. Thawing methods will be spot checked during the follow-up conducted on April 25th.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed onions stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Also observed cut tomatoes and sauce stored in the prep cooler to have no protective covering. Ensure food items are protected from splash, dust, or other contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed upright freezer in the dry storage area to have an accumulation of food debris and ice at the bottom of the freezer. Ensure freezers are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed window and fan behind hood system to be soiled with grease and dust deposits. The walls above the prep cooler were also observed to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure the walls, windows, and floors are cleaned frequently to avoid an accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed personal food items stored along with food items for the consumer. PIC was informed that personal food items pose a cross-contamination hazard when stored with food for the facility. Ensure a designated area is used (ex. Plastic bin or bottom shelf) to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee wash hands and not use a barrier to turn off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper hand washing technique. Ensure staff is properly washing hands to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a wall cooler to be cold holding foods between 45F-59F. Discussed with PIC, TCS foods were probed, pulled, and discarded. TCS foods placed this morning were pulled and relocated in walk in cooler/freezer to drop temperatures. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Observed a wall cooler to be holding incorrect temperatures. At the time of inspection, the cooler had just finishing a defrost cycle and items were above 41F. After a few minutes temperatures began to drop, however the whole unit was not holding the same temperature. The corners of the cooler and areas packed too tightly continued to hold temperatures ranging from 47F-53F. Discussed with PIC, this cooler has had issues in the past maintaining proper cold holding temperatures. A follow-up has been issued for 5/1/2025.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(Repeat x2) Observed the following areas in need of physical facility repairs:
1. Caulk the holes in the wall in the following places: above the triple sink, and next to the breading station. 
2. Caulking at the tripe sink is in a state of disrepair and black mold is present. 

Discussed with PIC, the following issues will be corrected. Ensure staff is monitoring physical facility.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
comment: Observed several employee drinks stored on the cookline without lids and straws. Employees can keep drinks in food preparation areas if they have a lid and straw to prevent contaminating employee hands and exposed food. The facility has to-go cups with lids and straws that the inspector suggests employees using. Ensure that all employees have drinks with a lid and straw by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee remove gloves and start putting on new gloves without hand washing in between. When the action was observed the inspector instructed the employee to wash hands before putting on the gloves. The PIC will be educating staff about proper glove use. Ensure that hands are always washed before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector demonstrated the proper hand washing procedure to the employee when the action was observed. The PIC will be educating employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed raw chicken stored over cut onions in the right walk-in cooler. The facility stores vegetables on one side of the walk-in cooler and raw meat on the other; however, an employee accidentally put the cut onions on the meat side. The PIC showed the employee the issue during the inspection and it was corrected. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below ready-to-eat foods. Due to the amount of repeat violations the inspector will follow-up on 4/24/2025.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a knife stored on a magnetic strip by the cookline hand washing sink that was soiled with debris. The PIC was shown the knife and it was removed for cleaning during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized after use.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed the following foods stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination: (1) Uncovered container of chips in the cookline kitchen on top of the warmer (by the entrance door); and (2) Uncovered deserts on the top shelf of the double cooler. The inspector educated that foods must be protected from contamination during storage. Ensure that the chips and deserts are covered by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the cove base to the right of the ice machine on the corner is falling off the wall. Additionally, the cove base across from the ice machine is missing a piece on the corner. The cove base must be repaired/replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the cove base is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order: (1) Raw shrimp stored over various ready-to-eat foods in the double cooler; and (2) Raw chicken stored over eggs in the walk-in cooler. The storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that all ready-to-eat foods must be stored above raw foods, and raw meats must be stored according to internal cooking temperatures. The inspector provided a handout that was posed outside the walk-in cooler by the PIC. The inspector will follow-up again for storage order on 4/28/2025 (the date of the second follow-up from the 4/17/2025 inspection).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed food in the clear sliding cooler stored on take out menus. The inspector educated that foods must be stored on surfaces that are easily cleanable to ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. The inspector will follow-up on 4/28/2025 (the date of the second follow-up from the 4/17/2025 inspection) to make sure take out menus are not being used to store food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. 

The kit intended for clean-up of vomit/diarrheal events is missing the chemical needed for disinfection of the affected area. The PIC was consulted and quickly ran to the store in order to acquire bleach for this procedure. They also stated that a new kit will be purchased/ordered for future use. They returned with the bleach during this inspection and was walked through its use in relation to these procedure. Ensure that the procedures needed for these events have all needed supplies available at all times moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.16(A) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE.

Acoustic type ceiling tiles are observed in the bathrooms. Ceiling coverings should be smooth and easily cleanable. The locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to replace prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: There isn’t hot water available at any of the hand-sinks throughout the establishment. The owner stated the water heater that’s responsible for supplying hot water to the sinks is down. The facility is planning to replace the water heater and is currently waiting for the replacement to arrive. Ensure that there is always hot water available to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the hand sink and to the left of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring/replacing caulking regularly.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled. The PIC was shown and had an employee clean them (wash/rinse/sanitize) during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are maintained clean at all times.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

TCS food in the reach in cooler next to the fryers are observed with internal temperatures of 67F. The PIC was shown and discarded the foods in the cooler to correct the immediate violation. Investigation showed that the breaker had been tripped. The breaker was reset and the cooler observed at acceptable temperature by the end of the inspection. A spot check will be conducted next week to ensure that this is an isolated event only.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

1) A mop is observed stored with the head pooled up in the bottom of the mop sink. 2) A mop is observed stored in heavily soiled water in a mop bucket. The PIC was shown and instructed to store the mops so that the bristles are allowed to hang and drip dry. Ensure mops are stored correctly moving forward.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) on site during today’s inspection. There are CFPM’s on staff at the facility, but none were present at the time of the inspection. Ensure there is a CFPM present at all times of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Thawed ROP fish was observed still sealed in its packaging that bore a label indicating the need to remove from packaging prior to thawing. CORRECTED- PIC cut the packages open. Ensure ROP fish packages are cut prior to thawing to introduce oxygen and prevent botulism.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The small freezer on the cookline was observed with frost accumulation on interior surfaces. Defrost the freezer regularly to prevent frost accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: 3rd REPEAT: The restroom door is not self-closing. Add a self-closer to the restroom door.
citation_text: 6-202.14 Toilet Rooms, Enclosed. Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. [C]

comment:

-Surfaces surrounding the sink should be smooth, nonabsorbent, easily cleanable. See that the wall to floor is covered/baseboard.

citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 3rd REPEAT: Trim tiles along the wall under the 3 compartment sink and dish machine are not sealed to the wall, creating a gap between the tile and the wall. Seal the wall to floor and eliminate the gap.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Observed the facility had several priority and priority foundation violations during today’s inspection. They need to improve on hand washing, food storage, sanitizing, and cleaning to increase food safety at the establishment. The PIC must prioritize education to staff. The inspector will follow-up on 4/28/2025 to check that the facility is improving safe food handling practices.
citation_text: 2-102.11(A) Demonstration. Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, during inspections and upon request the PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY knowledge of foodborne disease prevention, application of the HAZARD Analysis and CRITICAL CONTROL POINT principles, and the requirements of this Code. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall demonstrate this knowledge by: (A) Complying with this Code by having no violations of PRIORITY ITEMS during the current inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed PIC did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector demonstrated the proper hand washing procedure to the PIC. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the facet after hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed the PIC wash hands in the triple sink during the inspection. The PIC was educated and they re-washed hands in the hand washing sink. Ensure that employees always wash hands in the designated hand washing sink.
citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the hand washing sink was blocked with dishes when the inspector arrived. The PIC was educated and the dishes were removed from the hand sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks remain accessible to employees at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed sauce stored within the prep cooler in a can that was severely dented. The inspector educated that dented cans cannot be used for service. The dented can was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following stored in the incorrect storage order: (1) Raw chicken stored above raw beef in the double cooler; and (2) Raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler. The inspector educated that raw meats must be stored according to internal cooking temperatures (raw chicken has a higher cooking temperature than raw beef). The raw chicken was moved below the raw beef during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always stored in the proper storage order. The inspector will follow-up on 4/21/2025 to check on storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed there is a significant buildup of grease on the hood system that is causing drips. The drips pose the risk of contamination to food cooking below. The inspector will follow-up on 4/21/2025 to ensure that the hood system have been cleaned.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm at the start of the inspection. The PIC was informed and after adding bleach the saniztier bucket tested at 150 ppm (Cl). The inspector educated about the importance of testing sanitizing solutions on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration. The inspector will follow-up on 4/21/2025 to check that the facility has a sanitzier bucket available and testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed a bag of onions and a cardboard box of sweet potatoes stored directly on the floor. The inspector educated the PIC and the box was moved off the ground during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always stored at least 6-inches above the ground to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed a container of meat cooling on the triple sink drying rack. The meat was exposed to contamination from water splashes stored in this position. The PIC was educated and they moved the meat to a new location. Ensure that foods are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.

The PIC discarded the scoop during the inspection. Ensure that all ready-to-eat foods always have a handle to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the front reach-in freezer has a significant buildup of frost. The freezer must be defrosted to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the front reach-in freezer is de-frosted by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The tape is not an appropriate repair since it is not easily cleanable. The PIC stated they are trying to find a replacement lid. Ensure repairs or replacements by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed that the light bulb in the dry storage area is burnt out. The PIC was keeping the back door open to allow visible light but was instructed to immediately stop this practice. They must purchase a new light bulb for the dry storage room. Ensure there is sufficient light by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that the employees working either do not have food handler certificates or they have expired. All employees that handle food at the establishment (and do not have a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate) must have basic food handler training. Ensure that all required employees have a food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that no one at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. The inspector spoke with a translator on the phone who will be reaching back out to the inspector to get more information about the certificate for the PIC. There is also a handout about the allergen certificate in the red folder under the cash register. Ensure that all Certified Food Protection Managers have the allergen awareness certificate by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed packaged food items such as but not limited pasta salads and trail mixes stored throughout the facility without proper allergen and ingredient labeling. Refer to complaint #25-0118 for further details. The food items were pulled from the shelves. Ensure that packaged food items contain proper allergen and ingredient labeling.
citation_text: 3-602.11(B)(5) Food Labels. Major Food Allergen. (B) Label information shall include: (5) The name of the FOOD source for each MAJOR FOOD ALLERGEN contained in the FOOD unless the FOOD source is already part of the common or usual name of the respective ingredient.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Clean dishes were being stored underneath an exposed area where a ceiling tile was missing (in dish room). Discussed and shown to PIC. The missing space was filled with a ceiling tile. Ensure that clean dishes are stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: A pot of Chili that was being held on the frontline warmer was probed between 123F -126F. The PIC mentioned that the chili was recently placed on the warmer. The Chili was reheated in the steamer to at least 165F to correct the violation. Be sure that hot held foods are maineded at 135F or above to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Stainless steel lids and food debris were observed at the bottom of the drawer coolers. Discussed and shown to PIC. The surface was cleaned during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent buildup.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: The faucet of the triple sink was observed leaking water into the basin of the sink. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that faucets are maintained in good repair and are in leak free condition.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The paper towel dispenser next to the fryers is without paper towels during this inspection. The PIC was shown and had the roll replaced during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x3) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: The house made spicy mayonnaise stored in the walk in cooler is incorrectly date marked. The date marking exceeds the temperature/time combination requirement. PIC mentioned that the spicy mayonnaise was made yesterday, April 16, 2025 and discard date for the sticker was April 30, 2025. The date sticker was corrected to April 23, 2025. Discussed proper date marking with PIC. Any sauce made in house can be held up to 7 days after the date that it is prepared. Day 1 counts as day of preparation and Day 7 is the very last day that the sauce can be kept in house. Discard at the end of the day if sauce exceeds the 7 day timeframe.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

citation_text:
