citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the employees currently at the facility do not have signed reporting agreements or other similar paperwork available. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they looked for the form given out by this department. Blank copies of the form were found and copies made. The currently available employees signed copies during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all food handlers in the facility have been notified in a verifiable manner their responsibility to report foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

On arrival the hand sink in the kitchen had a table in front of it making it difficult for convenient use. The PIC moved the table to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained readily accessible at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sani bucket available in the kitchen area. The PIC was asked for one and immediately made a bucket using a CL solution. Ensure that sanitizers are available at all times that foods are being handled/prepared.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A soda is observed in a cup on the shelf over a prep cooler in the kitchen. Education was conducted with the PIC and the cup removed to correct. Ensure that employee drinks are stored so that contamination of consumer foods are not a concern.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Slight soil accumulation was observed in the main kitchen ice machine. Ensure the interiors of ice machines are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Single service containers on the main kitchen cookline were observed stored with food-contact surfaces up, exposed to potential contamination from above. Store single-service containers inverted to prevent potential contamination of the food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed no sanitizer in use at facility at time of arrival. PIC was asked to make a sanitizer bucket during the inspection, which tested 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are prepared at all times of food preparation and service to promote proper cleaning practices.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation
Observed shelving in kitchen to be soiled with food debris. Clean and sanitize shelves in kitchen.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the interior of microwave to be soiled with food debris. Ensure microwave is cleaned frequently to avoid the accumulation of soil and debris.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed floors in kitchen underneath fryers to be heavily soiled with grease residue. Clean floors in kitchen.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed triple sink at bar to be separating from wall. The counter needs to be sealed to wall (ex. Caulking) to ensure proper cleaning. Seal triple sink to wall by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed accumulation of grease on hood system filters in kitchen. Have hood system professionally cleaned.
citation_text: 4-204.11 Ventilation Hood Systems, Drip Prevention. Exhaust ventilation hood systems in FOOD preparation and WAREWASHING areas including components such as hoods, fans, guards, and ducting shall be designed to prevent grease or condensation from draining or dripping onto FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: 2-103.11(L) The operators are knowledgeable of the food code but are struggling to apply these safe food handling practices. New staff is not being trained on proper hand washing and sanitizing. And the practices of general cleaning, maintenance, date marking, and storage have lapsed. See that education to staff is completed prior to them starting to cook and handle food. See that staff does not forget to practice the knowledge known for safe food handling. Dr. Brian Chen was present to support education to staff. Will revisit safe food handling during the ten day follow-up. 


Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (L) EMPLOYEES are properly SANITIZING cleaned multiuse EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS before they are reused, through routine monitoring of solution temperature and exposure time for hot water SANITIZING, and chemical concentration, pH, temperature, and exposure time for chemical SANITIZING.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed several employees were not utilizing the proper hand washing procedure. Employees were failing to use soap, scrub hands for at least 10-15 seconds, and use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employees were educated during the inspection. The PIC must prioritize the education of hand washing to all employees for safe food handling. Ensure that employees always use the proper hand washing procedure.  Dr. Brian Chen was present to discuss hand washing with staff. Google translate was used to discuss proper technique with the present Spanish speaker.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed multiple employees wash hand in the triple sink. The employees were educated that hand washing can only occur in the hand washing sink. The PIC must continue to educate employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that employees only wash hands in designated hand washing sinks.
citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed there was not soap at the hand washing sink when the inspectors arrived. The PIC provided soap to the hand sink during the inspection. Ensure that there is always soap available at every hand washing sink. Dr. Brian Chen was present to discuss the importance of having soap present despite what operations are occurring. Staff was unable to wash hands prior to SCDPH arrival as no soap was present.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed raw shrimp stored over open ketchup and seasoning in the prep cooler bottom. The PIC was educated and moved the raw shrimp to the bottom shelf during the inspection. Shrimp is also observed being stored over sliced cabbage in the walk-in cooler. Storage order was discussed with operator with Dr. Brian Chen present to enforce knowledge gained. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Observed several bulk containers of dry goods to be stored uncovered in the back room. Sealed during the inspection. Also observed bulk cabbage in netted sleeve to be exposed to the potential pests in the back room. The facility has a pest problem in the back room and foods should be covered and protected. Store opened foods and foods in soft or porous containers in plastic or metal containers to prevent pest gnawing.  See that back room is properly maintained so that foods are not contaminated by pests. 


Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) TWICE REPEAT: The hood is observed with drips across nearly the entire hood system. The hood frequency was discussed with Dr. Brian Chen and operator. There should be daily cleaning of the hood to maintain free of drips. See that the top and bottom edge of the venting is cleaned so that baffles are maintained free of drips. 

Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed soiled scoop stored atop the cut broccoli (REPEAT). The facility was educated about cleaning processes. Produce is going to be cooked prior to service, however, see that utensils are maintained clean to prevent soiled contact with food.  Can opener is also observed with blade thickly coated with accumulated food debris (REPEAT). The can opener was removed for cleaning during the inspection. See that opener is cleaned between uses especially to protect against cross contamination and allergen.
citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-702.11 Observed an employee simply rinsing utensils under the triple sink faucet without proper wash, rinse, and sanitize. The operator was going to take the utensil from soiled dishes side, rinse, and then use for food service. Discussed proper wash, rinse, and sanitize with the staff member and then Dr. Brian Chen had a conversation with the operator/owner regarding the need to educate employees on proper safe food handling procedures in the kitchen. 

Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(E) Observed several items stored as clean, however, they are coated with old food debris. There is a pot of rice stored in the back room with several spoonfuls of rice remaining around the interior. There is a cutting board and another meat grinder stored in the back room with gross food debris attached to the surfaces. And, there is a meat grinder on a shelf adjacent to the hand sink stored with meat residue within the equipment. Discussed proper wash, rinse, sanitizing, and discuss proper storage of clean equipment. With pests being present, water and food sources should be eliminated. Clean the equipment. 


 Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A)  There is observed two containers of cooked foods in the walk-in cooler with dates beyond the seven days. One container of fried meats is marked as 4/4 with another container of fried foods marked as 4/7. These two products are beyond the allowed days and were discarded during the inspection. Date marking was discussed with operator using Dr. Brian Chen as a translator. 

Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: The facility continues to have mouse droppings in the back storage room. The safe storage of foods was discussed as was the proper use of pesticides. The facility has Orkin as their PCO and should see that they are present to support control within the rear exterior of the facility as well. There are observed several traps in the back room and outside but they are not appropriately positioned. The traps should be stored so the long side is pressed against the wall. A trap placed in the middle of the room or away from a wall may not capture a pest. Traps were moved (interior and exterior) during the inspection. See that droppings in the back room are cleaned.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Storage order and placement throughout the facility needs to be addressed. There is rice stored on the floor in the lobby and several opened containers in the back storage room. Food should be stored in a manner that allows for easy cleaning and protection from possible contamination. Revisit storage throughout the kitchen. 
Also, better storage solutions for the back room were discussed. There is a long and deep shelf in the back room that has become a catch-all for items and is too deep to properly view and clean. Removing this shelf and installing more narrow racks was discussed. See that storage is appropriate for food safety and ease of cleaning. 

Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wet wiping cloths stored on counter tops. The PIC moved the wiping cloths into sanitizer during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are stored in sanitizer between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed single-service items in the back dry storage room stored on the floor. Cease storing single-service items on the floor. Ensure that single-service items are stored 6-inches off the ground to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed chips at the front stored in a cardboard box. The PIC was educated about the improper storage procedure. Ensure that all foods are kept in containers that are easily cleanable and resistant to damage. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) REPEAT There remains duct tape being used as a repair material on a pitcher and several containers. See that these items in disrepair are discarded. Cease using duct tape as a repair material. 

Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Observed ketchup being stored in the can after a days use. Ketchup is an acidic food and will damage the can if not moved to a more appropriate container after opening. See the ketchup and other acidic foods are properly stored after opening. 

Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(A) Dishes were being conducted in a triple sink that was not properly set-up to reflect wash, rinse, and sanitize (see violation #16). Dishes and utensils are being moved through the ware washing process using a simple clean water rinse and no actual detergent or sanitizer. Discussed with operator and owner during the inspection. Wash, rinse, and sanitize sinks may need to be created between operational periods to allow for ease of ware washing during busy periods. 

Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the facility would benefit from a detail cleaning. There are a number of grooves, gaps, and hinges that are observed to be soiled. Specifically, the cooler gaskets and inside preparation coolers soiled with food debris. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12. Floors, walls, and ceilings throughout the facility are observed soiled with accumulated soil and food debris. The floor behind the prep counter adjacent to the hand sink is coated with food splash and crumbs, the floor around the two-door freezer is soiled with the same observed debris. The ceiling is observed dusty over the wok. Clean the floors, walls, and ceilings.  

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 There is an acoustic ceiling tile that is water damaged in-front of the woks. TWICE REPEAT: Ceiling tiles in the dry storage area by the back door are starting to show signs of ware from leaks. REPEAT: insulation is observed dropping onto the covered single-service items in the second dry storage room. The ceiling tiles has been pulled away to allow for maintenance to a gas line and never replaced. 

Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-305.11 Designation. Observed various hoodies and sweatshirts to be stored on shelving in the kitchen and back storage room. See that storage of employee clothes is kept separated from facility items. 

 (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

The paper towel dispenser at the hand sinks next to the three part sink would not produce paper towels during this inspection. The PICs were told and replaced the paper towels to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

The sanitizer dispenser is not consistently producing sanitizer of correct concentration. The PICs are currently making a solution manually using a CL based sanitizer. The Quat based dispenser needs repairs and/or adjustment from the company as basic troubleshooting was not sufficient to remedy the situation. A follow up is being set for 10 days to ensure repairs are made.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor under and behind the soda syrups in the dry storage area are in need of cleaning; 2) dust has accumulated on the tubes of the walk in cooler’s fan unit; 3) the floor around and behind the ice machine is in need of cleaning. These locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean thoroughly and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that facilities are maintained clean at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Mops are observed stored with the heads pooled up in the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mops so that the heads could hang dry. Education was conducted. Ensure regardless of equipment the bristles or the heads are stored so that they are able to hang and drip dry efficiently.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any paper towels available at the front of the house hand-sink. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. Be sure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink  to ensure hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn’t any soap available at the front of the house hand-sink. Discussed with PIC and hand soap was provided. Be sure that soap is available at every hand-sink to ensure that’s hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: An insect glue trap was stored in close proximity of clean dishes in the dish room. Discussed and showed to PIC. Ensure that glue traps are never stored near clean dishes to avoid contaminating food.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: The prep table in the back of the house is stored underneath vent covers that are significantly covered in dust. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that vent covers are frequently cleaned to prevent buildup and contaminating food items during preparation.
citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

Dishes need to be brought to the dish area in the kitchen to be washed. Dishes cannot properly be washed, rinsed, and sanitized in only a handwashing sink. Handwashing sinks cannot be used for a dump sink either. It is highly recommended to add a dump sink in the coffee bar. CORRECTED- The employees were educated to use a bucket to dump into and to take the dishes back to the dish area. This will be spot checked at the next routine inspection (at least 90 days).
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing and always have a sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands at that handwashing sink. This will be spot checked at the next routine inspection to ensure that this was done (at least 90 days).
