Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The particle board holding utensils on the wall outside the main walk-in cooler and the wall by the prep cooler in the on-the-go room must be sealed (ex. painted). 

(2) The plastic cornering in the small dish washing room by the entrance and the large dish washing room by the dish machine have fallen off the wall and must be replaced/repaired.

(3) The holes in the large dish washing room (near the triple sink) wall must be filled (ex. caulking).

(4) The caulking on the table behind the dish machine in the large dish washing room (attached to the rinsing table) is pulling away from the wall and must be re-sealed (ex. caulking). 

Ensure that all the above referenced are repaired/replaced/sealed to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that various coffee machines throughout the facility (including, but not limited to, the customer self service area and the bakery kitchen) have an accumulation of soil on the under shelf that is in contact with the coffee pot top. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the under shelf of the coffee machines are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the gaskets of the stacked double cooler (to the right of the Pepsi cooler) in the tray line kitchen are in disrepair. The gaskets must be replaced/repaired by the next routine inspection to ensure that physical facilities are always maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

The spray bottle identified as sanitizer in the dry storage and cleaning area of the facility bleached out the inspector’s test strips. This indicates a concentration capable of leaving harmful residues on food contact surfaces. Education was conducted and the bottle remade during this inspection to correct.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
citation_text:
3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in a manner as described in sections A-E of this code. 

At the time of this inspection packages of beef are observed in a pan thawing at room temperature. The PIC was consulted and instructed to educate staff as to safe thawing practices. The items were moved to the sink and water turned on to correct.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

During this inspection a sanitizer was not observed ready for use in the prep area. The PIC was consulted a sani bucket made with CL to correct. Ensure that a sanitizer is available for use at all times that foods are being prepared in the facility.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

Test strips are not available for the sanitizers used in the facility. The PIC is instructed to have test strips available for the sanitizers used prior to the follow up.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

Multiple rodent droppings are observed in the dry storage area of the facility. Droppings are restricted to one area and no other signs of pests are observed during this inspection. Cleaning was discussed and the PIC instructed to clean prior to the next routine inspection and maintain clean moving forward.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

An employee drink is observed on a wire shelf above foods and single service items. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The items was removed to correct. Ensure that all personal foods are stored that they do not pose a contamination concern for consumer products/foods.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed PIC of staff to have no certified food protection manager (CFPM) certification. PIC stated she has been out on medical leave and plans to take the course soon. Ensure there is a CFPM on staff at all times during operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. The faucet of the hand sink is touched with dirty hands, and therefore poses a cross-contamination hazard. Ensure staff are using a barrier such as a paper towel to turn off the hand sink to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handler’s certification on file for employees in the facility. There was one certification on the wall which was expired. Ensure staff are obtaining their food handler’s certification within 30 days of hire and all certificates are available for view.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Inspector observed tortillas being stored in a grocery bag on cook line. Discussed with PIC and PIC had them placed in a takeout box immediately. Ensure that tortillas are stored in food-grade containers at all times.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed two instanced of the facility needing maintenance.

1. (Repeat) Inspector observed there to be a build up of dust on the ceiling tiles in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC, and PIC stated that they would clean them as soon as possible. Ensure this area is cleaned enough to prevent the build up of debris.

2. Inspector observed duct tape being used to repair the door seal with PIC. PIC stated they had the replacement door seal and would repair the door as soon as possible. Ensure the door seal is repaired.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. To ensure that hands are getting washed properly, a barrier must be used to turn off faucet handles to prevent recontaminating freshly washed hands. Be sure to educate all employees on proper handwashing procedures.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Several handwashing sinks throughout the facility lacked proper handwashing signage. The signage notifies employees to wash hands. Handwashing signs were provided to owner to post at every hand-sink that is used by employees. Ensure that the handwashing signs are posted and clearly visible to food employees.
citation_text: 6-301.14 Handwashing Signage. A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A bowl of iodized salt stored in the dry storage cooler contained broken pieces of a foam cup. The facility was using the foam cup as a scooper. Discussed and shown to the owner. The owner instructed an employee to discard the bowl of salt. Ensure that all food items are safe and free from any contaminants during storage.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: The ice scoop handle was observed touching the ice stored in the cooler of the soda station(near dish machine). Ensure that ice scoops handles are stored upward and not touching food items.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility recently switched from Chlorine to Quaternary ammonium as their chemical sanitizer. The facility could not produce any quat test strips during the inspection. Ensure that test strips are available in order to accurately test sanitizer solutions.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
comment: There isn’t hot water available at any of the hand-sinks throughout the establishment. The owner stated the water heater that’s responsible for supplying hot water to the sinks is down. The facility is planning to replace the water heater and is currently waiting for the replacement to arrive. Ensure that there is always hot water available to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 5-103.11(B) Capacity. (B) Hot water generation and distribution systems shall be sufficient to meet the peak hot water demands throughout the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulk behind the dish table and along the dish machine is peeling from the wall. There is also a buildup of debris in the areas. Ensure that these areas are recaulked to prevent build up of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The only employee who has a Food Protection Manager Certification was not present at the start of the inspection. The employee who is food manager certified arrived during the inspection. Ensure that there is always a CFPM present during all hours of operation and when food preparation is occurring.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
The following raw animal proteins were observed to be stored in a manner that does not protect against contamination:
- Raw chicken was observed stored above beef in the walk in cooler
- Raw shelled eggs were stored above ready-to-eat foods such as but not limited to avocados, lemons, and limes

The raw animal proteins were rearranged during the inspection and the violations were corrected on site. Discussed proper storage order with PIC.  Foods that have higher cooking temperatures should always be stored below items with a lesser cooking temperature. Ensure that food items are stored in a manner that protects against cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Several containers of cooked foods were observed without date marking. These items in the walk in cooler include but aren't limited to chicken, beans, and beef. Discussed proper date marking with PIC. Ensure that any TCS food items that are stored in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: There were several ants observed along the wall of the service station. Discussed and shown to the PIC. The PIC noted that Orkin services the facility and that a follow-up will occur in two weeks to monitor the presence of insects. The facility was instructed to have Orkin provide treatment more frequently (at least 1x a week). Be sure to routinely clean the establishment to help reduce the presence of insects.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: The handle of the ice scoop stored in the cooler of the soda machine (bar area) was observed touching the surface of the ice. Ensure that ice scoop handles are stored upward and not touching the food item.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the coving throughout the back kitchen area to be damaged and separated from the wall. PIC stated that a repair request has been submitted. Ensure the coving is in good repair and the juncture between the wall and floor is sealed, smooth, and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed flooring under the drink dispenser and fryers to be soiled with food and debris. PIC was informed of soilage and stated that the equipment is moved and deep cleaned underneath once a week. Consider increasing the frequency of deep cleaning in the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: A food employee was observed to rinse their gloved hands at the cookline handsink. This is not adequate handwashing procedure. Gloves are not intended to be washed. Employees must remove gloves to wash hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC who provided education to the employee. Review proper handwashing procedure with all employees.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. [P]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: An employee was observed returning an edamame pod that had fallen from a dish onto a tray with their bare hands. CORRECTED- The container of edamame was voluntarily discarded. Discussed bare-hand contact with PIC who provided education to the employee. Employees need to use clean gloved hands or utensils to prevent bare hand contact when handling ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Foods at the sushi station heat lamp were observed below 135F: ribeye at 88F, eel at 130F, and eel at 98F, all probed. CORRECTED- Foods were cooked 1 hour prior and were allowed to be reheated to 165F before hot holding at 135F or above. For the heat lamp to work properly, foods need to be in a single layer directly under the lamp (not stacked or adjacent to the lamp). Moving forward, time as a control will be used to ensure that these foods are maintained safely. See General Comments for Time as a Control policy details.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Kewpie mayo and other sauces were observed stored at room temperature at the sushi station. The sauce original containers bear labels instructing refrigeration after opening. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who will ensure sauces are stored properly, including under refrigeration if the label instructs.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: A bowl of thawed still-sealed packages of tuna were observed in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Inspector provided education and discussed with PIC who will educate staff. ROP fish needs to be removed from the reduced oxygen environment (by cutting the packaging, for example) before thawing. PIC had an employee open the thawed packages. Ensure packages are cut prior to thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section. [Pf]

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Two wet wiping cloths were observed stored on the sushi station cutting board. Ensure wet wiping cloths are stored submerged in sanitizer solution between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D). [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The sushi station handwashing sink is not sealed to the wall and needs to be re-caulked.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

An employee was observed to sprinkle chopped nuts onto sauce with their bare hands. Education was conducted and the items discarded to correct. Ensure that ready to eat (RTE) foods are protected from contamination by the use of gloves or utensils while handling.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

1) Multiple cup holders in the kitchen are used for storing plastic utensils. These containers are observed soiled at the time of this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the holders to dish for cleaning. The plastic utensils were discarded as well. 2) A pen and a sharpie are observed in a container along with Dixie cups/lids. Pens and sharpies are not cleaned/sanitized and are not generally considered clean for the purposes of food contact. The PIC was shown and moved the implements to the pen cup observed a foot away and discarded the Dixie cups to correct. Ensure that all single service items are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture.

The hand sinks in the women’s bathroom and the employee bathroom in the back are observed with gaps forming at the wall/sink junctions. The PIC is instructed to re-seal these locations so that a smooth and easily cleanable surface is present at all times.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A pair of personal drinks (opened) are observed stored on the top shelf over multiple shelves of plates. The PIC was shown and told to place in use personal drinks under and/or away from food contact surfaces in the kitchen. The drinks were moved during this inspection to correct.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. Ensure staff are using the provided paper towels to turn off the hand sink to avoid cross-contamination. An employee was also observed using their clothing to dry their hands after washing. Clothing poses a cross-contamination risk and therefore cannot be used for drying.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the hand sink in the bakery area to be obstructed. PIC was informed that hand sinks need to be accessible at all times to promote proper hand washing. The hand sink obstruction was removed during the inpsection.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket next to the drive-thru window to have 50ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC was informed that the concentration was too low, and the sanitizer bucket was replaced. Sanitizer concentrations will decrease over time with use and evaporation. Therefore, the sanitizer buckets need to be replaced frequently to ensure proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed multiple large storage containers holding white powders to be unlabeled. PIC was informed that labels need to be placed on containers to allow for recognition of container contents. Ensure containers are labeled by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the shelves of the syrup dispensers to have a heavy accumulation of syrup and dust. PIC stated that the dispensers are cleaned every Thursday. PIC was advised that cleaning frequency may need to be increased to avoid the accumulation of soil and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed employee food items stored on upper shelving of cooler above food for the consumer. PIC was advised that a designated storage area should be assigned below food for consumers to avoid cross-contamination. Ensure designated areas are assigned and in use prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed coffee nozzles to be soiled with food debris. PIC was informed of accumulation and the nozzles were cleaned. Ensure staff are thoroughly cleaned frequently enough to avoid accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed hot dogs and brats in the back cooler to be opened with no date mark. There is a system in place which automatically prints a date marking label when the package is opened. It seems these two packages were simply missed. PIC was informed and will educate staff on proper date marking. Ensure staff are placing date marking labels on packages after opening to prevent the sale of out-of-date products.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Two of the employees along the cook line were observed to be bare hand touching ready-to-eat foods. CORRECTED- The manager immediately corrected this action and employees were educated to wear gloves. Ensure that all ready-to-eat foods are touched with either single-use gloves that are on WASHED hands or through a suitable utensil such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or dispensing equipment.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a trash can observed to be in front of the handwashing sink on the cook line. CORRECTED- The manager moved the trash can to a position that does not block the handwashing sink. Ensure that handwashing sinks are maintained to be accessible at all times. Employees are more likely to wash their hands, and do it more frequently, if handwashing sinks are easily accessible.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: There is a leak coming from under the handwashing sink in the coffee bar area. Ensure that this leak is repaired. Wastewater should be disposed of properly.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: SECOND REPEAT - The caulking on the triple sink on the 4th flow was observed to be in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC mentioned that they work order has been put in because all maintenance work has to go through the hospital. The cafe is located in the Springfield Clinic’s main campus east wing. Ensure that the necessary repair is done to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

Multiple employees were observed to change gloves and change tasks (to food handling) without hand washing. Education was conducted with the PIC and should be passed on to all employees moving forward. Hand washing is the most important method to preventing foodborne illnesses being spread and should be enforced at this facility. Ensure when to hand wash education is passed on to all staff at the facility.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sani buckets in the facility did not register on the inspector test strips. A manager was shown and remade the buckets to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are maintained at effective levels at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple pans both in use and on the storage shelves do not appear to have been completely cleaned when washed. Remaining sticker residue and stickers are still observed at the time of this inspection. The PIC is instructed to have the dishes re-cleaned period to the follow up being conducted on Monday.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector tested dish machine (puck). Dish machine was ran several times, starting initially at 135F and going up to 152F. Discussed machine not reaching 160F with PIC. PIC immediately put in a service call for the dish machine. Ensure that only triple sink is used until dish machine can be serviced. Inspector will return 04/14/2025 to re-asses dish machine.
citation_text: 4-501.111 Manual Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. If immersion in hot water is used for SANITIZING in a manual operation, the temperature of the water shall be maintained at 77°C (171°F) or above.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
1. Inspector observed the dish storage shelves in the facility to be dusty and tarnished. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the shelves are going to be cleaned soon and liners will be applied to each shelf. Ensure the shelves are maintained in a way that keeps them free of dust and debris.

2. Inspector observed the tops of the cook line equipment to contain dust and food debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the equipment is cleaned by the hood company regularly. Inspector recommends performing ancillary cleanings to keep surfaces free of debris between steam cleanings.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of caulking:
- The dish table to the right of the dish machine is in need of recaulking. 
- The hand-sink to the right of the cook-line is in need of recaulking
Ensure that these areas are recaulked back to the wall to prevent the buildup of debris.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The prep cooler in the food truck is still not operational and an ice bath is being utilized to keep items cold held. The equipment either needs to be repaired or replaced in the truck to ensure that food can be properly cold held at 41F or under. A follow up is scheduled for 4/15/2025 to ensure that the prep table has either been repaired and is functioning properly or has been replaced and the TCS items are being properly cold held.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility brought Chlorine test strips instead of Quaternary ammonium test strips for their Quaternary ammonium spray bottle sanitizer. Ensure QUATERNARY AMMONIUM test strips are available at all times on the truck to be able to test the concentration of the sanitizer. A follow up is scheduled for 4/15/2025 to ensure that these test strips are available on the food truck.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed soda nozzle in front self-service area or be soiled with debris. PIC was informed and nozzle was cleaned and sanitized. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned frequently to avoid accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods stored ambient on prep table with no proper marking for time as a control. The PIC stated that the employee forgot to label the items with the time control stickers. The tomato and lettuce that were unmarked were discarded. The rest of the produce was properly and clearly marked. Ensure staff are using the time as a control stickers at all times and discarding after 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.19(C)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (C) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 6 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate: (a) The time when the FOOD is removed from 5C (41F) or less cold holding temperature control, and (b) The time that is 6 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from cold holding temperature control.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed bins holding clean equipment and utensils to be soiled with food and debris. PIC was informed and bin was moved to the dish area. Ensure staff are cleaning the bins frequently to avoid accumulation of food debris.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed a container of raw beef to be stored above cooked breakfast sausages in the stacked freezer (across from cook-line). Discussed and shown to PIC and containers were rearranged. The beef was moved to the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw animal protein is always stored below cooked ready-to-eat foods to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The vent covers above the back prep station area were observed with a significant amount of dust. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that the ventilation unit, along with the vent covers are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent possible contamination of food, as well as buildup of dust.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

At the time of this inspection there is not a certified food protection manager (CFPM) available at this facility. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there are sufficient CFPMs on staff to cover all shifts.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

1) Multiple sets of tongs in the storage room are observed with remaining food debris; 2) Tubs in the storage room are observed with remaining food debris; 3) Multiple knives in the knife block are observed with remaining food debris on them. All three situations were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for re-cleaning. This situation has been noted multiple times in the past. Management should educate staff and ensure that all food contact surfaces are being completely cleaned prior to storage. Inspector will spot check moving forward to ensure that complaince is ongoing for this situation.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

The back door to the facility does not seal completely during this inspection. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair the door/seal prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all outer openings are protected from pest entry at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

Peppers and tomato sauce are observed remaining in their cans after opening and during storage. No covering is being provided beyond the open can top. The PIC was shown the jalapeño peppers in the walk in cooler and instructed to store all foods in sealable containers after opening.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

A pair of cloths next to the hand sink in the server area are observed on the counter and not in a sanitizer solution. The PIC was shown and instructed to maintain the rags used for wiping counters and other food contact surfaces in solution of effective concentration between uses at all times. The rags were moved to a bucket to correct.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

Multiple shelves throughout the facility are observed with chipping paint and rust. The PIC was shown an example and instructed to clean and re-seal the shelving units throughout the facility. Provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface for any potential food related surfaces.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

There is not currently a PIC with a current allergen certification training available during this inspection. The PIC was consulted and instructed to ensure that there is always a CFPM on site with allergen training. A copy of the certificate should be maintained at the facility at all times.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed 3 door cooler to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, cooler will be cleaned. Ensure facility is cleaning non food contact surfaces at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(Repeatx2) Observed the following physical facility areas in need of repairs:
1. Multiple areas of the facility need re-caulked: the prep sink in the back, the back triple sink, and the mop sink. All areas have black mold present. 
2.Liner on shelving unit next to the triple sink is broken and has holes. Replace liner. 
3. The wall paper in the women’s bathroom is severely fraying in multiple places. Wall paper needs resealed or replaced. Walls should be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Discussed with PIC, repairs will be made. Ensure physical facility is being monitored at a frequency that prevents the need for physical facility repairs.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the salad holding prep cooler to be cold holding at 54F. Discussed with PIC, cooler will be serviced. TCS items were moved to another working prep cooler and the walk in cooler. Ensure all TCS foods are being cold held at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the top of the back dish machine to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC, ensure non food contact surfaces are being cleaned at a frequency that prevents food debris and accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop to be resting in mop bucket. Discussed with PIC, mop was relocated to the strainer portion of bucket. Ensure mops after use are placed in a position that allows them to air-dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment: Observed only 1 certified food manager to have the required allergen training completed. Discussed with PIC, remaining CFM’s will acquire allergen certificate. Ensure all CFM’s have completed the required allergen training and certificates are kept within facility during hours of operation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed ice in the basin of the hand sink upon arrival. The hand sink appears to have been used for dumping a drink. PIC was informed that hand sinks may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. Ice was discarded.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

The following facility items are in need of repair: 
1. Silicon caulking in holes in wall behind meat slicer.
2. Seal front counter to wall (silicon caulking) and remove existing damaged trim piece
3. Seal or replace broken trim behind garbage can to left was you walk into back space
4. Replace damaged base tile as you enter the walk-in cooler

Ensure these facility items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed ice accumulation in front and back of kitchen walk-in freezer. Ice accumulation is not considered food-safe, and thus poses a cross-contamination hazard. Repair freezer as needed to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a build-up of soils in the catch tube and diffuser of the bar soda nozzle. Discussed with PIC and PIC had the piece of equipment cleaned immediately. Ensure that this piece of equipment is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build-up of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed a cart of clean dishes being stored under the EcoLab pest-control light in the dish room. Discussed placement of dishes with PIC. PIC removed the cart and placed it in a covered area where dishes will be safe from contamination. Ensure that no food or food-contact surfaces are stored under pest control devices.
citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed an area of the floor in the kitchen to be in disrepair. PIC informed inspector that a piece of equipment had just been removed from the area, and the facility is currently looking for a replacement. Inspector observed the floor sealant to be broken and removed from around a drain on the floor. This will need to be patched to render the surface smooth and easily cleanable. Inspector also noticed that there was a gap between the wall and floor in this area. Ensure this gap is sealed to prevent pest entry, and also to make the surface transition smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Signed reporting agreements were not on file for employees present during this inspection. Ensure signed reporting agreements are kept on file for all employees as proof that they have been educated on foodborne illness symptoms and diagnoses that would limit their ability to work in the kitchen. Inspector will follow up in 10 days to see that signed reporting agreements are on file.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A). [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed moving from the cash register to donning gloves without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Provided education to PIC and employees present. Review handwashing procedures with all employees. Ensure employees wash hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. [P]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to wash hands then turn the faucet off without using a barrier. CORRECTED- Provided education to employee and PIC. Educate all employees to use a paper towel or other barrier to turn the faucet off after washing hands. This prevents recontamination of newly-cleaned hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: 1st REPEAT: The 2 door cooler and prep cooler do not have an ambient thermometer inside. Ensure all cold holding units have ambient thermometers present inside and placed at the warmest part of the cooler.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a ceiling tile missing above the mop sink/water heater area. Replace the ceiling tile.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food handler certificates could not be located for two of the 3 employees present during this inspection. Ensure all employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates on file in the facility for review during health inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Gaskets on doors #2, 3, 4, and 6 were observed loose and separating from the doors. Repair or replace the broken gaskets.
citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities are in need of repair:
1) Damaged floor tiles were observed around the back door.
2) Caulking along the restroom handsink is not smooth or easily cleanable. Recaulk the sink so the seal is smooth.
3) The walk-in cooler floor is rusted and needs to be painted or otherwise resealed.

citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Metal shelving used for container storage was observed to be rusted. Shelving will need to be painted or replaced so that the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) certification on site during today’s inspection. The PIC stated that he has his CFPM, but the certificate is stored at the Isles location where he just transferred from. Ensure CFPM certification is available for view by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee fail to hand wash before donning new gloves to begin a new task. Education was conducted regarding when to wash. Hands must be properly washed before donning a new pair of gloves to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed one sanitizer bucket on the prep line which measured 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The sanitizer bucket was remade using the dispenser and measured 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are frequently replacing the sanitizer buckets and measuring the concentration with a test strip.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed an employee drink stored with food for consumers in the standing coolers. The employee drink was moved to the bottom shelf during the inspection. Ensure staff use designated areas to store personal times to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Food handler training
comment:
2nd Repeat Violation

PIC was unable to provide proof of food handler training certification for food employees at facility. Ensure valid food handler’s certifications are available for view for all employees by next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: The operator’s Certified Food Protection Manager certificate expired in January and no one else has their certificate. Ensure that there is always a person in charge who is a certified food protection manager.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was a trash can in front of the handwashing sink and a necklace inside of it. CORRECTED- The trash can was moved from being in front of it and the necklace was removed. It was also discovered that the handwashing sink did not have any power to it to provide running water. The operator brought a bucket of potable water with spout to create a temporary handwashing sink. The handwashing sink was supplied with paper towels and hand soap. Ensure that handwashing sins are maintained to be accessible at all times for employee use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The cold holding prep table in the truck is not functioning. The employees had the TCS food in a cooler on top of ice. The food was observed to be out of cold holding temperature. Cut tomatoes were probed to be at 68F, pico was probed to be at 69F, and lettuce was probed to be at 69F. CORRECTED- The operator created a suitable ice bath for the items in the top of the prep cooler and continuously stirred the items. The temperature is continuing to drop at this time. A follow up will be conduced tomorrow, 4/6/2025, to ensure that they have facility has proper cold holding. When doing an ice bath, it is important to submerge the bottom of the pans in both water and ice to allow the pans to be in an ice bath. This allows the temperature to reach the food in the pan.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The cold holding prep table in the truck is not functioning properly. The facility is using an ice bath to cold holding prep table. They are operating again tomorrow, 4/6/2025 and have someone coming to fix the cold holding prep table today. Ensure that this is repaired to allow for proper cold holding without the use of an ice bath.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The facility is using trash bags as liners for their chip containers and could not provide if they are food grade or not. Food should be stored in a container that is smooth and easily cleanable. Cease using trash bags and use the containers to store the chips. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility has a Quaternary ammonium sanitizer spray bottle that is being used for sanitizer and they do not have test strips for the sanitizer. The facility is operating again tomorrow and should have test strips for QUAT. A follow up will be conducted tomorrow, 4/6/2025, to ensure that they have obtained test strips for their sanitizer. Ensure that there is always a test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration of the sanitizer.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One employee on the truck that was stated to be there for on and off a year is observed to not have their food handlers certificate. Ensure that all employees who have been employed for greater than 30 days have their food handler certificate. These certificates should be printed and accessible to view to the inspector. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the accumulation of soils on the surface of the ice dispenser on the soda machine. Discussed with PIC and the accumulated soil was cleaned to sight of touch while inspectors were on site. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build-up of soils on the baffle of the ice machine in the facility. Discussed with PIC, and PIC cleaned and sanitized the baffle immediately. Ensure the baffle is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build-up of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of soils in the container that holds the ice scoop for the ice machine. Discussed with PIC. PIC removed ice scoop container and cleaned and sanitized the container. Ensure container is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build-up of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The PIC will be educating employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The fry slicer is observed soiled at the time of this inspection. 2) Multiple knives on the magnetic strip are observed soiled during this inspection. This inspection is being conducted as initial prep is about to begin and these items are stored this way since last night, indicating that sufficient cleaning did not take place. The PIC was shown and moved the items to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

A pan of cooked beef is observed with a date of 3-3 in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown and stated that it was from last night and was mislabeled by accident. The items appear new and were allowed to be relabeled to correct. Insure that all date marking is done correctly at all times moving forward.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A metal pot is stored on top of sheet pans in the storage room off of the kitchen. This pot has a metal spoon in it and the pot has standing oil in the bottom. This item should have been cleaned prior to storage with the cleaned food contact items. The PIC was shown and moved the items for cleaning to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The hand sink in the kitchen has a gap between it and the wall. The PIC was shown and instructed to seal so that a smooth and easily cleanable surface is available at all times.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of this inspection none of the current certified food protection managers (CFPMs) have an available allergen training certificate observable. Ensure that all CFPMs have completed allergen training and maintain copies of the certificate at this facility moving forward.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

On arrival only test strips for the quaternary ammonia sanitizer used for sani buckets are available. The dish machine is CL based and required a separate test strips to check. The situation was discussed with the PIC. A new set of test strips were brought to the facility during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the facility has test strips for all chemicals used on food contact surfaces in the facility at all times.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.
