Multiple knives are being stored between the knife rack and the wall. The wall is visibly discolored and possibly soiled around the knife rack and behind it. This is not a clean location for food contact surfaces to be in contact with while in storage. The PIC was shown and tthe situation discussed. The knives were move to dish for re-cleaning and should not be stored here moving forward. Ensure all food contact surfaces are stored in a clean location after cleaning and before use.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the separate staging area dump sink to not be caulked to the wall. PIC had the sink caulked immediately. Ensure that all equipment attached to walls in areas of high moisture are caulked.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed there to be raw beef being stored over ready-to-eat foods (bread pudding) in one of the walk-in coolers outside. Discussed with PIC. PIC rearranged the items being stored incorrectly so that they were in-compliance with regulations. Ensure that foods are stored in the correct order to prevent contamination. Inspector will return tomorrow with some storage order hand-outs to ensure staff are aware of storage order regulations.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Inspector observed food on the floor in 2 of the 4 walk-in units at the facility. Discussed with PIC and PIC picked up everything and placed it on shelves. Ensure that food items are stored at least 6 inches off of the floor to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspector observed a build-up of ice in both of the walk-in freezers. The larger freezer had a small amount of build-up on food boxes, which the PIC removed as soon as it was brought to his attention. The smaller freezer has a large amount of built-up ice on the walls and strip curtains. The seals on the door look OK, and the door was completely shut upon inspector’s arrival. Ensure this machine is serviced to mitigate the build-up of ice throughout the machine.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a build-up of food debris in the bottom of the cook-line ovens. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that ovens are cleaned frequently enough to prevent the build-up of food debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the baffle of the ice machine in the facility to be falling off. Discussed possible hazards of having a broken baffle with PIC. Ensure that the baffle is replaced or repaired to render the ice machine repaired.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulk behind the dish table to be cracked and peeling. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the caulk is replaced to create a smooth, durable, and easily cleanable surface transition between the dish table and wall.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed staff not using a barrier to shot the faucet after washing their hands. PIC was made aware of the proper procedures for hand washing. Ensure that staff follows the adequate procedures for handwashing to avoid recontaminating their hands in the process of making food.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple ants and a live roach in the dry storages area and mouse droppings in multiple areas in the kitchen and the dry storages area. PIC was made aware of pest activities in the facility. Per PIC, the pest control technician comes every two months. PIC ensured inspectors that they will make arrangements for the pest control technician to have a more frequent visit to the facility. Ensure that facility is routinely monitored for pest activities and the relevant action taken to eliminate pests in the facility.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed caulking around dish machine to be broken and damaged. Ensure countertop around dish machine is adhered to the wall with caulking to avoid accumulation of food debris and bacteria. Surfaces need to be smooth and easily cleanable to promote effective sanitizing.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) present at the beginning of the inspection. A manager was called and arrived during the inspection. Ensure there is a CFPM present at all times of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the employee bathroom to have no paper towels. Paper towels are necessary for handwashing using a protective barrier to turn off the faucet. Ensure there are paper towels in the restroom at all times. The bathroom was supplied properly during the inspection.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Observed the triple sink sanitizing station to read 10ppm chlorine. The employee handling dishwashing was made aware of the concentration was too low, and the triple sink was prepared with new sanitizer. The new sanitizer concentration as 100ppm chlorine. 

It was also observed that there were no sanitizer buckets prepared on the prep or cook line during the time of inspection. The PIC was able to educate staff on proper bucket preparation and triple sink setup. The new buckets measured 100ppm chlorine. Ensure a sanitizer buckets with cloths is available at all times of food preparation.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed the back door of the facility to be slightly open. A window with no screen was also open. PIC was informed that outer openings of the facility need to be protected to prevent the entry of insects and rodents.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the air conditioning system above the prep table to be soiled with grease accumulation and dust. The hood above the pizza oven was also heavily soiled with grease and dust. These non-food contact surfaces pose a cross-contamination risk, as the dust can fall directly onto food and food contact surfaces. Ensure these areas are cleaned frequently to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed coving throughout the kitchen and dry storage areas to be damaged or missing. Coving is essential for proper cleaning of the floors and walls in a food prep area. The floor wall junctures being properly sealed also inhibits the movement of pests throughout the facility. Ensure the coving in the food preparation and storage areas is repaired before the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the gasket of the white standing freezer to be broken. The gasket is necessary for proper sealing of the freezer. Ensure the seal is repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed floors and walls around dough mixing machines to be soiled with flour dust. Clean floors and walls around dough machine.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed bare wood being used to hold paper towel dispenser to wall in cook area. Bare wood is absorbent, and is therefore not considered smooth or easily cleanable. Either seal wood or replace with a different material prior to next routine inspection. 

Observed caulking in need of repair around hand sink in cooking area as well as around the triple sink. Caulking ensures that there is no soil accumulation between equipment and walls, and also creates a smooth surface for cleaning. Ensure the caulking is replaced prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop stored in the bottom of a dump sink in the back maintenance area. PIC was informed that mop heads need to be stored hanging so that they can drip dry. Mops left sitting on a surface can promote bacterial accumulation and cause cross-contamination. Ensure staff are hanging mop heads to drip dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floors of the walk-in freezer and back dry storage areas were observed to be soiled with food debris. Floors need to be kept clean to avoid cross-contamination and pest development in the facility. Ensure the floors are cleaned routinely to prevent the accumulation of soil.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Multiple personal drinks and a granola bar were observed to be stored on the upper-shelf of a cooler with food for consumers. Personal items need to be stored in a designated space away from food for consumers to prevent cross-contamination. This designated area can be a dedicated cooler or the bottom shelf of a cooler to prevent personal food falling onto food for consumers. Ensure a designated area is used for personal items prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food handler training
comment:
PIC was unable to find any food handler’s certificates on file. The CFPM is from another location, so is unsure of the location of the paper work. Ensure food handler’s certificates are available for view at the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed the following foods lacking proper date marking: (1) The salads in the display cooler that were prepared yesterday; (2) The package of cut ham in the front double cooler that was opened yesterday; and (3) Container of cut tomatoes in the front double cooler that were prepared yesterday. The salads, cut ham, and cut tomatoes were properly date marked during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the establishment for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day 1). Ensure that all required foods are properly date marked by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that underneath and between the fryers on the cookline has an accumulation of grease and foods debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues and other debris. Ensure that underneath and between the fryers is cleaned by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that the top under shelf of the coffee machine that is in contact with the coffee pot has an accumulation of soil residues. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides and other debris. Ensure that the top under shelf of the coffee machine is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the can opener blade to be soiled with food debris. Discussed the soiled can opener with PIC. PIC cleaned the entire can opener insert immediately. Ensure the can opener is cleaned regularly enough to keep the blade free of food debris.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the underside of the soda machine to contain food residue and soils. The specific area is the underside of the dispensers, next to the soda nozzles. The soda nozzles were clean. Discussed the soiled underside of the machine with the PIC. Ensure the machine is cleaned regularly enough to prevent the build up of food residue and soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspector observed the prep counter next to the back door to be cracked and showing particle board underneath the veneer. Discussed the cracking with PIC. Ensure that the surface is caulked, refinished, or replaced to allow for a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

Inspector observed bare wood on the wall behind the basket fryers on the cook line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that this wood is painted or sealed to create a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

A spray bottle in the front of the facility is observed with a clear liquid and no label indicating its use. The PIC indicated that the bottle contains a premixed sanitizer. The PIC was instructed to label the bottle as sanitizer and did so to correct the violation. Ensure that all chemicals are labeled at all times in the facility.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed multiple employees fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink. PIC was informed that employees need to use a clean barrier such as a paper towel to turn off the hand sink. This clean barrier prevents cross-contamination during hand washing. Ensure staff are using a barrier when turning off the hand sink.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the triple sink and 3 sanitizer buckets to read 0ppm quaternary ammonia with a test strip. The PIC stated that the opening shift must have failed to add sanitizer to the mix. The sink and buckets were remade and measured 150ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are testing the sanitizer concentration of the sink and buckets to avoid cross-contamination and food-borne pathogen transmission.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the following items to be out of temperature in the preparation coolers:
1. Sliced tomato (probe 47.4F)
2. Shredded lettuce (probe 53.2F)
3. Sliced tomato (probe 49.9F)

These items in the open-air prep cooler were “mounded” in their containers, which seems to be causing the temperature to be too high. A container of shredded lettuce which was less full measured 37F with the probe from the same cooler. To avoid improper cold holding, avoid “mounding” the food items in their containers when stored in the open-air prep coolers. The shredded lettuce and sliced tomatoes were only in the prep cooler for 1.5 hour. PIC enacted time as a control for those items and will discard after 4 hours. The other container of sliced tomatoes, since the time they were added to the cooler is unknown, was discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: (1) The soil on the coffee machine upper portion that is in contact with the coffee pot; (2) The food debris on the top of the microwave; and (3) The debris on the floor in the dry storage area underneath the shelves along the back wall. All non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced areas are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival all of the sanitizers in the facility are observed at 0 ppm quat. New buckets were ran. These registered intermittently at 0-200 ppm. It appears that the dispenser is not properly mixing the solution and large amounts of the concentrate are being off gassed in the bubbles on top of the solution. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. For the short term the PIC was able to manually make a solution of sufficient concentration to remain operational. This is not a long term solution. A follow up is being set for three days to ensure that the machine is repaired/adjusted and compliance attained.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

At the time of this inspection allergen training certificates were not available for the certified food protection managers (CFPMs). The PIC is instructed to have all of the CFPMs complete allergen training and maintain copies of the certifications at the facility at all times.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Th hand sink next to the mop sink is without paper towels at the beginning of this inspection. The PIC was notified and the paper towel dispenser refilled during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are supplied with needed supplies at all times.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

The soda gun in the bar area is observed stored submerged in the ice in the ice bin. The PIC was shown. This item is not regularly cleaned/sanitized on the outside or on the metal hose leading to it. Due to this this item should be stored outside of the ice (a Ready-to eat (RTE)) food to protect it from possible contamination. The gun was removed from the bin to correct.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink next to the mop sink is observed pulling away from the wall, which is producing a gap that is not easily cleanable. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facility equipment is maintained in good repair at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee filled up a sanitizer bucket with bleach and proceeded to continue prepping foods without removing gloves, hand washing, and donning new gloves. Other employees were also observed not washing hands before donning gloves during the inspection. Employees were educated that they must properly wash hands before donning gloves after contamination occurs. The PIC was tasked with educating employees on proper hand washing and glove use. Ensure that employees always wash hands and put on new gloves after contamination occurs. The inspector will follow-up on 4/3/2025 to check on hand washing.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the facet after hand washing. The employee was educated when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed that an employee dumped a drink and filled up a bucket in the sushi hand washing sink. The employees were reminded that only hand washing can occur in the hand washing sink. There is another sink on the left side of the sushi station that is the designated dump sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed there were several dented cans in the dry storage area. The PIC removed the dented cans during the inspection. Ensure that food packages are always in good condition to protect the integrity of food.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Required records available: molluscan shellfish identification, and parasite destruction.
comment: Observed that the facility does not have letters of parasite destruction from their suppliers for 2025. The inspector will follow-up on 4/11/2025 to check that the facility has the letters.
citation_text: 3-402.12(A) Records, Creation and Retention. (A) Except as specified in 3-402.11(B) and (B) of this section, if raw, rawmarinated, partially cooked, or marinated-partially cooked FISH are served or sold in READY-TO-EAT form, the PERSON IN CHARGE shall record the freezing temperature and time to which the FISH are subjected and shall retain the records of the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for 90 calendar days beyond the time of service or sale of the FISH.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following storage order violations: 
(1) Raw pork stored over seaweed, onions, batter, and other ready-to-eat foods in the clear door cooler on the cookline. 
(2) Raw beef, fish, and eggs stored over noodles, cooked, chicken, and various vegetables in the sliver refrigerator on the cookline. 
(3) Raw shrimp stored over cooked rice, mushrooms, and cut onions in the front walk-in cooler. 
(4) Raw fish stored over vegetables and creamer in the front walk-in cooler. 
(5) Raw fish stored over buckets of soy sauce in the back (alcohol) walk-in cooler. 
(6) Raw beef stored over eggs in the back walk-in cooler. 
(7) Raw fish stored over various vegetables in the clear door cooler by the walk-in cooler. 

The above storage order violations were corrected during the inspection. The PIC was reminded that ready-to-eat foods must be stored above raw foods, and that raw meats must be stored according to their internal cooking temperature. The inspector will follow-up on 4/3/2025 to check on storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the sanitizer bucket on the cookline was testing at 0-10 ppm during the inspection. After an employee added a capful of bleach to the sanitizer bucket it tested at 150 ppm. The PIC was reminded to test the concentration of saniztier buckets on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that the inside of the ice machine at the server station had an accumulation of soil inside. The PIC cleaned the ice machine to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed that cut zucchini in the front walk-in cooler was stored in its original box. The PIC was educated that cut and washed foods cannot be stored in their original packing to avoid contamination. An employee moved the cut zucchini into a clean container during the inspection. Ensure that foods are stored in food contact surfaces that are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed that the steam table had temperatures between 115F and 130F when the inspector arrived. The PIC turned up the steam table and when the inspector re-checked the temperatures were above 135F. The PIC was instructed to closely monitor the temperature of the steam table. The inspector will follow-up on 4/3/2025 to ensure that temperature are always above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed containers of cooked noodles and rice in the front walk-in cooler prepared yesterday that lacked date marking. The PIC was notified and an employee date marked the noodles and rice during the inspection. The inspector educated that ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (with the day the food was prepared being day 1). Ensure that all required foods are always properly date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed fish in reduced oxygen packaging (that stated on the package that it must be removed from the reduced oxygen environment before thawing) thawing in the clear door cooler by the walk-in cooler. The PIC was educated and an employee removed the fish from the packaging. Ensure that reduced oxygen packaged fish is always removed from the package before thawing.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed pans of salads stored stacked on top of each other without a barrier in between. The PIC was educated and an employees wrapped the salads in saran wrap during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always protected from cross contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment:
Observed the following ready-to-eat foods had scoops without a handle: 

(1) The vinegar used for the cooked sushi rice. 
(2) The cooked rice in the front walk-in cooler. 
(3) The scoop for the sugar bin in the dry storage area. 

The PIC was educated that all scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle. Ensure that all ready-to-eat foods have a scoop with a handle (which is not stored in-contact with the food) by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment:
Observed that the following plates were stored in a position that presents the risk of contamination: 

(1) Uncovered plates at the entrance to the sushi prep area. 
(2) Uncovered plates at the salad station across from the dish machine. 
(3) Uncovered plates at the table by the service station by the soy sauce bottles. 

The PIC was informed that plates must be stored invented with the food contact portion facing downwards or covered. All the plate storage was corrected during the inspection. Ensure that utensils and equipment are always stored to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed two boxes of single-service items (chop sticks and to-go containers) on the floor of the alcohol storage room. The PIC was educated that all single-use articles must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground. Ensure that the single-service items are stored properly by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed that the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces:

(1) The rusty shelves in the back walk-in cooler that must be repaired or replaced. 
(2) The reach-in freezer on the cookline has a significant buildup of frost that makes cleaning inefficient. The PIC unplugged the freezer to begin the defrost process during the inspection. It was observed to be free of ice at the end of the inspection, 

Ensure that the above referenced are made/remain smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the coving to the left of the doorway (the side with the drink station) in the server area is in disrepair. The coving must be repaired/replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the coving is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bottom portion of the walk-in freezer door has not been properly repaired. The current repair involves tin foil and the door is not shutting properly. There is still a build-up of ice on the air curtains and floor by the door. Ensure that materials are properly attached to that they are smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment:
Repeat Violation
Observed no staff member on site to have a certified food protection manager certification. Ensure there is a CFPM on site at all times of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment:
Repeat violation 

Observed no signed employee health and reporting agreements for food employees at facility. Provide a signed employee health and reporting agreement for all food employees at facility. Agreements were provided during the inspection.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand washing sinks in front area and back area of facility to be inoperable due to either leaks or obstruction. Have hand sinks cleared and serviced by a licensed plumbing contractor. A follow-up will be conducted on 4/11/2025 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed sink in front prep area to not have soap available for use. Soap dispenser was refilled during the inspection.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed sink in employee bathroom to not have paper towels available for use. Paper towels were refilled during the inspection.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the back hand sink to be fully obstructed. Observed the front hand sink to have a mason jar of food and a lighter stored in the sink basin. The front hand sink was also obstructed by a rolling cart of food items. The hand sinks need to be accessible at all times for employee use. A follow-up will be conducted on 4/11/2025 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed food items stored on the floor in dry storage as well as below display tables in the display area. Food items need to be protected from pests and cross-contamination by being stored at least 6 inches off the floor at all times. Ensure proper food storage requirements are met in the facility. Proper food storage will be spot checked along with the follow-up conducted on 4/11/2025.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed old mop water and drainage water from freeze-drying equipment to be retained in buckets in the facility. All wastewater needs to be efficiently conveyed and disposed through an approved sewage system. Wastewater cannot be retained onsite as it poses a risk of cross-contamination and pest development. The buckets were discarded during the inspection.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed employees on duty at facility to not have food handler’s certification. All food employees at facility must have certified food manager or food handler training within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: There was a bottle of ranch and a container of pulled pork in the prep cooler that was observed to be past the date that it was date marked for. CORRECTED- Both items were discarded and the PIC was educated. Ensure that food is discarded if it exceeds the date that it is date marked with or the manufacturer’s expiration date, whichever comes first.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: There was not any sanitizer made and available to clean food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- A bucket was made using bleach and tested at the correct concentration. PIC was educated. Ensure that there is always sanitizer available during all times of food preparation to make sure that food contact surfaces are being properly cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The paper towel dispenser at the hand-sink was observed without paper towels. Paper towels were added to the dispenser during the inspection. Ensure that paper towels are available at all times to be sure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The top inner surface of the microwave was observed with accumulated food debris. Discussed and shown to PIC. The microwave was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces of equipment are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation and contamination of food.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are in need of repair:
- Hand sink in kitchen area is pulling from wall. Caulk hand-sink back to wall
- Parts of the wall in between the triple sink and hand-sink are starting peel. Repaint affected areas.

See that areas are repaired. Physical facilities must be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The wall connecting the hand-sink/dish-sink is in extreme disrepair. The paint is peeling and the sink is pulling from the wall. See that repairs occur to the dish area. Ensure that sink is re-caulked and that the wall is repainted so that areas are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
The PIC could not produce proof of food handler’s certificate. Ensure that all employees that handle food are food handler certified if not a food protection manager. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the bar area would not register on inspector test strips. The machine was in use prior to observation by the inspector. The bar manager worked on the machine for a few minutes and the machine registered correctly afterwards. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours.

A gallon of milk in the walk in cooler is observed partially used. The PIC indicated that it had been opened approximately 5 days ago. Education was conducted and a date placed on the container to correct. Ensure that these items are given date markings if they are going to be at the facility longer than 24 hours and used or discarded prior to the end of the 7th day.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

The shelves in the walk in cooler are observed rusted and in need of repair. This can come in many forms but needs to have an end result of a smooth and easily cleanable surface. Repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Two of the three CFPMs at the facility are unable to show an allergen training certificate during this inspection. They are instructed to complete allergen training prior to the next routine inspection and maintain copies of the certificate at the facility moving forward.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the crock-pot on the cookline was not hot holding cooked chicken at 135F or above. The following internal temperatures were recorded: 105F, 104F, and 108F. The chicken was voluntary discarded during the inspection. An employee turned up the crock-pot and put water and broth inside to test its functionality. After about 10 minutes the crock-pot had an ambient air temperature of 168F. The PIC was instructed to closely monitor the temperature of the crock-pot. Ensure that foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed that the inside of the ice machine above the outside of the baffles is soiled with debris (near the hinge; not in contact with the ice). The inspector suggests draining the ice to clean inside. Ensure that the inside of the ice machine is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the floors of the walk-in freezer were soiled with food spills and debris. An employee cleaned the floors to sight and touch during the inspection. Ensure that the walk-in freezer floors are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of debris and other soils.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the dump sink is not sealed to the wall. All surfaces that are not easily movable must be sealed to the wall (ex. caulking). Ensure that the dump sink is sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The bottle of hand soap in the women’s restroom was empty. Discussed with PIC and soap bottle was refilled with liquid soap. Be sure that hand soap is available at every hand-sink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: The meatballs stored in a container in the walk in cooler were observed to be covered with mold. The meatballs were shown to the owner and were discarded. Ensure that meatballs are marked with the day of preparation and are discarded if not used within the 7-day timeframe. Day 1 counts as the day meatballs are prepared. The facility has an additional 6 days to hold the meatballs in house. Discard if meatballs aren't used at the end of day 7.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A bowl of cut lettuce stored inside of the service cooler was observed uncovered. Also, there were several containers of uncovered items in the walk in cooler such as but not limited to meats, tomato sauce, and broths. All foods stored in coolers must bear a covering to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: There were food items stored on the floors of the walk in cooler and walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC that foods must be placed on shelves or at least 6 inches above the floor. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed accumulated debris in several of the coolers throughout the facility. The inner surfaces of the coolers contained dried food debris. Ensure to clean inner surfaces of equipment as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed containers of mashed potatoes, fried chicken, and baked chicken in the right walk-in cooler prepared last week that were not date marked. The PIC voluntarily discarded the foods during the inspection. The PIC was educated that ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours must be date marked to indicate the 7 day maximum (with the day the food was prepared being day 1). Ensure that all foods are correctly date marked by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed containers of sugar, powdered sugar, and flour were not labeled. The inspector educated that all containers holding white powders (and other easily mistakable foods) must be labeled with the common name of the food. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that all easily mistakable foods not in their original packages are always labeled.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of food debris and grease underneath the fryers in the kitchen. The PIC was reminded that physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food, grease, and other debris. Ensure that the floor under the fryers is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that several employees have expired food handler certificates. All employees that handle food and do not have a CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must take the class. Ensure that all required employees obtain food handler certificates by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that hand washing is taking place at all times that it should be.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

On arrival the hand sink in the service area is observed with a trash can, a broom and a dust pan blocking access. The PIC was shown and moved the items prior to the inspector discussing the situation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible for ready use at all times in the facility.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Several cans are observed in dry storage with major dents in the sides and tops. The PIC was shown and moved the items to the back for credit to correct. Education was conducted. Ensure that all cans are recieved and maintained in good working order at all times of storage and until use/service.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
(REPEAT x4) 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple food contact surfaces in the facility are observed soiled in such a way that it appears that they were not sufficiently/completely cleaned prior to storage. Items include: 1) knives in the knife rack in the middle hallway; 2) pan lids on the racks int he middle hallway and; 3) lettuce tongs on the front line. All items were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all dishes are cleaned completely each time prior to storage for use. This is the 5th inspection in a row where this situation has been a concern! Ensure that the dish washers are educated and needed oversight is taking place to ensure that the food contact surfaces are clean!

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

The wedge slicer is observed soiled with dry food debris during this inspection. When asked the PIC indicated that it had not been used today, indicating that it was not cleaned at the end of last night and has been soiled for greater than 18 hours minimum. The PIC moved the slicer to dish for cleaning to correct.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD (TCS) shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

A container of minced garlic in oil with other seasoning is observed on a shelf in the middle hallway. Garlic in oil is considered a TCS food and needs temperature control for safety. The PIC was notified and education conducted. The container was discarded during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. The PIC is instructed to store this item in a refrigerator moving forward.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspectors observed the hand sink in the back of the kitchen area opposite the walk-ins to be out of paper towels for proper hand drying. Discussed with PIC and PIC got the paper towel dispenser refilled. Ensure that the hand sink is always supplied with the relevant accessories at all times to ensure proper hand washing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The accumulation of soils were observed on baffles of the ice machine. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that a work order had been submitted to get the ice machine cleaned. PIC had the technician pull the ice machine apart and got it cleaned while inspectors were on site. Ensure that food contact surfaces such as the ice machine is monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Accumulated soils were observed on the grates of the shelves opposite the mixing station in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the grates will be clean. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces such as the shelves use for storing utensils and dishes is monitored and cleaned at a at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspectors observed water sitting at the brink of the floor drain adjacent the mop sink in the back area. PIC was made aware of the water drainage and PIC said that they will get the drain checked. Ensure that drainages from point of discharge are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency to avoid sewage backup.
citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking on the sinks in the men bathroom were observed to be in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the caulking will be done in a couple days. Ensure that closed spaces such as the space between the sinks and the wall is caulk and properly sealed to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: . The pipe coverings that connect the pipes flush with the wall under the kitchen hand sink are observed to be in a state of disrepair. Discussed with PIC. Ensure these coverings are reattached to the wall to create a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
