comment: The sealing covering (wall juncture) on the wall next to the pizza prep cooler was observed to be in disrepair. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the sealing will be reattached. Ensure that the relevant sealing is done to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
citation_text: 6-201.13(B) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (B) The floors in FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain, and the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The shelves use for storing dishes and utensils above the triple sink and opposite the triple sink in the kitchen area were observed to have an accumulation of soils. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the shelves will be clean. Ensure that surfaces like the shelves are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer buckets were observed to be at 100ppm Quaternary ammonium at the beginning of the inspection. Discussed with PIC and the solution was remade to have it corrected to be at 400ppm. Ensure that the concentration of the sanitizer buckets are checked at a regular frequency and are remade if not at the label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: The bottom of the two door standing cooler by the coffee station was observed to be partially detached. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the unsealed/detached portion will be reattached to have the cooler in good repair. Ensure that equipments are maintained in a state of good repair.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspectors observed accumulated soil on the air dock vent above the coffee station in the kitchen area. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the vent would be clean. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facility areas were observed to need repairs.
1. Broken coving left of the hand sink.
2. Nudo board at the triple sink at the dish storage area was observed in disrepair
3. The accumulation of soils above the caulking on the dish machine countertop. 
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed two instances of date marking violations in the facility.

The first instance was at the bar, where the inspector observed the juice containers to not bear date marks. Discussed with the PIC, and they had date marks added to the containers. Ensure that containers are date marked within 24 hours of opening to preserve food safety. Violation is corrected on site.

The second instance was in the kitchen. Inspector observed 3 containers full of sauce cups to be past the 7-day maximum that date marked food can be kept. Discussed dates with PIC, and PIC immediately threw out the sauces and replaced them with fresh.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: Observed no employee reporting agreements to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, employee reporting agreements were provided by inspector and observed to be signed by current staff. Education was provided on the importance of employee reporting agreements, ensure each member of staff has signed the employee reporting agreements and they are kept within the mobile unit at all times.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed 4 large cans in dry storage to be dented on the seam of the can. Refuse dented cans at time of delivery or discard dented cans that are damaged onsite. Cans were discarded during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(7) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (7) Storing damaged, spoiled, or recalled food being held in the food establishment as specified under § 6-404.11.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the dish machine to read 0ppm chlorine. The PIC was informed that the sanitizer concentration was low. The bucket containing the sanitizer was nearly empty. Facility was able to top off sanitizer bucket for the dish machine. The dish machine measured 150ppm chlorine following the repair. Ensure staff are checking the concentration of the dish machine with test strips frequently to avoid improper sanitization of dishes and equipment.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed frozen pollock filets thawing on the countertop in its original packaging. PIC was informed that TCS foods must be thawed either in refrigeration or submerged under running water. Pollock was placed back in the walk-in cooler during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed a container of flour and a container of sugar to have no clear label. Ensure all containers are marked with common name to avoid mistaken recognition. The food containers were labeled during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed food in the walk-in freezer to be stored on the floor. PIC was informed that all food items need to be stored at least 6 inches above the ground. This allows for proper cleaning and protects the food items from pests.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed personal jackets stored on dry storage shelving. Also observed personal food items stored with food for the facility in the walk-in cooler. Ensure designated areas are used for personal items and food to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Two containers of meat sauce stored in the warmer were probed at 90F. The PIC wasn’t sure the exact time that the sauces were placed in the warmer, but it hadn’t been over 2 hours. The facility was instructed to reheat the meat sauce to the proper reheating temperature (at least 165F). Shortly afterwards, the sauces were probed again and read 167F. Be sure that TCS food items are always held at 135F to ensure proper hot holding temperatures.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed several containers of food stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler and freezer. Discussed and shown to the PIC. The containers of food were removed from the floor and put on shelves. Ensure that food items are never stored on the floor and are always stored at least 6 inches above the floor.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed staff handling ready to eat food without glove wear. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper food handling and glove wear. Ensure staff is wearing gloves when in contact with RTE foods to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed utensils in back hand sink. Discussed with PIC, utensil was removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sinks are solely being used for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no CFM present to have completed the required Allergen training. Discussed with PIC, ensure all CFM’s have completed the required Allergen training and said licenses are available within facility. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There was ice observed in the handwashing sink by the dish area from a drink being dumped in it. CORRECTED- Educated PIC that handwashing sinks can only be used for the intended purpose of handwashing. Handwashing sinks cannot be used as a dump sink or for any other purpose.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: There are multiple clear containers of food that have been removed from its package in dry storage that does not have a label on it. Ensure that these containers are labeled with the common name of the food.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The fans of both clear door coolers in the kitchen. 
2. The fans in the walk-in cooler. 
3. The nonfood contact surfaces of both soda machines. 
4. The dessert chest freezer in the kitchen needs to be de-frosted to allow it to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following physical facilities need to be repaired: 

1. There is a frost issue in the walk-in freezer that is causing frost/ice build up on the shelves, floor, and door. Ensure that this issue is repaired and the ice is scraped off to allow these surfaces to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The back prep table needs caulked to the wall. 
3. FIRST REPEAT- Behind the ice machine needs to be sealed, as there is paint that is peeling. Ensure that this is sealed and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
4. FIRST REPEAT- The table to the right of the soda machine in the kitchen needs to be caulked to the wall. Ensure that this is caulked and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed considerable ice accumulation in the walk-in freezer. The ice was stemming from the equipment behind the ventilation and falling onto food items in the freezer. The ice on food poses a cross-contamination hazard. Ensure the freezer is repaired to prevent cross-contamination with food items in the freezer.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A couple knives were observed to have soil build up on them on the magnetic knife holder in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and the knives were taken to be cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces and utensils are clean at all tmes.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The chlorine concentration in the dish machine did not register on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Discussed with PIC and PIC called the EcoLab technician to get it fix. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are ant effective levels at all times. Ensure that the concentration of sanitizer is monitored at a regular frequency. 
Facility is closed on Monday 3/31/2025 so inspector will be back on 4/2/2025
citation_text: 4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (B) An iodine solution shall have a: (1) Minimum temperature of 20°C (68°F), (2) PH of 5.0 or less or a PH no higher than the level for which the manufacturer specifies the solution is effective, and (3) Concentration between 12.5 MG/L and 25 MG/L.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: A jug of milk was observed opened and not date marked in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC and PIC mentioned that the jug had been open two days prior. The date marking was then corrected. Ensure that food items are date marked properly if they are not used within 24 hours after opening to prevent listeria growth.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION. The walk-in freezer is observed to have peeling paint on the ceiling. PIC was made aware that this is a repeat from previous inspection on 10/22/2024 and PIC ensured inspectors that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure the areas with the paint coming off are properly scraped and then a new sealant, such as paint, is utilized to reseal that area that was scraped. The repair in the walk-in freezer should be done in a manner that allows the repaired surfaces to be smooth, non-absorbent, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Inspectors observed an accumulation of grease build up in the following places in the kitchen.
1. On the side and underneath the fryers.
2. Underneath the table next to the fryers under the pass through window.
3. Behind and underneath the grill area.
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the above mentioned areas will be clean. Ensure that closed spaces like tha above mentioned areas are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: A mop head was observed being stored on the floor in a puddle of water at the beginning and during the inspection. Discussed with PIC and the mop storage was corrected. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed the wooden shelf above the pass through window to have exposed absorbent areas not coated. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the unsealed portion of the shelf will be coated.
citation_text: 6-201.16(B) Wall and Ceiling Coverings and Coatings. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Facility was observed to not be in compliance with allergen training. Discussed with PIC and PIC mentioned that they notice it had expired and will be getting the training done soon. Ensure that CFPMs receive allergen training to be in compliance with the LAW. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector shield of the ice machine in the bar area has slime build up observed. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean/sanitize and maintain clean/sanitized moving forward. The item was cleaned to correct.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

The bleach buckets in the kithcen are without labels and are the same type of buckets used for battering wash water and ice bath containers for foods. The PIC was notified and instructed to ensure that chemical containers are labeled so that they are not mixed up with food containers. Labels were added by an employee to correct the violation.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed hand sink in prep line to be used for dumping soda and ice down the drain. PIC was informed that hand sinks are strictly for hand washing only, and drinks should be discarded elsewhere. Ensure staff are only using the hand sink for hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed the triple sink in the ware-washing room to be leaking. The center sink is leaking below the drain into pans on the floor. PIC was informed of the leak and plans to schedule repair. Ensure plumbing in the facility is fully functional at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following facility areas to be in disrepair:
1. Hole in ceiling above fryer
2. Hole in wall near the air conditioner in the kitchen
3. Hole in wall next to fryers
4. Wall outlet pulled away from the wall below the air conditioner in the kitchen

PIC was informed that walls, floors, and ceilings in the facility need to be smooth and easily cleanable. This promotes a clean workspace to prevent soil accumulation and cross-contamination. Ensure these items are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed cutlery and dining trays to be stored with their food-contact surfaces face-up with no adequate coverings. PIC was informed that the food-contact surfaces of items need to be covered or inverted to protect from cross-contamination. All items were inverted during the inspection.
citation_text: 4-903.11(B) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (B) Clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be stored: (1) In a self-draining position that allows air drying; and (2) Covered or inverted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mops to be stored with their mop heads on the floor. The PIC was informed that mops need to be stored such that they can safely drip dry to prevent bacterial accumulation and cross-contamination. All mops were properly inverted during the inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
(REPEAT x3) 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

Raw chicken is observed over raw beef in the standing cooler to the right of the mop sink. Storage order for foods in a cooler was discussed with the PIC and the items re-arranged during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure foods are stored in relation to their cooking temperatures so as to prevent possible cross-contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket only registered at approximately 10 ppm on inspector test strips. The PIC stated that the bucket was made this morning. These chemicals will break down over time and require remaking throughout the day to maintain at effective concentration. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels throughout the day.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Cooked ground beef and gyro meat are observed in the bottom of the prep cooler without date marking. Per the PIC the items were prepared two days ago. Education was conducted and dates added to the containers to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that all time/temperature control for safety (TCS) ready to eat (RTE) foods held at the facility longer than 24 hours are given date marks.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the dish machine to be dispensing sanitizer at 10 PPM. Discussed with PIC and PIC called the service company immediately. Ensure that the dish machine sanitizer concentration is checked regularly to prevent food contamination. Inspector instructed facility to use triple sink until dish machine is fixed. Inspector will return 04/02/2025 to check the dish machine again.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed two packages of smoked Salmon stored in a floor reach cooler to exceed the 7-day holding timeframe. The packaging dates were 3/08/2025 and 3/14/2025. The items were pulled and discarded by the PIC. Ensure that cooked meats are never held in house longer than 7 days of preparation. If the 7-day time frame is exceeded, be sure to discard food items.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: No one with a CFPM certification were present at the beginning of the inspection. The only person with the CFPM had gone to the store and came to the facility at the end of the inspection. PIC was made aware that  at least one person with a valid CFPM should be at the facility during operational hours. Ensure that a certified food protection manager is at the facility during operational hours at all times.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Upon arrival, inspectors observed a loaded cart obstructing the hand sink. Discussed with PIC and the cart was removed to ensure an accessible hand sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are accessible at all time for handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food obtained from approved source.
comment: Inspectors observed multiple containers of barbecue sauce in the grill cooler and on the shelf that had been made by a source that is unknown to be approved. Discussed with PIC and PIC was unsure if the BBQ sauce was made in an approved kitchen or from and approved food source. Ensure that all food items are obtained from an approved food source to be in compliance with the LAW.
citation_text: 3-201.11(B) Compliance with Food Law. (B) FOOD prepared in a private home may not be used or offered for human consumption in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Inspectors observed the following violations in storage order:
1. Raw sausages were stored above cheese in the bottom of the prep cooler.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed bleu cheese and cooked pork stored in coolers in the kitchen without a proper date mark. Cooked pork and bleu cheese are both considered ready-to-eat (RTE), time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Any RTE TCS foods need to be date marked after opening, preparing, or portioning into a new container. These food items need to be discarded 7 days following the initial date on the marking. The bleu cheese was prepared yesterday, so a date mark was added to the container. The cooked pork had an unknown preparation date, and was therefore discarded. Ensure staff are practicing proper date marking to prevent bacteria accumulation in food.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. 3. Seafood. 
4. Whole cuts of beef and pork.
5. Ground beef and pork.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed employee fail to use a barrier to turn off the hand sink after washing hands. PIC was informed that a barrier such as a paper towel should be used to turn off the hand sink to prevent cross-contamination. Ensure all staff members are properly hand washing at all times.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand sink in server area to have ice in sink basin. PIC was informed that hand sinks are not to be used for any purpose other than hand washing. Ensure staff are using at dump sink to empty drink glasses rather than the hand sinks.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: Observed tap in kitchen for pressure washer to be leaking. The leak was a steady drip onto the floor. The hand sink in the server area has is also leaking into the sink basin. Ensure plumbing is in good repair at all times. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/27/2025 to ensure the plumbing issues have been repaired.
citation_text: 5-205.15(A) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed facility to have no available test strips for their quaternary ammonia sanitizer. Ensure test strips are present at all times to ensure compliance. A follow-up will be conducted on 4/3/2025 to ensure test strips are on site.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice machine interior to be soiled with mold. This violation is a repeat from the previous routine inspection conducted on 3/14/2025. An additional follow-up will be conducted on 4/3/2025 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code. 

A tray of cooling spaghetti noodles is observed with the noodle in contact with the shelf above. The kitchen manager was shown and instructed to store foods so that they are not in contact with soiled and un-sanitized equipment. Other storage options were discussed and the noodles discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that all foods are protected form contamination at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival all of the sani buckets in the kitchen area registered low on the inspector's test strips. The PIC was shown and remade the buckets to correct the violation. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels while in use.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The dish machine in the bar area did not register on the inspector’s test strips when checked. Investigation produced the belief that the chemical concentrate had off gassed sufficiently to not be effective in solution. The PIC was shown and changed the concentrate jug. Once primed the machine was effectively sanitizing again. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at proper levels at all times.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Nozzles on the fountain drink machine in the Tuscan Room are observed soiled. This equipment has not been used today and the nozzles should have been cleaned after its last use. The PIC was notified and had the nozzles removed for cleaning and sanitizing to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are clean regularly.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives in the kitchen do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage in the knife rack. The kitchen manager was shown and moved the items back to dish to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Multiple ice wands in the walk in freezer are observed soiled during this inspection. The kitchen manager was shown and moved the wands to dish for recleaning to correct. Ensure that all food contact items remain clean prior to contact with foods.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival the bar, pizza and server area do not have a sani bucket ready for use in the area. The PIC was asked and made buckets for these areas to correct the violation. Ensure that a sanitizer is available in the handling and preparation areas at all times that handling and preparation are taking place.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed foods in the market portion of the store stored in boxes on the floor. It appears that extra food is being stored on the floor underneath the relevant display. Food must be stored at least 6-inches above the ground. The PIC and inspector discussed using empty cardboard boxes, pallets, milk cartons, or another method. Ensure that all foods are stored 6-inches above the floor by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed hot water tap of hand sink to be nonfunctional. Only the cold tap was working during the inspection. Ensure the hot water to the hand sink is repaired. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/31/2025 to ensure the sink is repaired.
citation_text: 5-202.12(A) Handwashing Sink, Installation. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 29.4°C (85°F) through a mixing valve or combination faucet.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed baffles of ice machine to have mold accumulation. Ice is considered a ready-to-eat food, and therefore is a large risk for cross-contamination. PIC was informed of accumulation. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/31/2025 to ensure ice machine is emptied and deep cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed blue cheese used for Bloody Mary cocktails to be stored portioned in a ziploc bag with no date mark. PIC was informed of proper date marking practices and the cheese was voluntarily discarded. Ensure blue cheese and milk products are date marked if kept refrigerated longer than 24 hours after opening or portioning into a new container.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Observed three dead roaches in the facility. Two were located behind the bar and one was located in dry storage. Debris resembling rodent dropping was also observed under the bar. PIC stated that the owner of the facility handles pest control. Hiring a professional pest control company is advised. The dry storage area had some stray pretzels on the floor near the dead insect. Ensure the facility is frequently cleaned to avoid pest accumulation. Additional pest control measurements are recommended. A spot check for improvement will be conducted on 3/31/2025 during the scheduled follow-up.
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed facility to have no test strips available. Test strips were acquired during the inspection from a neighboring establishment. Ensure staff have test strips at all times and are using them to test proper sanitizer concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.116 Warewashing Equipment, Determining Chemical Sanitizer Concentration. Concentration of the SANITIZING solution shall be accurately determined by using a test kit or other device.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a few small holes next to and above the hand wash sink behind the bar. These holes can contribute to pest movement throughout the facility as well has accumulate soil and debris. Ensure walls, floors, and ceilings are smooth and easily cleanable to promote a clean space.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer bucket in prep line to measure 0ppm chlorine. PIC was informed of the low sanitizer concentration, and a new bucket was made. PIC stated that the bucket was made this morning. The chlorine in the bucket may have evaporated in that time, causing the low concentration. Ensure staff are checking the sanitizer concentration frequently and replacing when necessary.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed bare wood on shelving and next to fryers in kitchen. Bare wood next to the fryers is being used to cover the gap between the fryer and the counter. The bare wood on the shelving is above the microwave and used to extend shelves. Bare wood can harbor bacteria due to its absorbent characteristics. Ensure the shelving is painted or covered to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a soiled piece of cardboard being used as a filter at hood system. Discussed with PIC, cardboard will be removed and a proper piece of equipment will be used. Ensure facility is not using cardboard as a repair item, and that hood system is working to manufacturers standard. Follow up has been scheduled for 3/26/25.
citation_text: 6-201.17(A) Walls and Ceilings, Attachments. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, attachments to walls and ceilings such as light fixtures, mechanical room ventilation system components, vent covers, wall mounted fans, decorative items, and other attachments shall be EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A container of utensils in the kitchen is observed with a soiled inner bottom. The PIC was shown and moved the container and utensils to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they are protected from contamination until use.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed no Certified Food Protection Manager in kitchen during time of inspection. PIC reported that the CFPM is on break. Ensure that a CFPM is present at all times of food service/preparation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the following food items to measure above the maximum cold holding temperature for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods:
1. Cut tomato
2. Cut lettuce
3. Sour cream
4. Mayonnaise
5. Spicy mayonnaise

The cut tomato was measured with a probe thermometer, and measured 48F. The items on the above list were voluntarily discarded. The consumer-style refrigerator will now only be used for non-TCS foods. The newer commercial cooler will hold all TCS foods moving forward.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed the following ready-to-eat TCS foods to be missing proper date marking:
1. Cooked spaghetti in sauce
2. Cooked chicken
3. Sour cream
4. Cottage cheese
5. Milk

Ensure that all ready-to-eat TCS foods are date marked if stored longer than 24 hours after opening. These items need to be discarded 7 days following opening/preparation. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/31/2025 to ensure date marking compliance.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed food containers (aluminum pans and paper boats) stored without adequate coverings to avoid cross contamination. Ensure food containers are either covered or inverted to protect food-contact surface.
citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed grease and dust debris on hood baffles above fryers. Informed PIC that hood needs to be cleaned frequently enough to prevent the accumulation of grease and dust.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the kitchen flooring to be excessively sticky and soiled. Ensure flooring in the food prep areas are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed employee phone, purse, and other personal items stored on food contact and non-food contact surfaces in the kitchen. There is a shelf dedicated for personal items. Ensure the designated shelf is free of food items for sale, and there are no food items below the shelf. Ensure all personal items are stored in designated areas to avoid cross-contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed no CFPM on site with allergen certification. Ensure there is a CFPM on site at all times with valid allergen certification to properly educate consumers on risk of allergen exposure.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed a member of staff wash hands without using soap, and no barrier was used when turning off faucet. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and employee rewashed hands. Ensure staff is properly washing hands to prevent any possible contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.12(A) Cleaning Procedure. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands or arms for at least 20 seconds, using a cleaning compound in a HANDWASHING SINK that is equipped as specified under § 5-202.12 and Subpart 6-301.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to not use a barrier (a paper towel) to turn off the faucet after washing their hands. CORRECTED- Educated the employee on how to properly wash their hands and to use a barrier to prevent recontamination to your clean hands after washing. Ensure that all employees are educated on proper handwashing and are knowledgeable on the importance of using the proper cleaning procedure.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The tea nozzles in the lobby were observed to have an accumulation of soil residue in and on the nozzle. CORRECTED- The operator cleaned the nozzle during the inspection and was educated on the importance of cleaning drink nozzles daily. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There was observed to be two sinks of chicken being thawed in cold, still water. CORRECTED- Discussed this with the operator and the chicken was moved to the walk-in cooler to finish thawing. Ensure that if thawing under cold water that the water is running. Educate all employees on the importance of proper thawing procedures.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

Ensure that these boats, along with all other single-service utensils and articles, are inverted to protect the food contact surface from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

3. REPEAT- The dish shelves across from the ice machine are rusted and have an accumulation of soil residue. Ensure that the shelves are cleaned and are sealed to protect clean dishes from contamination. 

Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained cleaned.

SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

comment:
