title: Food handler training
comment:
The operator was unable to provide food handler certificates for any of the employees who are not CFPMs. Popeye’s is not on the Illinois Approved Food Handler Training List and therefore, must require all employees to have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. It is recommended to reach out to the Illinois Department of Public Health to be placed on this list if the onboarding training qualifies. Ensure that this process is taken or that all employees have their food handler certificate within 30 days of hire. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Inspectors observed a leakage in the standing cooler down in the basement. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that it was going to get fix. The facility has a rubber container at the top of the cooler shelf to catch the drips while they await the necessary repairs. Ensure that equipments are monitored and in good repair to avoid food contamination and spoilage.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee operate the cash register and then put on gloves to cook an omelet without hand washing inbetween. The inspector educated that all employees must wash hands before donning gloves for food preparation. The PIC will be reminding employees about proper glove use and hand washing procedures. Ensure that employees always wash hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is a buildup of grease on the right side of the grill. The PIC was reminded that non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease and other soils. Ensure that the right side of the fryer is cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the fan on the back kitchen door has an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. The inspector suggests creating a routine cleaning schedule for the fan. Ensure that the fan is clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there are small holes above the triple sink were a dispenser was recently removed. The holes must be sealed (ex. caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed a consignment of single-used food containers in boxes stored on the floor in the hallway. Discuss with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that they will get them store properly. The consignment had just been delivered the day before and had to be temporarily stored at the observed location.  Ensure that single-used articles are stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash and other contaminants. Singles-used articles shall be stored at least 6” above the floor always.
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed 2 ice baths holding chicken and lettuce to be cold holding at 54F. Discussed with PIC, the items were submerged in ice however no water had been added. Cold water was added to both ice baths, and both the chicken and lettuce dropped to 44F. Ensure staff is properly preparing ice baths to ensure proper cold holding temperatures are met.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed black mold to be present at the caulking on the triple sink. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure facility is monitoring caulking to prevent any black mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, santizer bucket was set up and tested at 200 ppm (Quat). Ensure sanitizing solution is set up at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the baffle of the ice machine to have a build up of soils on the bottom left edge. Discussed more frequent cleaning with PIC. Ensure the baffle is cleaned regularly to avoid contamination. Inspector will return 03/28/2025 to re-asses the condition of the baffle.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Inspector observed there to be multiple life stages of cockroaches behind and inside facility equipment. Cockroaches were observed behind coolers and on sticky traps. The pest presence has decreased since the last inspection, but some pests remain in the hard-to-service areas. Discussed cleaning of the inside of equipment with PIC. Ensure equipment is cleaned out to render it free of pest presence. Ensure facility keeps being treated 2x a week for pests as well to maintain the decrease in populations. Inspector will return 03/28/2025 to re-assess rest presence.
citation_text: 6-501.111(C) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (C) Using methods, if pests are found, such as trapping devices or other means of pest control as specified under §§ 7-202.12, 7-206.12, and 7-206.13.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspector observed the top of the dish machine to contain several dead cockroaches. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the machine is cleaned regularly enough to keep it clear of debris and dead pests.
citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Inspector observed a mop bucket being stored with water in it outside the mop room door. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. Ensure mop buckets are drained immediately after use and that mops are hung to dry as well. Ensure that mop water is never stored in the facility. Inspector will return 03/24/2025 to re-asses mop water storage.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulk connecting the triple sink to the wall to be degrading. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the caulk is replaced to maintain a smooth and easily cleanable surface transition.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink soap dispenser was out-of-order upon arrival. PIC explained that employees had been washing hands at the triple sink using mounted soap located there. Inspector advised that facility still uses hand-sink to wash hands, and to continue using soap from the triple sink, as they are located just opposite one another in the kitchen. PIC stated that a call to repair the soap dispenser has already been made, and that it should be fixed by tomorrow morning. Ensure that hand sinks are properly supplied to allow for hand washing procedures. Inspector will return 03/20/2025 to re-asses soap dispenser.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed raw eggs being stored over beef in the facility’s walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC, and PIC moved them so that they were above raw chicken instead. Ensure that raw meats are stored in proper order (fish, beef and pork, eggs, and poultry; top to bottom).
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
(REPEAT x2) 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD.

A tray of raw ground beef is observed stored on a shelf over containers of cooked ground beef used for sandwiches in the reach in cooler across from the hand washing station. The PIC was shown and rearranged the items during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that foods are stored so that cross contamination of pathogens is not a concern.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

Wet wiping cloths are observed on the counters throughout the kitchen. There is a CL smell to the cloths indicating that they are used for sanitizing. This was discussed with the PIC and they moved the cloths back to the bucket to correct. Ensure that all wiping cloths used in the kitchen are stored between uses in solution at all times.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Allergen training is not available for the certified food protection manager (CFPM) during this inspection. This situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to renew prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Employees were observed washing hands then using their newly-clean hands to turn the faucet off. CORRECTED- Inspector discussed proper handwashing with PIC, who will educate employees. Ensure a paper towel or other barrier is used to turn the faucet off to prevent recontaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Raw chicken in a ziplock bag in a plastic tub was observed stored over raw beef in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The raw chicken was sealed with no apparent leaks. PIC rearranged storage to keep chicken below other raw meats to prevent potential cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
comment: A large pot of queso was observed in the walk-in cooler at 61F (probed). PIC indicated that the queso was cooked the previous night and had cooled briefly at room temperature before being moved to the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded the queso. Ensure foods cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and reach 41F in no more than 6 hours total.
citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: Queso, cooked last night, was observed in a large pot in the walk-in cooler. Queso did not meet the necessary cooling benchmarks. Cooling methods are inadequate. Inspector discussed dividing queso into smaller portions and using ice wands to speed up the cooling process. Cooling foods need to be monitored to ensure they cool quickly. Review cooling methods and procedures with staff. Inspector will provide additional education in Spanish.
citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods. [Pf]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Daylight is visible along the floor/wall joint in both dry storage sheds. Seal both sheds along the floor/wall joints to prevent entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
1) Wire shelving in the walk-in cooler has become rusted and soiled with debris. Clean shelving and resurface, seal, or replace as needed to eliminate the rust and ensure shelving is smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Plastic protective coating is present on the shelf above the steam table. Remove the plastic coating.
citation_text: 4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Facility is cooking in pots too large to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized in the facility’s 3 compartment sink. Pots need to be able to fit in the 3 compartment sinks to adequately be washed, rinsed, and sanitized. PIC will modify processes to use smaller pots that will fit in the sink basins.
citation_text: 4-301.12(B) Manual Warewashing, Sink Compartment Requirements. (B) Sink compartments shall be large enough to accommodate immersion of the largest EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS. If EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS are too large for the WAREWASHING sink, a WAREWASHING machine or alternative EQUIPMENT as specified in (C) of this section shall be used. [Pf]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Owner’s allergen awareness training certificate expired in October 2024. Two other CFMs have not completed allergen awareness training. Ensure all CFMs complete allergen awareness training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer bucket and triple sink in kitchen to measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. PIC claimed that dispenser has been malfunctioning for some time. A different staff member was able to disassemble and replace to the nozzle of the dispenser. The sanitizer solution from the dispenser measured 100ppm quaternary ammonia after repair. The triple sink and sanitizer bucket was refilled with proper solution. This violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed three knives in the prep area metal rack to be soiled with food debris. The knives were removed from the rack and were placed in the ware-washing area to be cleaned and sanitized. Ensure staff are cleaning all equipment and utensils frequently enough to avoid accumulation of food debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed walk-in freezer to have rusty ice accumulating from the ceiling. There are tubs at the top of the shelf capturing the ice. The tubs were fairly full, suggesting the leak has been present for some time. Ensure repairs are conducted to prevent rust contamination with food items stored in the freezer.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed two jackets stored on dry storage shelves containing food. PIC was informed that employees need to use a designated area for personal item storage to prevent cross contamination. There seems to be a designated clothing rack in the office for personal items. Ensure staff are using this space rather than dry storage shelving for personal items.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed cook line to be in use with no sanitizer bucket prepared. PIC was informed that a sanitizer must be in use at all times during food preparation. A sanitizer bucket was created while on site and measured 100ppm chlorine. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed bare wood used as storage in the ware-washing area. PIC was informed that wood is absorbent and therefore not properly cleanable. Ensure facility is constructed with smooth, easily cleanable materials to prevent the accumulation of soil and bacteria.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed food handler’s certification for some employees to be absent or expired. PIC was informed that all employees who handle food, drinks, or ice need to have a valid food handler’s certificate within 30 days of hire. Ensure certificates are printed and readily available at next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. The hand-sink was observed to be obstructed by a food-tray cart when inspectors arrived at the facility. Discussed with PIC and the cart was removed to make the hand-sink accessible. Ensure that the hand sink is accessible at all time for use.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed eggs being stored over mushrooms in the walk-in cooler in the meat department. PIC was made aware of the appropriate storage order for food items and the eggs were moved a shelf below the mushrooms in order to correct the storage order. Ensure that all food items are stored appropriately to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: The open display cooler at the Sushi Kabar was observed to be out of temperature. PIC was made aware of the malfunction. The sushi in the cooler were probed and read at a temperature of 44F. The sushi in the cooler were moved to another cooler to enable the maintenance of the appropriate temperature. Ensure that cold holdings are often checked to ensure they maintain the adequate temperature to avoid food spoilage.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. Ensure that staff are aware of the possible accumulation of food debris under surfaces and need to extend cleaning procedures to closed spaces as well. Ensure that closed spaces and surfaces under equipments are routinely monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

comment: Employees were observed washing hands then using their newly-clean hands to turn off the faucet or dispense paper towels from the wall-mounted dispenser. CORRECTED- Inspector provided education. Employees need to use a paper towel or other barrier when dispensing paper towels and when turning off the faucet to prevent recontaminating their hands. Review handwashing procedures with all employees.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw shell eggs were eobserved stored on the top shelf of the short prep cooler, above squeeze-bottles of sauces and other ready-to-eat foods. Upon further discussion, PIC stated that the eggs are employee personal foods, not for service. CORRECTED- PIC designated the right-most door of the long prep cooler for storage of personal foods. The carton of eggs was moved to be stored away from foods for service. Ensure foods are stored to prevent potential cross contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Chlorine sanitizer in the 3 compartment sink was observed at 10ppm. CORRECTED- Inspector alerted the PIC, who added more chlorine to the sanitizer solution. Sanitizer was then observed at 50ppm Cl. Use test strips to verify sanitizer solution concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Six individual portions of mac & cheese were observed without dates in the 3 door cooler. CORRECTED- PIC labeled the portions with the date their original package was opened. Ensure all ready-to-eat TCS foods are labeled with the date they were opened, and used or discarded within 7 days after.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Ambient thermometers were not observed in the 3 door cooler or in the long prep cooler. Provide ambient air thermometers for all cold holding units.
citation_text: 4-203.12 Temperature Measuring Devices, Ambient Air and Water. (A) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled in Celsius or dually scaled in Celsius and Fahrenheit shall be designed to be easily readable and accurate to ±1.5°C in the intended range of use. (B) Ambient air and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±3°F in the intended range of use. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: 1st REPEAT: The end of the shelving holding Cajun seasoning is unfinished and needs to be sealed. Paint or otherwise seal the bare end of the shelf.
citation_text: 4-201.11 Equipment and Utensils. EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS shall be designed and constructed to be durable and to retain their characteristic qualities under normal use conditions. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
1) Frost accumulation was observed on the interior of the right chest freezer. Defrost the freezer regularly to eliminate frost accumulation and maintain the interior of the freezer smooth and easily cleanable.
2) Price tag stickers were observed on metal lids in the prep coolers. Clean lids to remove stickers.
3) Food debris was observed on the interior of the microwave. CORRECTED- PIC discussed with an employee, who cleaned the inside of the microwave.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
1st REPEAT: The following physical facilities items are in need of attention: 
1) An electrical outlet on the cookline is askew and does not cover the area cut out of the wall. See that outlets fit properly on the walls. 
2) Seal the handsink to the wall. The handsink, while secured to the wall, is not firmly in place and has some give which may make sealing it to the wall difficult.
3) Cracked caulking is observed at the bathroom handsink. Recaulk to eliminate the cracks.
4) Ceiling tiles in bathroom are acoustic and should be vinyl coated - replace tiles
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that both the gender-neutral customer bathrooms (located near the deli and the front service area) do not have covered trash cans. All toilet rooms used by females must have a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins. Ensure that bathrooms have covered trash cans by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-501.17 Toilet Room Receptacle, Covered. A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there are several holes in the wall directly above and to the left of the hand sink. The holes must be sealed (ex.caulking) to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a significant gap between walk in cooler and freezer and the ceiling. Discussed with PIC, ensure gap is filled. Walls should be easily cleanable with no gaps to prevent dust and debris accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer spray bottle to measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. A quaternary ammonia tablet was borrowed from a neighbor and a new sanitizer bucket was prepared, measuring 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer is being tested before use to ensure proper sanitization of food contact surfaces. Violation is considered corrected-on-site.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Inspector observed the paper towel dispenser at the hand sink to not have paper towels inside. Notified the PIC that there were no paper towels, and PIC replaced new paper towels in the dispenser. Ensure hand sinks are stocked with paper towels at all times to allow for proper hand drying and faucet turning procedures.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Inspector observed a few items in the facility to not bear date marks. Items include:

-Sliced cheese in a prep drawer in the kitchen.
-Half and Half in the bar display cooler.
-Juice in the bar reach-in cooler.

Discussed with PIC and PIC had them dated immediately. Ensure that temperature and time controlled food items are date marked within 24 hours of opening
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed hand wash sink next to the cook line to be obstructed by plastic containers and food. PIC was informed that hand wash sink needs to be accessible at all times. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/24/2025 to ensure the hand sink is accessible.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed food in prep cooler to be stored in a can used for original packaging. The can seemed to be repurposed for storage. The PIC was informed that the can is not protected from corrosion, and it is not considered a food safe container. The PIC moved the food into an appropriate container during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw shrimp and lobster in the walk-in cooler to be stored above garlic. PIC was informed that raw seafood needs to be stored below ready-to-eat foods. The juices from the raw seafood can fall into the food resulting in cross-contamination. The PIC moved the raw seafood to the bottom shelf during the inspection.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed ice machine on prep line to be soiled with pink slime mold. PIC was informed of mold and stated that the ice machine will be cleaned. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/24/2025 to ensure the ice machine has been properly cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The can opener and knives in the kitchen were observed to be soiled with food debris. PIC was informed and items were moved to the ware-washing room. Ensure staff are adequately cleaning equipment to avoid soil accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Raw shrimp, cooked chicken wings, and andouille sausage stored in the prep cooler were observed to be above the maximum cold holding temperature (41F). PIC stated that the raw shrimp had been placed in the cooler that morning, and the chicken wings and sausage were recently added to the prep cooler. The shrimp, since it had been out of temp for an unknown time, was voluntarily discarded. The chicken wings and sausage were placed in the walk-in cooler for reach an appropriate temperature. Below are the probed temperatures measured from the items:
1. Raw shrimp : 48F
2. Chicken wings : 48F
3. Andouille Sausage : 51F

Ensure staff are measuring the temperature of items in the cooler to ensure compliance. Since the items were either discarded or placed in the walk-in, the violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed fish to be thawing in still water at ambient temperature. The temperature of the fish in water was 63F (probe). Since the fish was improperly thawed, the items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are either thawing in the cooler or under running water.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed thawed fish to be in its original reduced oxygen packaging. The packaging indicated that the fish needed to be removed from packaging before thawing. Thawing the fish in its reduced oxygen packaging can promote the proliferation of the bacteria responsible for botulism. Ensure staff are removing the fish from its packaging prior to thawing. The fish was voluntarily discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed many boxes of food stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler. PIC stated that they received more food than usual this week and do not have adequate shelving. Ensure food is stored a minimum of 6 inches off the floor.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
comment: There is an apparent water leak above the hand wash sink on the cook line. The water seems to be coming from a small hole in the wall and steadily leaking down the wall into the hand sink. PIC was informed of leak and will be contacting the owner for repair. Ensure leak is repaired prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed mop to be stored in old mop water. Mops need to be stored such that they can drip dry. This will prevent pathogen accumulation in the mop head, and therefore cross-contamination of the kitchen space. Ensure staff are storing the mops such that they can safely drip dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed ceiling in walk-in cooler to be damaged and gapping. The ceiling was previously repaired with caulking, but the ceiling has gapped again. Ensure ceiling is repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed a bag of chips and over-the-counter pain medication to be stored on a food contact surface. PIC was informed and items were moved to the designated staff eating area. Ensure staff are using designated spaces for eating and drinking.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that facility has no food handler’s certificates available on site. All employees who handle food need to have a food handler’s certificate within 30 days of employment. Ensure employees have food handler’s certification available for view prior to next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Ensure no CFPM onsite to have valid allergen certification CFPM confirmed she has not taken the course. Ensure there is a CFPM onsite with allergen certification at all times. 


410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed the containers holding sugar, salt, and cracker meal were not labeled. All foods not in their original container that can be easily mistakably recognized (ex. white powders) must be identified with the common name. The PIC labeled the containers of salt, sugar, and cracker meal during the inspection. Ensure that all easily mistakable foods not in their original packages are labeled with the common name of the food.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the table holding the coffee machine (to the left of the dish machine) is not sealed to the wall. Since the coffee machinery is attached to the wall the table cannot be easily pulled out for cleaning. The PIC was instructed to seal the surface using caulking or another method. Ensure that the table holding the coffee machines is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the floors underneath the fryers and grill have an accumulation of grease and food debris. The PIC was instructed to pull out the equipment and clean underneath. An employee began the process of cleaning during the inspection. Ensure that the floors under the fryers and grill are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a bottle of oven cleaner to be in contact with clean utensils. Discussed with PIC, bottle was relocated and utensils in contact were pulled to be sanitized. Ensure chemicals are kept out of contact with food contact surfaces, and are not being stored on the same shelving as utensils.
citation_text: 7-301.11 Separation. POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS shall be stored and displayed for retail sale so they can not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS or TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed ice scoop to be resting in between ice machine and cooler. Discussed with PIC, ice scoop was moved to a sanitized tray. Ensure ice scoop is being stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed 2 mops to be resting in dirty mop water. Discussed with PIC, mops were moved to strainer part of mop bucket. Ensure mops are being stored in a way that allows them to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed food handlers licenses to be missing for multiple members of staff. Discussed with PIC, staff will completed food handlers training. Ensure all food handling staff have a valid food handlers license available within the facility during hours of operation. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen area was tested at 0ppm (quat). The PIC stated that the facility created the bucket earlier in the morning. The sani bucket was recreated and tested again at 200 ppm. Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize food contact surfaces and utensils.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Various cheeses such as but not limited to sliced American and shredded cheddar were probed at 51F and 53F. The temperature knob of the cooler was observed at the number 5. The facility was instructed to adjust the temperature knob to a higher number to ensure proper cold holding temperatures. 1% milk was recorded again 43F. PIC stated that the cooler was recently serviced because of the unit freezing. Ensure that TCS foods are always maintained at 41F or less.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The 2 door cooler in the serving area was observed with improper cold holding temperatures. The inside hanging thermometers read 50F and 51F. The temperature knob was observed at the number 5. The facility was instructed to adjust the knob to a higher number to lower the temperature of the unit. The ambient temperature of the unit was recorded again at 48F.  Ensure that cold holding units are sufficient enough to provide proper cold holding temperatures.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Accumulated soil and food debris were observed in the following areas:

1. The microwave was observed at to have an accumulation of grease drips and food debris on the base. 
2. Inspector observed the buildup of black mold in the far right compartment of the triple sink in the kitchen.
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the above mention areas would be cleaned. Ensure that non food contact surfaces are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed milkshake machine to be soiled with old food matter. PIC informed that a shake was just made. The current process for the milkshake machine is to clean the mixer attachment with clean water between uses, and clean/sanitize at the end of each day. Since the ice cream milk contacting the mixer attachment is a time/temperature for safety (TCS) food, the mixer attachment needs to be sanitized at minimum every four hours. Water is not an adequate form of sanitization. The mixer attachment needs to be submerged in sanitizer and air-dried to properly sanitize. PIC properly sanitized mixer attachment during the inspection. Ensure staff are sanitizing the attachment at least every four hours during use.
citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed two employees using their bare hands to shut off the faucet after washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff follow the adequate hand washing procedures at all times, including using a barrier to prevent recontamination of newly-clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12. [P]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Inspectors observed three dented cans (one oyster sauce and two soy sauce) being stored on the shelves in the dry storage. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. The dented cans were separated to be discarded. Ensure that the package integrity of cans are monitored as canned goods are received or stocked.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the no measurable concentration of the sanitizer in the dish machine. After several adjustments, a new bucket of sanitizer concentrate was connected and the machine primed to get the sanitation solution flowing properly. The chlorine concentration was then observed at 50ppm Cl. Inspectors informed PIC to educate staff to routinely test the dish machine chlorine concentration at the start of day and at the end to catch potential malfunctions early. Ensure that the sanitizer solution is monitored at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
1) The chicken in the cold holding on the customer make line was observed to at 47F (probed). CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and who voluntarily discarded the chicken. 
2) A pan of eggs on the customer make line were observed at 50F (ambient temperature), and stocked above the rim of the pan. CORRECTED- Eggs had been replenished after lunch. The pan of eggs was returned to cold holding to cool, and was replaced with a pan not filled above the rim.
Ensure that the temperature of food items in the cold holding are checked at all times regular frequency to avoid food spoilage. Educate staff to avoid stocking pans in in the cold holding unit above the rim of the pan. This will help keep foods 41F or below throughout.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
A rubber spatula with parts of the food contact surface chipping away was observed hanging in the back next to the triple sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the damaged spatula was discarded. Ensure that utensils use in food prep or items that are food contact surfaces are in good repairs are all times. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Inspectors observed an accumulation of grease and soils buildup on the exterior of the fryers and on the floor underneath. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the buildup will be clean. Ensure that the equipment and other kitchen surfaces are routinely cleaned to avoid the accumulation of grease and soil.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
4th REPEAT: Food handler certificates were not available for all food employees present. Ensure food handler certificates are on file for all employees who handle or prepare food.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed with a drink on the cook line without straw and lid. An employee was also observed using their cellphone with their gloves on. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the employee using a cellphone and reminded them to wash hands and change gloves before returning to work. Discussed with PIC and the behavior was corrected. Ensure that staff are educated to wash their hands and change their gloves after touching other items that may cause contamination.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and:(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspectors observed raw fish stored over cooked gumbo in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- Proper storage order was reviewed with PIC and the storage order was corrected. Ensure that the appropriate storage order is followed to avoid cross contamination between raw and ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
The following food contact surfaces were observed to have accumulated food debris:
1. Ladles and an egg slicer on the hanging rack above the 2 compartment sink were observed to have the accumulation of soil.
2. A utensil with damaged handle and accumulated food debris was observed on the rack adjacent to the cook line.
3. Blender cups used for crepes were observed with food debris inside.
CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the utensil with the damaged handle was discarded. The other items were taken to be cleaned. Ensure that food debris is fully cleaned from utensils in the warewashing process before returning them to clean equipment storage. While in constant use, food contact surfaces needed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized every 4 hours.
citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: An open half-gallon of chocolate milk in the front counter vertical cooler had passed the manufacturer’s printed date and without any in-house date marking. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and the chocolate milk was voluntarily discarded. Foods must be labeled with the date they are opened to ensure they are used or discarded within 7 days of opening. Ensure that the manufacturer’s printed dates of food items are monitored at a regular frequency to avoid spoilage or contamination of food items.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Inspectors observed an unlabeled container of white powder stored under the prep table in the back of the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and the labeling was corrected. Ensure that all white powders not in its original container is labeled with their common name to avoid confusion.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Inspectors observed a knife being stored hanging in the gap between another table and the prep table on the cook line. PIC was made aware of the appropriate storage of utensils during food preparation and the knife was taken away. Ensure that in-use utensils are always stored properly to avoid the contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The accumulation of grease buildup was observed between and under the equipments along the cook line. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the relevant cleaning will be done. Ensure that frequently used equipments are routinely cleaned to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Food handler training certificate was not available for one of the employees working during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates on file in the facility for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

There is not a CFPM available at the facility during this inspection. Information for the local CFPM courses will be sent in an email to the facility in the morning. Ensure that a CFPM is available at the facility at all times of operation.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival only a single signed reporting agreement is available at the facility. A fresh copy was observed in the public health binder. This was used to make multiple copies that were signed by all staff prior to the inspector leaving. Violation corrected.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

A knife is observed on the shelf above the center prep cooler with a personal phone making contact with the blade. The PIC was shown and the knife moved to dish for cleaning to correct. The observed location of the phone was acceptable in general, but if it’s located there food contact items cannot be stored in that corner as well. Ensure food contact surfaces are washed and maintained clean prior to use in the facility.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants.
