(b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

All observed food handler cards in the facility are expired at this time. The PIC is instructed to have all employees that handle food or food contact surfaces to complete food handler training and maintain a copy at the facility for verification.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

There is not a current allergen certification available at the facility at the time of this inspection. Hand outs will be sent to the PIC via email tomorrow for information purposes. Ensure that each certified food protection manager has a completed and up-to-date allergen certification. Keep copies of these certificates at the facility at all times.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed raw chicken stored above raw beef in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler. These storage order violations were also observed in the previous spot check and last routine inspection. Informed PIC that raw beef must be stored above raw chicken due to the beef’s lower minimum cooking temperature. All storage order violations were corrected on site. A spot check will be conducted in the near future to ensure storage order guidelines are being followed. Ensure staff are educated on the proper order of storage for raw meats.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed triple sink to measure 0ppm quaternary ammonia. The PIC immediately recognized that the Quat-San bucket under the triple sink was not properly connected; the tubing was not far enough into the sanitizer bucket. The triple sink was drained and refilled, with a quaternary ammonia concentration of 200ppm. The violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: There were raw shelled eggs above a bag of vegetables in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- The raw shelled eggs were moved to the bottom shelf and the vegetables were moved to the shelf above them. Ensure that food is protected from contamination during storage.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the kitchen was observed to be at a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The bucket was remade and tested to be at 100ppm of Chlorine. Ensure that the sanitizer bucket is frequently tested and remade if not at the label-recommended concentration.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The soda nozzles on the server line were observed to be soiled with an accumulation of black residue. CORRECTED- The soda nozzles were cleaned during the inspection and the staff was educated to ensure that these are being cleaned regularly. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: There was salmon in reduced oxygen packaging in the top of the prep cooler that was observed to be thawed with a label that stated to remove from packaging. Upon further investigation, the box of the frozen salmon stated to remove the fish from the packaging before thawing. CORRECTED- The staff was educated and the fish was removed from the packaging.
citation_text: 3-501.13(E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (E) REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGED FISH that bears a label indicating that it is to be kept frozen until time of use shall be removed from the reduced oxygen environment: (1) Prior to its thawing under refrigeration as specified in (A) of this section; or (2) Prior to, or Immediately upon completion of, its thawing using procedures specified in (B) of this section.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests.  The facility is observed to have a number of pests around the hot water tanks/booster heaters of the dish machine. There is a plumbing line traversing from the dish machine to the left wall. Pests are observed running the length of this pipe and accumulating around the warm equipment. Sentinel for pest control was just out today for service. Administrator called for additional service specifically to the dish machine area. The facility is asked to use chemical and other methods to deter and eliminate pests around the dish machine. THEN, use the glue traps to monitor around additional equipment in the kitchen to insure pests do not migrate to these locations.  Will return in two weeks to check on progress. Cleaning is not an apparent issue. Floors, walls, and ceilings are observed clean. 

The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Chlorine concentration was not measurable on the test strips after multiple cycles. PIC called the EcoLab technician and they are on the way to get the repair done. Ensure that the dish machine is dispensing sanitizer at a sufficient concentration to sanitize dishes (50-200ppm Cl). Facility will used the triple sink to sanitize the dishes in the meantime until the sanitizer pump in the dish machine is repaired.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed that the facility has Quat and Lactic Acid test strips available but they use Chlorine sanitizer (bleach). The inspector educated about the importance of using the correct type of test strip to ensure that sanitizer buckets are the proper concentration. The inspector had an extra package of Chlorine test strips which were provided to the facility during the inspection. The PIC will be purchasing more of the correct test strips as well. Ensure test kits are always available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: A pot of cooked potatoes was observed stored on the floor near the triple sink and next to a shelf that stores chemicals. Discussed with the PIC and the pot of potatoes were moved to a countertop. Food shall never be stored on the floor or near chemicals. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
comment: Potatoes stored in a pot on the floor were probed at 70F. The potatoes had been recently cooked and were in the process of cooling. The potatoes were placed in the cooler to finish completing the cooling process. Ensure that TCS foods that have been previously cooked are cooled properly and are cooled using approved cooling methods. Foods should be cooled from 135F to 70F within a 2 hour timeframe and from 70F to 41F (or below) within 4 hours.
citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the facility hot holding various food items in plastic containers such as but not limited to cheese sauces and gravies. Discussed with PIC that the containers are not approved to hold hot foods, nor are they sufficient enough to withstand repeat ware-washings. Instructed the facility to use stainless steel containers to hold hot foods. Ensure that materials used for hot holding are food safety approved, durable, and long lasting. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The surfaces above the drawer coolers and beneath the two flat top grills were observed with a significant amount of grease buildup. Discussed with PIC. Cleaning should occur as often as necessary to prevent buildup. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are clean and free up grease buildup.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The baffles of the hood system above the fryers were observed with a significant amount of grease buildup. SteamPower is scheduled to service the hood system every 6 months. The last service was October 2, 2024 and the next service is scheduled for April 2, 2025. Discussed with PIC that the facility should clean the baffles in house in between scheduled SteamPower visits due to the amount of frying that occurs. The baffles are able to be placed through the dish machine or manually cleaned in the triple sink. Ensure that baffles are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent grease accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: A cell phone was placed on the cutting board in the wait station area. The cell phone was removed by one of the employees. Ensure that cell phones are kept in designated places where they are not in direct contact with food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed the upper nozzles above the ground baskets on the coffee maker to have an accumulation of soils. Discussed with PIC. Ensure these nozzles are cleaned frequently enough to keep them clean to sight and touch. Inspector will return 03/21/2025 to follow-up on violation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of ice along the sides of the ice cream chest freezer next to the counter of the establishment. Discussed with PIC, and PIC stated that they defrost the machine regularly. Inspector recommends increasing the frequency of scheduled defrosting. Ensure the machine is defrosted regularly enough to render the inside surfaces smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Upon arrival at the facility and throughout the inspection, there was no CFPM present. Discussed with PIC and it was acknowledged that the two individuals with CFPM certification were out and won’t return till later. Ensure that at least one person with CFPM certification is present at all time during facility operation. [C]
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment:
Inspectors observed that the employees at the facility were missing the employee reporting paper work.
Discussed with PIC and PIC had no knowledge about the location (s) of the above paperwork. PIC mention that they were unsure whether the paperwork were available. Ensure that the relevant training and certification courses are completed by employees to remain compliant to the food code. [P]
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Inspectors observed an employee washing their hands and using their bare hands to dispense paper towel from the paper towel dispenser for hand drying. Inspectors educated PIC and the hand washing procedure was corrected. [P]
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The soap dispenser in the males’ bathroom was observed to be out of hand-soap. Discussed with PIC and the dispenser was refilled. Ensure that all available hands-sink that are actively being used are constantly checked and equipped with the relevant supplies. [P,Pf]
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Dishes and utensils were observed to have accumulated soil on the shelves. PIC was made aware of the accumulation of soils on the dishes and PIC ensured inspectors that they were going to get the utensils and dishes cleaned. Ensure that dishes and utensils are monitored and cleaned always. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/21/2025.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A few tongs and pizza spatula were observed to have accumulated soils and free hanging at the top of the pizza station. The was a spatula inserted in between an opening a the top of the shelf with accumulated soils and another pizza spatula that had been in used inserted in the gap as well. Items were moved to dish to correct. Ensure utensils are stored safely in a clean location.
citation_text: 4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

A gallon of milk in the front reach in cooler is observed without a date marking and with a manufacturers used by date of yesterday. PIC was shown and discarded the milk to correct.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Inspectors observed single use items being stored in a container that had accumulated food debris. Discussed with PIC and the Container was cleaned. Ensure that containers used to store single used items and accessories are routinely checked and cleaned to avoid contamination. [C]
citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
The following were observed to have been rusted.
1. The shelves in the walk-in freezer were observed to be rusted and containing the accumulation of soils on.
2. Inspectors observed rust on the shelves of the storage rack for the dishes and utensils.
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the shelves will be taken out and re-sealed to provide a smooth and easily cleanable surface. 
Ensure that these shelves and other food contact surfaces are regularly kept smooth and easily cleanable. 
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: The accumulation of mold and a leakage was observed at the bottom of the kitchen sink. There was visible sewage water dripping from the leak. PIC was made aware of the leakage and the mold accumulation. PIC ensured that it was going to get repaired. Ensure that sewage is disposed proper to avoid the growth of bacteria culture and ensure a sanitary environment.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The filter in the hood at the pizza oven was observed to have accumulated soils. Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured inspectors that the hood was scheduled to be cleaned.  Ensure that equipments are monitored cleaner at a regular frequency.
citation_text: 6-201.17(A) Walls and Ceilings, Attachments. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, attachments to walls and ceilings such as light fixtures, mechanical room ventilation system components, vent covers, wall mounted fans, decorative items, and other attachments shall be EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspectors observed a mop head being stored in dirty water, a mop head stored on the floor of the utility sink, and additional dirty water being stored in another mop bucked. PIC was made aware and the mope storage was corrected. Ensure that staffs are aware of proper mop storage. [C]
citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following were observed to obstruct cleaning. 
1. Inspectors observed broken floor tiles under the dish machine in the kitchen and in the hallway to the dry storage.
2. Inspectors observed the lack of coving in the back of the kitchen by the dish machine and the walls along the hallway to the dry storage and that of the back room used as a utility closet. 
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that floor junctures are repaired to provide smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
citation_text: 6-201.13(A) Floor and Wall Junctures, Coved, and Enclosed or Sealed. (A) In FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS in which cleaning methods other than water flushing are used for cleaning floors, the floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1 mm (one thirty-second inch).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The ventilation of the grill system was observed to been covered with cardboard that have absorbed grease over time. PIC stated that they used the cardboard to coverup the vent because their repair company stated that it would be difficult. Ensure that the cardboard is replaced with a more suitable covering to ensure that the grill system is in good repair.
citation_text: 6-201.17(A) Walls and Ceilings, Attachments. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, attachments to walls and ceilings such as light fixtures, mechanical room ventilation system components, vent covers, wall mounted fans, decorative items, and other attachments shall be EASILY CLEANABLE.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility is not compliant with the food handler law. Discussed  with PIC and PIC was not knowledgeable about whether the employee had valid food handler certifications. Ensure that employee handling foo acquire their food handler certifications. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Facility was observed to be out of compliance with food allergen awareness training. PIC was made aware and PIC had no knowledge of the possible location of the certification if any was available. Ensure that facility is compliant with this law. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: Observed that the PIC’s certified food protection manager (CFPM) certificate expired in February 2025. The PIC was reminded that someone with a CFPM certificate must be present during all hours of operation. Ensure that the PIC renews their CFPM certificate by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed that employee foods are being stored amongst foods for customers in the walk-in cooler and triple cooler. The personal foods currently stored intermixed with customer foods (including above or directly next to foods) pose the risk of contamination. The inspector suggests designating specific areas inside the coolers for personal storage. For example, the left side of the triple cooler or the bottom shelves in the walk-in cooler could be designated as personal storage. The PIC can choose whichever storage technique will work best for the facility as long as customer foods are being protected from contamination. Ensure that personal foods are always stored separate from customer foods to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed that the employee working food handler training is expired. The certificate posted in the kitchen pass through window expired in September 2022. The PIC was made aware and stated that the employee will be re-taking the certification. They were reminded that all employees who do not have a CFPM certificate must take the food handlers training. Ensure that the required employee renews their food handler certificate by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training expired in January 2025. The PIC was reminded that someone with an allergen certificate must be present during all hours of operation. Ensure that the PIC renews their allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Buttermilk observed in the cook-line prep cooler was out of date per the manufacturer’s label. PIC was informed and the buttermilk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff discarding any out of date items.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Shell eggs were observed to be stored in a prep cooler below raw beef slider patties. Raw eggs should be stored above raw ground meat, but below fresh produce and other ready-to-eat foods. PIC was informed of incorrect storage, and eggs were moved to the walk-in cooler. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Fourteen bottles of Simply brand orange juice were observed stored on an ambient shelf in dry storage. The bottles are marked “keep refrigerated,” and the Coca-Cola website states that the Simply branded juices contain no preservatives, and therefore require refrigeration at all times. Juices were discarded. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Peeled hard-boiled eggs were observed stored in water in both the prep cooler and walk-in cooler. Storing eggs in water presents an unnecessary risk of cross-contamination. PIC was informed that eggs should be kept in a food-safe container free of ice or water.
citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Two of the storage chest freezers upstairs have damage to the interior of the lid, creating cracks and crevices. Repair the cooler lids so the surface is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 4-202.16 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: The chest freezers upstairs were observed to be soiled with mold around the sides of the lids and lid seals. PIC was informed that chest freezers are in need of a deep clean. Ensure chest freezers are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent mold accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The flooring in the upstairs dry storage area was observed to be in disrepair. The floors are cracked, bubbled, and wearing thin. This makes it difficult to properly clean the floors, posing the risk of cross-contamination. Ensure floors are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The floors in the outdoor walk-in cooler were observed to be soiled with food debris. Ensure staff are cleaning floors of coolers often enough to avoid accumulation of food debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed sliced tomato in the walk-in cooler and prep cooler to be past its “discard by” date. The tomatoes in the walk-in were marked to be discarded on 3/10/2025, and the tomatoes in the prep cooler were marked to be discarded on 3/9/2025. The tomatoes were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking the date marking on all produce at the end of each day and discarding any out of date produce. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed spray bottle stored in chemical storage area to be filled with a clear liquid and no label. Informed PIC that all chemicals need to be clearly labeled to prevent toxin contamination of a food contact surface. PIC discarded contents of spray bottle. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: 2nd REPEAT: Food debris accumulation was observed inside drawer coolers and under-counter coolers. Clean non-food contact surfaces as often as needed to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
1) The dry storage shelving near the ice machine was observed to be soiled with dust and debris. 
2) The tea dispenser in the self-service drink area was observed to be soiled with dried tea. The tea dispenser itself seemed to have rust accumulation in the legs of the container. 
Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as often as needed to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed door and wall of walk-in cooler to be rusted and corroded. Rust and corrosion is not considered a smooth, easily cleanable surface, and is therefore at risk of cross-contamination. Ensure the walls and door of the walk-in cooler are repaired prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The flooring under the self-service soda dispenser was observed to be soiled with dust and debris. Ensure flooring is cleaned as often as necessary to avoid accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: The lights in the walk-in cooler were observed to be broken and missing their protective shielding. The shielding is necessary to avoid glass contaminating food items in the event that the light bulb were to shatter. PIC is aware of issue and plans to place a work order for the shields. Ensure the shielding is replaced prior to the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-202.11(A) Light Bulbs, Protective Shielding. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; or unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment:
1) A personal drink bottle was observed to be open on the top shelf above food items. 
2) A purse was also observed placed atop a plastic container holding food.
PIC was informed of these personal items and the items were moved. Ensure staff are using designated areas for personal items, food, and drinks to avoid cross-contamination with food or food-contact surfaces.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
Multiple food handler’s certificates for onsite employees were observed to be expired. PIC was informed that the certificates need to be renewed. Ensure all employees have a valid food handler’s certification prior to next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Repeat Violation

Observed hand sink in kitchen to be obstructed with paper towels and dish soap in sink basin. Informed PIC of issue, and items were removed from hand sink. Ensure hand sink is easily accessible at all times to promote frequent and proper hand washing. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed molded sliced tomato in prep cooler drawer. PIC was informed of unsafe food, and the tomatoes were discarded. To avoid serving unsafe food to the public, ensure cut produce is clearly date marked and discarded after 7 days. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed sanitizer spray bottle in the kitchen to “bleach out” test strip, indicating that the solution was too potent. PIC was informed that sanitizer was too strong, and the bottle was diluted. Ensure bleach sanitizer solutions are at an appropriate concentration to avoid toxicity. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed soda nozzles at the bar to be soiled. The drainage line and catch tube for the soda nozzles were also soiled and had mold growth. One of the catch tubes were clogged as well. PIC was informed of the issue and plans to use a designated brush to clean the catch tubes. A follow-up will be conducted on 3/20/2025 to ensure the soda nozzles and catch tubes have been cleaned.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed produce in prep cooler (tomato, lettuce, onion) and walk-in cooler (salads, creamer, milk) to have no date mark. Informed PIC that time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods that are considered ready-to-eat need to be date marked and discarded after 7 days. A follow-up has been scheduled for 3/20/2025 to ensure date marking compliance.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed hood in kitchen to be soiled dust and grease. Observed chest freezer in back storage area to be soiled with old food (french fries). Informed PIC that chest freezer and hood are in need of a cleaning. Routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces prevents cross-contamination with food and food-contact surfaces. Ensure that surfaces are clean for next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed floor of walk-in cooler to be soiled with food debris. Informed PIC that floor needed a cleaning. Keeping flooring in the facility clean not only prevents cross-contamination, but can prevent pest infestation as well. Ensure flooring is clean by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Observed dish machine in use following violation #16 from the inspection conducted on 3/6/25 being unresolved. The dish machine was out of temperature and inadequate for sanitization. It seems there is a lack of communication between the Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM) and the rest of the staff regarding necessary repairs and change of procedure. Ensure the dish staff is informed at all times regarding proper dish handling and sanitization as well as any changes to procedure. title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

All of the Allergen training certificates available at the facility have expired at the end of last year. The PIC was notified and instructed to have the current CFPMs retake the course/renew the certification.

They removed their gloves and went to grab new gloves. The inspector informed the employee that they must wash their hands before donning gloves. While hand washing, the employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. The inspector educated the PIC that a barrier must be used to turn off the faucet. The inspector proceeded to demonstrate the proper hand washing procedure for the employees in the kitchen and the PIC translated. Ensure that all employees always used the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed there were two coolers for cold holding foods at 14F or below during the inspection:

(1) The standing refrigerator was observed to malfunction distorting the temperature of various food items stored it. The following food items were discarded due to the refrigerator malfunction.
1. Cheese dips (9 containers) = 49-51F
2. Salsa = 49F
3. carnitas = 52F
4. Tamale =49.2F
5. Sheers cake (2 Containers)= 51F
6. Stuffed peppers = 48.7F
Discussed with PIC that the above items were to be discarded because they had been prepared 3/07/25 and place in the refrigerator from the preparation date. Four containers of beans were observed to have internal temperatures between 39-42F and were immediately moved into a functioning cooler. Ensure that equipments are routinely checked for temperature observation to avoid food spoilage.

(2) The prep cooler at the bar was not cold holding foods above 41F. The following temperatures were reordered:
1. Diced tomatoes 51F
2. Sour scream 55F
3. Guac 55F
The temperature-control for safety (TCS) foods inside the cooler (diced tomatoes, pico, sour cream, cheese, and ranch) were discarded during the inspection. The mango hot sauce was non-TCS and allowed to remain inside the cooler. The PIC will be using ice baths to keep TCS items inside the cooler below 41F or under. The PIC was instructed to check the temperature regularly to ensure that the ice baths are sufficient for cold holding. The PIC will be using ice baths until the cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.

 The PIC called and scheduled maintenance for tomorrow. The inspector will follow-up to check on the temperatures for both coolers on 3/14/2025. [P]
