title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed both hand sinks in kitchen as well as mop sink to not be properly sealed to wall. Ensure sinks are sealed to wall using a sealant such as caulking to avoid moisture retention between the sink and wall. Repairs should be completed prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed ventilation in bathroom to be inoperable and hanging from ceiling. Informed staff that bathrooms require adequate ventilation to keep room free of excessive vapors, obnoxious odors, fumes, and heat. Ensure ventilation is repairs prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-304.11 Mechanical. If necessary to keep rooms free of excessive heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes, mechanical ventilation of sufficient capacity shall be provided.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed employee drink without lid stored with food in dry storage room. Informed staff that a designated area is needed for employee drinks to avoid cross-contamination. Ensure a designated area is used for employee food/drink prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A scoop with a dirty handle was observed lying sideways in the sugar storage container. Discuss with PIC and the scoop was taken out to be cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are routinely monitored and cleaned to avoid contamination of food items. [Pf]
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: A bowl was observed containing shrimp in water thawing in the walk in refrigerator. Discuss with PIC and the thawing method was corrected. The Shrimp was received frozen and was put in the bowl of water and placed in the refrigerator to be thawed. Ensure that the adequate thawing methods are used for food items. [C]
citation_text: 3-303.12 Storage or Display of Food in Contact with Water or Ice. (A) PACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the FOOD is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water (B) Except as specified in (C) and (D) of this section, unPACKAGED FOOD may not be stored in direct contact with undrained ice. (C) Whole, raw fruits or vegetables; cut, raw vegetables such as celery or carrot sticks or cut potatoes; and tofu may be immersed in ice or water. (D) Raw poultry and raw FISH that are received immersed in ice in shipping containers may remain in that condition while in storage awaiting preparation, display, service, or sale.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soils. 
1. The exterior of the storage containers in the dry storage appeared to have an accumulation of soils. 
2. The accumulation of grease was observed on the top of the shelving on the grill.
3. The rice cooker table next to the fryer was observed to have an accumulation of grease build up on the sides and underneath.
4. The accumulation of ice buildup was observed in the sitting freezer at the entrance of the walk-in fridge.
Discuss with PIC and PIC noted that the above mentioned areas would be cleaned. Ensure that equipments in a facility are routinely monitored and cleaned to avoid the accumulation of soils. Make sure that food contact surfaces and non-food contact surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. [C]

6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

One of the sugar storage containers was observed broken. Discussed with PIC and the container will be replaced. Ensure that storage containers are continuously checked for possible repairs.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed heat-sanitizing dish machine to temp 157F after 5 passes with the dish puck. PIC was informed of the issue, and maintenance happened to be on site for  another repair. Dish staff prepared a triple sink, and the sanitizer was tested at 200ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure staff are using triple sink to sanitize until dish machine is repaired. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/17/2025 to ensure the dish machine is in working order with a temperature greater than 165F.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed 8 containers of cut vegetables in the salad bar cooler and 4 containers of cut vegetables on the salad bar itself to have date marking indicating the food items were past their acceptable serving date. PIC was informed that the containers were out of date, and all 12 containers were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff are checking date marks on produce containers at the start and end of each day and discarding away out-of-date items. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment: Observed floor drain in dish room to be overflowing. Dish machine is routed to floor drain, and drain overflows upon use of machine. PIC was informed of overflowing drain and plans to have a plumber inspect the drain. PIC stated that this issue is ongoing and has been using a drain snake “when the room floods.” A follow-up is scheduled for 3/10/2025 to ensure drain is operating properly.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: REPEAT: Cheese sauce dispensed from the Ortega dispenser was observed at 125F (probed). Several portion cups of cheese stored inside the dispenser were observed at 135F (probed). The bag of cheese inside the dispenser has a surface temperature of 135F as indicated using an infrared thermometer. Staff are going to change out the current dispenser for a new one already in the facility. Inspector will follow up tomorrow to see that the new dispenser is functioning properly.
citation_text: 3-501.16 (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Liquid egg and raw pork were observed to be stored above cabbage and potatoes. The egg had spilled onto the vegetables. CORRECTED- Discussed with the Person In Charge (PIC) who voluntarily discarded the vegetables. The storage order was rearranged to the appropriate standard, with raw proteins below vegetables and ready-to-eat foods. Ensure that food items are stored properly to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1)(a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: 1st REPEAT: The baffle of the ice machine was observed to have accumulated pink and black molds. Discussed with PIC, who said that they will have the machine cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are routinely monitored, cleaned, and always in adequate state to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The bar sanitizer bucket was observed low on concentration. The sanitizer dispenser also stopped working- an air bubble was observed not moving in the sanitizer hose. Discussed with PIC who reached out to their service provider. In the meantime, sanitizer will be mixed by hand and test strips will be used to ensure proper concentration. Ensure that all sanitizer buckets and solution meets the appropriate concentration as instructed by the label. [P]
citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling (200-400ppm). [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
A blue container with white powder (appeared to be flour) was observed in the dry storage. Discussed with PIC and the labeling of the substance was corrected. Ensure that all items such as white powders that are not easily identifiable are labeled properly.

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to have the accumulation of soils.
1. The floor drain area of the banquet room bar was observed to have an accumulation of soil.
2. The floor drain on the cookline, near the prep sink, was observed to have an accumulation of soil on the floor and the plumbing.
3. The heat lamp was observed to have an accumulation of soil coating.
4. The grill and fryers was observed to have an accumulation of soil and grease underneath and on the sides. 
5. The drain area of the tea machine station was observed to have an accumulation of slime mold.
PIC was made aware of the soil accumulation in the areas mentioned. PIC said that cleaning was schedule to happen soon. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned frequently enough to prevent soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
There were small containers of eggs and cartons of eggs that were observed to be stored above Frank’s Redhot Sauce in a dairy cooler. The facility was attempting to fill space due to a current egg shortage. CORRECTED- Educated PIC that raw eggs cannot be above Ready-to-Eat foods, such as the Frank’s Redhot Sauce. This storage order was corrected during the inspection. 

There was also meat from the meat department on a box of salmon in the cooler of the seafood department. CORRECTED- The meat was removed from the cooler and the operator was unsure why it was in the cooler. Educated PIC on proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: There was black soil residue accumulation on the sides of the ice machine in the seafood area. Discussed this with the PIC. A follow up is scheduled on 3/17/2025 to ensure that this has been cleaned. Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
The following food items were observed to be available for purchase past their sell by date: 

1. Multiple jugs of Prairie Farms Lactose Free Whole and Reduced Fat Milk dated sell by 3/5/2025. 
2. 4 containers of Oscar Meyer Chicken Breast lunch meat dated sell by 3/5/2025. 
3. 5 containers of Oscar Meyer Turkey Breast dated sell by 2/11/2025. 

All items were discarded and operator was educated on the importance of discarding food that is past its sell by date.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
The following walk-in cooler fans are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. All of the fans in the dairy cooler. 
2. The fans in the meat walk-in cooler. 

Ensure that these fans are cleaned and maintained cleaned. Nonfood contact surfaces should be kept free of an accumulation of debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The tiles under the seafood display cooler were observed to be coming loose. Ensure that these tiles are repaired to prevent pooling of debris or water under these tiles. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels observed to be at the handwashing sink in the kitchen of the deli area. CORRECTED- Paper towels were provided at this sink during the inspection. Discussed this with the PIC. Ensure that there are always paper towels at all handwashing sinks to allow for proper use of a barrier while turning off faucet during handwashing.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
REPEAT- The following areas throughout the deli are observed to need to be re-caulked: 

1. The horizontal triple sink inside the kitchen area. 
2. The triple sink outside the kitchen area. 
3. The handwashing sink outside of the kitchen. 

Ensure that these areas are re-caulked and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. The ice on the floor of the bakery walk-in cooler needs to be scraped off to allow the floor to be easily cleanable. The issue has been repaired but the ice is still present on the floor. 
2. The wall under and behind the triple sink inside the kitchen area of the deli. 
3. REPEAT- The floor under the triple sink in the prep area of the deli. 
4. The floor in the walk-in cooler of the deli. 
5. The floor in the prep area of the deli. 
6. The sliders of the deli coolers. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There was a bucket of used mop water that had a mop still in it observed to be in the deli area. Ensure that after use, mops are always hung to dry and the mop water is dumped. Used mop water can attract pests.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

A single set of frozen pizzas are observed in the display freezer with expiration dates of 2/26/25. The PIC discarded the items to correct. The PIC did state that they have been having issues with their supplier lately sending items that are past their expiration dates. Per the PIC these items are normally caught prior to being placed on the shelves but they have been off the past couple of days.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: The milk fridges in the rooms did not have a thermometer in them. CORRECTED- The PIC placed a thermometer in each unit. Ensure that all hot or cold holding units have a temperature measuring device placed in them.
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
The following items were observed to be stored improperly.
1. A jug of barbecue sauce made by Little Caesar was labeled to be refrigerated after opening was observed to be stored under the prep table.
2. Several bottles of Parmesan cheese were observed to be stored underneath the pizza prep table by the prep cooler. The packet of the Parmesan chess was labeled “refrigerate after opening” as a result of milk being a major ingredient. 
PIC was made aware and the jug of barbecue sauce was tossed in the trash. The Parmesan cheese was placed in the refrigerator as had been opened for less than 3 hours.
Ensure that label instructions of food items are carefully followed to avoid contamination. [P]
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Two containers of white powder were observed to be stored under the prep table.Discussed with PIC and the containers were labeled appropriately. Ensure that all secondary containers used for storage are labeled appropriately. [C]
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: A mop was observed to be stored improperly. Discussed with Person In Charge and the mop storage was corrected. Ensure that the adequate mop storage is used to avoid the growth of bacteria culture. [C]
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: A personal drink in a single used beverage container was observed to be store in the standing freezer by the prep table. PIC was made aware of the personal drink storage and the drink was taken away. Ensure that storage location for person items are designated to avoid contamination. [C]
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The baffle of the ice machine was observed to have an accumulation of pink and black molds on its surface. Discussed with PIC and an employee was instructed to note the location when cleaning the ice machine. Ensure that this item is observed and cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean and sanitized.[P]
citation_text: 4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (1) Except as specified in (B) of this section, before each use with a different type of raw animal FOOD such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, or POULTRY; (2) Each time there is a change from working with raw FOODS to working with READY-TO-EAT FOODS; (3) Between uses with raw fruits and vegetables and with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD; (4) Before using or storing a FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE; and (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: A packet of shrimp was observed in a bowl of water at the top of the triple sink to be thawed. PIC was made aware of appropriate thawing methods. The bowl with the shrimp was placed under running water for appropriate thawing. Ensure that staffs are aware of the adequate thawing methods to avoid the contamination of food items. [Pf]
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: A live roach was observed under the hand sink at the end of the cook line. PIC was made aware f the presence of pest and PIC ensured that a pest control company was going to be called to handle the presence of pest. Ensure that facility is routinely checked for pest presence and activities. [C]
citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following areas were observed to indicate the accumulation of soils and food debris.
1. Accumulated grease under the grill and oven on the cook-line.
2. Food debris under the prep cooler across from the cook-line
3. The walk-in freezer was observed to have spilled food debris on the floor. 
Discussed with PIC and PIC ensured that adequate cleaning will be done. Ensure that these areas are cleaned to remove their current buildup of residues and that surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. [C]
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

The facility did not have verifiable information of employee’s responsibility to report foodborne illness symptoms and diagnosis. Multiple copies of the reporting agreements given by SCDPH are observed blank in the paperwork binder. The PIC is instructed to make copies and have all food handlers sign a copy prior to the follow up. 10 days lands on a Saturday, the follow-up will be conducted on the following Monday.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment:
(REPEAT from the pre-opening) 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There is a gap observed at the bottom right corner of the back door. Repair the door to ensure that the gap is removed to prevent possible entrance of pests. Ensure that all outer openings of the facility seal.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple containers of foods in the walk in cooler are observed without lids or other coverings. Education was conducted and the PIC instructed to maintain foods covered when not in use. Ensure that all foods have coverings moving forward.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

On arrival multiple moist rags are observed on the counters in the kitchen. Rags are being used for wiping of counters and equipment. Education was conducted and the rags moved to newly provided buckets with a quat based sanitizer to correct. Ensure that sani rags are stored between uses in a sanitizer solution.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

On arrival the facility indicated that they were using an alcohol based sanitizer for their front prep surfaces. They do not currently have a test strip for this chemical. It should not be used in the food areas without a test strip available. Education was conducted and the bottle changed for a bucket with a quat based sanitizer to correct.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival the facility did not have a sanitizer ready for use in the main part of the kitchen. A bucket with a quat based sanitizer was produced during this inspection to correct the violation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT from the pre-opening) 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) Seal holes in walls with silicon caulking. 2) Floor cover for floor drain right of the dish machine. 3) Replace cracked light shield in dry storage.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing during the inspection. The PIC was informed of the violation and instructed to educate employees about the proper hand washing procedure. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed a pizza pan stored behind the faucet of the triple sink during the inspection. The PIC was educated that the pan could be contaminated by water splashes or food debris in this position. After education the PIC moved the pizza pan into a new location. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always stored in a position that allows them to remain clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the following improper use of scoops: (1) The scoop in the salt bin does not have a handle; (2) The scoop in the sugar bin is stored with the handle in contact with the sugar; and (3) The ice scoop in the ice bin under the soda dispenser is stored with the handle in contact with the ice. The PIC was reminded that scoops must be stored with the handles above the top of foods to avoid contamination. Ensure that all ready-to-eat foods have scoops with handles that are stored properly by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed there was not a sanitizer bucket available when the inspector arrived. An employee made a sanitizer bucket (testing at the correct concentration) during the inspection. The PIC was educated that sanitizer buckets must always be available to clean food contact surfaces. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observe there are two small holes in the wall above the pizza station where a hook was moved. The PIC was educated that walls must always be smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. Ensure that the holes are sealed (ex. caulking) by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Food handler training
comment:
THIS IS A REPAT VIOLATION: Observed that not all employees have completed the food handler training. The PIC was educated that all employees who do not have a CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must have food handler certificates. Ensure that all required employees complete the food handler training and copies of the certificates are kept at the facility by the next routine inspection. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

comment:

All employees who do not have the CFPM (certified food protection manager) certificate must complete basic food handler training. Ensure that all employees have food handler certificates by the next routine inspection.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed a wet wiping cloth drying on the basin of the triple sink when the inspector arrived. The inspector educated that wet wiping cloths must be stored in chemical sanitizer between uses. The PIC placed the wet wiping cloth in the laundry basket during the inspection. Ensure that wet wiping cloths are always stored in chemical sanitizer solution between uses and laundered daily.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

comment:

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed there is an accumulation of grease on the sides of the fryers, the floor under the fryers, the wall behind the fryers, and on the hood system above the fryers. The drips forming on the hood system above the fryers pose the risk of contaminating food cooking underneath. The PIC was instructed to clean around, underneath, and above the fryers at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of grease. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are kept free of grease deposits and other soil accumulations by the next routine inspection.
citation_text:
4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking 
EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the unused cooler across from the ice machine has an accumulation of food debris inside. The PIC was educated that equipment (even those currently not being used) must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of food debris. The inside of the cooler was cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are kept free of accumulations of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed there are holes in the wall above the mop sink and the ice machine that must be sealed. The holes can be sealed using caulking or another method that creates smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. Ensure that the holes are sealed by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment:
Repeat

A cook staff employee was observed handling fried foods on pass-through with bare hands. The fries and fried shrimp fell from the plate onto the pass-through surface, and the employee picked up the food items and placed them back on the plate with bare hands. PIC was informed of issue, and will re-educate staff. Ensure staff members are both handwashing and donning gloves prior to handling ready-to-eat (RTE) foods. A second follow-up will be conducted on 3/7/25 to ensure proper food handling is being conducted in the facility.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee fail to use a barrier when turning off the hand sink. Inspector interrupted the employee and provided education regarding handwashing procedure and barrier use. Advised PIC to educate employees on proper handwashing. Ensure a clean barrier such as a paper towel is used when turning off the hand sink.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed a sanitizer bucket stored in the prep line hand sink upon arrival. Also observed a plastic container stored in the back hand sink. Informed PIC that hand sinks cannot be used for any purpose aside from hand washing. PIC removed both containers from the handsink basins. Ensure staff are filling sanitizer and using containers in designated sinks rather than hand sinks.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine was observed with no measurable chlorine concentration. PIC was informed of the issue, and the triple sink was prepared for sanitizing as an alternative. PIC also scheduled service on the dish machine. Ensure staff are using triple sink to sanitize until the dish machine is repaired. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/7/2025 to ensure that the dish machine has been repaired.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).  [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Coleslaw stored on prep table in ice bath was observed at 55F (probed). The ice in the ice bath had melted, and was no longer sufficient. PIC was informed of out-of-temperature coleslaw and the item was discarded and replaced. The ice in the bath was replenished as well. Ensure that the ice bath is monitored with enough frequency to ensure the coleslaw is held at a temperature of 41F or lower at all times. Time as a control may be used as an alternative. Using time as a control, coleslaw could be kept on the counter at any temperature as long as it is used or discarded within 4 hours. A form will need to be completed with the Sangamon County Department of Public Health to enact time as a control for this item.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
Brownies stored by the cash register were observed without any labeling. Informed PIC that all foods packaged in the establishment need to be clearly labeled with the common name of the food, name of the establishment, and the ingredients of the product (preferably in descending order by weight). Ensure employees are placing labels on the brownies before presenting them to the public. 

3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed two sanitizer buckets to measure at 0ppm lactic acid. PIC was informed that sanitizer buckets were not correct, and PIC created new buckets. The new buckets tested at 700ppm lactic acid. Ensure sanitizer buckets are strong enough to properly sanitize food-contact surfaces and prevent food-borne illness transmission.
citation_text: 4-501.114(D) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (D) If another solution of a chemical specified under (A) - (C) of this section is used, the PERMIT HOLDER shall demonstrate to the REGULATORY AUTHORITY that the solution achieves SANITIZATION and the use of the solution shall be APPROVED.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
Repeat

Observed dish machine to only reach 151F after multiple attempts with the dish puck. The minimum temperature for proper sanitization is 165F. PIC has already placed a work order with Ecolab to have the dish machine serviced. Ensure for the time being that a sanitizer is prepared in the triple sink and all dishes are sanitized in the sink rather than the dishwasher. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/13/25 to ensure the dish machine has been repaired.
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed plates in service line to be soiled with food debris. Observed bowls stored on shelves in service line with food-contact surfaces and exposed to potential contamination. Informed PIC that plates were soiled and bowls need to be inverted or covered to protect food-contact surface. PIC removed soiled plates and inverted bowls. Violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed seal of standing cooler to be cracked and damaged. Observed shelving in walk-in cooler to be rusted and damaged. Informed PIC of damage. Ensure equipment is in good repair to promote proper cleaning and cold-holding.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled with dust/debris:
1. Containers holding clean utensils - REPEAT
2. Egg grill
3. Cook-line freezer
4. Biscuit pass-through warmer
5. Hood baffles above grills

Informed PIC that these surfaces must be cleaned frequently to avoid cross-contamination with food or food-contact surfaces. Ensure these surfaces are cleaned by next routine inspection.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed walls near server area, dish area, and mop sink area to have small holes. Informed PIC that walls should be maintained in good repair to avoid accumulation of soil. Ensure walls are repaired prior to next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following areas to be soiled with food debris/soil:
1. Floor below flour storage
2. Floor under ice machines
3. Floor of walk-in freezer
4. Floor of walk-in cooler

Informed PIC that these areas are in need of a deep clean. Soil accumulation can promote both food-borne pathogen growth as well as potential pest harborage. Ensure floors in facility are cleaned frequently to avoid soil accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Repeat

Observed mop to be stored in mop bucket. Informed PIC that mop heads should be hanging such that they can effectively air-dry. Proper mop drying prevents bacterial growth and cross-contamination. PIC moved mop to hanger, so violation is considered corrected on site.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
Repeat
Observed raw chicken stored above raw fish as well as raw beef stored over cottage cheese. These are the same storage order violations observed during the previous routine inspection. Informed PIC that raw fish must be stored above raw chicken due to fish’s lower cook temperature. Any raw meat must be stored below ready-to-eat (RTE) foods such as dairy products and sauces. All storage order violations were corrected on-site. Storage order will be spot-checked during the scheduled follow-up on 3/12/25.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment:
Repeat 
Observed multiple items to be missing date marking (deli meats in prep cooler, cut vegetables and cooked meat in walk-in cooler). PIC was informed that any time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food stored in refrigeration for more than 24 hours needs to be properly date-marked and discarded after 7 days of retention. PIC placed labels on all required foods in prep cooler and walk-in during spot check. A follow-up will be conducted in 10 days (3/12/2025) to ensure that proper date marking is being followed.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed a can of green beans being heated on a gas cook stove in its original packaging. Informed PIC that the can the green beans are packaged in is not a proper cooking utensil. The green beans were transferred to an appropriate vessel (metal pan) to complete its cooking. Violation is considered corrected on site.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed several times during the inspection employees did not wash hands before donning gloves or switching gloves. The PIC was informed that hands must be washed using the proper hand washing procedure before donning gloves. The inspector will follow-up on 3/6/2025 to ensure that employees are washing hands before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed the following foods stored in the incorrect storage order: (1) Raw chicken stored above raw steak in the triple cooler; and (2) Raw ground beef stored above bread, potatoes, and onions in the walk-in cooler. During the inspection the raw chicken was moved below the raw steak in the triple cooler and the raw ground beef was moved below all ready-to-eat foods in the walk-in cooler. The PIC was reminded that all raw foods must be stored below all ready-to-eat foods and raw meats must be stored according to their internal cooking temperatures. The PIC will follow-up on storage order on 3/6/2025.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed a cutting board stored behind the faucet of the triple sink. The PIC was educated that the cutting board could become contaminated by dirty water splashes or food debris in this position. The PIC removed the cutting board from behind the faucet and placed in a new location during the inspection. Ensure that the cutting board is always stored in a position that does not pose the risk of contamination to ensure that it remains clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the steam table was not holding foods at 135F or above. The steam table had an internal temperature of 122F in the front, 114F in the middle, and 112F in the back. The inspector noticed that the knob was turned on a low setting. After being informed the PIC turned up the steam table to a higher setting. When the inspector re-checked the internal temperatures at the end of the inspection they were at 142F in the front, 149F in the middle, and 150F in the back. The PIC was reminded to check the temperatures of the steam table on a regular basis. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods hot holding are always maintained at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: THIS IS A THREE TIMES REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed several temperature controlled for safety (TCS), ready-to-eat foods at the facility for longer than 24 hours were not date marked: (1) Desserts (candy covered grapes, cheesecake, and banana pudding) in the clear triple cooler; (2) Several large containers of par-cooked chicken wings in the stacked double cooler; (3) Containers of cut onions and tomatoes, shredded lettuce, cooked rice, and par-cooked chicken wings in the triple cooler; (4) Cooked gyro meat in the prep cooler bottom; and (5) Several large containers of par-cooked chicken wings in the walk-in cooler. The PIC stated that all the above referenced foods had been inside the coolers since at least yesterday (therefore over 24 hours). The PIC date marked all the foods during the inspection. The inspector educated that all temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods held at the establishment longer than 24 hours must be date marked. The inspector will follow-up on 3/13/2025 to ensure that all required foods are date marked.
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed that the bleach at the facility does not have an EPA registration. The inspector discussed the importance of using food contact surface sanitizing bleach in the facility. The inspector will follow-up on 3/6/2025 to ensure that the facility has bleach with an EPA registration.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed a container of raw beef was thawing in a container of water at room temperature when the inspector arrived. The PIC was educated that foods thawed using water must be thawed under continuous running water. The PIC placed the container holding the raw meat under continuous water in the triple sink during the inspection. The PIC was reminded of the approved thawing methods: (1) Within a cooler at 41F or below; (2) Under continuous running water; (3) As part of the cooking process; or (4) In the microwave. Ensure that foods are always thawed according to an approved method.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. comment: Baked potatoes stored in the heat and serve cooler (floor cooler) were observed without date marking. A label was created with the correct use-by-date. Ensure that cooked and cooled items served for grab-and-go service are date marked and never held for longer than 7 days.

The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.

Observed staff member touch lobster and potatoes on plate with bare hands and serve plate. Observed staff member pick up garnish (kale) with bare hands and place on plate. Staff member was interrupted and asked to use gloves; staff member discarded garnish and donned gloves to finish the plate. Informed PIC that bare-handing ready-to-eat (RTE) foods is a direct threat to food-borne pathogen transmission. PIC will educate staff on proper food handling procedures and the importance of wearing gloves anytime they are handling RTE foods. A follow-up is scheduled for 3/4/25 to ensure staff are using gloves to handle RTE foods.

Mold and debris on the surfaces of the ice machine can contaminate ice, resulting in food-borne pathogen transmission.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed dirty mop bucket to be kept in facility over night. Discussed with PIC, bucket will disposed of. Ensure staff is properly disposing of mop water after mopping.
citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Hand washing should be taking place regularly and consistently during food operations, and specifically prior to donning gloves and when changing tasks. Education was conducted and hand washing will be re-evaluated at the follow up in 10 days.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple plastic tubs are observed with sticker residue that has not been completely cleaned. They appear to have not been cleaned for multiple uses. Clean these items completely prior to use. The cleaning of food contact itmes will be evaluated again at the follow up in 10 days.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the left hand washing sink (closest to the sushi station) in the deli did not have paper towels when the inspector arrived. The inspector educated the deli PIC on the importance of having paper towels available for the proper hand washing procedure. The deli PIC re-filled the paper towel dispenser during the inspection. Ensure there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
The following improper hand washing sink uses were observed during the inspection: 

(1) Observed multiple deli employees dumping buckets into hand washing sinks. The inspector educated the deli PIC about the importance of dumping liquids into the designated dump sink not hand washing sinks. 
(2) Observed a meat department employee filling up a sanitizer bucket in the hand washing sink. The employee was educated when the action was observed and they filled the remainder of the bucket in the triple sink. 

Both of the department PIC’s were instructed to educate employees on the proper hand sink usage to ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed that portions of the salad bar are not holding food temperatures at 41F or below. The side closest to the coffee station is holding all foods at 41F or below. The opposite side (closest to the hot wing station) is not holding all temperatures at 41F of below. The areas not holding food at the proper temperature are from the far left side all the way to the lettuce. The following internal temperatures were recorded: chicken 55F, lettuce 50F, green peppers 53F, cheese 54F, and ham 55F. The deli PIC and store manger were instructed to use time-as-control for the temperature control for safety (TCS) foods in the cooler. The foods being temperature controlled are lettuce, mozzarella cheese, blue cheese, feta cheese, chicken, ham, turkey, crab, and eggs. The rest of the non-TCS foods are allowed to remain in the cooler all day. Since all foods had been put into the salad cooler at 9 am they were instructed to discarded all TCS foods at 1 pm. The salad bar only stays open until 4 pm, so all TCS foods will be discarded again when the salad bar closes. The deli PIC will be overseeing that time-as-control is correctly implemented. The store manager stated they will be scheduling maintenance for the salad cooler as soon as possible. Time-as-control must be used for all TCS foods until the salad cooler is properly functioning. The inspector will follow-up on 3/3/2025 to ensure that the salad cooler is cold holding all foods at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed that the deli and meat department did not have sanitizer buckets available when the inspector arrived. Both PIC’s of the departments were educated that sanitizer buckets must be available during all hours of operation. Sanitizer buckets were filled in the deli and meat department during the inspection. Ensure that there is always saniztier available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed that the floors underneath the fryers in the deli have an accumulation of food debris and grease. The PIC was instructed to pull out the equipment and deep clean underneath the fryers by the next routine inspection. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed the facility has chlorine test strips available but they use quat sanitizer. The inspector explained the importance of using the correct test strips to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions. The PIC asked the deli manager to use their quat test strips until they are able to purchase the correct type (the sushi station is directly adjacent to the deli). The deli manager agreed and showed the PIC where the test strips are stored. Ensure that there are always test strips available to accurately measure the concentration of sanitizing solutions.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

During this inspection there was no verification for responsibility to report for employees. The PIC found blank copies of the Sangamon County Reporting Agreements in their office that had been intended for this purpose. They need to have signed copies for this prior to the follow up scheduled for 10 days.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple pots, pans and utensils throughout the facility are observed to be stored “clean” and have food debris and sticker residue remaining on them. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-washing. Education has been done with the PIC and the dish washer educated as well. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are fully cleaned prior to storage.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. 

1) Two containers of yogurt in the walk in cooler are observed with use by dates that have been passed. Items expired in January 2025 and November of 2024. These items were discarded during the inspection to correct. 2) A mayonnaise based sauce in the walk in cooler is without date marking. The PIC indicated that it was from more than 7 days ago and discarded it to correct the violation. 3) RTE shrimp is observed in the walk in cooler, out of its packaging and without date marking. The PIC was shown and placed a date on it to correct. It had been opened 2 days prior to inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Ensure the following physical facilities are maintained in good repair:

(1) The holes in the wall behind the triple sink and hand washing sink outside the employee bathroom must be sealed (ex.caulking). 
(2) The foam caulking on the baseboards at the downstairs bar that is bubbled must be cut flush to the wall and pained/sealed. 
(3) The gap between the stainless steel wall and wood frame behind the dry storage tubs in the main kitchen must be sealed/repaired.
(4) The broken piece of plastic on the lid of the ice machine must be sealed/repaired. 
(5) The ends of the dry storage selves that have peeling paint must be sealed (ex.repainted). 
(6) The water damage on the ceiling of the employee bathroom must be repaired. 

Ensure that all physical facilities are repaired to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: A food employee was observed washing their hands at the 3 compartment sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who then spoke to the employee. The employee rewashed their hands at the designated handwashing sink. Ensure hands are washed at designated handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 2-301.15 FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Raw chicken was observed stored above vegetables in the walk-in cooler. Broccoli was observed stored below raw shrimp in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC rearranged storage so broccoli was not under raw animal proteins. Raw chicken was moved to storage on the bottom shelf, below all other foods. Ensure vegetables are stored above raw animal proteins.
citation_text: 3-302.11 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The kitchen sanitizer bucket was observed with no measurable chlorine concentration. CORRECTED- An employee remade the sanitizer bucket, which was then observed at 200ppm Cl. Ensure sanitizer buckets have 50-200ppm Cl and are changed regularly as they become soiled or sanitizer dissipates.
citation_text: 4-501.114 (A) A chlorine solution shall have a concentration of 50-200ppm. [P]

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Three live and several more dead cockroaches were observed on the cookline. Enlist pest control service and deep clean the kitchen. Use glue traps to monitor and identify active areas.
citation_text: 6-501.111 The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions. [C]

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: 1st REPEAT: The gaskets on the 2 door cooler near the back door are duct-taped on. Replace the gaskets so they are fully attached as intended.
citation_text: 4-501.11 (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

citation_text: 4-601.11 (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
