comment: A piece of trim tile is missing along the wall into the cookline. Replace the trim tile.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: There wasn’t a Certified Food Protection Manager present at the start of the inspection. Shortly afterwards, a CFPM arrived. Ensure that there is a CFPM present all hours of operation. There should be at least 2 employees that are food manager certified.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(A) Observed staff to don gloves without handwashing. Tasks were being changed and hair was touched. Discussed hand washing during the inspection with multiple staffers. Facility may benefit from revisiting hand washing as part of the onboarding education for new employees. See that hands are washed when changing tasks and at any other appropriate time. 


Cleaning Procedure. title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Observed an employee handling raw red onion that will not have a cook step prior to use with bare hands. Without provocation, employee donned gloves. Educated staff on proper hand washing and glove use. Make sure that gloves are always worn when handling ready-to-eat foods. 

Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

 Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.

- Can opener
- Meat slicer and Fry cutter

 Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed that the temperatures from multiple coolers on the cook-line were too high. Since they were in the middle of their lunch rush, we waited approximately 30 minutes after advising cook staff to keep covers closed on coolers to re-probe food. Some food items chilled to an appropriate temperature in that time. The food items that were still too hot are listed below : 
1. Dairy-based sauces (53F) - Broiler prep cooler top
2. Mayo (52F) - Broiler prep cooler top
3. Cut tomatoes (49F) - Broiler prep cooler top
4. Cut lettuce (50F) - Broiler prep cooler top
5. Bleu cheese (50F) - Broiler prep cooler top
6. Whipped cream (54F) - Dessert prep cooler
7. Chicken (50F) - Dessert prep cooler

All food items listed above were voluntarily discarded by the PIC. The broiler prep cooler was directly across from multiple operating broilers, and the area was very hot. Advised PIC to swap from temperature control to time as a control for time/temperature control (TCS) foods in that cooler. Cook staff already have an effective time keeping system in place for time as a control monitoring/labeling. Items in dessert cooler were advised to be placed in another cooler that holds temp more effectively, as those two food items are the only TCS foods stored there. The bottom of both coolers were well cooled (~35F), so advised cook staff to keep covers on cooler tops closed as frequently as possible to retain refrigeration. Inspector will perform a spot-check on 2/26/25 to ensure time as a control is being implemented correctly and remaining TCS foods in coolers are being maintained at the appropriate temperatures (less than 41F).

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment:
Observed the following food items in the salad bar to be out of the appropriate temperature range : 
1. Sliced tomato (54F)
2. Cooked chicken (52F)
3. Sliced cucumber (51F)
4. Cut lettuce (41F)
5. Shredded cheese (high-moisture, 49F)
6. Ranch, 7 bottles (49-52F)
7. Italian dressing (52F)
8. French dressing (53F)
9. Fat-free ranch (52F)

All of these temperatures were measured with a probe thermometer. The cut tomato, shredded cheese, chicken, and salad dressings (original package labeled “refrigerate after opening”) were voluntarily discarded. The cut lettuce, since the temperature was at the safety threshold, was placed back into the walk-in cooler to ensure safe cold holding until lunch. Non-TCS foods were allowed to remain in the salad bar cooler.  The food had been in the salad bar cooler since 9am, and failed to reach a safe temperature. Lunch is served from 11am-1:30pm, so time as a control will be utilized for the new salad bar items. These items will be discarded again after lunch. PIC was informed that TCS foods can only be kept out of temp for a maximum of 4 hours and must be discarded after use. PIC was reminded that a time log must be maintained to record what time foods must be discarded after being placed on the salad bar.  PIC will be using time as a control until the salad bar cooler is repaired and can maintain foods at a temperature of 41F or below. For more information regarding the salad bar cooler, see violation #33.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed small holes in wall next to door in ware-washing room. Also observed triple sink and tables to the left and right of the dishwashing machine in ware-washing room needs to be sealed to the wall (ex. caulking). Ensure this areas are sealed by the next routine inspection.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment:
(REPEAT x3) 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

A Certified Food Protection Manager is not available at this facility during this inspection This is the fourth inspection in a row where this violation has been noted. Ensure that there are sufficient CFPM’s so that there is one at the facility at all times that food handling and handling of food contact surfaces is taking place.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the proper cleaning procedure in order to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms.

Multiple hand washing procedures are observed throughout the inspection where the employee used their bare hands to turn off the faucet at the end of hand washing. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with all employees and ensure that proper hand washing is taking place at all times moving forward.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) Multiple tea jugs in the standing coolers next to the drive thru window are observed with sticker residue and other debris still remaining on the containers. 2) The blender jugs next to the drive thru window are observed soiled after cleaning. Two of the containers had debris floating in the water at the bottom of the container and the third had what appears to be berry juice on it. The PIC was shown and the items moved to dish for re-cleaning. More thorough cleaning of these items should be taking place between uses.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple moist rags are observed on counters in the facility. Education was conducted and the rags moved back to sani buckets to correct. Ensure that all wiping cloths are stored between uses in solution of sufficient concentration.

citation_text:

(A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Education was conducted and the PIC moved the container to dish for cleaning. The current batch of plugs were discarded. 2) Stacks of to-go containers are on a shelf above the steam table with the food contact surfaces facing up/exposed. This was discussed with he PIC and the items flipped over to correct. Ensure that all single service food contact surfaces are protected from contamination at all times.

citation_text:
6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

comment:
Observed no allergen training to be completed by certified food managers. Discussed with PIC, managers will complete allergen training. Ensure all certified food managers have completed the required allergen training and copies are kept within facility. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed no food handlers license to be present within facility. PIC was unable to provide proof of food handler’s certificates for all employees. Ensure all food handling employees have at least a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

Multiple utensils and pans in the dish room have been washed and put up without being completely cleaned. Food debris is still observed on each of them. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean these items again and to ensure that all food contact surfaces are completely cleaned prior to storage. All items were moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Observed RTE eat foods (sour cream, cottage cheese) to be dated according to expiration date on original packaging. Advised PIC that RTE foods transferred into new packaging must be dated to reflect 7 days following the opening of the original container. Dates were adjusted during this inspection to correct.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Observed cloths in-use for wiping food contact surfaces stored moist and on prep tables. Advised PIC that cloths must be stored in their sanitizer buckets between uses. This ensures that the cloth is clean and without potential contamination before each use. Cook staff placed in-use cloths to their sanitizer buckets during inspection.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Observed single-use utensils to be stored in metal tubs which were contaminated with dust and food debris. Observed single-use condiment cups to be stored with food contact surfaces exposed or without adequate coverings to protect from dust/debris contamination. Observed large sharpies to be in a container with plastic spoons. Advised PIC to keep containers holding single-use utensils clean and to keep single-use food contact surfaces covered or inverted on a clean surface such as the bottom of a container or clean work surface. Containers holding single-use utensils were washed and contaminated utensils were disposed of during inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Observed shelf of kitchen pass-through to be damaged (cleanable coating lifting from wood shelf). Observed 3-part sink in dishwashing room to have gaps between the sink and wall. Advised PIC to fix these areas such that the surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable. Any gaps/cracks/crevices on surfaces can harbor bacteria and other pathogens.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment:
Observed the following improper hand washing sink usage during the inspection:

(1) During the inspection an employee was observed washing the soda dispenser holder in the hand washing sink by the dish machine. When the action was observed the employee was educated that hand washing sinks cannot be used for any purpose other than hand washing.

(2) The inspector observed dumped ice in the bar hand washing sink. The PIC was reminded that hand sinks can only be used for hand washing. The bar currently has two sinks designated as hand washing sinks directly across from each other. The inspector suggests designating only one as the hand sink and using the other as a dump sink to avoid improper use. The sink that will not be used for hand washing must have the ‘employees must wash hands before returning to work’ signage removed.

Ensure that hand washing sinks are never used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed caulking to the left of the dish washing machine is a dark black color and deteriorating. This portion of the dish washing area experiences a high level of moisture from the rinsing nozzle. The calking must be removed and replaced when it starts to show signs of deterioration from moisture. Ensure that the caulking is replaced to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed there is an accumulation of ice inside the walk-in freezer underneath the fan and on the ceiling. The ice is also dripping onto the boxes of food underneath. The inspector suggests scheduling a defrost or contacting repair personal. Ensure that inside the walk-in freezer is smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the ice scoop holder at the right service station had an accumulation of soil residues. The ice scoop holder was removed and washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
comment: At the start of the inspection, there wasn't a Certified Food Protection Manager available at the facility. Suggested to PIC to get more individuals manager certified. Ensure that a CFPM is present to cover all hours of operation.
citation_text: 2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The sanitizer bucket in the bar area tested at 0ppm (CL). The bucket contained soap and water. The bucket was re-prepared and bleach was added to the solution (tested at 100ppm CL). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize surfaces.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine’s sanitizer concentration tested at 0ppm (CL). PIC contacted a technician to service the machine. The facility was instructed to use the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the machine is functioning properly. Ensure that the dish machine is testing at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to sanitize dishes correctly.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: There wasn't any light inside of the sushi prep cooler. Discussed with PIC the need for lighting inside of the cooler. Ensure that lighting is provided to all refrigerator units.
citation_text: 6-303.11(B) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (B) At least 215 lux (20 foot candles): (1) At a surface where FOOD is provided for CONSUMER self-service such as buffets and salad bars or where fresh produce or PACKAGED FOODS are sold or offered for consumption, (2) Inside EQUIPMENT such as reach-in and under-counter refrigerators; and (3) At a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor in areas used for handwashing, WAREWASHING, and EQUIPMENT and UTENSIL storage, and in toilet rooms.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility could not produce food handler certificates for cooks. Employees who are not manager certified must obtain a food handler’s certification if handling food.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed bar dish machine to test at 0 ppm CL. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will get serviced. Any dish washing needing to be done at the bar will now be done at the kitchen dish machine. Ensure sanitizing dish machines are testing at least at 50 ppm CL.
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed walk in freezer fan unit to have significant ice accumulation present. Discussed with PIC, fan unit will be serviced. Ensure equipment is working to meet manufacturer’s standards.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be present at bar. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure both kitchen and bar both have sanitizer solutions available at the proper concentration.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed kitchen dish machine to be soiled with food debris on top. Discussed with PIC, dish machine will be cleaned. Ensure staff is cleaning dish machine at a frequency that prevents food accumulation.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed a mop to be resting in dirty mop water. Discussed with PIC, mop water will be dumped and mop was placed in strainer part of bucket. Ensure mop water is being disposed of properly and that mops are being hung to dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed caulking to be in a state of disrepair at the following locations:
1) The front hand sink.
2) The back drain sink.
3) The back hand sink.

Discussed with PIC, caulking will get replaced. Ensure facility is checking caulking at a frequency that prevents mold accumulation.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed to leave the kitchen wearing gloves, retrieve soap, place it at the handsink, and return to handling clean dishes without removing/changing gloves or washing hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PICs, who will review handwashing with employees. Employees must wash hands after any activity that may have contaminated hands (such as leaving the kitchen), and before handling clean equipment and utensils.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: No soap was available at the front handwashing sink upon inspectors arrival. Upon request, an employee provided soap to the handsink. Ensure soap is always available at all handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Sanitizer buckets throughout the facility were observed with no measurable quat concentration. Upon further investigation, it was determined that sanitizer is not being dispensed from the wall-mounted dispenser at the proper concentration. Staff will mix sanitizer by hand and use test strips to check concentration until the wall-mounted dispenser is fixed. Use test strips regularly to monitor sanitizer concentrations. Inspector will follow up to verify that the wall-mounted dispenser has been repaired and is functioning properly.
citation_text: 4-501.114 (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall have a concentration of 200-400ppm as indicated on the manufacturer’s label. [P]

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Muffins and scones were observed prepackaged on the service counter without any labeling present. Ensure foods that are prepackaged in advance of sale are labeled with the information below.
citation_text: 3-602.11 (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; and (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Small portion cups of loose leaf tea, sealed tea bags, and containers of chai are stored under the barista prep/rinse sink. Store foods away from potential sources of contamination. Discussed storage in other cabinets or in plastic containers with lids.
citation_text: 3-305.12 FOOD may not be stored (I) Under other sources of contamination. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The caulking sealing the three compartment sink and drainboards to the wall is cracked, creating a surface that is not smooth or easily cleanable. Recaulk the three compartment sink and drainboards to the wall so the transition is smooth, easily cleanable, and cracks/crevices are eliminated.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

There was not any soap or paper towels observed at the handwashing sink. The operator was able to provide paper towels at the sink, but did not have any soap. Ensure that there is always soap and paper towels to allow for proper handwashing at the handwashing sink. A follow up is scheduled on 2/24/2025 to ensure that the facility has obtained soap.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. 

There are prepackaged cuts of meat, smoked fish parts, and frozen produce in the facility that are not labeled with the common name of the product or the cooking instructions. All food needs to be labeled with the common name of the product and all meat needs labeled with cooking instructions. Discussed placing a general cooking instructions label on the outside of the freezers. Discussed reaching out to supplier about labels for the cuts of meat. Ensure that produce that is placed into a bag to be froze has the common name of the product. A follow up is scheduled on 3/5/2025 to ensure that all of these items have been labeled.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed there was an open jug of milk in the front clear double cooler that was not date marked. The PIC stated the jug had been opened several days ago. The milk was correctly date marked during the inspection. The inspector suggested the PIC add labeling open milk to the kitchen’s closing routine. Ensure that all ready-to-eat, temperature control for safety foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are date marked to indicate the 7-day maximum (day 1 being the day food was opened).
citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: Observed the container of sugar in the dry storage room had a bowl being used as a scoop. The PIC was educated that scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle to avoid contact with food. The PIC discarded the bowls during the inspection. Ensure that dispensing utensils for ready-to-eat foods are stored with their handles not in contact with food to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed the rinsing surface to the left of the dish machine is not properly sealed to the wall in some locations. There is a gap between the caulking attached to the wall and the rinsing table surface. The surface must be re-sealed (ex. caulked) to the wall to make it smooth and easily cleanable. Ensure that the rinsing table surface is sealed to the wall by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that no one at the facility has a valid allergen awareness certificate. One of the PIC’s (Jason) stated he will be re-taking the test. Ensure that someone at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed a trash can to be blocking kitchen hand sink. Discussed with PIC, trash can was relocated. Ensure hand washing stations are kept accessible to encourage hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of won ton soup to be hot holding at 110F. Discussed with PIC, inspector recommended soup be moved to stove for reheating, however staff threw soup away and prepared a new batch. Ensure any TCS food being hot held is kept at or above 135F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be made upon inspection. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer was set up and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure sanitizer solution is made and available during all hours of operation.
citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
comment: PIC had copies of the employee health reporting agreements, but they were not signed. Advised that all employees need to sign the agreement and the signed copies should be kept in records. This form advises employees that if they are experiencing any of the symptoms mentioned, they should not handle food or food services, and should not come into work. Follow-up is scheduled for 2/27/25 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Repeat - Observed employee place soiled fruit storage container in bar handwashing sink. Food debris observed in kitchen handwashing sink. Advised that handwashing sinks are for washing hands ONLY, no dumping of food waste or cleaning equipment allowed in handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed cut lettuce, curry sauces, and dry noodles stored with no lid. Advised to keep food containers covered at all times. Regardless of the food being stored in a fridge or freezer, coverings help prevent contamination from dust, bacteria and other foods/equipment above the food container.  Follow-up is scheduled for 2/27/25 to ensure compliance.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment:
The following food storage/contamination violations were observed in the kitchen: 
1. Rice and rice noodles soaking in water in buckets on the floor. Advised to store elsewhere on a shelf or table. Never store open containers of food on the floor to prevent contamination. Staff moved rice and noodles off floor.
2. Raw beef stored in the deli cooler above open container of cut iceberg lettuce. Advised that the juices from the beef could drip into the lettuce, resulting in contamination. Always store raw meat at the lowest shelf, and produce above. Storage order was fixed immediately.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
comment: Observed wiping cloths used for cleaning food surfaces stored on food prep surfaces. Advised cook staff to store sanitizing cloths in sanitizer (water and bleach). This helps keep cloths clean and sanitized between uses.
citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed soup and rice bowls stored with food contact surface exposed to potential contamination. Advised cook staff to store dishes upside down on a clean surface or to cover to prevent cross-contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed fan covering in walk-in cooler to be soiled with dust/debris. Clean cooler with enough frequency to ensure no build-up of dust and debris. Dust from the fans can be blown in to soup pots/other containers in the cooler and contaminate food.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Inspectors observed soup bowls being handled by the inside rim of the bowl immediately after soup was put into the bowl. Discussed with PIC. PIC agreed to only handle bowls by the bottom face. Ensure bowls are handled properly to prevent food contamination. Inspector will return 02/24/2025 to re-asses violation.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspectors observed the dish machine to be testing at 0 PPM CL. Discussed with PIC. PIC ran regular bleach through the machine to test if the issue was the sanitizer bucket or with the dispensing mechanics. PIC deduced that the problem was with the sanitizing solution, and not with the machine itself. PIC stated that they will order a new bucket of sanitizer for the machine. Until new sanitizer is used, use triple sink to wash, rinse, and sanitize the dishes. Inspector will return 02/24/2025 to re-asses violations.

After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (1) Except as specified under Subparagraph (C)(2) of this section, a contact time of at least 10 seconds for a chlorine solution specified under 4-501.114(A).

comment: Inspectors observed there to be a build up of mold on the caulk beside and behind the dish sprayer arm. Along with this, the dish table was not caulked to the wall. Discussed repairs with PIC. PIC agreed to replace moldy caulk and add caulk to areas along the dish table
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

comment: PIC is not a certified food protection manager (CFM). Ensure facility is under the supervision of a CFM during all times of operation.

PIC will revisit handwashing procedure with staff. Ensure a paper towel or other barrier is used to turn the faucet off and prevent recontamination of newly cleaned hands.

comment:
1) The backsplash on the soda fountain counter (in the dining room) is not sealed to the countertop itself, with a gap along the bottom edge and apparent water damage. Repair or replace the backsplash, sealing the backsplash to the countertop and to the wall to eliminate any gaps.

Paint or otherwise seal bare wood so it is smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
PIC has not completed ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. Ensure the facility is under the supervision of a CFM who has completed allergen training during all hours of operation.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

There was no water source available at the mobile unit. Without water service the employees could not have washed their hands at this location when entering the mobile unit nor at other times that hand washing would be required throughout operations. The facility was in the middle of cooking and there was food preparation that occurred prior to creation of the fried rice product.  Hand washing should be taking place regularly and consistently during food operations. During the inspection, the rice was discarded and operations halted while water was made available. The facility acknowledged that they were going to stay closed while the water was unavailable - so the importance of water availability was known, but the application was lacking. The facility was advised that when the water freezes and any instance where water is unavailable they should close.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

It appears that food preparation is taking place in the storage shed next to the mobile unit. This location is only approved for use as dry storage and cannot be used for food preparation. This shall be evaluated again at the follow up in 10 days. Cease these operations moving forward unless approval is acquired. Approval would required renovations inside of the shed as this was previously discussed in the pre-opening inspection for the shed that no preparation was to occur in the space as no hand sink was available. Clean the top of the reach-in freezer where a knife and protein juices and vegetable remnants were observed. There is limited space within the mobile unit and the facility was warned against prepping in this space.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables.

Multiple items in the standing cooler (as you enter the unit) are observed stored in contact with or over items that allow for cross contamination prohibited by the Code. Items include: 1) raw chicken stored over broccoli; 2) shrimp over cooked noodles and; 3) raw scallops stored over carrots. Items were discussed with the PIC and instructed to store TCS foods correctly in the coolers. Items were not immediately moved. This will be one of the talking points to discuss with the Health Educator from SCDPH.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

On arrival a large quantity of fried rice was in the process of being cooked/reheated. Without water service sanitizing and hand washing are not available. Contamination of food is guaranteed in this situation. The rice was discarded during this inspection to correct. Discussed not opening or preparing foods when water is not available. These items should be cleaned regularly throughout the day and at the end of the night. Cleaning will be observed a the follow up in 10 days. Inspector did remove the items for cleaning during the inspection. 2) multiple plastic tubs are observed with sticker residue that has not been completely cleaned. They appear to have not been cleaned for multiple uses. Clean these items completely prior to use. The cleaning of food contact itmes will be evaluated again at the follow up in 10 days.

citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Large bags of rice and sugar in the shed are observed left open. These items have no protection from external contaminants as the vents in the facility do not prevent pest entrance. There are also observed holes in the shed walls independent of venting. Structural repair is an ongoing issue. The items should be sealed and protected from the entrance of pests and other contaminants at all times. Re-evaluation in 10 days.

Multiple rags are observed on various counters throughout the facility during this inspection. Education conducted. This will be evaluated again a the follow up in 10 days.

comment:
4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

Multiple food items in the coolers are observed being stored in grocery bags. These are not approved or safe items for food storage. Ensure that food items are stored in safe and proper containers at all times. This shall be re-evaluated at the follow up in 10 days.

4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

On arrival there was not a sanitizer prepared and ready for use in the mobile unit. There was not even a sanitizer capable of being made in the mobile unit. Sanitizer availability will be evaluated again at the follow up in 10 days.

title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure.
citation_text:
5-104.11 System. Water shall be received from the source through the use of: (A) An APPROVED public water main; or (B) One or more of the following that shall be constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW:  (1) Nonpublic water main, water pumps, pipes, hoses, connections, and other appurtenances, (2) Water transport vehicles, or (3) Water containers. 

On arrival there was no water service available in the unit and the unit is in operation. Water service was made available during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that potable water is available at all times that the facility is in operation. If water is not available the unit must close until water service is made available again.

6-501.11  The facility is using every inch of horizontal space to store equipment. The additional counter space is necessary for proper preparation of foods. Create more surface space for preparation processes.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties.
comment: Inspector facility to be using a faulty hot holding unit to serve day-old rice. The hot holding unit had been tested 10 days prior (02/07/25) and had been shown to not be holding temperature. Inspector instructed facility to not use the hot holding as a temperature controlled device. Facility agreed on 02/07/25 to use time as control for all rice held in the unit. On 02/17/2025, inspector returned to conduct a follow-up. Upon arrival, the hot holding unit was full of trays of day-old rice, and was still consistently probing below 135F (118-125F). Discussed hot holding procedure with PIC again, who again agreed to throw out the day old rice and use time as control for the rest of the rice in the unit (prepared at 11AM, must be thrown out by 3PM). Ensure that the unit is not used as a temperature controlled device until it can be serviced. Inspector will return 02/26/2025 to re-asses violation.
citation_text: 2-103.11(I) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (I) EMPLOYEES are properly maintaining the temperatures of TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOODS during hot and cold holding through daily oversight of the EMPLOYEES’ routine monitoring of FOOD temperatures.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Inspector observed the hot holding unit to be holding temperatures between 118F and 125F (Probed). Facility knew the unit was not holding temperature, but was still using it to store food for more than 4 hours. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated that the hot holding unit was still waiting to be serviced and should be done by tomorrow (02/18/25). Ensure hot holding unit is serviced to bring temperatures back up to proper holding temperatures. Food may be stored in the unit, but only for 4 HOURS AT A TIME. Because the unit is not measuring 135F, it is no longer considered temperature controlled for safety. Therefore, food stored in unit must be thrown out after 4 hours. Inspector will return 02/26/2025 to re-asses violation.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed CFPM on duty to not have allergen awareness training certification. Provide allergen awareness training certification for all CFPM.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee is observed to don gloves without hand washing taking place. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to review hand washing with all employees to ensure it is taking place when needed.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Only one employee at the facility has a food handlers certification available for observation. The maintenance person indicated that they should be on a computer somewhere but none were able to be shown during this inspection for verification. Ensure that all employees that do not have a Certified Food Protection Manager card have completed food handler training and that they are available for verification on inspections.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The dish machine (heat) was observed to have a sanitizing temperature of 155F. The machine was cycled more than 4 times and the temperature remained at 155F. The PIC contacted an Ecolab technician to service the machine. The facility was instructed to sanitize their dishes in the triple sink (set up during the inspection). Also, the dishes can be taken to the other restaurant located within the facility, Reggie’s Diner, to get sanitized. Ensure that the dish machine’s sanitizing temperature is at least 160F in order to properly sanitize dishes
citation_text: 4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: A container of hot dogs was observed to not be date marked inside of a prep cooler. Discussed with PIC and hot dogs were date marked. Ensure that any TCS foods that are held in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used with 7 days of opening.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee wash their hands in the dump sink during the inspection. The employee was educated that hand washing must only occur in designated hand washing sinks. After the education the employee rinsed their hands for about five seconds without soap and turned off the faucet with their bare hands in the hand washing sink. The inspector stepped in again and demonstrated the proper technique with the employee. After the demonstration the employee used the proper procedure, including using soap, scrubbing hands for 10-15 seconds, and using a barrier to turn off the faucet. The PIC was reminded of the importance of the proper hand washing procedure to avoid re-contaminating clean hands. Ensure that employees always wash hands in designated hand washing sinks and utilize the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

PIC stated that they had a suspicion that the hot holding unit was not holding temperature. PIC agreed to use time as control for the 3 trays of rice in the unit. The rice was prepared at 11am, so it must be discarded by 3pm. Ensure that all hot holding units are kept at proper temperature to maintain food safety. Test temperature regularly to ensure this is happening. Inspector will return 02/17/2025 to re-assess this violation.
