citation_text:
7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

On arrival and during the inspection the spray bottle used for the sanitizer in the service area is without a label. A label was added during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all chemicals not in their original containers have labeling indicating the common name of the chemical in them at all times that they are in use.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment:
3-501.13(A-E) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed in an approved manner. 

Raw fish are observed stored in the three part sink thawing in standing water. This was noticed while the inspector was washing their hands ant the beginning of the inspection and the PIC began running water before the situation could be addressed directly. Ensure that all TCS foods are thawed in an approved manner at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A box of frozen meat is observed on the floor under a table in the kitchen during this inspection. The PIC was shown and moved the box to a shelf in the walk in cooler to correct. Ensure that all foods are stored so that they are at least six inches above the floor at all times.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector educated the employee when the action was observed. Immediately afterwards the employee re-washed their hands using the proper procedure. Ensure that a barrier is always used to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed the single-use utensils in the student self-service station were stored with the food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The inspector educated about the importance of storing utensils in a manner that prevents students from touching the food contact portions of utensils. The PIC removed the utensils and brought them into the kitchen to correct the storage after lunch. Ensure that single-use articles are stored to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following physical facilities are observed to still need repaired from the pre-opening: 

1. REPEAT- Repair the flooring that is peeled at the door in the men’s room. 
2. REPEAT- Seal wood around floor drain of triple sink. 
3. Repair hole in wall of men’s restroom. 
4. REPEAT- Seal wood base/kick on right side of double sink in kitchen. 

Ensure that all physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

There were containers of lettuce observed in a standing cooler that did not have a lid on them. The fan in this cooler was observed to be soiled. Ensure that all food is protected from cross contamination by being in a covered container, a wrapper, or stored in its original, closed package. CORRECTED- Lids were placed on these containers during the inspection.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

An employee was observed to use a wiping cloth to wipe down food contact surfaces and leave it on the counter after use. Ensure that if wiping cloths are not in use that they are being stored in a sanitizer bucket that is at the label-recommended concentration. CORRECTED- The employee was educated and moved the cloth into the sanitizer bucket.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
citation_text:
4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. 

The steamer that the facility uses to prepare mashed potatoes and ribs is observed to be leaking and not working properly. It is creating large amounts of steam that is causing black mold to grow on ceiling tiles above this area. Ensure that this equipment is maintained in a state of good repair and condition. There will be a spot check on 3/17/2025 to ensure that this equipment has been repaired and is properly functioning.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The following areas throughout the facility are in need of a cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The fan of the standing cooler that contains the salad mixes.
2. REPEAT- The bottom of the standing cooler that contains the salad mixes. 
3. REPEAT- The fans in the walk-in cooler. 
4. The bottom of the bar cooler. 

Ensure that these areas are cleaned and maintained cleaned by next routine inspection.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of cleaning: 

1. REPEAT- The floor of the walk-in freezer. 
2. REPEAT- The floor throughout the bar area, specifically underneath the equipment.
3. The floors underneath the cook line. 
4. The floors underneath the back prep area/sink. 
5. The floors underneath the drink station. 
6. The ceiling tiles above the steamer as there is mold growth due to the large amounts of steam coming from the steamer. This will be checked on during the 3/17/2025 spot check that is scheduled to ensure it has been cleaned. 

Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned and maintained cleaned.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following physical facilities are observed to need repaired: 

1. The drink station needs re-caulked to the wall. 
2. REPEAT- There is broken coving to the left of the dish area. 
3. REPEAT- The handwashing sink on the end of the cook line needs re-caulked. 
4. REPEAT- There is a piece of broken coving in the walk-in freezer next to the door. 
5. REPEAT- There is broken coving to the right of the walk-in cooler entrance.
6. There are holes in the wall above the handwashing sink near the entrance door to the kitchen. These holes need caulked and made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
7. The triple sink next to the ice machine needs re-caulked. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. Physical facilities should remain in good repair.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
citation_text:
4-202.18 Ventilation Hood Systems, Filters. Filters or other grease extracting EQUIPMENT shall be designed to be readily removable for cleaning and replacement if not designed to be cleaned in place. 

The facility is observed to be using a steamer that is in a state of disrepair. It is creating large amounts of steam that is leading to black mold growth on the ceiling tiles above this area. If this equipment is not repaired and is going to continue to be used, there needs to be a ventilation hood that will prevent this mold growth and allow for proper ventilation. This is combined with the 3/17/2025 spot check as this equipment either needs repaired to function properly or a ventilation hood is needed.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Pink mold accumulation was observed on the baffle of the ice machine. CORRECTED- PIC cleaned and sanitized the baffle of the ice machine. Clean the ice machine as often as necessary to prevent mold growth.
citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: A sauce was observed stored in a 5-gallon bucket that originally contained chemicals. CORRECTED- PIC will cease the use of chemical buckets for food storage.
citation_text: 3-305.11 (A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: A piece of cardboard used to line the bottom shelf of the walk-in freezer has become soiled and needs to be replaced. CORRECTED- PIC replaced the cardboard. If cardboard is used to line shelves, ensure it is changed regularly and does not become soiled or degraded.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: The handsink near the dish machine is not sealed to the wall. Recaulk the handsink so it is sealed to the wall and no gap is present.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food handler training
comment:
No food handler certificate is available for the food employee working in the kitchen during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates available on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.112(A) Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Hot Water Sanitization Temperatures. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, in a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 90°C (194°F), or less than: (1) For a stationary rack, single temperature machine, 74°C (165°F); or (2) For all other machines, 82°C (180°F). 

It was observed that the dish machine is not reaching a heat sanitizing temperature of above 150F. A follow up is scheduled for 2/10/2025 to ensure that the dish machine is reaching a temperature of above 160F. Ensure that dish machines are properly sanitizing dishes by reaching a temperature of 160F or above.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple knives and pans in the kitchen are observed with remaining food debris on them as they are in storage as ready-for-use. These items were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for recleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage/use. It is highly suggested that the dish washers are educated to review dishes after washing and prior to storage.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

The scoop holder for the ice machine is observed with contaminants in the standing water at the bottom. The ice scoop sits in this holder consistently throughout the day. The item and contaminants were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are cleaned regularly and specifically whenever contamination has occurred.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests.

Numerous flies are observed in the dish and hand sink areas of the kitchen. The PIC was shown and instructed to contact their pest control agent (Orkin) for help in remediating the situation. A follow-up will be conducted in three weeks to allow for remediation to take affect throughout the life cycle of the flies observed.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The floor in the dry storage area has dried spills and debris observed. These areas should be cleaned often enough to prevent soilage from accumulating. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

A mostly empty gallon of milk has a manufacturers use by date of 1/29/25 and a facility date mark of 1-20. Today is day 10 since opening and one day over the manufacturers date. The PIC was shown and discarded the container during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are discarded within seven days of opening and prior to the manufacturers use by date.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed a can of butane fuel stored on a top shelf above various foods (including, but not limited too, seasoning, sauces, maple syrup, icing, sugar, and flour). The butane fuel was removed from the location and moved to the dry storage area. Ensure that chemicals are always stored separate from food.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service -and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the bar soda nozzle holder had an accumulation of soil and other debris. The soda holder was removed from service and washed, rinsed, and sanitized during the inspection. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed an employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The inspector immediately educated the employee when the action was observed. Ensure that a barrier it always used to turn off the faucet to avoid contaminating clean hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
comment: Observed an employee grab toast from the toaster and place it on a plate for serving with their bare hands. The PIC was immediately notified when the action was observed. The PIC stated that the facility had recently ran out of gloves and more were on order. The inspector explained the importance of immediate action to ensure a barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods. The PIC placed a pair of tongs by the toaster and another employee went to the store to purchase gloves. The employee returned with the gloves during the inspection. Ensure that gloves or another barrier is always used when handling ready-to-eat foods to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw hamburger meat stored above various vegetables in the right prep cooler bottom. An employee moved the raw meat below the vegetables during the inspection. The inspector explained the importance of storing raw foods underneath any ready-to eat foods to avoid contamination. Ensure that foods are always stored according to the proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the sanitizer bucket under the grill was testing at 10 ppm (Cl) during the inspection. After the PIC remade the bucket it was testing at 100 ppm (Cl). Due to the amount of repeat violations the inspector suggests increasing the frequency that sanitizer buckets are changed. Ensure that sanitizer buckets are always testing at the correct concentration (chlorine = 50-200 ppm).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed two containers of soup in the walk-in cooler had exceeded the 7-day maximum. The soups had a date mark indicating the food was prepared on 1/20/2025 meaning it should have been discarded on 1/26/2025. The PIC was notified and the soup was discarded during the inspection. The inspector educated about the importance of discarding foods after 7 days (the day the food is prepared being day 1). Ensure that foods are always discarded when they exceed the 7-day maximum.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the caulking behind the spray nozzle table to the left of the dish machine is not attached to the wall and is degrading in quality. The caulking must be removed and replaced with fresh caulking. Due to the area being subject to high amounts of moisture the caulking must be repaired/replaced frequently. Ensure the caulking is a smooth, easily cleanable surface by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed the PIC’s allergen awareness expired in August 2024. The PIC stated they were unaware it had expired and they will schedule a new training. No one else present at the facility has completed the allergen awareness training. Ensure that the PIC has a certificate in allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection.  

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: No paper towels were available at the kitchen handsink upon inspector’s arrival. Employees recognized the lack of paper towels and retrieved towels from another location to dry hands, but did not replace the paper towels at the handsink. CORRECTED- Upon request, paper towels were provided at the kitchen handwashing sink. Ensure towels are always available at handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: The kitchen dish machine was found to reach a plate temperature of 143F after two cycles. On the second cycle, the dish machine began leaking suds. PIC called to request maintenance on the machine to fix the leak and adjust the rinse temperature. Ensure the rinse temperature is sufficient to reach 180F from the baffle or achieve a surface temperature of 160F, as measured on an irreversible registering temperature indicator.
citation_text: 4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator. [P]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Facility does not have a way to verify that the dish machine is reaching sanitizing temperature. Ensure that an irreversible, maximum registering thermometer or heat-sensitive stickers are available to monitor the dish machine function.
citation_text: 4-302.13(B) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. [Pf]

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Inspector observed there to be a bucket of pickles left uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC. PIC placed the lid back on the bucket of pickles. Ensure foods that are being stored are protected from-cross contamination at all times; in this case, placing a lid on the bucket is sufficient.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: REPEAT Inspector observed the microwave to be soiled with food debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC had an employee start cleaning the microwave immediately. Ensure the microwave is kept clean to prevent cross-contamination between foods.
citation_text: 3-304.11 Food Contact with Equipment and Utensils. FOOD shall only contact surfaces of: (A) EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS that are cleaned as specified under Part 4-6 of this Code and SANITIZED as specified under Part 4-7 of this Code; (B) Single-service and single-use articles; or (C) LINENS, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed a build up of food residues on the milkshake mixer arms and machine surface. Discussed with PIC. PIC had the machine cleaned immediately. Ensure all food-contact areas on equipment are kept clean and sanitary.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment:
Inspector observed several non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning. 

The hot holding in the back of the kitchen has an accumulation of soils on the machine surfaces. Discussed with PIC. PIC stated that the machine builds up hard-water soils as water evaporates on the machine. Ensure the machine is cleaned regularly to eliminate buildup of soils.

The corner of the dish line between the dish machine and the sink/sprayer combo was observed to have a large amount of soils. Discussed with PIC, recommended a cleaning regiment that includes that area as a frequently visited spot. Ensure that this area is cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.

Underneath the dish machine was observed to have a build up of soils. Discussed with PIC and recommended a cleaning regiment that includes the dish machine area as part of regular cleaning. Ensure this area is cleaned to prevent the accumulation of soils and debris.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed there to still be an ice-buildup problem in the walk-in freezer. The lines have been repaired, as requested in the previous inspection. However, the buildup of ice persists to a lesser extent. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the machine is serviced to prevent this buildup of ice.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the bar hand washing sink did not have soap when the inspector arrived. The PIC provided the hand sink with soap during the inspection. Ensure that every hand washing sink always has soap available for the proper hand washing procedure.
citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed raw meat stored over onions and cooked food in the walk-in cooler. An employee moved the raw meat below the ready-to-eat foods during the inspection. Ensure that food is stored according to the proper storage order to avoid cross contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the steam table was not holding foods at 135F or higher when the inspector arrived. The internal temperature of beans was 120F, queso was 125F, and rice was 120F. An employee turned up the temperature of the steam table during the inspection. When the inspector re-checked the temperatures the internal temperature of the queso was 135F and beans was 140F. The PIC was reminded that temperatures must be checked on a regular basis using a probe thermometer. Ensure that temperature control for safety foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. Education was conducted and they hands rewashed to correct. Ensure education takes place with staff to ensure hand washing takes place at all times that it is required.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
citation_text:
2-301.12(B) Cleaning Procedure. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use the following cleaning procedure in the order stated to clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms, including surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms: (1) Rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) Apply an amount of cleaning compound recommended by the cleaning compound manufacturer; (3) Rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds while: (a) Paying particular attention to removing soil from underneath the fingernails during the cleaning procedure, and (b) Creating friction on the surfaces of the hands and arms or surrogate prosthetic devices for hands and arms, finger tips, and areas between the fingers; (4) Thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) Immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying using a method as specified under § 6-301.12.

An employee did not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet after hand washing. This recontaminated the hands prior to food handling. Education was conducted and the hands rewashed re-washed to correct. Ensure that hands are not immediately recontaminated after hand washing prior to food handling.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

On arrival the hand sink in the facility is observed with multiple bowls and utensils in it, preventing use. The PIC removed the items without asking after the inspector stepped in. Ensure that the hand sinks are maintained accessible at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.

title: Food separated and protected.

citation_text:
3-501.15(B) Cooling Methods. comment: Observed the cheese sauce was not being hot held at 135F or above. The cheese sauce had an internal temperature of 100F. The outside of the cheese sauce can stated that it ‘must be refrigerated after opening to maintain safety’. The inspector contacted CK to confirm that the cheese sauce must be hold held. The sauce must be held at 135F or above to keep the food out of the temperature danger zone (41F-135F). An employee mentioned that recently another employee had turned down the dial due to the cheese sauce being too hot. The dial of the warmer was turned up during the inspection. Before the inspector left the internal temperature of the cheese sauce was observed to be at 125F and still rising. Ensure that the temperature of the cheese sauce is checked on a regular basis to maintain food safety.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).
