comment: Observed eggs stored over avocados in the back silver double cooler. The PIC moved the eggs to the bottom shelf during the inspection. Ensure that raw foods are always stored below ready-to-eat foods to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the employee cleaning dishes in the triple sink was not properly using the wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure. The employee had a bucket filled with soap which they were using to wash the dishes and then rising in clean water before air drying. The inspector educated the PIC and employee about the proper procedure. Dishes must be first washed in soap, then rinsed in clean water, and lastly sanitized in a combination of water and the chosen sanitizer at the correct concentration. After education, the employee had three buckets set up for washing, rinsing, and sanitizing and was utilizing the proper technique. Ensure that dishes always undergo the proper wash, rinse, and sanitize procedure to keep food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text: 4-702.11 Before Use After Cleaning. UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be SANITIZED before use after cleaning.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed butane fuel stored on a shelf above the sushi prep cooler. The PIC was educated and moved the butane fuel to a new location. Ensure that toxic materials are stored in a position where they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, or single-use articles.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Observed fish thawing at room temperature during the inspection. The PIC moved the fish into the cooler during the inspection. They were educated on the importance of thawing using an approved technique (i.e, under continuous running water, inside a cooler, as part of the cooking process, or in the microwave). Ensure that foods are always thawed properly.
citation_text: 3-501.13(A) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the FOOD temperature at 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed a cell phone stored above the back prep cooler leaning against clean dishes and a personal drink stored on a wire shelf above an open container of food. The cell phone was removed from the location and the personal drink was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that personal items are always stored away from food and food prep areas.
citation_text: 6-305.11 Designation. (A) Dressing rooms or dressing areas shall be designated if EMPLOYEES routinely change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEES' clothing and other possessions.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Observed the employee working does not have food handler training completed. The PIC was instructed that all employees hired over 30 days ago must receive training in food handling principles. Ensure that the employee completes the training by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the front cold holding cooler to be at 58F. Discussed with PIC, cooler was not turned on. Cooler was turned on and ran a temperature of 41F. Ensure any TCS food being cold held is kept at or below 41F.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment: Observed ice accumulation on the hose under the fan unit in the walk in freezer. Discussed with PIC, ensure walk in freezer is serviced by a licensed individual. Ensure staff is regularly checking walk in freezer to ensure no ice accumulation is present.
citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(Repeat x2) Observed a majority of the cabinets in the kitchen needing replaced. Many have broken off doors/no doors at all. Discussed with PIC, renovations are scheduled for early March. Ensure areas in the kitchen are properly covered. 

Notice to correct letter will be postponed until renovations are completed.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the caulking to be missing to the right of dish machine. Discussed with PIC, caulking will be replaced. Ensure staff is checking caulking regularly.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment:
Observed waste water to be leaking in the following areas:
1) The pipe below sink next to dish machine.

Discussed with PIC, a licensed plumber will service leaks. Ensure facility is checking regularly that all waste water is being properly disposed of. Inspector will follow up on 02/03/25.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying wastewater. Wastewater shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector arrived. After adding a capful of bleach the sanitizer bucket was testing at 150 ppm (Cl). The inspector reminded the PIC of the importance of testing sanitizing solutions on a regular basis and re-making them as needed. Ensure that sanitizing solutions always test between 50-200 ppm (Cl).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed the beach at the facility does not have an EPA registration. The inspector educated about the importance of using food grade bleach at the facility. The inspector will follow-up on 1/27/2025 to ensure that the facility has bleach with an EPA registration.
citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions), or (B) Meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020 Pesticide Chemicals Not Requiring a Tolerance or Exemption from Tolerance-Nonfood determinations.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed several foods stored in cardboard boxes or containers directly on the floor. The locations of food stored on the floor included the walk-in cooler, walk-in freezer, and underneath the front counter. The PIC stated they are in the process of purchasing more shelving and pallets. During the inspection some pallets for underneath the front counter arrived. Ensure that foods are always stored at least 6-inches above the floor to protect food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: Observed the single use utensils by the takeout window were stored with the handles and food contact surfaces intermixed. The PIC was educated about the importance of storing handles in the same direction to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces. During the inspection the utensils were moved into a different container to allow the handles to be stored vertically. Ensure that single-use utensils are always stored properly.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
Observed construction has been done at the front service counter causing there to be a large amount of exposed wood. The PIC and inspector had a conversation about sealing (ex. paint) all the exposed wood to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. They were also reminded that any other bare wood exposed throughout the facility due to ongoing construction must also be sealed. Ensure that all surfaces remain smooth and easily cleanable. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following physical facilities need to be repaired: 

(1) The small holes throughout the facility, especially around the front hand washing sink, must be sealed.

(2) The edging piece that is coming off the wall to the right of the front hand washing sink must be re-attached to the wall. 

(3) The cove base to the left of the walk-in cooler, left of the walk-in freezer, and left of the back door must be repaired/replaced. 

(4) The triple sink must be sealed to the wall. 

Ensure that physical facilities are always maintained in good repair. Repeat violations from the pre-opening.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food handler training
comment:
Facility could not provide proof of food handler certifications for employees. Ensure that employees who are not manager certified obtain a food handler certification if handling food.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: A cellphone was observed to be placed on a shelf that stores clean dishes in the dish room. Discussed with PIC and phone was removed from area. Ensure that cellphones are placed in a designated area and not in dish room where clean dishes are stored.
citation_text: 6-501.110 Using Dressing Rooms and Lockers. (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
comment: Observed clean utensils to be stored with food contact surface faced upward along the cookline. Discussed with PIC proper storage technique. Ensure that clean utensils are stored with the handles facing upward to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(B) Kitchenware and Tableware. (B) Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and by CONSUMERS if CONSUMER self service is provided.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The back outside door was observed propped open. Discussed with PIC and door was shut. Ensure that doors are never propped open top avoid the entry of unwanted insects and pests.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Approved thawing methods used.
comment: Chicken in a sink was observed to be thawing improperly. There wasn’t a constant flow of running water. Discussed with PIC and running water was provided. If using the running water thawing method, be sure to always have a constant flow of running water at all times.
citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment:
Shredded mozzarella and mushrooms were observed to be improperly stored on ice. The ice method is being used to cold hold these food items. The containers of food were pushed further down into the ice so that the bottom and sides are
covered with ice. Be sure that containers are completely covered with ice to ensure that foods are at the proper cold holding temperature.
citation_text: 301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A container of uncovered tortilla shells was observed to be directly underneath a missing ceiling tile in the dry storage room. Discussed with PIC and shells were moved to a different area. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: A scraper was observed in the basin of one of the meat room handwashing sinks. CORRECTED- PIC removed the tool from the sink. Ensure handsinks are only used for handwashing, no other purpose. Keep handsinks clear to facilitate frequent handwashing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: PIC began to don gloves after handling a cellphone without washing hands first. CORRECTED- Inspector interrupted the behavior and reminded PIC to wash hands, which they did, then donned gloves to continue work. Ensure employees wash hands after any task that may have contaminated them and before donning gloves.
citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD. [P]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: The handwashing sink was observed blocked by a roll of plastic wrap upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- PIC moved the plastic wrap so the handsink is accessible. Keep handsinks clear and accessible at all times.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [Pf]

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
comment: 1st REPEAT: There is no ambient thermometer present inside of the bottom of the prep cooler. Ensure thermometers are provided inside all cold holding units (in addition to any digital thermometers that may be built in to the units).
citation_text: 4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit. [C]

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment:
Mold was observed on several blackberries stored in containers in the walk in cooler. The moldy blackberries were shown to the PIC and then discarded. PIC mentioned that their food distributor, Sysco, has delivered moldy product before. Ensure that food is always in good condition and never served moldy. 

Several containers of blackberries were observed to be moldy in the walk in cooler.
citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
citation_text:
3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

1) The scoop used for ice at the drink station is observed with the handle in contact with the ice during this inspection. 2) An employee was observed to use a cup to scoop out ice from the bin at the drink station. Education was conducted with the PIC and the scoop moved. Ensure that employees are storing and using the supplied equipment correctly at all times

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple pans and utensils are observed stored after cleaning, that have not been completely cleaned prior to storage. Items had observable food debris and sticker remains on them. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food and non-food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use. Education and training with the dish washers is highly suggested.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

A box in the walk in cooler is observed with moisture and mold on the bottom. This has reached to the shelf it is stored on as well. All packaging is observed sealed still and the concern of food contamination is minimal at this time. The box was discarded and the shelf cleaned during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that the non-food contact surfaces are maintained free of soilage at all times in the facility.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: A floor open cooler that stores dessert treats was observed to not have a cover to protect treats from contamination. Discussed with PIC and treats were pulled from floor cooler. The inspector suggested either individually plastic wrapping the desserts or providing clear disposable containers for storage. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that protects against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Shelled eggs were observed stored above corn on the cob in a prep cooler across from the cookline. Discussed with PIC and items were rearranged. Ensure that eggs are always stored on the bottom shelf to protect against contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A sani bucket placed along the sushi line was tested at 0ppm (CL). PIC added more bleach to the solution and was tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that sani buckets are at the proper concentration to accurately sanitize surfaces and utensils.
citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(4) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA registered label use instructions by providing: (4) A contact time used in relationship with a combination of temperature, concentration, and PH that, when evaluated for efficacy, yields SANITIZATION as defined in 1-201.10(B).

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: The facility could not locate a temperature measuring device for the dish machine. Discussed with PIC acceptable measuring devices. Ensure that a temperature measuring buffet is available to accurately test dish machine’ sanitizing temperature.
citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Several mop heads were observed in the basins of mop buckets. Discussed with PIC and mops were placed on hooks. Ensure that mop heads are placed in a position that allows for them to properly air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
The following places are in need of repairs:
- Missinh floor tiles at entrance of walk in freezer
- Missing wall piece to left of hibachi grill
Ensure that physical facilities are maintained and are always in good condition.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Hands clean and properly washed.
comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to turn off the faucet handles after washing hands. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing techniques. Ensure that a barrier is used to turn off faucet handles after handwashing process to avoid recontaminating hands.
citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There wasn't any paper towels located at the handwashing in the kitchen. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided to the dispenser. Be sure that paper towels are available at every handwashing sink to ensure that hands are getting washed properly.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: A slight accumulation of mold was observed on the inside surface of the ice shoot. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that the ice shoot is cleaned as often as necessary to avoid mold accumulation and possible contamination of ice.
citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (1) At any time when contamination may have occurred; (2) At least every 24 hours for iced tea dispensers and CONSUMER self service UTENSILS such as tongs, scoops, or ladles; (3) Before restocking CONSUMER self-service EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS such as condiment dispensers and display containers; and (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Inspector observed no date marks on juices being used in bar coolers. Discussed date marking procedures with PIC. PIC added date marks to the open juices in the cooler. Ensure all opened TCS foods are date-marked upon opening.
citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Inspector observed soda nozzles to have a build up of soils. Discussed soda nozzles cleaning with PIC. PIC removed and cleaned soda nozzles. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned regularly to prevent a build up of soils.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Inspector observed the caulking around the mop sink to be dirty and in disrepair. Discussed mop sink caulk replacement with PIC. Ensure mop sink caulk is repaired/replaced by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-602.11(A) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (A) Equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be cleaned: (5) At any time during the operation when contamination may have occurred.

Multiple pans, utensils and knives stored throughout the facility are observed with contaminants remaining after cleaning and in storage. The PIC was shown and the items moved back to dish for re-cleaning. It is highly suggested that education is conducted in house for dish washers to ensure that food contact items are completely cleaned prior to storage and use. Ensure that all dishes are completely cleaned prior to storage and future use.

title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
comment: Observed the front portion of the left roller had ambient food temperatures of about 68-74F. Upon investigation the PIC noticed that the front portion was turned off. The back portion of the roller was turned on and had an ambient air temperature of about 150F. The PIC discarded the food on the front portion of the roller and turned on the roller during the inspection. When the roller was checked at the end of the inspection the ambient air was 180F. Ensure that temperature control for safety (TCS) foods are always hot held at 135F or above.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records.
comment: Observed the pizzas at the front were not properly marked for time-as-control. When pizzas are brought from the back a sticker is placed above which indicates when the pizza was prepared and when it must be discarded. The pizzas currently on display did not have a sticker. The PIC and inspector discussed the importance of identifying the 4-hour window for time-as-control. The PIC voluntarily discarded the pizzas during the inspection. The newly made pizzas were properly marked with a sticker. Ensure when using time-as-control the time is marked to indicate when the 4-hour window has passed and food must be discarded.
citation_text: 3-501.19(B)(3) Time as a Public Health Control. (B) If time without temperature control is used as the public health control up to a maximum of 4 hours: (3) The FOOD shall be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the FOOD is removed from temperature control.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
comment: Observed several foods stored on the floor throughout the facility. The foods stored on the floor included: (1) Boxes of sliced banana peppers and various cans on the floor adjacent to the back hand sink; and (2) Boxes of food (including, but not limited too, creamer and pastries) stored on the floor of the walk-in cooler. Ensure that foods are stored at least 6-inches above the ground to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Observed a mop stored with the head in the mop sink basin. The PIC inverted the mop during the inspection. Ensure that mops are always stored in a position that allows the head to air dry.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: THIS IS A TWICE REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the facility attempted to fix the peeling cove base by stapling it to the wall, however, there are still gaps between the cove base and the wall. Specifically, the cove base that still has gaps is around the utility sink by the pizza prep station and the soda machine. The cove base needs to be more closely sealed to the wall. Either the facility needs to use more staples or they must use another technique. Ensure that all surfaces are smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the following must be cleaned: (1) The accumulation of garage and food debris in the walk-in cooler underneath the back shelving; and (2) The large drink spillage by the soda machine lines. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Observed a container of eggs stored on the bottom shelf of a prep table to temp at 68F. PIC mentioned that eggs were left on shelf overnight. Eggs were discarded. Ensure that eggs are always cold held at 45F or less and never kept unrefrigerated overnight.
citation_text: 3-501.16(B) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (B) EGGS that have not been treated to destroy all viable Salmonellae shall be stored in refrigerated EQUIPMENT that maintains an ambient air temperature of 7°C (45°F) or less.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Nonfood contact surfaces of the ice machine were observed to have an accumulation of debris on the inside surfaces. The accumulated surfaces were shown to the PIC. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces of the ice machine are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent accumulation.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

title: Food handler training
comment:
One of the kitchen employees isn't food manager or food handler certified. Ensure that employees who handle food are handler certified if not manager certified.  

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-203.11(A) Handwashing Sinks. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, at least 1 HANDWASHING SINK, a number of HANDWASHING SINKS necessary for their convenient use by EMPLOYEES in areas specified under § 5-204.11, and not fewer than the number of HANDWASHING SINKS required by LAW shall be provided. 

It is observed that the facility has removed their handwashing sink that was in the back storage room next to the fridge. This handwashing sink needs replaced to allow for handwashing. A follow up is scheduled for 2/19/2025 to ensure that this handwashing sink has been replaced.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment:
3-602.11(B)(1)-(4) and (6) Food Labels. (B) Label information shall include: (1) The common name of the FOOD, or absent a common name, an adequately descriptive identity statement; (2) If made from two or more ingredients, a list of ingredients and subingredients in descending order of predominance by weight, including a declaration of artificial colors, artificial flavors and chemical preservatives, if contained in the FOOD; (3) An accurate declaration of the net quantity of contents; (4) The name and place of business of the manufacturer, packer, or distributor; and (6) Except as exempted in the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act § 403(q)(3) - (5), nutrition labeling as specified in 21 CFR 101 - Food Labeling and 9 CFR 317 Subpart B Nutrition Labeling. 

There are prepackaged cuts of meat, smoked fish parts, and frozen produce in the facility that are not labeled with the common name of the product or the cooking instructions. All food needs to be labeled with the common name of the product and all meat needs labeled with cooking instructions. Discussed placing a general cooking instructions label on the outside of the freezers. Discussed reaching out to supplier about labels for the cuts of meat. Ensure that produce that is placed into a bag to be froze has the common name of the product. A follow up is scheduled on 2/19/2025 to ensure that all of these items have been labeled.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

The walk-in cooler fans in the meat department and the seafood department were observed to have a build up of dust accumulation. Ensure that nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency necessary to prevent accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The mop sink in the shared dish area between the deli and the bakery, the triple sink in the meat department, and the left of the triple sink in the shared dish area between the deli and the bakery are all observed to need re-caulked. The caulking is in a state of disrepair in each area. Ensure that these areas are re-caulked by next routine inspection. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Ice and juice was observed in the basin of the juicing station handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure handsinks are only used for handwashing (not used as a dump sink).
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

title: Food handler training
comment:
1st REPEAT: One of the 3 employees present during this inspection has not completed food handler training. PIC discussed the training with the employee and checked that they have access to the training in the computer-based learning system. Ensure all employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed.
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

On arrival the hand sink behind the bar had multiple items in it. Education was conducted with the PIC and the sink emptied to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained free of obstructions and available for use as a hand sinks at all times.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
citation_text:
3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306. 

Multiple bottles of Skinny Mixes are observed with small mold colonies growing on the outside of the containers. The PIC was shown and discarded them to correct.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

The available test strips have all expired in the spring of last year. The PIC was shown and instructed to acquire new test strips prior to the follow up in 10 days.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) Sections of the ceiling are observed damaged/missing during this inspection. PIC indicated that the plan is to have them replace around March. 2) A small section of the floor behind the bar is observed with laminate pulling up. The PIC is instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food handler training
comment:
(REPEAT x3) 410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

The employee/PIC for this facility has not competed food handler training at the time of this inspection. Education was conducted and they are instructed to complete the training and maintain a copy of the certificate moving forward. Putting “Illinois Food Handler Certification” into google should pull up multiple option to complete this. This was shown to the PIC during this inspection.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple items throughout the kitchen and prep areas do not appear to have been completely cleaned prior to storage. These items were shown to the PIC and moved back to dish for re-cleaning to correct. Ensure that all dishes and utensils are completely cleaned prior to storage.

title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
citation_text:
4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

1) Multiple tray lids are stored on a shelf soiled with old oil. Multiple loads are stored in a container with crumbs/dust in the bottom. Both items were shown to the PIC and they were moved to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they remain free of potential contamination prior to use.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the bathroom to the right of the water fountain did not have paper towels. The PIC provided paper towels to the bathroom during the inspection. Ensure there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed in the back receiving room to the right of the exit door there was a large crack in the wall. The PIC filled the crack with caulk during the inspection. Ensure the crack remains sealed to be a smooth, easily cleanable surface and prevent the entry of pests.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment:
4-302.14: The Quaternary ammonium test strips that are available in the facility are damaged and are not usable. Ensure that new test strips are obtained and are always usable and available to test the concentration of the sanitizer in the facility. A follow up is scheduled for 1/27/2025 to ensure that new Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. 

Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Proper date marking and disposition.
comment: Observed the cappuccino machine to be using powder with a discard date of 1/13/25. Discussed with PIC, powder was replaced. Ensure facility is following the 7 day date marking system and checking dates regularly.
citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
comment:
Observed waste water to be leaking in the following areas:
1) The pipe below sink next to dish machine.
2) The pipe below the triple sink. 
3) Ice accumulation present on the hose in the walk in freezer. 
Discussed with PIC, a licensed plumber will service leaks. Ensure facility is checking regularly that all waste water is being properly disposed of. Inspector will follow up on 1/23/25.
citation_text: 5-402.13 Conveying wastewater. Wastewater shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
Observed the following require repairs:

(1) The facility installed a new soda machine and the old soda line holes have not been covered. The holes are located on the wall near the ground by the front hand washing sink and the oven in the prep room. The holes need to be covered to create smooth, easily cleanable surfaces. 

(2) The wall panel holding the paper towel dispenser at the front hand washing sink is lifting up on the left side. The panel needs to be sealed to the wall to make a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

Ensure these locations are repaired to be smooth and easily cleanable by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed there was not paper towels at the hand washing sink when the inspector arrived. The PIC provided paper towels to the hand sink during the inspection. Ensure there is always paper towels available at every hand washing sink.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: Observed eggs stored over milk in the lobby cooler. The PIC moved the eggs below the milk during the inspection. The inspector reminded the PIC that ready-to-eat foods must always be stored above raw foods to prevent contamination. Ensure foods are always stored according to the proper storage order.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment: Observed the sanitizer bucket was testing at 0 ppm during the inspection. The PIC dumped and remade the solution which tested at 150 ppm (Chlorine). The inspector reminded the PIC that sanitzier buckets must be tested on a regular basis. Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always between 50-200 ppm (Chlorine).
citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed fryer cleaner stored on the shelf above various food (including, but not limited to, seasonings). The PIC removed the cleaner from this location and placed it by the mop sink away from food. Ensure that toxic materials are stored away from food to prevent contamination.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed there is not ingredients available for the pre-packaged items in the front display cooler (including, but not limited too, cakes, cookies, and other desserts). The inspector and PIC discussed keeping the original packaging with the ingredient list after the next shipment. The inspector suggests keeping all the ingredient lists in a binder by the cash register. Ensure that all foods packaged in the facility have labels available.
citation_text: 3-602.11(A) Food Labels. (A) FOOD PACKAGED in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, shall be labeled as specified in LAW, including 21 CFR 101 - Food labeling, and 9 CFR 317 Labeling, marking devices, and containers.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following have exposed bare wood: (1) The end of the shelving holding spices above the pass-thru window; and (2) The edges of pass-thru window. The bare wood needs to be sealed (ex. paint) to create a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Ensure these areas are sealed by the next routine inspection.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following physical facilities are not maintained in good repair: 

(1) The front area with the cash register requires cove base be added to the missing locations. 

(2) The cove base to the right of the back door and behind/around the triple sink needs to be sealed to the wall. 

(3) The corner wall edging to the right of cook line needs to be sealed to the wall. 

(4) The walls need to be repainted in food prep areas to be a light color. 

(5) The wall above the mirror in the bathroom needs to be sealed to the wall so there is not a gap. 

(6) There needs to be a self closer on the bathroom door. 

Ensure these physical facilities are repaired by the next routine inspection.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. The ice baffle was observed to have an accumulation of pink residue on the left side of it. CORRECTED- The operator cleaned it during the inspection and was recommended to use a flashlight when cleaning it to ensure it is fully cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. There were to-go containers, paper plates, and small bowls that were stored on the front counter with their food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are stored inverted or all facing the same way to avoid contamination to the food contact surface. 

(A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:

A follow up is scheduled for 1/24/2024 to ensure that Quaternary ammonium test strips have been obtained. 

A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. The triple sink in the back prep area has a significant leak coming from the pipes underneath it. Ensure that plumbing systems are maintained in good repair. 

 A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-501.11 Repairing. There is a missing piece of coving underneath the handwashing sink in the kitchen. Ensure that this coving is replaced. Physical facilities should be maintained in good repair. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.
