Replace or coat with multiple layers of gloss paint. The PIC was shown and instructed to complete update prior to the next routine inspection. 
2) There are two large holes in the ceiling in the dry storage area that are in need of repair. Repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: Daylight is visible along the bottom edge of the back door. Weather stripping is missing from that area. Replace the weather stripping on the back door so it is tight-fitting and daylight is not visible along the edges.
citation_text: 6-202.15(C) Outer Openings, Protected. (C) Exterior doors used as exits need not be self-closing if they are: (1) Solid and tight-fitting. [C]

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
PIC present at the beginning of this inspection has not completed ANSI-approved allergen awareness training. CORRECTED- A CFM with allergen training arrived near the end of this inspection. Ensure a CFM with allergen training is present during all shifts of food prep and service.
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: Observed the PIC dump a bucket of water containing food debris into the hand washing sink. The PIC was educated about only using the hand washing sink for washing hands. Ensure that hand washing sinks are not used for any other purpose other than hand washing.
citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
comment: Observed several dented cans on the can holding rack outside of the walk-in cooler. The cans were set aside and the PIC was educated about the importance of removing dented cans during the inspection. The PIC was instructed to remind all employees on the facility’s procedure for removing dented cans. Ensure that packages are always in good condition to protect food from contamination.
citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed several foods (including, but not limited too, cooked chicken, cooked rice, and cut vegetables) stored uncovered in the walk-in cooler. The uncovered items were covered during the inspection. Ensure that foods are always covered to protect them from contamination.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following food contact surfaces were not clean to sight and touch:
(1) The baffles of the ice machine were soiled with debris. The baffles were cleaned to sight and touch during the inspection. The baffles must be cleaned regularly to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
(2) Cutting boards stored behind the faucets of the triple sink and dump sink. Storing cutting boards in this position presents the risk of contamination from food debris or water splashes. The cutting boards were removed from behind the faucets and were placed in new location away from potential contamination. 
Ensure that food contact surfaces are always kept clean to sight and touch.
citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: Observed fryer and oil cleaner stored above clean dishes and WD-40 stored adjacent to food. Both of the chemicals were moved to shelves where they cannot pose the risk of contamination during the inspection. Ensure that toxic materials are stored separate from food and utensils.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

title: Food properly labeled; original container.
comment: Observed several white powders (flour, corn starch, and tempura batter) in large containers without a label. The PIC labeled the containers during the inspection. Ensure that foods not in their original packaging and easily mistakable are always labeled with the common name.
citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed single-use utensils at the front service area stored with the food contact surfaces and handles intermixed. The PIC corrected the storage during the inspection. The PIC was educated about the importance of storing handles in the same direction to avoid contaminating the food contact portion. Ensure that single-use utensils are stored in a manner that protects them from contamination.
citation_text: 4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. (A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Observed the floor directly underneath the fryers has an accumulation of grease and food debris. The inspector suggests pulling out the fryers to clean underneath. Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil and other debris.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed personal employee drinks stored on shelves intermingled with and above various food products and clean dishes. The PIC removed all the personal drinks and placed them on a bottom shelf which will be designated as the ‘personal storage shelf’. Ensure that all personal employee items are placed in designated areas.
citation_text: 6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
Observed that the PIC’s allergen awareness training is expired. No one else at the facility has completed the training. Ensure that the PIC completes training in basic allergen awareness principles by the next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

On arrival the hand sink by the juice machines was observed to have running water flowing through a catch tray that appears to be from one of the juice machines. Designated hand sinks are to be used for only hand washing and no other task per code. The PIC was shown and removed the tray to correct. Education is suggested for staff to ensure that this situation does not persist in the future.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

A package of raw chicken is observed on top of a package of pre-cooked chicken in the walk in cooler. The PIC saw it and removed the RTE chicken immediately to correct the violation. Education was conducted. Ensure that RTE TCS foods are stored above raw items in the coolers.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-501.114(F)(1) and (2) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

The sani bucket available in the kitchen at the time of this inspection would not register sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. The bucket was remade to correct. Ensure all in use sanitizers in the facility are maintained at effective levels at all times.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
citation_text:
6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors. 

There is a broken piece of framing around the AC unit in the 4th floor dry storage room. This leaves an opening to the outside through which pests could enter the facility. The PIC was shown and instructed to have repaired prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. 

The gasket on the door for the walk in freezer is pulling away from the door. Repair prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Of the kitchen staff that does not have a CFPM only one has food handler training on file. A conversation took place with the PIC and they are instructed to ensure that all food handlers that do not have a CFPM have completed food handler training prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
comment: There were no paper towels available at the kitchen handwashing sink upon inspector’s arrival. CORRECTED- Upon request, staff refilled the dispenser. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Grease or food was observed spilled on the lower shelf of the clean equipment shelves near the mop sink. Clean this area.
citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: 1st REPEAT: Three mops were observed stored with the mop-ends piled in the mop sink basin. Another mop was observed stored in dirty mop water in a nearby mop bucket. Ensure mop water is discarded immediately after use, and that mops are stored to promote air-drying.
citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Food debris was observed under the counter in the multi-use hallway area near the soda syrups. Sweep and clean under equipment.
citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The bottom of the yogurt cooler was observed to have an accumulation of trash on the lining. The facility uses a paper lining at the bottom of the coolers. The facility is getting new coolers soon and it was recommended to make sure that the bottom of those coolers stay clean and that the lining is changed more often. Nonfood contact surfaces should be maintained cleaned.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager.

A the time of this inspection there is not a Certified Food Protection Manager available at the facility. The PIC was consulted and stated that the one they have on staff starts next week. A copy of the known local courses is being attached to this report and the PIC is instructed to insure that there are enough CFPMs available to cover all shifts at the facility.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW.

During this inspection the PIC could not produce verification that employees were notified of their responsibility to report illnesses and symptoms related to foodborne illness. A copy of the Reporting Agreement given out by this facility was found in the paperwork given during the pre-opening. Another copy is being attached to the email of this report. The PIC is instructed to have all food employees sign a a copy and maintain the copies at this facility moving forward.

title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Multiple cans of foods are observed with significant dents. Education was conducted with the PIC and the noted cans separated out for discard/credit. Ensure that all food packaging is in good condition until use.

title: Food separated and protected.
citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented.

Raw chicken is observed over raw vegetables in the three door cooler in the prep room. This situation was discussed with the PIC and the items re-aranged during this inspection to correct. A hand out is being attached to the emailed report for an added visual.

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
citation_text:
7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

A bus tub of onions is observed on a shelf under cleaners, degreasers and bleach. Storage was discussed with the PIC and the container moved to correct. Ensure that all chemicals are stored in a manner that does not pose a risk of contamination for foods.

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
citation_text:
3-304.12(E) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(E) In a clean, protected location.

Two knives are observed being stored in the gap between two coolers. This gap is not able to be cleaned/sanitized. Education was provided and a new storage practice will be needed for these items. The items were moved to dish to correct the immediate violation.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
citation_text:
4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

A CL (bleach) based sanitizer is used in the facility. Only test strips effective for use with Quat sanitizers are available for checking the concentration of sanitizer solutions. Education was conducted and the PIC is instructed to ensure that the test strips and sanitizers match prior to the follow up.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-101.11(A)(3) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (3) Nonabsorbent for areas subject to moisture such as FOOD preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, WAREWASHING areas, toilet rooms, mobile FOOD ESTABLISHMENT SERVICING AREAS, and areas subject to flushing or spray cleaning methods.

Ceiling tiles above the bathroom, sink, mop sink and prep areas are of the acoustic type and are not acceptable for food preparation or moist locations. The PIC was consulted and will be replacing as able moving forward.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment:
(REPEAT FROM THE PRE-OPENING) 6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

The triple sink has a small gap between it and the wall that could allow for moisture and mold growth. The PIC was consulted and instructed to seal (caulking suggested) prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

A the time of this inspection food handler training certificates are not available for the food handlers in the facility. Training was discussed and the PIC is instructed to have the training completed by the staff and the certificates available prior to the next routine inspection.

title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs).

Allergen awareness training certification is not available for the only CFPM available at the facility. Education was conducted and a pair of hand outs attached to the emailed report. Ensure that the CFPMs at this facility have also completed allergen awareness training and the certificates are available moving forward.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
comment: Observed the following non-food contact surfaces need to be cleaned: (1) Dust on the walk-in cooler fans; and (2) Grease in between the fryers on the cook line. Ensure these areas are cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil resides.
citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
comment: Observed an employee storing their cell phone on a shelf adjacent to the pizza & salad prep cooler holding clean plates and utensils. The employee was educated and they removed their phone from the location. Ensure that personal items are stored away from food prep areas to avoid contamination.
citation_text: 6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
comment: The facility continues to have gaps around the base of the back door, specifically on the bottom right. There was discussion of using a solid material along the outside of the door instead of steel wool (which was repeatedly falling out). The door needs to be repaired to prevent the entrance of pests. The door is not used for deliveries and is able to be relatively sealed.
citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: Paint around the front counter handsink is chipped and deteriorating. Repaint the walls around the front counter handsink so the wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a leak in the ceiling in the middle of the kitchen (not over any food prep/storage). Per PIC, the landlord has been notified and is getting estimates for repairs. In the meantime, a bucket has been placed to catch the drip. Repair the ceiling to eliminate the leak.
citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. REPEAT- The soda nozzles in the buffet area have a buildup of black soil residue on them. The facility stated in the past that the syrup causes this buildup. It is recommended to reach out to Coke to see if there is a way to fix this issue or it is recommended to scrub them daily to avoid this build up. Clear soda nozzles are also a recommended option to be able to easily see this build up to clean it. CORRECTED- These soda nozzles were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. 

 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
citation_text:
4-204.112(A) Temperature Measuring Devices. There is not an air thermometer in the coolers in the grab and go section or in the yogurt cooler in the buffet area. Ensure that there is always a temperature measuring device in all refrigerated and hot food storage units to measure the air temperature. 

(A) In a mechanically refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, the sensor of a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure the air temperature or a simulated product temperature in the warmest part of a mechanically refrigerated unit and in the coolest part of a hot FOOD storage unit.

title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. There are single service plates by the buffet area and bowls by the cereal area that were stored in a manner that exposes them to contamination. CORRECTED- These items were inverted during the inspection. Ensure that all single service articles are stored inverted to protect them from contamination. 

 (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

title: Food separated and protected.
comment: 1st REPEAT: A carton of raw shell eggs was observed on the top shelf of the 2 door cooler, above bread, cream cheese, and salad dressing. CORRECTED- PIC removed the eggs and voluntarily discarded them. The eggs were delivered by accident and are not used in the facility. Ensure raw shell eggs are stored below ready-to-eat foods.
citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas. [P]

title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
comment: Foods in the countertop cooler were observed above 41F. Salsa portions were observed at 48F, sliced cheese at 50F, veggie sausage at 54F, and deli ham at 52F, all probed. PIC stated that the sliced cheese, veggie sausage, and ham were stocked in the cooler about 30 minutes prior to initial checks. Temperatures had not changed 30 minutes later, 1 hour after foods were placed in the cooler. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were moved to a functional cooler to quickly cool to 41F or below. Ensure TCS foods are held at 41F or below.
citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
comment: A spray bottle of Clorox Scentiva disinfectant was observed stored on the countertop in the back kitchen area, where food is prepared. CORRECTED- The spray bottle was moved to storage away from food prep surfaces. The disinfectant is used on the cash register countertop, not for food contact surfaces.
citation_text: 7-201.11 Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
comment: The countertop cooler is not holding foods at 41F or below. Salsa portions were observed at 48F, sliced cheese at 50F, veggie sausage at 54F, and deli ham at 52F, all probed. Discussed turning down the cooler temperature or moving TCS foods to the nearby prep cooler that is holding foods at 41F or below.
citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
comment: 1st REPEAT: An ice scoop in the small ice bin was observed with the handle in contact with the ice. Discussed proper storage with staff and PIC. Store ice scoops so that the handle does not touch the ice, and the scoop can be used without touching the ice.
citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
comment: No prepared sanitizer bucket was available during this inspection. CORRECTED- Upon request, a sanitizer bucket was prepared. Ensure sanitizer buckets are prepared before beginning to engage in food prep, and refreshed as needed throughout the day.
citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation. [Pf]

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
comment: There is a bare wood 2x4 on the wall holding a syrups rack on the wall. Paint or otherwise seal the bare wood so it is smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

title: Hands clean and properly washed.

The open sided cooler on the end of isle 16 is registering air temperatures on the bottom shelf in the 48F-55F range. Hams in this cooler are observed with internal temperatures of 44F-48F. The PIC asked employees who stated that the hams had been stocked approximately one hour prior to observation. The hams were allowed to be moved to another cooler to save. This indicates that the cooler is malfunctioning however and needs maintenance conducted. The PIC called RW Refrigeration and they arrived during this inspection. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The sani buckets in the facility do not register on the inspector test strips at the beginning of the inspection. The PIC indicated that any time that they put the wiping cloths into the solution the concentration drops quickly. A bit of investigation was completed by the inspector using different buckets and cloths. It appear that the temperature of the initial solution is not allowing for an effective mixing of the chemicals. When both hot and cold water was turned on equally the solution produced regular concentrations of Quat in solution. These should be verified on an ongoing basis and the chemical company consulted to ensure longevity of the system, but this appears to have corrected the issue. The bubbles from the initial mixing also appear to be giving false readings when contacted by test strips. All of this has been discussed with the PIC and the buckets remade.

1st REPEAT: Facility does not have a written policy for clean up of vomit/diarrhea. CORRECTED- Inspector provided a vomit/diarrhea clean up policy. Keep available for review in case it is needed and ensure supplies are available.
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11. [Pf]

comment:

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
3-501.14: Inspector found Tuna salad, made in house, at 51F when temperature was taken with a probe thermometer. The tuna salad was constructed and put to cool at 8am today. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less.

comment:

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION FROM THE 12/11/2023 INSPECTION. 

Observed a previously wet wiping cloth stored in an empty bucket. Wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer between uses and once soiled immediately separated for laundering. Wet cloths are not allowed to sit in empty buckets or other surfaces within the facility when not in use. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored properly by the next routine inspection. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
citation_text:
3-501.19 The facility has a routine for making and using small batches of boba. The boba still needs to have a time as a control marking of some sort. Discussed using a white board or the tile back splash. The boba on the counter top did not have a time as control tag. Make sure to mark in use boba with 4 hour time tag and use or discard any left after the 4 hours. Boba was marked.

(A) If time without temperature used for public health control, written procedure approved by regulatory authority shall be available upon request (Pf). (B) If time is used as control for up to 4 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F (or less) or 135F (or greater). FOOD shall be marked, cooked and served within 4 hour time limit. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 4-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (P) (C) If time is used as control for up to 6 hours, food shall have initial temperature of 41F or less. FOOD shall not exceed 70F. If FOOD is unmarked or marked exceeding 6-hour limit, FOOD shall be discarded. (D) HSP FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS cannot use time control for raw eggs.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed several TCS foods without date marking. Food without date marking included, but is not limited too, the entire top left side of the prep cooler (this included cut vegetables such as carrots, peppers, and onions), wasabi in the sushi prep cooler, shrimp in the sushi prep cooler, spicy tuna in the sushi prep cooler, bowl of cheese in the double cooler, bowl of cut veggies in the double cooler, bowl of rice in the double cooler, and half & half at the bar. The PIC was confident when all the foods were prepped so date marks were added to all the above mentioned foods. Ensure that TCS foods held in the facility for longer that 24 hours are date marked to clearly indicate the 7-day maximum. The day the food was prepped is day 1. After 7 days the food must be discarded.

There was also an incorrect date mark on the avocados in the prep cooler. The date was 08/25/2024 (which would mean the food needed to be discarded), but the PIC stated the avocados were prepped yesterday. It appears that an employee is not removing dates from containers when they are emptied. Old date marks must be removed and new dates be added. Ensure foods are date marked with the correct dates.

The inspector will return on 09/16/2024 to check on date marking.

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. The CFPM did not have their allergen training. Ensure that at least one CFPM has their allergen training in a high risk facility during all hours of operation. 

Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.112: Upon arrival the conveyor dish machine had an alarm sign on the display and the final rinse temperature gauge was sitting at 120F. The dish washer noted that the booster heater had not been turned on. The booster was turned on and the final rinse temperature gauge came up to over 189F quickly. A maximum registering thermometer was run and the dish machine is now sanitizing at 158F. Ensure that staff are properly trained for the job they are performing. The violation was corrected on site. 
(A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
3-501.13: Inspector found 11 portions of ROP fish thawed in the 2 door cooler still in the packaging. Package read remove from packaging before thawing. The fish portions were discarded in the garbage. Thaw foods properly.

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

(C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:

Approximately 9 drain flys/gnats are observed flying and on the walls in the corner behind the fountain drink machine. This is a reduction in the previously observed flies but is not sufficient for considering the situation resolved. The PIC was shown and instructed to clean the area and facility sufficiently to not provide an enticing location for pests to propagate. No obvious locations are currently observed for enticement and no specific harborage location is noted at this time. Contact pest control for maintenance. Fly strips were also discussed during this inspection. They cannot be placed in locations that pose a concern for contamination for foods and food contact surfaces.

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
Six (1 gal) containers of cheese sauce, in the walk-in cooler and labeled indicating cooling began at 10am, were observed at 104-136F (probed). title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-703.11: The facility has an empty sanitizing bucket attached to their dish machine. No sanitizer is available. The facility may not use the dish machine until proper chemical is provided. The dish machine should be monitored daily: every morning, between lulls in use, and between the switching of buckets. TEST, TEST, TEST to monitor. Sanitizing is one of the most critical steps in your safe food handling operations. The triple sink is being used throughout the day to support facility operations (thawing and food preparation). Without proper sanitizing, you are not reducing pathogens present from customer-to-customer and between raw proteins and ready-to-eat foods. 
The facility is going to get chemical from GFS. Do not use the dish machine until chemical is provided and TESTED within dish machine. 

After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: Chicken is observed thawing in a tub of water on the preparation counter. The chicken was almost through the thawing process and was becoming ambient temperature. Proper thawing practices were discussed. PLAN AHEAD and place frozen foods in the walk-in cooler days before needed. The walk-in cooler has space for additional shelving. This may be needed to support the growing business. Bakers racks are tall and have five or six shelves. More storage would support thawing. Chicken was returned to the walk-in cooler during the inspection. 
Also, a large number of shrimp are observed being stored on the preparation counter during lunch and then dinner. The food is returned to the walk-in cooler but this is an example of temperature abuse - the food is repeatedly moved through warm and then cooled practices. Think about portioning the shrimp prior to storage so you can grab a few bags during busy periods. OR simply bring less shrimp out of the cooler during busy periods. 
Shrimp was returned to cooler during the inspection. 
(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:
3-501.13: The facility is observed improperly thawing chicken and fish. Frozen bags were observed in the triple sink with no water running. The fish was moved to the walk-in cooler and the chicken was placed under running water. 

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cheesecake in the display cooler located in the consumer area is observed with an internal temperature of 48F. Temperatures throughout the cooler are observed acceptable (39F-41F) in the top section of the cooler and become progressively warmer as you move down the cooler. Cheesecake and pudding cups are the only items in this cooler needing temperature control for safety. As the PIC was consulted the retractable cover was pulled down to help contain the cool air produced by the unit. Per the PIC the cheesecake and pudding were placed in the unit after lunch (.5-1 hour prior to inspection). They were moved to the walk in to save while the cooler was given time to cool down. This does not seem to be effective during his inspection. The TCS items will be stored in the top of the cooler moving forward and maintenance is to be called to check the cooler over. It is also suggested to use extra thermometers (one is in the unit and is accurate) in this unit to see what temperatures different locations in the unit register at. Inspector will spot check after the fair to ensure that the cooler is functioning or that the new storage practice is being maintained.

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:

Smoking should not be taking place in the kitchen at any time to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces of foods.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: An employee was observed to wash their hands and then turn off the faucet without a barrier. When washing your hands, you always need to use a barrier, such as a paper towel, to turn off the faucet to avoid contamination to your hands. Educate all employees on proper handwashing procedure. CORRECTED: Staff was educated on proper handwashing. 

(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

title: Approved thawing methods used
comment:

CORRECTED- Staff was educated on thawing and the hot dogs were switched to a proper thawing method. 

TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process

title: Allergen training as required

(REPEAT x3) 410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
Observed the dish machine had a concentration of 0 ppm (Cl). The chemical sanitizers for dish machines must have a minimum concentration of 100 ppm. The heat of the dish machine was 111F. The dish machine was tested at the end of the entire cycle and at the end of the rinse cycle. It appears that the dish machine was testing low due to an air bubble in the line. After being properly primed, the dish machine was testing at 100ppm. Owner was initally notified of the concern and could not produce someone knowledgeable about properly using and testing the machine. 
After leaving the facility, the owner called to state the machine was operating properly. CK returned with HM to observe the machine primed at that time with an MJ Kellner representative to service the machine and a chemical log created to monitor the concentration of the machine at least three times per day. Discussed educating staff on service and testing. MJ Kellner representative confirmed he would educate available staff on methods to problem solve.

Ensure that chemical sanitizers meet the proper criteria and are tested regularly.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed several gallons of milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date in the standing cooler. The fat free milks were dated 7/19/2024 and 7/26/2024 and the 2% milk was dated 7/30/2024. Discussed with PIC and milks were pulled from the cooler and discarded. Ensure that milks never exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date and are discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:

title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
comment:
3-403.11: Inspector observed chicken and refried beans on the hot holding table at 119F and 122F respectively. The food had been on the hot holding table for approximately one half hour according to the facility manager. The food was put into the microwave and reheated to 178F and 197F respectively for hot holding. The violation is considered corrected on site. Take care to follow proper reheating procedures for hot holding. Use thermometer to verify temperatures before putting the food on the hot holding table. 

(A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:

[Pf]

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C). title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:

2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
comment:
Observed there was not a written procedure for employees to follow when responding to vomit or diarrheal events at the facility. A written procedure was given to the PIC during the inspection. There is sufficient bleach at the facility to respond to events. Ensure that the written procedure is always available at the facility and that bleach continue to be sufficient. 

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.

title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
comment:

Ensure that all hand sinks always have signs notifying employees that they must wash their hands before returning to work.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed the following food needs date-marking: (1) Par chicken in the walk-in cooler (REPEAT VIOLATION); and (2) Banana pudding and cheese-cake in the front standing cooler. Discussed date-marking with the PIC and provided a handout. Ensure that all containers not used within 24-hours are date marked to avoid food being held for longer than 7-days. There will be a follow-up on 07/22/2024 to ensure proper date-marking. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

comment:

C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

title: Proper cold holding temperatures
comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: A tub of cooked pork was observed at 66F (probed) on the kitchen counter. Employees stated that the pork was removed from the walk-in cooler at 7am (about 1.5 hours prior to the temperature observations) with the intention of portioning it into bags and freezing it. The facility was out of bags so the pork was returned to the walk-in cooler. When the temperature was checked again at 10:30am, the pork was 65F (probed) and was voluntarily discarded. Only remove foods from cold-holding when ready to work with them. Do not store foods on the countertops (out of refrigeration) for extended periods of time. (Previously observed 9/22/23).
2) Shell eggs in the top of the prep cooler were observed with an ambient temperature of 51F, and an internal temperature of 54F (probed) when an egg was cracked. CORRECTED- About 1.5 dozen eggs were voluntarily discarded. All other foods in the prep cooler were 41F or below.

Foods must be used or discarded within 7 days of prep, with the day prepared counting as Day 1 (the day prepared +6 days).

title: Proper cooling time and temperature
comment:
Three buckets and one pan of cheese sauce were not cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours. The cheese sauce was finished cooking at 11:30am. At 2:00pm, the cheese sauce temperatures were 74F in a pan near the grill and 96F, 101F, and 104F in buckets on the back prep counter. CORRECTED- Cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded. Monitor cooling foods and use cooling techniques to ensure they cool from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and ultimately reach 41F within no more than 6 hours total.
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. [P]

title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
comment:
A pan and three buckets of cheese sauce, a pan of cooked beef, and a pan of tamales were observed cooling on the back prep counter without additional cooling techniques in use. The cheese sauce was voluntarily discarded because it had not reached 70F within 2 hours. The beef was moved to the walk-in cooler. The tamales were 135F, and were spread out on a sheet tray and placed in the walk-in cooler to cool. Monitor cooling foods and use cooling methods to help foods cool quickly. 
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

comment:

2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

No CFPM is available at the time of this inspection. Hand outs were given during this inspection and the PIC is aware that a CFPM must be  present at the facility at all times of operation.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash their hands briefly (approximately 5 seconds) and then use their bare hand to turn off the faucet. The observed procedures also only rubbed the palm and palm side of the fingers. Proper hand washing was discussed with the PIC (and employee) and they are instructed to ensure that safe hand washing takes place at all times. Wash all of the hands to include between fingers, under fingernails and the top of the hands to ensure that all possible contaminants are removed. Then use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet in order to prevent recontaminating the hands prior to food handling.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival the sanitizer dispenser at the three part sink would not produce effective amounts of Quat in solution. Because of this the three part sink and available sani buckets do not register correctly on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. The jug of sanitizer was replaced and ran for several minutes. After this the concentration was observed at correct levels.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

Test strips are only available for the buckets and sink of the facility which use a Quaternary Ammonia based solution. The spray bottle used for cleaning/sanitizing the meat slicer is a CL based sanitizer. Ensure that correct test strips are available for all sanitizers used on food contact surfaces in the facility. Follow up is being scheduled for two weeks for compliance.

title: All food employees have food handler training
comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

Food handler cards were not available for employees at the time of this inspection. Food handler cards were discussed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that all employees who do not have a CFPM certificate have at least a food handler certification.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Observed several TCS foods stored in the walk in cooler not date marked. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that any TCS food held in house longer than 24 hours is date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
comment:
Observed several containers of raw chicken to be stored on the floor inside of the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that food is always stored at least 6 inches off the floor to prevent contamination. 

3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor.

comment:
Observed to-go containers stored in an upright position. Discussed with PIC and containers were turned upside down. Ensure that to-go containers are always stored in a manner that prevents contamination during storage. 

4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

comment:

All of the nozzles were removed and properly washed rinsed and sanitized before being put back on the machine, properly protected with gloved hands so that they are maintained free of contamination and do not contaminate the food. comment:

Treat the soda nozzles just like a fork, knife or spoon. The violation is considered corrected on site. Maintain the soda fountain nozzles clean and sanitized.

At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

comment:

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
The dish puck registered 154F at today’s inspection. The dish machine rinse temperature is reading 133F on the integrated thermometer. The breaker to the machines water booster heater has been turned off as the garbage disposal is in the same circuit and the garbage disposal is malfunctioning. The electricity to the dish machine must be left on so that the machine runs at the proper temperature to sanitizer equipment. The equipment and utensils can also be sanitized using the 3 part sink and proper concentration of sanitizer for the appropriate contact time. The items washed today will be rewashed in the dish machine. The machine is now functioning as the booster heater is working now that the circuit breaker was turned back on. The dish puck is now reading 166F.  The violation is considered corrected on site. If the electricity to the booster heater must be turned off, the dishes and equipment must be sanitized in the 3 part sink. Management is now going to require a daily log for dish puck temperature to ensure that the machine is running properly. 

Ensure that the dish puck is run daily to verify that the machine is functioning properly. 

4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices.

At the snack counter, the inspector noted a spray bottle of cleaner in a cabinet next to food related items. A container of sanitizer wiped is observed next to the coffee making supplies in a different base cabinet. The facility manager moved the items immediately. The employee working at this area was coached concerning this matter. The violation is considered corrected on site. Store chemicals in the open cabinet under the cash register with other chemical cleaners. 

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

title: Proper date marking and disposition
comment:
Sliced deli meats are observed in the walk in #2. Deli meats are not date marked. Ensure that all foods taken in are properly date marked. The items were received yesterday. The packages were properly date marked today. The violation is considered corrected on site. 


3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
comment:
Inspector observed shelf liner on shelf behind hot holding to be absorbent and not cleanable. Replace liner with a material that is consistent with the following section of the code. 

4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material.

comment:
Inspector observed a large quantity container holding some ranch dressing with no date marking and a same size container of Caesar dressing with the date 3-30 on it. The Ranch was discarded. Also quantities of pasta salads made in house are observed to have no date marking. Facility is closed Mondays so the pasta salads were fresh yesterday.  Yesterdays date was placed on the items immediately. Take care to properly date mark items and discard items in 7 days. The violation is considered corrected on site.

title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
comment:
Area around fan at the dish area is open to the outside. Provide proper covering of mesh to preclude pests.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
comment:
Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth on the counter at the wait station. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizing solution between uses every time. Do not let wet wiping cloths sit on surfaces. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
comment:
The following non food contact surfaces are observed soiled: inside of pasta magic, inside of fryers, drain tube and top of true pasta cooler and the area between the soda fountain and the tea holders in the back dining area.
Clean these areas and maintain them free of accumulated soil.

4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Two areas have base cove that is in disrepair of coming up off of the wall. One tile at the doorway to the dish room and rubber type base cove next to the dough cooler. 

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
The floor in the kitchen has areas of disrepair. There is are two areas behind the pasta magic machine, and an area where the kitchen floor meets the dish room.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
Inspector observed the floor under the fryers and around the wheel of the oven to be heavily soiled with food debris and grease. The area needs to be maintained clean as there are several glue traps in the area with pests on them. Grease and food debris is a strong attractant for pests. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
comment:
Inspector observed unopened cans of personal drinks stored randomly in cold holding units mixed with items for service to the public. Inspector suggests providing a bus tub or other solid container in which to store employee food items. The container can go on the floor of the walk in under the shelves. Items were moved to the walk in.
Two different phones and a speaker were observed on surfaces in the kitchen. The phones were located next to sheet pans that were going to be put into the oven and heated to well above 165F. These are still food related items and should be protected from personal items such as phones and speakers. The phones were moved to surfaces were food related items are not going to be stored. 
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the SPRING Care Center were not available. Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

title: Thermometers provided & accurate
comment:
Probe thermometers in the SUMMER kitchen were not accurate. One thermometer read 0F at room temperature. Another thermometer ready 35F when in ice water. CORRECTED- Thermometers were calibrated using ice water. Check thermometer calibration on a regular basis to ensure they are accurate to +/-2F.
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
There wasn’t a CFPM at the start of the inspection. CFPM arrived before inspection ended. Ensure that a CFPM is available at all hours of operation. 

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
Observed PIC not wash hands before engaging in food preparation. PIC shook inspector’s hand and proceeded to prepare food. Discussed with PIC to wash hands before engaging in food production. Ensure that hands are washed before engaging in food production after switching tasks. 

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
comment:
Observed PIC using bare hands to touch a ready-to-eat food item. PIC mentioned that the facility just received boxes of gloves prior to inspector’s arrival. Ensure that employees do not use  bare hand contact with RTE foods. 

3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved.

comment:

The freezer is used to store ice for the drinks in the bar area. Ensure that equipment of food contact surfaces are cleaned and maintained as frequent as necessary to prevent contamination.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

comment:

7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below).

comment:
Observed clean utensils stored in a container with food debris at the bottom. Discussed with PIC and container was switched. Ensure that utensils are always stored in manner that prevents them from contamination.

comment:
Observed the handwashing sink in the dish machine area to not have an adequate flow of hot water. PIC mentioned that the hand-sink barely gets used. Ensure that hand-sinks always have an adequate flow of hot water to properly wash hands.

comment:
Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning. 
- floors, walls, sides and underneath of equipment are soiled with food debris and splatter. 
- Shelving in the kitchen area has food debris
- Wall behind dish machine (mold on caulk where dish machine and wall meet)
Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent accumulated debris.

comment:
PIC is not allergen trained. Ensure that all CFPMs are allergen trained. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
