Observed several packages of beef in the process of being thawed at room temperature. Discussed different options of approved thawing methods with PIC. Ensure that TCS foods are thawed by approved methods and not thawed at room temperature. 

3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). 4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-602.12: (A) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking and baking EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours. This section does not apply to hot oil cooking and filtering EQUIPMENT if it is cleaned as specified in Subparagraph 4-602.11(D)(6). 

The racks in the chicken baking oven are heavily coated with baked on char. This is a food contact items and should be cleaned regularly to prevent this accumulation. The PICs were shown this and instructed to clean the equipment, and maintain it free of accumulated food debris.

title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

A thick accumulation of ice is observed along the floor/wall junction at the far right of the walk in freezer under the shelves. Remove the ice and maintain the floor both clean and easily cleanable.

title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

CFPM for the facility has an expired license (2023). See that at least one member is a certified food protection manager for the facility. At least one CFPM is needed for the events (such as a the Lenten fish fry occurring today). Correct by next routine inspection.

title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements available for the facility. Facility has misplaced the folder (paperwork was present during last few routine inspections). Provided copy for the facility. Ensure all staff read and sign the document (including bar staff). Ensure new hires read and sign the documents as a part of onboarding. Keep copies of the paperwork in a public health folder or binder. Inspector will follow-up on 4/1/24.

Inspector is leaving SCDPH on 3/29/24. Inspector instructed PIC to text AS photos of the signed employee health reporting agreements next week before 3/29 to put a Spot Check in CDP and close out the violation. Cell: 217-891-3012.

title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
comment:
The PERSON IN CHARGE shall: (A) FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations not conducted in private home/room with sleeping quarters;  (B) restricted access ; (C) visitors comply with Code; (D) monitor EMPLOYEES' handwashing; (E) monitor deliveries;  (F) approved source/unadulterated;  (G) proper cooking TCS Food; (H) proper cooling ; (I) monitoring temperatures; (J) consumer advisory conveyed; (K) proper sanitizing;  (L) buffets are controlled;  (M) preventing cross-contamination of RTE FOOD with bare hands; (N) EMPLOYEES are properly trained in FOOD; (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of responsibility to report information about health; (P) Written procedures and plans are maintained and implemented as required. 

The dish machine is not functioning correctly. Sanitizer concentration barely registers on inspector test strips and does not reach the 200 ppm Quat requirement for effective sanitizing. A temporary measure has been put in place until maintenance can be conducted. The maintenance person was available during this inspection and conversations were had in relation to the machine. The follow-up is being set for two weeks for compliance.

title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
comment:
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use  standard contact time 30 seconds. 

The dish machine is observed to barely register Quat sanitizer on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation showed that the jug of concentrate is only showing at 200-400ppm in solution. It is possible that the chemical is off gassing prior to use as the rate of consumption is so slow at the facility. The three part sink was set up to act as a sanitizing step as a temporary measure until that maintenance can be conducted. Refer to line item #1 for follow up.

title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
comment:
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. 

On arrival, the test strips used for the sanitizers in the facility are not working effectively. They appear to have been degraded, possibly by heat or moisture. Ensure that new test strips are acquired and maintained in a usable state.

title: Hands clean and properly washed
comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

An employee was observe to begin slicing a lemon for drinks without hand washing prior. Hand washing was discussed with the employee/PIC. Ensure that hand washing takes place prior to handling any RTE foods.

comment:

4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the reach-in cooler across from the hot holding steam table to have a broken gasket/seal. The gasket should be flush and connected to the door to properly seal the cooler. Temperature issues could arise from a broken gasket/seal. Discussed with PIC. Ensure the gasket/seal is replaced by the next routine inspection.

title: Allergen training as required
comment:
The CFPM present for the inspection could not show proof of allergen training. Ensure that all CFMSa are allergen trained. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
